quote: : “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 10:1: ““Whole in his Torah” corresponds to “with all your soul.” For “A person’s soul is Hashem’s lamp,” and “Your word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path”—the light of Torah. All Israel’s souls together constitute the words of Torah, as the sacred books explain the name Israel: “There are six hundred thousand letters in the Torah.” Each Jewish soul is a letter, or part of a letter, among the Torah’s letters; that letter illuminates and directs the Jewish soul’s path. Thus, “What are the righteous like before the Divine Presence? A lamp before a great flame.” “Whole in his Torah” therefore means that all Israel’s souls are within holiness.”

: ““These are the names of the children of Israel”—they are mentioned here in connection with Israel’s redemption. Reuben: “I have surely seen My people’s affliction.” Simeon: “God heard their groaning.” Levi: because the Holy One, blessed be He, joined in their distress, “from within the bush,” fulfilling, “I am with him in distress.” Judah: because they gave thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He. Issachar: the Holy One, blessed be He, rewarded their bondage with the spoil of Egypt and the sea, fulfilling, “Afterward they shall leave with great wealth.” Zebulun: because the Holy One, blessed be He, caused His Presence to dwell among them, as it says, “They shall make Me a sanctuary, and I shall dwell among them.” Zebulun signifies the Temple, as it says, “I have built You a lofty house, a place for You to dwell forever.” Benjamin: “Your right hand, Lord, is majestic in strength.” Dan: “The nation that enslaves them I shall judge, and afterward they shall leave with great wealth.” Naphtali: the Torah and commandments the Holy One, blessed be He, gave them, of which it is written, “Sweeter than honey and dripping honeycomb.” Gad: the manna the Holy One, blessed be He, fed them, which was “like coriander seed.” Asher: all who heard of their redemption and greatness acclaimed them, as it is written, “All nations shall call you fortunate, for you shall be a land of delight, says the Lord of hosts.” Joseph: because the Holy One, blessed be He, will again redeem Israel from the wic

Parallel: Kometz HaMinchah 2:79:1: “A name everywhere expresses a thing’s power, existence, and vitality, as Scripture says, “Whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.” Therefore the Sages say that, among the tribes, wherever “therefore” introduces the naming, the tribe had a numerous population: the name is its vitality, and the reason for the name is the source of that vitality. “Therefore” means that the name remains attached to its reason; when vitality remains attached to its source, it flows abundantly.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword, as it says, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” How does the verse indicate this? Mar Zutra—or, according to another report, Rav Ashi—said: From the beginning of the passage, “Let the devoted rejoice in honor; let them sing upon their beds,” followed by, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” Rabbi Yitzchak also said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed keeps destructive forces away, as it says, “The sons of reshef fly high.” “Flight” refers to Torah, as in, “Will you let your eyes fly toward it, and it is gone?” “Reshef” refers to destructive forces, as in, “Exhausted by hunger and devoured by reshef and bitter destruction.””

: ““Such as Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai and his companions.” But below, on 33b, it says that when the time for prayer arrived, he would dress, wrap himself, and pray. That reference to praying means the recitation of Shema.”

: “The exaltation of God is in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand: to carry out vengeance among the nations and rebuke among the peoples; to bind their kings with chains and their dignitaries with iron fetters; to execute upon them the written judgment. This is the splendor of all His devoted ones. Hallelujah!”

: “If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For the designation “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.””

: “Rava expounded: What does “How beautiful are your steps in sandals, daughter of the generous one” mean? How beautiful are Israel’s feet when they ascend for the pilgrimage festival. “Daughter of the generous one” means the daughter of our father Abraham, who was called generous, as it says, “The generous among the peoples gathered, the people of Abraham’s God.” Why “Abraham’s God,” rather than the God of Isaac and Jacob? Because Abraham was the first of the converts.”

: “R. Yohanan said: A gentile who engages in Torah incurs the death penalty, as it says, “Moses commanded us the Torah as an inheritance”—an inheritance for us, not for them. Why is this not counted among the seven commandments? According to the reading “inheritance,” he is stealing it; according to the reading “betrothed,” his judgment is like that of violating a betrothed young woman, which is stoning. They raised an objection: R. Meir used to say: From where do we know that even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest? It says, “Which a human being shall perform and live through them.” It does not say “priests, Levites, and Israelites,” but “a human being.” Thus even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest. That statement concerns their own seven commandments.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 11:1: “All the good things, and likewise all the rebukes stated in the Torah, serve only as assistance in His service. If “you walk in My statutes,” assistance comes through this world’s good things; if, Heaven forbid, “you reject My statutes,” assistance comes through this world’s rebukes and sufferings. David said, “Your rod and Your staff comfort me”: “Your rod” means sufferings, while “Your staff” means good things; both guide me toward the good and upright path. Suffering is only like a father disciplining his son to guide him toward goodness. Thus the Sages explain why the public reading of the curses is not interrupted: “My son, do not reject Hashem’s discipline.” It resembles a father raising his rod to discipline his son: the son immediately returns to the good path, and no further discipline is needed.”

: “Thus Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by “Those passing through the valley of weeping make it a spring; the teacher is also clothed in blessings”? “Those passing” are people who transgress the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. “The valley”—Gehinnom is deepened for them. “Weeping”—they weep and shed tears like a spring flowing into the depths. “The teacher is also clothed in blessings”—they accept their judgment as just, saying: Master of the world, You have judged well, acquitted well, condemned well, and rightly prepared Gehinnom for the wicked and Eden for the righteous. Is that so? Reish Lakish said: The wicked do not repent even at Gehinnom’s entrance, as it says, “They shall go out and see the corpses of the people who rebel against Me.” It does not say “who rebelled,” but “who rebel,” meaning that they continue rebelling forever. There is no difficulty: One statement concerns Israel’s sinners, the other the sinners of the nations. This is also reasonable, since otherwise Reish Lakish would contradict himself. Reish Lakish said: Gehinnom’s fire does not rule over Israel’s sinners. This follows all the more from the golden altar: Though covered by only a dinar’s thickness of gold, it stood for many years without fire ruling over it. How much more so Israel’s sinners, who are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate! For “Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate” may be read, “Even your empty ones are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate.” What then of

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: Adam was a heretic, as it says, “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, Where are you?”—where has your heart turned? R. Isaac said: He drew his foreskin forward. Here it says, “Like Adam, they transgressed the covenant,” and elsewhere it says, “He has broken My covenant.””

: “Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: During all the years that Adam was under ban, he fathered spirits, demons, and night-demons, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image.” This implies that before then he did not father beings in his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say: Adam was a great pious man. When he saw that death had been decreed through him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and placed a girdle of fig leaves upon his body for one hundred and thirty years. The earlier statement concerns semen that he emitted involuntarily.”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “‘These are the names.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him seeks discipline for him early.’ Ordinarily, if one person tells another, ‘So-and-so struck your son,’ the father pursues that man to the utmost. Why, then, does Scripture say, ‘One who withholds his rod hates his son’? To teach that whoever withholds discipline from his son will ultimately see him take a corrupt path and come to hate him.”

: ““These are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; each man came with his household.” This is what Scripture says: “One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him disciplines him early.” Ordinarily, if someone tells a man, “So-and-so struck your son,” he becomes his bitter enemy. What, then, does “One who withholds his rod hates his son” teach? Whoever withholds discipline from his son will ultimately see him fall into evil ways, and will hate him.”
: ““Joseph died, and all his brothers, and that entire generation.” This teaches that as long as any one of those who had descended to Egypt remained alive, the Egyptians did not enslave Israel.”

: “‘Jacob lived in the land of Egypt.’ Why is this section closed, unlike the other Torah sections? Once our father Jacob died, Israel’s enslavement in Egypt began. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because our father Jacob wished to reveal the end of the exile, but it was concealed from him. Another interpretation: Why is it closed? Because God closed off from him all the troubles of the world.”

: “When Jacob died, bondage began: they began feeling the evil inclination’s bondage through Egypt’s shell, and the labor of struggling against it began. Rashi therefore says that when Jacob our father died, Israel’s eyes and hearts were closed through the distress of bondage. The Zohar likewise says, 'When Jacob died, Israel’s eyes were closed.' Their eyes allude to wisdom in the brain, from which the eyes are rooted; therefore the Sanhedrin and Israel’s sages are called the congregation’s eyes. Their hearts mean understanding in the heart. Through the shell, Israel’s springs of wisdom and understanding were closed, and the bondage of Egypt’s shell entered heart and brain.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “The soul is called by five names: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, yechidah, and chayyah. Nefesh is the blood, as it says, ‘For the blood is the nefesh.’ Ruach ascends and descends, as it says, ‘Who knows whether the spirit of human beings ascends upward?’ Neshamah is one’s disposition, as people say, ‘His disposition is good.’ It is called chayyah because all the limbs are lifeless, while it lives within the body; and yechidah because all the limbs come in pairs, while it is alone within the body.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘How long shall the world continue in darkness? Let light come!’ ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to Abraham, as it says, ‘Who aroused righteousness from the east?’ Read not he’ir, ‘aroused,’ but he’ir, ‘illuminated.’”

: ““A man of exactions ruins it”—this is the generation of the Flood, who did not practice justice. See what is written concerning them: “They drive away the orphans’ donkey; they turn the needy away from the road.” Rabbi Acha said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give them four things: Torah, suffering, sacrificial service, and prayer. They did not want them, as it says, “They said to God: Depart from us”—this means suffering. “We do not desire knowledge of Your ways”—this means Torah. “What is Shaddai, that we should serve Him?”—these are the sacrifices. “What would we gain by entreating Him?”—this is prayer. The Holy One, blessed be He, told them: What caused you to perish from the evening of this world and the morning of the world to come? Your refusal to accept Torah, which contains justice, as it says, “From morning to evening they are crushed.” Why? “Without anyone taking notice, they perish forever.” “Taking notice” signifies judgments, as it says, “These are the judgments that you shall place before them.””

: “Rabbi Yose taught: in the very event in which judgment was found for the Egyptians, mercy was found for Israel, as in ‘I shall see the blood and pass over you.’ Likewise, in all the holy crowns above, where judgment is found, mercy is found, all at the same moment. Rabbi Chizkiyah taught: ‘The Lord shall strike Egypt, striking and healing’—striking Egypt and healing Israel. What is the healing? Having been circumcised, they needed healing.”

: “The two lights are described as two faces, male and female. ‘Let there be light’ is Passover: ‘On the evening of the fourteenth.’ ‘And there was light’ is Rosh Hashanah, of which it says, ‘And it was the day.’ Here it says vayhi, and there it says vayhi; wherever vayhi occurs, it is an expression of distress.”
: “For abundant wisdom brings abundant vexation, and whoever increases knowledge increases pain.”

: “An elder rose and began: ‘Let there be light, and there was light.’ ‘Let there be light’ is the right; ‘and there was light’ is the left, for vayhi always expresses distress. Therefore ‘And it was the day’ refers to Rosh Hashanah, the left, which judges the whole world. Because of it, ‘And there was light’ was said. ‘God saw that the light was good’ is the middle pillar, which is good. ‘God divided between the light and the darkness’: the light is Aaron the priest; the darkness is Korach. Moses said, ‘It falls to me to resolve the dispute, for I am the likeness of the goodness above.’ He saw that Korach clung to the darkness of the Other Side and contradicted creation, refusing to cleave to the left, Levi. He therefore said, ‘Separate yourselves from this congregation.’”

: “Because of the mystery of this light, which burns and illuminates this lamp, Aaron is told, ‘When you raise the lamps,’ for he comes from this light’s side. Of this light it says, ‘Let there be light, and there was light.’ Once ‘Let there be light’ was said, why add ‘And there was light,’ rather than the sufficient ‘And it was so’? ‘Let there be light’ is the primordial light, the right, belonging to the end of the right. ‘And there was light’ means that the left issued from the right’s mystery. Therefore ‘And there was light’ is the left.”

: “He began grieving over the breaking of the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, which contained only the Ten Commandments. In the second tablets I give you, there will be laws, midrash, and aggadot, as it is written, “He will tell you wisdom’s hidden things, for sound wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you receive the tidings that I have forgiven your sin, as it says, “Know that God remits some of your iniquity.””

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You suffered; by your life, you will not lose! The first tablets contained only the Ten Commandments. Now that you have suffered, I give you laws, midrashim, and aggadot, as it says, “Write for yourself these words.” Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, say “Write for yourself,” when it is written, “The writing was God’s writing, engraved upon the tablets,” and, “He wrote upon the tablets like the first writing”? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Write Torah, Prophets, and Writings, so that they shall be written; but laws, midrash, aggadot, and the Talmud shall remain oral. When Moses understood, he began saying, “It is good for me that I was afflicted”; “The Torah of Your mouth is good for me.””

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””

: “Wherever “these” is said, it rejects what preceded; “and these” adds praise to what preceded. “These are the generations of heaven and earth” rejects chaos and emptiness. “And these are the names” adds praise to the seventy souls mentioned above, for all of them were righteous.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

: “All the tribes were named in reference to Israel’s redemption. Reuben: ‘I have indeed seen the affliction of My people.’ Simeon: ‘God heard their groaning.’ Levi: ‘Many nations shall join the Lord.’ Judah: ‘I thank You, Lord, though You were angry with me.’ Issachar: ‘There is a reward for your labor.’ Zebulun: ‘I have surely built You a dwelling house.’ Benjamin: ‘The Lord has sworn by His right hand.’ Dan: ‘The nation whom they serve, I shall judge.’ Naphtali, read as nofet li, ‘honey for me’: ‘Your lips drip honey, bride.’ Gad: ‘The manna was like coriander seed.’ Asher: ‘All the nations shall call you fortunate.’ Joseph: ‘The Lord shall once again extend His hand.’”

: “‘You shall know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the grass of the field.’ Rabbi Yudan said: Our father Jacob did not depart this world until he had seen six hundred thousand of his descendants.”

: “Another interpretation: “He saw their burdens.” He saw that they had no rest. He went and told Pharaoh: If a person owns a slave and does not let him rest one day a week, the slave dies. These are your slaves; if you do not let them rest one day a week, they will die. He replied: Go and do for them as you say. Moses went and established Shabbat as their day of rest.”

: ““Let the work weigh heavily upon the men.” This teaches that they possessed scrolls in which they delighted from one Shabbat to the next, declaring that the Holy One, blessed be He, would redeem them, for they rested on Shabbat. Pharaoh told them, “Let the work weigh heavily upon the men, so that they work at it and pay no heed…” Let them neither delight in those scrolls nor rest on the Shabbat day.”

: ““Had Your Torah not been my delight…” Israel said: Had Your Torah not been with me as my delight, I would have perished in my affliction. Moses likewise says, “When my anxious thoughts multiply within me…” Pharaoh likewise says, “Let the work weigh heavily upon the men…” They had books in which they delighted from one Shabbat to the next. Therefore it says, “Had Your Torah not been my delight…””

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: “Rabbi Shimon also said: we learned that Shabbat is an image of the world to come, and certainly it is. Thus the sabbatical year and Jubilee mirror one another, as do Shabbat and the world to come. The additional soul comes from the mystery of ‘remember’ to this Shelter of Peace, which receives it from the world to come and gives this addition to the holy people. They rejoice in that addition and forget every weekday matter, every sorrow and distress, as in ‘On the day the Lord grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil and the hard labor,’ and so forth.”

quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 26:5: “The advised way to cleanse the heart of every sadness and trace of anxiety over worldly matters, even children, life, and livelihood, is the familiar teaching of our Sages, “Just as one blesses for the good…” The Gemara explains this as receiving it with joy, like the joy over a good that is openly seen. For “this too is for good,” but it is not manifest to bodily eyes: it comes from the concealed world, higher than the revealed world. The revealed world corresponds to the vav and heh of the blessed Name Havayah, and the concealed world to yod and heh. Hence the verse, “Happy is the man whom You discipline, Yah,” and so forth.”

: ““Who came to Egypt”—are they arriving today? Had they not already been in Egypt for many days? Rather, while Joseph lived, they did not bear the Egyptians’ burden. When Joseph died, they imposed the burden upon them. Therefore it says, “Who came,” as though they entered Egypt that very day.”

: “Why did Jacob merit life in this world without suffering and without the evil inclination, like what the Holy One, blessed be He, will give the righteous in the future? Because he sat in the house of study from youth to old age, proficient in Scripture, Mishnah, laws, and aggadot, as it says, “Jacob was a wholehearted man, dwelling in tents”; also, “Like arrows in a warrior’s hand are the sons of youth; fortunate is the man…”; and, “To whom shall he teach knowledge?… Those weaned from milk, withdrawn from the breast.” When he left his father’s house for Laban’s, the Divine Presence stood above him and answered: Jacob My son, raise your eyes to heaven. See the twelve constellations and the stars in the firmament, the twelve hours of day and twelve hours of night, corresponding to the twelve tribes I give you. When Jacob returned from Laban’s house and Joseph was sold, he wept and mourned twenty-two years, as it says, “All his sons and daughters arose to comfort him… His father wept for him.” Was he weeping only for Joseph? Rather, he said: Perhaps I incurred guilt by marrying two sisters, or by benefiting from Laban’s or Shechem’s wealth, and the covenant the Holy One, blessed be He, made with me has been annulled. Immediately the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, was stirred, and He gave Jacob seventeen good years near his old age, resembling the world to come.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

: “The name Yaakov has four letters, corresponding to four crowns with which his children crown the Holy One, blessed be He: yod corresponds to the Ten Commandments; ayin, to the seventy elders; qof, to the Temple his children built for Him, whose height was one hundred cubits, as it says, ‘The Temple: one hundred cubits’; and bet, to the two tablets.”

: “As soon as he comes, ‘A mist shall rise from the earth’: the alef-dalet of Adonai raises vav to him, becoming within her ‘Lord of all the earth.’ Immediately, ‘It waters the whole face of the ground.’ From him Israel below is watered through the seventy facets of Torah.”

: “Rabbi Eliezer again told them: “If the law follows my view, let Heaven prove it.” A heavenly voice declared: “Why do you contend with Rabbi Eliezer, when the law follows him everywhere?” Rabbi Yehoshua rose to his feet and declared: “It is not in heaven!” What does “It is not in heaven” mean? Rabbi Yirmiyah said: The Torah has already been given at Mount Sinai. We pay no attention to a heavenly voice, for You already wrote in the Torah at Mount Sinai, “Follow the majority.” Rabbi Natan met Elijah and asked him: “What was the Holy One, blessed be He, doing at that moment?” He answered: “He was smiling and saying, ‘My children have prevailed over Me! My children have prevailed over Me!’””

: “‘But I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.’ If it is true, why call it merely ‘inscribed’? And if it is merely inscribed, why call it ‘true’? Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi asked, ‘Did you not know how to answer?’ Rabbi Levi replied: ‘It is inscribed before the decree is issued; it is true once the decree has been issued.’ What is truth? The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our Master said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: It is emet, ‘truth.’ What is emet? Reish Lakish said: Alef stands at the beginning of the alphabet, mem in the middle, and tav at the end, corresponding to ‘I am the first, and I am the last.’”

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rav Yehudah said: Where does the Torah require the blessing after a meal? “You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.” Where does the Torah require a blessing before Torah study? “When I proclaim Hashem’s name, ascribe greatness to our God.””

: “Rabbi Yannai was walking along the road and saw a man who appeared very distinguished. He said: Will the master consent to be our guest? He replied: Yes. He brought him home, fed him, and gave him drink. He tested him in Scripture and found him unlearned; in Mishnah, aggadah, and Talmud, and found him unlearned. He said: Take the cup and recite the blessing. The man replied: Let Yannai bless in his own house. He asked: Can you repeat what I tell you? He replied: Yes. He told him to say: A dog has eaten Yannai’s bread. The man rose, seized him, and said: My inheritance is with you, and you withhold it from me! He asked: What inheritance of yours is with me? He replied: Once I passed a school and heard the children saying, “Moses commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.” It does not say “the congregation of Yannai,” but “the congregation of Jacob.” He asked: Through what merit did you eat at my table? He replied: Never have I heard an evil report and carried it back to its subject; never have I seen two people quarrelling without making peace between them. Yannai said: You possess all this proper conduct, yet I called you a dog! He applied to him, “One who orders his way”: one who evaluates his path is worth much. For Rabbi Yishmael bar Rav Nachman said: Proper conduct preceded Torah by twenty-six generations, as it is written, “To guard the way of the tree of life.” “The way” is proper conduct, and afterward, “the tree of life” is Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shoftim 11:1: “Afterward He says, “I have placed My words in your mouth.” Every Jew is capable of becoming one of those who labor in Torah. If Hashem delights in him and he thirsts for words of Torah, Hashem is ready to place Torah within him. “I have placed My words in your mouth”—then you yourself become one who “plants the heavens and establishes the earth’s foundation,” as the Zohar says: the Holy One rejoices with him as though He had planted heaven and earth that very day. Every Jew is capable of this. The Midrash says: “All wisdom and all Torah are one simple matter: whoever fears Me and practices Torah will have all wisdom and Torah in his heart.” Every Jew has a portion in Torah, as it says, “The inheritance of Jacob’s congregation.” The Midrash therefore says, “My inheritance is with you”—it does not say “the congregation of Yannai,” but “the congregation of Jacob.” Even the unlearned are called Jacob. Every Jew truly has a portion in Torah and can attain the standing of those who labor in it.”

: “‘These are the names of the children of Israel.’ Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Yose were traveling. Rabbi Eleazar said: ‘Open your mouth, and let your words shine.’ Rabbi Yose replied: ‘May I ask something difficult? I heard the Holy Lamp explain “the children of Israel” as Israel the Elder: all the hosts and camps descending into exile with Jacob, as it says, “with Jacob.” What then is “each man and his household came”?’ He answered: ‘Certainly so. We learned that whoever receives from another is that giver’s house. Hence “each man and his household came.”’”
: “Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chalafta said: All the kingdoms are called by the name ‘Egypt,’ because they bring distress upon Israel.”

: “He began grieving over the breaking of the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, which contained only the Ten Commandments. In the second tablets I give you, there will be laws, midrash, and aggadot, as it is written, “He will tell you wisdom’s hidden things, for sound wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you receive the tidings that I have forgiven your sin, as it says, “Know that God remits some of your iniquity.””

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You suffered; by your life, you will not lose! The first tablets contained only the Ten Commandments. Now that you have suffered, I give you laws, midrashim, and aggadot, as it says, “Write for yourself these words.” Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, say “Write for yourself,” when it is written, “The writing was God’s writing, engraved upon the tablets,” and, “He wrote upon the tablets like the first writing”? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Write Torah, Prophets, and Writings, so that they shall be written; but laws, midrash, aggadot, and the Talmud shall remain oral. When Moses understood, he began saying, “It is good for me that I was afflicted”; “The Torah of Your mouth is good for me.””
: “For abundant wisdom brings abundant vexation, and whoever increases knowledge increases pain.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chayei Sara 6:1: “The wisdom of all the people of the East was a place where the Oral Torah was in exile. Their wisdom stood on the opposing side of the Oral Torah. The holy Zohar explains that in those eastern mountains people taught others sorcery; Laban, Beor, and his son Balaam came from that eastern land. Balaam embodied knowledge on the side of impurity. Scripture says of Solomon’s wisdom—the lower wisdom, the Oral Torah—that it “surpassed” the wisdom of all the people of the East and all Egypt’s wisdom: it grew through the holy sparks he extracted from those forms of wisdom. Although Egypt’s wisdom opposed the Written Torah, Scripture includes Egypt here because the Oral Torah has its root in the Written Torah.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “Another interpretation: “He saw their burdens.” He saw that they had no rest. He went and told Pharaoh: If a person owns a slave and does not let him rest one day a week, the slave dies. These are your slaves; if you do not let them rest one day a week, they will die. He replied: Go and do for them as you say. Moses went and established Shabbat as their day of rest.”

: ““Let the work weigh heavily upon the men.” This teaches that they possessed scrolls in which they delighted from one Shabbat to the next, declaring that the Holy One, blessed be He, would redeem them, for they rested on Shabbat. Pharaoh told them, “Let the work weigh heavily upon the men, so that they work at it and pay no heed…” Let them neither delight in those scrolls nor rest on the Shabbat day.”

: “Was its fire created on the eve of Shabbat? Was it not taught that R. Yosei says: The fire the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the second day will never be extinguished, as it says, “They will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against Me, for their worm will not die and their fire will not be extinguished”? R. Benaah son of R. Ulla said: Why does the second day not say, “It was good”? Because the fire of Gehinnom was created on it. R. Elazar said: Although “It was good” was not said of that day, He included it again on the sixth day, as it says, “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good.””

: “Rabbi Yaakov, the son of Yaakov’s daughter, said: Anyone through whom another person is punished is not admitted into the presence of the Holy One, blessed be He. ... Rather, the proof comes from this verse: “Even punishment for the righteous is not good.” “Not good” means evil, and it is written, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You.” You are righteous, Lord, and evil will not dwell in Your dwelling.”
: “The Holy One, blessed be He, called it “evil,” as it says, “The inclination of the human heart is evil from youth.””

: “Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai says: It is neither a day nor Gehinnom, but a fire issuing from the bodies of the wicked themselves that burns them. What is the basis? It is written, ‘You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your own spirit is a fire that shall consume you.’”

: “Once division had begun, “that it was good” was not said concerning the second day, because the fire of Gehinnom was created on that day. Gehinnom itself was created before the world, but its fire was created on the second day. Scripture says, “Their fire shall not be extinguished.” It does not say “the fire of Gehinnom,” but “their fire.” This means the fire of the evil inclination, which is itself fire. As the Gemara relates, a pillar of fire emerged from him, and he told it, “See, you are fire.” Likewise, something like a fiery lion cub emerged from the Holy of Holies; the prophet told them, “This is the inclination… this is wickedness.” Bereshit Rabbah says: Neither a day nor Gehinnom, but fire issues from the bodies of the wicked and sets them ablaze, as it says, “Your own spirit is a fire that will consume you.” Since “good” was not mentioned at the evil inclination’s creation, it is evil, as in the teaching, “Anyone whose fellow…,” based on “Punishing the righteous is not good.” “Not good” means evil, and it is written, “Evil shall not dwell with You.” Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, called it evil. This is “creating evil”: He created the evil inclination, which is called evil.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: “On Rosh Hashanah everyone in the world passes before Him like bnei maron. What does bnei maron mean? Here they explained: like lambs. Reish Lakish said: like the ascent of Beit Maron. Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel’s name: like the soldiers of David’s army. Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Nevertheless, they are all surveyed in one glance. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Our Mishnah also teaches this, citing “He who forms their hearts together, who understands all their deeds.” What does that mean? If it means that He created everyone and made their hearts alike, we see that this is not so. Rather, it means that the One who formed them sees their hearts all together and understands all their deeds.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 3:1: “To repair the sin at its root, Eleazar had to be watching. We have explained “God saw the light, that it was good”: through His seeing the creation, He placed the light called “good” within it. Likewise, at every stage of creation, “God saw that it was good” means that He placed this light within each particular creature. This is the meaning of “Hashem’s eyes are toward the righteous”: the righteous merit something resembling Hashem’s eyes, as it were, so that through their seeing they too can introduce this light. Through it everything is repaired at the root, at the supernal crown, the tip of the yod that alludes to the concealed Ayin. This is why Eleazar had to watch here as well. This power is given to Aaron’s descendants in every generation.”

: ““Moses answered and said: They will not believe me.” At that moment Moses spoke improperly: the Holy One, blessed be He, had said, “They will listen to your voice,” yet he said, “They will not believe me.” Immediately the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him in keeping with his own approach, giving him signs corresponding to his words. See what follows: “The Lord said to him: What is that in your hand? He said: A staff.” Meaning: Through what is in your hand you deserve to be struck, for you malign My children. They are believers descended from believers: believers, as it says, “The people believed”; descendants of believers, as it says, “He believed in the Lord.” Moses adopted the serpent’s conduct, for it slandered its Creator, saying, “For God knows…” Just as the serpent was stricken, so he would be stricken. See what is written: “He said: Throw it to the ground. He threw it to the ground, and it became a serpent.” Because he acted like the serpent, He showed him the serpent—meaning: You acted as this one did.”

: “Another interpretation: “Then Moses sang.” This is what Scripture says: “They believed His words; they sang His praise.” Rabbi Abbahu said: Although it is already written that they believed while in Egypt—“The people believed”—they returned to unbelief, as it says, “Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand Your wonders.” When they came to the sea and saw the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, and how He judges the wicked—as it says, “My hand shall grasp judgment”—and He drowned Egypt in the sea, immediately “they believed in the Lord.” Through the merit of faith the holy spirit rested upon them, and they sang, as it is written, “Then Moses and the children of Israel sang.” “Then” signifies trust, as in, “From the time he entrusted him with his household,” and, “He placed all he possessed in his hand.” Thus: “They believed His words; they sang His praise.””

: “Our Rabbis said: The elders went with them, but secretly slipped away, one by one and two by two. When they reached Pharaoh’s palace, not one remained, as it is written, “Afterward Moses and Aaron came.” Where were the elders? They had gone away. The Holy One, blessed be He, told them: Is this what you have done? By your lives, I shall repay you. When? When Moses, Aaron, and the elders ascended Mount Sinai to receive the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, sent them back, as it says, “To the elders he said: Wait here for us.””

: ““Let the work weigh heavily upon the men.” This teaches that they possessed scrolls in which they delighted from one Shabbat to the next, declaring that the Holy One, blessed be He, would redeem them, for they rested on Shabbat. Pharaoh told them, “Let the work weigh heavily upon the men, so that they work at it and pay no heed…” Let them neither delight in those scrolls nor rest on the Shabbat day.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: Great is peace, for the Torah related words that were untrue for the sake of peace. Which words? ‘Thus shall you say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers’ wrongdoing and sin.’ We do not find that Jacob commanded any of those things. Rather, he knew Joseph’s piety and did not suspect or regard him as one who would shed blood.”

: “Then it is written, ‘The Lord said to Moses, Why do you cry to Me?’ Sifra DiTzeniuta teaches: ‘to Me’ is precise; everything depends upon the Ancient One. At that moment the Holy Ancient One was revealed, favor was present throughout all the upper worlds, and the light of everything shone.”

: ““This is my God.” Rabbi Eliezer says: How do you know that a maidservant at the sea saw what Isaiah and Ezekiel did not see? For it says, “Through the prophets I use likenesses,” and, “The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.” They compared it to a flesh-and-blood king entering a province, surrounded by bodyguards, with warriors on his right and left and troops before and behind him. Everyone asked, “Which one is the king?” because he was flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself at the sea, no one needed to ask, “Which one is He?” As soon as they saw Him, they recognized Him, and all opened their mouths and said, “This is my God, and I shall glorify Him; my father’s God, and I shall exalt Him!””

: “Of those who lacked faith, what is written? ‘The people wandered and gathered.’ What is ‘wandered,’ shatu? They took folly, shetuta, upon themselves, since they lacked faith. What follows? ‘They ground it in mills or pounded it in a mortar.’ Who imposed all this labor upon them? Their own lack of faith.”

: “Rava said: When a person is brought to judgment, they ask him: Did you conduct your dealings faithfully? Did you set fixed times for Torah? Did you engage in having children? Did you await salvation? Did you reason deeply in wisdom? Did you understand one matter from another? Even so, if the fear of the Lord is his treasure, yes; otherwise, no. It is like someone who told his agent: Bring a kor of wheat up to the loft for me. The agent brought it up. He asked: Did you mix a kav of preserving earth into it? He answered: No. He said: It would have been better had you not brought it up.”

: “Rabbi Tarfon and the elders were once reclining in the upper room of Nitza’s house in Lod. They were asked: Is study greater, or action greater? Rabbi Tarfon answered: Action is greater. Rabbi Akiva answered: Study is greater. They all answered: Study is greater, because study leads to action. A baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose says: Study is great, for it preceded the duty of halla by forty years, terumot and tithes by fifty-four, sabbatical years by sixty-one, and Jubilees by one hundred and three. One hundred and three? It was one hundred and four! He holds that the Jubilee releases slaves at its beginning. Just as learning precedes action, so judgment for it precedes judgment for action, as Rav Hamnuna said: A person is first judged concerning words of Torah, as it says, “Releasing water is the beginning of contention.” Just as judgment for it precedes judgment for action, so its reward precedes reward for action, as it says, “He gave them the lands of nations, and they inherited the toil of peoples, so that they might keep His statutes and observe His teachings.””

: ““A person is first judged concerning words of Torah.” Shabbat 31a says that when a person is brought to judgment, they ask him, “Did you conduct your dealings faithfully?” That concerns the question: They ask him about his dealings. Nevertheless, punishment is first exacted from him for not having fixed times for Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Matot 2:2: “The preserved jar of manna, commanded “so that your generations may know,” likewise did not arise from Moses’ own situation. He expected to enter the Land; had sin not intervened, he would have entered in the standing Israel possessed before the calf. There would have been no need to preserve the jar, for the knowledge that “a person does not live by bread alone” would have remained clear in their hearts forever. All their eating would consequently have been like eating manna, and concern for livelihood would not have distracted them. They would have lived through their faith that a person lives by what comes from Hashem’s mouth, as it says, “Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks.” The wording “This is the matter Hashem commanded” therefore addresses a later need. He knew that they would sin and faith would become deficient in the world. The jar would then be needed “so that your generations may know”—in Jeremiah’s time, when he brought out the jar and said, “You of this generation, see Hashem’s word!””

: ““Releasing water”: Throwing off the yoke of Torah. “The beginning of contention” means the beginning of his judgment. Water means Torah, as it is written, “All who are thirsty, come to the water.””

: “The Sages taught: A poor person, a rich person, and a wicked person come to judgment. They ask the poor person, “Why did you not engage in Torah?” If he says, “I was poor and occupied with earning my food,” they say, “Were you any poorer than Hillel?” They said of Hillel the Elder that every day he worked and earned a tropaik coin. He gave half to the guard of the study hall, and half he used for his own support and his household’s support. Once he found no work, and the guard would not allow him to enter. He climbed up and sat at the skylight’s opening, to hear the words of the living God from Shemaiah and Avtalyon. They said: It was the eve of Shabbat, in the season of Tevet, and snow fell upon him from heaven. When dawn broke, Shemaiah said to Avtalyon, “Avtalyon, my brother, every day the house is light, but today it is dark. Is it perhaps a cloudy day?” They looked up and saw the outline of a person at the skylight. They went up and found snow three cubits deep upon him. They freed him, washed him, anointed him, and seated him before a fire. They said, “This man deserves that Shabbat be overridden for him.””
: “He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what is in darkness, and light dwells with Him.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””

: “It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: You find that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, and gave them only through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. Torah: ‘Happy is the man whom You discipline, Lord, and whom You teach from Your Torah.’ The Land of Israel: ‘Know in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, the Lord your God disciplines you.’ What follows? ‘For the Lord your God brings you into a good land.’ The World to Come: ‘For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light, and disciplinary rebukes are the way of life.’ Whoever disciplines his son increases the son’s love and respect for his father, as it says, ‘Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and bring delight to your soul.’ Thus, ‘One who loves him seeks discipline for him early.’”

: “Rav said: One who deliberately arouses himself should be placed under a ban. Why not simply say that it is forbidden? Because he incites his evil inclination against himself. Rabbi Ami said: He is called a transgressor. Such is the evil inclination’s trade: Today it tells him, “Do this,” tomorrow, “Do this,” and eventually, “Go and worship an idol,” and he goes and does so. Some report Rabbi Ami’s statement this way: Whoever brings himself to sexual thoughts is not admitted into the Holy One’s presence. Here it is written, “It was evil in the Lord’s eyes,” and elsewhere, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.” Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by “Your hands are full of blood”? These are the people who commit adultery with their hands.”

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others.”

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: Adam was a heretic, as it says, “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, Where are you?”—where has your heart turned? R. Isaac said: He drew his foreskin forward. Here it says, “Like Adam, they transgressed the covenant,” and elsewhere it says, “He has broken My covenant.””

: “The Sages say that Joseph required them to fulfill circumcision. They sought Pharaoh’s advice, and he said, ‘Do whatever he tells you.’ The explanation follows what we have taught concerning Passover and the Exodus: the 130 years before Moses’ birth brought down the sparks of holy souls that Adam emitted through wasted seed during the 130 years before Seth was born; Seth, too, was an aspect of Moses. Those sparks first entered the people of the generation of the Flood, who wasted their seed upon the earth in accordance with their root. They reincarnated in the generation of the Dispersion and now among those Egyptians. Joseph knew through the holy spirit that they were those sparks, and therefore required circumcision to begin repairing their original damage to the holy covenant. After circumcision they began to be repaired and reincarnated in the next generation among Israel during those 130 years. Hard labor was decreed upon them to repair, purify and refine them, especially to repair the Dispersion’s sin of building the tower with mortar and bricks. Understand this well; see also the explanation of ‘A new king arose over Egypt.’”

: “‘The spirit of God hovered’: this is the spirit of the Messiah, as it says, ‘The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him.’ By what merit does it approach and come? ‘Hovering over the water’—through repentance, which is likened to water, as it says, ‘Pour out your heart like water.’”

: “What is “Pour out your heart like water before the Lord’s face”? From here they said: Whenever a Torah scholar sits, reads, repeats his learning, and occupies himself with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits opposite him, reading and repeating with him. Here it says, “Before the Lord’s face,” and there it says, “These camped opposite those…” Just as there, these faced those and those faced these, so here. What is written afterward there? “On the seventh day the battle drew near, and the children of Israel struck down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day; the survivors fled…” Had this not been written, it would be impossible to say, and anyone saying it would incur death.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? It is the utterance of David son of Jesse, who established the yoke of repentance. “The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: one ruling over humankind, a righteous man ruling in the fear of God.” What is the verse saying? Rabbi Abbahu explained: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: “I rule over humankind. Who rules over Me? The righteous person, for I issue a decree and he annuls it.””

Commentary: Rashi on Moed Katan 16b:21:1: ““He established the yoke of repentance”: He was the first to return and thereby provided a path for those who repent. As the opening chapter of Avodah Zarah teaches, David was not suited to that deed; rather, when an individual sins, people tell him, “Go to David: the Holy One forgave that sin of his. You too should return in repentance.””

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

: “After turning to a bad course, Acher asked Rabbi Meir: What does “Gold and glass cannot equal it, nor can vessels of fine gold be exchanged for it” mean? He answered: These are words of Torah, difficult to acquire like vessels of gold and fine gold, but easily lost like glass vessels. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. Rather, just as vessels of gold and glass can be repaired after breaking, so a Torah scholar can be restored even after going astray.” Rabbi Meir told him: “Then you too should return.” He answered: “I have already heard from behind the curtain: ‘Return, wayward children’—except Acher.””
