ref: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Shaar HaOtiyot, Hilchot Biah 1:32-33
quote: : “Had he persisted and greatly increased his prayer and afflicted himself with great, severe disciplines as Manasseh did, it is possible that he would have been received with abundant mercy. Although he heard from behind the curtain, 'Except Acher,' he should not have withheld himself from mercy, despite knowing His glory and rebelling against Him. We find a similar case concerning Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya, in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah. They said he had not left a prostitute whom he had not visited. Once he heard of a prostitute in the coastal cities who charged a purse of dinars. He took a purse and crossed seven rivers to reach her. During the act she passed wind and said, 'Just as this wind does not return, so Elazar ben Durdaya will not be received in repentance.' He went and sat among mountains and hills, saying, 'Mountains and hills, plead for mercy for me.' They answered, 'Before we plead for you...' He asked the sun and moon, then the stars and constellations, to plead for him, and finally said, 'The matter depends only upon me.' He placed his head between his knees and wept until his soul departed. A heavenly voice proclaimed, 'Rabbi Elazar ben Durdaya is destined for life in the World to Come.' The Gemara concludes there that because he was so deeply attached to it, it was like heresy. Likewise Acher should not have despaired of repentance. Although a heavenly voice proclaimed, 'Except Acher,' he should have done his part, even if he died through his repent

: “They asked him, “Why do you call yourself Rav Huna?” He replied, “That is my name.” “Why, when they told you to sit upon the bed, did you sit?” He replied, “Whatever the master of the house tells you, do—except leave.””

: “Tzur, “rock,” denotes firmness. Hashem places firmness in the penitent’s heart, as though speaking to him individually, so that he can “rule over man, a righteous one.” Even concerning matters about which Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai states in the Zohar that repentance does not help, the penitent has the power to overcome that judgment and bring rectification. “Ruling in the fear of God” also applies to words spoken by the Holy One, such as the heavenly voice that proclaimed, “Return, wayward children—except Acher.” Even so, Acher could have repaired himself through repentance, because that is Hashem’s will. Thus the Shelah and Reishit Chokhmah explain the allusion in “Do whatever the master of the house tells you, except ‘Leave.’””

: “As we heard from our holy teacher of blessed memory concerning “The Rock of Israel spoke to me: one who rules over man, a righteous one, ruling in the fear of God”: A penitent has great inner resolve, knowing that the Rock of Israel spoke particularly to him with strength and force. “Ruling over man, a righteous one” means Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai, who said that repentance does not help for a blemish of the covenant; the penitent should not heed that discouragement. “Ruling in the fear of God” means that even if a heavenly declaration says repentance will not help him—as Aḥer heard the heavenly voice say, “Return, wayward children, except Aḥer”—he would nevertheless have been accepted had he pressed himself to repent. The Shelah, citing Reshit Ḥokhmah, reads this into “Do whatever the master of the house tells you, except ‘Leave.’” Similarly, the Baal Shem Tov said of himself that he would serve God even without a share in the World to Come, attaining the higher level of serving without seeking reward.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya the Great expounded this. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it says, ‘The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.’ ‘The earth was waste and void’ refers to the deeds of the wicked; ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to the deeds of the righteous. Yet I do not know which He desires—the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, ‘God saw that the light was good,’ we know that He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wicked.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”
: “The Sages taught: Three had relations in the Ark, and all were punished: the dog, the raven, and Ham. The dog became bound, the raven spat, and Ham was stricken in his skin.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; all the males guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient merit for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””
: “Another interpretation: Just as the bush produces thorns and roses, so Israel contains both righteous and wicked people.”

: “Rabbi Yohanan said: For a burning fever, one takes a knife made entirely of iron, goes to a place where a thornbush grows, and ties a white thread to it. On the first day he cuts it a little and says, “An angel of the Lord appeared to him.” The next day he cuts it a little and says, “Moses said: Let me turn aside and see.” The following day he cuts it a little and says, “The Lord saw that he turned aside to see.” Rav Aha, Rava’s son, said to Rav Ashi: Should he not also say, “Do not come near here”? Rather, on the first day he says, “An angel of the Lord appeared to him,” and “Moses said”; the next day, “The Lord saw that he turned aside to see”; and the following day, “The Lord said: Do not come near here.” When cutting it, he lowers it and cuts it, saying: Thornbush, thornbush! Not because you are taller than all the trees did the Holy One, blessed be He, rest His Presence upon you, but because you are lower than all the trees did He rest His Presence upon you. Just as the fire saw Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah and fled before them, so may the fire see so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and flee before him.”
: “Vardinei: a thornbush.”

: ““Israel has sinned.” R. Abba bar Zavda said: Although he has sinned, he remains Israel. R. Abba said: This accords with the popular saying: A myrtle standing among reeds is named myrtle, and myrtle is what people call it.”

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

k: volume-i|116|0|Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruv
ref: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1:2
quote: Parallel: Dover Tzedek, Kuntres Dover Tzedek, Eruvin 1:2: “The Divine Presence has never departed from the western wall: the wall where the light sets. Even near sunset, in the time of darkness, the Divine Presence does not leave the wall that supports a person. “He dwells with them even amid their impurity.” All Israel’s souls are held and linked together like a chain, as in “Jacob is the cord of His inheritance.” Even when the revelation of divine light is hidden, concealed, and greatly contracted, it is never absent from any Jewish heart. Even the lowest of the low possesses a share of life that Hashem apportioned to him from the divine portion above.”

: “Rabbi Ila son of Yevarekhya said: Two Torah scholars who walk along the road without words of Torah between them deserve to be burned by fire, as it says, “As they went on, walking and speaking, behold, a chariot of fire.” It was because there was speech between them; had there been no speech, they would have deserved to be burned.”

: “This Speech is called Shabbat. Because Shabbat is called Speech, weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbat. The printed marginal gloss, Gilyon Maharshab, relates: Rabbi Shimon acted this way—when he saw his mother speaking, he would say to her, ‘Mother, be silent; it is Shabbat, and this is forbidden.’ For this Speech must rule, and no other. This Speech, coming from the side of darkness, reveals deep things from within it. That is the meaning of ‘from darkness’: specifically from that which comes from the side of darkness.”

: “The Sages taught: When our teachers entered the vineyard at Yavne, they said: Torah will one day be forgotten in Israel. For it says, “Days are coming, declares the Lord God, when I will send famine into the land—not a famine for bread or thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the Lord”; and, “They will wander from sea to sea, from north to east; they will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it.” “The word of the Lord” means halakha; “the word of the Lord” means the end of exile; “the word of the Lord” means prophecy. A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai says: Heaven forbid that Torah should be forgotten in Israel, for it says, “It will not be forgotten from the mouth of his descendants.” How, then, do I understand “They will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it”? They will not find a clear halakha and a clear Mishnah together in one place.”

: “‘He shall satisfy your soul with tzachtzachot.’ What is tzachtzachot? One brightness is when it joins the spirit in the lower garden; brightness within brightness is when they unite with the upper soul in the Bundle of Life. Tzach is one, tzachot is two, far above, in the soul’s preciousness: thus tzachtzachot. Who inherits this? Your nefesh—your actual nefesh. Happy is the righteous ones’ portion.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman opened: ‘A Song of Ascents: I lift my eyes to the mountains’—to my parents, who taught and raised me. ‘From where will my help come?’ When Eliezer went to bring Rebecca, Scripture says, ‘The servant took ten camels’; but I have not a single nose ring or bracelet! Rabbi Chanina said: Jacob was sent away with nothing. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Isaac sent possessions with him, but Esau rose and took them. Jacob reconsidered and said, ‘Am I to lose hope in my Creator? Heaven forbid! I shall not lose hope in my Creator. Rather, “My help comes from the Lord.”’”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””

: “Rav Kahana said: What is meant by “For He spoke, and it came to be”? This refers to a wife. “He commanded, and it stood”—this refers to children. It was taught: A woman is a skin-bag filled with excrement, and her mouth is filled with blood; yet everyone pursues her.”
: ““Israel settled in Shittim.” R. Eliezer says: Shittim was the place’s name. R. Joshua says: They occupied themselves with foolish matters.”

: “Reish Lakish said: A person commits a transgression only when a spirit of folly enters him, as it says, “If any man’s wife goes astray.” The word “goes astray” is written in a form that suggests folly.”

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: A gentile woman became seriously ill and said, “If this woman recovers, she will go and worship every idol in the world.” She recovered and worshiped every idol in the world. When she reached Peor, she asked the priests, “How is this one worshiped?” They told her, “People eat beets, drink beer, and defecate before it.” She said, “Better that this woman return to her illness than worship an idol in that manner.””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “One should likewise keep away from frivolity, drunkenness, and erotic talk, for these are powerful causes and steps leading to forbidden relations. He should not remain unmarried, for marriage promotes greater purity. Greater than all this, they said, is that he turn himself and his thoughts to Torah and broaden his mind with wisdom, because thoughts of forbidden relations grow strong only in a heart empty of wisdom. Concerning wisdom it says, 'A loving doe and a graceful mountain goat; let her breasts satisfy you at all times; be constantly absorbed in her love.'”

: “‘He meditates upon His Torah.’ Rabbi Shimon said: Abraham’s father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys to be like two teachers; they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written, ‘I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.’”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””

: “It is written, “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says, “One who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.””

: ““Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did the Lord desire you.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: I desire you because even when I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me. I gave greatness to Abraham, and he said, “I am dust and ashes”; to Moses and Aaron, and they said, “What are we?”; to David, and he said, “I am a worm and not a man.” The nations are otherwise. I gave greatness to Nimrod, and he said, “Let us build ourselves a city”; to Pharaoh, and he said, “Who is the Lord?”; to Sennacherib, and he said, “Who among all the gods of the lands?”; to Nebuchadnezzar, and he said, “I will ascend above the heights of the cloud”; to Hiram king of Tyre, and he said, “I have sat in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.” Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yohanan said: What was said of Moses and Aaron is greater than what was said of Abraham. Of Abraham it is written, “I am dust and ashes,” while of Moses and Aaron it is written, “What are we?””

: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, “Be stirred, and do not sin.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “Speak in your hearts.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recite Shema, as it says, “Upon your beds.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recall the day of death, as it says, “And be silent, selah.””

: “Rabbi Ami said: From Rabbi Yose’s words we learn that even if a person studied only one chapter in the morning and one in the evening, he has fulfilled “This book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth.” Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: Even if a person recited only the Shema in the morning and evening, he has fulfilled “It shall not depart.” It is forbidden to say this before people unlearned in Torah. Rava, however, said: It is a mitzvah to say it before people unlearned in Torah.”

: “Rabbi Mani said: One who recites Shema at its proper time is greater than one studying Torah. For the Mishnah teaches that a person who recites it later has not lost everything, since he is like someone reading Torah. This implies that reciting it at its proper time is superior.”

: “R. Shimon ben Lakish said: “Jacob called to his sons and said, Gather together and I will tell you.” Jacob wished to reveal the end of days to his sons, but the Divine Presence withdrew from him. He said, “Perhaps, God forbid, there is an unfit descendant among my children, as Ishmael came from Abraham and Esau from my father Isaac?” His sons said to him, “Hear, Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.” They meant: Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts. At that moment our father Jacob began and said, “Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.””

k: volume-i|137|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkut
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 3:13–15: “Daat takes its name from “Adam knew Eve”: it means attachment and joining. A person binds his awareness with a very firm and powerful bond, fixes his thought forcefully upon the greatness of the blessed Infinite One, and does not let his attention wander. Even someone wise and discerning about the greatness of the blessed Infinite One will not bring genuine fear and love to birth in his soul unless he binds his awareness and fixes his thought firmly and continuously; he will produce only empty imaginings. Daat therefore sustains the emotional qualities and gives them life. It includes Chesed and Gevurah, meaning love and its branches, and fear and its branches.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword, as it says, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” How does the verse indicate this? Mar Zutra—or, according to another report, Rav Ashi—said: From the beginning of the passage, “Let the devoted rejoice in honor; let them sing upon their beds,” followed by, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” Rabbi Yitzchak also said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed keeps destructive forces away, as it says, “The sons of reshef fly high.” “Flight” refers to Torah, as in, “Will you let your eyes fly toward it, and it is gone?” “Reshef” refers to destructive forces, as in, “Exhausted by hunger and devoured by reshef and bitter destruction.””

: “Rabbi Chiya said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and then lies down to sleep will not receive bad tidings, as it says, “He rests satisfied, untouched by evil.””

: “But what of the verse “He will strengthen your bones”? Rabbi Elazar said: This is the finest of blessings; Rava explained: It means vigor for the bones. Yes, the word can mean either strengthening or removing.”

: “It was taught: Othniel and Jabez are the same person. What was his name? Judah, Simeon’s brother. “Othniel”—God answered him; “Jabez”—he gave counsel and spread Torah in Israel. How do we know that God answered him? It is written, “Jabez called to the God of Israel, saying: If You will indeed bless me, enlarge my border, let Your hand be with me, and act against my harm so that it not grieve me; and God granted what he asked.” “If You will indeed bless me”—with Torah. “Enlarge my border”—with students. “Let Your hand be with me”—so that my learning not be forgotten from my heart. “Act against my harm”—so that I may find companions like myself. “So that it not grieve me”—so that the evil inclination not overpower me and prevent me from studying. If You do this, well and good; otherwise I shall go in my sorrow to Sheol. Immediately, “God granted what he asked.””

: “You too: If you marvel at the reward I paid that wicked man for four steps he ran in pursuit of My honor, how much more so when I pay the reward of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses! This is the meaning of “Concerning the prophets, my heart is broken within me, all my bones tremble; I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome by wine, because of Hashem and because of His holy words.””

: “Rav sat behind Rabbi Hiyya, and Rabbi Hiyya sat before Rabbi. Rabbi was teaching: From where do we learn that slaughter must be performed with something detached? For it says, “He took the knife to slaughter.” Rav asked Rabbi Hiyya: What is he saying? He answered: He is speaking of a letter vav written on a block of wood. But he cited a verse! The verse teaches Abraham’s zeal.”

Commentary: Rashi on Chullin 16a:5:2: ““He is speaking of a vav written on a block of wood”: He is giving an unsound reason, like someone writing a vav on a split log. The letter is broken into sections because the log’s teeth form grooves and its surface is not smooth. Another explanation is that those grooves themselves are called vavs. Rabbi Hiyya follows his own opinion, for above he permits slaughter with an attached implement.”

: “Rav Joseph said: Should we arise and learn from Abraham? Rava said: The tanna learned from Abraham, and should we not learn from him? It was taught: “On the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised”—this teaches that the whole day is valid for circumcision, but those who are eager perform commandments early, as it says, “Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled,” and so forth.”
: ““Should we arise and learn from Abraham?”—Have you come to teach us to be eager like Abraham?”

k: volume-i|146|0|Arizal, Pri Etz Chaim, Sha’ar HaShabbat
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 17:2-4
quote: : “From the companions: at every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should declare, ‘These are meals of complete faith.’ On Friday night one arranges twelve loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Field of Apples; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with her.’ This is Isaac’s meal: he is its master and guides it. Whoever delights in it is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Field of Holy Apples come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Abraham, the pious elder; through his merit one is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. At the afternoon meal one arranges four loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of Ze‘ir Anpin; the Field of Holy Apples and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Jacob, father of seventy souls; through his merit one is saved from the wars of Gog and Magog.”

: “A midrashic teaching likewise says: What is 'I will be who I will be'? Just as you are with Me, so I am with you. If they open their hands and give charity, I too shall open My hand, as it says, 'The Lord will open His good treasury for you.' If they do not open their hands, what is written there? 'He withholds the waters, and they dry up,' and so forth.”

: “Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: “Go and gather Israel’s elders”; tell them, “I have surely remembered.” He told him: They possess a tradition from Joseph that I redeem them with this expression. Go and tell them this sign. What is “I have surely remembered”? “Remembering”—in Egypt; “I have remembered”—at the sea. “Remembering”—for the future; “I have remembered”—for the past. “And what is being done to you in Egypt”: I shall call the Egyptians to account for what they do to you, as in, “I have remembered what Amalek did to you.” “I said: I shall bring you up”—tell them: As I told their father Jacob, so I shall do. What did He tell him? “I shall surely bring you up.” Jacob likewise told his sons, “God shall be with you and bring you back…” Immediately, “They shall listen to your voice.” Why? They possess a tradition of redemption: any redeemer who comes announcing remembrance in its doubled expression is a true redeemer.”

: “In Shemot Rabbah: 'They will immediately heed your voice.' Why? They possess a tradition of redemption: every redeemer who comes and says a doubled expression of visitation is a true redeemer. These are the words of that aggadah. You may ask: how would they know to believe him? Perhaps Moses had heard this tradition as they had. One may answer that this is what they received from Joseph, who heard it from their prophetic father: the first person to come and speak to them in this language would be their redeemer. It was revealed and known before the Holy One, blessed be He, that no one would come and deceive them; this was His promise to them.”

Parallel: Haamek Davar on Exodus 3:14:1: ““I will be as I will be.” The manner is not yet clear, because it depends on the preparation of the recipients. Accordingly, I will conduct My activity according to the power that Israel will, as it were, give Me. It would seemingly have been appropriate to say, “I will be as they will be”: as the congregation of Israel conducts itself in its deeds, so will I conduct Myself in Mine. In truth, however, this too proceeds from God’s providence: that Israel should be fit for this manner or that. Although this is wondrous to the human mind, it is nevertheless so. This is explained in Deuteronomy, in Moses’ blessing to Benjamin, on the basis of a teaching in the Mekhilta, through the remarkable parable of a king who commanded his elder son to awaken him three hours into the day, and his younger son to awaken him in the morning, and so forth. The application is explained there: the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the tribe of Judah the understanding that providence at the splitting of the Sea would operate through nature, while He gave Benjamin the understanding that it would operate through a wondrous miracle. Whichever prevailed at that moment directed the manner of the Sea’s splitting according to his will and understanding. Since both intended to serve Heaven, the Holy One, blessed be He, rewarded each tribe according to its understanding, as explained there at length. In the parable, the king himself bestowed the disposition of his sons.

: “Pe, pe: through it our ancestors were redeemed from Egypt, as it says, “I have surely remembered.” Tzadi, tzadi: through it the Holy One, blessed be He, will redeem Israel from subjugation to the four kingdoms, saying to them, “I have caused a shoot to sprout for you,” as it says, “You shall say to him: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold a man whose name is Shoot; from beneath him he shall sprout.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 2:2: “Through Moses, Hashem placed remembrance and desire for Torah in Israel’s heart. This is “I have surely remembered”: afterward divine assistance comes. In this world, however, the mouth is closed; in the world to come, when all Torah’s secrets are revealed, the mouth is open. The letters tzadi and final tzadi signify “A man whose name is Tzemach”—the Messiah, as it says, “I shall raise up for David a righteous sprout.” The Messiah will bring growth in Israel’s heart from the letter tzadi. Its principal completion will be the upright tzadi of the world to come, when evil is entirely annulled.”

: “That Jew told him: my father said to me as he departed this world, ‘Do not expect the Messiah’s footsteps until this rainbow appears in the world, adorned with brilliant colors and illuminating the world. Then await the Messiah.’”
: “Onkelos translated the first two names, 'I will be with whom I will be.' He did not translate at all the name in 'Thus shall you say to the children of Israel: Ehyeh has sent me to you.'”

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they said: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed? Did the Holy One, blessed be He, not tell Abraham, “They shall enslave and afflict them for four hundred years,” yet we have only two hundred and ten? He replied: Since He desires your redemption, He does not look at your calculations, but “leaps over the mountains.” The mountains and hills here signify appointed times and added periods: He leaps over calculations, appointed times, and added periods. You are being redeemed this month, as it says, “This month shall be yours, the first of months.” Rabbi Nechemya said: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they asked: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed, when we have no good deeds? He replied: Since He desires your redemption, He does not look at your evil deeds. At whom does He look? At your righteous people and their deeds, such as Amram and his court. “Leaping over mountains, bounding over hills”—mountains signify courts, as in, “I shall go down upon the mountains.” You are being redeemed this month, as it says, “This month shall be yours, the first of months.” The Rabbis said: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they said: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed when all Egypt is

: “Ramban, in Shemot, cites Targum Onkelos—although this is not found in the Targum Onkelos before us—as translating “I shall be what I shall be” as “I shall be with whomever I shall be.” The meaning is that, when Hashem promises to be with someone in the future, He is already with him from the moment of the promise. Thus, “I shall show favor to whom I shall show favor”—in the future. Although the Name Ehyeh indicates the future, it immediately shines in the present. Hashem similarly told Abraham, “I shall make you into a great nation”: I am creating you anew, so that those five organs too will come under your control. “A great nation” means that the Jewish people is included within him, bound at the root to the attribute of greatness, extending without limit to the root. Through this promise, Abraham already attained being a vehicle for the attribute of greatness.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: then, when everything shone together, the sea performed the upper ordinances, and those above and below were entrusted into its hands. Therefore everything is difficult before God like the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as the teachings explain. Why? Because the splitting of the Sea of Reeds depends upon the Ancient One.”

Parallel: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Miketz 40:2: “The name Ehyeh signifies, as the Zohar says, “I am ready to draw forth and give birth to all.” Hashem will illuminate in the future and open the storehouse of light to illuminate everything. From what the Holy One will bestow in the future, deliverance grows even now, lifting one from the depths; joy and strength are born in Israel’s heart. This is the allusion of “Ehyeh asher Ehyeh”: because in the future I shall give birth to deliverance, I shall be with you even now.”
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Certainly ‘Her husband is known in the gates’ refers to God, who becomes known and cleaved to according to what each person measures within his heart, insofar as he can cleave through a spirit of wisdom. According to what he measures in his heart, so He becomes known in his heart. Therefore ‘known in the gates’—through those measures. But no one can grasp and know Him as He truly is.”

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “He said: Elder, elder, do you ask this? This certainly concerns a righteous person’s soul. Although it must descend in reincarnation among all these—even servant, maidservant, animals corresponding to the wheels, or all the living creatures from which human souls proceed—‘You shall do no work’ is said of it. This is ‘You shall not impose a slave’s labor upon him.’ Upon the Righteous One, the Shabbat day, you shall not impose a slave’s labor, which belongs to a weekday.”

: “Rav said: One who deliberately arouses himself should be placed under a ban. Why not simply say that it is forbidden? Because he incites his evil inclination against himself. Rabbi Ami said: He is called a transgressor. Such is the evil inclination’s trade: Today it tells him, “Do this,” tomorrow, “Do this,” and eventually, “Go and worship an idol,” and he goes and does so. Some report Rabbi Ami’s statement this way: Whoever brings himself to sexual thoughts is not admitted into the Holy One’s presence. Here it is written, “It was evil in the Lord’s eyes,” and elsewhere, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.” Rabbi Elazar said: What is meant by “Your hands are full of blood”? These are the people who commit adultery with their hands.”

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

Parallel: Machshavot Charutz 11:7: “This occurs through the voice that is above speech and the actual articulation of letters; within it the letters of thought and the heart’s cry are revealed. No thought in the heart can fail to produce some voice expressing how deeply that thought has taken hold. “The voice is Jacob’s voice”—Jacob, whose offspring are complete. Through it the light that “Israel arose in thought” becomes manifest. Even the sinners of Israel have a hold in this voice: at some point in their lives they utter a true cry to Hashem from the heart’s depths, whether a cry of joy from love and recognition of His kindness and compassion, or a sound of groaning and weeping from fear and dread. This is the shofar’s voice. Through it our remembrance rises for good, recalling all the voices of awakening from below. We sweeten the sounds of fear through sounds of joy—the simple blast before and after—for His love truly surrounds us on every side.”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”

: “R. Samuel bar Nahmani said in R. Yonatan’s name: What is meant by “Why is there money in a fool’s hand to acquire wisdom when he has no heart”? Woe to those Torah scholars who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven.”

: ““Happy is the man who fears Hashem.” Is a man happy, but a woman not? Rav Amram said in Rav’s name: Happy is one who repents while still a man in his strength. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Happy is one who masters his inclination like a man.”

: “Rava often said: Wisdom’s purpose is repentance and good deeds. A person must not read Scripture and study Mishnah while rebelling against his father, his mother, his teacher, or someone greater than he in wisdom and seniority, as it says, “The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them.” It does not merely say “those who practice,” but “those who practice them”: those who act for its own sake, rather than those who do not. Whoever acts otherwise would have been better off not having been created.”

Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:11:2: ““One who acts not for its own sake would have been better off not having been created”: this means that he does not learn in order to fulfill the teaching, but in order to provoke. For in the chapter Makom Shenahagu, Rava contrasts “Your kindness reaches to the heavens” with “Your kindness is above the heavens,” distinguishing learning not for its own sake from learning for its own sake. That passage concerns someone who fulfills the teaching in order to receive honor. This also appears from the Jerusalem Talmud on our chapter.”

: “‘A great shofar shall be sounded.’ What difference does it make whether it is great or small? It is the upper shofar, through which slaves continually go free: Jubilee, the great and upper Jubilee. When it awakens, all the worlds’ freedoms awaken through it. Hence it is called the great shofar.”

: “'Do not approach here': Moses had not yet reached his great level of prophecy, for at Mount Sinai he 'approached the thick cloud where God was.' His hiding his face has the same meaning: he had not yet attained the level described by 'He beholds the likeness of the Lord.'”

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: Amram merited a son who attained the great Voice, as it says, ‘God answered him with a voice.’ Amram himself attained a bat kol, as in ‘He took the daughter of Levi’—the daughter of the Voice. Hence ‘he went’: he advanced to this level. It was taught: when Moses was born, God attached His Name to him, as in ‘She saw that he was good,’ and ‘The Lord is good to all,’ and ‘Taste and see that the Lord is good.’”

: “‘But you, stand here with Me.’ From here Moses separated entirely from his wife, cleaving and ascending to another place, the masculine rather than feminine. Happy is Moses the faithful prophet’s portion: he merited upper levels no other person ever attained. Hence ‘One who is good before God escapes her.’ Who is good? Moses, as in ‘He was good.’ Because he was good, he ascended to another, higher level. Therefore ‘The place upon which you stand is holy ground’—precisely ‘upon which you stand.’ Why? Because he was good, and good is masculine.”
: “‘The Lord said to Abram, Go to yourself.’ Rabbi Eleazar said: go for yourself, to repair yourself and repair your level. Go for yourself: you cannot remain here among these wicked people.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: this matter of Moses must be contemplated through upper wisdom. Why is it written, ‘I drew him from the water’? One drawn from the waters—the upper judgment—does not fear fire. Rabbi Yehudah taught: no other person was hewn from the place from which Moses was hewn. Rabbi Yochanan said: he was perfected through ten levels, as in ‘He is faithful in all My house,’ not merely ‘faithful of My house.’ Happy is the person whose Master testifies thus about him.”
: “Rabbi Chelbo said in Rav Huna’s name: The words of anyone who possesses fear of Heaven are heeded, as it says, “The conclusion of the matter: everything is heard—fear God.””

: “When a person takes to heart that the King of kings stands over him, fear reaches him. This is 'The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord'; the Sabbath of Friday night is fear, and fear rests within it. The lower Divine Presence is also called heart, as the sages expounded 'He has no heart' concerning one who lacks fear of Heaven. Through fear he comes to repentance: in Avodah Zarah and Berakhot, fear is interpreted in relation to repentance, since through fear he remembers, regrets his sins, and returns from them. When fear enters the depths of the heart, 'His heart will understand, and he will return' is fulfilled. This is 'Understanding is the heart.'”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 10:1: “Although the words of one who fears Heaven are heard, the hearer must also be a prepared vessel, at least capable of letting the words enter his heart. Before Joseph revealed himself to his brothers, they were not yet vessels prepared to receive his words.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said: Esther had a greenish complexion, but a thread of grace was drawn over her.”

: “In the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts punishment from Esau, what will Esau do? He will wrap himself in his cloak like an elder and come sit beside Jacob. From where do we know this? ‘Though you set your nest among the stars.’ The stars mean Israel, as it says, ‘Look toward heaven,’ and ‘So shall your descendants be.’ What will Jacob tell him? ‘My brother, you cannot be a brother like me,’ as it says, ‘I shall be your plagues, Death; I shall be your destruction, netherworld; compassion shall be hidden from My eyes.’ ‘I shall be your plagues, Death’ refers to the decrees you issued against me: you imposed a twofold decree that I worship idols. Had I done so, I would have incurred death at Heaven’s hand; if I refused to worship, you would kill me. Therefore, ‘I shall be your plagues, Death.’”

: “He went and raised Balaam through necromancy, and asked him: “Who is esteemed in that world?” Balaam answered: “Israel.” He asked: “Should one attach himself to them?” Balaam answered: “Do not seek their peace or welfare all the days.” He asked: “What is that man’s punishment?” Balaam answered: “Boiling semen.” He then raised Jesus the Nazarene through necromancy and asked: “Who is esteemed in that world?” He answered: “Israel.” He asked: “Should one attach himself to them?” He answered: “Seek their welfare; do not seek their harm. Whoever touches them is as though he touches the pupil of His eye.” He asked: “What is that man’s punishment?” He answered: “Boiling excrement,” for the Master taught that anyone who mocks the Sages’ words is judged in boiling excrement. Come and see the difference between Israel’s transgressors and the prophets of the nations.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: A decree was also issued against Noah, but he found favor in Hashem’s eyes, as it says, “I regret that I made them,” followed by, “Noah found favor in Hashem’s eyes.””

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: ‘For I regret that I made them,’ yet ‘Noah found favor’—is that not surprising? Rather, even Noah, who alone remained of them, was not deserving; he survived because he found favor.”

: “Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: This is like a king who built a palace, saw it, and was pleased with it. He said, ‘Palace, palace, may you always find favor in my eyes as you have at this moment!’ So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to His world: ‘My world, My world, may you always find favor before Me as you have at this moment!’”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: Great is peace, for the Torah related words that were untrue for the sake of peace. Which words? ‘Thus shall you say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers’ wrongdoing and sin.’ We do not find that Jacob commanded any of those things. Rather, he knew Joseph’s piety and did not suspect or regard him as one who would shed blood.”

: “Another interpretation of “an Egyptian man”: It is like someone bitten by a serpent who ran to place his feet in water. He put them in a river, saw a child sinking in the water, reached out his hand, and rescued him. The child said: Without you I would have died! He replied: I did not rescue you; the serpent that bit me, from which I fled, rescued you. So Jethro’s daughters told Moses: May your strength be firm, for you rescued us from the shepherds. Moses told them: That Egyptian whom I killed rescued you. Therefore they told their father, “An Egyptian man”—meaning: What caused this man to come to us? The Egyptian man he killed.”

: ““Pharaoh commanded all his people”: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said: He decreed it against his own people too. Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina also said: He issued three decrees. First, “If it is a boy, kill him”; afterward, “Every newborn boy you shall throw into the Nile”; finally, he decreed it against his own people too.”

Commentary: Rashi on Exodus 1:22: ““All his people”: He decreed it against them too. On the day Moses was born, his astrologers told him: Today their deliverer has been born. We do not know whether he is Egyptian or Israelite, but we see that he will eventually suffer through water. Pharaoh therefore decreed that day against the Egyptians too: it says “every newborn boy,” without specifying “born to the Hebrews.” They did not know that he would ultimately suffer on account of the waters of Meribah.”
: ““She bore”—but she only raised him! This teaches that whoever raises an orphaned boy or girl in his home is credited by Scripture as though he had given birth to that child.”

: ““She brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter.” Pharaoh’s daughter kissed, embraced, and cherished him as though he were her son, never taking him out of the royal palace. Because he was beautiful, everyone wished to see him; whoever saw him could not tear himself away. Pharaoh would kiss and embrace him, while he took Pharaoh’s crown and placed it on his own head, just as he would do to him when grown. Likewise the Holy One, blessed be He, told Hiram, “I brought forth fire from within you…” So Pharaoh’s daughter raised the one who would eventually punish her father. Likewise the Messiah, who will eventually punish Edom, dwells with them in their country, as it says, “There a calf shall graze, and there it shall lie down…””

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”
: “They sent this message to Mar Ukva: “To the one whose radiance is like that of Bithiah’s son: peace.””

: ““The one whose radiance is like the son of Bithiah”—like Moses, who was Bithiah’s son: to the one whose face shines like Moses our teacher, whom Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, raised. Another reading is “like the member of His household,” meaning Moses, a member of God’s household, as it says, “He is faithful throughout My house.” “Whose radiance” refers to his wisdom, as it is written, “A person’s wisdom lights up his face.””

: ““The one whose radiance is like the son of Bithiah”—like Moses, who was Bithiah’s son: to the one whose face shines like Moses our teacher, whom Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, raised. Another reading is “like the member of His household,” meaning Moses, a member of God’s household, as it says, “He is faithful throughout My house.” “Whose radiance” refers to his wisdom, as it is written, “A person’s wisdom lights up his face.””

: ““Like scarlet”—shanim? Should it not say shani, in the singular? Rabbi Yitzhak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years, shanim, ordered in succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.”

: “He shall be exalted beyond Abraham, as it says, ‘I have raised my hand to the Lord’; lifted above Moses, as it says, ‘For You tell me: Carry them in your bosom’; and higher than the ministering angels, as it says, ‘Their heights were full of eyes.’”

: “‘I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.’ Rabbi Chiyya said: Jacob was the patriarchs’ glory, for he is the perfection of everything. Of the others it says ‘to Abraham,’ ‘to Isaac’; with him a letter is added, ‘and to Jacob.’ Vav is added to show that he is more complete than them all. Nevertheless, he did not merit employing it as Moses did.”

: “The Sages taught: Objects used for a commandment may be discarded; objects serving holiness must be stored away. Objects used for a commandment include a sukkah, a lulav, a shofar, and tzitzit. Objects serving holiness include cases for sacred books, tefillin, and mezuzot; a Torah-scroll case; a tefillin pouch; and their straps.”
: “'The clean animal': that which was destined to be clean for Israel. From this we learn that Noah studied Torah, as taught in Bereshit Rabbah 26.”

: ““The Jews had light, joy, gladness, and honor.” Rav Yehuda said: “Light” means Torah, as it says, “For a commandment is a lamp, and Torah is light.” “Joy” means a festival, as it says, “You shall rejoice on your festival.” “Gladness” means circumcision, as it says, “I rejoice over Your word.” “Honor” means tefillin, as it says, “All the peoples of the earth will see that the name of Hashem is proclaimed upon you, and they will fear you.” Rabbi Eliezer the Great teaches that this refers to the tefillin worn on the head.”

: “Rabbi Yose said: how beloved are Israel before God! At first He called them a holy nation, as it says, ‘For you are a holy people.’ Afterward He called them holiness itself: ‘Israel is holiness to the Lord, the first of His harvest.’ What distinguishes these? Rabbi Abba said: kodesh, ‘holiness,’ is higher than all. We learned that when all the holy ones unite, they are called kadosh, ‘holy.’ They all ascend and gather into that upper place called kodesh.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””
: ““Those who come shall cause Jacob to take root; Israel shall blossom and flower.” Rav Yosef taught: These are the Torah scholars of Babylonia, who make buds and flowers for the Torah.”

: “Rabbi Abba avoided Rav Yehudah because he wished to ascend to the Land of Israel. Rav Yehudah said that anyone who ascends from Babylonia to the Land of Israel transgresses a positive commandment, as it says, “They shall be brought to Babylon and remain there until the day I attend to them, says Hashem.””

: “Resh Lakish was bathing in the Jordan. Rabba bar bar Hana came and offered him his hand. He said to him, “By God, I hate you, for it is written, ‘If she is a wall, we will build upon her a silver turret; if she is a door, we will enclose her with a cedar board.’ Had you made yourselves like a wall and all ascended in Ezra’s days, you would have been compared to silver, which rot cannot affect. Now that you ascended like doors, you are compared to cedar, which rot can affect.” … Rav Pappa said: Insert another person between them: either it was Resh Lakish and Zeiri, or Rabba bar bar Hana and R. Elazar. When he came before R. Yohanan, he said to him: That is not the reason. Even had everyone ascended in Ezra’s days, the Divine Presence would not have rested in the Second Temple, as it says, “May God grant Japheth expansiveness and dwell in Shem’s tents.” Although “God grants Japheth expansiveness,” the Divine Presence rests only in Shem’s tents.”

quote: : “The Arizal wrote that Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. The Midrash accordingly says that matters not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva. This is the meaning of the Talmud’s account that Moses did not understand what they were saying. Rabbi Akiva descended from converts and attained the fiftieth gate, which is especially associated with the penitent.”

: “It is also written, ‘These things I have done, and I have not forsaken them.’ It does not say, ‘I shall do,’ but ‘I have done’: I have already done this for Rabbi Akiva and his companions. Things that were not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his companions. ‘His eye has seen every precious thing’ refers to Rabbi Akiva and his companions.”

: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and attaching crowns to the letters. Moses asked: “Master of the world, what holds You back?” He answered: “After many generations there will be a man named Akiva son of Yosef, who will derive heaps upon heaps of laws from every tiny stroke.” Moses said: “Master of the world, show him to me.” He answered: “Turn around.” Moses went and sat at the back of eight rows, but did not understand what they were saying, and his strength failed him. When they reached one matter, his students asked him: “Rabbi, how do you know this?” He answered: “It is a law given to Moses at Sinai.” Moses’ mind was put at ease. He returned before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: “Master of the world, You have such a man, yet You give the Torah through me?” He answered: “Be silent; this is what arose in My thought.””

: “Happy are the masters of repentance! In one hour, one day, one instant, they draw close to God in a way that even the completely righteous, who approached Him over many years, did not. Abraham did not enter those upper days until he was old, as stated. Likewise David: ‘King David was old, advanced in days.’ The master of repentance, however, immediately enters and cleaves to God. Rabbi Yose said: we learned that in that world, the wholly righteous are not permitted to stand where masters of repentance stand. For they are closer to the King than anyone, drawing Him toward themselves with a greater desire of the heart and with great force to draw near to the King.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: All the prophets’ prophecies concern penitents; as for the completely righteous, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu, who said: In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near”—first the far, then the near. Rabbi Yochanan would explain: “Far” means one who was far from transgression from the outset; “near” means one who was once close to transgression but has now distanced himself from it.”

: “We learned: Torah gives a person 613 kinds of counsel for becoming complete with his Master, because his Master wishes to benefit him in this world and the world to come—especially the world to come. Everything through which God perfects a person is perfected through the good he merits in the world to come. Why? Because the world to come belongs to God.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””

: “This is the Oral Torah, which is difficult to learn and involves great hardship; it is therefore likened to darkness, as it says, ‘The people walking in darkness saw a great light.’ These are the masters of Talmud who saw a great light, for the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes in questions of prohibition and permission, impurity and purity.”

: “One verse says, “His throne was flames of fire,” while another says, “Until thrones were set, and the Ancient of Days sat.” There is no contradiction: one is for Him and one for David. A baraita teaches this as Rabbi Akiva’s view. Rabbi Yose the Galilean told him: “Akiva, how long will you make the Divine Presence ordinary? Rather, one throne is for judgment and the other for righteousness.” Did Rabbi Akiva accept this? Come and hear: “One is for judgment and the other for righteousness”—Rabbi Akiva’s view. Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah told him: “Akiva, what business have you with aggadah? Turn your discourse to the laws of skin lesions and tent impurity. Rather, one is a throne and the other a stool: the throne for sitting, the stool for His feet, as it says, ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth My footstool.’””

: “For this reason too, Rabbi Akiva was told, “Turn your words toward Negaim and Ohalot.” He was the root of the Oral Torah, and his great spiritual comprehension anticipated the future, as the Midrash says: Matters not revealed to Moses were revealed to Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: From here you learn that whoever suspects another of something he has not done is stricken in his body.”

He wished to return the world to chaos because of Zedekiah’s generation; when He considered Zedekiah, He was appeased. Rather, the discussion concerns forcefulness and gentleness.”

: “Another interpretation: Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: “A locked garden”—because Israel in Egypt guarded themselves against sexual immorality, they were redeemed from Egypt. Consequently, “Your shoots”—your sending forth, as it says, “It happened when Pharaoh sent out…” Rabbi Huna said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Our mother Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; Israel guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: Restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient for Israel to be redeemed through it.”
: “We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.”
: “Moses heard the people weeping by their families, each at the entrance of his tent. Hashem’s anger burned greatly, and Moses was displeased.”

: ““We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt.” Rav and Samuel differed: one said this means fish, and the other said forbidden sexual relations. The one who says fish relies on “we ate”; the one who says forbidden sexual relations relies on “freely.” But according to the opinion that it means forbidden sexual relations, does it not say “we ate”? Scripture uses a refined expression, as it says, “She ate, wiped her mouth, and said, I have done no wrong.” According to the opinion that it means fish, what does “freely” mean? They brought them from ownerless sources, for the Master said: When Israel drew water, the Holy One, blessed be He, provided small fish for them in their pitchers. According to the opinion that it means fish, but they were not promiscuous regarding forbidden sexual relations, the verse “A locked garden is my sister, my bride” is understandable. But according to the other opinion, what does “a sealed spring” mean? Regarding the relations already forbidden to them, they were not promiscuous. According to the opinion that it means forbidden sexual relations, “Moses heard the people weeping by their families” is understandable: they wept concerning family relationships with whom intercourse had become forbidden. But according to the opinion that it means fish, what does “weeping by their families” mean? Both matters were present.”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: During all the years that Adam was under ban, he fathered spirits, demons, and night-demons, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image.” This implies that before then he did not father beings in his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say: Adam was a great pious man. When he saw that death had been decreed through him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and placed a girdle of fig leaves upon his body for one hundred and thirty years. The earlier statement concerns semen that he emitted involuntarily.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Acha said in Rabbi Chanin’s name: What does “a nation from within a nation” mean? Like someone who pulls a fetus from an animal’s womb, so the Holy One, blessed be He, brought Israel out of Egypt, as it says, “a nation from within a nation”—like the expression, “the innards and the legs.” We have learned the pain of the one being pulled out. How do we know the pain of the one pulling? It says, “He brought you out of the iron furnace”: like someone taking gold from a furnace without tongs or cloths. So, as it were, was Israel’s case.”

Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “If you ask, ‘Why did He create the evil inclination, of which it says, “The inclination of the human heart is evil from youth”?’—you call it evil; who can make it good? The Holy One, blessed be He, says: ‘You make it evil. How so? A child of five, six, seven, eight, or nine does not sin. From ten onward, he begins to cultivate the evil inclination.’ If you say, ‘A person cannot guard himself,’ the Holy One replies: ‘You made it evil. You were a child and did not sin; you grew up and sinned. There are many things in the world harsher and more bitter than the evil inclination, yet you sweeten them. Nothing is more bitter than the lupin bean, yet you labor to boil and sweeten it in water seven times until it becomes sweet; so too mustard, capers, and many other things. If you sweeten for your own needs the bitter things I created, how much more can you sweeten the evil inclination, which is entrusted to your control!’”

What is “I have surely remembered”? “Remembering”—in Egypt; “I have remembered”—at the sea. “Remembering”—for the future; “I have remembered”—for the past. “And what is being done to you in Egypt”: I shall call the Egyptians to account for what they do to you, as in, “I have remembered what Amalek did to you.” “I said: I shall bring you up”—tell them: As I told their father Jacob, so I shall do. What did He tell him? “I shall surely bring you up.” Jacob likewise told his sons, “God shall be with you and bring you back…” Immediately, “They shall listen to your voice.” Why? They possess a tradition of redemption: any redeemer who comes announcing remembrance in its doubled expression is a true redeemer.”

Will this person be strong or weak, wise or foolish, rich or poor?” But he does not ask whether the person will be wicked or righteous. This accords with Rabbi Chanina’s statement: Everything is in Heaven’s hands except the fear of Heaven, as it says, “Now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you other than to fear Him,” and so forth.”

: “Has any god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from within another nation—with trials, signs, wonders, warfare, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors—like everything Hashem your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?”

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

: “These three shells stand opposite the three patriarchs in holiness. Abraham our father brings all loves into holiness; Isaac brings the powers of severity into holiness. One stands opposite the other: the right of one faces the other’s left, so jealousy precedes desire. Honor stands opposite Jacob the small, as in 'I am small' and 'Who will raise Jacob, for he is small?' These correspond to the three elements, alef-mem-shin. Haughtiness comes from the element of elevated spirit; these are wicked Balaam’s three qualities, wishing to rise higher and higher like fire’s nature. In holiness, however, the spirit is lowly. Through this one is also saved from desire.”

Egypt’s magicians had said: You have no cure unless we slaughter a hundred and fifty of Israel’s children in the evening and a hundred and fifty in the morning, and you bathe in their blood twice daily. When Israel heard this harsh decree, they began groaning and lamenting.”

: “Who are the fish? The messengers in the world, appointed to fulfill their Master’s will, appointed through a spirit of wisdom. Therefore we learned that some waters produce sages, and some waters produce fools, according to the rivers branching in every direction.”

: “Rabbi Ba said in Rav Kahana’s name: how did the prophets obtain any of those drops? We learned: with every drop that proceeds from Eden, a spirit of wisdom comes forth. Hence the teaching determines: some waters produce sages, while other waters produce fools. The waters that produce sages come from the drops of Eden.”

: “What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”
