quote: : “Everyone thus receives an additional nefesh, ruach and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person should direct his intention so that some of this addition remains with him through the weekdays; if he does so properly, his ways will be set right. He is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends on the intention.”

: “'On the donkey': the particular donkey—the donkey Abraham saddled for the binding of Isaac, and the one upon which the King Messiah will be revealed, as it says, 'Humble and riding on a donkey,' as taught in Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer 31. 'He returned to the land of Egypt; Moses took the staff': Scripture does not always arrange events in strict chronological order.”

: “Abraham rose early in the morning, took Ishmael, Eliezer, and his son Isaac with him, and saddled the donkey. This was the donkey Abraham rode, the offspring of the she-donkey created at twilight, as it says, “Abraham rose early in the morning.” This was the donkey Moses rode when coming to Egypt, as it says, “Moses took his wife and his sons and mounted them on the donkey.” This is the donkey upon which the son of David will ride, as it says, “Humble, and riding on a donkey.””

: “Rav said: Everyone agrees that a slave has no recognized lineage, as it says, “Stay here with the donkey”—a people comparable to a donkey. An objection was raised: “Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty slaves”! Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov replied: This is like the expression “a bull, son of cattle.””

Parallel: Maharal of Prague, Gevurot Hashem 29:8: “That is why they rode the donkey created at twilight: their riding was upon a creature of twilight, and twilight creation stands above nature. What was created during the six days of Creation belongs wholly to nature, since these are weekdays. Twilight, however, is partly weekday and partly holy, so things were created then that do not belong wholly to nature. Although this donkey is natural like any other donkey, these righteous people rise above the world. The order of creation belonging to twilight therefore required this donkey for them: they rode upon things created at twilight, and their donkey accordingly came from that order. Just as the creation of the six days provides for ordinary riding, the order of twilight provides for this special riding by which they rose above the world. This donkey was appointed for them within that twilight order; it was not because the animal itself possessed any special importance, as explained. This is the essential point.”

: “What does it say of Abraham? “Abraham rose early in the morning and took his two lads with him.” Who were they? Ishmael and Eliezer. What does it say of Saul? “He went, and two men with him.” Who were they? Abner and Amasa.”

: “'His two young men': Ishmael and Eliezer. An important person may not travel without two companions, as taught in Bereshit Rabbah, so that if one needs to relieve himself and goes some distance away, the second will remain with him.”

: “If you ask why it says, “Moses went”—where did he go? He went to take his wife and sons. Jethro asked: Where are you taking them? He replied: To Egypt. Jethro said: Those in Egypt seek to leave, and you are taking them there! He replied: Tomorrow they will leave and stand at Mount Sinai to hear from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, “I am the Lord your God.” Shall my children not hear as they do? Immediately, “Jethro said to Moses: Go in peace.” He told him: Go in peace, enter in peace, and return in peace.”

: “R. Judah expounded: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it before the righteous and the wicked. To the righteous it appears like a high mountain, and to the wicked like a strand of hair. Both groups weep. The righteous weep and say, “How were we able to conquer such a high mountain?” The wicked weep and say, “How were we unable to conquer this strand of hair?” The Holy One, blessed be He, also marvels with them, as it says, “Thus says Hashem of Hosts: Though it is wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it will also be wondrous in My eyes.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 3:1: “What principally remains in the future is desire for Torah, the purpose for which Hashem created it. The Talmud accordingly concludes: a person should apply himself to Torah “like an ox to a yoke and a donkey to a burden.” The Zohar says: “They brought about Issachar’s coming into the world because the fragrance of Torah rose before the Holy One—as it says, ‘The mandrakes…’” It likewise says: “The mandrakes are those that Reuben found; new Torah teachings arose in Israel only through him,” as in “The descendants of Issachar,” and so forth. This is the donkey in holiness.”

: “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Yose’s name: The Holy One, blessed be He, never withdrew any favorable utterance He issued, even if it was conditional. How do we know? From Moses, to whom He said, “Leave Me, and I will destroy them, and make you a mighty nation.” Although Moses prayed for mercy and the threatened destruction was canceled, God nevertheless fulfilled the promise through Moses’ descendants: “The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer; the son of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief; and the children of Rehabiah multiplied exceedingly.” Rav Yosef taught: “Exceedingly” means beyond six hundred thousand. This is derived by comparing “multiplication” here with “multiplication” there: here, “They multiplied exceedingly”; there, “The children of Israel were fruitful, swarmed, and multiplied.””

: “When the Omnipresent told Moses, “Go and bring My people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt,” as it says, “Now come, and I shall send you to Pharaoh,” he came and took his wife and two sons, as it says, “Moses took his wife and his sons, mounted them on the donkey, and returned toward the land of Egypt.” At that time Aaron was told, “Go to meet Moses in the wilderness”; “He went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.” He went to meet Moses, embraced him, and kissed him. He asked: My brother Moses, where have you been all these years? He replied: In Midian. He asked: Who are these women and children with you? He replied: My wife and sons. He asked: Where are you taking them? He replied: To Egypt. He said: We grieve over those already there, and now you have brought these others upon us! At that moment Moses told her: Go to your father’s house. She went to her father’s house, taking her two sons with her. Therefore it says, “After he had sent her away.””

: “'After she had been sent away': when the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses in Midian, 'Go, return to Egypt,' Moses took his wife and sons. Aaron went out to meet him and encountered him at the mountain of God. He asked, 'Who are these?' Moses replied, 'This is my wife, whom I married in Midian, and these are my sons.' Aaron asked, 'Where are you taking them?' He answered, 'To Egypt.' Aaron said, 'We are distressed over those already there, and you come to add to them!' Moses told her, 'Go to your father’s house.' She took her two sons and departed, as taught in Mekhilta.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah taught: while the upper King’s engravings are properly arranged in their places, every world rejoices and every work stands firmly in its existence. Thus ‘The Lord’s work, for it is awesome.’ What is awesome? Rabbi Eleazar said: the perfection of everything, as in ‘the great, mighty and awesome God.’ Who is awesome? Jacob: ‘Jacob was a tam man,’ rendered ‘a complete man’—complete in everything. Likewise all God’s works are fully perfected and completely established.”

: “Testimony to creation: all creation consists of words known through understanding and stands within a reckoning. The Elohim of creation points above and points below: above, in the mystery of the world to come; below, in the mystery of the Congregation of Israel.”
: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Behibare’am, ‘when they were created,’ may be read be’Avraham, ‘through Abraham’: they were created in Abraham’s merit.”

: “‘For the Lord God had not sent rain upon the earth’: Scripture uses the complete divine name over a complete world. Rabbi Chalfai said: Just as it uses the complete divine name over a complete world, so it uses the complete divine name when rain falls.”

: “We have learned: when is it called the complete Name? When ‘the Lord God’ is written. This is the complete Name of the Ancient of all and of Zeir Anpin; together it is called the complete Name. The other forms are not called the complete Name. As we explained, ‘The Lord God planted’ is the complete Name in the planting of the garden. Wherever ‘the Lord God’ appears, it is called the complete Name. ‘The Lord, the Lord’ includes everything; at that time compassion is awakened throughout all.”

: “Five things are one sixtieth of something greater: fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. Fire is one sixtieth of Gehinnom; honey, one sixtieth of manna; Shabbat, one sixtieth of the World to Come; sleep, one sixtieth of death; and a dream, one sixtieth of prophecy.”

: ““Then Moses sang.” This is what Scripture says: “Your throne was established from then.” Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Abbahu’s name: Although You have existed forever, Your throne was not settled, and You were not known in Your world, until Your children sang. Therefore it says, “Your throne was established from then.” It is like a king who fought a war and won, and they made him Augustus. They told him: Before this war you were king; now we have made you Augustus. What honor distinguishes a king from Augustus? The king stands upon the platform, whereas Augustus sits. So Israel said: Truly, before You created Your world, You existed; since creating it, You remain the same. Yet, as it were, You stood, as it says, “He stood and measured the earth.” But when You stood at the sea and we sang before You with “then,” Your kingship became settled and Your throne established. Thus, “Your throne was established from then”—through “Then Moses sang.””

: “Since He is unified above through six directions, she too is unified below through six other directions, so that there is One above and One below, as in ‘The Lord shall be One and His Name One.’ One above, in six directions: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One’—six words corresponding to six directions. One below, in six directions: ‘Blessed is the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever’—six other directions in six words. The Lord is One above, and His Name One below.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; all the males guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient merit for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” followed by “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed. For it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Sabbaths,” and afterward, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.””
: “I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El Shaddai, but by My name Hashem I did not make Myself known to them.”

: “'I also established My covenant': when I appeared to them as El Shaddai, I likewise set up and established My covenant between Me and them. 'To give them the land of Canaan': to Abraham, in the passage concerning circumcision, it was said, 'I am El Shaddai...I will give you and your descendants after you the land of your sojourning.' To Isaac: 'For to you and your descendants I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath I swore to Abraham.' That same oath that I swore to Abraham as El Shaddai I repeated to Jacob: 'I am El Shaddai; be fruitful and multiply...the land which...' Thus, I promised them but had not fulfilled it.”
: “Hashem was standing over him and said, “I am Hashem, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. The land upon which you lie I will give to you and your descendants.””

: “'I also established My covenant': when I appeared to them as El Shaddai, I likewise set up and established My covenant between Me and them. 'To give them the land of Canaan': to Abraham, in the passage concerning circumcision, it was said, 'I am El Shaddai...I will give you and your descendants after you the land of your sojourning.' To Isaac: 'For to you and your descendants I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath I swore to Abraham.' That same oath that I swore to Abraham as El Shaddai I repeated to Jacob: 'I am El Shaddai; be fruitful and multiply...the land which...' Thus, I promised them but had not fulfilled it.”

: “Rav Yehudah said: Where does the Torah require the blessing after a meal? “You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.” Where does the Torah require a blessing before Torah study? “When I proclaim Hashem’s name, ascribe greatness to our God.””

: “‘He meditates upon His Torah.’ Rabbi Shimon said: Abraham’s father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys to be like two teachers; they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written, ‘I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.’”

: “The ninth is Shaddai—another reading has El Shaddai—who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ Enough means sufficiency, and sufficiency comes to the world only from the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ The tenth is Adonai, for the kingdom’s law is certainly law. This wages the King’s battles in the world; it is lower Might, Tzedek.”

: “‘After my skin has been cut away, from my flesh I shall behold God.’ Abraham said: ‘After I circumcised myself, many converts came to join this covenant. “From my flesh I shall behold God”: had I not done this, how would the Holy One, blessed be He, have appeared to me?’ Thus, ‘The Lord appeared to him.’”

: “Rabbi Yudan said in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: I would have thought that Reuben and Simeon had already been born, and Benjamin had already issued from Jacob’s loins, though he was still in his mother’s womb. But I reconsidered: ‘A nation’ refers to Benjamin, and ‘an assembly of nations’ refers to Manasseh and Ephraim, as it says, ‘His descendants shall become a multitude of nations.’”

: “Rabbi Chelbo asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, “When Rachel had given birth to Joseph”—why did Joseph’s birth make the difference? He answered: Our father Jacob saw that Esau’s descendants could be delivered only into the hands of Joseph’s descendants, as it says, “The house of Jacob shall be fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble.” He objected: “David struck them from twilight until the evening of the following day.” He answered: The person who taught you Prophets did not teach you Writings, where it says, “When he went to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Yozavad, Yediael, Michael, Yozavad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of the thousands belonging to Manasseh.” Rav Yosef objected: “Five hundred men from the children of Simeon went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Yishi; they struck the remnant of Amalek that had escaped and lived there to this day.” Rabbah bar Shila answered: Yishi descended from Manasseh, as it is written, “The sons of Manasseh: Chepher and Yishi.””

: “What did the house of Amalek do? They cut off the circumcised organs of the Israelites and threw them upward, saying, ‘Is this what You chose? Take what You chose!’ Thus it is written, ‘Their reproach, with which they have reproached You, Lord.’”

: “Therefore Joseph and Benjamin are two righteous ones. Joseph merited being the Righteous One above because he guarded the covenant’s sign. Benjamin is the righteous one below, so that the sabbatical realm is crowned between two righteous ones: Joseph the Righteous and Benjamin the Righteous.”

: “According to the way of truth, the verse is understood in its plain meaning. It says: I, the Lord, appeared to them through the speculum of El Shaddai, like 'In a vision I make Myself known to him.' But as for Myself, the Lord, I was not made known to them: they did not gaze through the luminous speculum to know Me, like 'Whom the Lord knew face to face.' The patriarchs knew the unique Name, but it was not made known to them through prophecy. Therefore, when Abraham speaks with God, he mentions the unique Name together with alef-dalet, or alef-dalet alone.”

: “‘According to the pace of the work’: what work? The mirror that does not shine, through which the world’s work is performed. ‘Which is before me’: this is ‘from before the Lord’ wherever it occurs. ‘According to the pace of the children’ is the mystery of the cherubim, demonstrating faith’s mystery, to which he cleaves.”

: “Rabbi Shimon was sitting with his son Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba. Rabbi Eleazar asked: why does the verse say, ‘I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob’? It should say, ‘I spoke.’ He answered: ‘Eleazar, my son, this is a supernal secret. There are colors that can be seen, and colors that cannot. Both are faith’s upper mystery, unknown and unexamined by people. No one attained those visible colors until the patriarchs came and stood upon them. Therefore “I appeared” is written: they saw the colors that are revealed.’”

: “Through what merit does Israel sing? Through the merit of Abraham, who believed in the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “He believed in the Lord.” This is the faith Israel inherits. Concerning it Scripture says, “The righteous person shall live through his faith.” Thus: “You shall sing from the summit of Amanah.””

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”

: “Certainly ‘Her husband is known in the gates’ refers to God, who becomes known and cleaved to according to what each person measures within his heart, insofar as he can cleave through a spirit of wisdom. According to what he measures in his heart, so He becomes known in his heart. Therefore ‘known in the gates’—through those measures. But no one can grasp and know Him as He truly is.”
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Alas for those who are lost and cannot be found! Many times I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El Shaddai, yet they did not question My ways or ask Me, “What is Your name?” I told Abraham, “Arise, walk through the land’s length and breadth, for I will give it to you.” He sought a place to bury Sarah and found none until he purchased one for four hundred silver shekels, yet he did not question My ways. I told Isaac, “Dwell in this land, and I will be with you and bless you.” His servants sought drinking water and found none until a dispute arose, as it says, “The shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s shepherds, saying: The water is ours.” Yet he did not question My ways. I told Jacob, “The land upon which you lie I will give you.” He sought a place to pitch his tent and found none until he purchased one for a hundred kesitah, yet he did not question My ways. They did not ask Me, “What is Your name?” But you asked Me, “What is Your name?” at the outset, and now you say to Me, “You have not rescued Your people.” “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh”: you will see the war with Pharaoh, but you will not see the war with the thirty-one kings.”

: “This Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, is neither mentioned nor found. Being the head above all the highest, He is mentioned only as a single head without a body, sustaining everything.”

: ““I shall be what I shall be.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: “Go and tell Israel: I was with you in this enslavement, and I shall be with you in enslavement under other kingdoms.” Moses said before Him: “Master of the world, the trouble of its own time is enough.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: “Go and tell them: ‘I shall be’ has sent me to you.””
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Creation’s purpose was to reveal the glory of His kingship in the world. When the wicked prosper and the righteous do not, His glory’s revelation is concealed. God showed Moses and told him, 'You shall see My back.' I heard from my holy teacher concerning the Targum, 'You shall see what is after Me, but what is before Me shall not be seen,' that its meaning is: after an action became manifest, Moses immediately recognized its depth and the good within it. Before the action became manifest, however, its depth could not be grasped, for His thoughts are exceedingly deep, beyond apprehension.”

: “Then comes 'I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring out My people': you will be able to bestow complete faith upon all Israel. This follows 'Anyone possessing fear of Heaven has his words heard.' We already explained that fear of Heaven is called heart, as 'He has no heart' is expounded concerning someone lacking fear of Heaven. 'Understanding is the heart' means that fear enters the depth of the heart’s inner point. One who becomes a vehicle for kingship—which is fear—has his words heard because they emerge from the heart. One who merits the aspect 'Understanding is the heart' has his words heard still more. His words are like God’s words: 'So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; it shall not return to Me empty, but accomplish...and succeed in what I sent it for.'”

: “‘By My Name the Lord I was not known to them’: these are the concealed, shining upper colors that Moses merited contemplating. This is the secret of the eye closed and open: closed, it sees through the shining mirror; open, through the mirror that does not shine. Hence ‘I appeared’ concerns the nonshining mirror, which is revealed and described through seeing. The shining mirror, which is concealed, is described through knowing: ‘I was not known.’ Rabbi Eleazar and Rabbi Abba came and kissed his hands. Rabbi Abba wept: ‘Woe, when you depart the world and leave it orphaned! Who will illuminate the Torah’s words?’”

: “‘As El Shaddai’: I appeared to them through the mirror that does not shine, not through the shining mirror. If you say they employed only the feminine aspect and nothing more—come and see: they are never separated. Thus ‘I also established My covenant with them,’ for the covenant was joined with her.”

: “The verse 'Her husband is known at the gates' uses the language of knowledge. The Zohar explains: her husband is the Holy One, blessed be He, who becomes known and attached according to what each person measures in his heart. Through faith, one can apprehend the name Havayah, each according to the measure of his heart. This is through the nonluminous speculum, the name Adonai, and is therefore termed seeing. Through complete faith, the patriarchs recognized all the attributes included in Havayah. Moses our teacher, however, merited the luminous speculum: he was the inward aspect of Jacob and brought all Torah down to earth. This is the secret of knowledge.”

: “Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi raised this contradiction: It is written, “I am with you and will guard you wherever you go,” yet it is also written, “Jacob was greatly afraid.” He feared that sin might change the outcome.”
: “'God spoke to Moses': He spoke judgment with him because Moses had spoken harshly, saying, 'Why have You harmed this people?'”

: “Rabbi Yehudah HaLevi bar Shalom said: They told Moses, ‘Let us state a parable of what we are like. A wolf came to seize a lamb from the flock. The shepherd ran after it to rescue the lamb from the wolf’s mouth, but between the shepherd and the wolf the lamb was torn apart. So,’ Israel told Moses, ‘between you and Pharaoh we are dying.’ Thus, ‘Moses returned to the Lord.’ If You ask, ‘Why is this your concern?’—‘Why, then, did You send me?’ ‘Since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name’: Your name brings life and healing to all in the world, yet through Your name this people has suffered harm! What will become of those immured within the brickwork? God told him: ‘Now you shall see.’”

: “The world to come is a palace for that upper point. When she stands and carries the patriarchs upon her wings to be crowned above, everything is called Shabbat. When the patriarchs are crowned above within the upper point, it is called Shabbat. When the lower point is crowned with the patriarchs, she is called Shabbat.”
: “I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El Shaddai, but by My name Hashem I did not make Myself known to them.”

: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: When the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, it continued to expand like two balls of warp thread unwinding, until He rebuked it and brought it to a standstill, as it says, “The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke.” This is Reish Lakish’s teaching: What does “I am God Shaddai” mean? I am the One who told the world, “Enough.””

: “Rabbi Yohanan said: Had Torah not been given, we would have learned modesty from the cat, avoidance of robbery from the ant, sexual fidelity from the dove, and proper marital conduct from the rooster, which first appeases its mate and afterward mates.”

: “Another interpretation: Amon means ‘craftsman.’ The Torah says: I was the instrument of the Holy One’s craftsmanship. Ordinarily, when a human king builds a palace, he does not build it according to his own understanding, but according to an architect’s understanding. The architect, too, does not proceed solely from his own understanding: he has plans and notebooks showing how to make rooms and doorways. So the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world. The Torah says, ‘In the beginning God created.’ ‘Beginning’ means Torah, as it says, ‘The Lord acquired me at the beginning of His way.’”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”
: “'Wisdom': what a person hears from others and learns. 'Understanding': discerning something in one’s own heart from things one has learned. 'Knowledge': the holy spirit.”

: ““A man of exactions ruins it”—this is the generation of the Flood, who did not practice justice. See what is written concerning them: “They drive away the orphans’ donkey; they turn the needy away from the road.” Rabbi Acha said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give them four things: Torah, suffering, sacrificial service, and prayer. They did not want them, as it says, “They said to God: Depart from us”—this means suffering. “We do not desire knowledge of Your ways”—this means Torah. “What is Shaddai, that we should serve Him?”—these are the sacrifices. “What would we gain by entreating Him?”—this is prayer. The Holy One, blessed be He, told them: What caused you to perish from the evening of this world and the morning of the world to come? Your refusal to accept Torah, which contains justice, as it says, “From morning to evening they are crushed.” Why? “Without anyone taking notice, they perish forever.” “Taking notice” signifies judgments, as it says, “These are the judgments that you shall place before them.””

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Alas for those who are lost and cannot be found! Many times I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El Shaddai, yet they did not question My ways or ask Me, “What is Your name?” I told Abraham, “Arise, walk through the land’s length and breadth, for I will give it to you.” He sought a place to bury Sarah and found none until he purchased one for four hundred silver shekels, yet he did not question My ways. I told Isaac, “Dwell in this land, and I will be with you and bless you.” His servants sought drinking water and found none until a dispute arose, as it says, “The shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s shepherds, saying: The water is ours.” Yet he did not question My ways. I told Jacob, “The land upon which you lie I will give you.” He sought a place to pitch his tent and found none until he purchased one for a hundred kesitah, yet he did not question My ways. They did not ask Me, “What is Your name?” But you asked Me, “What is Your name?” at the outset, and now you say to Me, “You have not rescued Your people.” “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh”: you will see the war with Pharaoh, but you will not see the war with the thirty-one kings.”

: “Rabbi Acha said: Abraham began to wonder: ‘These instructions are astonishing. Yesterday You said, “Through Isaac your descendants shall be called”; then You said, “Take your son”; now You tell me, “Do not stretch out your hand against the lad”!’ The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: ‘Abraham, “I shall not violate My covenant or change what has issued from My lips.” When I told you to take your son, I did not say, “Slaughter him,” but “Bring him up.” I said it as an expression of affection. You have brought him up and fulfilled My word; now bring him down.’”

: “‘God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.’ It is written, ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches, and He adds no sorrow with it.’ ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches’ refers to Shabbat, as it says, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ‘He adds no sorrow with it’ refers to mourning, as in the verse, ‘The king was grieved over his son.’”
: “Hashem’s blessing brings wealth, and He adds no sorrow with it.”

: “Similarly, Scripture says, “A poor man and a man of intrigues meet; the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” When a student approaches his teacher and says, “Teach me Torah,” if he teaches him, “the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” If not, “Rich and poor meet; the Lord makes them all”: the One who made this one wise makes him foolish, and the foolish one He makes wise. This is Rabbi Natan’s teaching.”

: “He told them: ‘I am speaking of those rich in Torah, not those rich in money. How so? A person became great and rich in Torah, taught many students, spread Torah publicly, and was filled with Torah. Although he dies, the students he established do not allow him to sleep: they sit and study Torah, Talmud, laws, and aggadot. His students repeat laws and teachings in his name, mention his name continually, and do not allow him to sleep in the grave.’”
: “All toil brings some gain, but mere words from the lips lead only to want.”

: ““The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and commanded them concerning the children of Israel.” This is what Scripture says: “In every toil there is gain, but mere talk brings only loss.” In all matters in which a person occupies himself with Torah, he receives reward. Could idle speech be the same? Scripture says, “Mere talk brings only loss.” You find that Joseph should have spent only ten years in prison because he spoke ill of his ten brothers. But because he told the chief cupbearer, “Remember me with you, and mention me to Pharaoh,” two more years were added, as it says, “At the end of two years.””

: “R. Isaac said: What is meant by “To the wicked God says: What right have you to recount My statutes?” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Doeg the wicked: What right have you to recount My statutes? When you reach the passage about murderers and the passage about slanderers, how do you expound them? “You carry My covenant upon your mouth.” R. Ami said: Doeg’s Torah goes no deeper than his lips.”

: “Rava contrasted two verses: It is written, “Your kindness is great up to the heavens,” and it is written, “Your kindness is great above the heavens.” How can both be true? One concerns those who act for its own sake, the other those who act without doing so for its own sake. This accords with Rav Judah, who said in Rav’s name: A person should always engage in Torah and commandments even without doing so for its own sake, for from doing so without that intention he comes to doing so for its own sake.”
: “Rabbi Chelbo said in Rav Huna’s name: The words of anyone who possesses fear of Heaven are heeded, as it says, “The conclusion of the matter: everything is heard—fear God.””

: “R. Samuel bar Nahmani said in R. Yonatan’s name: What is meant by “Why is there money in a fool’s hand to acquire wisdom when he has no heart”? Woe to those Torah scholars who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven.”

: “Rabbi Zeira said in Rav’s name: What does “All the poor man’s days are bad” mean? It refers to one occupied with Talmud. “But the cheerful heart has a constant feast” refers to one occupied with Mishnah. Rava says the reverse. This accords with Rav Mesharshiya’s statement in Rava’s name: What does “One who moves stones is hurt by them; one who splits wood benefits through them” mean? “One who moves stones is hurt by them” refers to those occupied with Mishnah; “one who splits wood benefits through them” refers to those occupied with Talmud.”
Commentary: Rashbam on Bava Batra 145b:10:4: ““Yiskan” expresses warmth, as in “She became a warming attendant for the king”; that is, he derives benefit from them.”

There the proof is drawn from Moses, whose prophecy never ceased; this is the meaning of “rests His Presence.” Although wealth is also proved from Jonah, Jonah too was a prophet without interruption, even though he was sent only to Nineveh.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 1:1: “The Oral Torah likewise divides into these three levels. First is what is called a law given to Moses at Sinai. Second are laws resembling prophecy, without an explicitly stated reason, as Hillel said: “Leave Israel alone; if they are not prophets, they are prophets’ children.” Third is the Oral Torah that comes through the holy spirit, corresponding to the Writings.”
: “Moses spoke before Hashem, saying, “The Israelites have not listened to me. How, then, will Pharaoh listen to me, when my lips are uncircumcised?””

: ““Go down.” He said: Master of the universe, yesterday You told me, “You shall ascend, and Aaron with you,” and, “To Moses He said: Ascend to the Lord.” Yet here You say, “Go down”! He replied: You ascend here for My children’s honor, not your own. I told their ancestor, “Behold, angels of God were ascending and descending upon it.” What does “upon it” mean? I told him: When your children are righteous, they rise and are exalted in the world, and their emissaries rise with them. When they descend, they and their emissaries descend. “Go down”—why? “For your people have corrupted themselves.” He told him: Since they sinned, you and they descend.”
: “He dreamed: a ladder was set upon the earth, its top reaching heaven, and God’s angels were ascending and descending upon it.”

: “Moses said to Hashem, “Please, my Lord, I am not a man of words—not yesterday, not the day before, nor since You began speaking to Your servant—for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue.” Hashem said to him, “Who gave a person a mouth? Who makes one mute or deaf, sighted or blind? Is it not I, Hashem? Now go. I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say.””

: “The evil inclination is a foreign power resulting from the presence of the shells in the world, entering Israel’s heart somewhat. It stands in the foolish heart and entices one away from serving God, although it has no inherent connection to Israel. It resembles the foreskin covering the sign of the covenant: something foreign. The uncircumcision of the mouth is similar. Moses said, 'I am of uncircumcised lips,' although anyone possessing fear of Heaven has his words heard. Why, then, did Israel not listen? His explanation was 'I am of uncircumcised lips': as though an alien obstruction rested upon his lips, preventing his speech from accomplishing its effect. Otherwise, his words would certainly have been heard.”
: “So shall be My word that goes out from My mouth: it will not return to Me empty, but will accomplish what I desire and succeed in the task for which I sent it.”
: “So shall be My word that goes out from My mouth: it will not return to Me empty, but will accomplish what I desire and succeed in the task for which I sent it.”
: “Moses spoke before Hashem, saying, “The Israelites have not listened to me. How, then, will Pharaoh listen to me, when my lips are uncircumcised?””

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “Rather, this is a secret: Moses is Voice, while Speech, his word, was in exile. He was therefore blocked from articulating words. Hence he said, ‘How will Pharaoh hear me while my word is in his exile? I have no word. I am Voice, lacking Speech, for she is in exile.’ Therefore God joined Aaron with him.”

ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:2
quote: Parallel: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 11:2: “Moses possessed this power: all his speech disclosed the essence of his vitality, for he embodies knowledge, joining wisdom and understanding, father and mother. This reveals the covenant of the tongue. He is therefore called the Matron’s husband: kingship is the mouth, and he has the power to impart influence to the mouth. He said “This is the word,” because his speech was literally Hashem’s word, the Divine Presence speaking from his throat. He spoke from his essential vitality—the letters of his soul. As his words took shape, so were the letters of his soul combined at that moment. All his soul’s vitality was gathered into his speech as he spoke with his whole power, so the letters of his soul actually formed that combination. This is the Written Torah, called “Moses’ Torah”: it became his Torah, the very combination of letters at the source of his soul’s vitality, because his words disclosed his vitality. “This is the word” is like pointing with a finger: whoever saw him speaking saw the actual word Hashem had spoken. The root vitality of every creature is literally Hashem’s word, for He creates and gives creatures life. Moses’ speech disclosed that divine speech: Hashem spoke those words, meaning that the vitality Hashem gave him was itself those very words while he spoke.”
: “So shall be My word that goes out from My mouth: it will not return to Me empty, but will accomplish what I desire and succeed in the task for which I sent it.”
: “A man of God came to Eli and said to him, “Thus says Hashem: Did I not reveal Myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt, belonging to Pharaoh’s household?””
: “I will also judge the nation they serve; afterward they will go out with great possessions.”

: “Until this point the prophets prophesied through the holy spirit. From this point onward, “Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise,” as it says, “For it is pleasant if you keep them within you,” and, “That your trust may be in the Lord”; also, “Have I not written for you thirty teachings,” and, “To make known to you the truth.” Likewise it says, “Ask your father and he will tell you; your elders, and they will say to you.” Could this mean ordinary elders in the marketplace? Scripture says, “They will say to you.” You thus learn that an elder is one who has acquired wisdom.”

: “As we have explained, the Greeks occupied the corresponding position in the impure realm, opposing the holiness of the Oral Torah. Its principal expansion came through Shimon HaTzaddik, one of the last surviving members of the Great Assembly, from whom the chain of the Mishnah began. Alexander of Macedon lived in his time. Greek wisdom then began through Aristotle, standing in the impure realm opposite the holiness of the Oral Torah. They too devised forms of wisdom and ethics from their own minds concerning worldly conduct. They therefore sought to abolish the Oral Torah among Israel.”

: “Voice is the name Havayah, the Holy One, blessed be He—the Written Torah, as the blessing before Torah study is derived from 'When I call the name of the Lord.' Speech is the Divine Presence, the Oral Torah, as Shabbat 138 b says, 'The word of the Lord: this is halakhah.' Sefer Yetzirah associates Shabbat in the year with the mouth in the person, and the Zohar says, 'The day is sanctified; the mouth ruling over all ascends—the mouth of the Lord.' Certainly the human mouth was not created on Shabbat, since Adam spoke on Friday. Rather, the mouth of the Lord means that a person speaks and his words become God’s word, 'My words that I placed in your mouth.' This was created on Shabbat when the day was sanctified. This is 'Kingship is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah.'”
: “Hashem said to Moses, “See, I have made you as a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.””
: “He will speak to the people for you. He will be a mouth for you, and you will be to him in the place of God.”
: “For a priest’s lips should preserve knowledge, and people should seek Torah from his mouth, for he is an angel of Hashem of Hosts.”
: “God spoke all these words, saying:”
: “Hashem spoke to Moses, saying: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn, whatever first opens a womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal; it is Mine.””

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””

: “The ninth is Shaddai—another reading has El Shaddai—who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ Enough means sufficiency, and sufficiency comes to the world only from the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ The tenth is Adonai, for the kingdom’s law is certainly law. This wages the King’s battles in the world; it is lower Might, Tzedek.”

: “Rabbi Yudan, Rabbi Aivu, and Rabbi Mishin ben Nagri said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Your children are destined to act like a nation among the assembly of peoples: just as an assembly of other peoples offers sacrifices when private altars are prohibited to Israel, so your children will offer sacrifices at such a time. Rabbi Chanina derives it from the verse, ‘Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the Lord had come, saying: Israel shall be your name.’ From the moment he was given that name, he was also told, ‘A nation and an assembly of nations shall come from you.’”

: ““Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head like purple.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: The poor among you are as dear to Me as Elijah, who ascended Carmel, as it is written, “Elijah ascended to the top of Carmel, bent down to the ground, and placed his face between his knees.” Why did he place his face between his knees? He said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, if we possess no merit, look to the covenant of circumcision.”
: “Answer me, Hashem, answer me, so that this people will know that You, Hashem, are God, and that You have turned their heart backward.”

: “‘Joseph was brought down to Egypt.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘Come, see the works of God, awesome in His dealings with human beings.’ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Even the awesome events You bring upon us, You bring through a pretext. Consider: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created the angel of death on the first day. From where do we know this? Rabbi Berekhya said: ‘Darkness was over the face of the deep’—this is the angel of death, who darkens people’s faces. Adam was created on the sixth day, yet the blame was attached to him, as though he had brought death into the world: ‘On the day you eat from it, you shall surely die.’ To what is this comparable? To a man who wishes to divorce his wife. Before going home he writes a bill of divorce, then enters his house holding it and looks for a pretext to give it to her. He tells her, ‘Mix me a cup to drink.’ She does so. When he takes the cup from her, he says, ‘Here is your bill of divorce.’ She asks, ‘What was my offense?’ He replies, ‘Leave my house: you mixed me a lukewarm cup!’ She says, ‘You already knew that I would mix a lukewarm cup, since you wrote the bill of divorce and brought it with you!’ So Adam said before the Holy One: ‘Master of the world, two thousand years before You created Your world, the Torah was with You as a craftsman, as it says, “I was beside Him as a craftsman, a delight day by day”—two thousand years. It already contained, “This is the Torah: when a person dies in a tent.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Without these three verses, Israel would have lost its footing. One says, “And those whom I have afflicted”; another says, “Like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel”; and another says, “I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.” Rav Pappa derived it from, “I will put My spirit within you, and bring it about that you walk in My statutes.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 32a:2:1: ““Without these three verses”: they testify that the Holy One, blessed be He, has the power to rectify our inclination and remove the evil inclination from us.”
: “On that day, declares Hashem, I will gather the limping, assemble those driven away, and those whom I afflicted.”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”

: “The Sages taught: A person should always live in the Land of Israel, even in a city with a gentile majority, rather than outside the Land, even in a city with a Jewish majority. For one who lives in the Land of Israel is like someone who has a God; one who lives outside it is like someone who has no God, as it says, “To give you the land of Canaan, to be your God.” Does someone who does not live in the Land have no God? Rather, it teaches that living outside the Land is as though serving idols. Thus David says, “They have driven me away today from sharing in Hashem’s inheritance, saying: Go, serve other gods.” Who told David to serve other gods? Rather, it teaches that one who lives outside the Land is as though serving idols.”

: “Come and see: ‘Jacob dwelt in the land of his father’s sojournings.’ What are ‘his father’s sojournings,’ megurei? As in ‘terror all around,’ magor: throughout his life he feared and remained in fear. Rabbi Eleazar said: he bound himself and dwelt in the place connected to darkness. ‘The land of his father’s sojournings, in Canaan’s land’: one place was bound to its corresponding place. ‘His father’s sojournings’ is harsh judgment; ‘the land’ is gentle judgment, joined to harsh judgment. In it Jacob settled and bound himself. That land is the mirror that does not shine.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; all the males guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient merit for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””

: “'These are the heads of their ancestral houses': because Scripture needed to give the genealogy of Levi’s tribe down to Moses and Aaron on their account, it began tracing the ancestry in birth order, from Reuben. In Pesikta Rabbati I saw that because our father Jacob reproached these three tribes at his death, Scripture returned here to record their genealogies alone, showing that they are esteemed.”

: “Why does he trace their lineage alongside Moses and Aaron? If you say that, because their father rebuked them, he counted the three separately, that is well. But why place them beside Moses and Aaron—“The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron”? Rabbi Bei, son of Rabbi Simon, said in Rabbi Shmuel son of Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: Because they accepted their father’s rebukes, they merited having their lineage recorded beside Moses and Aaron, fulfilling, “An ear that hears life-giving rebuke shall dwell among the wise.””

: “Rami bar Abba said: It is written “Abram,” and it is written “Abraham.” At first the Holy One, blessed be He, made him ruler over two hundred and forty-three limbs; afterward He made him ruler over two hundred and forty-eight. The additional limbs are his two eyes, two ears, and the head of the organ of circumcision.”

: ““Two eyes and two ears”: At first the Holy One, blessed be He, made Abraham ruler over the limbs that were already under his control, so that he could guard against transgression. A person’s eyes and ears, however, are not under his control: He sees with his eyes and hears with his ears even against his will. After Abraham was circumcised, the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him mastery even over these, so that he would look at and hear only something connected with a mitzvah. “The head of the organ”: It was circumcised.”
: “Your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” whether you turn right or turn left.”

: “This is “Your eyes shall see your Teacher.” From everything a person sees, he should learn something for Hashem’s service: this was certainly not shown to him without a purpose, but so that he might learn Hashem’s way. Likewise, from what he hears he should learn the paths of divine service, as in “Your ears shall hear a word behind you: This is the way; walk in it.” He knows that Hashem did not arrange for him to hear this without a purpose; it must teach him His way. This is “Who is wise? One who learns from every person”: he learns from everything he hears and sees, even when the other person did not intend to teach him. Abraham attained this after circumcision, becoming a new creation whose eyes and ears would see and hear only matters of mitzvah, learning Hashem’s way.”

: “‘It is Aaron and Moses, to whom the Lord said, Bring the children of Israel out of Egypt.’ Why the singular ‘it is Aaron and Moses,’ rather than ‘they are’? To include one within the other, spirit within water. ‘It is Moses and Aaron’ includes water within spirit. Therefore it says ‘it is,’ not ‘they are.’”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”

: “Torah repairs this blemish, as we explained concerning 'Healing for all his flesh.' Flesh alludes to it, called holy flesh in holiness. Thus Bereshit Rabbah’s opening to Vayera expounds 'From my flesh I behold...' concerning circumcision. This is kol-vav, Torah. 'And with voice' means prayer, whose essence is crying out—a voice without words, as the Zohar says: one cries out and says nothing. It then says: one who prays, weeps, and cries until unable to move his lips offers the complete prayer, which is in the heart and never returns empty, citing 'I will surely hear his cry.' This helps even for this blemish: although the Zohar says it has no repentance, crying out nevertheless helps.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: ““The Lord strengthened Pharaoh’s heart.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that he had not turned back after the first five plagues, from then onward the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Even if he wishes to repent, I shall strengthen his heart so that I may exact the entire judgment from him, “as the Lord had spoken to Moses,” for it is written, “I shall harden Pharaoh’s heart.””

: “Metatron likewise pleads merit for his birds, the spirits that fly among human beings. The neshamot come from the Throne, the ruchot from this living creature, and the nefashot from the wheel. These correspond to Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah.”
: “R. Levi said: Great is repentance, for it reaches the Throne of Glory, as it says, “Return, Israel, to Hashem your God.””

: “Our holy master expounded: Great is the power of repentance! As soon as a person considers repentance in his heart, it immediately ascends—not ten miles, twenty, or a hundred, but a journey of five hundred years; not merely to the first heaven but to the seventh, and not merely to the seventh heaven but to stand before the Throne of Glory. Thus Hosea says, “Return, Israel, to the Lord your God.” Another interpretation of “to the Lord your God”: They said, Master of the universe, we fear our numerous sins. David said, “My iniquities have passed over my head,” and Ezra said, “Our iniquities have multiplied above our heads, and our guilt has grown to heaven.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Do not fear this. If they reach heaven and you repent, I forgive—not only the first, second, or third heaven, but even the seventh, up to the Throne of Glory. If you repent, I immediately accept you. “Return, Israel, to the Lord your God”—return, Israel, even if your sins reach the Lord your God.”

: “Egypt’s plagues numbered ten, and everywhere ten indicates the ten sefirot. With each plague Israel emerged from one attribute of the ten shells, which stand opposite holiness, and entered a corresponding holy attribute. This is 'a blow for Egypt and healing for Israel,' as the Zohar expounds. God therefore began the plagues from below upward. First He turned water to blood, and the fish in the river died. This corresponds to kingship, the Oral Torah, the sea of Talmud, and the fish of Torah’s precious delight. Opposite this, among Egypt’s shells, are malicious waters and sexually unrestrained fish.”
: “'Boils': an expression of heat. There are many examples in the language of the Mishnah, such as 'a hot year' in Yoma 53.”

: “Some captive women were brought to Nehardea and lodged in the upper room of Rav Amram the Pious. The ladder was removed from before them. When one of them passed by, light fell through the opening. Rav Amram took the ladder, which ten men could not lift, and lifted it alone. He began climbing. Halfway up, he braced himself apart and cried: Fire in Amram’s house! The Sages came and said: You have embarrassed us. He answered: Better that you be embarrassed through Amram in this world than through him in the World to Come. He made the evil inclination swear to leave him; it emerged like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am stronger than you.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; all the males guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient merit for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””

: “We learned: what is ‘a tam man’? As the Targum renders it, complete. Complete in everything; complete toward both sides, the Holy Ancient One and Ze‘ir Anpin; complete toward upper Kindness and upper Might, bringing completion to both.”

: “The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining understanding. She took some of its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.”
: “'She gave also to her husband': so that she would not die while he lived and married another woman.”

: “The serpent went and said to the woman: I touched it and did not die; you too may touch it and will not die. The woman went and touched the tree, and saw the angel of death coming toward her. She said: Woe to me for touching it! Now I shall die, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will make another woman and give her to Adam. Instead, I shall cause him to eat with me. If I die, we shall both die; if I live, we shall both live. She took of the tree’s fruit, ate, and gave it to her husband.”

: “Rava said: If a children’s teacher teaches adequately and another teacher teaches better, we do not remove the first, lest the replacement become negligent. Rav Dimi of Nehardea says: On the contrary, he will teach all the more diligently, for the rivalry of scholars increases wisdom.”

: “Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda expounded: Why is “Hashem God formed the human being” written with two letters yod? The Holy One, blessed be He, created two inclinations, one good and one evil. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak objected: If so, does an animal, whose “formed” is not written that way, have no inclination? Yet we see it cause harm, bite, and kick. Rather, the spelling follows Rabbi Shimon ben Pazzi’s teaching: “Woe to me because of my Maker, and woe to me because of my inclination.””

: “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He created male and female. Even Leviathan the fleeing serpent and Leviathan the twisted serpent were created male and female. Were they to mate, they would destroy the entire world. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He castrated the male, killed the female, and salted her for the righteous in the future, as it says, “He will kill the sea monster in the sea.” He likewise created the Behemoth of a thousand hills male and female; were they to mate, they would destroy the entire world. He castrated the male, cooled the female, and preserved her for the righteous in the future, as it says, “See, his strength is in his loins”—the male—“and his vigor in the muscles of his belly”—the female. Why not also castrate the male Leviathan and cool the female? Fish are unrestrained. Why not do the reverse, killing the male? One answer is that the female is better salted. Another is that, since it is written, “This Leviathan You formed to sport with,” it would be improper to sport with a female. Why not salt the female Behemoth as well? Salted fish is good, but salted meat is not.”

: “In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the evil inclination and slaughters it. This means that from the inclination of desire there will remain a longing for Torah, the very purpose for which it was created. Midrash HaNeelam says that without the inclination there would be no joy in Torah learning; this will remain in the future. This is the banquet of Leviathan prepared for the righteous: the delicacies that remain are the precious delights of Torah, the purpose for which desire was created. The Gemara likewise says God will make a sukkah for the righteous from Leviathan’s skin. We do not find anything remaining from the wild ox. Desire will remain in holiness as Torah’s precious delight, whereas the wild ox alludes to jealousy and murder, of which nothing will remain in the future.”

: “'If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him to the study hall' means introducing this craving of desire, called repulsive, into holiness, turning it into joy in Torah learning, as it will be in the future according to Midrash HaNeelam. Israel are therefore compared to holy fish. Bereshit Rabbah 97 says: just as fish grow in water and receive a drop from above thirstily, so Israel grow in water—in Torah—and when they hear a new Torah teaching, they receive it thirstily, like someone who has never heard words of Torah. Thus Torah’s precious delight is also compared to fish.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel said: Four are regarded as dead: a person afflicted with tzara’at, a blind person, one who has no children, and one who has lost his property. A person with tzara’at: ‘Let her not be like one dead.’ A blind person: ‘He has placed me in darkness, like the eternally dead.’ One without children: ‘Give me children, or I am dead.’ One who has lost his property: ‘For all the men seeking your life have died.’ Were they actually dead? They were Dathan and Abiram! Rather, they had lost their property.”

k: volume-i|494|1|Rashi on Genesis 30:1, s.v. va-teqanne R
quote: : “'Rachel envied her sister': she envied her good deeds, saying, 'Had she not been more righteous than I, she would not have merited children,' as taught in Bereshit Rabbah.”

: “‘Of the sons of Issachar, those who understood the times.’ What does ‘the times’ mean? Rabbi Tanchuma said: The recurring seasons. Rabbi Yosei ben Kitzri said: The intercalation of years. ‘Their chiefs were two hundred, and all their brothers followed their word’: Issachar supplied two hundred heads of courts. ‘All their brothers followed their word’ means that all their brothers accepted their halakhic rulings, and Issachar answered their questions with rulings as authoritative as a law given to Moses at Sinai.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: A woman who seeks her husband for the marital mitzvah has children whose like were not found even in Moses’ generation. In Moses’ generation it says, “Provide wise, understanding, and known men from your tribes,” but afterward it says, “I took your tribal heads, wise and known men”—he did not find understanding men. Of Leah it says, “Leah went out to meet him and said: You shall come to me, for I have hired you”; and it says, “Of the sons of Issachar, men of understanding of the times, knowing what Israel should do; their heads were two hundred, and all their brothers followed their direction.” Is that so? Rav Yitzhak bar Avdimi said: Eve was cursed with ten curses: “I will greatly increase” refers to two flows of blood, menstrual blood and blood of virginity. “Your pain” is the pain of raising children. “Your pregnancy” is the pain of pregnancy. “In pain you shall bear children” bears its plain meaning. “Your desire shall be toward your husband” teaches that a woman longs for her husband when he goes on a journey. “He shall rule over you” teaches that a woman seeks him in her heart, while a man asks aloud; this is a good quality in women. The earlier teaching concerns her making herself pleasing before him.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “For you are a people holy to Hashem your God. Hashem your God chose you to be His treasured people from all the peoples upon the earth.”
