ref: Derekh Hashem, Part Four, On Divine Service and the Calendar 3
quote: Parallel: Ramchal, Derekh Hashem IV, On Divine Service and the Calendar 3: “Israel’s conduct on this day should accord with the elevated standing they attain in it. As explained above, involvement in the world binds a person to materiality, lowers his condition, and brings him down from the dignity and elevation that should be his. On Shabbat he must disengage from this, since his standing is raised above that of the weekday; he should maintain himself at a level suited to this elevation. Yet complete disengagement from bodily life and its concerns is impossible: he is still in this world, and bodily bonds remain upon him. Supreme Wisdom therefore measured the degree to which he should withdraw from bodily involvement and the degree in which he must remain. It commanded withdrawal to the proper extent and warned him not to neglect it. This comprises all the forms of labor prohibited on Shabbat.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “Likewise Torah scholars, children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they are not workers like the other servants, children of the ordinary realm. Their reward in this world and the world to come is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it says, ‘Honor it with clean clothing.’ Whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals should be done for them.”
: “Then you will delight in Hashem. I will have you ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for Hashem’s mouth has spoken.”

: “A midrashic teaching likewise says: What is 'I will be who I will be'? Just as you are with Me, so I am with you. If they open their hands and give charity, I too shall open My hand, as it says, 'The Lord will open His good treasury for you.' If they do not open their hands, what is written there? 'He withholds the waters, and they dry up,' and so forth.”

: “Your being with Me requires the beginning to come through an awakening from below. But when the appointed time arrives, He Himself awakens them even to that awakening. This answers the question 'What is His name?'—what grasp could they possess while so deeply submerged, without any awakening of their own? He therefore said, 'Who I will be': even your being with Me comes from Me; I will act to bring about your being with Me.”

Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik 185:1: “Fear of Heaven is the choice entrusted to a person; yet choice itself also truly comes from Hashem, who created the human being with free choice. Fear of Heaven—the recognition that choice too comes from Hashem—means being afraid to choose evil; this remains in the person’s hands. The initial desire to learn from a teacher is choice itself. Yet the end is embedded in the beginning: this too truly comes from Hashem. Therefore it is called “Hashem’s Torah.””

k: volume-i|507|0|R. Chaim of Volozhin, Nefesh HaChayim II
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim of Volozhin, Nefesh HaChayim III 12:8: “This is a great matter and a remarkable means of removing and nullifying all judgments and alien wills, so that they cannot govern him or leave any impression at all. A person fixes in his heart: Hashem is the true God; there is no power at all besides Him, blessed be He, in this world or in any of the worlds, and everything is filled only with His simple unity. Within his heart he nullifies every other power completely, pays no attention to any power or will in the world, and subjects and attaches the purity of his thought only to the one Master, blessed be He. Correspondingly, He will enable him to have all the powers and wills in the world become nullified of themselves, so that they cannot act upon him at all.”

: ““There is nothing besides Him”—Rabbi Hanina said: Even sorcery. A woman was trying to take earth from beneath Rabbi Hanina’s feet. He told her: Take it; your undertaking will not succeed, for it is written, “There is nothing besides Him.” But Rabbi Yohanan said: Why is sorcery called keshafim? Because it contradicts the heavenly retinue. Rabbi Hanina was different, because his merit was great.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Lech Lecha 10:1: “One must not imagine, Heaven forbid, that because everything comes from Hashem, one may follow the heart without any effort and rely on divine assistance—“for You are with me.” The Midrash therefore concludes, “Hashem’s word is refined; He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.” This means a person who strives and exerts himself with all his power to conquer his inclination, wishes to shelter beneath His wings, looks toward Hashem, and prays and pleads before the Holy One. Such a person is assured that Hashem will not abandon him to the inclination. “He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him”: the inclination will not rule over him at all. A shield conceals a person from his enemy so the enemy cannot approach him.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘If I lead them by a direct route, each person will immediately take possession of a field or vineyard and neglect Torah. Rather, I shall lead them through the wilderness. They will eat the manna and drink the water of the well, and Torah will become settled within their bodies.’”
: “For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 11:1: ““Two olive trees beside it, one to the right of the bowl and one to its left,” alludes to two forms of effort in Torah. The one on the left signifies Torah study that uproots and eradicates the evil inclination from the heart’s left chamber, refining the foolish heart of this world’s wishes and desires. The one on the right signifies that even after purifying the heart of those desires, one must labor in Torah to bring His holiness into the heart. As the Talmud says, after praising one who has not attended theaters and similar places, lest a person say, “I shall go and indulge in sleep,” Scripture continues, “In His Torah he meditates day and night.” Merely purifying the heart of the evil inclination does not yet acquire His holiness. Torah study brings holiness into the heart, for the aim of His will is that the utterance “I am Hashem”—knowledge of Him—enter the heart.”
: “As for me, may my prayer to You, Hashem, be at a time of favor. God, in Your abundant kindness, answer me with Your faithful deliverance.”

: “The forehead of the skull is the will of wills; the will of Ze‘ir Anpin stands opposite that will. An alternative reading says that the skull’s forehead is called Favor, for the will of wills is revealed there, corresponding to the forehead below. Thus ‘It shall be upon his forehead always, for favor.’ That forehead, called Favor, reveals the whole head and skull concealed in 420 worlds—another reading has 410.”
: “The third prayer, ‘You are One and Your Name is One,’ corresponds to the Lord, the middle pillar, which unites with both.”
: “Grant faithfulness to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our ancestors in days of old.”
: “A truthful lip endures forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.”

: “Why specifically the letter tav? Rav said: Tav stands for tihyeh, “you shall live,” and tav for tamut, “you shall die.” Shmuel said: The merit of the ancestors has come to an end. Rabbi Yohanan said: The merit of the ancestors will bestow favor. Reish Lakish said: Tav is the final letter of the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Rabbi Hanina said: The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He, is truth.”

: “‘But I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.’ If it is true, why call it merely ‘inscribed’? And if it is merely inscribed, why call it ‘true’? Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi asked, ‘Did you not know how to answer?’ Rabbi Levi replied: ‘It is inscribed before the decree is issued; it is true once the decree has been issued.’ What is truth? The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our Master said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: It is emet, ‘truth.’ What is emet? Reish Lakish said: Alef stands at the beginning of the alphabet, mem in the middle, and tav at the end, corresponding to ‘I am the first, and I am the last.’”

: “Rabbi Yudan bar Rabbi said in Rabbi Berekhya’s name: If you see that the merit of the patriarchs has slipped away and the merit of the matriarchs has faltered, go and occupy yourself with acts of kindness. Thus it is written, “For the mountains may depart and the hills falter”: the mountains are the patriarchs, and the hills the matriarchs. What follows? “But My kindness shall not depart from you.””

: “Both “You shall return” and “Forever” are needed. Had the Torah written only “Forever,” I would have thought it meant literally forever; therefore it wrote, “You shall return.” Had it written only “You shall return,” I would have thought this applies when he has not yet served six years; but if he has served six, his later service should not be more severe than his first service: Just as the first was six years, so the later service should be six. “Forever” therefore teaches: Until the Jubilee’s term.”

: “‘Behold, the kings assembled.’ Rabbi Yehudah said: here is faith’s mystery. When favor is present and the bond is crowned together, two worlds join and meet as one: one opens the treasury, and the other gathers and collects within it. Then ‘Behold, the kings assembled’: the two holy worlds, the upper world and the lower world.”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry is described by ‘A river goes out from Eden’—vav—‘to water the garden.’ The river is the middle pillar; ‘goes out from Eden’ means from the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ means the lower Shekhinah.”
: “Trust in Hashem forever, for in Yah, Hashem, is an everlasting Rock.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah the Nasi asked Rabbi Ami: What does the verse mean, “Trust in Hashem forever, for through Yah, Hashem, is the Maker of worlds”? He answered: Whoever places his trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, has a refuge in this world and in the World to Come. Rabbi Yehudah said: My question is why it says “through Yah,” rather than simply “Yah.” This follows Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai’s exposition: These are the two worlds the Holy One, blessed be He, created—one with the letter heh and one with yod. I would not know whether the World to Come was created with yod and this world with heh, or this world with yod and the World to Come with heh. But Scripture says, “These are the generations of heaven and earth when they were created”—behibaram. Read it as: “With heh He created them.””
: “They told him everything Joseph had said to them. He saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, and the spirit of their father Jacob revived.”

: “The Rabbis interpreted the verse concerning Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: “My light”—on Rosh Hashanah; “my salvation”—on Yom Kippur. “Whom shall I fear?”—“My strength and song is the Lord.” “When evildoers approach me”—these are the princes of the nations. “To eat my flesh”—for the princes of the nations come and accuse Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying: Master of the universe, these worship idols and those worship idols; these commit sexual immorality and those commit sexual immorality; these shed blood and those shed blood. Why do these descend to Gehinnom while those do not? “My enemies and adversaries”—there are three hundred and sixty-five days in the solar year, while “the satan” has the numerical value of three hundred and sixty-four, for the satan accuses throughout the year but does not accuse on Yom Kippur. Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “If an army encamps against me”—Samael’s army—“my heart will not fear,” for You promised me, “With this Aaron shall enter the sanctuary.””
: “Of David. Hashem is my light and my deliverance; whom should I fear? Hashem is the stronghold of my life; whom should I dread?”

: “In the Shabbat evening prayer we say, “You blessed it above all days and sanctified it above all appointed times.” “Appointed times” ordinarily means the holiness of the three pilgrimage festivals, whose holiness is also included in Shabbat. The holiness of Passover concerns redemption from Egypt, and its root is found in the holiness of Shabbat, as the Sages said: If Israel kept two Sabbaths properly, they would immediately be redeemed.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””

: “On Yom Kippur, Satan has no permission to accuse. From where do we know this? Rami bar Hama said: The numerical value of ha-satan is three hundred and sixty-four. For three hundred and sixty-four days he has permission to accuse; on Yom Kippur he has no permission to accuse.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: when they unite, the world’s inhabitants cannot withstand them. Therefore, ‘Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together’—precisely together. We learned that a person should not make room for evil kinds, for a person’s action below arouses what should not be aroused. When they unite, their combined force brings forth what is called Dog, the most brazen of all. Hence ‘Against all the children of Israel, no dog shall sharpen its tongue.’ God said: ‘You asked, “Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?” I now hand you over to the dog.’ Immediately, ‘Amalek came.’”

: ““There is one people”: Rava said: No one understood malicious speech as Haman did. He said to Ahasuerus: Come, let us destroy them. The king replied: I fear their God, lest He deal with me as He did with earlier rulers. Haman answered: They have fallen asleep in their observance of the commandments. The king said: There are rabbis among them. Haman replied: They are all one people. Perhaps you think I am making a gap in your kingdom? They are scattered among the nations. Perhaps you think they benefit you? They are “separate,” like a mule that bears no offspring. Perhaps you think they occupy one province? Scripture says, “In all the provinces of your kingdom.” “Their laws differ from every people’s”: they neither eat our food nor marry our women, nor give their women to us in marriage. “They do not observe the king’s laws”: they spend the whole year saying, “It is Shabbat today; it is Passover today.” “It is not worthwhile for the king to leave them”: they eat, drink, and disparage the king. If a fly falls into someone’s cup, he throws it out and drinks; but if my lord the king touches the cup, he smashes it on the ground and will not drink.”
Commentary: Rashi on Megillah 13b:19:3: ““They spend the year with ‘Shabbat today; Passover today’”: It is Shabbat today, it is Passover today, and we are forbidden to work.”
: “A psalm of David. Hashem is my shepherd; I will lack nothing.”

: “Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: You find no occupation more lowly than that of a shepherd, who walks about all day with his staff and his bag. Yet David called the Holy One, blessed be He, a shepherd! Rather, David said, “I gain understanding from elders.” Jacob called Him a shepherd, saying, “The God who has shepherded me.” I too shall call Him a shepherd, as it says, “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.””

: “Although a person knows God in a general manner as the One who created the worlds, this is what 'What does the Lord ask of you, except to fear' addresses: through this recognition come fear and the person’s effort to choose good. They acquired this knowledge immediately upon leaving Egypt. Nevertheless, if you wish to know that the Lord is God—the particular way of knowing that there is nothing besides Him—'Bring it back to your heart.' Through one’s effort to subdue the inclination and unite both hearts, one afterward attains this holiness: everything is from God, even one’s overcoming and choosing good.”

: “From where do we learn that the Divine Presence accompanies even one person who sits and studies Torah? It says, “In every place where I cause My name to be recalled, I will come to you and bless you.””

: “Rav Yehudah said: Where does the Torah require the blessing after a meal? “You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.” Where does the Torah require a blessing before Torah study? “When I proclaim Hashem’s name, ascribe greatness to our God.””

: “The Torah means the commandments commanded by God. Although the patriarchs observed the entire Torah before it was given, they fulfilled it on their own initiative. Bereshit Rabbah 61 says that Abraham’s two kidneys were appointed as two teachers, flowing with and teaching Torah and wisdom. God, however, did not command them any commandment apart from circumcision. Adam had been commanded in seven commandments incumbent upon all nations; these belong to proper conduct that preceded Torah. Seder Eliyahu interprets 'To guard the way' as proper conduct, which preceded the Tree of Life, meaning Torah. God commanded Abraham concerning circumcision; its root is El Shaddai, the sixth of the seven names that may not be erased, corresponding to the righteous one, foundation of the world. At that time the light of Shaddai was revealed to Abraham. 'By My name Havayah'—the root of all Torah’s commandments—'I was not made known to them' through knowledge, the Torah’s light, as in 'Illuminate our eyes through Your Torah.'”

: “'The God before whom my fathers walked' means that God did not lead them; rather, through their wisdom they followed His way according to their capacity to apprehend. God did not show them the path to take. This is called walking before God: they attained Torah according to their intellectual apprehension through creation, completed through El Shaddai, sufficient to recognize His kingship. Jacob had a greater connection to knowledge than Abraham and Isaac, as in 'The God who has shepherded me,' although Torah was not yet openly given. Thus Tikkunei Zohar says, 'Jacob is outside; Moses is within.' Moses was the inner knowledge, and all his conduct and path were through knowledge, the holy spirit, as Rashi explains. His entire generation was called the generation of knowledge, and he brought down the holy Torah, which is called knowledge.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”
: “R. Isaac ben Tavlai said: Why is it called Lebanon? Because it whitens Israel’s sins.”

: ““Like scarlet”—shanim? Should it not say shani, in the singular? Rabbi Yitzhak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years, shanim, ordered in succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Minchah, Amidah, Sanctity of the Day 1
quote: : “You are One and Your name is One; who is like Your people Israel, one nation upon the earth?”
: “This day belongs to souls, rather than the body, for the Bundle of Souls rules. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional upper holy spirit.”

: “Although Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed about co-wives, sisters, an old bill of divorce, a woman whose marital status was uncertain, a man who divorced his wife and then lodged with her at an inn, silver and its equivalent, and a perutah and its equivalent, Beit Shammai did not refrain from marrying women from Beit Hillel, nor Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai. This teaches that they treated each other with affection and friendship, fulfilling “Love truth and peace.” Rabbi Shimon says: They refrained in definite cases, but did not refrain in doubtful cases. … Do not read “in doubtful cases,” but “in unspecified cases”: they would inform one another, and the others would abstain.”

: ““Go out and see, daughters of Zion, King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on his wedding day and on the day of his heart’s joy.” “On his wedding day”—this is the giving of the Torah. “On the day of his heart’s joy”—this is the building of the Temple; may it be rebuilt speedily in our days.”

k: volume-i|547|1|Rashi on Taanit 26b, s.v. ba-melekh Shel
quote: : ““With King Solomon”—with the King to whom peace belongs. “His mother”—the congregation of Israel. “This is the giving of the Torah”—Yom Kippur, when the later tablets were given.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: I searched all Scripture and did not find that Bathsheba made Solomon a crown. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai asked Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei: Have you perhaps heard from your father the meaning of “with the crown his mother crowned him”? He replied: Yes. It is like a king who had an only daughter and loved her exceedingly. He called her “my daughter,” and continued cherishing her until he called her “my sister,” and then “my mother.” So the Holy One, blessed be He, first called Israel daughter, as it says, “Hear, daughter, and see; incline your ear, and forget your people and your father’s house.” He continued cherishing them until He called them sister, as it says, “Open to me, my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew, my locks with drops of night.” He continued cherishing them until He called them mother, as it says, “Listen to Me, My people; My nation, give ear to Me, for Torah shall go forth from Me, and My judgment I shall establish as a light for peoples.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai rose and kissed him on his head.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “He began grieving over the breaking of the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, which contained only the Ten Commandments. In the second tablets I give you, there will be laws, midrash, and aggadot, as it is written, “He will tell you wisdom’s hidden things, for sound wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you receive the tidings that I have forgiven your sin, as it says, “Know that God remits some of your iniquity.””

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”
: “They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be filled with knowledge of Hashem as the waters cover the sea.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “‘God said, Let there be light, and there was light.’ The parenthetical reading explains: ‘God said’—to whom does He speak? He speaks to others. ‘Let there be light’ is for this world; ‘and there was light,’ for the world to come. This is the light God first created, the light of the eye. God showed it to Adam, who saw through it from one end of the world to the other. God showed it to David, who praised Him: ‘How abundant is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You.’ God showed it to Moses, who saw through it from Gilead to Dan.”
: “Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.”
: “Happy are those whose way is wholehearted, who walk in Hashem’s Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Elul 5:1: “Even one who is not so fully refined nevertheless receives, through “mighty waters”—Torah and fear—a path: “the path of the heh,” a fine trail through the holiness of Jacob toward the lower heh, kingship. Thus, after Scripture says, “Saying: This is the way; walk in it”—addressing one who merits “He makes a way in the sea,” whose way is illuminated plainly enough to point to it with a finger—it continues, “whether you turn right or left.” When a person is not so thoroughly refined, the right and left, these “mighty waters” of Torah and fear, still open for him the path of the heh: through the vav, the middle bar, Jacob’s holiness, a fine trail shines from the supernal crown to the lower heh.”
: “God is exalted in His power; who is a teacher like Him?”

: ““Thus says the Lord: By this you shall know…” This is what Scripture says: “Behold, God is exalted in His strength; who teaches like Him?” Ordinarily, a person who wishes to harm his enemy does so suddenly, before the enemy notices. The Holy One, blessed be He, however, warns Pharaoh before each plague, so that he may repent. Thus it is written, “By this you shall know that I am the Lord.””

: “Nowadays the Edomites’ wine does not turn sour until they add barley to it, and they call it Edomite vinegar. This fulfills the verse, “I will be filled from her destruction”: if this one is full, that one is desolate; if that one is full, this one is desolate. Rav Nahman bar Isaac said that it is derived from here: “One nation will be stronger than the other.””

: “It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: You find that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, and gave them only through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. Torah: ‘Happy is the man whom You discipline, Lord, and whom You teach from Your Torah.’ The Land of Israel: ‘Know in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, the Lord your God disciplines you.’ What follows? ‘For the Lord your God brings you into a good land.’ The World to Come: ‘For a mitzvah is a lamp and Torah is light, and disciplinary rebukes are the way of life.’ Whoever disciplines his son increases the son’s love and respect for his father, as it says, ‘Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and bring delight to your soul.’ Thus, ‘One who loves him seeks discipline for him early.’”

: “R. Abba said to Rabba bar Mari: It is written, “All the illness I placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you, for I am Hashem your healer.” If He does not place it upon you, why is healing necessary? He answered: R. Yohanan said that the verse explains itself, for it says, “If you listen carefully to the voice of Hashem your God.” If you listen, I will not place it upon you; if you do not listen, I will place it upon you. Even then, “I am Hashem your healer.””

: “The exaltation of God is in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand: to carry out vengeance among the nations and rebuke among the peoples; to bind their kings with chains and their dignitaries with iron fetters; to execute upon them the written judgment. This is the splendor of all His devoted ones. Hallelujah!”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword, as it says, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” How does the verse indicate this? Mar Zutra—or, according to another report, Rav Ashi—said: From the beginning of the passage, “Let the devoted rejoice in honor; let them sing upon their beds,” followed by, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” Rabbi Yitzchak also said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed keeps destructive forces away, as it says, “The sons of reshef fly high.” “Flight” refers to Torah, as in, “Will you let your eyes fly toward it, and it is gone?” “Reshef” refers to destructive forces, as in, “Exhausted by hunger and devoured by reshef and bitter destruction.””

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

: “Rav Shmuel bar Ami said—or, according to another report, Rav Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rav Yonatan’s name: How do we know that a decree accompanied by an oath is not torn up? For it says, “Therefore I have sworn concerning Eli’s house that the guilt of Eli’s house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.” Rava said: It is not atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it can be atoned for by Torah. Abaye said: It is not atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it can be atoned for by Torah together with acts of kindness. Rabbah and Abaye descended from Eli’s house. Rabbah, who devoted himself to Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who devoted himself to Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty. The Sages taught: A Jerusalem family’s members used to die at eighteen. They informed Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. He said, “Perhaps you belong to Eli’s family, of which it is written, ‘All the increase of your house will die as men.’ Go, occupy yourselves with Torah, and live.” They did so and lived, and the family came to be called after Rabban Yochanan.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: now we must reveal secrets bound above and below. Why is it written ‘Come to Pharaoh’? It should say ‘Go to Pharaoh.’ What is ‘come’? God brought Moses through chamber after chamber to a mighty upper serpent, from which many levels unfold. What is it? The secret of the great dragon.”

: “Come and see: the lowest of all the levels was struck first. Rabbi Shimon said: God began from the lowest, and His hand struck with every finger. When He reached the highest of all levels, He Himself performed His act, passing through Egypt and killing all. He therefore killed every firstborn in Egypt, for this is the upper level and firstborn of all.”

k: volume-i|569|0|Arizal/Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 3
quote: : “‘The uppermost serpent’: the marginal gloss identifies it as Arikh of the realm of kelippah.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya the Great expounded this. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it says, ‘The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.’ ‘The earth was waste and void’ refers to the deeds of the wicked; ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to the deeds of the righteous. Yet I do not know which He desires—the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, ‘God saw that the light was good,’ we know that He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wicked.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Scripture says, “As he wrestled with him”—like a person embracing another, whose hand reaches the other’s right thigh. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said: The wrestler appeared to Jacob as a gentile, for the Master said: An Israelite joined by a gentile on the road should place him on his right. Rav Shmuel bar Aha, teaching before Rav Pappa in Rava bar Ulla’s name, said: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar, for the Master said: One who walks on his teacher’s right is an uncultivated person. The Sages hold that he came from behind Jacob and displaced both thigh-sinews.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Scripture says, “As he wrestled with him”—like a person embracing another, whose hand reaches the other’s right thigh. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said: The wrestler appeared to Jacob as a gentile, for the Master said: An Israelite joined by a gentile on the road should place him on his right. Rav Shmuel bar Aha, teaching before Rav Pappa in Rava bar Ulla’s name, said: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar, for the Master said: One who walks on his teacher’s right is an uncultivated person. The Sages hold that he came from behind Jacob and displaced both thigh-sinews.”

: “R. Isaac said: Why were the reasons for the Torah’s laws not revealed? Two verses revealed their reasons, and the greatest man in the world stumbled through them. It is written, “He shall not multiply wives for himself.” Solomon said, “I will multiply them and not turn aside.” Yet it is written, “In Solomon’s old age, his wives turned his heart aside.” It is written, “He shall not multiply horses for himself.” Solomon said, “I will multiply them and not send people back.” Yet it is written, “A chariot was brought up from Egypt for six (hundred),” and so forth.”

k: volume-i|574|0|R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yeshar
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yesharim 20:9–10: “One must understand that acts of piety cannot be judged by their first appearance. One must examine and consider how far an action’s consequences reach. Sometimes the action itself looks good, yet its consequences are bad, and one is therefore obliged to refrain from it. To perform it would make one a sinner rather than a pious person. The case of Gedaliah son of Ahikam is before our eyes. In his great piety, unwilling to judge Ishmael unfavorably or to accept slander, he told Johanan son of Kareah, “You are speaking falsely about Ishmael.” What resulted? He himself was killed, Israel was scattered, and its remaining ember was extinguished. Scripture even attributes to him the killing of the men who were slain, as though he had killed them himself, as the Sages explain concerning the verse, “All the corpses of the men who were struck down through Gedaliah.””

: “The account of Creation is read and translated publicly. Is this not obvious? One might have thought that people would come to ask what is above, what is below, what was before, and what is after. The teaching therefore tells us that it is nevertheless read and translated.”
: “He said, “Throw it to the ground.” He threw it to the ground, and it became a snake; Moses fled from it.”

: “'He said: Cast it to the ground; he cast it to the ground.' I did not understand why He performed the signs for Moses, since Moses believed that the Holy One, blessed be He, was speaking with him. He should have said, 'Cast the staff in your hand to the ground before them, and it will become a serpent,' and similarly concerning the second sign, as He said concerning the third, 'Take some water from the Nile.' The sages’ words are therefore trustworthy: the first sign alluded to his having spoken slander against them, and the second punished him for it. This explains 'Moses fled from it': he feared that he might be punished and bitten by the serpent. Every person distances himself from what harms him, even knowing that if this is God’s will, no one can deliver him from His hand.”

: “When the words of Torah and Shabbat were taken away from them, Moses our teacher said that harm had been done to this people: they might, God forbid, become corrupted and no longer fulfill 'One who loves him disciplines him early.' God showed him that this resembled the darkness before dawn. On the contrary, this would be the principal preparation for 'Let there be light,' through which Israel would emerge from darkness into light. It corresponds to the darkness mentioned in the first utterance, Bereshit, for this was the order of the world’s creation: first darkness, then light.”

: “Rav and Shmuel differed. One said: Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world, and Moses received all but one, as it says, “You made him only a little less than God.” “Kohelet sought to find words of delight”: Kohelet wanted to be like Moses. A heavenly voice replied, “And what is written uprightly is words of truth”—“No prophet arose again in Israel like Moses.” The other said: None arose among prophets, but one did arise among kings. How, then, do I explain “Kohelet sought to find words of delight”? Kohelet wanted to decide cases by what was in his heart, without witnesses and without prior warning. A heavenly voice replied, “And what is written uprightly is words of truth”—“By the testimony of two witnesses,” and so forth.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 14, paragraph 1: “At first, when a person puts on tzitzit, although they protect him from the evil inclination—as Scripture says, ‘You shall see it and remember,’ and the Gemara relates that the four fringes appeared to him as four witnesses—the evil inclination can still tempt a person, blind his eyes, and call evil good. This is what the Gemara means when it says that the evil inclination sits between the two entrances of the heart: sometimes it takes its seat at the wise heart on the right and presents itself as guiding him toward good. Even with our father Jacob we find that it appeared as a Torah scholar and attached itself at his right, presenting itself as a good guide. Jacob immediately recognized that this was false, and it could not overcome him; another person, however, might be led astray. After a person is crowned with tefillin, the mitzvah’s tallit becomes an encompassing light, a garment through which God protects him beyond his understanding. This resembles Rashi’s explanation in the name of the Jerusalem Talmud: ‘For the Lord will be at your confidence’—even in matters in which you are foolish. The intellect concealed beyond all thought guards him beyond the reach of his own apprehension.”
: “'Into a tannin': a serpent.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Shalom asked: if so, what are Leviathan and the ox, of which it says, ‘The mountains yield their produce for him’? Rabbi Yose answered: ‘At that time the Lord will visit with His harsh, great and mighty sword Leviathan the straight serpent and Leviathan the winding serpent, and kill the dragon in the sea.’ Here are three. Rather, this is an allusion to kingdoms. Rabbi Tanchum said: one must not contradict what the Rabbis said; certainly it is so.”
: “On that day Hashem will punish, with His harsh, great, and mighty sword, Leviathan the fleeing serpent and Leviathan the twisting serpent; He will slay the sea-monster in the sea.”

: “These three are all from the shell of desire, and are therefore called the straight serpent and twisting serpent. The serpent’s initial corruption was the desire for eating; it came upon Eve, and through the impurity it introduced caused the blemish of the 130 years. The Gemara says fish are sexually unrestrained. They are therefore called Leviathan the straight serpent and Leviathan the twisting serpent. The dragon in the sea likewise indicates desire. In holiness, water belongs to kindness; from this branches the shell of malicious waters, desire, alluding to Babylon, Media, and Greece. … The wild ox, however, alludes to the shell of jealousy and murder, of which nothing will remain in the future, as it says, 'No survivor shall remain.'”

: “Abaye heard a man say to a woman, “Let us set out early on the road.” He said, “I will go and keep them from wrongdoing.” He followed them for three parasangs through a marsh. When they parted, he heard them saying, “The road is long, but our company was pleasant.” Abaye said, “Had I been there, I could not have restrained myself.” He went, leaned against the door bolt, and grieved. An elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater evil inclination.”

: “Some captive women were brought to Nehardea and lodged in the upper room of Rav Amram the Pious. The ladder was removed from before them. When one of them passed by, light fell through the opening. Rav Amram took the ladder, which ten men could not lift, and lifted it alone. He began climbing. Halfway up, he braced himself apart and cried: Fire in Amram’s house! The Sages came and said: You have embarrassed us. He answered: Better that you be embarrassed through Amram in this world than through him in the World to Come. He made the evil inclination swear to leave him; it emerged like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am stronger than you.”

: “Likewise, the Cause of causes made ten sefirot and called Keter ‘Source.’ In it, the flowing of His light has no end. He therefore called Himself Ein Sof, ‘Without End.’ He has no likeness or form, and there is no vessel there that can grasp Him or attain any knowledge of Him at all. Therefore it was said of Him: do not expound what is too wondrous for you, nor investigate what is concealed from you.”

: “This Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, is neither mentioned nor found. Being the head above all the highest, He is mentioned only as a single head without a body, sustaining everything.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: now we must reveal secrets bound above and below. Why is it written ‘Come to Pharaoh’? It should say ‘Go to Pharaoh.’ What is ‘come’? God brought Moses through chamber after chamber to a mighty upper serpent, from which many levels unfold. What is it? The secret of the great dragon.”

: “'Come to Pharaoh.' Keep this principle in mind: wherever it says 'Come to Pharaoh,' it means that Moses should enter his reception hall without asking permission. Although Pharaoh had palace guards, as kings do, Moses was nevertheless to go in without permission. Indeed, the sages relate that Pharaoh had many armed guards, lions, and dogs, yet Moses entered without anyone stopping him. I found clear proof for their words in Pharaoh’s warning to Moses: 'Take care...do not see my face again.' Why did Pharaoh need to warn Moses? He should have instructed the palace guards, since kings station guards and order them not to admit someone. Certainly, then, they could not stand against him, not even the lions; this was an immense miracle. God therefore needed to tell him, 'Come to Pharaoh'—enter and approach him, paying no attention to any obstacle in the world. When Pharaoh went out to the water, God said, 'Go to Pharaoh,' because there were no guards there to fear, requiring Him to say, 'Approach him.' Rather, because that time was unsuitable for approaching—Pharaoh was discharging his repulsive bodily waste, making an approach discourteous—He told Moses, 'Go,' nevertheless.”
: “Draw me after you; let us run. The king has brought me into his chambers. Let us exult and rejoice in you; let us recall your love more than wine. They have loved you uprightly.”
: “Through knowledge its chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.”

: “Come and see: the lowest of all the levels was struck first. Rabbi Shimon said: God began from the lowest, and His hand struck with every finger. When He reached the highest of all levels, He Himself performed His act, passing through Egypt and killing all. He therefore killed every firstborn in Egypt, for this is the upper level and firstborn of all.”

: “Another interpretation: this is Joseph the Righteous, for Joseph’s coffin traveled beside it. Why ‘merchant,’ rokhel? Because he reported his brothers’ conduct to his father. Another explanation: just as a shopkeeper holds bundles of spices and fragrant powders, Joseph sustains Torah because he fulfilled it. All the Torah’s commandments are bound to guarding the holy covenant.”

: “‘Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.’ The companions explained this verse. Dominion is Abraham: ‘You are a prince of God among us,’ and ‘I shall bless you and magnify your name.’ Fear is Isaac: ‘The Fear of Isaac was mine.’ ‘He makes peace in His heights’ is Jacob: ‘Grant truth to Jacob,’ and ‘Love truth and peace.’ Truth and peace are bound to one another. Therefore he is the perfection of everything.”
: “'All My plagues': from here we learn that the plague of the firstborn is equivalent to all the plagues.”

: “Why does Scripture say “when it gores” concerning a person, but “when it strikes” concerning an animal? Concerning a person, who possesses mazal, it says “when it gores”; concerning an animal, which lacks mazal, it says “when it strikes.” In passing, Scripture also teaches that an ox established as dangerous to people is established as dangerous to animals; one established as dangerous to animals is not thereby established as dangerous to people.”
Commentary: Rashi on Bava Kamma 2b:12:1: ““A person, who possesses mazal”: he has the understanding to protect his own body.”
: ““Pushing”: It pushed with its body and caused damage intentionally.”

: ““The Lord strengthened Pharaoh’s heart.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that he had not turned back after the first five plagues, from then onward the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Even if he wishes to repent, I shall strengthen his heart so that I may exact the entire judgment from him, “as the Lord had spoken to Moses,” for it is written, “I shall harden Pharaoh’s heart.””
: “What does “the call of the gever” mean? Rav says: A man calls. R. Sheila says: A rooster crows.”

: “Rav Yehuda said: Kaat is the kuk; raham is the sherakrak. Rabbi Yohanan said: Why is it called raham? When the raham arrives, mercy comes to the world. Rav Bibi bar Abaye said: This applies when it sits on something and makes the call sherakrak. We have a tradition that if it sits on the ground and whistles, the Messiah has come, as it says, “I will whistle to them and gather them.” Rav Adda bar Shimi said to Mar bar Rav Iddai: But one sat in a plowed field and whistled, and a clod struck it on the head! He answered: That one was a liar.”

: ““Mercy”: Rain. “On something”: On any object. “It makes the call sherakrak”: When it chirps, it sounds as though it says sherakrak. “If it sits on the ground”: It does not stand but sits and chirps; this is a sign of good tidings. “On the ground”: That is not its usual manner. “In a plowed field”: A plowed area. “A clod”: A stone rolled down from above. “A liar”: Related to “he invented it”; it was a liar and false speaker, and was therefore struck.”

: “Afarsemon is the upper palace, concealed and hidden. Appiryon is the lower palace, which has no support until supported from within the upper palace. Therefore the letter samekh is closed on all its sides, like the closed letter samekh—an alternative reading has mem.”

: “Rabbi Yochanan said: Why is the letter nun absent from Ashrei? Because it alludes to Israel’s downfall, as it says, “Fallen, she shall not rise again, the virgin of Israel.” In the Land of Israel they resolve the verse by reading it: “She has fallen and shall fall no more; rise, virgin of Israel.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Even so, David returned and gave them support through the holy spirit, as it says, “Hashem supports all who fall.””

: “The letter samekh entered and said: ‘Master of the worlds, may it please You to create the world through me, for I contain support for the fallen: “The Lord supports all who fall.”’ He answered: ‘For precisely that reason you are needed in your place and must not move. If you left your place, what would become of the fallen, who depend upon you?’ She immediately departed from before Him.”

: “Rav Nahman said to R. Isaac: Have you heard when Bar Nafli will come? He asked: Who is Bar Nafli? He answered: The Messiah. Do you call the Messiah Bar Nafli? He replied: Yes, for it is written, “On that day I will raise the fallen booth of David.””

: “Joel called it “the hidden one,” as it says, “I will remove the hidden one far from you.” The Sages taught: “I will remove the hidden one far from you”—this is the evil inclination, hidden and standing within a person’s heart.”
: “Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children the generation afterward.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, now informed Moses of the plague of locusts and instructed him to tell Pharaoh. Otherwise, what would be the purpose of 'Come to Pharaoh' if Moses were to say nothing to him? Yet the plague is mentioned only in Moses’ words to Pharaoh, because Scripture abbreviated here. Similarly, in the earlier plague of hail, it related God’s words to Moses, 'Stand before Pharaoh and say to him,' but did not mention Moses’ words to Pharaoh at all, as I explained. The reason is that Scripture does not wish to elaborate on both; sometimes it abbreviates one, sometimes the other.”

: “Rav said: Our father Abraham observed the entire Torah, as it says, “Because Abraham listened to My voice,” and so forth. Rav Shimi bar Hiyya said to Rav: Perhaps this means the seven commandments? But there was circumcision as well! Perhaps it means the seven commandments and circumcision? He answered: If so, why does Scripture say, “My commandments and My teachings”? Rav, or according to others Rav Ashi, said: Our father Abraham observed even eruv tavshilin, as it says, “My teachings”—one is the Written Torah and one the Oral Torah.”

: “Rava said: When a young Torah scholar grows heated, it is Torah that heats him, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem?” Rav Ashi said: Any Torah scholar who is not hard as iron is no Torah scholar, as it says, “Like a hammer that shatters rock.” Rabbi Abba said to Rav Ashi: You derive it from there; we derive it from “A land whose stones are iron”—read not “its stones,” but “its builders.” Ravina said: Even so, a person must train himself to be gentle, as it says, “Remove anger from your heart.””

: “The Sages taught: When our teachers entered the vineyard at Yavne, they said: Torah will one day be forgotten in Israel. For it says, “Days are coming, declares the Lord God, when I will send famine into the land—not a famine for bread or thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the Lord”; and, “They will wander from sea to sea, from north to east; they will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it.” “The word of the Lord” means halakha; “the word of the Lord” means the end of exile; “the word of the Lord” means prophecy. A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai says: Heaven forbid that Torah should be forgotten in Israel, for it says, “It will not be forgotten from the mouth of his descendants.” How, then, do I understand “They will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it”? They will not find a clear halakha and a clear Mishnah together in one place.”

: “‘He meditates upon His Torah.’ Rabbi Shimon said: Abraham’s father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys to be like two teachers; they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written, ‘I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.’”

: “Rather, specifically Abraham had to be included in judgment, for previously Abraham contained no judgment at all. Now water was included in fire. Abraham had not been complete until now, when crowned to perform judgment and establish it in its place.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 13, paragraph 1: “‘And with the good wine’ signifies the holiness of the Oral Torah, ‘the wine I have mixed.’ It is the dew of the Ancient One, as Scripture says, ‘May my speech flow like dew.’ With dew, one cannot discern how it descends from heaven; one knows it only from the moisture visible on the earth. So too with the Oral Torah: although the sages speak it in their own words, it is truly what shines from heaven into their hearts.”

: “Then it is written, ‘The Lord said to Moses, Why do you cry to Me?’ Sifra DiTzeniuta teaches: ‘to Me’ is precise; everything depends upon the Ancient One. At that moment the Holy Ancient One was revealed, favor was present throughout all the upper worlds, and the light of everything shone.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak taught: ‘A mother of children rejoicing, hallelujah.’ The Mother is known; who are the children? Rabbi Shimon said: we learned that God has two children, male and female. He gave the male to Jacob: ‘My firstborn son, Israel,’ and ‘Israel, in whom I glory.’ The daughter He gave to Abraham: ‘The Lord blessed Abraham with All.’ Abraham had a daughter named Bakol.”
: ““He said: See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.” Rav Yehuda son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said in Rav’s name: Like the fragrance of an apple orchard.”

: “Another interpretation: This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him the Temple built, destroyed, and rebuilt. ‘See, my son’s fragrance’ signifies its being built, as it says, ‘You shall take care to offer My pleasing fragrance.’ ‘Like the fragrance of a field’ signifies its destruction, as it says, ‘Zion shall be plowed as a field.’ ‘Which the Lord has blessed’ signifies its being built and perfected in the future, as it says, ‘For there the Lord commanded the blessing: life forever.’”

: “Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said: What is meant by “Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest”? Why is Israel compared to an apple tree? To tell you: Just as this apple tree puts its fruit before its leaves, so Israel put “We will do” before “We will hear.””

: “Rather, not like Abraham, of whom “mountain” is written, as it says, “As it is said today: On Hashem’s mountain He will be seen”; and not like Isaac, of whom “field” is written, as it says, “Isaac went out to converse in the field”; but like Jacob, who called it a “house,” as it says, “He called the name of that place Bethel.””

: “Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: Both brothers took land, and both took movable property. What, then, was their dispute? One said, ‘The Temple will be built in my territory,’ and the other said, ‘The Temple will be built in my territory.’ For it says, ‘When they were in the field,’ and ‘field’ means the Temple, as it says, ‘Zion shall be plowed as a field.’ Because of this, ‘Cain rose against Abel his brother.’”
: “Blessing comes from Zion, as it says, “May the Lord bless you from Zion.””

: “It was called Shetiyah. It was taught: The world was founded from it. Our Mishnah follows the opinion that the world was created from Zion, for it was taught: R. Eliezer says: The world was created from its center, as it says, “When the dust was poured into a solid mass and clods adhered together.””

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: how did Abraham enter the cave? He was pursuing that calf, as it says, ‘Abraham ran to the herd.’ The calf fled to that cave; Abraham entered after it and saw what he saw. Moreover, because he prayed every day, he would go out to that field, which gave off sublime fragrances. He saw light issuing from the cave and prayed there, and there the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with him. Therefore he wanted it, for his desire was always for that place.”

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

: “Rav Kahana said: What is meant by “For He spoke, and it came to be”? This refers to a wife. “He commanded, and it stood”—this refers to children. It was taught: A woman is a skin-bag filled with excrement, and her mouth is filled with blood; yet everyone pursues her.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: The loss of purity took away taste and fragrance; the neglect of tithes took away the richness of grain. The Sages say: Sexual immorality and sorcery have destroyed everything.”

Commentary: Rashi on Sotah 49a:9:1–2: ““Purity”—which ceased among Israel. “Took away taste”—the taste and fragrance of the fruit. When they were pure and observed purity, God likewise purified their fruit of bad fragrance and bad taste.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Whoever says that David sinned is mistaken, for it says, “David acted wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.” Could a sin have come into his hands while the Divine Presence remained with him? How, then, do I understand “Why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil”? He sought to do it, but did not do it. Rav said: Rabbi, who descended from David, interprets the passage in David’s favor. “Why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil”—Rabbi says: This evil differs from all the evils described in the Torah. Everywhere else it says, “He did”; here it says, “To do,” meaning that he sought to do it but did not. “You struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword”—you should have tried him before the Sanhedrin, but did not. “You took his wife as your wife”—you had the right to marry her. For Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Anyone going out to the wars of David’s house wrote a bill of divorce for his wife. It says, “Bring these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand; inquire after your brothers’ welfare, and take their pledges.” What are “their pledges”? Rav Yosef taught: The matters connecting husband and wife. “You killed him by the sword of the Ammonites”—just as you are not punished for the Ammonites’ sword, so you are not punished for Uriah the Hittite. Why? He was a rebel against the monarchy, for he said to David, “My lord Joab and my lord’s servants are camped in th
: “David called it “impure,” as it says, “Create a pure heart for me, God,” implying the presence of an impure heart.”

: “This may be explained through 'He will sense through fear of the Lord,' and concerning Joseph, 'I fear God.' Thus the Gemara says, 'The mandrakes give fragrance' refers to Israel’s young men who have never tasted sin. The expression 'Israel’s young men' appears to concern this blemish, which youth causes. Likewise, in Sotah: 'I smell the fragrance of chanunita'; he told him, 'My son, you possess purity.' This too follows 'He will sense through fear of the Lord' and 'Fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.' A complete sense of smell indicates fear and purity; therefore 'The mandrakes give fragrance' is said of those pure from this blemish.”

: “On the sixth day, corresponding to the righteous one, the foundation of the world, God created the human being, who was created circumcised. The Gemara says, 'He drew out his foreskin': through the serpent’s blemish his foreskin was drawn out, and he and all his descendants became uncircumcised. It follows that he was created circumcised. He was the righteous one, the foundation of the world, for whose sake the world was created, as in Yoma 38 b; he is the single pillar called Righteous in Chagigah 12 b. This is the attribute called All, joining heaven and earth. After the serpent’s corruption through desire for eating, its introduction of impurity into Eve, and the resulting blemish of the 130 years, the month of Shevat was formed through the letter tzadi in eating, to rectify the root of the corruption.”
: “Abraham instituted the morning prayer, as it says, “Abraham arose early in the morning, to the place where he had stood.” “Standing” means prayer, as it says, “Pinchas stood and prayed.””

: “‘Ephron’s field arose’: it had been lowly and was elevated; it had belonged to an insignificant man and became the possession of a great man. ‘Ephron’s field, which was in Machpelah’: this teaches that it was doubled in everyone’s estimation, for anyone buried within it is assured that his reward is doubled and redoubled.”
: “The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, to consecrate him as most holy, he and his sons forever: to burn incense before Hashem, serve Him, and bless in His name forever.”

: “Resh Lakish said: It is derived from “Your temple is like a slice of pomegranate”—even the empty ones among you are filled with commandments like a pomegranate. R. Zeira said: It is derived from “He smelled the fragrance of his garments.” Do not read begadav, “his garments,” but bogedav, “his betrayers.””

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

: “‘I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan’—because they were circumcised. Whoever is circumcised inherits the land, for only the righteous one inherits the land, and whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Thus ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. Look at Joseph: throughout his days he was not called righteous until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous: Joseph the Righteous.”

: “Afarsemon is the upper palace, concealed and hidden. Appiryon is the lower palace, which has no support until supported from within the upper palace. Therefore the letter samekh is closed on all its sides, like the closed letter samekh—an alternative reading has mem.”

: “At that time, while the cave was under Ephron’s ownership, it did not yet possess holiness. Thus the Zohar says that “upper fragrances arose,” for the reason explained, but does not add “holy.” Later Abraham purchased the field and cave, as it says, “Ephron’s field arose.” The Midrash explains that it had been fallen and now arose. The Zohar says that nothing was revealed to Ephron: he saw only darkness. “It arose” means that it truly gained an elevation. Once it was under Abraham’s ownership, the Zohar says of Isaac’s entrance into the cave that “he saw the Divine Presence upon it, and upper, holy fragrances arose.” Holiness is now mentioned, although it was not mentioned when Abraham entered the cave. Wherever holiness is present, blessing is present.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””
Commentary: Rashi on Taanit 8b:12:2: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak taught: ‘To behold the Lord’s pleasantness and visit His palace.’ This is what the righteous long to see, yet you said ‘above the Lord’? Rabbi Shimon answered: all is one. ‘The Lord’s pleasantness’ indicates that it comes from the Holy Ancient One to this Heaven. This is certainly the righteous ones’ desire. Above Heaven it says, ‘Then you shall delight above the Lord.’ Happy is one who merits it; certainly they are few.”

: “‘Remember’ pertains to the male, ‘guard’ to the female, without separation. Shabbat’s day is the mystery of all faith, depending from the highest head to the end of every level. Shabbat is everything.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, is included from the upper place, concealed beyond all concealment, in a hundred—the secret of the hundred blessings each day. So too the twenty years. Therefore the singular ‘year’ is written, expressing the union in which Thought and Jubilee never separate. The seven years are differentiated, emerging from the concealed whole above. Although all is a single unity, they are differentiated in judgment and mercy through many sides and paths, unlike what is above. Hence the singular ‘year’ expresses the union that never separates. The seven years are differentiated in judgment and mercy through many sides and paths, unlike what is above. Therefore these seven are called ‘years,’ not ‘year.’ All are called life: ‘These were Sarah’s lives,’ truly created and established above.”

: “All sanctifications above rest in this place and issue from it to the Congregation of Israel, giving her delights, bread of pleasure. Thus it is written, ‘From Asher his bread is rich, and he gives royal delicacies.’ ‘From Asher’ is the complete covenant: what had been bread of poverty becomes bread of delight. ‘He gives royal delicacies’: who is the king? The Congregation of Israel. He gives all the worlds’ delights, and every sanctification flowing from above proceeds from this place. Hence ‘He sanctified it’: that sign of the covenant.”

: “The Gemara teaches that the loss of purity took away taste and fragrance, and there it asks, “My son, do you possess purity?” Purity concerns this matter. Thus, although King David had not sinned, since a sin in this area was recorded and attached to him, he said, “Create a pure heart for me.” The Sages say, “David called it impure,” and he asked Hashem to create a pure heart for him. The young men of Israel who remain free of this blemish give forth a good fragrance.”

quote: Commentary: Rashi on Sotah 49a, s.v. Taharah and Bitelah ta’am: ““Purity”—meaning that it had ceased among Israel. “It abolished taste”—the taste and fragrance of fruit. While they were pure and observed purity, the Holy One likewise kept their fruit free of bad fragrance and bad taste.”

: “Rabbi Elazar said: By the light the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the first day, a person could see from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One, blessed be He, looked upon the generations of the Flood and the Dispersion and saw their corrupt deeds, He concealed it from them, as it says, “Their light is withheld from the wicked.” For whom did He conceal it? For the righteous in the future, as it says, “God saw the light, that it was good.” “Good” means the righteous, as it says, “Say of the righteous that it is good.” On seeing the light reserved for the righteous, He rejoiced, as it says, “The light of the righteous rejoices.””

: “Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: I too say that not everyone attains light, and not everyone attains joy. The righteous attain light, and the upright attain joy. The righteous attain light, as it says, “Light is sown for the righteous”; the upright attain joy, as it says, “And joy for the upright of heart.””

: “This Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, is neither mentioned nor found. Being the head above all the highest, He is mentioned only as a single head without a body, sustaining everything.”

: “Rava said: Length of life, children, and livelihood depend on mazal rather than merit. After all, Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous sages: when either prayed, rain came. Yet Rav Chisda lived ninety-two years, while Rabbah lived forty. Rav Chisda’s household celebrated sixty weddings; Rabbah’s suffered sixty bereavements. At Rav Chisda’s house, fine flour was available even for the dogs, and they did not want it. At Rabbah’s house, there was not even enough barley bread for the people.”

: “It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. No word of Torah, nor even a small letter, fails to allude to upper Wisdom; heaps upon heaps of its secrets depend on each, as in ‘His locks are curled in heaps.’”

: “All blessings mean life, children, and sustenance, which depend not upon merit but upon mazal, as Moed Katan 28 states. The holy mazal is Atika, above the Lord, as in 'Cast your burden above Havayah,' and 'Hannah prayed above Havayah'—above, specifically, as the Zohar explains. This is alluded to in the yod’s upper tip, which indicates Nothing, the supernal crown. 'Above the Lord' therefore means above the Name’s four letters. These blessings were entrusted to the level of kingship, for the supernal crown is the crown of kingship.”
: “He reveals deep and hidden things. He knows what is in darkness, and light dwells with Him.”
: “Woe to those who go deep to hide their plans from Hashem! Their deeds are done in darkness, and they say, “Who sees us, and who knows us?””
: “He sent darkness, and it grew dark; they did not rebel against His word.”

: ““The Lord said to Moses: Stretch your hand toward heaven.” This is what Scripture says: “He sent darkness and made it dark, and they did not defy His word.” Our Rabbis said: It was because they had not accepted the authority of the word of the Holy One, blessed be He, over themselves.”

: “All ten plagues were measure for measure. Blood: why did He bring blood upon Egypt? Because they would not allow the daughters of Israel to immerse and become pure from their impurity, so that Israel would not have children and multiply.”

: ““The Lord strengthened Pharaoh’s heart.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that he had not turned back after the first five plagues, from then onward the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Even if he wishes to repent, I shall strengthen his heart so that I may exact the entire judgment from him, “as the Lord had spoken to Moses,” for it is written, “I shall harden Pharaoh’s heart.””

: “Our Rabbis said: Israel did not wish to circumcise themselves in Egypt; they all abandoned circumcision there except the tribe of Levi, as it says, “Of Levi he said: Your sacred lots and Your Urim…” Why? “For they guarded Your word and preserved Your covenant”—in Egypt. The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to redeem them, but they had no merit. What did He do? He called Moses and told him: Go and circumcise them. Some say Joshua was there and circumcised them, as it says, “Again circumcise the children of Israel a second time.” Many would not accept circumcision. The Holy One, blessed be He, commanded that they prepare the Passover offering. When Moses prepared it, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the four winds of the world, which blow in the Garden of Eden; winds from the Garden went and attached themselves to that offering, as it says, “Awake, north wind; come, south wind.” Its fragrance traveled a forty-day journey. All Israel gathered to Moses and begged: Feed us from your Passover offering! For they were faint from its fragrance. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If you are not circumcised, you may not eat, as it says, “The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: This is the statute of the Passover…” They immediately submitted and were circumcised. The Passover blood mingled with the circumcision blood. The Holy One, blessed be He, passed by, took each one, kissed him, and blessed him, as it says, “I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood…” Live through the Pa

: “This is what a heretic said to R. Abbahu: When will the Messiah come? He answered: When darkness covers those people. The man asked: Are you cursing me? He answered: A verse states it: “Darkness will cover the earth and thick gloom the peoples, but Hashem will shine upon you, and His glory will appear over you.””
: “For darkness will cover the earth and thick gloom the peoples, but Hashem will shine upon you, and His glory will appear over you.”

: “The other interpretation is that David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, am I not devoted to You? All the kings of east and west sit among their companies in honor, while my hands are soiled with blood, fetal tissue, and placenta in order to permit a woman to her husband. Moreover, I consult Mephibosheth my teacher about everything I do, asking: ‘Mephibosheth my teacher, did I judge correctly? Did I rightly impose liability, grant exemption, declare purity, declare impurity?’ And I was not ashamed.””

: “Rava expounded: What is meant by “Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field, let us lodge in the villages; let us rise early to the vineyards, see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the grape buds have opened and the pomegranates flowered; there I will give you my love”? “Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, do not judge me like city dwellers among whom there are robbery, sexual transgressions, vain oaths, and false oaths. “Let us go out to the field”—come, and I will show You Torah scholars who study in hardship. “Let us lodge in the villages”—read “among the deniers”: Come, and I will show You those upon whom You bestowed goodness, yet they denied You. “Let us rise early to the vineyards”—these are synagogues and study halls. “See whether the vine has blossomed”—these are masters of Scripture. “Whether the grape buds have opened”—these are masters of Mishnah. “Whether the pomegranates have flowered”—these are masters of Gemara. “There I will give You my love”—I will show You my honor, my greatness, and the excellence of my sons and daughters.”

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

: “Rabbi Zeira found Rav Yehuda standing at the entrance of his father-in-law’s house.
