He saw that Rav Yehuda was in a cheerful frame of mind, so that if asked about all the world’s hidden matters he would answer. He asked him: Why do goats walk first, followed by sheep? He answered: It is like the world’s creation, in which darkness came first and light afterward.”

: ““They lent to them.” Rabbi Ami said: This teaches that they lent against their will. Some say against the Egyptians’ will; others say against Israel’s will. The first view derives this from, “The household-dweller shall divide the spoil.” The view that it was against Israel’s will explains that the goods were a burden to carry.”

: “The Rabbis said: “God saw”—the intermediate people had repented, and even the wicked had considered repentance, as it is written, “The fig tree has formed its early figs.” “God knew”—even one person did not know about another; only the Holy One, blessed be He, knew. This one directed his heart, and that one directed his heart, and they repented. Yet even though they repented, they would not have left there without the merit of the patriarchs, because the attribute of justice accused them over the calf they would eventually make.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai says: It is neither a day nor Gehinnom, but a fire issuing from the bodies of the wicked themselves that burns them. What is the basis? It is written, ‘You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your own spirit is a fire that shall consume you.’”

: “Further, there is another secret. One must welcome the Mistress on Shabbat with many lamplights, many delights, beautiful clothes, a prepared house and fine furnishings, with a lovely setting for everyone. Through this joy and adornment, the wicked maidservant is left in darkness, hunger, weeping and lamentation, dressed in black like a widow. For when this one is full, that one is desolate.”

: “Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: This is like a king who built a palace, saw it, and was pleased with it. He said, ‘Palace, palace, may you always find favor in my eyes as you have at this moment!’ So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to His world: ‘My world, My world, may you always find favor before Me as you have at this moment!’”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: “‘The goat shall bear upon itself’ refers to Esau, as it says, ‘Esau my brother is a hairy man.’ ‘All their iniquities,’ avonotam, can be read as ‘the iniquities of the blameless man,’ avonot tam, as it says, ‘Jacob was a blameless man.’”

: “Rav Hisda said: Binding one item is not considered a bundle; three items are considered a bundle; two are disputed by R. Yosei and the Sages. For we learned: The required hyssop consists of three stalks with three branches. R. Yosei says: The required hyssop consists of three branches; its remnant may be two, and its stumps may be any size.”

: “These three shells stand opposite the three patriarchs in holiness. Abraham our father brings all loves into holiness; Isaac brings the powers of severity into holiness. One stands opposite the other: the right of one faces the other’s left, so jealousy precedes desire. Honor stands opposite Jacob the small, as in 'I am small' and 'Who will raise Jacob, for he is small?' These correspond to the three elements, alef-mem-shin. Haughtiness comes from the element of elevated spirit; these are wicked Balaam’s three qualities, wishing to rise higher and higher like fire’s nature. In holiness, however, the spirit is lowly. Through this one is also saved from desire.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: I see that Wisdom encompasses everything. Upper Kindness proceeds from Wisdom; Might, harsh judgment, proceeds from Binah. Jacob completes both sides. The patriarchs encompass everything, and Jacob encompasses the patriarchs.”

: “Certainly the teaching that a person should recall the day of death is correct, for it breaks his heart. The evil inclination rests only where there is wine’s merriment and arrogance. When a broken spirit is present, it departs and does not remain with him. He must therefore recall the day of death, humbling his body, and the inclination goes away.”

: “Akavya ben Mahalalel says: Consider three things and you will not come to sin. Know where you came from, where you are going, and before whom you will have to give judgment and account. Where did you come from? A putrid drop. Where are you going? To a place of dust, maggots, and worms. Before whom will you give judgment and account? Before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, “Be stirred, and do not sin.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “Speak in your hearts.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recite Shema, as it says, “Upon your beds.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recall the day of death, as it says, “And be silent, selah.””

: “What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.”

: “The tenth commandment: ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat.’ The Shekhinah is called Shabbat from the side of the three upper levels: shin, with three crowns—Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. She is bat, daughter, the fourth with them. The six days, from Chesed through Yesod, are those in which work is done, for building begins with Chesed, as in ‘The world is built through kindness.’ From Binah upward, however, there is rest, delight and cessation from all work.”
: “Thus says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place could be My resting place?”
: “My hand made all these things, and all these things came to be, declares Hashem. But to this one I look: the poor and crushed in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

: “‘Let no one leave his place on the seventh day.’ We learned: ‘his place’ is the place within which he is fit to walk. Its secret is ‘Blessed is the Lord’s glory from His place’: this is the Place. This is also the secret of ‘The place upon which you stand is holy ground.’ We call that known site ‘Place,’ where the upper glory becomes known.”

: “Where are these four cubits written? A baraita teaches: “Let each man remain beneath himself”—an area corresponding to what lies beneath him. His body occupies three cubits, with another cubit to stretch out his hands and feet: Rabbi Meir’s view. Rabbi Yehuda says: His body occupies three cubits, with another cubit so that he can take an object from beneath his feet and place it beneath his head. What is the difference between them? Whether the four cubits are measured precisely.”

: “The reason the Shabbat boundary is two thousand cubits is that the measure of goodness is five hundred times greater. We find that the opposite extends four cubits, as with a corpse, prostitution, heresy, and a foul odor. Since goodness is five hundred times greater, it acquires two thousand cubits. Jacob therefore merited to inherit the world without measure, and it is written of him, “You shall spread out westward and eastward.” His holiness could extend everywhere, even outside the Land; wherever Israel would be, the holy Divine Presence would be among them. The principal time when the Divine Presence rests within Israel is Shabbat. The Zohar explains, “Let no one leave his place”: the inner meaning is “Blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place.” This is the lower Divine Presence, which rests in the Jewish heart. Tikkunei Zohar says, “Fortunate is one who prepares a trustworthy dwelling for Her in his heart.” This applies on Shabbat. Berakhot teaches that since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One has only the four cubits of halakhah in His world, for there the Divine Presence rests. Our holy master explained that this means a person who overcomes his inclination, refrains from what is forbidden in accordance with halakhah, and accepts the sovereignty of Heaven. This is the essential purpose of halakhah. Such a person makes his heart a dwelling for the Divine Presence. Throughout Shabbat, a person continually refrains from desecrating it, for in a moment one could

: “The rabbinic boundary of two thousand cubits likewise alludes to the holiness of place. Everything occupies its own four cubits—even manifestations of the opposite, such as excrement, the entrance to a prostitute’s house, and a corpse. Since the measure of goodness is five hundred times greater, the holiness of a place extends two thousand cubits: five hundred times the four cubits occupied by the opposite. Thus Jacob’s encampment is described as expressing the holiness of Israel’s camp, for Israel’s holiness had already become permanently established in him. He therefore inherited the world without limit: he could sanctify even a place outside the Land with the holiness of the Land of Israel, just as every place where Israel encamps becomes sanctified. Scripture states this explicitly of Jacob, indicating that this holiness is established forever.”
: “I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood. I said to you, “In your blood, live!” I said to you, “In your blood, live!””

: ““You shall dip in the blood in the basin.” Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, protect them through blood? To remember for them the blood of Abraham’s circumcision. Israel was saved from Egypt through two bloods: the blood of the Passover offering and the blood of circumcision, as it says, “I said to you: In your blood, live! I said to you: In your blood, live!”—through the blood of Passover and the blood of circumcision.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 5, paragraph 1: “Nevertheless, in chronological order matzah came first. On the very first night of Passover, they merited, from God’s side, the complete removal of the evil inclination from the heart, as it says, ‘In the evening you shall eat matzot.’ At that time, however, the prohibition of leaven applied for only one day, as stated in Pesachim 96b; afterward the evil inclination returned to its place. At the splitting of the sea, ‘the waters were a wall for them’ is written defectively, indicating anger: there was an accusation against Israel, as the Mekhilta explains, and Samael protested, ‘For these You split the sea?’ Subsequently, through the bitterness they merited becoming mighty in conquering their inclination, as it says, ‘The people feared the Lord.’ Through this they attained the level at which a maidservant at the sea saw what Ezekiel did not see. Even so, the light was again concealed, as it says, ‘They came to Marah,’ and as the Zohar explains concerning the wilderness of Shur. Yet the bitterness accomplished its purpose: through it they later merited the giving of the Torah. The Gemara likewise says that Torah was attained through suffering. This was the ultimate purpose of the bitterness, and this is the meaning of ‘they shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs.’”

: “The head of the court says, “Sanctified,” and all the people respond, “Sanctified, sanctified.” Whether the new moon was seen at its proper time or later, they sanctify the month. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says: If it was not seen at its proper time, they do not sanctify it, because Heaven has already sanctified it. The Gemara asks: From where is the head of the court’s declaration derived? Rabbi Chiyya bar Gamda said in Rabbi Yose ben Shaul’s name, in Rabbi’s name: Scripture says, “Moses declared the appointed times of the Lord”; this teaches that the head of the court says, “Sanctified.” From where is the people’s response derived? Rav Pappa said: “Which you shall proclaim”—read it as “you yourselves.” Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: “These are My appointed times”—they shall declare My appointed times. Why say “Sanctified” twice? Because it is written, “Holy convocations,” in the plural.”

: “If an ordinary vessel becomes holy when filled with something sacred, how much more so Israel, who are holy and sanctify the month! The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am holy, and I sanctify Myself. Rather, I sanctify Israel, and they sanctify Me. Therefore it is written, “You shall be holy to Me,” and, “For I, the Lord who sanctifies you, am holy.” David likewise says, “You are holy, enthroned upon Israel’s praises.” When did Israel begin sanctifying the month? In Egypt, as it is written, “This month shall be yours.””

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

Parallel: Divrei Soferim 16: “The entire building of the Israelite nation took place after complete despair: ‘Abraham and Sarah were old,’ and ‘Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children?’ No one any longer imagined believing this, even after the angel’s promise. Righteous Sarah knew and believed that God can do everything; nevertheless she laughed inwardly. Knowing Abraham’s old age—as Bereishit Rabbah describes, he could no longer emit seed—and her own old age, she found it remote from belief. Had God wished to grant them a child, He could have done so earlier, since it is preferable to minimize a miracle and He does not perform a miracle unnecessarily. In truth, however, this came from God: the nation was to be built specifically after complete despair, when no one, not even Sarah, believed that she would yet be remembered. This is the very character of an Israelite: to believe that one must never despair, for God can always help. ‘Is anything beyond the Lord?’ One should not investigate why God arranged matters this way. Likewise, concerning the future deliverance it says, ‘Who believed our report?’ The Sages say that the son of David will not come until people despair of redemption. Therefore Scripture says, ‘Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who gave you birth’: your own beginning, too, came after despair.”
: “Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chalafta said: All the kingdoms are called by the name ‘Egypt,’ because they bring distress upon Israel.”

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”
: “'The people bowed': for the news of redemption, of entering the Land, and of the children they would have.”

: ““When your children say to you: What is this service to you?” “When your children say to you”—Israel received bad tidings at that moment: eventually Torah would be forgotten. Some say Israel received good tidings at that moment: they would live to see children and grandchildren, as it says, “You shall say: It is a Passover sacrifice to the Lord, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when He struck Egypt and rescued our houses. The people bowed and prostrated themselves.” Why did they prostrate themselves? Because it is said, “The children of Israel went up armed”—one in five; some say one in fifty, and some say one in five hundred went up.”

: “It happened that Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus’s brothers were plowing on level ground while he was plowing on a hillside. His cow fell and was injured. He said, ‘It is for my good that my cow was injured.’ He fled and went to Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai. He ate clods of earth until his mouth developed a foul odor. People went and told Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai that Rabbi Eliezer was suffering from foul breath. He told him: ‘Just as your mouth has become foul for the sake of Torah, so the fragrance of your learning shall spread from one end of the world to the other.’”

: “But when an Israelite prays before You in this house, ‘Give each person according to all his ways, for You know his heart; You alone know the heart of every human being.’ If he asks for children, and You know they will anger You, do not give them to him. Likewise, if he asks for possessions and You know that he will rebel through them, do not give them to him. But for a foreigner, ‘Do according to all that the foreigner calls to You for, so that they may know.’”

: “What does “You shall die and shall not live” mean? “You shall die”—in this world; “you shall not live”—in the World to Come. Hezekiah asked Isaiah: “Why so severe a judgment?” He answered: “Because you did not engage in procreation.” Hezekiah said: “Because I foresaw through the holy spirit that unworthy sons would descend from me.” Isaiah answered: “What business have you with the Merciful One’s hidden matters? You must do what you were commanded, and let the Holy One, blessed be He, do what pleases Him.””

: “Those who expound the scriptural records used to say: All of them enter the World to Come, as it says, “Gilead is Mine and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is the stronghold of My head, Judah My lawgiver. Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I cast My shoe; over Philistia I shout in triumph.” “Gilead is Mine” refers to Ahab, who fell at Ramoth-gilead. “Manasseh” means Manasseh himself.”

: “Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and Hashem your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore Hashem your God commanded you to observe the Shabbat day.”
: “For in six days Hashem made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu said: This is like a king who purchased two servants in a single deed of sale and for the same price. He decreed that one should be maintained from the treasury, while the other should work to obtain his food. The latter sat bewildered and said, ‘We were both bought in one deed and for the same price. This one is maintained from the treasury, while if I do not work, I cannot eat!’ So the earth sat bewildered and said, ‘The upper beings and the lower beings were created together. The upper beings are sustained by the radiance of the Divine Presence, while the lower beings cannot eat unless they work.’”

: “R. Judah ben Teima used to say: Adam reclined in the Garden of Eden, and the ministering angels roasted meat for him and strained wine for him. The snake peered at him, saw his honor, and became jealous of him.”
: “For a human being is born to toil, just as sparks rise upward in flight.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, does likewise for a person created from the four elements. When he returns in repentance and occupies himself with Torah, God takes him out from there. Of this it says, ‘From there it separates’: he separates himself from their desire, and God places him in His garden, the Shekhinah, ‘to work it’ through positive commandments and ‘to guard it’ through prohibitions. If he merits guarding her, he becomes head over the four elements, becoming the river through which they are watered, rather than through another. They recognize him as their master and ruler.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Have you ever seen a wild animal or bird with a trade? Yet they are sustained without distress. They were created only to serve me, and I was created to serve my Maker. Does it not follow that I should be sustained without distress? But I worsened my deeds and damaged my livelihood.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya, Rabbi Chiyya, and the sages there said in Rabbi Yehudah’s name: No day passes without the Holy One, blessed be He, originating a halakhah in the heavenly court. What is the scriptural basis? ‘Listen closely to the trembling of His voice and the utterance that issues from His mouth.’ ‘Utterance’ means Torah, as it says, ‘You shall meditate upon it day and night.’ Abraham knew even those halakhot.”

: “Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Chanina’s name: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it says, “All your children are taught by Hashem, and abundant is your children’s peace.” Read “your builders” in place of “your children.””

: “For we learned: Rabbi Yose says: On the garments of builders, a stain on one side is an obstruction to immersion; on an ordinary person’s garments, it is an obstruction only when it penetrates both sides. A saddlecloth should not be more important than an ordinary person’s garment. Who are these “builders”? Rabbi Yohanan said: They are Torah scholars, who devote all their days to building the world.”

k: volume-i|715|0|R. Chaim of Volozhin, Nefesh HaChayim IV
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim of Volozhin, Nefesh HaChayim IV 11:6–8: “Once the Torah descended, as it were, from its hidden root into this world—as the Sages say, Moses came and brought it down to earth—the life and continued existence of all the worlds depend solely on the breath of our mouths and our meditation upon it. It is unquestionably true that if the entire world, from end to end, were wholly empty, even for one actual moment, of our engagement in Torah and reflection upon it, all the upper and lower worlds would instantly be destroyed and become nothingness and chaos, God forbid. The abundance or diminution of their light likewise depends entirely on the character and extent of our engagement in Torah. Therefore we bless God for having “planted eternal life within us.” A planting is planted to produce fruit and increase goodness. Similarly, when we hold firmly to the holy Torah with all our strength, as we should, we impart enduring life and draw from its hidden root, above all the worlds, additional holiness, blessing, and great light into every world. Thus Midrash Mishlei explains “Guard your heart above all else”: do not flee from Torah. Why? “For from it flow the outgoings of life”—teaching that life goes forth into the world from words of Torah.”

: “R. Joshua ben Levi said: To what do these twenty-six expressions of thanksgiving correspond? They correspond to the twenty-six generations the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world before giving them the Torah, sustaining them through His kindness.”

: “Give thanks to Hashem, for He is good, for His kindness lasts forever. Give thanks to the God of gods, for His kindness lasts forever. Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who alone performs great wonders, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who made the heavens with understanding, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who spread the earth over the waters, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who made the great lights, for His kindness lasts forever. The sun to rule by day, for His kindness lasts forever. The moon and stars to rule by night, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who struck Egypt through its firstborn, for His kindness lasts forever. And brought Israel out from their midst, for His kindness lasts forever. With a strong hand and an outstretched arm, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who divided the Sea of Reeds into divisions, for His kindness lasts forever. And brought Israel through its midst, for His kindness lasts forever. But shook Pharaoh and his army into the Sea of Reeds, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who led His people through the wilderness, for His kindness lasts forever. To Him who struck great kings, for His kindness lasts forever. And killed mighty kings, for His kindness lasts forever. Sihon, king of the Amorites, for His kindness lasts forever. And Og, king of Bashan, for His kindness lasts forever. And gave their land as an inheritance, for His kindness lasts forever. An inheritance to

: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Every day a heavenly voice comes forth from Mount Horeb and declares: “The whole world is sustained for the sake of My son Chanina, yet My son Chanina is satisfied with one kav of carobs from one Shabbat eve to the next.””
: ““A heavenly voice goes forth and says: The whole world”—the words “from Mount Horeb” are not part of our reading.”

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth”—would that He fix Torah study in our hearts as before! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it says, “I shall put My Torah within them and write it upon their hearts.” Rabbi Nechemya said: When Israel heard “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us—“You speak with us, and we shall hear”; “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” The evil inclination immediately returned to its place. They returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth!” He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it is written, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.””

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

: “Rabbi Haggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahman’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for eating and drinking. Because the mouth takes pleasure in its utterance, they permitted a person to occupy himself with words of Torah on them. Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Hiyya bar Ba’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for occupying oneself with words of Torah. A baraita supports each view: What does one do? Either sit and eat, or sit and occupy oneself with words of Torah. One verse says, “It is a Sabbath to the Lord,” and another says, “An assembly to the Lord your God.” How are they fulfilled? Give a portion to Torah study and a portion to eating and drinking.”

k: volume-i|721|2|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:4: ““Because this mouth blossoms”: This uses the expression “It will blossom and flower.” The meaning is that, because a person enjoys the breath issuing from his mouth, they permitted him to occupy himself with words of Torah on Shabbat and festivals, which were originally given only for delight through eating and drinking.”

k: volume-i|721|3|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:7: ““One verse says”: This is another baraita. It should read: One verse says, “An assembly to the Lord your God,” and another says, “An assembly shall be for you.” How can both be fulfilled? Divide the day. This supports Rabbi Berekhya, because one must in any event occupy oneself with words of Torah, while also giving a portion to eating and drinking, to fulfill “for you.””

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “Pesikta records a dispute: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says Sabbaths were given only for delight, while Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman says for Torah study. It explains that they do not disagree: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman addresses laborers, and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba addresses scholars. The explanation is that Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman was a master of aggadah, as stated in various places, and aggadah was delivered before the masses. Thus Moed Katan 17 notes that he had not come to the academy for years. Those immersed in worldly affairs throughout the weekdays find their Shabbat delight in Torah study. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, however, occupied himself with halakhic teaching; Sotah 40 explains that everyone left him because the masses desire aggadah. He therefore spoke to the scholars with whom he studied in the academy; for them, the main purpose is delight. This does not mean eating, drinking, and bodily pleasure.”
: “When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech, Judah became His sanctuary and Israel His dominion.”
: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: All your brothers will be called by your name. A person does not say, ‘I am a Reubenite,’ or ‘I am a Simeonite,’ but ‘I am a Jew,’ a Yehudi.”

: ““Let Reuben live and not die, and let his men be counted—and this for Judah.” Throughout Israel’s forty years in the wilderness, Judah’s bones rolled loose in his coffin, until Moses came and pleaded for mercy: “Master of the world, who caused Reuben to confess? Judah!” Immediately, “Hear, Hashem, Judah’s voice”—his limbs returned to their joints. They would not admit him to the heavenly academy: “Bring him to his people.” He did not understand what the Sages were saying or join their deliberations: “May his hands contend for him.” His conclusions did not accord with the law: “Be his help against his adversaries.””

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? It is the utterance of David son of Jesse, who established the yoke of repentance.”

Commentary: Rashi on Moed Katan 16b:21:1: ““He established the yoke of repentance”: He was the first to return and thereby provided a path for those who repent. As the opening chapter of Avodah Zarah teaches, David was not suited to that deed; rather, when an individual sins, people tell him, “Go to David: the Holy One forgave that sin of his. You too should return in repentance.””

: “Rabbi heard that Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair had arrived, went out to meet him, and asked: Would you like to dine with me? He answered: Yes. Rabbi’s face shone. Rabbi Pinhas said: Do you imagine that I have vowed not to benefit from Israel? Israel are holy. Some are willing to give but have nothing; others have something but are unwilling to give. Of the latter it is written, “Do not eat the bread of a begrudging man, nor desire his delicacies, for as he calculates within himself, so he is; he says to you, ‘Eat and drink,’ but his heart is not with you.” You, however, are willing and have the means. For now I am in haste, since I am occupied with a mitzvah; when I return, I will come in to you.”

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

: ““They stood at the foot of the mountain.” Rav Avdimi bar Hama bar Hasa said: This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, held the mountain over them like a vat and said: If you accept the Torah, well and good; if not, there will be your burial. Rav Aha bar Yaakov said: From here there is a weighty declaration of coercion regarding Torah. Rava said: Nevertheless, they accepted it again in the days of Ahasuerus, for it says, “The Jews established and accepted”: They established what they had already accepted.”

: “Rabbi Yudan, Rabbi Aivu, and Rabbi Mishin ben Nagri said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Your children are destined to act like a nation among the assembly of peoples: just as an assembly of other peoples offers sacrifices when private altars are prohibited to Israel, so your children will offer sacrifices at such a time. Rabbi Chanina derives it from the verse, ‘Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the Lord had come, saying: Israel shall be your name.’ From the moment he was given that name, he was also told, ‘A nation and an assembly of nations shall come from you.’”

: ““Answer me, Hashem, answer me.” Rabbi Abbahu said: Why did Elijah say “answer me” twice? This teaches that he said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “Master of the world, ‘answer me’ by sending fire from heaven to consume everything upon the altar, and ‘answer me’ by diverting their thoughts so that they do not say it was sorcery,” as it says, “You have turned their hearts backward.””

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””

: “That is why, after this plague, it does not say, “Hashem strengthened Pharaoh’s heart,” even though it belonged to the five plagues concerning which the Midrash says: Once the Holy One saw that Pharaoh had not returned after the first five plagues, He said, “I shall strengthen his heart.” Of this plague, however, Scripture says, “He made his heart heavy, he and his servants,” and, “Pharaoh’s heart became strong.” During this plague it was not necessary for Hashem to strengthen his heart: Pharaoh strengthened himself and made his own heart heavy when he saw that all seven plagues had been completed.”

: “Rabbi Elazar said: By the light the Holy One, blessed be He, created on the first day, a person could see from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One, blessed be He, looked upon the generations of the Flood and the Dispersion and saw their corrupt deeds, He concealed it from them, as it says, “Their light is withheld from the wicked.” For whom did He conceal it? For the righteous in the future, as it says, “God saw the light, that it was good.” “Good” means the righteous, as it says, “Say of the righteous that it is good.” On seeing the light reserved for the righteous, He rejoiced, as it says, “The light of the righteous rejoices.””
: “Rather, this is what it means: The Merciful One summoned light and appointed it to the duties of daytime, and summoned darkness and appointed it to the duties of nighttime.”

: “Did Ezra institute public Torah reading on Mondays and Thursdays? It had already been instituted earlier. A baraita teaches: “They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.” Those who expound the verse’s allusions said: Water means Torah, as it says, “Let everyone who thirsts come to the water.” After three days without Torah they grew weary. The prophets among them therefore instituted reading on Shabbat, pausing on Sunday, reading on Monday, pausing on Tuesday and Wednesday, reading on Thursday, and pausing on Friday, so that they would not pass three days without Torah. Initially they instituted either one person reading three verses, or three people reading three verses, corresponding to priests, Levites, and Israelites. Ezra then instituted three readers and ten verses, corresponding to the ten men who remain available for the community.”

: “But you, My servant Jacob, do not fear, and do not be dismayed, Israel. I will save you from afar and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and secure, with no one to make him afraid.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: All the prophets’ prophecies concern penitents; as for the completely righteous, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu, who said: In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near”—first the far, then the near. Rabbi Yochanan would explain: “Far” means one who was far from transgression from the outset; “near” means one who was once close to transgression but has now distanced himself from it.”
: “There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation, no peace in my bones because of my sin.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 34, paragraph 2: “On Shabbat and festivals we say, ‘You have granted us Your Shabbat and holy festivals in love and favor, in happiness and rejoicing.’ Love is without a reason; it is simply His will, as it says, ‘Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? Yet I loved Jacob.’ That is, even when their deeds are alike—even if Jacob, God forbid, acts as Esau does, or Esau acts as Jacob does—nevertheless, ‘I loved Jacob’: a love without a reason. ‘In happiness and rejoicing’ means that one truly deserves love because of one’s deeds, as in ‘A wise son brings joy to his father,’ and ‘My son, if your heart is wise, my heart too will rejoice.’ Concerning Jacob we say, ‘Jacob Your son, Your firstborn: because of Your love for him and Your joy in him.’ He possesses both: love arising from God’s will without a reason, and the joy God takes in him because his pleasing deeds make him worthy of love. ‘You called his name Israel’ refers to love without a reason. Of this the Sages said, ‘Even though he sinned, he remains an Israelite,’ for Jacob’s family is complete. Even if one of his descendants accumulates sins reaching heaven—as the Gemara enumerates concerning Achan—he still does not lose the name Israel. The name Yeshurun, however, refers to the uprightness of his deeds.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”
: “But against any of the Israelites, from person to animal, not even a dog will sharpen its tongue, so that you may know that Hashem distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: when they unite, the world’s inhabitants cannot withstand them. Therefore, ‘Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together’—precisely together. We learned that a person should not make room for evil kinds, for a person’s action below arouses what should not be aroused. When they unite, their combined force brings forth what is called Dog, the most brazen of all. Hence ‘Against all the children of Israel, no dog shall sharpen its tongue.’ God said: ‘You asked, “Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?” I now hand you over to the dog.’ Immediately, ‘Amalek came.’”

: ““There is one people”: Rava said: No one understood malicious speech as Haman did. He said to Ahasuerus: Come, let us destroy them. The king replied: I fear their God, lest He deal with me as He did with earlier rulers. Haman answered: They have fallen asleep in their observance of the commandments. The king said: There are rabbis among them. Haman replied: They are all one people. Perhaps you think I am making a gap in your kingdom? They are scattered among the nations. Perhaps you think they benefit you? They are “separate,” like a mule that bears no offspring. Perhaps you think they occupy one province? Scripture says, “In all the provinces of your kingdom.” “Their laws differ from every people’s”: they neither eat our food nor marry our women, nor give their women to us in marriage. “They do not observe the king’s laws”: they spend the whole year saying, “It is Shabbat today; it is Passover today.” “It is not worthwhile for the king to leave them”: they eat, drink, and disparage the king. If a fly falls into someone’s cup, he throws it out and drinks; but if my lord the king touches the cup, he smashes it on the ground and will not drink.”
Commentary: Rashi on Megillah 13b:19:3: ““They spend the year with ‘Shabbat today; Passover today’”: It is Shabbat today, it is Passover today, and we are forbidden to work.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: When Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them. Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina explained this in his father’s name: It is like a shepherd taking his flock across a river. A wolf came to attack the flock. The experienced shepherd took a large goat and gave it to the wolf, saying: Let it struggle with this until we cross the river; afterward I will retrieve it. So, when Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, until now these people worshipped idols, and You are splitting the sea for them! What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He handed him Job, who had been one of Pharaoh’s advisers and of whom it is written, “A blameless and upright man.” He told him: He is in your hand. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: While he is occupied with Job, Israel will enter the sea and emerge, and afterward I will rescue Job.”

: “When Israel approached the sea and God wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, Egypt’s appointed ruler, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: ‘Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All are guilty before You, and all Your ways are judgment and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and those worship stars and constellations; these commit sexual transgressions, and those commit sexual transgressions; these shed blood, and those shed blood.’”

: “Israel was commanded concerning ten commandments at Marah: the seven that Noah’s descendants had accepted, to which were added laws of justice, Shabbat, and honoring father and mother. Laws of justice, as it says, “There He established for them a statute and an ordinance.” Shabbat and honoring father and mother, as it says, “As Hashem your God commanded you.” Rav Judah said: “As He commanded you”—at Marah.”

: ““There He established for him statute and judgment.” “Statute”—this is Shabbat; “judgment”—this is honoring father and mother: the words of Rabbi Yehoshua. Rabbi Elazar of Modi’in says: “Statute”—these are forbidden sexual relationships, as it says, “Not to practice the abominable statutes practiced before you, and not to become impure through them; I am the Lord your God.” “Judgment”—these are laws of coercion, monetary penalties, and injuries.”

: ““See that the Lord has given you Shabbat.” It should have said “Know”; why “See”? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, told them: If idolaters ask why you observe Shabbat on this day, tell them: See, the manna does not descend on Shabbat. What does “given you” mean? It was given to you, not to idolaters. From here they said: If idolaters come and observe Shabbat, not only do they receive no reward, and so forth, for it says, “Day and night shall not cease.” Likewise it says, “Between Me and the children of Israel…” It is like a king seated with a queen seated opposite him: one who passes between them incurs liability.”

: “So Isaiah says, ‘Therefore the netherworld has enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without limit’—for one who lacks the covenant of circumcision. How do we know that circumcision is called a chok, an established decree? ‘He established it for Jacob as a decree, for Israel as an everlasting covenant.’”

: “The Sages taught: The circumciser says, “Who has sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us concerning circumcision.” The child’s father says, “Who has sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us to bring him into the covenant of Abraham our father.” Those standing there say, “Just as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter Torah, the wedding canopy, and good deeds.” The one reciting the blessing says, “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb, placed a statute in his flesh, and sealed his descendants with the sign of the holy covenant. Therefore, in reward for this, living God, our portion, command that our beloved kin be rescued from destruction, for the sake of His covenant that He placed in our flesh. Blessed are You, Lord, who establishes the covenant.””

: “Scripture specifies these six upper days: ‘Yours, Lord, are greatness, might and beauty,’ and so forth. ‘For all’ is the Righteous One; ‘in heaven’ is Tiferet; ‘and on earth’ is the Congregation of Israel. The Targum renders it ‘which unites heaven and earth’: the foundation of the world, called All, unites Tiferet, called heaven, with the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.”

: “Eating on Shabbat is holy. The Zohar says, “In this place all the upper sanctities abide, and from it they flow to the Congregation of Israel to give her delight, delicate bread. ‘From Asher’—this is the complete covenant; ‘his bread is rich.’ What had been bread of poverty is transformed into delicate bread.” This means that the eating is holy and gives forth a good fragrance, as explained in discourse four.”

: “Rabba bar Yitzḥak said in Rav’s name: Uncovering the corona as part of circumcision was not commanded to our father Abraham, as it says, “At that time Hashem said to Joshua: Make yourself flint knives.” Perhaps this concerned those who had not been circumcised, as it says, “All the people who left were circumcised, but all the people born …”? If so, why does it say “again”? It must refer to uncovering the corona. What does “a second time” teach? It compares the conclusion of circumcision to its beginning: just as omitting the beginning invalidates it, so does omitting the conclusion.”

: “'When he was circumcised, the flesh of his foreskin': concerning Abraham, et is not stated, because he needed only the flesh cut, since it had already been flattened through intercourse. Ishmael, however, was a child and needed both removal of the foreskin and uncovering of the circumcision. Et is therefore written concerning him, as taught in Bereshit Rabbah.”

: “‘Abraham was ninety-nine years old.’ Here Scripture says ‘the flesh of his foreskin,’ but there it says ‘et, the flesh of his foreskin.’ Because Abraham’s foreskin had already been worn through relations with a woman, it says ‘the flesh of his foreskin’; because Ishmael’s had not been worn through relations with a woman, it says ‘et, the flesh of his foreskin.’”

: “The Master taught: Gentiles value Israel’s livestock more than their own wives. For Rabbi Yochanan said: When the serpent approached Eve, he infused her with defilement. If so, does this not also apply to Israel? Israel stood at Mount Sinai, and their defilement ceased; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, retained their defilement.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu expounded: What does “Who has counted Jacob’s dust, or numbered Israel’s quarter” mean? It teaches that the Holy One sits and counts Israel’s acts of marital union, awaiting the drop from which a righteous person will be formed. This was why the wicked Balaam’s eye was blinded. He said, “Would One who is pure and holy, whose attendants are pure and holy, look upon such a thing?” At once his eye was blinded, as it is written, “The utterance of the man whose eye is closed.””

: “Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina differed: One said that descendants of Noah offered peace offerings, while the other said that they did not. What is the reason of the view that they offered peace offerings? “Abel too brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat.” What offering has its fat offered upon the altar without the whole animal being offered? A peace offering. What is the reason of the view that they did not? “Awake, north wind; come, south wind”: Let the nation whose service is confined to the north give way, and let the nation whose service includes north and south come. But according to the latter view, is it not written, “From their fat”? This means their choicest animals. And according to the former view, is it not written, “Awake, north wind”? That passage concerns the ingathering of the exiles.”

: “Rabbi Akiva told him: ‘What difference is there between you and them? You eat and drink, and they eat and drink; you reproduce, and they reproduce; you die, and they die. Yet you became angry because I called them by your names! The Holy One, blessed be He, stretches out heaven, establishes earth, puts to death and gives life. When you take a piece of wood and call it “god,” using His name, how much more reason has He to hate you!’ Thus, ‘But Esau I hated.’”

k: volume-i|762|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkut
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 7:2–4: “Kelipat nogah is an intermediate realm between the three entirely impure husks and the domain and level of holiness. It is therefore sometimes incorporated into the three impure husks, as Etz Chaim explains in the Zohar’s name, and sometimes incorporated into holiness, ascending to its domain and level. This happens when the good mixed into it is separated from the evil, gains the upper hand, and rises to be included in holiness. For example, a person may eat rich beef and drink fragrant wine to broaden his understanding for God and His Torah, as Rava said concerning wine and fragrance, or to fulfill the mitzvah of delighting in Shabbat and festivals. The vitality of the meat and wine, which had flowed from kelipat nogah, is then refined and rises to God like a burnt offering and a sacrifice.”

: “‘I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan’—because they were circumcised. Whoever is circumcised inherits the land, for only the righteous one inherits the land, and whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Thus ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. Look at Joseph: throughout his days he was not called righteous until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous: Joseph the Righteous.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””

: “Adam encountered Cain and asked him, ‘What happened at your judgment?’ He replied, ‘I repented, and a settlement was reached.’ Adam began striking his face and said, ‘Such is the power of repentance, and I did not know!’ Immediately Adam arose and recited, ‘A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day.’ Rabbi Levi said: Adam composed this psalm, but it was forgotten by his generation; Moses came and renewed it under his own name: ‘A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day. It is good to give thanks to the Lord.’”

: “In the seventh hour on the eve of Shabbat, Adam entered the Garden of Eden; the ministering angels praised him and brought him into the Garden. At twilight on the eve of Shabbat he was expelled and went out. The ministering angels called out concerning him, “A human does not remain in honor overnight; they are likened to beasts that perish.” It does not say “like a beast,” but “like beasts”—both of them. The Shabbat day came and became Adam’s advocate. It said before Him: Master of the worlds, throughout the six days of creation no one was killed; will You begin with me? Is this my holiness and my blessing? As it says, “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.” Through the merit of Shabbat, Adam was saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. Adam saw Shabbat’s power and said: The Holy One, blessed be He, did not bless and sanctify Shabbat in vain. He began singing praise to Shabbat, as it says, “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.” Rabbi Yishmael says: Adam composed this psalm. It was forgotten through all generations until Moses came and renewed it: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day”—for the day that is entirely Shabbat and rest in the life of the world to come.”

: “Why is Havdalah included in the blessing “Who grants knowledge”? Rav Yosef said: Because distinguishing is an act of wisdom, they placed it in the blessing of wisdom. The Sages say: Because Havdalah concerns the weekday, they placed it in the first weekday blessing.”

: ““Happy is the man who fears Hashem.” Is a man happy, but a woman not? Rav Amram said in Rav’s name: Happy is one who repents while still a man in his strength. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Happy is one who masters his inclination like a man.”
: “Rabbi was holding and reading the Book of Lamentations. When he reached the verse “He cast from heaven to earth,” the book fell from his hand. He said: “From a high roof to a deep pit.””
: “This day belongs to souls, rather than the body, for the Bundle of Souls rules. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional upper holy spirit.”

: “Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.” “He summons the heavens above”—this is the soul. “And the earth to judge His people”—this is the body.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Noach 7, paragraph 1: “God graciously grants this as a free gift. The day of Shabbat also has the character of a loan: through Shabbat’s holiness, holiness is brought into the weekdays that follow, so that they too become holy. Through this a person merits observing the next Shabbat properly. The weekdays then help him become sanctified with the holiness of Shabbat, increasingly with every Shabbat. This is the aspect of a loan.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””
Commentary: Rashi on Taanit 8b:12:2: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”
: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn, whatever first opens a womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal; it is Mine.”

: “From Michael’s side, he is called firstborn, for Michael’s level is silver, whiteness. Therefore redeeming a firstborn requires silver, five sela‘im, corresponding to Abraham’s he. If he grows wise in Torah, yod is added to him, which is holiness; through it one must sanctify the firstborn animal, as in ‘Israel is holy to the Lord.’ Through it one must tithe the offspring, for every offspring comes from the side of ben Yah, the son of yod-he, who is vav.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: it is concealed within yod of the holy Name. This is one compartment of the tefillin, the passage ‘Sanctify to Me every firstborn’: the upper brain—another reading says Father—Wisdom.”

: “The first passage is ‘Sanctify to Me every firstborn.’ This is yod, holiness, firstborn of all the upper sanctifications. ‘Opening every womb’ refers to the fine path descending from yod, which opens the womb to produce fruits and offspring properly. This is upper holiness.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘How long shall the world continue in darkness? Let light come!’ ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to Abraham, as it says, ‘Who aroused righteousness from the east?’ Read not he’ir, ‘aroused,’ but he’ir, ‘illuminated.’”

: “Rabbi Yehudah the Nasi asked Rabbi Ami: What does the verse mean, “Trust in Hashem forever, for through Yah, Hashem, is the Maker of worlds”? He answered: Whoever places his trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, has a refuge in this world and in the World to Come. Rabbi Yehudah said: My question is why it says “through Yah,” rather than simply “Yah.” This follows Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai’s exposition: These are the two worlds the Holy One, blessed be He, created—one with the letter heh and one with yod. I would not know whether the World to Come was created with yod and this world with heh, or this world with yod and the World to Come with heh. But Scripture says, “These are the generations of heaven and earth when they were created”—behibaram. Read it as: “With heh He created them.””
: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Behibare’am, ‘when they were created,’ may be read be’Avraham, ‘through Abraham’: they were created in Abraham’s merit.”

: “This is ‘These are the generations of heaven and earth when they were created,’ behibare’am. It was taught: ‘He created them with he’; it was also taught: ‘through Abraham.’ What do these mean? One is Chesed and the other the Shekhinah; all descend together. There is no difficulty: both interpretations hold.”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”
: “If you do well, will there not be uplift? But if you do not do well, sin crouches at the entrance. Its desire is toward you, yet you can rule over it.”

: “Antoninus also said to Rabbi: From when does the evil inclination control a person—from the moment he is formed, or from the moment he emerges? He answered: From the moment he is formed. Antoninus said: If so, he would kick his way out of his mother’s womb! Rather, it begins when he emerges. Rabbi said: Antoninus taught me this, and Scripture supports him, as it says, “Sin crouches at the entrance.””

: “Rabbi heard that Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair had arrived, went out to meet him, and asked: Would you like to dine with me? He answered: Yes. Rabbi’s face shone. Rabbi Pinhas said: Do you imagine that I have vowed not to benefit from Israel? Israel are holy. Some are willing to give but have nothing; others have something but are unwilling to give. Of the latter it is written, “Do not eat the bread of a begrudging man, nor desire his delicacies, for as he calculates within himself, so he is; he says to you, ‘Eat and drink,’ but his heart is not with you.” You, however, are willing and have the means. For now I am in haste, since I am occupied with a mitzvah; when I return, I will come in to you.”

: “In these lands they have practiced reciting this blessing. In France and Germany, however, they have not practiced reciting it. We do not find that any blessing is recited unless it is mentioned in the Mishnah, Tosefta, or Gemara, for after the compilation of Rav Ashi and Ravina we do not find a new blessing introduced. Furthermore, I do not understand the beginning of the blessing, 'Who sanctified the fetus in its mother’s womb.' If this refers to firstborn sanctity, the Merciful One made that depend upon opening the womb, and one is permitted to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn animal before most of it emerges.”

: “The Master taught: Gentiles value Israel’s livestock more than their own wives. For Rabbi Yochanan said: When the serpent approached Eve, he infused her with defilement. If so, does this not also apply to Israel? Israel stood at Mount Sinai, and their defilement ceased; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, retained their defilement.”

: “An objection was raised: Four died because of the serpent’s consequence: Benjamin son of Jacob, Amram father of Moses, Jesse father of David, and Chileab son of David. All are known by tradition except Jesse, father of David, for whom Scripture makes it explicit: “Absalom appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab; Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who came to Abigail daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.” Was she Nahash’s daughter? Was she not Jesse’s daughter, as it says, “Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail”? Rather, she was the daughter of one who died because of the serpent’s consequence. Whose teaching is this? If it is the view expressed in the account of the ministering angels, Moses and Aaron should also be included. Rather, it must be Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar’s view. It therefore follows that there is death without sin and suffering without wrongdoing. This refutes Rav Ammi; it is a refutation.”

: “'My days are fulfilled': the days my mother told me of. Furthermore, my own days are fulfilled: I am eighty-four years old; when shall I establish the twelve tribes? This explains his statement, 'And I will come to her.' Even the most frivolous person does not speak like that! Rather, he said it for the sake of producing offspring.”

: “After they finished eating, Rabbi Yitzḥak told Rav Naḥman: Rabbi Yoḥanan said that our father Jacob did not die. He replied: Was it then for nothing that the mourners mourned him, the embalmers embalmed him, and the buriers buried him? Rabbi Yitzḥak answered: I am interpreting a verse: “Do not fear, My servant Jacob, declares Hashem, and do not be dismayed, Israel, for I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity.” The verse compares Jacob to his offspring: Just as his offspring are alive, so he too is alive.”

: “At Rabbi’s death, he raised his ten fingers upward and said: “Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I labored in Torah with my ten fingers, but took no pleasure even with my little finger. May it be Your will that my repose be peaceful.” A heavenly voice declared: “Let him come in peace; let them rest upon their beds.””

: ““Radish and lettuce, neither in summer nor in winter”: Eruvin 56 says, “When radish appears, a life-giving medicine appears,” but another baraita says, “A deadly medicine appears.” It resolves this by distinguishing summer from winter. Here the statement concerns the season when it is life-giving. Furthermore, some texts distinguish the leaves from the roots; the roots are always life-giving, and here too the roots are meant. Although Rabbi is said not to have enjoyed this world even with his little finger, many people ate at his table.”

: “Shabbat likewise contains the mystery of the covenant, as the Zohar says, for it resembles the World to Come. Then 'Your people are all righteous' will become clear: everyone circumcised is called righteous. Shabbat is the time to rectify this blemish, making the body holy flesh. Therefore there is a commandment to delight the body; as the Ari writes, even eating for bodily enjoyment on Shabbat is holy. The special rank of one who delights the Sabbath, however, is as we explained: intending to delight the additional soul called Shabbat. One then merits all the benefits mentioned in the Gemara.”

: “Our holy teacher would appear in the fine garments he had worn on Shabbat, rather than in shrouds, indicating that he remained in his former strength. He discharged the public’s obligation through the day’s Kiddush, unlike other dead people, who are free of the commandments. Rather, he was as a living person, in the clothes he had worn during his lifetime. The righteous are called living even after death, and he discharged his household’s obligation in Kiddush.”

k: volume-i|794|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “The holy Ari wrote that Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi was a spark of the soul of our father Jacob; nasi is an acronym for ‘a spark of our father Jacob.’ Now the added letter in avvon, ‘iniquity,’ is vav. The holy Ari also teaches that wherever a letter of God’s Name is added, holiness is present there—certainly with vav, the letter of truth, as the Zohar states at the beginning of Vayikra.”

k: volume-i|795|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “The holy Ari wrote that Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi was a spark of the soul of our father Jacob; nasi is an acronym for ‘a spark of our father Jacob.’ Now the added letter in avvon, ‘iniquity,’ is vav. The holy Ari also teaches that wherever a letter of God’s Name is added, holiness is present there—certainly with vav, the letter of truth, as the Zohar states at the beginning of Vayikra.”

: “The Sages taught: “You shall place”—vesamtem—may be read sam tam, a perfect medicine. Torah is compared to a life-giving medicine. A man struck his son a severe blow, placed a dressing upon the wound, and told him: My son, while this dressing remains on your wound, eat what gives you pleasure, drink what gives you pleasure, and bathe in hot or cold water without fear. If you remove it, the wound will develop sores. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be delivered into its hand, as it says, “If you do well, will there not be uplift?” If you do not occupy yourselves with Torah, you will be delivered into its hand, as it says, “Sin crouches at the doorway.” Moreover, its entire concern is with you, as it says, “Its desire is toward you.” If you wish, however, you can rule over it, as it says, “You shall rule over it.””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: ““Like scarlet”—shanim? Should it not say shani, in the singular? Rabbi Yitzhak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years, shanim, ordered in succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.”

: “‘He meditates upon His Torah.’ Rabbi Shimon said: Abraham’s father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys to be like two teachers; they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written, ‘I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.’”
: “Rabbi Chanina said: The names of the months came up from Babylonia. Reish Lakish said: So did the names of the angels—Michael, Raphael, and Gabriel.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The names of the angels, too, came up with them from Babylonia. Earlier Scripture says, “One of the seraphim flew to me,” and, “Seraphim stood above Him.” From then onward it says, “The man Gabriel,” and, “Except Michael your prince.””

: ““You will surely fall before him”: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai expounded: Why are two expressions of falling used? They told Haman: This nation is compared to dust and to the stars. When they descend, they descend to the dust; when they rise, they rise to the stars.”

: “Rabbi Yose bar Hanina said: Torah was given only to Moses and his descendants, as it says, “Write for yourself” and “Carve for yourself”: Just as the chips belong to you, so the writing belongs to you. Moses acted generously and gave it to Israel; of him Scripture says, “The generous eye shall be blessed.” Rav Hisda objected: “The Lord commanded me at that time to teach you.” The response is: He commanded me, and I passed it to you. “See, I have taught you statutes and laws as the Lord my God commanded me.” Again: He commanded me, and I passed it to you. “Now write this song for yourselves.” That concerns the song alone. But it says, “So that this song shall be a witness for Me among the children of Israel”! Rather, the original statement concerns the reasoning and analysis of Torah.”

: ““This is forever incumbent upon Israel.” Rav Giddel said in Rav’s name: This refers to an altar already built, at which Michael, the great prince, stands and offers a sacrifice. Rabbi Yochanan said: It refers to Torah scholars engaged in studying the laws of the Temple service; Scripture credits them as though the Temple had been built in their days.”
: “But I will tell you what is recorded in the writing of truth. No one supports me against these powers except Michael, your prince.”

: “Rabbi Zekharya said in Rabbi Yishmael’s name: The Holy One, blessed be He, intended to bring forth the priesthood from Shem, as it says, “He was a priest of God Most High.” Once Shem put Abraham’s blessing before God’s blessing, He brought it forth from Abraham. For it says, “He blessed him and said: Blessed is Abram to God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth; and blessed is God Most High.” Abraham said to him: Does one place a servant’s blessing before his Master’s blessing? The priesthood was immediately given to Abraham, as it says, “The Lord’s declaration to my master: Sit at My right until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet,” followed by, “The Lord has sworn and will not relent: You are a priest forever, because of the speech of Melchizedek”—because of Melchizedek’s words. Thus it says, “He was a priest of God Most High”: He was a priest, but his descendants would not be priests.”

k: volume-i|807|0|Megalleh Amukot, teaching quoted by R. T
quote: : “Megalleh Amukot states that the additional letters in the spelled-out letters of Moshe—mem, yod, nun and aleph—have the numerical value one hundred and one, the same as Mikhael. A person’s name is his essential vitality, as we have explained; the filling of the name is its inward dimension, one with the name itself. Thus the Zohar says that Jacob and Joseph are one. This is the mystery of the letter vav spelled with two vavs, which go together. Jacob is the attribute of truth, the primary vav, called the letter of truth: “You shall give truth to Jacob,” and, “A lip of truth shall be established forever.” Defilement had ceased, his offspring were whole, and holiness already existed in Israel’s embryos. Joseph is the filling vav, the small vav, revealing “Your people are all righteous”; they are one. Likewise, Moses is the root of the Written Torah, called Moses’ Torah, and its filling includes the numerical value of Mikhael, the aspect of Oral Torah, as explained.”

: “Therefore the Shekhinah is bound to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph: they are together and have a single likeness. Thus ‘These are Jacob’s generations: Joseph.’ Hence ‘From all the merchant’s fragrant powder,’ for from the place of the river that flows and proceeds, everything is watered and every face is illuminated.”

: “The eighth is El Chai, the living God, as in ‘There the Lord commanded blessing, life,’ and so forth. This is the Righteous One, from whom all life proceeds, also called by the divine Name, as in ‘The Lord tests the righteous.’ This is the small vav of the holy Name. Therefore vav is spelled with two vavs.”

: “Rabbi Simlai expounded: What is an unborn child like in its mother’s womb? Like a folded writing tablet: its hands rest at its temples, its elbows upon its knees, its heels upon its buttocks, and its head between its knees. Its mouth is closed and its navel open. It eats from what its mother eats and drinks from what she drinks. It does not discharge waste, lest it kill its mother. When it enters the world, what was closed opens and what was open closes; otherwise it could not survive even a single hour.”
: “You granted me life and kindness, and Your care guarded my spirit.”

: “Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who sanctified the fetus from its mother’s womb, divided its 248 limbs at forty days, and breathed a soul into it, as it says, 'He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human became a living soul.' He clothed it in skin and flesh and enclosed it in bones and sinews, as it says, 'You clothe me in skin and flesh, and weave me together with bones and sinews.' He ordained food and drink for it and appointed two ministering angels to guard it in its mother’s womb, as it says, 'You bestowed life and kindness upon me, and Your providence guarded my spirit.' Its father says, 'This is my firstborn son'; its mother says, 'This is my firstborn son, through whom the Holy One, blessed be He, opened the doors of my womb.' We have become obligated to give five selaim to a priest for its redemption, as it says, 'You shall redeem him from one month old, at the valuation of five shekels, by the sacred shekel, twenty gerah to the shekel'; and, 'You shall surely redeem the human firstborn and redeem the firstborn of an unclean animal.' Just as this firstborn has merited redemption, so may God grant him Torah, marriage, and good deeds. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies Israel’s firstborn for their redemption.”

: “Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who sanctified the fetus from its mother’s womb, divided its 248 limbs at forty days, and breathed a soul into it, as it says, 'He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human became a living soul.' He clothed it in skin and flesh and enclosed it in bones and sinews, as it says, 'You clothe me in skin and flesh, and weave me together with bones and sinews.'
