He provided food and drink for it and appointed two ministering angels to guard it in its mother’s womb, as it says, 'You bestowed life and kindness upon me, and Your providence guarded my spirit.' Its father says, 'This is my firstborn son'; its mother says, 'This is my firstborn son, through whom the Holy One, blessed be He, opened the doors of my womb.' Five selaim must be given to a priest for its redemption, as it says, 'You shall redeem him from one month old, at the valuation of five shekels, by the sacred shekel, twenty gerah to the shekel'; and, 'You shall surely redeem the human firstborn and redeem the firstborn of an unclean animal.' Just as this firstborn has merited redemption, so may He grant him Torah, marriage, and good deeds. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies Israel’s firstborn for their redemption.”
: “Your lips drip honeycomb, bride; honey and milk are beneath your tongue. The fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.”

: “Rav Yosef told them: We have learned concerning these matters, “Honey and milk are under your tongue”—things sweeter than honey and milk should remain beneath your tongue. Rabbi Abbahu derived it from, “Lambs are for your clothing”: matters that are the world’s hidden mysteries should remain beneath your clothing.”

: “If one transgresses the Torah, the limbs are watered from the bitterness of the evil tree, the evil inclination. Of all the limbs composed of the four elements it says, ‘They embittered their lives’: they embittered them with the bitterness of bile. Of the holy limbs of the body, belonging to the good side, it says, ‘They came to Marah and could not drink the waters of Marah.’ Likewise the masters of Mishnah explained: ‘They embittered their lives with hard labor’—difficult questions; ‘with mortar’—arguments from the less to the greater; ‘with bricks’—clarifying halakhah; ‘with all labor in the field’—baraita; ‘all their labor’—Mishnah.”

: “Faithful Shepherd, in you was fulfilled ‘There He set for him statute and judgment, and there He tested him.’ Through this Tree of Knowledge of good and evil—prohibition and permission—and the secrets revealed through you, ‘the waters became sweet.’ As salt sweetens meat, the secrets revealed through you will sweeten all those difficulties and disputes: the bitter waters of the Oral Torah become sweet waters of Torah. Through these secrets your sufferings, too, will be sweetened, and all your distress will become like passing dreams. Chalom, ‘dream,’ rearranges the letters of melach, ‘salt,’ which sweetens meat; suffering likewise sweetens, as explained.”

: “A lamp burns above the unborn child’s head, and the child gazes from one end of the world to the other, as it says, “When His lamp shone above my head, by His light I walked through darkness.” Do not find this astonishing: A person sleeps here and sees a dream in Spain. No days offer a person greater well-being than those days, as it says, “If only I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me.” Which days are measured in months but not in years? The months of pregnancy. The child is taught the whole Torah, as it says, “He taught me and said to me: Let your heart hold fast to my words; keep my commandments and live,” and also, “When God’s counsel rested upon my tent.” Why is the second verse needed? You might say that the first concerns a prophet; therefore the text brings, “When God’s counsel rested upon my tent.” Once the child enters the world, an angel strikes its mouth and makes it forget the whole Torah, as it says, “Sin crouches at the entrance.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 7:26: “Before the child enters the world, the soul is not yet fully clothed within the body’s interior; it stands instead as an encompassing light above his head. He can therefore gaze and apprehend through it a foretaste of the World to Come. Of this the Sages said that no days are as good for him as those days. Sefer Yetzirah states that there is nothing higher in goodness than delight. This is the delight of Shabbat, a foretaste of the World to Come, the day wholly Shabbat, when one rests from toil and delights only in God. It is the ‘light that is good,’ then disclosed in the apprehension that ‘they will all know Me’ and ‘no one will teach his fellow.’ In the womb, too, the child is taught the whole Torah, through gazing by that lamp. This is his apprehension of his own portion at Mount Sinai, where all souls were present, as Shabbat 146a teaches. Once the soul is clothed in the body, everything is forgotten. He must attain and reach it through his own effort and toil after he acquires understanding and the capacity to grasp. In his mother’s womb, apprehension comes from the encompassing light, for he has as yet no developed awareness or faculties of mind.”

: “Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master and the Matron with every kind of delight, fulfilling ‘This is the table before the Lord.’ Until now all delight in the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread’: the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, the varied flavors of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”

: “What does “for stately covering” mean? It refers to one who conceals things concealed by the Ancient of Days. What are these? The Torah’s secrets. Others say: It refers to one who reveals things concealed by the Ancient of Days. What are these? The Torah’s reasons.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Whoever prolongs his prayer and awaits its result will ultimately suffer heartache, as it says, “A prolonged expectation makes the heart ill.” What is his remedy? Let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “A tree of life is a desire fulfilled.” “A tree of life” means Torah, as it says, “It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it.””

Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:1: ““And awaits its result”: he expects his request to be granted because he prolonged his prayer. In the end it is not granted, and his expectation has been drawn out in vain. That is the heartache of a person who waits for something he desires but does not receive it.”

: ““To guard the way”—this is proper conduct. “The tree of life”—this teaches that proper conduct preceded the tree of life. The tree of life means Torah, as it says, “It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it.””

: “R. Elazar said: What is meant by “She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the Torah of kindness is upon her tongue”? Is there a Torah of kindness and a Torah that is not of kindness? Rather, Torah studied for its own sake is the Torah of kindness; Torah studied not for its own sake is not the Torah of kindness. Others say: Torah studied in order to teach is the Torah of kindness; Torah studied without the intention to teach is not the Torah of kindness.”

: “Eleazar ben Poira said to King Yannai: King Yannai, is this the treatment even an ordinary Israelite deserves—and you are both king and High Priest? Yannai asked: What should I do? He answered: If you listen to my advice, trample the Sages. But what will become of Torah? It lies rolled up in a corner; anyone who wishes to learn may come and learn. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak said: At once heresy was cast into him, for he should have said: That may suffice for Written Torah, but what about Oral Torah? Immediately evil sprang up through Eleazar ben Poira: All Israel’s Sages were killed, and the world was desolate until Shimon ben Shetah came and restored Torah to its former state.”

: “R. Simlai attended a firstborn son’s redemption. They asked him: Clearly, the child’s father recites the blessing, “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the redemption of the son.” But who recites, “Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time”—the priest or the child’s father? Does the priest bless because the benefit reaches his hand, or does the father bless because he performs the mitzvah? He did not know. He went and asked in the study hall, where they told him: The child’s father recites both blessings. The ruling is that the child’s father recites both.”

: “Rav Yosef said in Rav Yehuda’s name, in Shmuel’s name: The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda regarding hair threads. Abaye said to him: Saying “the halakha follows him” implies a dispute. Perhaps you think that unless Rabbi Yehuda had heard the first tanna discuss hair threads, he would not have discussed them either. But perhaps he meant: Just as you concede to me about hair threads, concede to me about wool threads as well. It was stated: Rav Nahman said in Shmuel’s name: The Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda regarding hair threads. A baraita likewise teaches: Wool threads form an obstruction to immersion; hair threads do not. Rabbi Yehuda says: Neither wool nor hair threads form an obstruction. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak said: The Mishnah also indicates this, for it teaches that a woman may go out with hair threads, whether her own or another woman’s. Whose view is this? If Rabbi Yehuda’s, wool threads would also be permitted. Rather, it is the Sages’ view. Thus they do not dispute hair threads. This is indeed the conclusion.”
: ““I give you your priesthood as a service of gift, and the outsider who approaches shall die.” They treated the eating of terumah outside the Temple as equivalent to Temple service.”

: “Rather, Mar Zutra said: The Sages established these three matters as fixed laws without an explanation: first, this transfer in the presence of the three parties; second, Rav Yehudah’s ruling in Shmuel’s name that one who writes all his property to his wife has made her only its administrator; and third, Rav Chananya’s ruling that, when a father marries off his grown son in a house, the son acquires that house.”

: ““R. Simlai attended,” and so forth: Since the Mishnah discusses two kinds of blessing for one person and one interconnected act—for example, the Pesach offering and the other sacrifice, since the festival offering accompanies the Pesach offering—it also includes this incident, in which the child’s father recites two blessings.”

: “Further, they all traveled peacefully, according to their souls’ desire. By the day they received Torah, fifty complete days had passed, days and nights as fitting: there is no day without night and no night without day; night and day are called one day. Since they traveled fifty complete days, the fifty days of Jubilee rested upon them, and Torah was given them from Jubilee’s side. They therefore traveled by day and by night.”

: “‘He was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights.’ How did Moses know when it was day? When the Holy One, blessed be He, taught him the Written Torah, he knew it was day; when He taught him Mishnah and Talmud orally, he knew it was night. For day and night are alike before the Holy One, as it says, ‘Light dwells with Him’; and ‘Even darkness is not dark for You; night shines like day, darkness like light.’”
: “Rav, Shmuel, and Rav Asi came to a celebration of a son’s week; others report that it was a celebration of a son’s deliverance.”

k: volume-i|830|1|Rashi on Bava Kamma 80a, s.v. yeshu’a ha
quote: : ““The son’s salvation”: A feast held for the redemption of a firstborn son. Yeshu’a is translated into Aramaic as purkan, deliverance, like redemption.”

k: volume-i|830|2|Tosafot on Bava Kamma 80a, s.v. le-vei y
quote: : ““To the house of the son’s salvation”: Rashi explains this as the redemption of the firstborn, and so does the Arukh. This is difficult: Although redemption is translated purkan, the term salvation is still not appropriate. Rabbenu Tam explains that a son had been born there. The expression salvation is used because the child was saved and escaped from his mother’s womb, as it says, “She delivered a male.” They customarily held a feast.”

: “The Rabbis interpreted the verse concerning Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: “My light”—on Rosh Hashanah; “my salvation”—on Yom Kippur. “Whom shall I fear?”—“My strength and song is the Lord.” “When evildoers approach me”—these are the princes of the nations. “To eat my flesh”—for the princes of the nations come and accuse Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying: Master of the universe, these worship idols and those worship idols; these commit sexual immorality and those commit sexual immorality; these shed blood and those shed blood. Why do these descend to Gehinnom while those do not? “My enemies and adversaries”—there are three hundred and sixty-five days in the solar year, while “the satan” has the numerical value of three hundred and sixty-four, for the satan accuses throughout the year but does not accuse on Yom Kippur. Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “If an army encamps against me”—Samael’s army—“my heart will not fear,” for You promised me, “With this Aaron shall enter the sanctuary.””

: “He began grieving over the breaking of the tablets. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: Do not grieve over the first tablets, which contained only the Ten Commandments. In the second tablets I give you, there will be laws, midrash, and aggadot, as it is written, “He will tell you wisdom’s hidden things, for sound wisdom is doubled.” Moreover, you receive the tidings that I have forgiven your sin, as it says, “Know that God remits some of your iniquity.””

: “Rabbi Hanina said: If one who is not commanded but acts receives such a reward, how much more one who is commanded and acts! For Rabbi Hanina said: One who is commanded and acts is greater than one who is not commanded and acts. Rav Yosef said: At first I used to say: If someone tells me the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that a blind person is exempt from the commandments, I will make a feast for the Sages, since I act despite not being commanded. Now that I have heard Rabbi Hanina’s teaching that one who is commanded and acts is greater, I say the reverse: If someone tells me the halakha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda, I will make a feast for the Sages.”

k: volume-i|833|1|Rashi on Kiddushin 31a, s.v. yoma tava l
quote: : ““Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion”: That a blind person is exempt from the commandments, as stated in Bava Kamma, chapter Ha-Hovel, 87a. “A festive day for the Sages”: A meal for the students. “I am not commanded”: Because Rav Yosef was blind.”

: “Rabbi Haggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahman’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for eating and drinking. Because the mouth takes pleasure in its utterance, they permitted a person to occupy himself with words of Torah on them. Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Hiyya bar Ba’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for occupying oneself with words of Torah. A baraita supports each view: What does one do? Either sit and eat, or sit and occupy oneself with words of Torah. One verse says, “It is a Sabbath to the Lord,” and another says, “An assembly to the Lord your God.” How are they fulfilled? Give a portion to Torah study and a portion to eating and drinking.”

k: volume-i|834|2|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:4: ““Because this mouth blossoms”: This uses the expression “It will blossom and flower.” The meaning is that, because a person enjoys the breath issuing from his mouth, they permitted him to occupy himself with words of Torah on Shabbat and festivals, which were originally given only for delight through eating and drinking.”

k: volume-i|834|3|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:7: ““One verse says”: This is another baraita. It should read: One verse says, “An assembly to the Lord your God,” and another says, “An assembly shall be for you.” How can both be fulfilled? Divide the day. This supports Rabbi Berekhya, because one must in any event occupy oneself with words of Torah, while also giving a portion to eating and drinking, to fulfill “for you.””
: “'A holy convocation': mikra is a noun. Designate it as holy through eating, drinking, and clothing, as taught in Mekhilta.”
: “He made the letter tzadi king, bound a crown upon it, and through it formed Aquarius in the universe, Shevat in the year, and the stomach in the person.”
: “Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His harvest. All who consume him incur guilt; calamity will come upon them, declares Hashem.”
: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn, whatever first opens a womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal; it is Mine.”
: “You shall say to Pharaoh, “Thus says Hashem: Israel is My son, My firstborn.””
: “When the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy—”
: “If a person merits it, he is told, ‘You preceded the ministering angels.’ If he does not, he is told, ‘A fly preceded you; a mosquito preceded you; this worm preceded you.’”
: “He makes winds His messengers and blazing fire His attendants.”
: “I said to you, “Send out My son so that he may serve Me,” but you refused to send him out. Now I will kill your son, your firstborn.”

: “‘I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan’—because they were circumcised. Whoever is circumcised inherits the land, for only the righteous one inherits the land, and whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Thus ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. Look at Joseph: throughout his days he was not called righteous until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous: Joseph the Righteous.”

: “The he was added to Abraham when he was commanded concerning circumcision. He then became holy flesh: his body was sanctified with Israel’s holiness, and his heart became a dwelling for the Divine Presence. In Lech Lecha 94 a, the Zohar opens the third exposition with 'From my flesh I behold': when he was circumcised, from it he beheld the Holy One, blessed be He, literally from it, and a holy soul became attached to him. It cites 'From the soul of God,' making clear that the holy soul means God’s portion, supernal seed, the congregation of Israel. This is the he added to him then. Through this he became a native among Israel, for he is Israel’s root, in whom God takes glory, and the beginning of creation’s thought was for him.”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”
: “Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.”

: “Rabbi Yannai was walking along the road and saw a man who appeared very distinguished. He said: Will the master consent to be our guest? He replied: Yes. He brought him home, fed him, and gave him drink. He tested him in Scripture and found him unlearned; in Mishnah, aggadah, and Talmud, and found him unlearned. He said: Take the cup and recite the blessing. The man replied: Let Yannai bless in his own house. He asked: Can you repeat what I tell you? He replied: Yes. He told him to say: A dog has eaten Yannai’s bread. The man rose, seized him, and said: My inheritance is with you, and you withhold it from me! He asked: What inheritance of yours is with me? He replied: Once I passed a school and heard the children saying, “Moses commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.” It does not say “the congregation of Yannai,” but “the congregation of Jacob.” He asked: Through what merit did you eat at my table? He replied: Never have I heard an evil report and carried it back to its subject; never have I seen two people quarrelling without making peace between them. Yannai said: You possess all this proper conduct, yet I called you a dog! He applied to him, “One who orders his way”: one who evaluates his path is worth much. For Rabbi Yishmael bar Rav Nachman said: Proper conduct preceded Torah by twenty-six generations, as it is written, “To guard the way of the tree of life.” “The way” is proper conduct, and afterward, “the tree of life” is Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””
: “Which Torah passage? Rav Hamnuna said: “Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.” Which part of the Shema? The first verse.”

: “He began: ‘This month shall be yours, the head of months.’ Do not all seasons and months belong to God? Rather: ‘This month shall be yours’—it is Mine, but I hand it over to you. Yours is revealed; the seventh is Mine, and therefore concealed rather than revealed. Your month follows the order of the letters: aviv, alef-bet-gimel; yod-bet is the mystery of gimel. An alternative reading says simply that it follows the letters in order. My seventh month, however, comes from the alphabet’s end—Tishrei. Why? You go from below upward, while I go from above downward.”

ref: Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sermons on Rosh Hashanah 1:1:4
quote: : “Know that I once heard another discourse on this subject from my teacher. Although it appears contrary to what was said above, anyone who explains it properly will see that the teachings lead to one place. The years are counted from Tishrei and the months from Nisan, as stated in Rosh Hashanah. The six winter months, Tishrei through Adar, correspond to the six extremities of Tiferet, from Chesed to Yesod in Ze‘ir Anpin. They therefore belong to the aspect of ‘year,’ rather than ‘month.’ After Adar, Ze‘ir Anpin’s Yesod, the feminine aspect, Malchut, begins below him: her six extremities are the six summer months, Nisan through Elul. Accordingly, Av is the feminine Hod, which becomes davah, ‘anguish,’ and the Temple was therefore destroyed in it.”

: ““And with the crushed and humble of spirit”: Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda disagree. One says it means, “The crushed one is with Me”; the other says, “I am with the crushed one.” The second view is more convincing: the Holy One, blessed be He, passed over all the mountains and hills and rested His Presence on Mount Sinai; Mount Sinai did not rise upward.”

k: volume-i|854|0|Arizal, Pri Etz Chaim, Sha’ar HaLulav, c
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of Lulav 8
quote: : “The secret of Isru Chag is the absorption of the seed, as explained. As is known, Isru Chag also has an element of rejoicing: it is the second day of the seed’s absorption, when it is bound within the female womb. Isru Chag thus means: bind and strengthen the union that took place on the festival. Once the third day begins, part of the day counts as the whole, and the binding is already complete. Hence rejoicing is observed on the second day, Isru Chag, rather than on the third.”

: “When Israel approached the sea and God wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, Egypt’s appointed ruler, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: ‘Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All are guilty before You, and all Your ways are judgment and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and those worship stars and constellations; these commit sexual transgressions, and those commit sexual transgressions; these shed blood, and those shed blood.’”

ref: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Vayehi Beshalach 7
quote: : ““The children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.” The ministering angels were astonished. They said: Master of all worlds, human beings who worship idols walk on dry land in the midst of the sea! How do we know that even the sea became filled with anger against them? Above it says “wall,” written like “anger,” and likewise here it says “wall.” What caused them to be rescued? “On their right and on their left.” “On their right”—through Torah’s merit, as it says, “From His right hand, a fiery law for them.” “On their left”—this is prayer.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: When Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them. Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina explained this in his father’s name: It is like a shepherd taking his flock across a river. A wolf came to attack the flock. The experienced shepherd took a large goat and gave it to the wolf, saying: Let it struggle with this until we cross the river; afterward I will retrieve it. So, when Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, until now these people worshipped idols, and You are splitting the sea for them! What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He handed him Job, who had been one of Pharaoh’s advisers and of whom it is written, “A blameless and upright man.” He told him: He is in your hand. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: While he is occupied with Job, Israel will enter the sea and emerge, and afterward I will rescue Job.”
: “The Sages taught: Three things are harmful in excess but beneficial in small measure: leaven, salt, and reluctance to accept an invitation to lead prayer.”

: “It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai likewise said: Gentile graves do not impart impurity through a shared covering, as it says, “You are My sheep, the sheep of My pasture; you are adam.” You are called adam, whereas the nations are not called adam. An objection was raised: “Sixteen thousand human persons”! There the term distinguishes them from animals. Another verse says, “In which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left”! There too it distinguishes them from animals. But Scripture says, “Everyone who killed a person or touched a slain person must purify himself”! Perhaps an Israelite was killed. The Rabbis reply: “Not a man of ours is missing.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai understands that verse to mean none was lost through sin. Ravina said: Granted, the verse excludes them from imparting impurity through a shared covering, for it says, “An adam who dies in a tent”; does Scripture exclude them from impurity through touching or carrying?”

: “She may not go out wearing a totefet. What is a totefet? Rav Yosef said: A charm of balsam. Abaye said to him: Then let it be treated as an effective amulet and permitted! Rather, Rav Yehuda said in Abaye’s name: It is a forehead ornament. A baraita likewise teaches: A woman may go out wearing a golden hairnet, with the totefet and sarvitin fastened to it. What are the totefet and the sarvitin? Rabbi Abbahu said: The totefet surrounds her from ear to ear; the sarvitin extend to her cheeks. Rav Huna said: Poor women make them from colored materials; rich women make them from silver and gold.”

: ““Totafot”: The word appears to denote the head near the forehead, as with the totefet and sarvitin in Shabbat 57: A circlet surrounding the entire forehead. Alternatively, they are called totafot because they are on the head between the eyes, a term connected with looking, as in Megillah 14: “The goose walks bent low, but its eyes look far.” Similarly, tzitz denotes looking because it is above the space between the eyelids. Tefillin appears connected with argument, as in Sanhedrin 44, “He argued”—he made a case before his Maker—because tefillin are testimony and proof that God’s Name is called upon him, and people fear him. As Menahot 35 says, “All the peoples of the earth will see that the Lord’s Name is called upon you”—these are the tefillin on the head. From my teacher.”

: “Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: From where do we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, puts on tefillin? “Hashem swore by His right hand and by the arm of His strength.” “His right hand” means Torah, as it says, “From His right hand came a fiery law for them.” “The arm of His strength” means tefillin, as it says, “Hashem gives strength to His people.” From where do we learn that tefillin give Israel strength? “All the peoples of the earth shall see that Hashem’s name is proclaimed upon you and shall fear you.” A baraita teaches that Rabbi Eliezer the Great said: This refers to the tefillin upon the head.”

: “The Master said: “Your arm” means the fleshy upper arm. How is this derived? The Sages taught: “Upon your arm” means its upper part. Do you say it means the upper part, or perhaps the hand itself? The Torah says to place tefillin on the arm and tefillin on the head. Just as those on the head are at its upper part, so those on the arm are at its upper part. Rabbi Eliezer says: This derivation is unnecessary, for it says, “It shall be a sign for you”—a sign for you, rather than for others. Rabbi Yitzchak says: This derivation is unnecessary, for it says, “Place these words of Mine upon your hearts,” followed by “You shall bind them”: their placement must be opposite the heart. Rabbi Chiya and Rav Acha son of Rav Avya carefully placed them opposite the heart. Rav Ashi was sitting before Ameimar, who had a wound on his arm, and his tefillin could be seen. Rav Ashi asked: “Does the Master not accept ‘a sign for you,’ rather than for others?” Ameimar answered: “That was said about the place of ‘a sign for you.’””

Commentary: Rashi on Menachot 37b:4:2: ““That was said about the place of ‘a sign for you’”: a place that, for most people, is not visible to others—namely, the fleshy upper arm. If the garment is torn, it is nevertheless permitted.”

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

Parallel: Et HaOchel 16: “The first dipping, that of karpas, has the esoteric meaning taught by the Arizal: it alludes to the mental faculties of a limited state of consciousness. Its meaning corresponds to the Sages’ instruction, ‘So that the children will notice and ask.’ Asking is associated with children and the young because limited consciousness entails a lack of knowledge. Nevertheless it is already a measure of awareness: one needs these limited faculties in order to recognize that one should ask. Thus the Sages established, from Scripture’s phrase ‘When your son asks you,’ that the telling of the Exodus takes the form of questions and answers; one even asks oneself. This is the order by which the light of this night is attained: through the question one attains the answer, and through the preceding limited state the expanded state afterward shines within him.”

: “Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda said in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: From where do we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, puts on tefillin? “Hashem swore by His right hand and by the arm of His strength.” “His right hand” means Torah, as it says, “From His right hand came a fiery law for them.” “The arm of His strength” means tefillin, as it says, “Hashem gives strength to His people.” From where do we learn that tefillin give Israel strength? “All the peoples of the earth shall see that Hashem’s name is proclaimed upon you and shall fear you.” A baraita teaches that Rabbi Eliezer the Great said: This refers to the tefillin upon the head.”
: “Ascribe strength to God; His majesty is over Israel, and His strength is in the heavens.”

: “When Israel’s deeds are improper, the appointed messengers who come to stand concerning those deeds stand, as it were, against the Lord Himself. When Israel act improperly, they weaken God’s power, as it were; when they act properly, they give Him strength and power. Thus ‘Give strength to God’—through what? Proper deeds. Hence on that day all the great appointed rulers gathered against the Lord: certainly against Him, for gathering against Israel means gathering against Him.”

Parallel: Ramban on Exodus 13:16:1, concluding paragraph: “From the great, publicly known miracles a person comes to acknowledge hidden miracles, which are the foundation of the entire Torah. A person has no share in the Torah of Moses our teacher until we believe that all our affairs and occurrences are miracles, containing neither nature nor the world’s ordinary course, whether for the community or the individual. Rather, if he fulfills the commandments, his reward will bring him success; if he transgresses them, his punishment will cut him off. All is by the decree of the Most High, as I have already explained. Hidden miracles become publicly known in communal affairs when the Torah’s promised blessings and curses come to pass. Scripture says, “All the nations will say: Why has God done this to this land? They will say: Because they abandoned the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.” It will become known to all the nations that their punishment is from God. Concerning observance, it says, “All the peoples of the earth will see that God’s name is called upon you, and they will fear you.” I shall explain this further, with God’s help.”

: “Rava said: At first the Torah is called by the Holy One’s name, but ultimately it is called by the learner’s own name, as it says, “His desire is in Hashem’s Torah,” and then, “He meditates in his Torah day and night.””

: “The intention resembles the Midrash’s teaching: Three gifts were created in the world. One who merits wisdom merits everything; one who merits strength merits everything; one who merits wealth merits everything. When? When they are gifts from Heaven and come through the power of Torah. Abraham merited wisdom: he observed the whole Torah before it was given and was an elder who sat in the academy. From where did he learn Torah? No father had taught him, and he had no teacher. God instead made his two kidneys like two teachers, flowing forth and teaching him Torah and wisdom. His wisdom thus came from God’s own hand, a heavenly gift through Torah’s power, and he merited everything. Isaac merited strength, in the sense of “Who is strong? One who conquers his inclination.” This too came from God, for without God’s help a person could not overcome it; and it came through Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. Jacob merited wealth. All the patriarchs were wealthy: Abraham possessed much livestock, and Isaac grew exceedingly great, so that people preferred the manure of Isaac’s mules to Abimelech’s silver and gold. Yet they made no effort to acquire wealth; God gave it to them. Jacob, by contrast, made efforts with Laban’s sheep and the rods. Nevertheless, he knew that everything came from God. Even his own efforts, in worldly affairs and divine service alike, he attributed entirely to God, as he said, “The God who has shepherded me from my beginning.” All h

: ““Jacob was left alone.” Rabbi Elazar said: He remained behind for small vessels. From here we learn that the righteous hold their money dearer than their bodies. Why is that? Because they do not stretch out their hands to take what belongs to others.”

: “R. Simlai attended a firstborn son’s redemption. They asked him: Clearly, the child’s father recites the blessing, “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the redemption of the son.” But who recites, “Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time”—the priest or the child’s father? Does the priest bless because the benefit reaches his hand, or does the father bless because he performs the mitzvah? He did not know. He went and asked in the study hall, where they told him: The child’s father recites both blessings. The ruling is that the child’s father recites both.”

quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Toldot 5649, discourse beginning “Veyitten lekha,” paragraph 4: “On the verse “May God give you,” Rashi and the Midrash explain: if you are worthy. Yet “give” signifies a gift. The gift is indeed to come through justice as well. As I have often cited in my grandfather’s name concerning “I labored and found”: a find comes unexpectedly, so how can one say, “I labored and found”? In truth, no human exertion is proportionate to attaining the word of God. Rather, as a reward for the exertion, it is given as a gift, in the manner of a find. His explanation is well said. A gift has the advantage of supernal kindness, without measure, with a king’s generosity. Yet it has a disadvantage: one who eats what is not his own is ashamed to look upon his benefactor. God therefore arranged that both should be present together: through his deeds a person earns the readiness to receive the gift. This is “May God give you”—it remains according to justice. Of this it says, “How abundant is Your goodness that You have hidden away”: because it comes through justice, the evil eye has no power over it.”

: “Why include sin-offerings and guilt-offerings while excluding the firstborn? I include sin-offerings and guilt-offerings because their sanctity is imposed through a declaration, and exclude the firstborn because it is holy from its mother’s womb. The one who prohibits responds: A firstborn too has sanctity imposed through a declaration. For a baraita teaches in Rabbi’s name: From where do we learn that when a firstborn is born in one’s household, it is a mitzvah to consecrate it? From “The male you shall consecrate.” The one who permits responds: Even if he does not consecrate it, is it not already holy?”

: “I can explain both my reasoning and yours. Your reasoning is this: Shabbat is already fixed and established, so both in prayer and in Kiddush one says, “Who sanctifies Shabbat.” A festival is established by Israel, who intercalate the months and determine the years, so one says, “Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.””

: “Rava bar Mehasya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: A person who gives a gift to another must inform him, as it says, “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” A baraita likewise teaches: “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: I have a fine gift in My treasure house, and its name is Shabbat. I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them. From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: One who gives a child bread must inform the child’s mother.”

: “This is what the teaching means: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it over wine as it enters. This establishes the obligation at night; from where do we derive it by day? Scripture says, “Remember the Shabbat day.””

: “Likewise it says, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” Could this mean in your heart? When it says “Observe,” guarding in the heart is already stated. How, then, do I fulfill “Remember”? By repeating it with your mouth.”
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”

: “He selected the first portion for himself, for there the lawgiver’s portion was concealed. He came with the leaders of the people; he carried out Hashem’s righteousness and His judgments with Israel.”

: “R. Shimon ben Lakish said: “Jacob called to his sons and said, Gather together and I will tell you.” Jacob wished to reveal the end of days to his sons, but the Divine Presence withdrew from him. He said, “Perhaps, God forbid, there is an unfit descendant among my children, as Ishmael came from Abraham and Esau from my father Isaac?” His sons said to him, “Hear, Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.” They meant: Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts. At that moment our father Jacob began and said, “Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.” The Sages said: What should we do? If we say it, Moses our teacher did not say it; if we do not say it, Jacob said it. They instituted its quiet recitation. R. Isaac said, reporting the school of R. Ami: This resembles a princess who smelled the seasoned residue of a cooked dish. If she asks for it, she is embarrassed; if she does not, she suffers. Her servants began bringing it to her secretly.”

: “Therefore the masters of Mishnah explained: study is not the principal thing, but action. God is concealed within the Torah’s secrets; through what is He known? Through the commandments, which are His Shekhinah, His likeness. As He is humble, His Shekhinah is humility; He is pious and she is pious; He is mighty and she is mistress over all nations; He is truth and she is faith; He is prophet and she prophetess; He is righteous and she righteous; He is King and she kingship; He is wise and she wisdom; He understands and she is His understanding; He is Crown and she His crown, a crown of beauty. Therefore the Rabbis ruled: anyone whose inside does not match his outside should not enter the study hall. This mirrors God: He is the inside and the Shekhinah the outside. He is within; she is without. The outside does not differ from the inside, making known that she is His emanation, without any separation at all: ‘Within and without you shall cover it.’”

: “Come and see: the lowest of all the levels was struck first. Rabbi Shimon said: God began from the lowest, and His hand struck with every finger. When He reached the highest of all levels, He Himself performed His act, passing through Egypt and killing all. He therefore killed every firstborn in Egypt, for this is the upper level and firstborn of all.”

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they said: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed? Did the Holy One, blessed be He, not tell Abraham, “They shall enslave and afflict them for four hundred years,” yet we have only two hundred and ten? He replied: Since He desires your redemption, He does not look at your calculations, but “leaps over the mountains.” The mountains and hills here signify appointed times and added periods: He leaps over calculations, appointed times, and added periods. You are being redeemed this month, as it says, “This month shall be yours, the first of months.” Rabbi Nechemya said: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they asked: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed, when we have no good deeds? He replied: Since He desires your redemption, He does not look at your evil deeds. At whom does He look? At your righteous people and their deeds, such as Amram and his court. “Leaping over mountains, bounding over hills”—mountains signify courts, as in, “I shall go down upon the mountains.” You are being redeemed this month, as it says, “This month shall be yours, the first of months.” The Rabbis said: “The voice of my beloved! Here he comes”—this is Moses. When he told Israel, “You are being redeemed this month,” they said: Moses our teacher, how can we be redeemed when all Egypt is

: “He began: ‘This month shall be yours, the head of months.’ Do not all seasons and months belong to God? Rather: ‘This month shall be yours’—it is Mine, but I hand it over to you. Yours is revealed; the seventh is Mine, and therefore concealed rather than revealed. Your month follows the order of the letters: aviv, alef-bet-gimel; yod-bet is the mystery of gimel. An alternative reading says simply that it follows the letters in order. My seventh month, however, comes from the alphabet’s end—Tishrei. Why? You go from below upward, while I go from above downward.”

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

: “Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak asked Rav Chiya bar Avin: “What is written in the Master of the world’s tefillin?” He answered: “‘Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?’” Does the Holy One, blessed be He, glory in Israel’s praise? Yes, for it says, “You have singled out Hashem this day,” and, “Hashem has singled you out this day.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: “You have made Me unique in the world, and I will make you unique in the world. You made Me unique by saying, ‘Hear, Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.’ I will make you unique, as it says, ‘Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?’””

: “When Pharaoh sent the people away, God did not lead them along the road through the Philistines’ land, although it was near, for God said, “The people might change their minds when they see war and return to Egypt.””

: ““It happened in the days of Ahasuerus”: Rabbi Levi—or, according to another version, Rabbi Yonatan—said: We have a tradition from the Men of the Great Assembly that wherever “It happened” is stated, it expresses distress. “It happened in the days of Ahasuerus”—there was Haman. … Rav Ashi said: “It happened” can occur in either a joyful or a sorrowful setting; “It happened in the days of” always expresses distress.”

: “Another interpretation: “It happened when Pharaoh sent out…” This is what Scripture says: “Thus says the Lord of hosts: The children of Israel and the children of Judah are oppressed… Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is His name.” To what may this be compared? A man owned an orchard. His friend asked him to sell it, and he sold it for one maneh, without knowing what it contained. They asked: For how much did you sell the orchard? He said: One maneh. They told him: It contains olives worth a hundred maneh, vines worth a hundred, pomegranates worth a hundred, kinds of spices worth a hundred—and each variety is worth a hundred. Did you not know what you were selling, and what the orchard contained—“henna with nard, nard and saffron”? Had the purchaser acquired only its springs, that would suffice: “A spring of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.” The seller began to regret it. So Pharaoh, when he sent Israel away, regarded them as nothing. His royal officials said: What have you done? Their spoil alone would have sufficed, as it says, “A mixed multitude also went up with them.” Moreover, how many wealthy people, wise people, and skilled craftsmen were among them: “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.” How many men, women, and children there were: “All their captors held them fast”! What follows? “Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is His name.” At that moment he began crying, “Woe, woe!” Hence: “It happened when he sent out.”

: “Another interpretation: “It happened when Pharaoh sent out…” When Pharaoh sent the people, who cried “Woe”? Pharaoh. It is like a king whose son traveled to a province and lodged with a wealthy man, who received the prince warmly. When the king heard who had received his son and in which province he was, he sent letters to the man: Send My son! He sent repeatedly, at every time and hour, until he went and brought his son out himself. The man began crying because the prince had left his house. His neighbors asked: Why are you crying? He said: It was an honor for me when the prince stayed with me: the king wrote me letters, attended to me, and esteemed me. Now that the prince has left, the king has no business with me. Therefore I cry. So Pharaoh said: When Israel was with me, the Holy One, blessed be He, attended to me and esteemed me, sending me messages continually: “Thus says the Lord, God of the Hebrews: Send My people.” Pharaoh heard Moses say, “Send My son,” yet would not send them. When the Holy One, blessed be He, descended to Egypt and brought Israel out, as it says, “I have descended to rescue him from Egypt’s hand,” Pharaoh began crying: Woe, that I sent Israel away! Therefore it says, “It happened when Pharaoh sent out.””

: “Has any god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from within another nation—with trials, signs, wonders, warfare, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors—like everything Hashem your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua bar Nechemya said in Rabbi Chanan ben Pazi’s name: “A nation from within a nation.” It does not say “a people from within a nation,” but “a nation from within a nation”: these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised; these grew forelocks and those grew forelocks. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Shmuel bar Nachman said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed from Egypt. Why? “Therefore say to the children of Israel…” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: It is written, “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”
: “But against any of the Israelites, from person to animal, not even a dog will sharpen its tongue, so that you may know that Hashem distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.”

: “In this portion it says, “Against all the children of Israel no dog shall sharpen its tongue, against man or beast.” The dog means the impure power of Amalek. The Zohar explains that the ox and donkey are the impure powers of Esau and Ishmael; when they join, their combined force produces what is called a dog. “I shall hand you over to the dog”—and immediately, “Amalek came.” As we have explained, the inner letters of shor and chamor have the numerical value of kelev, “dog.” Yet it is only a dog that barks, “How are these different from those?” Its chief accusation concerns the holiness of the covenant. Amalek cut off Israel’s circumcisions and cast them upward, challenging the truth of “Your people are all righteous,” since some Jews also damage this holiness. Of Haman, his descendant, the Gemara says, “No one knew how to speak slander like Haman”: he accused Israel above of being asleep in regard to the commandments, including its sages. This accusation also arose during the Exodus: “How are these different from those?””

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: When Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them. Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina explained this in his father’s name: It is like a shepherd taking his flock across a river. A wolf came to attack the flock. The experienced shepherd took a large goat and gave it to the wolf, saying: Let it struggle with this until we cross the river; afterward I will retrieve it. So, when Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, until now these people worshipped idols, and You are splitting the sea for them! What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He handed him Job, who had been one of Pharaoh’s advisers and of whom it is written, “A blameless and upright man.” He told him: He is in your hand. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: While he is occupied with Job, Israel will enter the sea and emerge, and afterward I will rescue Job.”

: “When Israel approached the sea and God wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, Egypt’s appointed ruler, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: ‘Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All are guilty before You, and all Your ways are judgment and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and those worship stars and constellations; these commit sexual transgressions, and those commit sexual transgressions; these shed blood, and those shed blood.’”

: “Rabbi Benaya says: In Abraham’s merit I split the sea for them, because of what he did, as it says, “He split the wood for the burnt offering,” and, “The waters were split.” Rabbi Akiva says: In Jacob’s merit I split the sea for them, as it says, “You shall spread out westward and eastward.””

ref: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Vayehi Beshalach 4
quote: : “Rabbi Akiva says: Through the merit of their father Jacob I split the sea for them, as it says, “Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out westward and eastward.””

: “Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth. You will spread out westward, eastward, northward, and southward, and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you and through your descendants.”

: ““You will surely fall before him”: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai expounded: Why are two expressions of falling used? They told Haman: This nation is compared to dust and to the stars. When they descend, they descend to the dust; when they rise, they rise to the stars.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, gave Jacob a sign, telling him, “Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth.” When your children reach the dust of the earth, at that moment, “You shall spread out westward and eastward.” Thus: “He raises the poor from the dust.” The Holy One, blessed be He, exalted them above all.”
: “As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.”
: “R. Alexandri said: R. Joshua ben Levi contrasted the verses, “At its time” and “I will hasten it.” If they merit, “I will hasten it”; if they do not merit, “at its time.””

quote: : “The Midrash Rabbah then asks: Who cried “woe”? Moses cried “woe,” saying, “I shall not enter the land with them.” Moses’ cry is also connected with “when Pharaoh sent them,” which indicates that Israel had not yet attained perfection through their own effort. They were not worthy to leave with an uplifted hand without Pharaoh’s permission; rather, they departed with his consent, as we explained, and would therefore still require further exiles. From this Moses knew that he would not enter the land with them. For had he entered with them, Israel would never again have been subjected to any exile, as stated in Megalleh Amukot. Seeing that they had not departed with an uplifted hand without permission, but that Pharaoh had consented and sent them, Moses cried “woe” because he would not enter the land with them.”

: “Come and see: when Israel left Egypt, their spirits were broken within them. They heard those praises but could not rejoice. When all the hosts and chariots went forth with the Shekhinah, they all raised praises and songs before God. God stirred Israel’s spirits; they heard those praises, and their spirits remained within them rather than flying away. When a person ceases his labor, he then recognizes the brokenness of his bones and spirit. So too, when Israel left Egypt, they then tasted death, and the Holy One, blessed be He, healed them, as it says, ‘The Lord went before them by day.’ All the roads gave off healing fragrances, which entered their bodies and healed them. The sounds of praise they heard brought joy and rest to their spirits.”
: “A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, concerning shigyonot.”
: “Hashem, I heard the report of You and was afraid. Hashem, revive Your work amid the years; amid the years make it known. In anger, remember compassion.”
: “A prayer of the afflicted person when he grows faint and pours out his plea before Hashem.”
: “A prayer of David. Incline Your ear, Hashem, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.”
: “A prayer of Moses, the man of God. My Lord, You have been a dwelling place for us from generation to generation.”

k: volume-i|905|0|Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah
ref: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 2:2
quote: : “What is the path to loving and fearing Him? When a person contemplates His wondrous, great works and creatures, and sees in them His wisdom, which has neither measure nor end, he immediately loves, praises, and glorifies Him and yearns intensely to know the great Name. As David said, 'My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.' When he considers these very things, he immediately recoils in fear and recognizes that he is a small, lowly, obscure creature, standing with slight and limited understanding before the One perfect in knowledge. As David said, 'When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers...what is man that You remember him?' Accordingly, I explain broad principles concerning the works of the Master of the worlds, so that they may offer an opening for an understanding person to love God. As the sages said regarding love: through this you come to recognize the One who spoke and the world came into being.”

: ““Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did the Lord desire you.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: I desire you because even when I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me. I gave greatness to Abraham, and he said, “I am dust and ashes”; to Moses and Aaron, and they said, “What are we?”; to David, and he said, “I am a worm and not a man.” The nations are otherwise. I gave greatness to Nimrod, and he said, “Let us build ourselves a city”; to Pharaoh, and he said, “Who is the Lord?”; to Sennacherib, and he said, “Who among all the gods of the lands?”; to Nebuchadnezzar, and he said, “I will ascend above the heights of the cloud”; to Hiram king of Tyre, and he said, “I have sat in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.” Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yohanan said: What was said of Moses and Aaron is greater than what was said of Abraham. Of Abraham it is written, “I am dust and ashes,” while of Moses and Aaron it is written, “What are we?””
: “At that time I pleaded with Hashem, saying:”

: “‘I pleaded with the Lord.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘The poor speak in supplications, but the rich answer harshly.’ Rabbi Tanchuma said: ‘The poor speak in supplications’ refers to Moses, who approached his Creator with pleas. ‘The rich answer harshly’ refers to the One who possesses the riches of the world—the Holy One, blessed be He—who answered him firmly: ‘Do not continue speaking to Me.’”

: “Rav Nahman said in Rav’s name: What is meant by “The poor person speaks entreaties, but the rich person answers harshly”? “The poor person speaks entreaties”—this is Moses. “The rich person answers harshly”—this is Joshua.”
: “But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach among people and despised by the nation.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? It is the utterance of David son of Jesse, who established the yoke of repentance.”

Commentary: Rashi on Moed Katan 16b:21:1: ““He established the yoke of repentance”: He was the first to return and thereby provided a path for those who repent. As the opening chapter of Avodah Zarah teaches, David was not suited to that deed; rather, when an individual sins, people tell him, “Go to David: the Holy One forgave that sin of his. You too should return in repentance.””

: “It was taught: R. Meir used to say: Great is repentance, for because of one individual who repents, the whole world is forgiven, as it says, “I will heal their waywardness; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.” It does not say “from them,” but “from him.””
: “David called it “impure,” as it says, “Create a pure heart for me, God,” implying the presence of an impure heart.”

: “When a person wishes to draw near to Hashem’s holiness, the Holy One shines upon him from the holiness of Atika, beyond the reach of human understanding. He apprehends the life of holiness without any intervening screen, and his whole being is filled with light. This is the meaning of Sefer HaRokeach’s statement, “No strength equals the strength of piety at its beginning.” Through that great light, a longing and desire for holiness burn in his heart with tremendous force. Yet this light lasts only for a time, so that he may see that the light of His divinity exists in the world. That light is then concealed from him, and he sees everything he has done against Hashem’s will throughout his past. His heart breaks within him, and no spirit remains in him. He prays to the Holy One with all his heart and returns in complete repentance. This resembles David’s prayer: “Create a pure heart for me.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach Sheni 2, paragraph 2: “It is known that on the first night of Passover, when ‘the Lord passed over,’ there was an awakening from above, from God’s side: He caused the light of His holiness to shine in the hearts of Israel with great clarity. Afterward that light withdrew, leaving in Israel’s hearts a longing for the light they had merited on Passover night. For this reason we were commanded to count seven weeks, corresponding to the seven holy qualities, so that through an awakening of our own we might purify ourselves and become sevenfold refined by Shavuot, ready to receive the Torah in holiness and purity.”

k: volume-i|915|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkut
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 31:6–7: “In truth, a broken heart and the soul’s bitterness over its distance from the light of God’s countenance and its enclosure in the other side are not called “sadness” at all in the holy tongue. Sadness means that the heart is blocked like a stone and has no vitality. Bitterness and a broken heart are the opposite: there is life in the heart, allowing it to be moved and to feel bitterness. This vitality comes from the holy severities, whereas joy comes from kindnesses; the heart includes both. At times one must awaken the holy severities in order to sweeten the judgments—the animal soul and evil inclination when they rule over a person, God forbid—for judgments are sweetened only at their root. Therefore our Sages said that a person should always stir his good inclination against his evil inclination. This applies whenever he sees within himself that it is needed.”

: “‘The Lord went before them by day’: the Holy One, blessed be He, and His court. Rabbi Yitzchak said: this is what we learned, that the Shekhinah travels with the patriarchs. ‘Went before them by day’ is Abraham; ‘in a pillar of cloud’ is Isaac; ‘to guide them on the way’ is Jacob, of whom it says, ‘Jacob went on his way.’ ‘At night in a pillar of fire to give them light’ is King David.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah bar Simon said: With the light by which the world was created, Adam could see from one end of the world to the other. When the Holy One, blessed be He, saw that the deeds of the generations of Enosh, the Flood, and the Dispersion were corrupt, He concealed that light from them, as it says, ‘Their light is withheld from the wicked.’ For whom did He conceal it? For the righteous in the future, as it says, ‘God saw that the light was good’—and ‘good’ means the righteous, as it says, ‘Say of the righteous that it is good.’ How do we know that He concealed it for the righteous? It says, “The path of the righteous is like radiant light.” Upon seeing that the light was stored for the righteous, he rejoiced, as it says, “The light of the righteous rejoices.” Rabbi Levi said in Rabbi Nezira’s name: That light served for thirty-six hours: twelve on Friday, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. When Adam sinned, He wished to conceal it, but accorded honor to Shabbat, as it says, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ With what did He bless it? With light. When the sun set at the beginning of Shabbat, that light continued to shine, and everyone began praising the Holy One, blessed be He.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 8, paragraph 1: “We must understand what it means that deliberate sins become unintentional ones. If the sin has been entirely forgiven, no trace should remain; if it has not been forgiven, the act was intentional. The matter follows the rule that a thought cannot undo an act, although a thought can undo another thought that has not become an act; similarly, speech can cancel speech. When a person deliberately transgresses, the damage lies both in the act and in the thought, since he acted intentionally and defiantly. When he takes the punishment to heart, he regrets and retracts the past in thought, and also in speech, through repentance and confession. This uproots the original sinful intention. The sinful act, however, remains, like the act of someone who transgressed without intention; hence the sins become unintentional ones. Some damage from the deed still remains and requires atonement and affliction. In repentance from love, by contrast, God shines upon the person and repairs the deed itself, so that it becomes a merit. He is therefore more elevated than someone righteous from the outset: he possesses new merits that the original righteous person cannot attain. As the Zohar says, there is no light like that which emerges from darkness and no good like that which emerges from evil; then it becomes ‘very good.’”

: “Another interpretation: “It happened when Pharaoh sent out…” This is what Scripture says: “Thus says the Lord of hosts: The children of Israel and the children of Judah are oppressed… Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is His name.” To what may this be compared? A man owned an orchard. His friend asked him to sell it, and he sold it for one maneh, without knowing what it contained. They asked: For how much did you sell the orchard? He said: One maneh. They told him: It contains olives worth a hundred maneh, vines worth a hundred, pomegranates worth a hundred, kinds of spices worth a hundred—and each variety is worth a hundred. Did you not know what you were selling, and what the orchard contained—“henna with nard, nard and saffron”? Had the purchaser acquired only its springs, that would suffice: “A spring of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.” The seller began to regret it. So Pharaoh, when he sent Israel away, regarded them as nothing. His royal officials said: What have you done? Their spoil alone would have sufficed, as it says, “A mixed multitude also went up with them.” Moreover, how many wealthy people, wise people, and skilled craftsmen were among them: “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.” How many men, women, and children there were: “All their captors held them fast”! What follows? “Their Redeemer is strong; the Lord of hosts is His name.” At that moment he began crying, “Woe, woe!” Hence: “It happened when he sent out.”

: “Another interpretation: “It happened when Pharaoh sent out…” When Pharaoh sent the people, who cried “Woe”? Pharaoh. It is like a king whose son traveled to a province and lodged with a wealthy man, who received the prince warmly. When the king heard who had received his son and in which province he was, he sent letters to the man: Send My son! He sent repeatedly, at every time and hour, until he went and brought his son out himself. The man began crying because the prince had left his house. His neighbors asked: Why are you crying? He said: It was an honor for me when the prince stayed with me: the king wrote me letters, attended to me, and esteemed me. Now that the prince has left, the king has no business with me. Therefore I cry. So Pharaoh said: When Israel was with me, the Holy One, blessed be He, attended to me and esteemed me, sending me messages continually: “Thus says the Lord, God of the Hebrews: Send My people.” Pharaoh heard Moses say, “Send My son,” yet would not send them. When the Holy One, blessed be He, descended to Egypt and brought Israel out, as it says, “I have descended to rescue him from Egypt’s hand,” Pharaoh began crying: Woe, that I sent Israel away! Therefore it says, “It happened when Pharaoh sent out.””
: “They said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.””
: “When you go out to war against your enemies, and Hashem your God delivers them into your hand, you shall take their captives.”

k: volume-i|922|0|Ibn Ezra, Long Commentary on Exodus 14:1
quote: Parallel: Ibn Ezra, Long Commentary on Exodus 14:13:1: ““Stand and see the Lord’s deliverance”: you will not wage war; you will only see the deliverance that the Lord will bring you today. One must ask: how could a great camp of six hundred thousand men fear those pursuing them? Why would they not fight for their lives and their children? The answer is that the Egyptians had been Israel’s masters. The generation leaving Egypt had learned from its youth to endure Egypt’s yoke, and its spirit was lowly. How could it now fight its masters? Israel was weak and untrained for war. See how Amalek came with only a small force; without Moses’ prayer, it would have overcome Israel. God alone, who does great things and before whom deeds are weighed, arranged that all the men who had left Egypt should die, for they lacked the strength to fight the Canaanites, until another generation arose—the generation of the wilderness, which had not experienced exile. Their spirit was elevated, as I explained concerning Moses in the portion “These are the names.””

: “Although Rabbi Akiva said, “Make your Shabbat like a weekday rather than depend on others,” nevertheless a person should take a little meat and a little wine, without excessive meat and wine. If he indulges excessively, Scripture testifies against him: “Do not be among wine-drinkers, among those who gorge on meat, for the drunkard and glutton will become poor.” If a person has not merited to ask for mercy that words of Torah enter his inward parts, he should at least ask for mercy that excessive food and drink not enter them, as it says, “I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.” Just as a furnace burns and consumes all the wood in the world you put into it, so a human throat swallows and consumes all the fine foods in the world you put into it.”
: “Rabbi Elazar was eating terumah when the Angel of Death appeared to him. He said to him, “I am eating terumah; is it not called holy?” The appointed moment passed him by.”
: ““I give you your priesthood as a service of gift, and the outsider who approaches shall die.” They treated the eating of terumah outside the Temple as equivalent to Temple service.”

Parallel: Et HaOchel 11: “It is impossible to exist without nourishment, for God established that every finite creature needs nourishment to sustain its life. Only then, in the future, nourishment will be stripped of its garment and will consist of the radiance of the Divine Presence. In this world it is clothed in a garment; the blessing is the recognition of what lies within that garment, in its interior. Just as the serpent’s bread is dust—even amid every delicacy, it tastes dust, the lowest element of the world of action—so the person separated from the serpent’s power, meaning the power of craving, tastes only God’s life-force clothed within the food, even while eating every delicacy. Rabbi Judah the Patriarch exemplified this: he did not die, like our father Jacob, and was entirely free of the serpent’s corruption.”

: “Some say: There is also a prohibition here; rather, Rav Yosef’s statement was made about the latter clause. From the first clause we could not learn that performing the mitzvah personally is preferable to using an agent, since its reason might be the prohibition: A man who can betroth her himself but uses an agent acts improperly, lest she later become repulsive to him. If he had already seen her, however, that concern would disappear, and one might allow an agent even initially. From the latter clause we can learn that personal performance is always preferable. For a woman there is no concern that she will see something repulsive in him, as Reish Lakish says, “It is better to sit as two than to sit widowed”—a saying women apply to any husband. Tan means a body, and du means two. Nevertheless, the Mishnah teaches that her own participation is preferable to an agent’s. Although a woman is not commanded to have children, she still performs a mitzvah because she helps her husband fulfill his commandment. You might ask: Here too, if he gives the betrothal to her agent without seeing her, is there not a prohibition? Indeed there is. But the Mishnah’s latter clause concerns her, saying that she may become betrothed personally or through her agent. Its mention of personal participation therefore teaches a mitzvah, since no prohibition applies on her side. The first clause, which concerns him, mentions personal participation because of the prohibition.”

: “The Friday-night meal is called “the meal of the field of holy apples.” This follows the exposition of “like the fragrance of a field blessed by Hashem” as the fragrance of an apple field. The Midrash says that the Garden of Eden entered with Jacob. These are one idea, for the souls of Israel are called apples. The attribute of the Congregation of Israel—the garden in which Israel’s souls dwell—is called an apple field, or, in the Zohar’s language, “the field of holy apples.” At the entrance of Shabbat, Israel attains the quality of apples, just as at the giving of the Torah on Shabbat, when they put “we shall do” before “we shall hear.” The lower garden, the attribute of the Congregation of Israel, is the field of holy apples.”

: “Shammai wanted his eating to be a meal of a commandment. He therefore prepared everything for Shabbat and ate in order to leave something better for Shabbat, experiencing in his eating the commandment’s delight of Shabbat. With Hillel, however, Vayikra Rabbah 34 says, 'One who shows kindness to his soul is a man of kindness' refers to Hillel the Elder. He said he was going to show kindness to the guest within his house, asking, 'Is this poor soul not a guest?' Thus, 'He had a different quality, for all his deeds were for Heaven': all his eating was a meal of a commandment. He felt no bodily pleasure, but was like someone feeding a guest and fulfilling the commandment of kindness; he did not need Shammai’s method. Every holy person similarly seeks to make his eating a meal of a commandment.”
: “A prayer of the prophet Habakkuk, concerning shigyonot.”
: “One day Elisha passed through Shunem. A prominent woman was there, and she urged him to eat bread. Whenever he passed through, he would turn aside there to eat bread.”

: “We learned: Elisha attained in this world what no other prophet except Moses attained; nevertheless, he did not wish to trouble his Master. Come and see: ‘One day Elisha passed through Shunem, where there was a great woman.’ Why ‘a great woman’? Great in her deeds: all her household praised her, and she was the household’s foundation. Because her husband was not present at home as its foundation, she, rather than he, was mentioned.”
: “Hebron’s former name was Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. The land rested from warfare.”

k: volume-i|932|2|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 44a, pre
quote: : “‘Great, above all the other women of the world’: a marginal gloss suggests that this was because she was a reincarnation of Eve. He is called ‘the great man,’ and she is called ‘a great woman.’”

: “Rabbi Benaah was marking burial caves. When he reached Abraham’s cave, he found Abraham’s servant Eliezer standing at its entrance. He asked, “What is Abraham doing?” Eliezer answered, “He lies in Sarah’s lap while she examines his hair.” He said, “Go and tell him that Benaah is standing at the entrance.” Abraham answered, “Let him enter. It is well known that there is no evil inclination in this world.” Rabbi Benaah entered, inspected the cave, and left. When he reached Adam’s cave, a heavenly voice declared: “You have looked upon the likeness of My image; do not look upon My image itself.” He protested: “But I need to mark the cave!” He was answered: “The inner chamber has the same dimensions as the outer chamber.” According to the view that they were two chambers one above the other: “The lower chamber has the same dimensions as the upper chamber.” Rabbi Benaah said: “I looked at his two heels, and they resembled two orbs of the sun.””
: “She said to her husband, “I know that the man who regularly passes our way is a holy man of God.””

: “Rav said: The evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two entrances to the heart, as it says, “Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink and bubble.” Shmuel said: It resembles a grain of wheat, as it says, “Sin crouches at the opening.””

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “When Shabbat enters, a herald proclaims throughout the heavens: ‘Prepare, chariots; prepare, camps, to meet your Master.’ A spirit then issues from the south and spreads over all the right side’s hosts and camps, clothing them. This spirit is called Shabbat’s garment of glory. Then this world’s tables are arranged within a palace. Happy is the person whose table’s arrangement appears there properly prepared, without shame, each according to his ability.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: One who wishes to become wise should turn south, and one who wishes to become wealthy should turn north. Remember this by the table in the north and the menorah in the south.
