Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: He should always turn south, for through becoming wise he becomes wealthy, as it says, “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, wealth and honor.” But did Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi not say that the Divine Presence is in the west? He should incline somewhat to the side while facing west.”

: “Rabbi Yaakov said in Rabbi Chiyya’s name—another reading has Rabbi Akiva—that our father Jacob is the Throne of Glory. The school of Elijah likewise taught: our father Jacob is a throne in his own right, as in ‘I shall remember My covenant with Jacob.’ God made a covenant with Jacob himself beyond all his fathers, making him a Throne of Glory, apart from the first.”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”

: “Jacob is the body, encompassing the holiness of all Israel’s bodies, who are his descendants. Moses is the soul, the root of all Israel’s souls: the totality of 600,000, deriving from the 600,000 letters and portions of letters in the Torah. Moses our teacher encompasses all the Torah’s letters, and it is called 'the Torah of Moses.' Scripture says, 'Moses commanded us Torah,' although it should have said 'Moses wrote' or 'Moses spoke,' since God commanded. Rather, Moses caused this to shine within Israel: Torah’s words are 'the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.' Vayikra Rabbah says, 'It does not say the inheritance of the congregation of Yannai, but the congregation of Jacob.' Thus, even ignorant people, whose deliberate sins count as inadvertent because they do not know what is forbidden, and who are called 'the house of Jacob,' nevertheless possess a share in Torah.”

k: volume-i|941|0|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 44a, pre
quote: : “‘Great, above all the other women of the world’: a marginal gloss suggests that this was because she was a reincarnation of Eve. He is called ‘the great man,’ and she is called ‘a great woman.’”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘How long shall the world continue in darkness? Let light come!’ ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to Abraham, as it says, ‘Who aroused righteousness from the east?’ Read not he’ir, ‘aroused,’ but he’ir, ‘illuminated.’”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “The promise the Holy One, blessed be He, made to women is greater than the promise to men, as it says, “Women at ease, arise and hear my voice; confident daughters, listen to my words.” Rav asked Rabbi Chiya: “Through what do women gain this merit?” Through bringing their children to the synagogue for instruction, enabling their husbands to study in the Sages’ house, and waiting for their husbands until they return from the Sages’ house.”
: “She went upstairs and laid him upon the bed of the man of God, shut the door upon him, and went out.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

: “Why? Prayer is not that audible voice; the voice that is heard is not prayer. What is prayer? Another voice depending upon the audible voice. What is the audible voice? The voice spelled with vav. The voice depending upon it is qol spelled without vav.”

: ““I praised joy” means the joy of a mitzvah; “What does joy accomplish?” means joy that is not of a mitzvah. This teaches that the Divine Presence rests upon a person neither through sadness, idleness, laughter, frivolity, conversation, nor idle talk, but through the joy of a mitzvah, as it says, “Now bring me a musician”; and when the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon him. Rav Yehuda said: The same applies to a halakhic teaching. Rava said: The same applies to a good dream. Is that so? Rav Giddel said in Rav’s name: Any Torah scholar who sits before his teacher and whose lips do not drip bitterness should have his lips burned, as it says, “His lips are lilies dripping flowing myrrh.” Read “flowing bitterness” instead of “flowing myrrh,” and “those who study” instead of “lilies.” There is no difficulty: one teaching concerns the teacher and the other the student. Alternatively, both concern the teacher: one concerns the time before he begins, and the other the time after he begins. Thus Rabba, before beginning his teaching, would say something amusing, and the Sages would become cheerful. Then he would sit in awe and begin his discourse.”
: “They journeyed from Sukkot and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.”
: “He made the letter tav king, bound a crown upon it, and through it formed the moon in the universe, Shabbat in the year, and the mouth in the person.”

: “Rabbi Shimon began: ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.’ The ayin is large, and so is the dalet; together they form ed, ‘witness,’ as in ‘The Lord is witness among you.’ The letters shin-mem remain, with an open mem. Why is it not closed? The closed mem is the upper King—an alternative reading says upper world; the open mem is the lower King, or lower world. From the other word, alef-chet remain. ‘The glory of God is to conceal a matter.’”

: “Rabbi Abba asked: what is ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Were Israel so foolish that they did not know this? They saw the Shekhinah before them and clouds of glory surrounding them. Those who saw their King’s glorious radiance at the sea—for we learned that a maidservant saw at the sea what Ezekiel did not see—could they be foolish enough to ask, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Rather, Rabbi Shimon explained: they wished to distinguish between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, called Nothingness, and Ze‘ir Anpin, called the Lord. Thus it does not say, ‘Is the Lord among us or not?’ as in ‘Will he follow My Torah or not?’ It says, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’”
: “God led the people around by the wilderness road toward the Sea of Reeds. The Israelites went up from Egypt equipped for battle.”

: “‘God led the people around by the wilderness route of the Sea of Reeds’—to prepare the road to His place. Rabbi Yehudah asked: while Israel were in Egypt, why did it say ‘Send My people away,’ ‘If you refuse to send My people away,’ and ‘My firstborn son, Israel,’ although they were then uncircumcised and not properly bound to Him? Now that they were circumcised, had performed Passover and were bound to Him, why does He call them merely ‘the people’? Because the mixed multitude had attached themselves and mingled with them, He calls them simply ‘the people,’ as in ‘The Lord struck the people because they made the calf,’ ‘The people gathered around Aaron,’ and ‘The people saw that Moses delayed.’ So it is throughout.”

: “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah taught: Israel saw here what Ezekiel son of Buzi did not see, and all cleaved to precious upper Wisdom. Israel saw five levels of voices at Sinai, and Torah was given through these five levels. The fifth is ‘the voice of the shofar.’ Corresponding to them, Ezekiel saw five levels outside these: storm wind, a great cloud, flashing fire, radiance surrounding it and the appearance of Chashmal.”
: “For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: All the prophets’ prophecies concern penitents; as for the completely righteous, “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu, who said: In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand, as it says, “Peace, peace, to the far and to the near”—first the far, then the near. Rabbi Yochanan would explain: “Far” means one who was far from transgression from the outset; “near” means one who was once close to transgression but has now distanced himself from it.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach Sheni 2, paragraph 2: “In truth, both opinions are words of the living God. A wholly righteous person who advances from strength to strength throughout his life without falling short stands at a greater level than a penitent. As the Zohar says of ‘Abraham was old, advanced in days,’ his deeds brought him near each day, from level to level. The penitent, however, separates himself from his deeds and leaps from darkness into the light of God’s holiness, outside the orderly pathways of life. Menachot 29b explains why the leg of the letter heh is suspended: if a person returns in repentance, he can be brought in there. The Gemara asks why he cannot enter through the other opening, and answers that he would not be assisted. He cannot return by the way through which he went out, but only through a power above him and beyond human understanding. God has mercy on him and suddenly brings him into His palace. As the Zohar says, penitents draw near to God in one hour and one moment. In this particular dimension he is greater than the wholly righteous person.”
: “Hashem strengthened the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and he pursued the Israelites, while the Israelites were going out with a raised hand.”

k: volume-i|960|0|Ohr Zarua, Volume I, Alpha Beta 5:2
ref: Ohr Zarua, Volume I, Alpha Beta 5:2
quote: : “Alef has the letters of afel, 'dark.' This is the meaning of 'If you bring forth the precious from the worthless, you shall be like My mouth.' In Bava Metzia, chapter HaSokher et HaPoalim, we read: Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name—or, according to another version, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, or Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name—anyone who teaches his fellow’s son Torah merits to sit in the heavenly academy, as it says, 'If you bring back, I will bring you back; you shall stand before Me.' If you restore Israel through your rebuke, I will bring you back to Me and you will stand before Me. Anyone who teaches the son of an ignorant person Torah—even when the Holy One, blessed be He, issues a decree, He annuls it for his sake, as it says, 'If you bring forth the precious from the worthless, you shall be like My mouth': you possess the power to annul My decree. Thus, teaching the son of an ignorant person, who is dark and obscure in the world, is greater than teaching the son of one’s fellow who is a Torah scholar. This is our exposition of alef as afel: teach Torah to the son of an ignorant person, who is dark in the world because he has no Torah. A person without Torah is called am haaretz, meaning one who is dark in the land, just as 'the affliction has faded' is translated 'the affliction has become dim.' Ordinarily the son of an ignorant person does not know Torah, since he has not learned it from his father. Therefore you, who k

: “The soul is called by five names: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, yechidah, and chayyah. Nefesh is the blood, as it says, ‘For the blood is the nefesh.’ Ruach ascends and descends, as it says, ‘Who knows whether the spirit of human beings ascends upward?’ Neshamah is one’s disposition, as people say, ‘His disposition is good.’ It is called chayyah because all the limbs are lifeless, while it lives within the body; and yechidah because all the limbs come in pairs, while it is alone within the body.”

: “He said to him: This is what I was asking you: In relation to what did David say these five instances of “Bless Hashem, O my soul”? He said them in relation to the Holy One, blessed be He, and to the soul. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the entire world, the soul fills the entire body. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, sees but is not seen, the soul sees but is not seen. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, nourishes the whole world, the soul nourishes the whole body. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, is pure, the soul is pure. Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells in the innermost chambers, the soul dwells in the innermost chambers. Let the one possessing these five qualities come and praise the One possessing these five qualities.”

: “The Tanchuma, on “Abraham was old,” cites “Bless Hashem, my soul.” Why did David choose the soul with which to bless the Holy One? Because the soul sees without being seen and guards the body. The Midrash lists two qualities here. The Gemara in Berakhot lists five “Bless Hashem, my soul” passages corresponding to the soul, and names five qualities. These correspond to the five levels of the soul listed in Bereshit Rabbah: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah and yechidah. They correspond to the four letters of Hashem’s Name and the tip of the yod, which alludes to the supreme Keter. Nefesh derives from Malkhut, the lower heh; ruach from Tiferet, the vav of the holy Name; and neshamah from the upper heh. The soul of the soul contains two levels: chayah, from the yod, Chokhmah, and yechidah, from the yod’s upper tip, alluding to the supreme Keter. Scripture and the Midrash use nefesh, whereas the Gemara speaks of neshamah. Just as every sefirah includes all ten sefirot, so each soul level contains all five levels: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah and yechidah.”

: “Metatron likewise pleads merit for his birds, the spirits that fly among human beings. The neshamot come from the Throne, the ruchot from this living creature, and the nefashot from the wheel. These correspond to Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah.”

: “The secret is this: Ehyeh encompasses everything. When the paths are closed, not differentiated, and included together in one place, it is called Ehyeh: embracing everything, concealed and unrevealed.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “In truth, it is well known that the plagues were not necessary in themselves: nothing could prevent Hashem from bringing Israel out against Pharaoh’s will without a single plague. They were needed because of the accusations, “How are these different from those?” Israel was surrounded by impurity like an embryo in its mother’s womb, as the exposition of “a nation from within a nation” teaches. The Midrash says, “These and those are uncircumcised.” The plagues were therefore necessary as a blow to Egypt and a healing for Israel, through which Israel was purified. With each plague they emerged from one level of impurity and entered one attribute of holiness, from below upward. For this reason they needed to depart with Pharaoh’s permission. Thus Scripture says, “When Pharaoh sent the people”: they departed with his consent because they had been immersed in impurity.”
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”
: ““The children of Israel went up armed”—they went up equipped with weapons.”

: “Rava asked Rabbah bar Mari: What is the source of the Sages’ teaching, “Rise early and eat in summer because of the heat, and in winter because of the cold,” and of the popular saying, “Sixty runners run, but cannot catch the man who ate bread in the morning”? He answered: It is written, “They shall neither hunger nor thirst; scorching heat and sun shall not strike them.” Rava said: You derive it from there, but I derive it from here: “You shall serve Hashem your God”—this is reciting Shema and praying. “He will bless your bread and your water”—this is bread with salt and a jug of water. Thereafter, “I will remove sickness from your midst.” A baraita teaches: “Sickness” here means bile. Why is it called machalah? Because eighty-three illnesses are associated with it, the numerical value of machalah. Morning bread with salt and a jug of water counteract them all.”

: “Someone used to go about saying, “A thief is not killed for two or three thefts.” Samuel said to Rav Judah: A verse states it: “Thus says Hashem: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four I will not reverse it.””

: “Shin: the great Shabbat is Binah; the small Shabbat is Malchut. Bet: the two arms, greatness and might. Tav: Tiferet. Through it, Shabbat equals the entire Torah. The three crowns of shin are the three upper sefirot. All are included in repentance, the upper Shekhinah, of whom it says, ‘the prayer of every mouth.’”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” followed by “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed. For it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Sabbaths,” and afterward, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.””
: “For thus says Hashem to the eunuchs who observe My Shabbats, choose what I desire, and hold fast to My covenant:”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Rabbi Aha said in Rabbi Tanhum son of Rabbi Hiyya’s name: If Israel repented for one day, the son of David would come immediately. What is the reason? “Today, if you listen to His voice.” Rabbi Levi said: If Israel observed one Shabbat properly, the son of David would come immediately. What is the reason? “Moses said: Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord”—one day. It also says, “Through returning and rest you shall be saved”: Through repentance and rest you will be redeemed.”

: ““Today, if you heed His voice.” Rabbi Levi said: If Israel observed even a single Shabbat properly, they would immediately be redeemed, as it says, “Today, if you heed His voice,” and it is written, “Observe the Shabbat day to sanctify it.””

: “Rabbi Levi said: If Israel properly observes Shabbat for even one day, the son of David will come. Why? Because it equals all the commandments. Thus it says, “For He is our God, and we are the people He shepherds, the flock of His hand—today, if you heed His voice.” Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Although I have set a fixed time for the end, which will arrive in its appointed season whether they repent or not, if they repent for even one day, I will bring it before its appointed season. Thus: “Today, if you heed His voice.” Just as we find that the son of David comes through all the commandments, so he comes through observing one Shabbat, because Shabbat equals all the commandments.”

: “Through this, the deadly poison—the profaned female—and her husband, the alien god who desecrates Shabbat, have no permission to approach. Therefore the ancients said: if Israel observed one Shabbat properly—another reading has ‘two Shabbatot properly’—they would immediately be redeemed.”

: “On Rosh Hashanah our ancestors’ labor in Egypt ceased. They were redeemed in Nisan, and their future redemption will be in Tishrei. Rabbi Yehoshua says: The world was created in Nisan; the patriarchs were born in Nisan and died in Nisan. Isaac was born on Passover. On Rosh Hashanah Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah were remembered for childbearing; Joseph left prison on Rosh Hashanah; and our ancestors’ labor in Egypt ceased on Rosh Hashanah. They were redeemed in Nisan, and their future redemption will be in Nisan.”

: “Another teaching states: R. Eliezer says: If Israel repents, they will be redeemed, as it says, “Return, wayward children; I will heal your waywardness.” R. Joshua said to him: Is it not already stated, “You were sold for nothing, and you will not be redeemed with money”? “You were sold for nothing”—through idolatry; “you will not be redeemed with money”—not through repentance and good deeds.”

: ““Let the work weigh heavily upon the men.” This teaches that they possessed scrolls in which they delighted from one Shabbat to the next, declaring that the Holy One, blessed be He, would redeem them, for they rested on Shabbat. Pharaoh told them, “Let the work weigh heavily upon the men, so that they work at it and pay no heed…” Let them neither delight in those scrolls nor rest on the Shabbat day.”

: “‘God blessed the seventh day.’ Rabbi Yishmael says: He blessed it through the manna and sanctified it through the manna. He blessed it through the manna because on every other day one omer fell, while on the eve of Shabbat two omers fell. He sanctified it through the manna because none at all fell on that day.”

: “What does “those who play with children” mean? If it means intercourse with males, those people are liable to stoning! Rather, does it mean other bodily sexual contact? Those are people of the generation of the Flood! Rather, it means men who marry girls not yet capable of bearing children. For Rabbi Yose said: The son of David will not come until all the souls in the treasury called Guf have been exhausted, as it says, “For the spirit shall faint before Me, and the souls that I have made.””

: “Because she is stone from the right side and a coal from the left, through her God takes vengeance upon Ishmael and Edom, the alien fires and raging waters. Their appointed powers are Samael and the Serpent. Samael, the fire of Gehinnom, is appointed over Esau’s nation. The Serpent is appointed over Ishmael’s nation; this is Rahab, appointed over the waters.”

: “The explanation follows what was said above. These souls had sunk into the kelippot among the Egyptians. Because they first sinned in the generation of the Flood by wasting seed, and were therefore dissolved in the Flood’s boiling waters, Pharaoh now likewise decreed, ‘Every newborn son you shall cast into the Nile.’ The decree concerned males, who had committed this sin, rather than females. Corresponding to their sin in the generation of the Dispersion—‘Come, let us make bricks and burn them,’ to build the city and tower, rise up, deny the divine foundation and wage war against Him—‘Come, let us deal wisely with him’ now answered ‘Come, let us make bricks.’ ‘They embittered their lives,’ building Pithom and Raamses, corresponded to that city and tower.”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality; all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality; all the males guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint from sexual immorality itself was sufficient merit for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. What is the proof? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””

: ““We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt.” Rav and Samuel differed: one said this means fish, and the other said forbidden sexual relations. The one who says fish relies on “we ate”; the one who says forbidden sexual relations relies on “freely.” But according to the opinion that it means forbidden sexual relations, does it not say “we ate”? Scripture uses a refined expression, as it says, “She ate, wiped her mouth, and said, I have done no wrong.” According to the opinion that it means fish, what does “freely” mean? They brought them from ownerless sources, for the Master said: When Israel drew water, the Holy One, blessed be He, provided small fish for them in their pitchers. According to the opinion that it means fish, but they were not promiscuous regarding forbidden sexual relations, the verse “A locked garden is my sister, my bride” is understandable. But according to the other opinion, what does “a sealed spring” mean? Regarding the relations already forbidden to them, they were not promiscuous. According to the opinion that it means forbidden sexual relations, “Moses heard the people weeping by their families” is understandable: they wept concerning family relationships with whom intercourse had become forbidden. But according to the opinion that it means fish, what does “weeping by their families” mean? Both matters were present.”

: “Our Rabbis said: Israel did not wish to circumcise themselves in Egypt; they all abandoned circumcision there except the tribe of Levi, as it says, “Of Levi he said: Your sacred lots and Your Urim…” Why? “For they guarded Your word and preserved Your covenant”—in Egypt. The Holy One, blessed be He, sought to redeem them, but they had no merit. What did He do? He called Moses and told him: Go and circumcise them. Some say Joshua was there and circumcised them, as it says, “Again circumcise the children of Israel a second time.” Many would not accept circumcision. The Holy One, blessed be He, commanded that they prepare the Passover offering. When Moses prepared it, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded the four winds of the world, which blow in the Garden of Eden; winds from the Garden went and attached themselves to that offering, as it says, “Awake, north wind; come, south wind.” Its fragrance traveled a forty-day journey. All Israel gathered to Moses and begged: Feed us from your Passover offering! For they were faint from its fragrance. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: If you are not circumcised, you may not eat, as it says, “The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: This is the statute of the Passover…” They immediately submitted and were circumcised. The Passover blood mingled with the circumcision blood. The Holy One, blessed be He, passed by, took each one, kissed him, and blessed him, as it says, “I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood…” Live through the Pa

: “‘I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan’—because they had been circumcised. Whoever is circumcised inherits the land, for only a righteous person inherits the land, and whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Thus ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. Consider Joseph: he was not called righteous throughout his life until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous—Joseph the Righteous.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: When Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them. Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina explained this in his father’s name: It is like a shepherd taking his flock across a river. A wolf came to attack the flock. The experienced shepherd took a large goat and gave it to the wolf, saying: Let it struggle with this until we cross the river; afterward I will retrieve it. So, when Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, until now these people worshipped idols, and You are splitting the sea for them! What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He handed him Job, who had been one of Pharaoh’s advisers and of whom it is written, “A blameless and upright man.” He told him: He is in your hand. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: While he is occupied with Job, Israel will enter the sea and emerge, and afterward I will rescue Job.”

: “Is splitting the Sea of Reeds difficult before Him? It says, ‘He rebukes the sea and dries it,’ and ‘He calls the sea’s waters and pours them upon the earth.’ Once the will arises before Him, everything is counted as nothing. Yet you say splitting the sea is difficult? Rather, when Israel approached the sea and God wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, Egypt’s appointed ruler, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: ‘Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All are guilty before You, and all Your ways are judgment and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and those worship stars and constellations; these commit sexual transgressions, and those commit sexual transgressions; these shed blood, and those shed blood.’”

: “After turning to a bad course, Acher asked Rabbi Meir: What does “God made this opposite that” mean? He answered: Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created has a counterpart: He created mountains and hills, seas and rivers. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. Rather, He created the righteous and the wicked, the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom. Every person has two portions, one in the Garden of Eden and one in Gehinnom. If a righteous person merits, he takes his own portion and his fellow’s portion in the Garden of Eden; if a wicked person is found guilty, he takes his own portion and his fellow’s portion in Gehinnom.” Rav Mesharshiya said: What verses support this? Of the righteous, “They shall inherit a double portion in their land”; of the wicked, “Break them with a double breaking.””

: “After good and evil became intermingled, although God created a righteous person and a wicked person, each also contains a portion of the opposite. “God made one corresponding to the other”: opposite every righteous person stands a wicked person corresponding to his evil portion. The righteous person must refine himself, separating the evil from himself so that it remains entirely with the wicked person opposite him, while absorbing the good in that wicked person that belongs to him. He thereby becomes wholly complete in holiness: good is separated from evil, and he takes his fellow’s share in the Garden of Eden. The evil goes to destruction, and the wicked person takes his fellow’s share in Gehinnom.”

: ““We shall make you ornaments of gold.” “Ornaments of gold”—this is the spoil of the sea. “With points of silver”—this is the spoil of Egypt. Just as gold is superior to silver, so the wealth of the sea surpassed the spoil of Egypt, as it says, “You came with the finest ornaments”: “ornaments” is Egypt’s spoil; the doubled expression is the sea’s spoil.”

: “Another interpretation: It saw Joseph’s coffin descending into the sea. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let it flee before the one who fled, as it says, “He fled and went outside.” The sea too shall flee before him. Thus: “The sea saw and fled.””

: “‘For Leah was hated’: she acted as one who was to be joined to the hated man—another reading says, ‘she was destined for the hated man.’ For the arrangement was that the older brother should marry the older sister, and the younger brother the younger sister. She wept and said, ‘May it be Your will that I not fall to the lot of a wicked man.’ Rav Huna said: Prayer is powerful: it annulled the decree. Moreover, Leah was answered before her sister.”

: “‘All these are the twelve tribes of Israel.’ Since Scripture already says, ‘He blessed them,’ what does it add by saying, ‘He blessed each according to his blessing’? He had blessed Judah as a lion, Dan as a serpent, Naphtali as a deer, and Benjamin as a wolf. He then included them all together, making all of them lions and all of them serpents. You can see that this is so: ‘Dan shall be a serpent,’ yet Scripture also calls him a lion, as it says, ‘Dan is a lion’s cub.’ This fulfills, ‘You are entirely beautiful, My beloved, and there is no blemish in you.’”

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

: “Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous. He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden, and each will point with his finger, as it says, “On that day they will say: This is our God, for whom we hoped, that He would save us. This is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us exult and rejoice in His salvation.””
Beit Yaakov’s printed Zohar reference appears to read page 43. The matching quoted words are found at Zohar II 46b, Beshalach 4:52.

: “We learned: whoever emits his seed wastefully is called evil and does not behold the Shekhinah’s face, as in ‘You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,’ and ‘Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil.’ So here: ‘Woe to the evil wicked one’—woe to the guilty one who made himself evil. ‘The recompense of his hands shall be done to him’ includes one who commits sexual sin with his hands, emitting and wasting his seed. He is driven away in that world more than all others. Come and see: once ‘Woe to the wicked one’ is written, why add ‘evil’? As explained, he made himself evil. ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’: others ascend, but he does not. What of other sinners who killed people? They all ascend, but he does not. They killed other people; he killed his own children, shedding much blood. Of other sinners it does not say ‘What he did was evil in the Lord’s eyes,’ but here it does, because ‘he wasted it upon the earth.’ Rabbi Yehudah taught: there is no offense in the world without repentance except this one, and no sinners who fail to behold the Shekhinah’s face except this one, as in ‘Evil shall not dwell with You’—at all. Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come: ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ What is this inheritance? As in ‘I shall walk before the Lord in the lands of the living.’”

: “Rav Shmuel bar Ami said—or, according to another report, Rav Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rav Yonatan’s name: How do we know that a decree accompanied by an oath is not torn up? For it says, “Therefore I have sworn concerning Eli’s house that the guilt of Eli’s house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.” Rava said: It is not atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it can be atoned for by Torah. Abaye said: It is not atoned for by sacrifice or offering, but it can be atoned for by Torah together with acts of kindness. Rabbah and Abaye descended from Eli’s house. Rabbah, who devoted himself to Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who devoted himself to Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty. The Sages taught: A Jerusalem family’s members used to die at eighteen. They informed Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai. He said, “Perhaps you belong to Eli’s family, of which it is written, ‘All the increase of your house will die as men.’ Go, occupy yourselves with Torah, and live.” They did so and lived, and the family came to be called after Rabban Yochanan.”

: “Shmuel said: If someone finds tefillin in the marketplace, he may assess their value and immediately keep them for use. Ravina objected: If he finds sacred books, he reads them once every thirty days; if he cannot read, he unrolls and rerolls them. This permits rolling them, but not assessing their value and keeping them. Abaye answered: Tefillin are readily available at Bar Chavu’s establishment; sacred books are not readily available.”
: “He swallowed wealth, but he will vomit it up; God will drive it out of his belly.”

: “Does Rabbi Akiva hold that Shabbat is a time for tefillin? A baraita teaches: Rabbi Akiva says: Might a person put on tefillin on Shabbat and festivals? Scripture says, “It shall be a sign for you upon your hand”: This concerns days that require a sign, excluding these days, which are themselves a sign.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “‘How abundant is Your goodness’ is the goodness that was hidden; ‘for those who fear You’ means those who fear sin. ‘You have made for those who shelter in You’: what is ‘made’? The work of creation. Rabbi Abba said: this is the Garden of Eden, which God skillfully made on earth after the pattern above, for the righteous to find strength within it. Thus ‘You have made for those who shelter in You, before human beings’: this one stands opposite humanity, the other opposite the holy ones above. Rabbi Shimon said: the upper Garden of Eden, too, is before human beings, so that the righteous who do their Master’s will may gather there.”

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “What is repentance? The sinner must abandon his sin, remove it from his thoughts, and resolve in his heart never to do it again, as it says, 'Let the wicked abandon his way.' He must also regret the past, as it says, 'After I returned, I regretted.' The Knower of hidden things must testify concerning him that he will never return to this sin, as it says, 'We will no longer call the work of our hands our god.' He must confess with his lips and articulate these matters that he has resolved in his heart.”

: “If a man betroths a woman “on condition that I am righteous,” even if he is completely wicked, she is betrothed, because he may have entertained a thought of repentance. If he says, “On condition that I am wicked,” even if he is completely righteous, she is betrothed, because he may have entertained a thought of idolatry.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 3, paragraph 1: “This explains the statement that the burnt offering atones for the heart’s sinful thoughts. Together with repentance, a person brings a burnt offering as an image of surrendering himself: he has resolved in his heart that he does not wish to live against God’s will—what purpose would such a life serve? After this inward self-surrender, the evil inclination no longer controls him, and at that moment he is a complete penitent. Even if afterward his inclination overcomes him—as generally happens, since no one escapes such thoughts every day—at the time of the act he had repented, and the Knower of hidden things could testify to his broken heart. Although his inclination later prevails and he returns to his former conduct, at that moment he was wholly righteous, as we demonstrated from the passage in Kiddushin.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “Thus says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place could be My resting place? My hand made all these things, and all these things came to be, declares Hashem. But to this one I look: the poor and crushed in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

: “Scripture says, “To this one shall I look: to the poor and broken-spirited, who trembles at My word.” On Shabbat a Jew attains these three kinds of humility. “Poor” corresponds to “From where have you come? From a putrid drop”: he is poor at his very root. “Broken-spirited” means that, when he takes to heart “Where are you going? To a place of dust,” his heart breaks within him. When he considers that he must render an account before the Holy One, King of kings, he becomes one who “trembles at My word”: who can stand before His judgment or be vindicated before Him? He becomes utterly humble in his own eyes, escapes all three impure powers, and can attain complete redemption.”
: “He made the letter tzadi king, bound a crown upon it, and through it formed Aquarius in the universe, Shevat in the year, and the stomach in the person.”

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”
: “Hashem will fight for you, and you shall remain silent.”

: “‘Call Shabbat a delight’: delight for all, for soul and body, for those above and below. What does ‘call’ mean? Invite it, as in ‘sacred convocations’—invited occasions, like inviting a guest into one’s home. ‘Call Shabbat a delight’ thus means inviting it as one invites a guest, with a properly prepared table and house, and suitable food and drink, beyond the other days. ‘Call Shabbat’ while it is still day. ‘The Lord’s holy one, honored’ is Yom Kippur: two that are one. ‘Honor it by refraining from your own ways’ is as we have explained.”

: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Why were our patriarchs unable to have children? Because the Holy One, blessed be He, longs for the prayers of the righteous. Rabbi Yitzḥak also said: Why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork? Just as a pitchfork turns grain from place to place, so the prayers of the righteous turn the Holy One’s attribute from anger to mercy.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Whoever makes Shabbat a delight is granted the requests of his heart, as it says, “Delight in the Lord, and He will grant you the requests of your heart.” I do not know what kind of delight is meant. When Scripture says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight,” you must conclude that this refers to the delight of Shabbat.”

: “As soon as he comes, ‘A mist shall rise from the earth’: the alef-dalet of Adonai raises vav to him, becoming within her ‘Lord of all the earth.’ Immediately, ‘It waters the whole face of the ground.’ From him Israel below is watered through the seventy facets of Torah.”

: “Shabbat encompasses all ten attributes. Its three meals express the mystery of oneg—Eden, River and Garden—as stated in the Zohar. Eden includes all three upper sefirot: Tikkunei Zohar says that Eden is none other than the supreme Keter, while elsewhere the Zohar asks, “What is Eden?” and answers, “The higher Chokhmah.” In Bereishit, the Zohar identifies “flowing from Eden” with the higher Mother. This is the meaning of Ra’aya Meheimna: the Divine Presence is called Shabbat through three levels. Shin represents the three crowns—Keter, Chokhmah and Binah—and She is the daughter, the fourth with them.”

: “Bereshit bara can be read ‘house, head’: Father and Mother. Bara is rendered in Aramaic bera, ‘son,’ the middle pillar, of which it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden.’ There is one Eden and another, as in ‘You give them drink from the stream of Your delights’—Your Edens, indeed. Upper Eden is the upper Crown; a lower Eden is yod. There is another lower Eden, the upper Mother, dalet: she is Eden relative to the river beneath her. Thus it is written, ‘A river goes out from Eden to water the garden.’”

: “What distinguishes lower Eden from upper Eden? As light surpasses darkness. Lower Eden is called feminine Eden; upper Eden is called masculine Eden, of which it says, ‘No eye has seen, O God, besides You.’ Lower Eden is called a garden in relation to Eden above, while this garden is called Eden in relation to the garden beneath it. Those in the lower garden delight in this Eden above them every Shabbat and every new moon, as in ‘From new moon to new moon and from Shabbat to Shabbat.’”

: “'The Lord is a man of war; the Lord is His name.' Sefer HaBahir records Rabbi Amorai asking what 'The Lord is a man of war' means. It resembles a king who had beautiful dwellings, each with a name, one better than another. He said, 'I will give my son this dwelling, called alef; this one, called yod, is also good; this one, called shin, is also good.' What did he do? He joined all three, made them one name, and made them one house. They asked, 'How long will you conceal your words?' He answered, 'My children, alef is first; yod is second to it; shin encompasses the whole world.' Why does it encompass the whole world? Because repentance is written in it. He was troubled by the word ish, 'man,' being applied to the exalted Name, and explained it through its letters. According to this teaching, alef alludes to the supernal crown, yod to wisdom, the second level, as I explained in Bereshit, and shin to repentance, which is understanding. Some explain that yod alludes to understanding and shin to the world’s instruction; the first interpretation is primary.”

: “Rabbi Amora‘i asked the meaning of ‘The Lord is a man of war.’ Mar Rechumai replied: do not ask about something obvious; listen, and I shall advise you. It resembles a king who had beautiful dwellings, each named and each better than the next. He said: I shall give my son this dwelling named alef, and this good one named yod, and this good one named shin. He gathered the three together, made them a single name and a single house. ‘How long will you conceal your words?’ ‘My son, alef is the head, yod comes second, and shin embraces the whole world. Why does shin embrace the whole world? Because repentance is written within it.’”

: “The tenth commandment: ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat.’ The Shekhinah is called Shabbat from the side of the three upper levels: shin, with three crowns—Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. She is bat, daughter, the fourth with them. The six days, from Chesed through Yesod, are those in which work is done, for building begins with Chesed, as in ‘The world is built through kindness.’ From Binah upward, however, there is rest, delight and cessation from all work.”

: “When Shabbat enters, a herald proclaims throughout the heavens: ‘Prepare, chariots; prepare, camps, to meet your Master.’ A spirit then issues from the south and spreads over all the right side’s hosts and camps, clothing them. This spirit is called Shabbat’s garment of glory. Then this world’s tables are arranged within a palace. Happy is the person whose table’s arrangement appears there properly prepared, without shame, each according to his ability.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “This accords with Tikkunei Zohar: Shabbat is mentioned twice here, corresponding to the upper and lower Divine Presence. “For their generations”—fortunate is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination is removed from there. Whoever attains both kinds of holiness within one Shabbat—the lesser Shabbat, Malkhut, and the greater Shabbat, Binah—is redeemed immediately through observing that single Shabbat. This is the meaning of the teaching found in the Jerusalem Talmud, the Midrashim, Zohar Chadash and Tikkunei Zohar: If Israel observed one Shabbat properly, the son of David would come immediately.”

: “R. Eliezer son of R. Yosei the Galilean says: The dead whom Ezekiel revived ascended to the Land of Israel, married, and had sons and daughters. R. Judah ben Beteira stood up and said, “I am one of their descendants, and these are the tefillin my grandfather left me from them.” … Rav said: They were the descendants of Ephraim who calculated the end and erred, as it says, “The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son, Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead; the men of Gath born in the land killed them,” and so forth. It is also written, “Their father Ephraim mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.””

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “In every dispute of the sages, both opinions are the words of the living God. Thus, beginning with Jacob, whose offspring were complete and without defect, Israelite fetuses were established in holiness: at that stage the evil inclination is absent, for it rules only from birth, as in 'Sin crouches at the opening.' There is then no impurity in the fetus. Nevertheless, after it leaves its mother’s womb and the evil inclination rules, something of the serpent’s impurity still remains. This continued until the giving of the Torah, when 'You shall be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation' was said. Priests are called holy of holies, as in 'Aaron was set apart to sanctify him as holy of holies.' At the giving of the Torah, when 'I said: You are divine' was said, all Israel were fit to be like priests. 'A holy nation' means that every Israelite is holy, as Scripture subsequently repeats in several expressions, 'For you are a holy people,' and the Gemara says, 'Israel are holy.' This is the meaning of 'Israel who stood at Mount Sinai had their impurity cease.'”

: “The Rabbis interpreted the verse concerning Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: “My light”—on Rosh Hashanah; “my salvation”—on Yom Kippur. “Whom shall I fear?”—“My strength and song is the Lord.” “When evildoers approach me”—these are the princes of the nations. “To eat my flesh”—for the princes of the nations come and accuse Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He, saying: Master of the universe, these worship idols and those worship idols; these commit sexual immorality and those commit sexual immorality; these shed blood and those shed blood. Why do these descend to Gehinnom while those do not? “My enemies and adversaries”—there are three hundred and sixty-five days in the solar year, while “the satan” has the numerical value of three hundred and sixty-four, for the satan accuses throughout the year but does not accuse on Yom Kippur. Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: “If an army encamps against me”—Samael’s army—“my heart will not fear,” for You promised me, “With this Aaron shall enter the sanctuary.””

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Rabbi Nathan says: The construction of the Ark is as precious as the heavenly Throne of Glory, as it says, ‘The place established for Your dwelling, which You have made.’ The Sanctuary corresponds to the heavenly Temple, and the Ark corresponds to the Throne. He made a cover above it, corresponding to the seraphim who stand above Him.”
: “Your throne has been established from of old; You are from eternity.”

: ““Then Moses sang.” This is what Scripture says: “Your throne was established from then.” Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Abbahu’s name: Although You have existed forever, Your throne was not settled, and You were not known in Your world, until Your children sang. Therefore it says, “Your throne was established from then.” It is like a king who fought a war and won, and they made him Augustus. They told him: Before this war you were king; now we have made you Augustus. What honor distinguishes a king from Augustus? The king stands upon the platform, whereas Augustus sits. So Israel said: Truly, before You created Your world, You existed; since creating it, You remain the same. Yet, as it were, You stood, as it says, “He stood and measured the earth.” But when You stood at the sea and we sang before You with “then,” Your kingship became settled and Your throne established. Thus, “Your throne was established from then”—through “Then Moses sang.””
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”

: ““And His name One”—what does “One” mean? Is His name not One already? Rav Nahman bar Isaac said: The World to Come is unlike this world. In this world, it is written with yod-heh and read with alef-dalet. In the World to Come it will be entirely one: read with yod-heh and written with yod-heh.”
: “Then hear from heaven, act, and judge Your servants: condemn the guilty by bringing his conduct upon his own head, and vindicate the righteous by giving him according to his righteousness.”

: “‘In the beginning God created et the heavens and ve’et the earth.’ What is et? The ancients explained that every et adds something. This et is the Torah, embracing alef through tav, through which heaven and earth were created. Further, in ‘et the heavens,’ heaven is the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, ‘You shall hear, heaven’; ve’et includes His mate with Him. Ve’et is the Righteous One and his mate. The earth is the vessel for all, bringing forth seeds and fruits. This is the secret of ‘Every shrub of the field before it was on the earth,’ and so forth.”

: “How do we know that ‘heaven’ refers to the Holy One, blessed be He? It is written, ‘You shall hear, heaven.’ Did Solomon pray to heaven to hear their prayer? Rather, he meant the One whose Name is proclaimed over heaven, as it says, ‘Heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain You.’ It is therefore the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. But heaven is fire, and you said it preceded! Say instead: the power of the forms in that place preceded, and afterward came those holy forms. What is their power? As it says, ‘There is none holy like the Lord, for there is none besides You, and no rock like our God.’”
: “Do not rejoice over me, my enemy. Though I have fallen, I will rise; though I sit in darkness, Hashem is my light.”
: “For a commandment is a lamp and Torah is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.”

: “Happy are the righteous to whom all these holy matters have been revealed—matters spoken through the upper holy spirit, in which all the supremely holy ones are included, and to which those above and below listen. Happy are you, masters of masters, reapers of the field! You will know and contemplate these matters, and know your Master face to face, eye to eye. Through them you will merit the world to come, as it says, ‘Know today and bring it back to your heart.’ ‘The Lord’—the Ancient of Days—‘is God.’ All is one; blessed is His Name forever and for all eternity.”

: “God sowed this light in His delightful garden, arranging it in rows through the Righteous One, the garden’s gardener. He takes the light and sows it as a true planting, making rows in the garden. It produces, sprouts and bears fruit, from which the world is nourished. Thus ‘Light is sown for the righteous.’”

: “He said, “If you listen carefully to the voice of Hashem your God, do what is upright in His eyes, attend to His commandments, and observe all His statutes, I will place upon you none of the illnesses I placed upon Egypt, for I am Hashem, your healer.””
: “For Hashem your God is a consuming fire, a zealous God.”

: “Rava intended to expound it publicly. An elder said to him, “It is written le-alem—to conceal.” R. Avina raised a contradiction: It is written, “This is My name forever,” and also, “This is My remembrance from generation to generation.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am not read as I am written. I am written with yod-heh, but read with alef-dalet.”
: “Her husband is known at the gates, where he sits with the elders of the land.”

: “Certainly ‘Her husband is known in the gates’ refers to God, who becomes known and cleaved to according to what each person measures within his heart, insofar as he can cleave through a spirit of wisdom. According to what he measures in his heart, so He becomes known in his heart. Therefore ‘known in the gates’—through those measures. But no one can grasp and know Him as He truly is.”
: “The first commandment, Anokhi, ‘I am,’ is so called from the side of Keter, the Ayin, Nothingness, from our God. Anokhi contains kaf, for Keter, and also the letters of Ayin.”
: “But You do not possess a defined tzedek, which is judgment, nor a defined mishpat, which is mercy. None of these attributes applies to You at all.”

: “All the more so for one who removes her from her place and puts a maidservant in her place. Wherever there is a blemish, the Matron does not dwell; the maidservant, herself blemished, dwells in the blemished place. A person’s sin-induced damage blemishes all his limbs, until the Matron finds no place to dwell there. He has no repair until he restores her upon all his limbs.”

: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me? says Hashem of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. Yet you ask, “How have we despised Your name?””
: “All the people saw the thunder, the flames, the sound of the shofar, and the smoking mountain. The people saw, trembled, and stood at a distance.”

: “A baraita teaches: “So that His fear may be upon your faces”—this is shame. “So that you do not sin”—this teaches that shame leads to fear of sin. From here they said: Being bashful is a good sign in a person. Others say: Someone who feels shame will not readily sin; whoever lacks shame shows that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.”
: “To what do the seven Shabbat blessings correspond? Rabbi Chalafta son of Shaul said: To the seven occurrences of “voice” that David spoke concerning the waters.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”
: “I have placed My words in your mouth and sheltered you in the shadow of My hand, to plant the heavens, establish the earth, and say to Zion, “You are My people.””

: “As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says Hashem: My spirit that rests upon you and My words that I placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, your descendants’ mouths, or the mouths of your descendants’ descendants, says Hashem, from now and forever.”

: “Why was it hidden? So that the world’s wicked would not benefit from it; because of them, the worlds do not benefit. It is concealed for the righteous—specifically, for the Righteous One—as it says, ‘Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright of heart.’ Then the worlds will be sweetened and all will be one. Until the day when the world to come arrives, it remains concealed and hidden.”

: “‘The earth opened et its mouth’: et includes Dumah, who is the mouth of the earth. ‘Et the donkey’s mouth’ includes Kamri’el, who is called the donkey’s mouth. The mouth of the well follows the same pattern. What is the mouth of the well? The level appointed over it below, beneath the Lord’s mouth; its name is Yehadri’el. These three mouths were created on the eve of Shabbat at twilight. When the day is sanctified, the mouth appointed over all other mouths ascends: the day that rises and is sanctified in every respect, called the Lord’s mouth. The other mouths were created on Shabbat eve at twilight; when the day was sanctified, the mouth ruling over all, the Lord’s mouth, ascended.”

: “God therefore did not want Israel to arouse any matter at all. Were they to arouse something, they would fail to arouse the Name of Mercy, and judgment would not be performed with mercy. Thus ‘The Lord will fight for you, while you remain silent’: arouse nothing. The Name of Mercy must be stirred against them, to execute judgment with mercy. He therefore desired that you make no defect by arousing something else.”
: “Hashem will fight for you, and you shall remain silent.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: When Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them. Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina explained this in his father’s name: It is like a shepherd taking his flock across a river. A wolf came to attack the flock. The experienced shepherd took a large goat and gave it to the wolf, saying: Let it struggle with this until we cross the river; afterward I will retrieve it. So, when Israel left Egypt, the angel Samael stood to accuse them, saying before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, until now these people worshipped idols, and You are splitting the sea for them! What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He handed him Job, who had been one of Pharaoh’s advisers and of whom it is written, “A blameless and upright man.” He told him: He is in your hand. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: While he is occupied with Job, Israel will enter the sea and emerge, and afterward I will rescue Job.”

: “Is splitting the Sea of Reeds difficult before Him? It says, ‘He rebukes the sea and dries it,’ and ‘He calls the sea’s waters and pours them upon the earth.’ Once the will arises before Him, everything is counted as nothing. Yet you say splitting the sea is difficult? Rather, when Israel approached the sea and God wished to split the Sea of Reeds for them, Rahab, Egypt’s appointed ruler, came and demanded judgment before Him. He said: ‘Master of the world, why do You wish to judge Egypt and split the sea for Israel? All are guilty before You, and all Your ways are judgment and truth. These worship stars and constellations, and those worship stars and constellations; these commit sexual transgressions, and those commit sexual transgressions; these shed blood, and those shed blood.’”
: ““I have loved you,” says Hashem. You ask, “How have You loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” declares Hashem. “Yet I loved Jacob.””
: “Hashem will go out and fight against those nations, as on the day He fought in the day of battle.”
: “Hashem goes out like a mighty warrior; like a man of war, He stirs His zeal. He cries aloud and raises a battle shout, prevailing over His enemies.”

: “If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored; if you honor it by refraining from your usual ways, pursuing your affairs, and speaking of business—”

: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: When Moses ascended on high, he found the Holy One, blessed be He, sitting and attaching crowns to the letters. Moses asked: “Master of the world, what holds You back?” He answered: “After many generations there will be a man named Akiva son of Yosef, who will derive heaps upon heaps of laws from every tiny stroke.” Moses said: “Master of the world, show him to me.” He answered: “Turn around.” Moses went and sat at the back of eight rows, but did not understand what they were saying, and his strength failed him. When they reached one matter, his students asked him: “Rabbi, how do you know this?” He answered: “It is a law given to Moses at Sinai.” Moses’ mind was put at ease. He returned before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said: “Master of the world, You have such a man, yet You give the Torah through me?” He answered: “Be silent; this is what arose in My thought.””

: “In this arrangement they are called: Chesed, the right arm; Gevurah, the left arm; Tiferet, the torso; Netzach and Hod, the two legs; Yesod, the body’s extremity, the sign of the holy covenant; Malchut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah. Chokhmah is the brain, inward thought. Binah is the heart, through which the heart understands. Of these two it is written, ‘The concealed things belong to the Lord our God.’ The upper Keter is the royal crown, of which it says, ‘Declaring the end from the beginning.’ It is the skull of the tefillin; another reading says, the skull that does not put on tefillin. Within is yod-he-vav-he, the path of emanation.”

: “Ten sefirot of restraint: restrain your mouth from speaking and your heart from pondering. If your heart runs, return to the place, for this is why it says, ‘The living creatures ran and returned.’ Concerning this matter a covenant was made.”
: “The living creatures darted forward and returned, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.”

: “Mishnah: One who has had a seminal emission reflects upon the Shema in his heart, but does not recite its blessings, either before it or after it. After food he recites the blessing afterward, but not beforehand. Rabbi Yehudah says: He recites the blessings both before and afterward. Gemara: Ravina said: This shows that mental recitation is equivalent to speech. For if you suppose it is not equivalent, why should he reflect upon it? But if it is equivalent to speech, let him utter it with his lips! The restriction follows what we find at Sinai. Rav Chisda, however, said: Mental recitation is not equivalent to speech, for if it were, let him utter it with his lips. But if it is not equivalent to speech, why should he reflect upon it? Rabbi Elazar answered: So that everyone else should not be occupied with it while he sits idle. Then let him study another chapter! Rav Adda bar Ahavah answered: He should be occupied with the matter in which the congregation is engaged.”

Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 20b:19:1: ““As we find at Sinai”: He separated them from their wives, as it says, “Do not approach a woman.” Ezra relied upon this separation when instituting immersion for men who had emitted semen before they engaged in Torah. For “You shall make them known to your children” is followed by “The day you stood before Hashem your God at Horeb,” as explained later in this chapter.”

: “As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says Hashem: My spirit that rests upon you and My words that I placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, your descendants’ mouths, or the mouths of your descendants’ descendants, says Hashem, from now and forever.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi says: Great is circumcision, for no one occupied himself with commandments as Abraham did, yet he was not called whole until circumcision, as it says, “Walk before Me and be whole,” followed by, “I will place My covenant between Me and you.” Another interpretation: Great is circumcision, for it is equal to all the commandments of the Torah, as it says, “For according to these words.” Another interpretation: Great is circumcision, for without it heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, “If not for My covenant by day and night.” This disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer, who said: Great is Torah, for without Torah heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, “If not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the ordinances of heaven and earth.””

: “If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For the designation “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.””

: “Resh Lakish said: A gentile who observes a day of cessation incurs the death penalty, as it says, “Day and night shall not cease.” The Master said: For them, a warning constitutes the basis of the death penalty. Ravina said: Even on a Monday.”

: “R. Yohanan said: A gentile who engages in Torah incurs the death penalty, as it says, “Moses commanded us the Torah as an inheritance”—an inheritance for us, not for them. Why is this not counted among the seven commandments? According to the reading “inheritance,” he is stealing it; according to the reading “betrothed,” his judgment is like that of violating a betrothed young woman, which is stoning. They raised an objection: R. Meir used to say: From where do we know that even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest? It says, “Which a human being shall perform and live through them.” It does not say “priests, Levites, and Israelites,” but “a human being.” Thus even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest. That statement concerns their own seven commandments.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: blessing is prepared for those upper days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills Ze‘ir Anpin’s head with dew descending from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all. Three times from Shabbat’s entrance, He casts it upon the Field of Holy Apples, so that all may be blessed together.”

: “Two children extend downward from them. From Father’s side, yod, a son emerges, joined to yod and to that river. From Mother’s side a daughter emerges, the lower river. The son afterward extends and proceeds from them: he is vav, inheriting Father and Mother, with the faith of everything bound within him. The daughter is nourished from him, from the inheritance he received.”

: “‘I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan’—because they had been circumcised. Whoever is circumcised inherits the land, for only a righteous person inherits the land, and whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Thus ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’ Whoever is circumcised and guards this sign of the covenant is called righteous. Consider Joseph: he was not called righteous throughout his life until he guarded that covenant, the sign of the holy covenant. Once he guarded it, he was called righteous—Joseph the Righteous.”
: “He stretches the north over emptiness and suspends the earth upon nothing.”

: “Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yohanan said: The world endures only because of Moses and Aaron. Here it says, “What are we?” and elsewhere, “He suspends the earth upon nothing.” Rabbi Ilaa said: The world endures only because of one who restrains himself during a quarrel, as it says, “He suspends the earth upon restraint.” Rabbi Abbahu said: Because of one who makes himself as though he were nothing, as it says, “Underneath are the everlasting arms.””
: “But wisdom—from where can it be found? And where is the place of understanding?”
: “Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Words of Torah endure only in one who makes himself as though he did not exist, as it says, “Wisdom is found from nothingness.””
: “Not so My servant Moses; he is faithful throughout My house.”

: “This koach, ‘strength,’ is the secret of the twenty-eight joints of the ten fingers, through which ‘whenever Moses raised his hand, Israel prevailed.’ Therefore the Sages explained, ‘To whom do they raise their hands? To the height of heaven.’ This strength must be raised to Chokhmah, the height of heaven: the Name spelled yod-he-vav-he resting upon the ten fingers and this strength. Chokhmah is koach mah, ‘the strength of mah.’”

: “There is another below, called Mah, ‘What.’ What distinguishes the two? The first concealed one, called Mi, ‘Who,’ stands open to questioning. A person questions, searches, seeks to contemplate and know, ascending from level to level to the end of every level. Once he reaches there—Mah: what have you known, what have you contemplated, what have you searched out? Everything remains concealed as at first.”

: “Rather, Rabbi Shimon explained: they wished to distinguish between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, called Nothingness, and Ze‘ir Anpin, called the Lord. Thus it does not say, ‘Is the Lord among us or not?’ as in ‘Will he follow My Torah or not?’ It says, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’”

: “One may not expound the laws of forbidden relationships before three students, the work of creation before two, or the divine chariot before even one, unless that student is wise and understands through his own knowledge.”

Additional source: Chagigah 13a:5: ““Nor may the Chariot be expounded to one individual.” Rabbi Chiya taught: But its chapter outlines may be transmitted to him. Rabbi Zeira said: Chapter outlines are transmitted only to the head of a rabbinic court, and to anyone whose heart is anxious within him. According to another version: Provided that his heart is anxious within him.” Context: This additional passage supports Rav Tzadok’s later claim in the same paragraph about transmitting the outlines of esoteric teaching to one whose heart is anxious within him.

Commentary: Rashi on Chagigah 13a:5: ““Chapter outlines”: the beginnings of its sections. “Whose heart is anxious”: he does not behave with levity. “According to another version: Provided that his heart is anxious within him”: both conditions are required.”

k: volume-i|1088|0|R. Eliyahu de Vidas, Reshit Chokhmah, Ga
quote: Parallel: R. Eliyahu de Vidas, Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 11:44–45: “Another excellence of silence is taught in the Mishnah: “Silence is a fence for wisdom.” Just as tithes are a fence for wealth—one must tithe in order to attain wealth, as the Sages expound, “Tithe so that you may become rich”—and the Mishnah’s other fences work in this way, so a person cannot attain wisdom without acquiring the quality of silence. The Sages likewise explain that when a Torah scholar speaks an idle word, a corresponding measure of Torah departs from him; we have copied their words in the next chapter. Along these lines, the reason may be that through silence he withdraws from the activity of the six directions, which are voice and speech, and ascends to the place of silence: thought, the mystery of wisdom. Thus it is said, “Be silent; thus it arose in thought.” A further reason is that by being silent a person makes himself a vehicle for the place of silence. He then merits an outpouring of Torah’s secrets, which remain in silence and were not entrusted to disclosure, as the Zohar often says. Among the forty-eight ways through which Torah is acquired is minimizing conversation.”
