: “If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored; if you honor it by refraining from your usual ways, pursuing your affairs, and speaking of business—”

: “Regarding the statement, “Since the Temple was destroyed, although prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages”: Rashi explains that it was taken from prophets who were not Sages. This may be challenged, since Nedarim 38a says that the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His Presence only upon someone wise, mighty, and wealthy. Some answer that uninterrupted indwelling requires wisdom, but prophecy for a particular mission, such as Jonah son of Amittai’s mission to Nineveh, does not. I am not satisfied with that answer. Rather, the meaning is this: Although the prophets’ prophecy, consisting of appearances and visions, was taken away, the Sages’ prophecy, which comes through wisdom, was not taken away. They know the truth through the holy spirit within them. For a time He may rest His Presence even upon pious people who are not Sages. There the proof is drawn from Moses, whose prophecy never ceased; this is the meaning of “rests His Presence.” Although wealth is also proved from Jonah, Jonah too was a prophet without interruption, even though he was sent only to Nineveh.”

: “As soon as he comes, ‘A mist shall rise from the earth’: the alef-dalet of Adonai raises vav to him, becoming within her ‘Lord of all the earth.’ Immediately, ‘It waters the whole face of the ground.’ From him Israel below is watered through the seventy facets of Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chukat 8, paragraph 1: “Rather, what was created on Shabbat was ‘the mouth of God’: the capacity for a person to speak Torah and for his words to be called words of the living God. This is the meaning of ‘and speak a word.’ Scripture does not say ‘from speaking a word,’ as it says ‘from pursuing your affairs,’ which would suit Rashi’s explanation that one must not utter prohibited speech. Instead it means: speak—but let it be God’s word. This is ‘the mouth of God.’ They say in the name of Rabbi Dov Ber that even words of Torah and prayer may fail to be true words. Certainly a person should always engage in Torah and mitzvot even without pure intention, as the Gemara teaches, and all the more so when he engages in them ordinarily, with no particular ulterior intention. Nevertheless, regarding holy inspiration and higher apprehension, even such words can be detrimental if he does not speak in the aspect of ‘the mouth of God.’ Thus the Gemara interprets ‘His discourse’ as referring to masters of the Talmud, all of whose conversation is Torah. This is ‘and speak a word’: everything he says should be Torah and the mouth of God.”

: “‘The Lord said to Moses, Why do you cry to Me?’—precisely ‘to Me.’ ‘Speak to the children of Israel, and let them journey’—precisely ‘journey.’ It depended upon mazal, for He wished to honor His beard.”

: “It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. No word of Torah, nor even a small letter, fails to allude to upper Wisdom; heaps upon heaps of its secrets depend on each, as in ‘His locks are curled in heaps.’”

: ““I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but great trembling fell upon them, and they fled into hiding.” Who were these men? Rabbi Yirmeya—or, according to another version, Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba—said: Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi. They had an advantage over him, and he had an advantage over them. Their advantage was that they were prophets, whereas he was not a prophet. His advantage was that he saw the vision, whereas they did not. Since they did not see it, why were they frightened? Although they did not see it, their supernal counterparts saw it. Ravina said: Learn from this that when someone becomes frightened, although he sees nothing, his supernal counterpart sees.”

k: volume-i|1097|0|Teaching attributed to the Yehudi HaKado
quote: : “Israel is bound at the root to the Will of wills: “In the beginning”—for the sake of Israel, who are called “the beginning.” Despite the accusations, Hashem chose Israel as His treasured possession. As the teaching transmitted from the holy Yehudi puts it, this is like a segulah that operates without a reason. This comes from Atika, the Will of wills.”

: “Another interpretation: “Then Moses sang.” This is what Scripture says: “They believed His words; they sang His praise.” Rabbi Abbahu said: Although it is already written that they believed while in Egypt—“The people believed”—they returned to unbelief, as it says, “Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand Your wonders.” When they came to the sea and saw the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, and how He judges the wicked—as it says, “My hand shall grasp judgment”—and He drowned Egypt in the sea, immediately “they believed in the Lord.” Through the merit of faith the holy spirit rested upon them, and they sang, as it is written, “Then Moses and the children of Israel sang.” “Then” signifies trust, as in, “From the time he entrusted him with his household,” and, “He placed all he possessed in his hand.” Thus: “They believed His words; they sang His praise.””

: “This Speech is called Shabbat. Because Shabbat is called Speech, weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbat. The printed marginal gloss, Gilyon Maharshab, relates: Rabbi Shimon acted this way—when he saw his mother speaking, he would say to her, ‘Mother, be silent; it is Shabbat, and this is forbidden.’ For this Speech must rule, and no other. This Speech, coming from the side of darkness, reveals deep things from within it. That is the meaning of ‘from darkness’: specifically from that which comes from the side of darkness.”

: “Laws of Shabbat dependent on speech, containing twenty-two sections. 'And speaking a word': your Shabbat speech should not resemble your weekday speech. It is therefore forbidden to say, 'I will do such-and-such tomorrow,' or 'I will buy such-and-such merchandise tomorrow.' Even idle conversation must not be excessive. Gloss: People who enjoy recounting reports and novel events may recount them on Shabbat as on weekdays. Someone who does not enjoy them, however, may not recount them merely so that his fellow will enjoy them, as stated in Terumat HaDeshen 61.”

: “The initials of oneg, “delight,” stand for Eden, Nahar and Gan—Eden, River and Garden—as stated in the Zohar. Although the Zohar there identifies Eden as the higher Mother, when one attains the higher Shabbat, Eden encompasses all three upper sefirot, as we explained from the Zohar and Tikkunei Zohar. The Zohar says that the lower Eden is called a garden in relation to the higher Eden. Just as the middle pillar is a river flowing from the lower Eden—the upper heh—to water the garden below, the lower Divine Presence, so the yod, Chokhmah, flows from the higher Eden, the supreme Keter, to water the garden that is the upper heh.”

: “Israel was commanded concerning ten commandments at Marah: the seven that Noah’s descendants had accepted, to which were added laws of justice, Shabbat, and honoring father and mother. Laws of justice, as it says, “There He established for them a statute and an ordinance.” Shabbat and honoring father and mother, as it says, “As Hashem your God commanded you.” Rav Judah said: “As He commanded you”—at Marah.”
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”
: “For in six days Hashem made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.”

: “Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and Hashem your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore Hashem your God commanded you to observe the Shabbat day.”

: “If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored; if you honor it by refraining from your usual ways, pursuing your affairs, and speaking of business—”

: “‘Call Shabbat a delight’: delight for all, for soul and body, for those above and below. What does ‘call’ mean? Invite it, as in ‘sacred convocations’—invited occasions, like inviting a guest into one’s home. ‘Call Shabbat a delight’ thus means inviting it as one invites a guest, with a properly prepared table and house, and suitable food and drink, beyond the other days. ‘Call Shabbat’ while it is still day. ‘The Lord’s holy one, honored’ is Yom Kippur: two that are one. ‘Honor it by refraining from your own ways’ is as we have explained.”

: “The festivals are called “sacred convocations” because Israel imparts holiness to them. Although Shabbat’s holiness is fixed and enduring, the portion of Emor also calls it a “sacred convocation”: a Jew must bring holiness into Shabbat as well. Thus “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it” is fulfilled through the day’s Kiddush, and the second version says, “Observe it to sanctify it”: accepting the sovereignty of Heaven through observing Shabbat brings holiness into it. The essential ability of Israel to impart holiness exists only through the Exodus. Before this, holiness was mentioned only regarding Shabbat—“He sanctified it”—meaning holiness bestowed by Hashem. When the Exodus began, “This month shall be for you” gave Israel the power to sanctify the month. Thus the head of the court declares, “Sanctified.””

: “On your day of rejoicing, your festivals, and your new moons, you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace sacrifices. They will be a remembrance for you before your God. I am Hashem your God.”

: “It was taught: R. Judah ben Beteira says: When the Temple stood, rejoicing was possible only through meat, as it says, “You shall sacrifice peace offerings, eat there, and rejoice before Hashem your God.” Now that the Temple does not stand, rejoicing is possible only through wine, as it says, “Wine gladdens the human heart.””

: “Rabbi Chiyya said: this is what we learned—action below awakens action above. If the action below is holy, holiness awakens above, comes to rest upon him, and he is sanctified through it. If he defiles himself below, a spirit of impurity awakens above, comes to rest upon him, and he is defiled through it. The matter depends upon action.”

: “If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored; if you honor it by refraining from your usual ways, pursuing your affairs, and speaking of business—”

: “The exilarch asked Rav Hamnuna: What is meant by “And call the Lord’s holy day honored”? He answered: This is Yom Kippur, on which there is neither eating nor drinking. The Torah says: Honor it with clean garments.”
: ““Remember” and “Observe” were spoken in a single utterance—something the human mouth cannot say and the human ear cannot hear.”

: “From the aspect of Chesed, however, the Holy One, blessed be He, is “Remember,” and the Shechinah is “Observe,” as the masters of the Mishnah have explained: “Remember” is for the male, and “Observe” for the bride. For on the right and on the left the branches are distinct, like the lobes of the lung, which are separated above. Corresponding to these are the living creatures—“Their faces and their wings were separated above”—and the open sections in a Torah scroll. Below, both are united in a single union, like the closed sections in a Torah scroll, where there is no separation. Therefore, at the place of union, the body, resembling the spine of the lulav, if its leaves are broken loose or separated, it is invalid.”
: “The Merciful One says: Rest on the Sabbath day, just as I rested on it, as it is written, ‘He rested on the seventh day; therefore the Lord blessed’ it.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”
: “These are the laws you shall set before them.”

: “‘They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.’ Water means Torah, as it says, ‘Everyone who thirsts, come to the water.’ Rabbi Yeisa asked: who had given them Torah here? The Torah had not yet been given to them. Rabbi Eleazar answered: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah said: certainly one receives everything even in the second month, but not as one who receives it at its proper time. Why? One who partakes of Passover at its proper time rises from below upward and does not descend, for we ascend in holiness and do not descend. One who partakes after its proper time descends from above downward. Thus they are equal in every respect, yet unequal: one ascends without descending; the other descends without ascending. One who offers Passover at its proper time therefore has greater praise. Happy are Israel, who merit everything, who merit Torah; whoever merits Torah merits the holy Name. Happy are Israel in this world and the world to come.”

: “Likewise, when this Speech proceeds from God’s mouth, the fiery living creatures are silent; when He is silent, the fiery living creatures speak. Thus ‘All the people saw the voices’: the voices of the roaring living creatures. ‘And the torches’: these issued from the living creatures’ speech through many kinds of melody before the King. Those who remain silent for the Torah scroll are in the likeness of those living creatures.”

: “A baraita teaches: “Moses brought back the people’s words to the Lord,” and it also says, “Moses told the people’s words to the Lord.” What did the Holy One, blessed be He, say to Moses? What did Moses say to Israel? What did Israel say to Moses? And what did Moses report before the Almighty? This concerns the command to set a boundary—Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda’s view. Rabbi says: At first he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses brought back”—words that unsettle a person’s mind. Finally he explained its reward, as it says “Moses told”—words that draw a person’s heart like aggada. Some say: At first he explained its reward—words that restore a person’s mind. Finally he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses told”—words as hard for a person as sinews.”
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”

: “A human being heals bitterness with something sweet, but the Holy One, blessed be He, heals bitterness with bitterness. How? He places a harmful thing within another harmful thing, performing a miracle within a miracle. Similarly, ‘Isaiah said: Let them bring a cake of figs and spread it on the boil, and he shall recover.’ Yet fresh flesh upon which one places a fig cake immediately decays! He placed a harmful thing upon another harmful thing to perform a miracle. Similarly, ‘He went out to the spring of water, cast salt into it, and said: Thus says the Lord, I have healed these waters; death and miscarriage shall no longer come from them.’ Yet sweet water into which one puts salt is immediately spoiled! He places a harmful thing within another harmful thing to perform a miracle. The Holy One told Moses: ‘Is this not My manner? With the very thing with which I strike, I heal. Therefore, since these waters are bitter, I shall heal them with something bitter.’”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

: “Likewise Torah scholars, children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they are not workers like the other servants, children of the ordinary realm. Their reward in this world and the world to come is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it says, ‘Honor it with clean clothing.’ Whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals should be done for them.”

: “Regarding the statement, “Since the Temple was destroyed, although prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages”: Rashi explains that it was taken from prophets who were not Sages. This may be challenged, since Nedarim 38a says that the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His Presence only upon someone wise, mighty, and wealthy. Some answer that uninterrupted indwelling requires wisdom, but prophecy for a particular mission, such as Jonah son of Amittai’s mission to Nineveh, does not. I am not satisfied with that answer. Rather, the meaning is this: Although the prophets’ prophecy, consisting of appearances and visions, was taken away, the Sages’ prophecy, which comes through wisdom, was not taken away. They know the truth through the holy spirit within them. For a time He may rest His Presence even upon pious people who are not Sages. There the proof is drawn from Moses, whose prophecy never ceased; this is the meaning of “rests His Presence.” Although wealth is also proved from Jonah, Jonah too was a prophet without interruption, even though he was sent only to Nineveh.”

: “It was taught that humanity is called by several names: adam, gever, enosh and ish. The greatest is adam, for it says, ‘God created adam in His image,’ and ‘In God’s image He made adam,’ rather than gever, enosh or ish. Rabbi Yehudah asked: but it says, ‘When an adam among you brings an offering to the Lord’—who needs an offering? A sinner, yet he is called adam. Rabbi Yitzchak replied: the offering sustains the upper and lower worlds and brings God contentment. Who is worthy to bring this contentment before Him? Adam, the most precious of all. He objected: ‘When an adam has upon the skin of his flesh…an affliction of tzara‘at.’ He answered: God wishes this one to be purified more than all, so that one at the highest level of all should not remain thus.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction: It is written, “I will take My grain in its season,” but also, “You shall gather your grain.” There is no contradiction: one concerns a time when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will; the other, a time when it does not. The Sages taught: What does “You shall gather your grain” teach? Since it says, “This book of Torah shall not leave your mouth,” one might take that literally. “You shall gather your grain” therefore teaches that one should combine Torah with the ordinary conduct of worldly life. This is Rabbi Yishmael’s view. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: If a person plows at plowing time, sows at sowing time, reaps at reaping time, threshes at threshing time, and winnows when the wind blows, what will become of Torah? Rather, when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will, its work is done by others, as it says, “Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks.” When Israel does not fulfill His will, it must do its own work, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Moreover, it does the work of others, as it says, “You shall serve your enemy.” Abaye said: Many followed Rabbi Yishmael’s course and succeeded; they followed Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s course and did not succeed.”

: “The Gemara says of “Israel has sinned”: although he has sinned, he remains Israel. Rabbi Abba compares this to a myrtle standing among thorns: it is still named and called a myrtle. A child is circumcised on the eighth day, without his conscious understanding, and thereby becomes a Jew. This shows that he is bound to Hashem at the root, in the beginning of thought. Whatever befalls him, in truth “our will is to do Your will; what prevents us is the leaven in the dough.” The myrtle stands among thorns, and from the surrounding roots of evil the leaven also spreads into the Jewish heart. The Gemara therefore attaches every possible evil to Achan, even transgression of the five books of Torah and the undoing of circumcision. Why describe him so harshly? Because “Israel has sinned” was written about him to teach that, despite sin, he remains Israel. Every evil is attached to him to teach that, whatever befalls a Jew, no castaway is ultimately cast off: the name Israel has not been uprooted from him.”

: “R. Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “A human being is born to toil.” I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or for manual labor. When it says, “For his mouth compels him,” you must conclude that he was created for toil of the mouth. But I still do not know whether this means toil in Torah or toil in conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must conclude that he was created for toil in Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies must labor; fortunate is the one who merits laboring in Torah.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 99b:2:1: ““Burdened with toil”—that is, all bodies were created for labor.”
: “Hashem will fight for you, and you shall remain silent.”

: “There is thought that consists of an undeveloped mental conception. There is also reflection in the heart, concerning which the Sages say, “Reflection is equivalent to speech”: a person mentally considers the whole subject and its words as though speaking, but does not utter them with his lips. This is called reflection. The explanation of belimah is therefore, “Restrain your mouth from speaking,” and also restrain your heart from reflecting. “If your mouth runs,” return to the place, for it is said, “The living creatures run and return.” A person’s vitality likewise runs and returns like a flash of lightning. When he restrains his mouth from speech and his heart from reflection, da’at can shine upon him. Rashi explains da’at as the holy spirit. For a moment, light from Atika can shine upon him, since da’at is the inward dimension of Keter. This is attained through silence.”

: “He said to them, “This is what Hashem spoke: tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Shabbat for Hashem. Bake what you need to bake and cook what you need to cook; whatever remains, put aside to keep until morning.””

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””
: “He said, “For I will be with you. This shall be your sign that I sent you: when you bring the people out of Egypt, you will serve God upon this mountain.””

: “Thus ‘They returned from exploring the land’: they return to the evil side and turn away from the path of truth. They say: what does it matter to us? We have yet to see good in the world. We labored in it, yet our house is empty and we sit in disgrace among the people. Who will merit that world, who will enter it? Better had we not toiled so much. ‘They recounted to him and said’: we labored and wearied ourselves to know our portion in that world. ‘It indeed flows with milk and honey’: that upper world is good, as we know from Torah—but who can merit it?”
: “He encountered you on the road and attacked all the weak stragglers behind you, while you were weary and exhausted; he did not fear God.”
: “If Hashem delights in us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Tzidkat HaTzadik 154:1: “Just as a person must believe in God, so afterward he must believe in himself. That is, God has concern with him: he is not a useless being who is here for a night and gone, nor like the wild beasts that are lost and cease to exist after death. He must believe that his soul comes from the Source of Life, blessed be His name, and that God delights and takes pleasure in it when it does His will. This is the meaning of “They believed in God and in Moses His servant”: Moses denotes the whole of the six hundred thousand souls of Israel in that generation. They believed that God desired them … and that He wishes for and accepts satisfaction from the good within them.”
: “Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chalafta said: All the kingdoms are called by the name ‘Egypt,’ because they bring distress upon Israel.”
: “She lusted after their lovers, whose members were like those of donkeys and whose emission was like that of horses.”
: “Moses said to the people, “Do not fear. Stand firm and see the deliverance Hashem will perform for you today. For the Egyptians you have seen today, you will never see again.””

: “A baraita teaches: One who recites Shema in the morning must mention the Exodus from Egypt in the blessing “True and Firm.” Rabbi says: He must mention kingship in it. Others say: He must mention the splitting of the Sea of Reeds and the striking of the firstborn in it. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: He must mention all of these and say, “Rock of Israel and its Redeemer.””
: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: when Israel camped by the sea, they saw many multitudes, armies and camps above and below, all assembled against Israel. Out of their distress they began to pray.”
: “Hashem will not abandon him into his hand, nor allow him to be condemned when he is judged.”
: “You of this generation, consider Hashem’s word: Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of deep darkness? Why have My people said, “We have broken loose; we will no longer come to You”?”

: “Rabbi Levi said: If Israel properly observes Shabbat for even one day, the son of David will come. Why? Because it equals all the commandments. Thus it says, “For He is our God, and we are the people He shepherds, the flock of His hand—today, if you heed His voice.” Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Although I have set a fixed time for the end, which will arrive in its appointed season whether they repent or not, if they repent for even one day, I will bring it before its appointed season. Thus: “Today, if you heed His voice.” Just as we find that the son of David comes through all the commandments, so he comes through observing one Shabbat, because Shabbat equals all the commandments.”
: “Yet you have not called upon Me, Jacob, for you have grown weary of Me, Israel.”
: “For this matter is very close to you: it is in your mouth and in your heart, for you to carry it out.”

: “‘Those who practice it’: A person says, ‘I have studied wisdom but have not studied Torah; what place have I there?’ The Holy One, blessed be He, says to Israel: ‘By your lives, all wisdom and all Torah are one simple matter. Whoever fears Me and practices the words of Torah has all wisdom and all Torah in his heart.’ From where do we know this? ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord; good understanding belongs to all who practice them’; ‘Fear of the Lord is pure and endures forever’; and ‘Fear of the Lord is wisdom.’”
: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”

: “Hashem said to Moses, “Write this as a memorial in the book and place it in Joshua’s hearing: I will utterly erase the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens.” Moses built an altar and called its name “Hashem is my banner.” He said, “For a hand is upon the throne of Yah: Hashem is at war with Amalek from generation to generation.””
: “He saw Amalek and took up his discourse, saying, “Amalek was first among nations, but his end is utter destruction.””

: “When Hashem your God grants you rest from all your surrounding enemies, in the land Hashem your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall erase the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens. Do not forget.”

: ““Whenever Moses raised his hand, Israel prevailed.” Do Moses’ hands wage war or defeat an army? Rather, this teaches that whenever Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they prevailed; otherwise they fell. Similarly, “Make yourself a fiery serpent and place it upon a pole, and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.” Does a serpent bring death or give life? Rather, when Israel looked upward and subjected their hearts to their Father in Heaven, they were healed; otherwise they wasted away.”

: “‘An angel of the Lord called to him from heaven and said, Abraham, Abraham.’ Rabbi Chiyya taught: This is language of affection and encouragement. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said: It addresses him and the generations to come. No generation lacks someone like Abraham; no generation lacks someone like Jacob; no generation lacks someone like Moses; and no generation lacks someone like Samuel.”

: “The Mishnah speaks of boats tied to one another. Is this not obvious? Rava said: The ruling is needed to permit carrying through the small boat between them. Rav Safra said to him: Moses, have you really stated this correctly? The Mishnah says, “One may carry from this boat to that one.” Rather, Rav Safra said: It is needed to permit establishing an eruv and carrying from one to the other, as a baraita teaches: If boats are tied to one another, an eruv may be established and one may carry from one to the other.”

k: volume-i|1163|2|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “In every generation there is such a soul, as Bereshit Rabbah teaches: no generation is without someone like Abraham, and no generation is without someone like Moses. This is also known from the holy Ari’s explanation of the Talmud’s expression, ‘Moses, you have spoken well.’ The root of his soul is the Torah, which bears his name. His raising his hand in prayer to God is prayer empowered by Torah.”
: “Hashem is close to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him truthfully.”

: “It is written, “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says, “One who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.””
: “He restores my soul and leads me along paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.”
: “Because of the sin of his greed I became angry and struck him; I hid Myself and was angry, yet he went on waywardly along the path of his heart.”
: ““Return, wayward children; I will heal your waywardness.” “Here we are; we have come to You, for You are Hashem our God.””

: “R. Hama bar Hanina contrasted two statements: It is written, “Return, wayward children,” implying that from the outset you were merely wayward; but it is written, “I will heal your waywardness.” There is no contradiction: one concerns repentance from love, and the other repentance from fear.”
: ““From the outset you were wayward”—when you repent, He regards you as though the original sin had come about through youthful folly and waywardness.”

: “It was stated: If an infant died within thirty days and its mother then became betrothed to another man, Ravina said in Rava’s name: If she is married to an Israelite, she must undergo halitza; if she is married to a priest, she need not undergo halitza. Rav Sherevya, in Rava’s name, said: In either case she must undergo halitza. Ravina said to Rav Sherevya: Rava said that in the evening, but by morning he had retracted it. Rav Sherevya said to him: Have you permitted her? May it be your will to permit forbidden fat!”

: “Rava expounded: A courtyard damaged by rainwater may be covered with straw. Rav Pappa said to Rava: But a baraita teaches: When spreading it, one may not use a basket or a large basket, but must use the bottom of a basket. Rava then appointed a public speaker and expounded: What I told you was mistaken. Rather, this was said in Rabbi Eliezer’s name: When spreading the straw, one may not use a basket or a large basket, but must use the bottom of a basket.”

: “This excludes Rava’s earlier exposition. Rava had expounded: If two women gave birth to two boys in hiding, the sons may authorize one another to claim the firstborn’s share. Rav Pappa told Rava: But Ravin sent word, “I asked all my teachers about this and they gave me no answer. They did, however, report in Rabbi Yannai’s name: If the children’s identities were initially known and subsequently confused, they may authorize one another; if their identities were never known, they may not.” Rava then appointed a public speaker beside him and expounded: “The statements I previously gave you were mistaken. Rather, they reported in Rabbi Yannai’s name: If their identities were known and later confused, they may authorize one another; if their identities were never known, they may not.””

: “Rava expounded: A woman may wash her hair on Friday and immerse after Shabbat. Rav Pappa said to Rava: But Ravin sent in his letter, “A woman must not wash her hair on Friday and immerse after Shabbat.” Consider: How can she wash during the day and immerse at night? Immersion should follow the washing immediately, which it does not! Rava again appointed a spokesman and announced, “The words I told you were a mistake on my part. Rather, this is what was said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: A woman must not wash her hair on Friday and immerse after Shabbat. Consider: How can she wash during the day and immerse at night? Immersion should be close to the washing, which it is not!” The ruling is that a woman washes her hair during the day and immerses at night. Yet the ruling is also that a woman should wash her hair only at night. Do these rulings not contradict one another? There is no difficulty: One concerns a case where daytime preparation is possible, and the other a case where it is impossible.”

Commentary: Rashi on Niddah 68a:3:1: ““Consider how a woman can do so”: Even the allowance to separate preparation from immersion by that much time was made only with difficulty. It is permitted because, if she prepared on the night of immersion, she might not wash her hair thoroughly, since she is hurrying to immerse and is anxious to return home.”

Commentary: Rashi on Niddah 68a:6:1–2: ““Where it is possible”: If she can prepare her hair during the day, she does so during the day. “Where it is impossible”: If she cannot prepare then—for example, when immersion falls after a festival—she prepares only at night.”

: “Rava later said—or, according to another version, Rav Ashi said: What I said was not correct. Reish Lakish said: Wherever you find a positive commandment and a prohibition, if you can fulfill both, that is preferable; if not, let the positive commandment override the prohibition. Here too, ḥalitzah is possible, allowing both the positive commandment and the prohibition to be fulfilled. An objection was raised: “If they had intercourse, they acquired the women as wives.” This is a refutation.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel’s name: A weaver’s implements may be moved on Shabbat. They asked Rav Yehuda: What is the law of the upper and lower beams? He said yes, and then no; the ruling remained uncertain in his hands. It was stated: Rav Nahman said in Shmuel’s name that a weaver’s implements may be moved on Shabbat, including the upper and lower beams, but not the posts.”

: “Ben Azzai says: Run to a light commandment as to a weighty one, and flee from transgression. For one commandment draws another in its wake, and one transgression draws another. The reward of a commandment is a commandment; the reward of a transgression is a transgression.”

k: volume-i|1176|0|Tosafot Yom Tov on Pirkei Avot 4:2:3
ref: Tosafot Yom Tov on Pirkei Avot 4:2:3
quote: : ““The reward of a transgression is a transgression”: God leaves him in the hands of his evil nature; this does not mean that Heaven helps him, as Bartenura said regarding the reward of a mitzvah. For Yoma 38 and Shabbat 104 say: One who comes to purify himself receives help; one who comes to defile himself is given an opening. Midrash Shemuel likewise explains this in Rabbenu Yonah’s name.”
: “Add wrongdoing to their wrongdoing, and let them not enter into Your righteousness.”
: “Let them be erased from the book of life and not be inscribed with the righteous.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Scripture says, “As he wrestled with him”—like a person embracing another, whose hand reaches the other’s right thigh. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said: The wrestler appeared to Jacob as a gentile, for the Master said: An Israelite joined by a gentile on the road should place him on his right. Rav Shmuel bar Aha, teaching before Rav Pappa in Rava bar Ulla’s name, said: He appeared to him as a Torah scholar, for the Master said: One who walks on his teacher’s right is an uncultivated person. The Sages hold that he came from behind Jacob and displaced both thigh-sinews.”

: “Rav said: The evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two entrances to the heart, as it says, “Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink and bubble.” Shmuel said: It resembles a grain of wheat, as it says, “Sin crouches at the opening.””
: “When a wicked person turns back from his wickedness and practices justice and righteousness, he will live because of them.”

: “It was taught: R. Meir used to say: Great is repentance, for because of one individual who repents, the whole world is forgiven, as it says, “I will heal their waywardness; I will love them freely, for My anger has turned away from him.” It does not say “from them,” but “from him.””
: “It is good to give thanks to Hashem and sing praise to Your name, Most High.”

: ““It is good to give thanks to the Lord.” Adam said: Let all generations learn from me that whoever confesses his transgressions and abandons them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, “It is good to give thanks to the Lord.””

k: volume-i|1185|0|Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 1, para
quote: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 1, paragraph 1: “Of this Solomon said, ‘If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread.’ Holy works explain that sometimes the evil inclination sees that a person has become so mired in sins that there is no holiness left for it to draw from; it then tempts him to perform a mitzvah, so that afterward it can draw holiness from him. This certainly comes from hatred: God did not send it to tempt a person to do good so that it could feed on him; its task of tempting toward evil should have sufficed. This additional act is hatred. Solomon therefore said, ‘If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread’: burden him with the battle of Torah. ‘If he is thirsty, give him water’ also refers to Torah, as Rashi explains. ‘For you heap coals upon his head.’ Do not think or fear that Torah will add strength to the impure forces. The Arizal explains from ‘To the wicked God said: What right have you to recount My statutes?’ that a wicked person’s good deeds can add strength to impurity. Nevertheless Solomon teaches that with Torah the remedy is ‘feed him bread’; it will not harm you. When a person wants Torah in order to escape the evil inclination, Torah will help for good: ‘You heap coals upon his head,’ rather than strengthening impurity, God forbid. As the Sages said, just as a nut’s interior is not spoiled when it is soiled with mud, so the Torah of a scholar who has sinned is not spoiled. The dirt lies only in the outer shell, Esau’s garments; what is insid

: “Every day we bless the luminaries of light, the upper lights established in that primordial light. All levels are blessed and shine together from the upper lamp. These are called luminaries of fire. Because of this mystery, we bless ‘who creates the luminaries of fire.’”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”
: “Delight in Hashem, and He will grant you your heart’s requests.”

: “Likewise Torah scholars, children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they are not workers like the other servants, children of the ordinary realm. Their reward in this world and the world to come is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it says, ‘Honor it with clean clothing.’ Whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals should be done for them.”
: “For a commandment is a lamp and Torah is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.”

: “Isaac our father was the pillar of divine service, bound as an offering to Hashem. The Zohar says, “God called the light day”—this is Abraham; “and the darkness He called night”—this is Isaac, whose eyes became too dim to see. This is the light of the Temple’s service, which shines out of darkness, for Isaac said, “I have offered my soul before You.” The light of Torah is an intrinsic light shining for the whole world: Hashem is God of heaven and God of earth. Abraham thus brought light to the entire world. The light of divine service, by contrast, shines in one’s heart from within the darkness. Isaac spoke only of offering his own soul before Him.”

: “Someone who conducts himself according to medicine, intending only that his whole body and its limbs be healthy and that his children perform his work and labor for his needs, does not follow a good path. Rather, he should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul may be upright in knowing God. A person cannot understand and contemplate wisdom when hungry or ill, or when one of his limbs hurts. He should intend to have a child who may become wise and great in Israel. A person who follows this path serves God constantly throughout his life, even while doing business or having marital relations, because his purpose in everything is to obtain his needs so that his body may be healthy enough to serve God. Even when sleeping, if he deliberately sleeps to rest his mind and body, lest he become ill and unable to serve God while ill, his sleep itself becomes service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this the sages commanded, 'Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.' Solomon likewise said in his wisdom, 'Know Him in all your ways, and He will straighten your paths.'”

: “R. Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “A human being is born to toil.” I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or for manual labor. When it says, “For his mouth compels him,” you must conclude that he was created for toil of the mouth. But I still do not know whether this means toil in Torah or toil in conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must conclude that he was created for toil in Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies must labor; fortunate is the one who merits laboring in Torah.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 99b:2:1: ““Burdened with toil”—that is, all bodies were created for labor.”
: “Does the Master not hold that using a torch for Havdalah is the preferred way to fulfill the mitzvah?”

: “Torah purifies the body’s flesh to a greater degree, as the conclusion of Chagigah says, 'Torah scholars, whose entire bodies are fire...' This is heavenly fire that consumes fire. It therefore burns Gehinnom’s fire and the inclination’s fire, which is also fire, as in Kiddushin 81, 'See that you are fire,' and the fiery lion of idolatry in Yoma. Hosea likewise says, 'Like an oven heated by a baker...burning like a flaming fire.' The 903 kinds of death in Berakhot 8 equal, numerically, three times 'fire,' corresponding to jealousy, desire, and honor, which remove a person from the world, as taught in Avot. These are also the three things called the evil eye, the evil inclination, and hatred of other people, which remove one from the world.”

: “For all other fires are hidden and put away on Shabbat, except one fire of upper holiness, which is revealed and included in Shabbat’s holiness. When this fire is revealed, all other fires are hidden and put away before it. This is the fire of Isaac’s binding, which blazed upon the altar. Therefore one must bless the light of fire. The fire required is not ordinary weekday fire, but Shabbat’s fire; this fire issues from that upper fire.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “Rav Yosef said: While a person is engaged in a commandment, it protects him and saves him; when he is not engaged in it, it protects him but does not save him. Torah protects and saves him whether or not he is presently engaged in it. Rabba objected: Did Doeg and Ahithophel not engage in Torah? Why did it not protect them? Rather, Rava said: While a person is engaged in Torah, it protects him and saves him; when he is not engaged in it, it protects him but does not save him. A commandment protects him but does not save him, whether or not he is presently engaged in it.”

: ““A commandment protects but does not save, whether one is engaged in it or not”: This is puzzling. What does the baraita mean when it says that Scripture compares a commandment to a lamp—just as a lamp protects only temporarily, so does a commandment? If this means protection from the evil inclination, a commandment does not protect at all; if it means protection from punishment, it protects always. Why, likewise, does Scripture compare Torah to light, because it protects always? If this means protection from punishment, a commandment also always protects; if it means rescue from the evil inclination, Torah rescues only temporarily.”

: “Rabbi Levi said: The ear is to the body as a fumigating stand is to vessels. Many vessels are placed upon the stand; one puts incense beneath it, and they all absorb its fragrance. So all two hundred and forty-eight limbs of a person receive life through the ear. From where do we know this? ‘Listen, and your soul shall live.’”
: “Incline your ear and come to Me; listen, and your soul will live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful kindnesses promised to David.”

: “But it is written, “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices”! That passage describes events after the giving of the Torah. This is satisfactory according to the view that Jethro came after the giving of the Torah; but according to the view that he came beforehand, what can be said? For the sons of Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi differed: One said that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah, and the other said afterward. The view that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah holds that descendants of Noah offered peace offerings.”

: ““They shall be a people for Me.” Rabba bar Rav Huna said: Israel possesses an additional distinction in comparison with converts. Regarding Israel it is written, “I will be their God, and they shall be My people.” Regarding converts it is written, “Who is this who pledged his heart to approach Me, declares the Lord?” followed by, “You shall be My people, and I will be your God.””
: “My dwelling will be over them. I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
: “You will be My people, and I will be your God.”
: “I will take you to Myself as a people, and I will be your God. You will know that I am Hashem your God, who brings you out from under Egypt’s burdens.”

: “You have seen what I did to Egypt: I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Me. Now, if you listen carefully to My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasure among all peoples, for the whole earth is Mine.”
: “No stranger spent the night outdoors; I opened my doors to the traveler.”
: “Now, if you listen carefully to My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasure among all peoples, for the whole earth is Mine.”
: ““I have loved you,” says Hashem. You ask, “How have You loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” declares Hashem. “Yet I loved Jacob.””

: “In the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts punishment from Esau, what will Esau do? He will wrap himself in his cloak like an elder and come sit beside Jacob. From where do we know this? ‘Though you set your nest among the stars.’ The stars mean Israel, as it says, ‘Look toward heaven,’ and ‘So shall your descendants be.’ What will Jacob tell him? ‘My brother, you cannot be a brother like me,’ as it says, ‘I shall be your plagues, Death; I shall be your destruction, netherworld; compassion shall be hidden from My eyes.’ ‘I shall be your plagues, Death’ refers to the decrees you issued against me: you imposed a twofold decree that I worship idols. Had I done so, I would have incurred death at Heaven’s hand; if I refused to worship, you would kill me. Therefore, ‘I shall be your plagues, Death.’”
: “Though you soar high like an eagle and place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares Hashem.”

k: volume-i|1210|0|R. Chaim ibn Attar, Or HaChaim on Exodus
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim ibn Attar, Or HaChaim on Exodus 18:21:6: “It appears that the reason is that God wished to show the Israelites of that generation, and every succeeding generation, that there are people among the nations of great understanding and intelligence. Consider Jethro’s insight in his advice and in the way he chose to organize people: among the nations are people who recognize sound courses of action. The purpose is to teach that Israel were not chosen because their understanding and discernment surpassed all the nations. Jethro’s insight proves this. Thus you learn that God chose Israel not because of their abundant wisdom and intelligence, but because of supernal kindness and love for the patriarchs. This explanation is even more satisfying according to the view that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah, as stated in Zevachim 116a. God wisely arranged this before the Torah was given: although the nations include people wiser than Israel, God nevertheless brought us to Him and chose us. For this especially we must praise Him who chose us because of His kindnesses. Even according to the view that Jethro came after the Torah was given, there is a reason for placing his arrival earlier: to make this purpose apparent; otherwise it would not be revealed. Understand this.”

: ““Regarding Israel it is written”: “I will be their God,” even though they are not yet a people for Me. Because I draw them near, they will become a people for Me. Converts, however, are not drawn near from Heaven unless they first draw themselves near to become good.”

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua bar Nechemya said in Rabbi Chanan ben Pazi’s name: “A nation from within a nation.” It does not say “a people from within a nation,” but “a nation from within a nation”: these were uncircumcised and those were uncircumcised; these grew forelocks and those grew forelocks. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Shmuel bar Nachman said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed from Egypt. Why? “Therefore say to the children of Israel…” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: It is written, “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”
: “As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.”
: “As I live—declares the Lord Hashem—I will surely reign over you with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured fury.”

: “I will give you a new heart and place a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will place My spirit within you and bring it about that you follow My statutes, observe My laws, and carry them out.”
: “Bring us back to You, Hashem, and we will return. Renew our days as in ancient times.”

: “From the days of your ancestors you have turned away from My statutes and have not observed them. “Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says Hashem of Hosts. But you ask, “How shall we return?””

Parallel: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 46:5: “The Holy One, blessed be He, set aside the beings above and below and chose none of them, but only His people Israel. He brought them out of Egypt, the nakedness of the earth, a place of filth and impurity, not through an angel or the like, but the Holy One in His own glory descended there, as it says, ‘I descended to rescue him.’ This was to draw them close to Him in true nearness and union, an actual bond of the soul: mouth-to-mouth kisses signify speaking the word of God, which is halakhah; spirit cleaving to spirit signifies comprehending Torah and knowing His will and wisdom, which are truly one. Embracing signifies performing the practical commandments with the 248 limbs, for the 248 commandments are the 248 limbs of the King, as explained above. In general, these fall into three aspects: right, left and middle—kindness, judgment and mercy—the two arms and the body.”
: “Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They asked after each other’s well-being and entered the tent.”

: “'Moses’ father-in-law': here Jethro took honor in Moses—'I am the king’s father-in-law.' Previously, Moses had attributed his greatness to his father-in-law, as it says, 'He returned to Jether his father-in-law.' 'To Moses and Israel': Moses was equivalent to all Israel, as taught in Mekhilta.”
: “And her two sons: one was named Gershom, for he said, “I was a stranger in a foreign land.””
: “He sent word to Moses: “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons accompanying her.””

: “‘And her two sons.’ Rabbi Chiyya said: were they her sons rather than Moses’ sons? Because she cared for them without her husband, the Torah called them her sons rather than his. Rabbi Yose said: although they were Moses’ sons, they were certainly her sons in truth. Rabbi Elazar said: Moses was united with another, exalted holy place, and calling these his sons did not befit his honor. Although they were his sons, in honor of that place with which he was united, it calls them her sons here; afterward it calls them his sons. Why? When they first arrived, Moses was speaking with the Shekhinah. After he withdrew and went out to his father-in-law, it says, ‘Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with his sons and his wife.’”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said in Rabbi Ami’s name: If the woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male; if the man emits seed first, she gives birth to a female, as it says, “When a woman brings forth seed and bears a male.” The Sages taught: Originally they used to say, “If the woman emits seed first she bears a male, and if the man emits seed first she bears a female,” but the Sages did not explain the basis until Rabbi Tzadok came and explained: “These are Leah’s sons, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, and Dinah his daughter.” Scripture associates the males with the female, and the females with the male.”
: “She gave birth to a son, and he named him Gershom, for he said, “I was a stranger in a foreign land.””
: “The other was named Eliezer, for “My father’s God came to my aid and saved me from Pharaoh’s sword.””
: “According to the Sages, what does “one” mean? The outstanding one in his flock.”

: ““Go down, for your people have corrupted themselves.” It does not say “the people,” but “your people.” Moses said: Master of the universe, how are they my people? The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: They are your people. While they were still in Egypt I told you, “I shall bring out My hosts, My people.” I told you not to mingle a mixed multitude with them. In your humility and goodness you told Me: Those who return are always accepted. I knew what they would do; I told you no, yet fulfilled your wish. They were the ones who made the calf. They worshipped idols, made it, and caused My people to sin. See what is written: Not “These are our gods,” but “These are your gods,” for the converts who went up with Moses made it and told Israel, “These are your gods.” Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses, “Go down, for your people have corrupted themselves.””
: “In the morning you will see Hashem’s glory, because He has heard your complaints against Hashem. What are we, that you should complain against us?”
: “The other was named Eliezer, for “My father’s God came to my aid and saved me from Pharaoh’s sword.””
: “And her two sons: one was named Gershom, for he said, “I was a stranger in a foreign land.””

: “'The name of the one was Gershom, for he said: I was a stranger...and the name of the one was Eliezer, for the God of my father was my help...' Here 'for he said' is not written. One may say that it refers back to the earlier 'for he said.' Concerning Gershom, 'for he said' is written because a midrash relates that when Jethro gave Moses his daughter, Moses had to stipulate that the first son would be for idolatry. He was therefore not circumcised until the angel encountered Moses on the road and sought to kill him; then Zipporah circumcised him and released him from the condition made with her father. Here, therefore, 'for he said' means that it now became known to everyone that he had been compelled into this condition: he was a stranger and had to comply with Jethro’s demand. Nevertheless, through this condition Jonathan descended from him and became a priest to Micah’s idol. 'For he said' is not written concerning Eliezer because Moses did not wish to reveal that he had killed a man and Pharaoh had sought to kill him. The Gemara, however, implies that Eliezer son of Moses was not circumcised until the angel encountered Moses, who said, 'If I circumcise him and set out, it will endanger the infant.' This was Eliezer, since we do not find that Moses had another son after coming to Egypt.”

: “He told them: “This is the tradition I received from my grandfather’s household: A person should always hire himself out for foreign service rather than depend upon others.” He understood this as actual idolatrous service. That was not its meaning: “foreign service” means work that is foreign to him. Thus Rav told Rav Kahana, “Skin a carcass in the marketplace and earn your wage. Do not say: I am a great man, and this work is beneath my dignity.” When David saw how greatly he valued money, he appointed him over the treasuries, as it says, “Shevuel son of Gershom son of Manasseh was chief over the treasuries.” Was his name Shevuel? Was it not Yonatan? Rabbi Yochanan said: He returned to God with all his heart.”

: “Strangers will stand and tend your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers. You will be called priests of Hashem; you will be spoken of as servants of our God. You will consume the wealth of nations and take pride in their splendor.”
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”

: “The French authorities say that conversion was required because this was before the giving of the Torah, when his legal status followed the male, according to the statement, 'Among the nations, follow the male.' At birth, therefore, they did not circumcise him, since his legal status was Egyptian; when he grew up, he chose to convert and was circumcised. My view is otherwise: from the time Abraham entered the covenant, they were Israelites and were not counted among the nations. Thus, concerning Esau it is asked, 'Perhaps an apostate Israelite is different?' The argument follows all the more: after the giving of the Torah, a gentile’s union with a daughter of Abraham is prohibited by a negative commandment and cannot create betrothal, yet she is a pool of purification for the nations, rendering her child fit and like herself. Certainly before the Torah she would purify her child to be like herself, obligating him in circumcision as Abraham’s seed and including him among the children of Israel.”

: “In many places God warns the holy seed to take care concerning the convert. Then a concealed matter emerges from its sheath; once revealed, it immediately returns into its sheath and clothes itself there. After all those warnings about the convert, the matter emerges and declares, ‘You know the nefesh of the convert.’ Immediately it reenters its sheath, returns into its garment and becomes hidden: ‘For you were strangers in the land of Egypt.’ Scripture reckons that, since it immediately reclothed itself, no one would notice. Through this nefesh of the convert, the holy neshamah knows the matters of this world and benefits from them; an alternative reading adds that it draws them in.”
: “Do not oppress a stranger. You know the stranger’s feelings, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.”
: “The woman conceived and gave birth to a son. She saw that he was good and hid him for three months.”

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””
: “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.”

: “Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina differed: One said that descendants of Noah offered peace offerings, while the other said that they did not. What is the reason of the view that they offered peace offerings? “Abel too brought from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat.” What offering has its fat offered upon the altar without the whole animal being offered? A peace offering. What is the reason of the view that they did not? “Awake, north wind; come, south wind”: Let the nation whose service is confined to the north give way, and let the nation whose service includes north and south come. But according to the latter view, is it not written, “From their fat”? This means their choicest animals. And according to the former view, is it not written, “Awake, north wind”? That passage concerns the ingathering of the exiles.”
: “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.”

: “If he accepts, they circumcise him immediately. If portions of skin remain that invalidate the circumcision, they circumcise him again. Once he has healed, they immerse him immediately. Two Torah scholars stand over him and inform him of some lighter and some weightier commandments. Once he has immersed and come up, he is an Israelite in every respect. … “Two Torah scholars stand over him”—but Rabbi Ḥiyya said in Rabbi Yoḥanan’s name that a convert requires three! Rabbi Yoḥanan told the reciter: Teach “three.””

: “'It was on the following day': it was the day after Yom Kippur, as we learned in Sifrei. What does 'on the following day' mean? The day after he descended from the mountain. Necessarily, it can only mean the day after Yom Kippur, because before the giving of the Torah he could not have said, 'I make known God’s statutes...' From the giving of the Torah until Yom Kippur, Moses did not sit to judge the people: on the seventeenth of Tammuz he descended and broke the tablets; early the next morning he ascended, remained for eighty days, and descended on Yom Kippur. This passage is not written in chronological order, for the event 'It was on the following day' did not take place until the second year. Even according to the view that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah, his departure for his own land did not occur until the second year. Here it says, 'Moses sent his father-in-law away,' while, at the departure of the tribal camps, we find Moses saying to him, 'We are journeying to the place...' and 'Please do not leave us.' If this passage were before the giving of the Torah, where do we find that he returned after being sent away? If you say that there it mentions Hobab rather than Jethro, and Hobab was Jethro’s son: Hobab and Jethro are the same person, as it says, 'Of the descendants of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law.'”
: “You shall discern among all the people capable men who fear God, men of truth who hate unjust gain. Set them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””
: “For abundant wisdom brings abundant vexation, and whoever increases knowledge increases pain.”

: “No longer will one person teach his fellow or his brother, saying, “Know Hashem,” for all will know Me, from their smallest to their greatest, declares Hashem. For I will forgive their wrongdoing and remember their sin no more.”

: “We learned: Torah gives a person 613 kinds of counsel for becoming complete with his Master, because his Master wishes to benefit him in this world and the world to come—especially the world to come. Everything through which God perfects a person is perfected through the good he merits in the world to come. Why? Because the world to come belongs to God.”

: “Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous. He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden, and each will point with his finger, as it says, “On that day they will say: This is our God, for whom we hoped, that He would save us. This is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us exult and rejoice in His salvation.””

: “Moses our teacher’s root was the Written Torah, the Tree of Life, introducing words of Torah into the wise heart at the right. Moses knew nothing of evil, since at his birth the house was filled with light, and he wished all Israel to be like this, as at the giving of the Torah, when 'I said: You are divine' was said. Rabbi Akiva, who descended from converts and said, 'When I was ignorant...' was rooted in the Oral Torah: the abundant wisdom that rectifies abundant anger. As Nedarim 22 b says, had Israel not sinned, they would have received only the five books of Torah. Why? 'For in much wisdom is much anger.' Thus his root was the utterance 'You shall have no other,' uprooting evil from the foolish heart so that only the good Tree of Knowledge remains.”
