quote: : “The holy Ari teaches that Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah. The Talmud places the account of the giving of the Torah in tractate Shabbat’s chapter ‘Rabbi Akiva.’ Shabbat is connected to the giving of the Torah because everyone agrees that the Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Its placement in ‘Rabbi Akiva’ reflects his being the root of the Oral Torah. He descended from converts; yet the Written and Oral Torah are truly one.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “It was taught: Naaman was a resident alien; Nebuzaradan was a full convert. Haman’s descendants studied Torah in Bnei Brak; Sisera’s descendants taught children in Jerusalem; Sennacherib’s descendants taught Torah publicly. Who were they? Shemayah and Avtalyon.”

: ““Let us appoint Rabbi Akiva—he lacks ancestral merit.” This is found in Sanhedrin, chapter Kol Yisrael Yesh Lahen Helek, 96: Some of Sisera’s descendants learned Torah in Jerusalem. Who were they? Rabbi Akiva. It is also found in Gittin, chapter Ha-Nizzakin, 57.”
: “You shall discern among all the people capable men who fear God, men of truth who hate unjust gain. Set them over the people as leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.”

: “Chovav: he loved the Torah. When he came to the Land, they gave him the fertile district of Jericho. He said, ‘I left everything I possessed and came for no purpose but to study Torah. If I am now to sow and reap, when shall I study?’ They told him, ‘There is someone who teaches Torah in the city, but the place is dry wilderness and has no wheat.’ When his descendants heard this, they went there, as it says, ‘The children of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the children of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, south of Arad, and dwelled with the people.’ They found Jabez sitting in the study house, with priests, Levites, kings, and all Israel seated there. They said, ‘We are converts; how can we sit there among these?’ They sat at the entrances of the study house, listening and learning, as it says, ‘The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites; these are the Kenites.’ Tirathites: they sat at the entrance; Shimeathites: they listened and learned; Sucathites: Israel sheltered them. Another interpretation of Tirathites: when Israel enters distress, they sound an alarm and are answered. Who are the Kenites? The descendants of Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law. Of them it says, ‘Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you shall find it.’ In reward for ‘Call him, and let him eat bread,’ said of Moses, of whom it says, ‘For I drew him from the water,’ Jethro’s descendants merited seats in the Chamber of
: “The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez were the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. They are the Kenites who came from Hammath, ancestor of the house of Rechab.”

: “It was taught in a baraita: One thousand seven hundred inferences from lesser to greater, verbal analogies, and fine points of the scribes were forgotten during the mourning for Moses. Rabbi Abbahu said: Nevertheless, Othniel son of Kenaz restored them through his dialectical reasoning, as it says, “Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, captured it, and he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.””

: “Chovav: he loved the Torah. When he came to the Land, they gave him the fertile district of Jericho. He said, ‘I left everything I possessed and came for no purpose but to study Torah. If I am now to sow and reap, when shall I study?’ They told him, ‘There is someone who teaches Torah in the city, but the place is dry wilderness and has no wheat.’ When his descendants heard this, they went there, as it says, ‘The children of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the children of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, south of Arad, and dwelled with the people.’ They found Jabez sitting in the study house, with priests, Levites, kings, and all Israel seated there. They said, ‘We are converts; how can we sit there among these?’ They sat at the entrances of the study house, listening and learning, as it says, ‘The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites; these are the Kenites.’ Tirathites: they sat at the entrance; Shimeathites: they listened and learned; Sucathites: Israel sheltered them. Another interpretation of Tirathites: when Israel enters distress, they sound an alarm and are answered. Who are the Kenites? The descendants of Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law. Of them it says, ‘Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you shall find it.’ In reward for ‘Call him, and let him eat bread,’ said of Moses, of whom it says, ‘For I drew him from the water,’ Jethro’s descendants merited seats in the Chamber of

: “And it draws near those who are distant—as we learn from Jethro. R. Yohanan said: As a reward for “Call him, and let him eat bread,” his descendants merited sitting in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, as it says, “The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites; these are the Kenites who came from Hammath, ancestor of the house of Rechab.” Elsewhere it says, “The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law, went up from the city of palms with the children of Judah, into the wilderness of Judah in the Negev of Arad, and went and settled with the people.””
: “Moses listened to his father-in-law’s advice and did everything he had said.”

: “Come and see: Jethro advised Moses about arranging judgments, as was needed. His acknowledgment of God and his setting out the order of judgments demonstrate ‘Judgment belongs to God,’ not the Other Side. Judgments were given to Israel, not another: ‘His statutes and judgments to Israel.’ Further, a person should not treat another with contempt; an ordinary person’s word is still a word. For of Moses it says, ‘Moses listened to his father-in-law’s voice.’”
: “Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person, as it says, “From all my teachers I have gained understanding, for Your testimonies occupy my thoughts.””
: “Your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” whether you turn right or turn left.”

: “Even the organs not normally under a person’s control—his eyes and ears—would come under his control, so that he would hear and see only a matter of mitzvah, as the Ran explains. This is “Your eyes shall see your Teacher”: from everything he sees he learns something for Hashem’s service, knowing that it was certainly not shown to him without a purpose, but so that he might learn Hashem’s way. Likewise, from what he hears he learns the paths of divine service: “Your ears shall hear a word behind you: This is the way; walk in it.” He knows that Hashem did not arrange for him to hear this without a purpose; it must teach him His way. Thus, “Who is wise? One who learns from every person”: he learns from everything he hears and sees, even when the other person did not intend to teach him. After circumcision Abraham attained this new creation: his eyes and ears would see and hear only matters of mitzvah, learning Hashem’s way.”
: “You will surely wear yourself out, both you and this people with you, for the task is too heavy for you; you cannot carry it out alone.”
: “Now listen to me; I will advise you, and may God be with you. You shall represent the people before God and bring their matters to God.”
: “Moses listened to his father-in-law’s advice and did everything he had said.”

Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik 231:1: “All elevation and authority come through words of Torah, as it says, ‘Through me kings reign.’ Therefore the appointment of leaders is stated close to the giving of the Torah, in that same parashah. This came through Jethro, because the Israelite soul cannot really tolerate anyone’s elevation over it, even that of someone great in wisdom. Every Jew has a share in Torah, as it says, ‘An inheritance of the congregation of Jacob,’ just as that unlearned man said to Rabbi Yannai in the Midrash Rabbah, Tzav, chapter 9. As is known, each person holds to a letter of the Torah, and a Torah scroll missing one letter is invalid. Consequently, just as this person needs that one, that one needs this person. Although one has a larger portion of Torah, he knows nothing of the smaller person’s particular portion. This explains ‘From my students more than from them all’ in Taanit 7a. A person has only one teacher, as Avodah Zarah 19a says concerning one who learns from one teacher: for the received teaching, one teacher is preferable. Even if he has more teachers, he has more colleagues, and more students than all the others, for their number has no limit. He takes in the words of Torah present in each student that are absent from himself. Because they are so numerous, he therefore learns more from them.”

: “But it is written, “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt offering and sacrifices”! That passage describes events after the giving of the Torah. This is satisfactory according to the view that Jethro came after the giving of the Torah; but according to the view that he came beforehand, what can be said? For the sons of Rabbi Chiya and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi differed: One said that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah, and the other said afterward. The view that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah holds that descendants of Noah offered peace offerings.”
: “Strike a scoffer, and the simple person becomes shrewd; rebuke one who understands, and he will gain knowledge.”

: “Another interpretation: “Jethro heard.” This is what Scripture says: “Strike a scoffer, and the simple will become discerning”; likewise, “When a scoffer is punished, the simple grows wise.” Amalek and Jethro had shared Pharaoh’s counsel. When Jethro saw that the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed Amalek from this world and the world to come, he reconsidered and repented. For above it is written, “I will utterly erase Amalek’s memory,” and afterward, “Jethro heard.” He said: I have nowhere to go but to the God of Israel.”
: “When a scoffer is punished, the simple person becomes wise; when the wise person is instructed, he acquires knowledge.”

: “The tannaim likewise differed: “Jethro, priest of Midian, heard.” What report did he hear that brought him to convert? Rabbi Yehoshua says: He heard of the war with Amalek, for alongside this passage it is written, “Joshua weakened Amalek and his people with the sword.””

: “Go and call out in Jerusalem’s hearing: Thus says Hashem: I remember for you the devotion of your youth, the love of your bridal days, when you followed Me into the wilderness, into an unsown land.”

: “Likewise, when Moses sought provision for Israel’s needs, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “Tell me, you whom my soul loves…” How many women in childbirth are there among them? How many pregnant women? How many nursing women have you provided for the infants? What soothing provisions have you prepared for the pregnant women? The Holy One, blessed be He, answered him: “If you do not know”—if you have not known, you will eventually know. “Go out in the footsteps of the flock”: you shepherd the sheep and the kids—that is, the fathers will die in the wilderness and the children enter the land—but you will not shepherd the children. Rather, “beside the shepherds’ dwellings”: in Sihon’s land, for you will not enter beyond it.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 3:2: “It says, ‘On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai.’ The Pesikta asks why the Torah was given in a wilderness: to teach that unless a person makes himself ownerless like a wilderness, he does not merit words of Torah. Just as the wilderness has no end, so words of Torah have no end, as it says, ‘Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.’ Eruvin 54a expounds ‘From the wilderness, a gift’: if a person makes himself like a wilderness, his learning endures in his possession. Here, however, it says that he merits Torah only by making himself like a wilderness; this is the preparation for receiving the Torah. The Midrash at the beginning of Bamidbar likewise expounds ‘In the wilderness of Sinai,’ at the opening of the Book of Numbers: someone who does not make himself ownerless like a wilderness cannot acquire wisdom. The Pesikta applies this to their coming to the wilderness before the Torah was given. Its principal concern is the Oral Torah, of which it says that it is endless like a wilderness and ‘broader than the sea’; the letters of the Written Torah are counted and numbered. This accords with Tanchuma, Noach 3: the principal coercion of the mountain held over them like a barrel concerned the Oral Torah, which requires toil and hardship and is not found with someone seeking this world’s pleasure. Thus ‘On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai’ means that they relinquished all worldly concerns

: “Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel’s name: If someone rises early to study before reciting Shema, he must recite the Torah blessing. After reciting Shema he need not recite it, for he has already fulfilled that obligation through the blessing Ahavah Rabbah.”

: “An objection is raised: “Would that their heart were always like this”—it was impossible to remove the angel of death from them, for the decree had already been issued. Israel received the Torah only so that no nation or tongue would rule over them, as it says, “So that it may be well with them and their children forever.” Reish Lakish follows the other tanna, for a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose says that Israel received the Torah only so that the angel of death would not rule over them, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings, all of you children of the Most High.” But you ruined your deeds, and therefore, “Yet like Adam you shall die.””
: “I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.””

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth”—would that He fix Torah study in our hearts as before! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it says, “I shall put My Torah within them and write it upon their hearts.” Rabbi Nechemya said: When Israel heard “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us—“You speak with us, and we shall hear”; “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” The evil inclination immediately returned to its place. They returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth!” He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it is written, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.””

: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction: It is written, “I will take My grain in its season,” but also, “You shall gather your grain.” There is no contradiction: one concerns a time when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will; the other, a time when it does not. The Sages taught: What does “You shall gather your grain” teach? Since it says, “This book of Torah shall not leave your mouth,” one might take that literally. “You shall gather your grain” therefore teaches that one should combine Torah with the ordinary conduct of worldly life. This is Rabbi Yishmael’s view. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: If a person plows at plowing time, sows at sowing time, reaps at reaping time, threshes at threshing time, and winnows when the wind blows, what will become of Torah? Rather, when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will, its work is done by others, as it says, “Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks.” When Israel does not fulfill His will, it must do its own work, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Moreover, it does the work of others, as it says, “You shall serve your enemy.” Abaye said: Many followed Rabbi Yishmael’s course and succeeded; they followed Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s course and did not succeed.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: I have never seen a deer drying figs, a lion carrying burdens, or a fox keeping a shop; yet they are sustained without distress. They were created only to serve me, and I was created to serve my Maker. If those created only to serve me are sustained without distress, should I, created to serve my Maker, not be sustained without distress? But I worsened my deeds and damaged my livelihood, as it says, “Your sins have turned these away.””
: “I will give your land’s rain at its proper time, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.”
: “By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground, for from it you were taken. For you are dust, and to dust you will return.”

: “The explanation follows the Gemara: when Israel does not perform the Omnipresent’s will, their work is done by their own hands, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Maharsha asks: the passage begins, “If you diligently listen ... to love Hashem your God,” and then says, “You shall gather your grain.” How can this describe those who do not perform His will? We have explained that the Gemara does not say that they fail to perform His commandments, but His will. Hashem certainly did not command rest on every day, only on Shabbat and in the Sabbatical year, which Israel observes. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says, however, that His will is known: a person should be free for Torah alone, as before the corruption, when no involvement in worldly affairs was necessary. Thus, a Jew should perform that will. The Sages say, “When it says, ‘It shall not depart,’ conclude that he was created for the toil of Torah ... fortunate is one who attains being devoted to Torah.” One must attain this: to be set apart for Torah’s toil alone. Such a person performs the Omnipresent’s will, and his work is done by others. This, however, requires attainment, as in the case of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa.”

: “That passage speaks of those who do not fulfill the Omnipresent’s will, as Berakhot 35 b explains: when they fulfill His will, their labor is performed by others. We explained that His will was that the human being remain occupied only with Torah. After the corruption, however, when 'By the sweat of your brow...' was decreed, God commanded rest only on Shabbat, while the weekdays required occupation with worldly matters. Nevertheless, when they act according to His command, 'I will give rain...' is written: God gives the rain, and evil does not come through His hand.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “Then you will understand the fear of Hashem and find knowledge of God.”

: “R. Shimon ben Lakish said: “Jacob called to his sons and said, Gather together and I will tell you.” Jacob wished to reveal the end of days to his sons, but the Divine Presence withdrew from him. He said, “Perhaps, God forbid, there is an unfit descendant among my children, as Ishmael came from Abraham and Esau from my father Isaac?” His sons said to him, “Hear, Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.” They meant: Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our hearts. At that moment our father Jacob began and said, “Blessed is the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.””
: “You shall say, “It is a Pesach sacrifice to Hashem, who passed over the Israelites’ houses in Egypt when He struck Egypt and saved our houses.” The people bowed down and prostrated themselves.”
: “Hashem will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will return to Hashem, and He will respond to their entreaties and heal them.”

: “Come and see: the lowest of all the levels was struck first. Rabbi Shimon said: God began from the lowest, and His hand struck with every finger. When He reached the highest of all levels, He Himself performed His act, passing through Egypt and killing all. He therefore killed every firstborn in Egypt, for this is the upper level and firstborn of all.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: then, when everything shone together, the sea performed the upper ordinances, and those above and below were entrusted into its hands. Therefore everything is difficult before God like the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as the teachings explain. Why? Because the splitting of the Sea of Reeds depends upon the Ancient One.”

: “'To the wilderness': we already know that they were in the wilderness. Rather, Scripture speaks in Jethro’s praise: he lived amid worldly honor, yet his heart moved him to go out to the wilderness, a desolate place, to hear words of Torah.”

: “Rabbi Eliezer says: The Holy One, blessed be He, told him to go out. “He said to Moses”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: I am the One who spoke and the world came into being, as it says, “God, God, the Lord, spoke and called the earth.” I bring near and I distance, as it says, “Am I a God only from nearby, says the Lord?” I brought Jethro near and did not distance him. This man who came to Me came solely for Heaven’s sake, solely to convert. You too must bring him near; do not distance him. Immediately, “Moses went out to meet his father-in-law.” They said: Moses went out, Aaron, Nadab and Abihu went out, and seventy elders of Israel. Some say the Ark too went out with them. Therefore it says, “The wise inherit honor.””
: “Jethro rejoiced over all the good Hashem had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from Egypt’s hand.”

: ““Jethro rejoiced”—Rav and Samuel explained it differently. Rav said: He passed a sharp sword over his flesh. Samuel said: His whole body became covered with prickles. Rav said: This is the popular saying: In the presence of a convert, do not disparage an Aramean even after ten generations.”

: “The essential vitality of the sons of Heth likewise lies in their name, for “You give life to them all.” When the Torah writes “the sons of Heth” ten times, it indicates that the entire root of their vitality and holiness was drawn out from them. Ten signifies a complete number. This is the meaning of “corresponding to the Ten Commandments,” as we say, “Ten I know: the Ten Commandments.” Wherever the number ten is mentioned, it alludes to them. Thus the Zohar speaks of ten for Creation and ten for the giving of the Torah, and the ten utterances correspond to the ten sefirot—a complete number. Mentioning their name ten times therefore indicates that their vitality and holiness were completely drawn out.”

: “‘If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings.’ Rabbi Shimon said: ‘Ten, ten, each spoon by the sacred shekel.’ What do the two tens indicate? Ten for creation and ten for the giving of Torah: ten sayings in creation and ten sayings at the giving of Torah. What is the meaning? The world was created only for Torah. While Israel labor in Torah, the world endures. When they desist, ‘Were it not for My covenant day and night, I would not have established heaven and earth’s laws.’ Come and see: creation’s ten sayings are as we learned, ‘Through ten sayings the world was created.’ The ten sayings at the giving of Torah are the Ten Commandments: ‘I am the Lord your God.’ In creation it says, ‘Let there be light, and there was light.’ This is faith in God, called light: ‘The Lord is my light and salvation; whom shall I fear?’”

: “'In the beginning God created': this verse calls out for interpretation, as our sages expounded: for the sake of Torah, which is called 'the beginning of His way,' and for the sake of Israel, who are called 'the beginning of His produce.'”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” followed by “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed. For it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Sabbaths,” and afterward, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.””

ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 1:3-4
quote: : “Everyone thus receives an additional nefesh, ruach and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person should direct his intention so that some of this addition remains with him through the weekdays; if he does so properly, his ways will be set right. He is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends on the intention.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “Jethro, priest of Midian and Moses’ father-in-law, heard everything God had done for Moses and for Israel, His people—that Hashem had brought Israel out of Egypt.”
: “But wisdom—from where can it be found? And where is the place of understanding?”

: “‘Wisdom—from where is it found?’ Torah proceeds from Wisdom, the place called Holiness. Wisdom proceeds from the place called Holy of Holies. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Jubilee is likewise called holy, as in ‘It is Jubilee; it shall be holy to you.’ Israel includes these aspects, as it says, ‘You shall be people of holiness to Me.’”

: “Rabbi Abba asked: what is ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Were Israel so foolish that they did not know this? They saw the Shekhinah before them and clouds of glory surrounding them. Those who saw their King’s glorious radiance at the sea—for we learned that a maidservant saw at the sea what Ezekiel did not see—could they be foolish enough to ask, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Rather, Rabbi Shimon explained: they wished to distinguish between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, called Nothingness, and Ze‘ir Anpin, called the Lord. Thus it does not say, ‘Is the Lord among us or not?’ as in ‘Will he follow My Torah or not?’ It says, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’”

: “Come and see: within holiness’s mystery—another reading says the holy Name—there is a king, with a priest serving beneath him, above and below alike. Above is a King, the mystery of the Holy of Holies, the upper King. Beneath Him is a priest, the mystery of primordial light, serving before Him. This is the priest called Great, the right side.”

: “‘A great light’: the light created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, concealed for those who labor in the Oral Torah day and night. Through their merit the world endures, as it says, ‘Thus says the Lord: Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.’ Which covenant applies both by day and by night? The study of Talmud.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”
: “Speak and say: Thus says the Lord Hashem: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great sea-monster lying amid his waterways, who says, “My Nile is mine, and I made myself.””

: “Rabbi Shimon said: now we must reveal secrets bound above and below. Why is it written ‘Come to Pharaoh’? It should say ‘Go to Pharaoh.’ What is ‘come’? God brought Moses through chamber after chamber to a mighty upper serpent, from which many levels unfold. What is it? The secret of the great dragon.”

k: volume-i|1300|0|Arizal/Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 3
quote: : “‘The uppermost serpent’: the marginal gloss identifies it as Arikh of the realm of kelippah.”
: “A poor but wise youth is better than an old, foolish king who no longer knows how to heed a warning.”

: “It was taught: Naaman was a resident alien; Nebuzaradan was a full convert. Haman’s descendants studied Torah in Bnei Brak; Sisera’s descendants taught children in Jerusalem; Sennacherib’s descendants taught Torah publicly. Who were they? Shemayah and Avtalyon.”
: “He saw Amalek and took up his discourse, saying, “Amalek was first among nations, but his end is utter destruction.””
: “She lusted after their lovers, whose members were like those of donkeys and whose emission was like that of horses.”
: “Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the land’s vulnerable places.””
: “Then the raging waters would have swept over our soul.”

: “Rabbi Shimon taught: he is cunning, always cunning, and the evil inclination, which is cunning, dwells there. Thus ‘the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean’ means the cunning bone; ‘from Paddan Aram,’ from a pair of deceivers, for padna denotes a yoke of oxen, a pair. ‘Laban’s sister’ means the sister of the cunning evil inclination. As we learned: at first, when it was filthy with sins in this world, it was called Lot. In the future, when it is no longer filthy as before, like one who bathes and immerses to remove impurity, it is called Laban. The evil inclination is nevertheless not abolished from the world. Hear how we explained in the teaching: Lot’s two daughters are the two bodily powers that stir the evil inclination. Now that it is less filthy and has immersed away its dirt, it is called Laban. Those two daughters are not utterly abolished; thus ‘Laban had two daughters.’”

: “After turning to a bad course, Acher asked Rabbi Meir: What does “God made this opposite that” mean? He answered: Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created has a counterpart: He created mountains and hills, seas and rivers. Acher told him: “Rabbi Akiva your teacher did not explain it that way. Rather, He created the righteous and the wicked, the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom. Every person has two portions, one in the Garden of Eden and one in Gehinnom. If a righteous person merits, he takes his own portion and his fellow’s portion in the Garden of Eden; if a wicked person is found guilty, he takes his own portion and his fellow’s portion in Gehinnom.” Rav Mesharshiya said: What verses support this? Of the righteous, “They shall inherit a double portion in their land”; of the wicked, “Break them with a double breaking.””

: ““And I shall give people in your place”: do not read adam, “people,” but Edom. Likewise, he interprets “nations” as referring to Esau, as in “one nation shall be stronger than the other.” This is spoken of the future. Hashem prepares for every penitent a ransom for his soul from whatever corresponds to him within the impure realm. This is the meaning of the Ari’s explanation of the saying, “He takes his own portion and his fellow’s portion”: it refers to his counterpart, within whom there is a good spark connected with his own soul.”

: “After good and evil became intermingled, although God created a righteous person and a wicked person, each also contains a portion of the opposite. “God made one corresponding to the other”: opposite every righteous person stands a wicked person corresponding to his evil portion. The righteous person must refine himself, separating the evil from himself so that it remains entirely with the wicked person opposite him, while absorbing the good in that wicked person that belongs to him. He thereby becomes wholly complete in holiness: good is separated from evil, and he takes his fellow’s share in the Garden of Eden. The evil goes to destruction, and the wicked person takes his fellow’s share in Gehinnom.”
: ““They despoiled Egypt.” Rabbi Ami said: This teaches that they made it like a trap with no grain remaining in it. Reish Lakish said: They made it like a sea-depth with no fish remaining in it.”
: “Hashem granted the people favor in the Egyptians’ eyes, and they let them have what they requested. Thus they emptied Egypt.”

: “‘David said to the young man who reported to him: Where are you from? He replied: I am the son of an Amalekite convert.’ Rabbi Yitzchak said: He was the son of Doeg the Edomite. ‘David told him: Your blood is upon your head, for your own mouth’ testified against you. The word ‘your blood’ is written in the plural: you shed much blood; you destroyed Nob, the city of priests.”
: “Now go and strike Amalek. Devote everything he has to destruction and do not spare him. Put to death man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.”

: “The house of Jacob will be fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau straw. They will ignite them and consume them; no survivor will remain of the house of Esau, for Hashem has spoken.”

: “According to this, we must understand why it says concerning Haman, 'To the sinner He gave the occupation of gathering and collecting, to give to the good...'—Mordechai. Rather, this follows the statement in Sanhedrin 96 b that descendants of Haman studied Torah in Bnei Brak; Ein Yaakov adds, 'Who was this? Rav Shmuel bar Shilat.' Although converts from Amalek are not accepted, as stated above, it appears that Rav Shmuel bar Shilat descended from one of them who had relations with a Jewish woman, and thus emerged from Haman without Haman’s intention.”

: “After this very pattern and mystery, God acted on earth, breaking the old and foolish king, Pharaoh. When Moses came to Pharaoh and said, ‘The God of the Hebrews has called upon us,’ Pharaoh answered, ‘I do not know the Lord.’ God wished His Name to be honored on earth as above. Once He struck Pharaoh and his people, Pharaoh came and acknowledged God. Afterward that priest of On, Jethro, who served beneath him, was broken and subdued until he came and acknowledged the Holy One, blessed be He, saying, ‘Blessed is the Lord, who rescued you,’ and ‘Now I know that the Lord is great.’ This is the priest of On, the Other Side, the left side. This is also the mystery of Rachel’s words when she saw that she was dying: ‘Ben Oni.’ Therefore Jacob answered with ‘Binyamin,’ son of the right, rather than ‘Ben Oni’: the right side, rather than the left.”

: “Come and see: Jethro advised Moses about arranging judgments, as was needed. His acknowledgment of God and his setting out the order of judgments demonstrate ‘Judgment belongs to God,’ not the Other Side. Judgments were given to Israel, not another: ‘His statutes and judgments to Israel.’ Further, a person should not treat another with contempt; an ordinary person’s word is still a word. For of Moses it says, ‘Moses listened to his father-in-law’s voice.’”

: “Ulla of Bira said in Rabbi Elazar’s name: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle for the righteous. He will sit among them in the Garden of Eden, and each will point with his finger, as it says, “On that day they will say: This is our God, for whom we hoped, that He would save us. This is Hashem, for whom we hoped; let us exult and rejoice in His salvation.””

: “The Torah then presents the judicial laws, although this occurred after Yom Kippur, as Rashi explains from the Sifrei. This too prepares for the giving of the Torah. Appointing officers over thousands, hundreds, and so forth belongs specifically to the Oral Torah, in which there are different levels. When Moses received the Torah, everything was included in the Written Torah. The Sages said that had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah. Only through an abundance of anger did they require the Oral Torah—an abundance of wisdom to repair the abundance of anger. At the giving of the Torah, when Israel heard “I am,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts, as the Midrash says. This resembles the future, when “No one will teach his fellow … for they will all know Me.” The 613 commandments are 613 kinds of counsel, whose purpose is to illuminate “I am” within the heart. When that declaration shone in their hearts at Sinai, and all Torah became fixed there, they did not need to be taught, nor were there ranks of officers over thousands and the like. Similarly, the Talmud says that God will make a circle for the righteous in the future. A circle has neither beginning nor end, signifying the absence of differences in rank, as in “No one will teach.” Only after the corruption, when the abundance of anger needed repair after Yom Kippur, did they require officers over thousands.”

: “Once that king and priest acknowledged God and were broken before Him, God rose in His glory over all, above and below. The Torah was not given until He was exalted through their acknowledgment. Only after Jethro came and declared, ‘Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods,’ and ‘Blessed is the Lord, who rescued you,’ did God rise in His glory above and below. Afterward He gave Torah in completeness, with dominion over everything.”
: “He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel.”
: “Thus says Hashem: Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi says: Great is circumcision, for no one occupied himself with commandments as Abraham did, yet he was not called whole until circumcision, as it says, “Walk before Me and be whole,” followed by, “I will place My covenant between Me and you.” Another interpretation: Great is circumcision, for it is equal to all the commandments of the Torah, as it says, “For according to these words.” Another interpretation: Great is circumcision, for without it heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, “If not for My covenant by day and night.” This disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer, who said: Great is Torah, for without Torah heaven and earth would not endure, as it says, “If not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the ordinances of heaven and earth.””

: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant. It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.”

: “Rava asked Rabbah bar Mari: What is the source of the popular saying, “The wine belongs to its owner, but thanks go to the one who serves it”? He answered: It is written, “You shall lay your hand upon him,” and, “So that the whole congregation of Israel may listen and fear.” Yet it is also written, “Joshua son of Nun was filled with a spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands upon him, and all the children of Israel listened to him.””

: “Someone used to go about saying, “A thief is not killed for two or three thefts.” Samuel said to Rav Judah: A verse states it: “Thus says Hashem: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four I will not reverse it.””
: “Your ears will hear a word behind you, saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” whether you turn right or turn left.”

: “Rabbi Shefatya said in Rabbi Yoḥanan’s name: From where do we know that one may take guidance from an overheard voice? It says, “Your ears will hear a word behind you, saying.” This applies when one hears a man’s voice in town or a woman’s voice in the countryside, and when the voice says “Yes, yes” or “No, no.””

: “Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose went up to visit Rabbi Aha, who was ill. They said: Let us follow the hearing of a heavenly voice. They heard a woman saying to her companion, “The lamp has gone out.” The other woman answered, “May the lamps of Israel neither go out nor be extinguished.””
: “Come and see: all the hidden depths proceeding from Thought and borne by Voice are not revealed until the word reveals them. What is ‘the word’? Speech.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

: “They asked him, “Rabbi, if someone forgot and did not bring a knife before Shabbat, what should he do?” He said, “I learned this law and forgot it. But leave Israel alone: if they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.” The following day, one whose Pesach offering was a lamb tucked the knife into its wool, and one whose offering was a goat tucked it between its horns. He saw what they did, remembered the law, and said, “This is what I received from Shemaiah and Avtalyon.””

: “‘A great light’: the light created on the first day, which the Holy One, blessed be He, concealed for those who labor in the Oral Torah day and night. Through their merit the world endures, as it says, ‘Thus says the Lord: Were it not for My covenant by day and night, I would not have established the laws of heaven and earth.’ Which covenant applies both by day and by night? The study of Talmud.”
: “Light is planted for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Yisrael Kedoshim 10:26: “On “He was wiser than all people,” the Midrash says: even from that fool of Tzippori, for he drew from everyone. Even from a fool one can receive a hint of wisdom. This is the prophecy given to them, as stated in Bava Batra 12b, and a sage such as Mar bar Rav Ashi there can discern such an utterance. For folly, although the opposite of wisdom, also contains a root of wisdom. Without it folly could have no existence, since everything draws its life from wisdom, as it says, “Wisdom gives life.” The deepest wisdom, which cannot be disclosed through human intellect on its own but only through the prophetic spirit, is revealed through fools.”
The printed source gives Bava Batra 12a; the episode Rav Tzadok refers to appears at Bava Batra 12b:3.
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”

: “Rabba bar Rav Huna visited the house of Rabba bar Rav Nahman. They served him three se’a of cakes prepared with rich oil. He asked them: Did you know I was coming? They replied: Are you more important to us than Shabbat?”

: “If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For the designation “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.””
: “He has not done this for any other nation; they have not known His judgments. Hallelujah!”

: “R. Yohanan said: A gentile who engages in Torah incurs the death penalty, as it says, “Moses commanded us the Torah as an inheritance”—an inheritance for us, not for them. Why is this not counted among the seven commandments? According to the reading “inheritance,” he is stealing it; according to the reading “betrothed,” his judgment is like that of violating a betrothed young woman, which is stoning. They raised an objection: R. Meir used to say: From where do we know that even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest? It says, “Which a human being shall perform and live through them.” It does not say “priests, Levites, and Israelites,” but “a human being.” Thus even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest. That statement concerns their own seven commandments.”

: “They raised an objection: R. Meir used to say: From where do we know that even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest? It says, “Which a human being shall perform and live through them.” It does not say “priests, Levites, and Israelites,” but “a human being.” Thus even a gentile who engages in Torah is like a High Priest. That statement concerns their own seven commandments.”

: “Anyone who accepts the seven commandments and takes care to observe them is among the righteous of the nations of the world and has a share in the World to Come. This is provided that he accepts and fulfills them because the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded them in the Torah and informed us through Moses our teacher that the descendants of Noah had previously been commanded concerning them.”

: “The Sages taught: The descendants of Noah were commanded concerning seven commandments: laws of justice, and the prohibitions of blasphemy, idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, bloodshed, theft, and a limb taken from a living animal.”
: “One will say, “I belong to Hashem”; another will call himself by Jacob’s name. Another will write upon his hand, “For Hashem,” and take the name Israel.”
: “Now listen to me; I will advise you, and may God be with you. You shall represent the people before God and bring their matters to God.”
: “Jacob drew near to his father Isaac, who felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are Esau’s hands.””

: “Rabbi Yose understood this verse as referring to the Shekhinah’s descent into Egyptian exile. Rabbi Shimon said it concerns the mystery of faith’s union: ‘With me from Lebanon, bride.’ Voice says to Speech, ‘With me,’ for Voice comes to Speech and leads her with it, uniting without any separation. Voice is general; Speech is particular. The general needs the particular, and the particular needs the general, for there is no Voice without Speech and no Speech without Voice. Hence ‘With me from Lebanon, bride’: the root of both comes from Lebanon.”
: “Moses listened to his father-in-law’s advice and did everything he had said.”

: “'It was on the following day': it was the day after Yom Kippur, as we learned in Sifrei. What does 'on the following day' mean? The day after he descended from the mountain. Necessarily, it can only mean the day after Yom Kippur, because before the giving of the Torah he could not have said, 'I make known God’s statutes...' From the giving of the Torah until Yom Kippur, Moses did not sit to judge the people: on the seventeenth of Tammuz he descended and broke the tablets; early the next morning he ascended, remained for eighty days, and descended on Yom Kippur. This passage is not written in chronological order, for the event 'It was on the following day' did not take place until the second year. Even according to the view that Jethro came before the giving of the Torah, his departure for his own land did not occur until the second year. Here it says, 'Moses sent his father-in-law away,' while, at the departure of the tribal camps, we find Moses saying to him, 'We are journeying to the place...' and 'Please do not leave us.' If this passage were before the giving of the Torah, where do we find that he returned after being sent away? If you say that there it mentions Hobab rather than Jethro, and Hobab was Jethro’s son: Hobab and Jethro are the same person, as it says, 'Of the descendants of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law.'”

: “The Torah then presents the judicial laws, although this occurred after Yom Kippur, as Rashi explains from the Sifrei. This too prepares for the giving of the Torah. Appointing officers over thousands, hundreds, and so forth belongs specifically to the Oral Torah, in which there are different levels. When Moses received the Torah, everything was included in the Written Torah. The Sages said that had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah. Only through an abundance of anger did they require the Oral Torah—an abundance of wisdom to repair the abundance of anger. At the giving of the Torah, when Israel heard “I am,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts, as the Midrash says. This resembles the future, when “No one will teach his fellow … for they will all know Me.” The 613 commandments are 613 kinds of counsel, whose purpose is to illuminate “I am” within the heart. When that declaration shone in their hearts at Sinai, and all Torah became fixed there, they did not need to be taught, nor were there ranks of officers over thousands and the like. Similarly, the Talmud says that God will make a circle for the righteous in the future. A circle has neither beginning nor end, signifying the absence of differences in rank, as in “No one will teach.” Only after the corruption, when the abundance of anger needed repair after Yom Kippur, did they require officers over thousands.”
: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not My ways, declares Hashem.”

: “We have already explained in chapter 2 of the Laws of the Foundations of the Torah that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not know through knowledge external to Himself, as human beings do, where the person and his knowledge are two. Rather, He—may His name be exalted—and His knowledge are one, and the human mind cannot fully apprehend this. Just as a person cannot apprehend and discover the Creator’s true essence, as it says, 'A human being cannot see Me and live,' so a person cannot apprehend and discover the Creator’s knowledge. This is what the prophet said: 'My thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not My ways.' Consequently, we cannot know how the Holy One, blessed be He, knows all creatures and actions. Yet we know without doubt that a person’s actions are in his own hands: God neither draws him toward them nor decrees that he act in a particular way. This is known not only through accepting the religion, but also through clear rational proofs. Accordingly, prophecy states that a person is judged for his actions according to what he has done, good or bad. This is the principle upon which all the words of prophecy depend.”

It would have been better to leave it in the innocent simplicity of the innocent, rather than awaken their hearts and leave their minds in doubt, lest at some moment a troubling thought about this enter their hearts.”

: “We already explained that Rambam’s statement that this is the prophet’s 'My thoughts are not your thoughts' also intends what Zohar Chadash says: where knowledge exists, there is no choice at all, while God created a place where choice is entrusted to the person. In the future God will clarify this through all Israel’s repentance from love, turning deliberate sins into merits. This is 'If your sins are like the years ordered from the six days of creation until now.' In the utterance Bereshit, 'formless and void' alludes to the wicked’s deeds. k: volume-i|1344|1|Arizal, Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef, teachin
quote: : “We have already said that Rambam’s words are explained at the end of Zohar Chadash, and by the holy Ari in Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef: God sees the act of choice itself, although human understanding finds this contradictory. Where there is divine knowledge, there is indeed no choice; but in this world, the place of choice, God does not govern according to that knowledge—that belongs to the future. Thus, ‘My thoughts are not your thoughts,’ as Rambam writes.”

: “The essence of repentance is that God illuminates a person’s eyes until deliberate sins become merits. This means recognizing and understanding that everything he sinned was also within God’s will, as the sages taught concerning the three verses: 'You turned their hearts,' 'Whom I harmed,' and so forth. This follows the meaning of knowledge and choice, which the Ari explained at the end of Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef: both are true, each in its own place. Where choice exists, there is no place for knowledge; where knowledge exists, there is truly no place for choice.”

: “‘Joseph was brought down to Egypt.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘Come, see the works of God, awesome in His dealings with human beings.’ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Even the awesome events You bring upon us, You bring through a pretext. Consider: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created the angel of death on the first day. From where do we know this? Rabbi Berekhya said: ‘Darkness was over the face of the deep’—this is the angel of death, who darkens people’s faces. Adam was created on the sixth day, yet the blame was attached to him, as though he had brought death into the world: ‘On the day you eat from it, you shall surely die.’ To what is this comparable? To a man who wishes to divorce his wife. Before going home he writes a bill of divorce, then enters his house holding it and looks for a pretext to give it to her. He tells her, ‘Mix me a cup to drink.’ She does so. When he takes the cup from her, he says, ‘Here is your bill of divorce.’ She asks, ‘What was my offense?’ He replies, ‘Leave my house: you mixed me a lukewarm cup!’ She says, ‘You already knew that I would mix a lukewarm cup, since you wrote the bill of divorce and brought it with you!’ So Adam said before the Holy One: ‘Master of the world, two thousand years before You created Your world, the Torah was with You as a craftsman, as it says, “I was beside Him as a craftsman, a delight day by day”—two thousand years. It already contained, “This is the Torah: when a person dies in a tent.”
: “Come and see God’s deeds; His acts toward humankind inspire awe.”
: “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.”

: “Rabbi Avin the Levite said: Whoever enjoys a meal at which a Torah scholar is present is as though he enjoys the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it says, “Aaron and all Israel’s elders came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.” Did they eat before God? Did they not eat before Moses? Rather, it teaches that enjoying a meal in a Torah scholar’s presence is like enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence.”

: “Rabbi Avin the Levite said: Whoever enjoys a meal at which a Torah scholar is present is as though he enjoys the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it says, “Aaron and all Israel’s elders came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.” Did they eat before God? Did they not eat before Moses? Rather, it teaches that enjoying a meal in a Torah scholar’s presence is like enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence.”

: ““I did not enjoy even with my little finger”: A Midrash says that before a person prays for Torah to enter his body, he should pray that delicacies not enter his body, and it cites this account of Rabbi.”

: “Although Rabbi Akiva said, “Make your Shabbat like a weekday rather than depend on others,” nevertheless a person should take a little meat and a little wine, without excessive meat and wine. If he indulges excessively, Scripture testifies against him: “Do not be among wine-drinkers, among those who gorge on meat, for the drunkard and glutton will become poor.” If a person has not merited to ask for mercy that words of Torah enter his inward parts, he should at least ask for mercy that excessive food and drink not enter them, as it says, “I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.” Just as a furnace burns and consumes all the wood in the world you put into it, so a human throat swallows and consumes all the fine foods in the world you put into it.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”
: “On the following day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.”

: “'It was on the following day': it was the day after Yom Kippur, as we learned in Sifrei. What does 'on the following day' mean? The day after he descended from the mountain. Necessarily, it can only mean the day after Yom Kippur, because before the giving of the Torah he could not have said, 'I make known God’s statutes...' Here it says, 'Moses sent his father-in-law away,' while, at the departure of the tribal camps, we find Moses saying to him, 'We are journeying to the place...' and 'Please do not leave us.' If this passage were before the giving of the Torah, where do we find that he returned after being sent away? If you say that there it mentions Hobab rather than Jethro, and Hobab was Jethro’s son: Hobab and Jethro are the same person, as it says, 'Of the descendants of Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law.'”

: ““On the following day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.” “On the following day”—the day after Yom Kippur. “Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning until evening.” Moses judged Israel. Yet judges judge only until mealtime! What, then, does “from morning until evening” teach? Whoever renders a judgment in complete truth is as though he were a partner in creation. Here it says, “From morning until evening,” and there it says, “There was evening and there was morning, one day.””

: “On the Other Side, which is not holiness, there is a mystery called king, which we explained as ‘an old and foolish king.’ Beneath him is the priest of On. This is the secret of ‘Ephraim said, I have become rich; I have found on, power, for myself.’ This power ruled over Jeroboam’s deed; without finding this power, he could not have succeeded in that deed.”

: “After Pharaoh, the head of the unholy power, the “old and foolish king,” was broken, Jethro—the priest of falsehood serving beneath him—was subdued, until he came and acknowledged God. Jethro corresponded to the holy priest, the aspect of wisdom; on the opposing side he was a priest of falsehood. This aspect can be brought into holiness. Jethro therefore converted and was named Yitro because he added a passage to the Torah, which is an aspect of wisdom. Although the Zohar calls it “a common person’s word,” this means that Jethro did not comprehend the root of Torah as it will be in the future. The Sages said that God will make a circle for the righteous, indicating equality of rank, like a circle with neither beginning nor end. Had Israel remained at the level attained through the first tablets, there would have been no differences in rank; they would have attained the future state. Indeed, “You shall discern” was said after Yom Kippur, after the second tablets were given. In this world, however, after the corruption, there are differing ranks: officers over thousands, hundreds, and so forth. This is what Jethro added to the Torah. Jethro’s story precedes the giving of the Torah because it prepared for it. As the Zohar says, the Torah was not given until Jethro came and acknowledged God. This follows the opinion that Jethro came before the Torah was given, as the Zohar’s marginal gloss also states.”

: “Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Simai’s name: Three took part in that counsel: Balaam, Job, and Jethro. Balaam, who advised it, was killed. Job, who remained silent, was judged through suffering. Jethro, who fled, merited descendants who sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, as it says, “The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez … these are the Kenites who came from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab,” and, “The descendants of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law.””

: “Jethro was one of Pharaoh’s wise men. Pharaoh had three wise men: Jethro, Job and Balaam. Jethro knew the fitting worship and service of every object of worship, appointed power, heavenly minister and star exercising dominion. Balaam was a sorcerer versed in every kind of sorcery, whether by action or speech. Job possessed fear, and fear was his essential quality. For in any upper matter, whether of holiness or of the Other Side, a person cannot draw a spirit from above down below and approach it except through fear. He must direct his heart and will with fear and a broken heart; then he can draw down the upper spirit and the needed favor.”
: “I will also judge the nation they serve; afterward they will go out with great possessions.”
: ““They despoiled Egypt.” Rabbi Ami said: This teaches that they made it like a trap with no grain remaining in it. Reish Lakish said: They made it like a sea-depth with no fish remaining in it.”
: “Hashem granted the people favor in the Egyptians’ eyes, and they let them have what they requested. Thus they emptied Egypt.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: now we must reveal secrets bound above and below. Why is it written ‘Come to Pharaoh’? It should say ‘Go to Pharaoh.’ What is ‘come’? God brought Moses through chamber after chamber to a mighty upper serpent, from which many levels unfold. What is it? The secret of the great dragon.”
: “Who wrote them? Moses wrote his own book, the account of Balaam, and Job.”
: “Remember the Torah of Moses My servant, whom I commanded at Horeb concerning all Israel—statutes and laws.”

: “Rabbi Eleazar began: ‘The ark rested in the seventh month…upon the mountains of Ararat.’ How precious are the words of Torah! Every word contains upper secrets, and the entire Torah is called supernal. We learned among its thirteen interpretive principles: anything included in a general rule that is singled out to teach does not teach about itself alone, but about the whole general rule. The Torah is a supernal whole. Even when an ordinary narrative emerges from it, it certainly does not come merely to display that story, but supernal matters and secrets. It does not teach about itself alone, but the entire whole. A narrative or deed in Torah, although singled out from the Torah’s whole, emerges to reveal not merely itself but the supernal entirety of Torah.”
: “Moses told his father-in-law everything Hashem had done to Pharaoh and Egypt on Israel’s account, all the hardship that had befallen them on the road, and how Hashem had rescued them.”
: “Now I know that Hashem is greater than all gods, for in the very thing through which they acted arrogantly against them, He prevailed.”

k: volume-i|1364|1|Mikdash Melekh, teaching quoted by R. Tz
quote: : “As Mikdash Melekh explained regarding ‘Moses recounted to his father-in-law’: previously, ‘Jethro heard’ was merely a report that did not penetrate his heart. Once Moses recounted it to him, it became Torah and affected his heart, so that he said, ‘Now I know’—specifically, now.”
: “Hashem placed a word in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak.””

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Balaam: ‘Wicked man! Do you imagine that blessing for My children—or its opposite—will come about and endure through you? They have no need of you, as people say to the hornet. Return to Balak. When you open your mouth, it will not be under your control, nor will speech depend upon your mouth. Rather, “Thus—koh—you shall speak.” Koh stands ready to bless them; Koh will speak My children’s blessing. When you open your mouth, she will speak the words that will endure for My children, for I will not leave the words to you.’”

: “‘No prophet ever again arose in Israel like Moses’: in Israel none arose, but among the nations one did. This was so that the nations could not claim, ‘Had we possessed a prophet like Moses, we would have served the Holy One, blessed be He.’ Which prophet did they possess who was like Moses? Balaam son of Beor.”
: “No prophet has since arisen in Israel like Moses, whom Hashem knew face to face.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: Eleazar, all the words of wicked Balaam are powerful. The companions have explained ‘No prophet arose again in Israel like Moses’: in Israel none arose, but among the nations one did—Balaam. We have explained the matter: Moses had no equal among the upper crowns; Balaam had no equal among the lower crowns. One belonged to the side of holiness, the other to the side of the left.”

: “‘Thus—koh—you shall bless the children of Israel; say to them.’ ‘Thus shall you bless’—in the holy tongue, in fear, in humility. Rabbi Abba said: we learned that this Tzedek, Righteousness, is called Koh, for all judgments awaken from Koh. Hence Rabbi Eleazar’s explanation of ‘a great blow’: a blow from Koh. Likewise, ‘You have not listened until koh,’ as Moses warned, and ‘Through this—zot—you shall know that I am the Lord.’ All is one. ‘He did not take even this—zot—to heart’: she stood ready to devastate his land.”
: ““He placed a word in Balaam’s mouth.” R. Elazar says: An angel. R. Yonatan says: A hook.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 2:2: “This explains God’s earlier statement to Balaam, ‘Only the word that I speak to you shall you do.’ Why ‘do’? It should have said ‘speak.’ Previously, ‘to do anything small or great’ appropriately used the language of doing; here, however, the matter is only speech. According to what we have explained, Balaam himself would not speak; the Divine Presence would speak, while he would only make the movements of the organs of speech. This accords with Bava Metzia 90b: moving one’s mouth constitutes an action. Afterward, when the angel tells Balaam, ‘The word that I speak to you, that shall you speak,’ it again uses ‘that,’ indicating something as immediate as ‘this’: precisely that word which God places in his mouth, without any alteration. Balaam’s first statement to Balak likewise was ‘That shall I speak,’ without any alteration. Later, when he saw more clearly that his speech was not within his power, he said, ‘That shall I be careful to speak’: he was only a guardian of the words God would place in his mouth. Then, when ‘He placed a word in his mouth,’ and the Midrash Rabbah says that the Holy One forcibly opened his mouth, he saw that even remaining silent was beyond his power. He therefore said, ‘Everything that God speaks, that shall I do.’ He merely performed the action of moving his mouth, which constitutes an action.”
: “Who can count Jacob’s dust or number even a quarter of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.”

: “There is no doubt that if Balaam’s words were not fulfilled, they would not have been spoken prophetically or written in the Torah—such as ‘Let my soul die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.’ This is understood through what I have explained: Moses killed the Egyptian, in whom Cain’s evil soul had reincarnated, but who also contained good sparks. Moses, who was Abel his brother, wished to repair him through reincarnation and killed him with the explicit forty-two-letter Name to raise his soul to holiness. Balaam, however, had utterly defiled himself through divination, sorcery, seminal emission and intercourse with his donkey, as the Zohar describes. Phinehas, who came from Cain’s root, therefore did not wish to kill him with the explicit Name, but with his impure sword, engraved with an idolatrous serpent, as the Zohar explains ‘Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, they killed by the sword.’ His body thus died through impurity. His soul, however, was subsequently reincarnated through that impure sword among Israel, who are called upright, and was then repaired. This is ‘Let my soul die the death of the upright’: the good sparks mingled in his soul would reincarnate among Israel and then die the death of the upright, unlike his body.”

: “All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever—the shoot of My planting, My handiwork, through which I display My glory.” These have no share in the World to Come: one who says that resurrection of the dead is not taught in the Torah, one who says that the Torah is not from heaven, and a heretic. … Three kings and four ordinary people have no share in the World to Come. The three kings are Jeroboam, Ahab, and Manasseh. R. Judah says: Manasseh does have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “He prayed to Him, and He heard his supplication and returned him to Jerusalem, to his kingship.” They said to him: He returned him to his kingship, but did not return him to the life of the World to Come. The four ordinary people are Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel, and Gehazi.”

: “Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He bent with all his strength, and the house fell upon the rulers and all the people within it. Those he killed at his death were more numerous than those he killed during his life.”

: “Some say Samson has no portion in that world. Why? Because he said, ‘Let my soul die with the Philistines,’ surrendering his portion into theirs, so that his soul would die with them in that world. Thus they would proclaim concerning the nazirite: ‘Go away, go away, nazirite! Go around, go around; do not approach the vineyard.’ The companions have explained this.”
