quote: : “Anyone for whom the rule is 'transgress rather than be killed,' but who is killed instead of transgressing, is responsible for his own life. Anyone for whom the rule is 'be killed rather than transgress,' and who is killed instead of transgressing, has sanctified the Name. If this occurs before ten Jews, he has sanctified the Name publicly, like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah, Rabbi Akiva, and his companions. These are the martyrs killed by the government, whose exalted rank is unsurpassed. Of them it says, 'For Your sake we are killed all day; we are considered sheep for slaughter.' Of them it also says, 'Gather to Me My faithful ones, who covenant with Me through sacrifice.'”

: “According to Torah law, Abraham was not required to surrender himself to be thrown into the furnace: a Noahide is not commanded in sanctifying the Name, while he is commanded and warned against destroying himself—“Your blood, for your lives, I shall require.” According to Rambam, someone whose rule is “transgress rather than be killed,” but who is killed instead of transgressing, incurs liability for his own life. Abraham, however, perceived that the needs of that hour called for strengthening the boundary and sanctifying Heaven’s Name. He surrendered himself to the furnace so that the glory of His kingship would become known. This belongs to the root of the Oral Torah. Tosafot explains that even without a prophet, a Torah rule may be set aside temporarily to strengthen the boundary. Elijah’s established prophetic standing was needed so that people would rely on his promise that fire would descend, thereby strengthening the boundary and sanctifying the Holy One’s Name. Abraham likewise perceived the need of the hour to sanctify Heaven’s Name. That is why this trial appears in the Written Torah only by allusion.”

: “According to Abraham’s attribute of love, he should have disobeyed God and not bound Isaac, so that God’s divinity would become public through Isaac. This resembles his giving himself over to the fiery furnace, although it was contrary to the law and he was not permitted to do so, as explained in Noach 9. Out of love, however, he wished to sanctify the Name even if, God forbid, he thereby lost his share in the World to Come. Similarly, in the trial of the binding, he should have refused to obey so that Isaac would remain alive and God’s divinity would become known through him. But his extraordinary fear made him afraid to disobey God, suspecting that perhaps some personal interest—his love of his son—was involved.”

: “Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He bent with all his strength, and the house fell upon the rulers and all the people within it. Those he killed at his death were more numerous than those he killed during his life.”

: “All Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever—the shoot of My planting, My handiwork, through which I display My glory.” These have no share in the World to Come: one who says that resurrection of the dead is not taught in the Torah, one who says that the Torah is not from heaven, and a heretic. … Three kings and four ordinary people have no share in the World to Come. The three kings are Jeroboam, Ahab, and Manasseh. R. Judah says: Manasseh does have a share in the World to Come, as it says, “He prayed to Him, and He heard his supplication and returned him to Jerusalem, to his kingship.” They said to him: He returned him to his kingship, but did not return him to the life of the World to Come. The four ordinary people are Balaam, Doeg, Ahithophel, and Gehazi.”

: “Who listed them? Rav Ashi said: The Men of the Great Assembly listed them. Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: They wished to include one more. The likeness of his father came and prostrated itself before them, but they paid it no heed. Fire came from heaven and licked their benches, but they paid it no heed. A heavenly voice proclaimed: “Have you seen a man diligent in his work? He will stand before kings, not before obscure men.” He put My house before his own; moreover, he built My house in seven years, but his own in thirteen. “He will stand before kings, not before obscure men.” They paid it no heed. A heavenly voice proclaimed: “Should He repay on your terms because you reject His judgment, because you must choose and not I?””
: “Should He repay on your terms because you reject His judgment? You must choose, not I; speak, then, what you know.”

: “Who listed them? Rav Ashi said: The Men of the Great Assembly listed them. Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: They wished to include one more. The likeness of his father came and prostrated itself before them, but they paid it no heed. Fire came from heaven and licked their benches, but they paid it no heed. A heavenly voice proclaimed: “Have you seen a man diligent in his work? He will stand before kings, not before obscure men.” He put My house before his own; moreover, he built My house in seven years, but his own in thirteen. “He will stand before kings, not before obscure men.” They paid it no heed. A heavenly voice proclaimed: “Should He repay on your terms because you reject His judgment, because you must choose and not I?””

: “An objection is raised: There was a pious man among the nations named Job, who came into the world only to receive his reward. The Holy One, blessed be He, brought suffering upon him, and he began to revile and blaspheme. The Holy One, blessed be He, doubled his reward in this world in order to exclude him from the World to Come. The answer is that the tannaim disagree about Job.”

: “Come and see: Jethro advised Moses about arranging judgments, as was needed. His acknowledgment of God and his setting out the order of judgments demonstrate ‘Judgment belongs to God,’ not the Other Side. Judgments were given to Israel, not another: ‘His statutes and judgments to Israel.’ Further, a person should not treat another with contempt; an ordinary person’s word is still a word. For of Moses it says, ‘Moses listened to his father-in-law’s voice.’”
: “You will surely wear yourself out, both you and this people with you, for the task is too heavy for you; you cannot carry it out alone.”

: “Appointing officers over thousands, hundreds, and so forth belongs specifically to the Oral Torah, in which there are different levels. When Moses received the Torah, everything was included in the Written Torah. The Sages said that had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah. Only through an abundance of anger did they require the Oral Torah—an abundance of wisdom to repair the abundance of anger.”
: “'Wisdom': what a person hears from others and learns. 'Understanding': discerning something in one’s own heart from things one has learned. 'Knowledge': the holy spirit.”

: “Her face shines with upper illumination, and she is crowned below among the holy people, all of whom are crowned with new souls. Then prayer begins: to bless her joyfully, with a shining face, saying, ‘Bless et the Lord who is blessed.’ Et is precise, opening toward her through blessing.”

: “On this day she is crowned with seventy crowns. The upper holy Name is completed on every side, all levels are illuminated, and everything rejoices in blessings, holiness upon holiness, and additional holiness.”
: “When the Most High allotted nations their inheritance, when He separated humankind, He established the boundaries of peoples according to the number of Israel’s children.”

quote: : “Also intend the following, as already explained regarding ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion.’ When Moses ascended the mountain to receive the Torah, he was given a thousand portions of light, represented by the large alef of ‘Adam, Seth, Enosh.’ When Israel made the calf, these were lost through Israel’s sin. quote: : “‘Fifty crowns less one’: the marginal gloss explains why the Torah is sometimes said to have seventy facets and sometimes forty-nine facets of purity: both are present. Twice forty-nine is ninety-eight, which is twenty-six plus seventy-two. The explanation is that the seventy branches are actually seventy-two, since the two scribes are not counted, as is known. : “‘I am’ and ‘You shall have no other’ are spoken within Torah’s mystery: these are ‘remember’ and ‘guard.’ ‘I am’ is a concealed and hidden mystery, encompassing all the upper world’s levels as one. Once ‘I am’ was spoken, everything joined together in a single mystery.”

: “R. Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “A human being is born to toil.” I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or for manual labor. When it says, “For his mouth compels him,” you must conclude that he was created for toil of the mouth. But I still do not know whether this means toil in Torah or toil in conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must conclude that he was created for toil in Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies must labor; fortunate is the one who merits laboring in Torah.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 99b:2:1: ““Burdened with toil”—that is, all bodies were created for labor.”

: “Rabbi Levi said: If Israel properly observes Shabbat for even one day, the son of David will come. Why? Because it equals all the commandments. Thus it says, “For He is our God, and we are the people He shepherds, the flock of His hand—today, if you heed His voice.” Rabbi Yochanan said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Although I have set a fixed time for the end, which will arrive in its appointed season whether they repent or not, if they repent for even one day, I will bring it before its appointed season. Thus: “Today, if you heed His voice.” Just as we find that the son of David comes through all the commandments, so he comes through observing one Shabbat, because Shabbat equals all the commandments.”

: “Therefore Shabbat is equal to Torah, and whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah. Thus ‘Happy is the person who does this, and the human being who holds fast to it: guarding Shabbat from profaning it, and guarding his hand from doing any evil.’ It follows that one who guards Shabbat is like one who guards the entire Torah.”

: “This is what the teaching means: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it over wine as it enters. This establishes the obligation at night; from where do we derive it by day? Scripture says, “Remember the Shabbat day.””

: ““To sanctify it”—with what do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. Rabbi Chanan said: From here we learn that a person should have two garments, one for weekdays and one for Shabbat. When he taught this in Tiberias, they said: Our weekday clothing is also our Shabbat clothing. He told them: You must make a change, as it says, “Wash, anoint yourself, and put on your clothes.” Was she naked? Rather, she told her: Put on your Shabbat clothes.”

: ““It is good to give thanks to the Lord.” Adam said: Let all generations learn from me that whoever confesses his transgressions and abandons them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, “It is good to give thanks to the Lord.””
: “One who conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but one who acknowledges and abandons them will receive compassion.”
: “It is good to give thanks to Hashem and sing praise to Your name, Most High.”

: “‘Remember’ is the masculine mystery, the male receiving all the upper world’s limbs. ‘Et Shabbat’s day’: et includes Shabbat eve, the night. ‘To sanctify it’: sanctification is needed from the holy people, to be crowned with them properly.”
: “All the Torah’s commandments have two forms that are one: ‘remember’ and ‘guard.’ ‘Remember’ pertains to the male, and ‘guard’ to the female. All belong to a single whole.”

: “If you say ‘remember’ needs no sanctification because all the world’s sanctifications issue from it, that is not so. This one must be sanctified by day and that one by night. Afterward Israel receive all those sanctifications and are sanctified with God’s sanctity.”

: “This is what the teaching means: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it over wine as it enters. This establishes the obligation at night; from where do we derive it by day? Scripture says, “Remember the Shabbat day.””

: “From here you have learned that the holiness of the Holy One, blessed be He, the holiness of Shabbat, and the holiness of Israel are all valued as one. Concerning the holiness of the Holy One, blessed be He, what is written? “You are holy, enthroned upon Israel’s praises; in You our ancestors trusted…” Concerning Shabbat’s holiness: “You shall observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you.” Concerning Israel’s holiness: “Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of His produce.””
: “Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”
: “Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His harvest. All who consume him incur guilt; calamity will come upon them, declares Hashem.”
: “Yet You are holy, enthroned upon Israel’s praises.”
: “Likewise: “You shall be holy.” Could you be like Me? Scripture says, “For I am holy”—My holiness is above your holiness.”
: “Speak to the entire congregation of the Israelites and say to them: You shall be holy, for I, Hashem your God, am holy.”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”
: “For you are a people holy to Hashem your God. Hashem your God chose you to be His treasured people from all the peoples upon the earth.”
: “Your throne has been established from of old; You are from eternity.”

: ““Then Moses sang.” This is what Scripture says: “Your throne was established from then.” Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Abbahu’s name: Although You have existed forever, Your throne was not settled, and You were not known in Your world, until Your children sang. Therefore it says, “Your throne was established from then.” It is like a king who fought a war and won, and they made him Augustus. They told him: Before this war you were king; now we have made you Augustus. What honor distinguishes a king from Augustus? The king stands upon the platform, whereas Augustus sits. So Israel said: Truly, before You created Your world, You existed; since creating it, You remain the same. Yet, as it were, You stood, as it says, “He stood and measured the earth.” But when You stood at the sea and we sang before You with “then,” Your kingship became settled and Your throne established. Thus, “Your throne was established from then”—through “Then Moses sang.””

: “After gathering these Names—another reading says striking them—seventy branches emerge from them in every direction. All unite into a single chariot and throne for the upper pearl, which rules with its crowns: the King upon His throne on this day, gladdening everything. Once all rejoices, the King sits upon the throne, and the throne rises through seventy branches, as we said.”

: “Rather, this is what was taught: all the miracles and mighty acts performed for Israel, when the light of the Holy Ancient shone in His crowns, are carved and inscribed in az, in its alef. The alef pierces darkness and shines in every direction. When the light of alef joins and reaches zayin—what is zayin? ‘The Lord has a sword filled with blood’—He then performs miracles and mighty acts, because alef has joined with zayin. This is song, song from every side; this is ‘Then Moses will sing.’”
: “Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His harvest. All who consume him incur guilt; calamity will come upon them, declares Hashem.”

: “Come and see: when nourishment is found below, nourishment is found above. A king prepared his own meal but not his servants’. Once he prepared theirs, he ate his meal and they theirs. ‘I ate my honeycomb with my honey’ is the King’s meal; ‘Eat, friends, drink and become intoxicated, beloved ones’ is their meal, from the fragrance of the offering when it ascends. Hence ‘a pleasing fragrance to the Lord’: fragrance for His servants, contentment for the Lord, from the place of the Ancient One’s delight. The King’s meal therefore waits for His servants’ meal. Thus we learned that Israel sustain their Father in heaven. Who eats of the King’s meal? The righteous ones’ souls.”

: ““Michael, the great prince, stands and offers a sacrifice upon it.” The Midrashim differ: One says that he offers the souls of the righteous; another says lambs of fire. This is what we say in the service blessing of the Amidah: “The fire-offerings of Israel and their prayer, swiftly accept with love and favor.” Some say that “the fire-offerings of Israel” belongs with the preceding phrase, “Restore the service to the inner chamber of Your house.” I have found no more.”

: ““This is forever incumbent upon Israel.” Rav Giddel said in Rav’s name: This refers to an altar already built, at which Michael, the great prince, stands and offers a sacrifice. Rabbi Yochanan said: It refers to Torah scholars engaged in studying the laws of the Temple service; Scripture credits them as though the Temple had been built in their days.”

: “At that time He immediately planted Israel in the holy Garden of Eden, as it says, ‘The Lord God planted’—Father and Mother. ‘Garden’ is the lower Shekhinah; ‘Eden’ is the upper Mother. ‘The man’ is the middle pillar. She will be his planting, his mate, never departing from him, and will be his delight. At that time the Holy One, blessed be He, planted Israel as a holy planting in the world, as it says, ‘The branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which to glory.’”

: “If you say ‘remember’ needs no sanctification because all the world’s sanctifications issue from it, that is not so. This one must be sanctified by day and that one by night. Afterward Israel receive all those sanctifications and are sanctified with God’s sanctity.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Shekalim 7:2: “Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 10, section 11, says: it does not say ‘When you raise the children of Israel,’ but ‘the head’; Israel’s head is none other than the Holy One, as it says, ‘Their king passed before them, and God at their head.’ This is understood through Vayikra Rabbah, at the end of chapter 24: ‘You shall be holy’—could you be like Me? Scripture says, ‘For I am holy’: My holiness is above your holiness. The holy books explain that God’s holiness above comes, so to speak, from your holiness, from Israel’s holiness. Yet the Midrash also says, ‘You shall be holy’ means ‘You shall separate yourselves’: as I am separate, so shall you be separate. A Jew must be holy, separate from all this world’s concerns, ‘like Me.’ However, whenever a person sanctifies himself below, he is sanctified above; he sanctifies himself a little and is sanctified greatly, as Yoma 39a says. The more he sanctifies himself, the more he perceives of God’s holiness, which is above his present level. This is ‘My holiness is above your holiness’: each time, My holiness is higher, for greater sanctification below brings sanctification above and a perception that God’s holiness is higher still. This also accords with the other explanation: the relevant holiness of God is what a person perceives of it. God in Himself cannot be described as holy, for no thought grasps Him at all, as explained in Yitro VII. Thus, when one raises Israel’s head, one thereby raises
: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.”

: “Another interpretation: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” With what do you sanctify it? With Scripture and Mishnah, food, drink, clean clothing, and rest. Whoever delights in Shabbat is as though he honors the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Call Shabbat a delight, the Lord’s holy day honored.” This teaches: If you call Shabbat a delight, then the holy Lord is honored.”

: “Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: It is written, ‘Sanctify My Sabbaths.’ How do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. What follows? ‘They shall be a sign between Me and you, so that you know that I am the Lord your God.’ ‘I am the Lord’ means: I am faithful to pay you your reward. Thus, ‘He is entirely delightful.’”

: “Do you suppose that I gave you Shabbat to your detriment? I gave it to you only for your good. How so? Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said: You sanctify Shabbat with food, drink, and clean clothing, delighting yourself, and I give you a reward. From where do we know this? ‘You shall call Shabbat a delight.’ What follows? ‘Then you shall delight in the Lord,’ and ‘He shall grant you your heart’s requests.’”

: ““To sanctify it”—with what do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. Rabbi Chanan said: From here we learn that a person should have two garments, one for weekdays and one for Shabbat. When he taught this in Tiberias, they said: Our weekday clothing is also our Shabbat clothing. He told them: You must make a change, as it says, “Wash, anoint yourself, and put on your clothes.” Was she naked? Rather, she told her: Put on your Shabbat clothes.”

: “If you restrain your foot because of Shabbat, from pursuing your affairs on My holy day, and call Shabbat a delight and Hashem’s holy day honored; if you honor it by refraining from your usual ways, pursuing your affairs, and speaking of business—”

: ““Honor it by refraining from your usual ways.” “Honor it” means that your Shabbat clothing should differ from your weekday clothing, as Rabbi Yohanan called his garments “those that honor me.” “From your usual ways” means that your manner of walking on Shabbat should differ from your weekday manner. “From seeking your affairs” means that your own affairs are forbidden, while the affairs of Heaven are permitted.”
: “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it separates into four headwaters.”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry is described by ‘A river goes out from Eden’—vav—‘to water the garden.’ The river is the middle pillar; ‘goes out from Eden’ means from the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ means the lower Shekhinah.”

quote: : “Although the Arizal wrote that eating on Shabbat is holy even when done for bodily pleasure, this means that it does not bring the evil inclination’s domination and accusation as weekday eating for bodily pleasure does. The subsequent instruction in Tanna DeVei Eliyahu not to overindulge in meat and wine has been interpreted as referring to Shabbat, but such language does not seem appropriate to Shabbat eating, which, as the Arizal wrote, is always holy. Nevertheless, the Sages’ praise of one who delights Shabbat applies only when the intention is for Heaven.”

: “Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Yose’s name: Whoever makes Shabbat a delight is given an inheritance without boundaries, as it says, “Then you shall delight in the Lord; I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth, and I will feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father.” It is not like Abraham’s inheritance, of which it says, “Arise, walk through the land, through its length”; nor like Isaac’s, of which it says, “To you and your descendants I will give all these lands.” Rather, it is like Jacob’s, of which it says, “You shall spread out westward, eastward, northward, and southward.””

: “There is another secret within this mystery. On this day the spirit benefits from Israel’s pleasures and delight. Therefore one must give it delight through food and drink three times, at the three meals corresponding to faith’s three levels, as explained. This spirit receives joy and delight through Israel’s meals. Happy is the portion of one who gives it enjoyment and delight on this day.”

: “Therefore ‘Between Me and the children of Israel’ is written. Because all faith is found within Shabbat, a person is given another soul: an upper soul containing every perfection, an image of the world to come. Hence it is called Shabbat. What is Shabbat? God’s Name, the Name complete on every side.”
: “My God, I desire to do Your will; Your Torah is within my innermost being.”
: “Come, eat of my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.”

: “Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master and the Matron with every kind of delight, fulfilling ‘This is the table before the Lord.’ Until now all delight in the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread’: the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, the varied flavors of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””

: “Shabbat encompasses all ten attributes. Its three meals express the mystery of oneg: Eden, River and Garden. Eden includes the three upper sefirot. Tikkunei Zohar identifies Eden as the supreme Keter; elsewhere the Zohar calls it the higher Chokhmah, and in Bereishit it identifies “flowing from Eden” with the higher Mother. This explains the teaching that the Divine Presence is called Shabbat through three levels: shin represents the three crowns, Keter, Chokhmah and Binah, and She is the daughter, the fourth with them. The River, the middle pillar, includes the holiness of all the patriarchs, for Jacob encompasses them. Thus the Zohar says that Shabbat’s shin is the mystery of the three patriarchs, united with the only daughter, who is crowned with them. It includes all six attributes. “Draw near, attendants” refers to Moses and Aaron, the vehicles for Netzach and Hod, branches of Abraham’s Chessed and Isaac’s Gevurah. Jacob and Joseph are one, as the Zohar says; elsewhere body and covenant are counted as one. Zohar Chadash assigns the additional Shabbat prayer to Joseph’s holiness: Shabbat’s additional holiness comes from Joseph. Malkhut, Shabbat’s seventh attribute, is the daughter crowned with the patriarchs, and they are crowned with the three upper sefirot. She thus includes the holiness of all ten attributes.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “Likewise Torah scholars, children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they are not workers like the other servants, children of the ordinary realm. Their reward in this world and the world to come is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it says, ‘Honor it with clean clothing.’ Whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals should be done for them.”

: “When the Tree of Good and Evil rules—that is, the ordinary realm of purity and the ordinary realm of impurity—the sages, who are likened to Sabbaths and festivals, have only what those belonging to the ordinary realm give them. It is like the day of Shabbat, which has only what is prepared for it on the weekdays.”
: “For wisdom offers shelter, as money offers shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.”

: “The highest nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions who labor in Torah. They eat nourishment of spirit and soul, not bodily nourishment at all, from the exalted place more precious than all, called Wisdom. The companions’ bodies are therefore weaker than those of other people, for they do not eat bodily nourishment; they eat nourishment of spirit and soul from that distant, exalted and supremely precious place. This food is subtler than the subtlest, beyond all else. Happy is their portion: ‘Wisdom gives life to its possessors.’ Happy is the body that can be nourished by the soul’s food.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 6:1: “Bava Batra 12b says that before a person eats and drinks he has two hearts. This corresponds to the interpretation of ‘with all your heart’ as ‘with both your inclinations,’ the good inclination and the evil inclination: the wise heart and the foolish heart. After eating and drinking, he has only one heart. The passage does not specify which one remains. This depends on the intention with which he eats. When he eats in holiness, he repairs even the foolish heart and has only one heart directed toward his Father in heaven. If, God forbid, he eats without holiness, merely to satisfy his desire, the evil inclination grows stronger through his eating. The Zohar II, 61b, says that the nourishment of the companions who labor in Torah comes from the exalted place, more precious than all, called Wisdom, as in ‘Wisdom gives life to its possessors.’ God established that life is sustained through nourishment. ‘Come, eat of My bread and drink of the wine I have mixed’ refers to the bread of the Written Torah and the wine of the Oral Torah, as Zohar III, 271b, explains. This sustains a Torah scholar’s life, hence ‘Your Torah is within my inward parts.’ Tanna Devei Eliyahu, chapter 26, likewise says: ‘If a person has not merited to ask for mercy that words of Torah enter his inward parts, nevertheless he should ask,’ and so forth. A Torah scholar’s eating is itself like words of Torah. We have explained that eating on Shabbat is a Torah scholar’s eating.
: ““Remember” and “Observe” were spoken in a single utterance—something the human mouth cannot say and the human ear cannot hear.”
: “Observe the Shabbat day to sanctify it, as Hashem your God commanded you.”
: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.”

: “Likewise it says, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.” Could this mean in your heart? When it says “Observe,” guarding in the heart is already stated. How, then, do I fulfill “Remember”? By repeating it with your mouth.”

: “This is what the teaching means: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it over wine as it enters. This establishes the obligation at night; from where do we derive it by day? Scripture says, “Remember the Shabbat day.””

: ““One who separates himself out of love; one who separates himself out of fear”: The Jerusalem Talmud, in the chapter HaRoeh, says: Act out of love and act out of fear. Act out of love, so that if you come to hate, you will remember that you love Him, and one who loves does not hate. Act out of fear, so that if you come to rebel, you will remember that you fear Him, and one who fears does not rebel.”

: “Their intention is that 'remember' is a positive commandment: He commanded us to remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it and not forget it. 'Guard,' in their interpretation, is a prohibition, for every occurrence of 'take care,' 'lest,' and 'do not' denotes a prohibition. It warns us to guard it for sanctification, so that we do not profane it. It would not be fitting for Moses to change God’s words from a positive commandment into a prohibition. … I wonder: if 'remember' and 'guard' were spoken by the Almighty, why was the latter not written on the first tablets? It is possible that both the first and second tablets had 'remember' written on them, and Moses explained to Israel that 'guard' had been spoken together with it. This is their true intention. … It is also true that they alluded to the attribute of 'remember' through a positive commandment, arising from love and belonging to mercy: someone who fulfills his master’s command is beloved, and his master has mercy upon him. The attribute of 'guard' is expressed through a prohibition, belongs to judgment, and arises from fear, because someone who refrains from doing what displeases his master fears him.”

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth”—would that He fix Torah study in our hearts as before! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it says, “I shall put My Torah within them and write it upon their hearts.” Rabbi Nechemya said: When Israel heard “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us—“You speak with us, and we shall hear”; “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” The evil inclination immediately returned to its place. They returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth!” He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it is written, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.””
: “I said in my heart, “The fool’s fate will befall me too; why, then, have I become so exceedingly wise?” I said in my heart that this too is emptiness.”

: “What was created on the seventh day? Shabbat. He looked this way and that, seeking to find a flaw in it, but found only holiness and rest. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Afterward he considered that a person sins on it and incurs death, and said: This too is vanity. Therefore he said, “All is vanity”—making seven.”
: “Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”
: “For in six days Hashem made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.”

: “Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and Hashem your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore Hashem your God commanded you to observe the Shabbat day.”

: “The later tablets came after the sin, when labor in worldly affairs became necessary. Shabbat is then rest from the exertion of providing for bodily needs, and on Shabbat one occupies oneself with Torah; this is one’s rest. Hence the commandment there is “observe,” which means vigilance in the heart. Someone occupied during the working week with bodily needs might forget on Shabbat and do something forbidden, and so needs vigilance. The first commandments say “remember,” the place where forgetfulness does not exist or have any hold, as the Zohar teaches. In the later commandments, Shabbat commemorates the Exodus: leaving servitude to Pharaoh in order to become servants of Hashem. So too, on Shabbat a person is freed from worldly labor to engage in Hashem’s service through Torah. Every Jew has something of both these aspects of Shabbat, but one predominates in some people and the other in others.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Has any god ever attempted to come and take a nation for himself from within another nation—with trials, signs, wonders, warfare, a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and great terrors—like everything Hashem your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?”

: “Rabbi Elazar interpreted the verse concerning the redemption from Egypt: Just as a rose among thorns is difficult for its owner to pluck, so Israel’s redemption was difficult for the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written, “Has God attempted to come and take for Himself a nation from within a nation?” These and those were uncircumcised; these and those grew forelocks; these and those wore forbidden mixtures. The attribute of justice would therefore never have allowed Israel to be redeemed from Egypt. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: Had the Holy One, blessed be He, not bound Himself by an oath, Israel would never have been redeemed. Thus it is written, “Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord.” “Therefore” signifies an oath, as in, “Therefore I have sworn concerning the house of Eli.” Rabbi Berekhya said: “With an arm You redeemed Your people”—by overriding force.”

: “From the side of Chesed, God is ‘remember,’ and the Shekhinah is ‘guard.’ The masters of Mishnah explained: ‘remember’ pertains to the male, and ‘guard’ to the bride. On right and left the branches are separate, like the lung’s lobes, separated above; corresponding to them are the living creatures, ‘their faces and wings separated above,’ and the open sections of a Torah scroll. Below, the two form a single union, like a Torah scroll’s closed sections, where there is no separation. Therefore in the place of union, the body, resembling the lulav’s spine, if its leaves are broken apart or separated it is invalid.”

: ““To sanctify it”—with what do you sanctify it? With food, drink, and clean clothing. Rabbi Chanan said: From here we learn that a person should have two garments, one for weekdays and one for Shabbat. When he taught this in Tiberias, they said: Our weekday clothing is also our Shabbat clothing. He told them: You must make a change, as it says, “Wash, anoint yourself, and put on your clothes.” Was she naked? Rather, she told her: Put on your Shabbat clothes.”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry is described by ‘A river goes out from Eden’—vav—‘to water the garden.’ The river is the middle pillar; ‘goes out from Eden’ means from the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ means the lower Shekhinah.”

: “What do the people of faith say? ‘If the Lord desires us, He will give it to us.’ Once a person labors toward God with the heart’s desire, He asks of us only the heart, and that they guard that holy mark, as in ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’”
: “The human soul is Hashem’s lamp, searching all the innermost chambers.”
: “In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt, on this very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.”
: “'On this day': on the New Moon. It should have said only 'on that day'; why does it say 'on this day'? So that the words of Torah should be new to you, as though He had given them today.”

: “It is written, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” whereas there it says, “The Lord delivered on that day.” This teaches that every year a person must see himself as though he stood at Mount Sinai. Therefore, concerning the giving of the Torah, it is written, “On this day.””

: “Rabbi Yehudah also began an exposition in honor of Torah: “Be attentive and hear, Israel; this day you have become a people.” Was the Torah given to Israel on that day? It was the end of the forty years. Rather, it teaches that Torah is as dear to those who learn it every day as on the day it was given at Mount Sinai.”
: “These words that I command you today shall be upon your heart.”
: ““Which I command you today”—let them not seem to you like an old royal decree, which no one esteems, but like a new decree that everyone runs to read.”

: “In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt, on this very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai. They journeyed from Rephidim, came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there opposite the mountain.”

: “Go and call out in Jerusalem’s hearing: Thus says Hashem: I remember for you the devotion of your youth, the love of your bridal days, when you followed Me into the wilderness, into an unsown land.”
: “They journeyed from Rephidim, came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there opposite the mountain.”

: “What does the name Rephidim mean? R. Eliezer says: Rephidim was its name. R. Joshua says: They weakened their commitment to words of Torah, as it says, “Fathers did not turn back to their children because their hands had grown weak.””

: “Resh Lakish said: What is meant by “If it is scoffers, He scoffs at them, but to the humble He gives favor”? For one who comes to become impure, the way is opened; one who comes to become pure is assisted.”

: ““Open to Me.” Rabbi Yasa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: My children, open for Me one opening of repentance as narrow as the point of a needle, and I shall open for you openings through which wagons and carriages can enter.”

Parallel: Mesillat Yesharim 7:22: “For someone in whom this yearning does not burn as it should, good counsel is to act promptly by a deliberate effort of will, so that yearning will thereby arise in him naturally. Outward movement awakens the inward movement, and the outward is certainly more under his control than the inward. If he uses what is in his control, he will in time acquire what is not: inner joy, willingness and yearning will be born from his deliberately bringing ardor into his movements. This is what the prophet said: ‘Let us know; let us pursue the knowledge of God,’ and it is written, ‘They shall follow God; He shall roar like a lion.’”

: “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Yosei ben Chalafta’s name: Abraham, of whom Scripture does not record the observance of Shabbat, inherited the world within fixed limits, as it says, ‘Arise, walk through the land, its length and its breadth.’ But Jacob, of whom Scripture records the observance of Shabbat—as it says, ‘He encamped before the city,’ meaning that he entered at dusk and established the Sabbath boundaries while it was still day—inherited the world without fixed limits, as it says, ‘Your descendants shall be like the dust of the earth.’”
: “Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, on his return from Paddan-aram, and camped facing the city.”
: “‘He encamped’: the word suggests Shabbat and rest. ‘Before the city’ indicates that he had to camp and observe Shabbat outside the city because he did not have time to enter it.”
: “Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, came with Moses’ sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.”
: “Moses was tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, priest of Midian. He led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to the mountain of God, to Horeb.”

: ““He led the flock beyond the wilderness.” Rabbi Yehoshua said: Why did he pursue the wilderness? Because he saw that Israel would be exalted through the wilderness, as it says, “Who is this ascending from the wilderness?” From the wilderness they received the manna, the quail, the well, the Tabernacle, the Divine Presence, priesthood, kingship, and the clouds of glory.”
: “Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with every fragrant powder of the merchant?”
: “'Israel encamped there': like one person with one heart. All the other encampments, however, involved complaint and dispute.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

: “Although Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed about co-wives, sisters, an old bill of divorce, a woman whose marital status was uncertain, a man who divorced his wife and then lodged with her at an inn, silver and its equivalent, and a perutah and its equivalent, Beit Shammai did not refrain from marrying women from Beit Hillel, nor Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai. This teaches that they treated each other with affection and friendship, fulfilling “Love truth and peace.” Rabbi Shimon says: They refrained in definite cases, but did not refrain in doubtful cases. … Do not read “in doubtful cases,” but “in unspecified cases”: they would inform one another, and the others would abstain.”

: “Thus says Hashem of Hosts: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become joy, gladness, and good festivals for the house of Judah. Therefore love truth and peace.”

: “What is meant by “With enemies at the gate”? Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said: Even a father and son, a teacher and student, who study Torah at one gate become enemies to one another. Yet they do not leave there until they become loving friends, as it says, “Vahev in Supha”: Read the phrase as “Love at its end.””
: “Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of Hashem: “Vaheb in Suphah, and the ravines of Arnon.””

k: volume-i|1516|0|Orot HaKodesh, vol. I, The Purpose of Un
quote: Parallel: Orot HaKodesh, vol. I, The Purpose of Unifications, 107: “All the world’s shortcomings, material and spiritual, arise because each individual apprehends only one side of reality, material or spiritual, which seems good to him; the other sides, which he does not apprehend, seem to him fit to disappear from the world. This thought imprints its force upon individuals and communities, generations and periods: whatever lies outside their own circle, they destroy and obstruct. Complications therefore increase in opinions and beliefs, systems of life and communal conduct. An individual likewise suffers from the many complications within himself: one feeling does not greet another with due affection, and one thought rejects another with contempt and hostility. Friendly exchanges of spirit become impossible, and the perception of an encompassing beauty that restores the soul dwindles. The righteous, who effect unifications in understanding and will, are called to repair, join and complete the work of making peace amid all these harms from which the whole world, and we especially, suffer. They bring peace into the world by bringing peace into their own souls, through the appearance of an integral, comprehensive understanding that continually sends light and life in every direction.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, came to create Adam, the ministering angels formed opposing parties and groups. Some said, ‘Let him not be created,’ and others said, ‘Let him be created.’ Thus it is written, ‘Kindness and truth met; righteousness and peace kissed.’ Kindness said, ‘Let him be created, for he performs acts of kindness.’ Truth said, ‘Let him not be created, for he is entirely falsehood.’ Righteousness said, ‘Let him be created, for he performs righteous deeds.’ Peace said, ‘Let him not be created, for he is entirely strife.’ What did the Holy One do? He took Truth and cast it to the earth, as it says, ‘You cast truth to the earth.’ The ministering angels said before Him, ‘Master of the worlds, why do You dishonor Your royal insignia? Let truth rise from the earth!’ Thus it is written, ‘Truth shall sprout from the earth.’”
: “An army was delivered up, along with the regular offering, because of transgression. It cast truth to the ground, acted, and prospered.”

: “Jacob came and desired it, but it was not given to him. He was told: since Abraham is above and Isaac below him, you shall stand in the middle and take all three. What is the middle? Peace. But does it not say, ‘You grant truth to Jacob’? Truth and peace are one, as in ‘words of peace and truth’ and ‘there shall be peace and truth in my days.’ This is ‘I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father’: a complete inheritance, containing kindness, fear, truth and peace. Thus ‘The stone rejected by the builders became the cornerstone’: the stone rejected by Abraham and Isaac, who built the world, has now become the cornerstone.”
: “He sent letters to all the Jews in the one hundred and twenty-seven provinces of Ahasuerus’s kingdom, words of peace and truth.”

: “‘Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.’ The companions explained this verse. Dominion is Abraham: ‘You are a prince of God among us,’ and ‘I shall bless you and magnify your name.’ Fear is Isaac: ‘The Fear of Isaac was mine.’ ‘He makes peace in His heights’ is Jacob: ‘Grant truth to Jacob,’ and ‘Love truth and peace.’ Truth and peace are bound to one another. Therefore he is the perfection of everything.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 11:1: “The Second Temple was destroyed because of baseless hatred. The Men of the Great Assembly had abolished the inclination toward idolatry, as Yoma 69b says; their failing was baseless hatred between people, wrong toward other human beings rather than toward Heaven. The Second Temple period had exceptionally great righteous people and a powerful expansion of the Oral Torah. The Men of the Great Assembly said, ‘Raise up many students,’ and the ordinances and safeguards whose founders are unknown were generally established by them. Seder Olam accordingly says, ‘From here onward, incline your ear and hear the words of the sages.’ Corresponding to the Oral Torah’s powerful expansion, baseless hatred grew strong on the opposing side. Kiddushin 30b expounds ‘They speak with enemies at the gate’: even a father and son studying Torah at one gate become enemies to each other. Yet of Torah study it says that they do not leave until they become lovers of one another, as in ‘Love at its end.’ When they reach a clarification of the law, love, brotherhood, and peace arise between them.”
: “God spoke all these words, saying:”

: “‘God spoke all these words, saying: I am the Lord.’ Rabbi Yitzchak said: Even the prophecies that the prophets would one day utter were all received at Mount Sinai. From where do we know this? ‘Those who are here with us, standing today’ refers to those already created: ‘are here’ means those present in the world. ‘Those who are not here’ refers to those yet to be created, who are not yet present. It does not say of them, ‘standing with us,’ but ‘with us today’: these are the souls yet to be created, of whom standing is not said, for they too were included.”

: “'The stone tablets, the Torah, and the commandment that I wrote to instruct them': all 613 commandments are included within the Ten Commandments. In the liturgical warnings he composed, Rav Saadiah explained, for each utterance, the commandments dependent upon it.”
: “May my teaching fall like rain and my speech flow like dew, like showers upon fresh grass and abundant rain upon vegetation.”
: “You will say in your heart, “Who bore these for me? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and cast aside. Who raised these? I was left alone—where were these?””

: “‘He said’: what is this? As explained, ‘You shall say in your heart’—speech in silence. ‘Gather yourselves’: should it not say ‘Gather,’ as in ‘Gather My pious ones to Me’? We have established that ‘gather yourselves’ comes from the place above. Gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single union. ‘I shall tell you’: what is ‘tell’? A mystery of wisdom.”

: “Mishnah: If someone said, “This cow said: I am a nazirite if I stand up,” or “This door says: I am a nazirite if I open,” Beit Shammai say he is a nazirite, while Beit Hillel say he is not. Rabbi Yehudah says: Even when Beit Shammai said this, they meant only one who says, “This cow is forbidden to me like an offering if it stands up.” Gemara: Does a cow speak? Rami bar Chama said: The case is that a cow was lying before him, and he said, “This cow thinks it will not stand up; I am a nazirite from its meat if it stands up by itself,” and it did stand up by itself. Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel each follow their own approach. Beit Shammai, who say that a vow to be a nazirite “from dried figs and pressed figs” makes one a nazirite, likewise say here that “from its meat” makes him a nazirite. Beit Hillel say he is not a nazirite.”
: “Moses said to the people, “Do not fear, for God has come to test you, and so that awe of Him will be upon your faces, so that you do not sin.””

: “A baraita teaches: “So that His fear may be upon your faces”—this is shame. “So that you do not sin”—this teaches that shame leads to fear of sin. From here they said: Being bashful is a good sign in a person. Others say: Someone who feels shame will not readily sin; whoever lacks shame shows that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.”

: “Akavya ben Mahalalel says: Consider three things and you will not come to sin. Know where you came from, where you are going, and before whom you will have to give judgment and account. Where did you come from? A putrid drop. Where are you going? To a place of dust, maggots, and worms. Before whom will you give judgment and account? Before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.”
: “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of trouble come and years arrive of which you will say, “I have no desire for them.””

: “We learned elsewhere: Akavya ben Mahalalel says: Consider three things and you will not come to transgression. Rabbi Abba, son of Rav Pappi, and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: Akavya expounded all three from a single verse, “Remember your Creator.” Read it as be’erekha, your well; borekha, your pit; and bor’ekha, your Creator. Your well refers to where you came from. Your pit refers to where you are going. Your Creator refers to the One before whom you will give judgment and an account.”

: “Akavya ben Mahalalel says: Consider three things, and you will not come to sin. Know from where you came—from a putrid drop; where you are going—to dust, maggots, and worms; and before whom you will give judgment and account—before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in Rav Pappi’s name, and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin in Rabbi Levi’s name: Rabbi Akiva derived all three from one verse, “Remember your Creator.” “Your well”—the putrid fluid; “your pit”—maggots and worms; “your Creator”—the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, before whom you will give judgment and account.”

: “Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Adam, “human being,” alludes to efer, dam, marah—ashes, blood, and bile. Basar, “flesh,” alludes to bushah, seruḥah, rimmah—shame, putrefaction, and worms. Some give sheol, the grave, as the first word, for basar is written with the letter sin.”
: “From new moon to new moon, and from Shabbat to Shabbat, all flesh will come to bow down before Me, says Hashem.”
: “Thus says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place could be My resting place?”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: Did I not write for you in My Torah, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth”? Although you work throughout the six days, let Shabbat be devoted entirely to Torah. From here they said: A person should rise early on Shabbat and study, go to the synagogue and house of study, read Torah and study the Prophets, and afterward go home, eat, and drink, fulfilling, “Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a good heart.” For the Holy One, blessed be He, finds rest only with those who practice Torah, as it says, “All these My hand has made… But to this one I shall look: to the poor and broken in spirit, who trembles at My word.””
: “My hand made all these things, and all these things came to be, declares Hashem. But to this one I look: the poor and crushed in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

: “There are three kinds of humility, corresponding to the Mishnah’s “Consider three things, and you will not come to transgression.” These oppose the three impure powers just mentioned. “From where have you come? From a putrid drop” opposes jealousy, the desire to overpower another, like Esau’s “By your sword you shall live.” When a person humbles himself by recalling that he came from a putrid drop, what grounds has he for pride or for overpowering another? “Where are you going? To a place of dust” can overcome the impure power of desire. Thus the final counsel in Berakhot for overcoming the evil inclination is to remember the day of death, when every desire comes to an end. “Before whom will you render an account?” saves him from pride and the pursuit of honor. Even if the evil inclination deceives him into imagining that he has qualities of which to boast, when he remembers that he must account before the Holy One, King of kings, he recognizes: What am I, and what is my life beside His greatness? How could he become proud?”
: “Make Me an altar of earth and sacrifice upon it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and cattle. Wherever I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak opened with the verse, ‘An altar of earth you shall make for Me.’ Rabbi Yitzchak said: If the Holy One declares, ‘I appear to and bless one who has merely built an altar in My name,’ how much more Abraham, who circumcised himself in My name! Thus, ‘The Lord appeared to him among the terebinths of Mamre.’”

: “‘He said: Because the Lord your God made it happen before me.’ Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish differed. One said: If the Holy One, blessed be He, provided what was needed for your sacrifice—as it says, ‘Abraham lifted his eyes and saw a ram’—how much more would He provide what was needed for your meal!”

: “There is also a meal belonging to the sage’s level. The Zohar says that the highest nourishment of all is the companions’ nourishment, food of spirit and soul: 'Wisdom gives life to its possessors.' This is the utterance of God’s mouth within food, eating in holiness far beyond merely fulfilling a commandment. It comes from the Torah’s letters—'Come, eat My bread'—and introduces holiness into the heart. This is called 'the table before the Lord,' which is literally like an offering. Thus the sages say that hosting a Torah scholar in one’s house is like offering the daily sacrifices; whoever wishes to pour wine upon the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine; and bringing a gift to a Torah scholar is like offering firstfruits. Every offering is for the name Havayah, and this is the King’s meal.”

: “It was taught: They said of Hillel the Elder that when he rejoiced at the celebration of the water-drawing, he would say: “If I am here, everything is here; if I am not here, who is here?” He also used to say: “To the place I love, my feet carry me. If you come to My house, I will come to your house; if you do not come to My house, I will not come to your house,” as it says, “Wherever I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.””
: “I will enter Your house with burnt offerings and fulfill my vows to You.”

: “On Shabbat, Israel too is described as “coming to My house,” for Shabbat is called God’s house. As stated in the responsa of the Geonim, quoted in HaPardes attributed to Rashi, section 3, the reason we do not conclude on Shabbat with “Who guards His people Israel,” as on weekdays, is the parable of a king: when he comes home, he does not need guarding. On Shabbat, the King is described as being in His own house.”

k: volume-i|1543|2|Shibbolei HaLeket 65:2, in the name of R
quote: : “Rav Sher Shalom Gaon, of blessed memory, said: On Sabbath nights and festival nights, the practice in the academy and in our master’s house in Babylonia is not to say 'Who guards His people Israel forever,' but to conclude 'Who spreads a canopy of peace.' We in exile follow our master’s practice of spreading peace. This resembles a king who became separated from his army and entered among another people who did not protect him. He grew afraid and took weapons to defend himself from those seeking his life. But when he reached his army, he laid down his weapons, indicating that he no longer needed to guard himself, since his officers and ministers were with him to protect him. Likewise, throughout the weekdays Israel are afraid: they are occupied and cannot fulfill the commandments then, and weekdays lack the merit of Shabbat. They therefore need to pray not to be harmed by destructive forces, saying, 'Guard our going out and coming in,' and blessing, 'Who guards His people Israel forever.' Prayer is like a weapon. When Sabbath eve arrives, everyone works for Shabbat’s honor, to delight in it and rest. The merit of Shabbat is great and protects those who remember it to sanctify it. They therefore need no guarding; spreading peace suffices for them.”

: “Rav Chisda said: What does “Hashem loves the gates of Zion more than all Jacob’s dwellings” mean? Hashem loves the gates distinguished by halakhah more than synagogues and houses of study. This accords with Rabbi Chiya bar Ami’s statement in Ulla’s name: Since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has only the four cubits of halakhah in His world.”

: “From where do we learn that the Divine Presence accompanies even one person who sits and studies Torah? It says, “In every place where I cause My name to be recalled, I will come to you and bless you.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 14:3: “‘Establish the work of our hands for us’: certainly not everyone merits having his body serve entirely as a vessel of Torah; a person may need to work with his hands for his livelihood. We therefore pray, ‘Establish the work of our hands for us,’ that its intention be for Heaven, like the work of the Tabernacle. We can then draw these three forms of holiness into it as well. The holiness of the month is the holiness of Torah. By fulfilling the commandments governing business between one person and another, the place becomes ‘four cubits of halakhah,’ because a halakhic teaching is being fulfilled there. The intention of a commandment is also called ‘the light of Torah,’ as explained in Chanukah II and XXIII. The holiness of the covenant is called ‘the work of our hands,’ because the action issues from the body made holy with this holiness. The Zohar’s introduction, 8a, accordingly says that the masters of the covenant are called His handiwork, as in ‘Establish the work of our hands’—the enduring covenant. Shabbat’s holiness, too, can be drawn into the weekdays. Zohar III, 29b, calls Torah scholars ‘Shabbatot’; they possess Shabbat’s additional soul even on weekdays, as Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 21, says. Zohar III, 179b, also says that the Divine Presence does not depart from Israel, even on the ‘Shabbatot’ of the weekdays. This is ‘Establish the work of our hands.’”

: “This is Torah’s way: eat bread with salt, drink water by measure, sleep upon the ground, live a life of hardship, and labor in Torah. If you do so, “Happy are you, and it is good for you”—happy are you in this world, and it is good for you in the World to Come.”
: “The righteous person eats to satisfy his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes wanting.”
: “Young men who enjoy jumping and running may do so. It is likewise permitted to look at anything that gives pleasure. Walking for enjoyment on Shabbat is also permitted.”

: “This is the version in the Tosefta: He used to say, “To the place I love, my feet carry me. If you come to My house—” It seems to me that this is also the reading required here, because R. Yohanan says afterward, “A person’s feet,” and so forth. Without that reading, what connection would R. Yohanan’s statement have here?”

: ““If I am here, everything is here”—he expounded publicly in the Holy One’s name, warning them not to sin: If I am here, everything is here. As long as I desire this house and My Divine Presence rests in it, its honor will endure and everyone will come here. But if you sin and I remove My Divine Presence, who will come here?”

: “Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: If you come to My house, I shall come to yours; if you do not come to My house, I too shall not come to yours. To the place my heart loves, my feet carry me. From here they said: Whenever ten people enter a synagogue, the Divine Presence is with them, as it says, “God stands in the congregation of God.” How do we know that this applies even to three who sit in judgment? “In the midst of judges He judges.” Even two? “Then those who feared the Lord spoke, each to his fellow.” Even one? “In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I shall come to you.””
: “I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently will find me.”
: “Indeed, along the path of Your judgments, Hashem, we have awaited You. Our soul longs for Your name and Your remembrance.”

: “Abaye said: Let us also say that blessing follows closely upon the presence of Torah scholars, as it says, “Hashem blessed me because of you.” Alternatively, derive it from, “Hashem blessed the Egyptian’s house because of Joseph.””
: “For what you had before I came was little, but it has increased greatly. Hashem has blessed you wherever I turned. Now, when will I also provide for my own household?”
: “A psalm of David. Hashem is my shepherd; I will lack nothing.”

: “Through this favor Moses, the holy faithful prophet, departed the world, making known that he did not depart through judgment. At that hour his soul went out through the Holy Ancient One’s favor and was concealed within Him. Therefore ‘No one knew his burial place.’ Just as the Holy Ancient One is concealed beyond all concealment, unknown above and below, so this soul was concealed within that favor revealed at Shabbat’s afternoon prayer. Hence ‘No one knew his burial place.’ He is hidden beyond all the world’s concealments, and judgment does not rule over him. Happy is Moses’ portion.”

: “Three departed this world at this time, all included in Moses: Moses, the exalted faithful prophet; Joseph the Righteous; and King David. Hence three acknowledgments of divine justice are said here. First is righteous Joseph’s: ‘Your righteousness is like mighty mountains; Your judgments are a great deep.’ Joseph alone is like all the upper mountains. Moses the faithful prophet’s verse is ‘Your righteousness, God, reaches on high, You who have done great things,’ for he embraces every side, right and left. King David’s is ‘Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth.’ ‘Everlasting’ refers to King David.”
: “Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and his father’s entire household with bread, according to the needs of the children.”

: “‘You shall know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the grass of the field.’ Rabbi Yudan said: Our father Jacob did not depart this world until he had seen six hundred thousand of his descendants.”

: “Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: Three good sustainers arose for Israel: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. Through them three good gifts were given: the well, the cloud, and the manna. The well came through Miriam’s merit, the pillar of cloud through Aaron’s merit, and the manna through Moses’ merit.”

: “Even previously, while Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them back. Hashem said to you, “You shall shepherd My people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.””

: “When daybreak arrived, Israel’s sages entered David’s presence. They said: “Our lord the king, your people Israel need sustenance.” He answered: “Go and support one another.” They said: “A handful does not satisfy a lion, and a pit cannot fill itself with its own earth.” He answered: “Go and send your forces out to war.” Immediately they would consult Achitophel, seek the Sanhedrin’s approval, and inquire of the Urim and Tummim.”
: “He blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me all my life until this day—””
: “I am diminished by all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. For I crossed this Jordan with only my staff, and now I have become two camps.”

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””
: “Light is planted for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.”

: “After they finished eating, Rabbi Yitzḥak told Rav Naḥman: Rabbi Yoḥanan said that our father Jacob did not die. He replied: Was it then for nothing that the mourners mourned him, the embalmers embalmed him, and the buriers buried him? Rabbi Yitzḥak answered: I am interpreting a verse: “Do not fear, My servant Jacob, declares Hashem, and do not be dismayed, Israel, for I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of their captivity.” The verse compares Jacob to his offspring: Just as his offspring are alive, so he too is alive.”
: “Some say that Moses did not die. Here it is written, “He died there,” and elsewhere, “He was there with Hashem.” Just as there he stood ministering, so here too he stands ministering.”
: “He buried him in the valley, in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor, and to this day no one knows his burial place.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: What is meant by “Show me a sign for good, so that those who hate me may see and be ashamed”? David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, forgive me for that sin. He answered: It is forgiven. David said: Show me a sign during my lifetime. He answered: I will not make it known during your lifetime; I will make it known in the lifetime of Solomon your son. When Solomon built the Temple, he sought to bring the Ark into the Holy of Holies, but the gates clung together. Solomon uttered twenty-four expressions of prayer and was not answered. He began: “Lift up your heads, gates; be lifted, eternal entrances, that the King of glory may enter.” They rushed toward him to swallow him, asking, “Who is this King of glory?” He answered, “The Lord, mighty and strong.” He repeated, “Lift up your heads, gates; lift up, eternal entrances, that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts—He is the King of glory, Selah,” but was not answered. Once he said, “Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed; remember the faithful deeds of David Your servant,” he was immediately answered. At that moment the faces of all David’s enemies turned dark like the bottom of a pot, and all the people, all Israel, knew that the Holy One, blessed be He, had forgiven him for that sin. Did Solomon not speak well when he said, “I praise the dead who have already died”?”

: “What did Solomon do? Our Rabbis of blessed memory said: He went and brought David’s coffin, saying, “Lord God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed.” Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chelbo’s name: At that moment David came to life. You may derive the whole matter from David’s words: “Lord, You raised my soul from Sheol; You revived me from among those descending to the pit.” Solomon said: Master of the worlds, act through this man’s merit, as it says, “Remember the faithful deeds of David Your servant.” He was immediately answered.”

: “Throughout Israel’s years in the wilderness, these two chests—the coffin of a dead man and the Ark of the Divine Presence—traveled together. Passersby would ask: What are these two chests? They answered: One is a dead man’s coffin, and one is the Ark of the Divine Presence. Is it fitting for a dead man to travel beside the Divine Presence? They replied: This man fulfilled everything written in this Ark.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: Jethro is not called priest of On, but priest of Midian. He answered: all is one. Earlier Joseph’s father-in-law was called priest of On; afterward Moses’ father-in-law was priest of Midian. It is a single mystery, for Moses and Joseph stand at the level of one mystery: the letter vav spelled with two vavs together. ‘Priest of Midian’ contains the mystery of the contentious woman, eshet midyanim. Moses and Joseph stand in one mystery, the two vavs together.”

: “‘These are Jacob’s generations: Joseph.’ As explained, Jacob’s entire likeness was present in Joseph. Everything that happened to one happened to the other, and both proceed together. This is the mystery of the letter vav spelled vav-vav, both proceeding together, for they are one mystery and one likeness.”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”

: “Therefore ‘The dead do not praise Yah’: the living must praise the Living One; the dead do not praise the living. ‘But we shall bless Yah,’ for we are alive and have no portion in the side of death. Hezekiah said, ‘The living, the living, he shall thank You, as I do,’ for the living draws near to the Living One. King David is alive, and his nearness is to the Life of the worlds. Whoever approaches Him is alive: ‘You who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today.’ Likewise ‘Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a living man, mighty in deeds, from Kabze’el.’”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 2:1: “The books explain that although death was decreed upon Adam as a curse, after the corruption death became necessary for a person’s benefit. Many things that he cannot perceive while embodied become perceptible after death. Before the corruption, when his body was refined, he did not need the repair accomplished through death. On this basis the authority abbreviated here as MaharY Birbi explained ‘Now, why should we die? If we continue hearing the voice of the Lord our God, we shall die.’ Although they saw that God spoke with them and they lived, they said: ‘Today we have seen that God speaks with a person and he lives.’ Now that we can attain this while alive, why should we die? Why do we need the repair of death? ‘If we continue hearing’ means an additional, higher level beyond what we attained while alive; ‘we shall die’ means that death would then be necessary. Thus far his words. Sleep, which is one sixtieth of death, has this same benefit: in sleep a person can perceive what he cannot possibly perceive while awake. Thus it is related that the holy Ari once said that, during his Shabbat sleep in the week of Balak, he received and perceived what he could not expound in eighty years. The Gemara calls a dream one sixtieth of prophecy, and the Midrash Rabbah calls dreaming the fallen fruit of prophecy. King Solomon attained all Solomon’s wisdom, the lower Wisdom, through one dream. ‘He became wiser than all people’: such wisdom

: “They asked: If a person recited Havdalah over a cup, must he still include it in prayer? Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Infer it a fortiori from prayer. Prayer is the original institution, yet they said that one who recites Havdalah in prayer must also recite it over a cup. Certainly one who recites it over a cup, which was not the original institution, must also include it in prayer.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Whoever recites Havdalah over wine at the departure of Shabbat will have sons. For it is written, “To distinguish between the sacred and the ordinary,” and elsewhere, “To distinguish between the impure and the pure,” followed by, “When a woman conceives…” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Sons qualified to give halakhic rulings, as it is written, “To distinguish… and to instruct.””
: “He began and said: “Who distinguishes between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the peoples, between the seventh day and the six days of work.””

: “Therefore we do not recite the eighteen blessings on Shabbat. If a person had someone ill at home, he would remember him at ‘Who heals the sick of His people Israel’ and become distressed. Shabbat was given to Israel for holiness, delight, and rest, not for distress. Therefore he recites the first three blessings, the last three blessings, and a blessing of rest between them. Hence David said, ‘Seven times a day I praise You’: these are the seven blessings recited on Shabbat.”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”

: “Rabbi Berekhiah sat and expounded: what do we mean by saying ‘the world to come’ every day without understanding our words? Its Aramaic rendering is ‘the world that comes.’ Before the world was created, the thought arose to create a great illuminating light. A great light was created that no creature could command.
