God saw that they could not bear it, so He took one-seventh and put it in place for them; the rest He hid for the righteous in the future. He said: if they merit this seventh portion and guard it, I shall give them the rest in the final world. This is ‘the world to come,’ which had already come before the six days of creation, as it says, ‘How abundant is Your goodness, which You have hidden for those who fear You.’”
: “God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” There was evening and there was morning: one day.”

: “Rabbi Chanina bar Yitzchak said: There are three lesser offshoots: sleep is an offshoot of death, a dream is an offshoot of prophecy, and Shabbat is an offshoot of the World to Come. Rabbi Avin adds two more: the sun’s orb is an offshoot of the light above, and Torah is an offshoot of the wisdom above.”
: “It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.”

: ““See that the Lord has given you Shabbat.” It should have said “Know”; why “See”? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, told them: If idolaters ask why you observe Shabbat on this day, tell them: See, the manna does not descend on Shabbat. What does “given you” mean? It was given to you, not to idolaters. From here they said: If idolaters come and observe Shabbat, not only do they receive no reward, and so forth, for it says, “Day and night shall not cease.” Likewise it says, “Between Me and the children of Israel…” It is like a king seated with a queen seated opposite him: one who passes between them incurs liability.”
: “This day belongs to souls, rather than the body, for the Bundle of Souls rules. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional upper holy spirit.”

: “Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.” “He summons the heavens above”—this is the soul. “And the earth to judge His people”—this is the body.”
: “'He kept the matter': he waited expectantly for it to happen. Similarly, 'Keeping faith,' and 'Do not keep watch over my sin'—do not wait.”
: “His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.”
: “These are the laws you shall set before them.”

: “What is written above this passage? “They shall judge the people at all times.” Here He says, “These are the judgments,” with the commandments in the middle. It is like a queen walking with armed guards on this side and armed guards on that side, while she is in the middle. So the Torah has judgments before it and judgments after it, while it is in the middle. Likewise it says, “I walk in the path of righteousness.” The Torah says: On what path do I walk? I walk in the way of those who practice righteousness. “Amid the paths of justice”: the Torah is in the middle, with judgments before and after it. Before it: “There He established for him statute and judgment”; after it: “These are the judgments.””
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”
: “They shall judge the people at all times. Every major matter they shall bring to you, but every minor matter they shall judge themselves. Lighten your burden, and let them bear it with you.”

: “Rabbi Shimon began: ‘These are the judgments you shall set before them.’ The Targum renders: ‘These are the judgments you shall arrange before them.’ These are the arrangements of reincarnation, judgments concerning souls, each judged according to its punishment.”

: “Here it says, ‘If a man sells his daughter’: this is the soul undergoing reincarnations because of evil deeds in the world. ‘As a maidservant’ means that Other Side, in an ill-fated return of the turning wheel. The soul has been oppressed, and must be brought out from there.”
: “I walk along the path of righteousness, within the ways of justice.”

: “Concerning Torah, where “truth” is written—as in “Acquire truth and do not sell it”—the Holy One, blessed be He, does not go beyond the strict line of judgment. Concerning judgment, where “truth” is not written, the Holy One, blessed be He, does go beyond the strict line of judgment.”

: “According to the view that Job lived in Moses’ time, why not place Job first? We do not begin with calamity. But Ruth also begins with calamity! Its calamity has a hopeful outcome, for Rabbi Yochanan said: Why was she named Ruth? Because David descended from her, and he abundantly offered the Holy One, blessed be He, songs and praises.”
: ““It has a future”: The end of the calamity turns into a future and hope, because David emerged from there.”
: “For I know the plans I am planning for you, declares Hashem—plans for peace, not for harm, to give you a future and hope.”
: ““To give you a future and hope”: Rav Yehuda son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said in Rav’s name: This refers to date palms and linen garments.”
: “But R. Yohanan said: “I thought it was yours, but it is theirs!””

Commentary: Rashi on Sukkah 44a:11:1: ““But R. Yohanan said: I thought it was yours, but it is theirs”—Rav Kahana was one of Rav’s students and exceptionally sharp. He fled to the Land of Israel, to R. Yohanan, because of an incident in which he had killed a man, as related in the final chapter of Bava Kamma 117. R. Yohanan needed him to resolve several uncertainties. R. Yohanan used to say to the people of the Land of Israel: I thought the Torah was yours, since you had not been exiled from your land or suffered mental disruption. But I have seen that it belongs to the Babylonians: despite their exile, the wisdom of the craftsmen and smiths exiled with Jeconiah endured for them. It says, “All were mighty men, makers of war.” Seder Olam teaches: What feats of strength could people bound in iron chains perform? Rather, they were mighty in the warfare of Torah. Thus R. Yohanan held that Torah was not forgotten during the Babylonian exile.”

: “Resh Lakish said: May I be an atonement for R. Hiyya and his sons! At first, when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra ascended from Babylon and established it. It was forgotten again; Hillel the Babylonian ascended and established it. It was forgotten again; R. Hiyya and his sons ascended and established it.”

: “Rabbi Levi said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: In her destruction she raised righteous people for Me; in her flourishing she raised wicked people for Me. In her destruction she raised righteous people: Daniel and his companions, Mordecai and his companions, Ezra and his companions. In her flourishing she raised wicked people: Ahaz and his companions, Manasseh and his companions, Amon and his associates. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, concerning Rabbi Levi’s teaching: “For the children of the desolate are more numerous than those of the married woman.” Thus she raised more righteous people for Me in her destruction than in her flourishing.”
: “Ulla said: So that they would eat dates and engage in Torah.”
: “Rabbi Hanina said: Forty years before Israel was exiled to Babylonia, date palms were planted in Babylonia, so that Israel would be drawn to sweetness, which trains the tongue for Torah.”

: “Rabbi said to Levi: Describe the Persians to me. He answered: They resemble the troops of David’s house. Describe the Habbar priests to me. They resemble angels of destruction. Describe the Ishmaelites to me. They resemble the demons of the privy. Describe the Torah scholars of Babylonia to me. They resemble ministering angels.”

: ““They resemble ministering angels”: They wear white and are wrapped like ministering angels, as it is written, “The man dressed in linen.” Similarly, Shabbat 25b says of Rabbi Yehuda that he would wrap himself and sit in fringed linen garments, resembling an angel. Nedarim 20b likewise says: Who are the ministering angels? The Sages. Why are they called ministering angels? Because they distinguish themselves like ministering angels through fine clothing.”

: “Rabbi Yohanan said: This is Yohanan ben Dehavai’s opinion. The Sages, however, said that the halakha does not follow Yohanan ben Dehavai: A man may do whatever he wishes with his wife. It is like meat from the butcher: If he wishes to eat it with salt, he may; roasted, he may; cooked, he may; thoroughly boiled, he may. The same applies to fish from the fisherman. Amemar said: Who are the ministering angels mentioned in his report? The Sages. If he meant actual ministering angels, why would Rabbi Yohanan say that the halakha does not follow Yohanan ben Dehavai? They understand the formation of the fetus better! Why, then, are the Sages called ministering angels? Because they distinguish themselves in dress like ministering angels.”

: “Why do the Torah scholars of Babylonia distinguish themselves through their clothing? Because they are away from their own place. As people say: In my own city, my name establishes me; away from my city, my clothing establishes me.”

: “Adam was the firstborn of the world. When he offered his sacrifice—as it says, ‘It shall please the Lord more than an ox or bull with horns and hooves’—he wore the garments of the High Priesthood, as it says, ‘The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and clothed them.’ They were garments of distinction, and the firstborn would serve in them.”
: “I raised my eyes and saw a man dressed in linen, with a belt of pure gold from Uphaz around his waist.”

: ““This is forever incumbent upon Israel.” Rav Giddel said in Rav’s name: This refers to an altar already built, at which Michael, the great prince, stands and offers a sacrifice. Rabbi Yochanan said: It refers to Torah scholars engaged in studying the laws of the Temple service; Scripture credits them as though the Temple had been built in their days.”

: “I found the following in a manuscript: Know that wearing linen garments contains a great secret, benefiting the living and the dead, young and old. For every deceased person clothed in white linen shrouds, even one who died outside the Land of Israel, every accuser is transformed into an advocate. Whoever wishes to investigate, examine, test, and experience the wondrous property of wearing linen garments without any other fabric—even an infant whose father is known to have lost many children through wicked Lilith, an evil spirit, or any spiritual force of the left side—is protected from all these harms by the special property of these garments.”

Parallel: Da'at Tevunot 52:2: “Nevertheless, He did not wish to leave His world perpetually agitated by the partnership of good and evil. Rather, His great goodness established a mode of governance and a profound design, directing all things, through good and evil themselves, toward the complete repair possible for them. It belongs to His perfection that His works should ultimately be perfected and not remain deficient. This, however, is not the action of His simple perfection as it is in itself, which cannot be apprehended; His simplicity has no place in our discussion at all. Rather, this is what I said: it belongs to His perfection that, even when He wishes to act only according to the measure of created beings, He should act with them in perfection. This is the source of providential governance: the profound design I mentioned, which turns and draws everything toward complete repair.”

: “Did Ezra institute public Torah reading on Mondays and Thursdays? It had already been instituted earlier. A baraita teaches: “They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.” Those who expound the verse’s allusions said: Water means Torah, as it says, “Let everyone who thirsts come to the water.” After three days without Torah they grew weary. The prophets among them therefore instituted reading on Shabbat, pausing on Sunday, reading on Monday, pausing on Tuesday and Wednesday, reading on Thursday, and pausing on Friday, so that they would not pass three days without Torah. Initially they instituted either one person reading three verses, or three people reading three verses, corresponding to priests, Levites, and Israelites. Ezra then instituted three readers and ten verses, corresponding to the ten men who remain available for the community.”
: “They came to Marah, but could not drink the water of Marah because it was bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.”

: “A baraita teaches: “Moses brought back the people’s words to the Lord,” and it also says, “Moses told the people’s words to the Lord.” What did the Holy One, blessed be He, say to Moses? What did Moses say to Israel? What did Israel say to Moses? And what did Moses report before the Almighty? This concerns the command to set a boundary—Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda’s view. Rabbi says: At first he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses brought back”—words that unsettle a person’s mind. Finally he explained its reward, as it says “Moses told”—words that draw a person’s heart like aggada. Some say: At first he explained its reward—words that restore a person’s mind. Finally he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses told”—words as hard for a person as sinews.”

: “Gad: wormwood. In Shabbat 86, 'He told' is interpreted as words hard as gidin. The explanation is that the dalet is doubled, and it means wormwood. 'I will feed this people wormwood' is translated with bitterness like gidin; similarly, 'Those who turn justice into wormwood,' and 'Her end is bitter as wormwood'—bitter like gidei.”

: “He said, “If you listen carefully to the voice of Hashem your God, do what is upright in His eyes, attend to His commandments, and observe all His statutes, I will place upon you none of the illnesses I placed upon Egypt, for I am Hashem, your healer.””
: “For I am about to give the command and shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as one shakes a sieve, without a single pebble falling to the ground.”

: “‘In all that I have said to you, you shall be guarded.’ Why tishameru, ‘be guarded,’ rather than tishmeru, ‘guard’? Precisely ‘be guarded.’ ‘All that I have said’ means the assurance I have given you concerning My service: you shall be guarded so that no evil reaches you, through My protection alone. ‘Do not mention the name of other gods’ is as explained. Another interpretation: do not bring about your falling among the nations in a foreign land, so that ‘There you shall serve other gods’ is fulfilled in you.”
: “Be watchful concerning everything I have told you. Do not mention the name of other gods; let it not be heard from your mouth.”

: “Go and see: a king who loves his son, even when he curses and strikes him, loves him in his innermost being. When he displays fierce anger, compassion for him is present. So too with the Holy One, blessed be He: although He curses, His words are spoken in love. Outwardly they appear as curses, yet they are many benefits, because these curses were given in love. This was not so with the earlier ones, which were all given with severe judgment. In these there are judgment and love together, like a father who loves his son and holds a whipping strap in his hand: he makes a great roar and loud threats, but the lashes are light, administered with compassion.”

: “'Moses ascended': on the second day. All his ascents were early in the morning, as it says, 'Moses rose early in the morning.' 'Thus shall you say': in this language and this order. 'To the house of Jacob': these are the women; speak to them gently, as taught in Mekhilta. 'And tell the children of Israel': explain the punishments and precise requirements to the males—words as hard as sinews, as taught in Shabbat 87.”
: “Moses ascended to God, and Hashem called to him from the mountain, saying, “Thus shall you say to the house of Jacob and declare to the children of Israel.””

: “A baraita teaches: “Moses brought back the people’s words to the Lord,” and it also says, “Moses told the people’s words to the Lord.” What did the Holy One, blessed be He, say to Moses? What did Moses say to Israel? What did Israel say to Moses? And what did Moses report before the Almighty? This concerns the command to set a boundary—Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda’s view. Rabbi says: At first he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses brought back”—words that unsettle a person’s mind. Finally he explained its reward, as it says “Moses told”—words that draw a person’s heart like aggada. Some say: At first he explained its reward—words that restore a person’s mind. Finally he explained its punishment, as it says “Moses told”—words as hard for a person as sinews.”

: “A person must bless God for misfortune as he blesses Him for good, as it says, “You shall love Hashem your God with all your heart.” “With all your heart” means with both your inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination. “With all your soul” means even if He takes your soul. “With all your might” means with all your property. Another interpretation: Whatever measure He measures out to you, acknowledge Him for it.”

: “Earlier authorities wrote that kol, 'all,' applies to at least three. In truth, we find several verses and statements of the Mishnah and Gemara using 'all' even for two. Nevertheless, Bereshit Rabbah’s exposition of 'There was famine in all lands' says: in three lands—Phoenicia, Arabia, and Palestine. They appear to infer three lands from 'all,' following the earlier authorities. It appears that 'all' is indeed three: two extremes and the middle that includes them, the usual reckoning in holiness. Opposite this, the shells have three familiar evil qualities: jealousy, desire, and honor, the three roots of idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.”

: “‘With all your heart’ means with two hearts, the two inclinations: one good and one evil. Each is called heart: one a good heart, the other an evil heart. Therefore levavkha, ‘your heart,’ denotes two: the good and evil inclinations.”

: “Warnings and punishments are read and translated publicly. Is this not obvious? One might have thought that we should be concerned lest people come to serve God out of fear. The teaching therefore tells us that they are nevertheless read and translated.”

: “Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak said: One who makes Shabbat a delight is rescued from subjugation by the exiles. Here it is written, “I will cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth,” and elsewhere it is written, “You shall tread upon their high places.””

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name, in the name of Bar Kappara: Whoever fulfills the duty of three Shabbat meals is rescued from three calamities: the travail of the Messiah, the judgment of Gehinnom, and the war of Gog and Magog. For the Messiah’s travail, “day” appears here and also in “Behold, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the day.” For Gehinnom’s judgment, “day” appears here and also in “That day is a day of wrath.” For the war of Gog and Magog, “day” appears here and also in “On the day Gog comes.””

: “‘These are the names.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him seeks discipline for him early.’ Ordinarily, if one person tells another, ‘So-and-so struck your son,’ the father pursues that man to the utmost. Why, then, does Scripture say, ‘One who withholds his rod hates his son’? To teach that whoever withholds discipline from his son will ultimately see him take a corrupt path and come to hate him.”
: “Know in your heart that Hashem your God disciplines you as a father disciplines his child.”
: “One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him is diligent in disciplining him.”

: ““These are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; each man came with his household.” This is what Scripture says: “One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him disciplines him early.” Ordinarily, if someone tells a man, “So-and-so struck your son,” he becomes his bitter enemy. What, then, does “One who withholds his rod hates his son” teach? Whoever withholds discipline from his son will ultimately see him fall into evil ways, and will hate him.”

: “Thus Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by “Those passing through the valley of weeping make it a spring; the teacher is also clothed in blessings”? “Those passing” are people who transgress the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. “The valley”—Gehinnom is deepened for them. “Weeping”—they weep and shed tears like a spring flowing into the depths. “The teacher is also clothed in blessings”—they accept their judgment as just, saying: Master of the world, You have judged well, acquitted well, condemned well, and rightly prepared Gehinnom for the wicked and Eden for the righteous. Is that so? Reish Lakish said: The wicked do not repent even at Gehinnom’s entrance, as it says, “They shall go out and see the corpses of the people who rebel against Me.” It does not say “who rebelled,” but “who rebel,” meaning that they continue rebelling forever. There is no difficulty: One statement concerns Israel’s sinners, the other the sinners of the nations. This is also reasonable, since otherwise Reish Lakish would contradict himself. Reish Lakish said: Gehinnom’s fire does not rule over Israel’s sinners. This follows all the more from the golden altar: Though covered by only a dinar’s thickness of gold, it stood for many years without fire ruling over it. How much more so Israel’s sinners, who are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate! For “Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate” may be read, “Even your empty ones are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate.” What then of
: “They will go out and see the corpses of the people who rebelled against Me. Their worm will not die, and their fire will not be extinguished, and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.”

: “Just as praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, rises to Him from the righteous in the Garden of Eden, so it rises from the wicked in Gehinnom, as it says, “Those passing through the valley of weeping make it a spring.” What is “make it a spring”? They shed tears like springs until they cool Gehinnom with their tears, and from there praise rises, as it says, “The teacher too shall be clothed in blessings.” What do they say? Rabbi Yochanan said: Rightly You spoke; rightly You judged; rightly You declared pure; rightly You declared impure; rightly You found liable; rightly You taught; rightly You instructed.”

: “Thus Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by “Those passing through the valley of weeping make it a spring; the teacher is also clothed in blessings”? “Those passing” are people who transgress the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. “The valley”—Gehinnom is deepened for them. “Weeping”—they weep and shed tears like a spring flowing into the depths. “The teacher is also clothed in blessings”—they accept their judgment as just, saying: Master of the world, You have judged well, acquitted well, condemned well, and rightly prepared Gehinnom for the wicked and Eden for the righteous. Is that so? Reish Lakish said: The wicked do not repent even at Gehinnom’s entrance, as it says, “They shall go out and see the corpses of the people who rebel against Me.” It does not say “who rebelled,” but “who rebel,” meaning that they continue rebelling forever. There is no difficulty: One statement concerns Israel’s sinners, the other the sinners of the nations. This is also reasonable, since otherwise Reish Lakish would contradict himself. Reish Lakish said: Gehinnom’s fire does not rule over Israel’s sinners. This follows all the more from the golden altar: Though covered by only a dinar’s thickness of gold, it stood for many years without fire ruling over it. How much more so Israel’s sinners, who are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate! For “Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate” may be read, “Even your empty ones are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate.” What then of

: “Come and see: first it says, ‘What are you doing here, Elijah?’ He answered, ‘I have been exceedingly zealous for the Lord…for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant.’ God told him: ‘By your life, wherever My children inscribe this holy mark in their flesh, you shall be present. The mouth that testified that Israel forsook the covenant shall testify that Israel fulfill it.’ We learned: why was Elijah punished before God? Because he spoke accusations against His children.”

k: volume-i|1634|0|Gloss in Nefesh HaChayim, Gate I 12:9–10
quote: Parallel: Gloss in Nefesh HaChayim, Gate I 12:9–10: “The measure of good is greater, by an immense difference and advantage: the radiance and added holiness produced by a person’s good deeds endure eternally, and his soul delights in them with everlasting pleasure. But the forces of impurity and destructive beings created and multiplied by his sins die and perish of themselves after he has received the entire punishment allotted to him. Their very vitality comes only from the damage of sin and the destruction he caused in the holy powers and worlds. From this they receive a flow of vitality and a little light through crooked channels, as in ‘I shall be filled from her devastation.’ Once he has undergone judgment through them, ‘He swallowed wealth and shall vomit it out’: their vitality is automatically cut off, and they perish of themselves. This is why Gehinnom is called a leech. A leech draws out the bad blood and immediately dies from it; so it is with Gehinnom, as explained.”

: “In the Jerusalem Talmud we read: Rabbi Chaggai said, 'Sabbaths and festivals were given only for eating and drinking.' Rabbi Berechyah said, 'They were given only to occupy oneself with Torah.' Tanchuma explains that they do not disagree. Rabbi Berechyah’s statement about Torah study concerns laborers, who work throughout the week and come on Shabbat to study Torah. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement about enjoyment concerns Torah scholars, who labor in Torah throughout the week and enjoy themselves on Shabbat. As for Rava’s statement that everyone agrees Shabbat requires an element 'for you,' as explained in section 242: one may answer that he addresses Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua; alternatively, there he requires some enjoyment, whereas here the discussion concerns devoting the whole day to enjoyment.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “Those immersed in worldly affairs throughout the weekdays find their Shabbat delight in Torah study. Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, however, occupied himself with halakhic teaching, as Sotah 40 explains that everyone left him, for the masses desire aggadah. He therefore spoke to the scholars with whom he studied in the academy; for them, the main purpose is delight. This does not mean eating, drinking, and bodily pleasure. Shabbat 118 says 'one who delights the Sabbath,' rather than 'one who enjoys himself on Shabbat.' … Only on Shabbat, which resembles the World to Come, does the Zohar say concerning the second meal, 'Then you shall delight above the Lord'—above the Lord, literally, for at that time the Holy Ancient One is revealed. Elsewhere it explains 'above the Lord' as the place concerning which 'from nothing' is said. This means above the name Havayah, which begins with wisdom, as explained.”
: “Then you will delight in Hashem. I will have you ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for Hashem’s mouth has spoken.”
: “Moses led Israel onward from the Sea of Reeds. They went out into the wilderness of Shur and traveled three days in the wilderness without finding water.”

: “‘They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.’ Water means Torah, as it says, ‘Everyone who thirsts, come to the water.’ Rabbi Yeisa asked: who had given them Torah here? The Torah had not yet been given to them. Rabbi Eleazar answered: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”
: “He cried out to Hashem, and Hashem showed him a tree. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There He established a statute and an ordinance for them, and there He tested them.”

: “He said, “If you listen carefully to the voice of Hashem your God, do what is upright in His eyes, attend to His commandments, and observe all His statutes, I will place upon you none of the illnesses I placed upon Egypt, for I am Hashem, your healer.””

: “But for one guilty of profaning the Name, repentance alone cannot suspend punishment, nor can Yom Kippur atone, nor sufferings purge it. Rather, all of them together suspend punishment, and death purges it, as it says, “Hashem of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: This wrongdoing will not be atoned for you until you die.””

k: volume-i|1641|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “The holy Ari teaches that the portions of Shovavim are a time for repairing damage to the covenant: the sequence extends through ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave.’ We have already explained that this damage brings enslavement. Canaan, who resulted from Ham’s violation of the covenant in the ark, was cursed to slavery. Thus ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ concerns one whose damage brought him to be sold as a slave; nevertheless, ‘in the seventh he shall go free’—he can be repaired through the holiness of the lower Sabbath.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””

: “Rabbi Yose taught: in the very event in which judgment was found for the Egyptians, mercy was found for Israel, as in ‘I shall see the blood and pass over you.’ Likewise, in all the holy crowns above, where judgment is found, mercy is found, all at the same moment. Rabbi Chizkiyah taught: ‘The Lord shall strike Egypt, striking and healing’—striking Egypt and healing Israel. What is the healing? Having been circumcised, they needed healing.”
: “He will bring back upon you all the illnesses of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.”

: “Another interpretation of ‘Guard my soul, for I am pious’: why? So that I may show kindness to Ani, ‘I,’ of which ‘Ani and Vahu’ are said. Woe to one who separates ‘I’ from ‘He,’ as in ‘He made us, and not we ourselves.’ All is one, without separation: ‘See now that I, I am He; I cause death and give life, I wound and I heal, and none rescues from My hand.’ ‘I am the Lord’: I am He and no other. This Ani comes from Adonai; the Name yod-he-vav-he is the middle pillar.”
: “I have seen his ways, and I will heal him. I will guide him and restore comfort to him and to those who mourn for him.”

: “These verses are written in the passage 'The righteous one has perished,' which concerns the blemish of the covenant throughout. Thus 'Those who slaughter the children' is expounded in Niddah 13 concerning this blemish. The passage concludes, 'For the spirit would faint before Me, and the souls I made,' which is expounded there to mean that the son of David will not come until all the souls in the body have been exhausted. This entire Torah portion likewise discusses rectification of the covenant’s blemish.”

: “Come and see: ‘He went waywardly in the path of his heart.’ Immediately afterward, ‘I have seen his ways and shall heal him; I shall guide him and restore consolations to him and his mourners.’ ‘He went waywardly’: although the wicked deliberately do whatever they do, following their hearts, and although others warn them and they refuse to listen, when they return in repentance and take its good path, healing stands ready to meet them.”
: “Because of the sin of his greed I became angry and struck him; I hid Myself and was angry, yet he went on waywardly along the path of his heart.”
: “Now go; lead the people to the place I told you. My angel will go before you, but on the day I call them to account, I will call them to account for their sin.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 11:1: “The principal healing, the healing of the soul, certainly comes through words of Torah, as it says, ‘Healing for all his flesh’; this concerns the past. Deliverance from the evil inclination for the future also comes through Torah, as Zohar I, 202a, says: nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. Sometimes healing comes through Torah conveyed by a reprover who brings words of Torah into the heart, so that the person returns in repentance and is healed. Some sins, however, cannot be healed through Torah conveyed by an emissary, but only by God Himself. Although the principal repairing Torah is the Oral Torah—the abundant wisdom that repairs abundant anger—and comes through a teacher, when Torah illuminates the heart until the very name of God shines there, as in ‘Though I sit in darkness, God is a light for me,’ it is called healing by God Himself. That illness never returns. Bodily suffering likewise comes through sin, as Shabbat 55a says, ‘There is no suffering without iniquity.’ When the sin is repaired, the bodily suffering also receives lasting healing. This is ‘Heal me, God, and I shall be healed.’ Deliverance for the future can likewise come through Torah learned from a teacher, and is called deliverance through an emissary. It can sometimes be reversed: it is no greater than the giving of the Torah, of which it says, ‘I said, you are divine’—they would not die, as Avodah Zarah 5a explains. They were free from the angel of dea

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”
: “When you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years; in the seventh he shall go free without payment.”

: “In an individual case, however, someone may become corrupted and need to be sold as a slave to rectify this blemish. Of him it says, 'When you acquire...' and 'In the seventh year he shall go free': he has rectification through the aspect of the sabbatical year, the lower Sabbath. Even someone so deeply submerged that he says, 'I love my wife...' nevertheless has rectification through the jubilee, the higher Sabbath, the great shofar: 'Those cast away in the land of Egypt shall come.' Even those submerged in Egypt’s shell, the nakedness of the land, will have repentance awakened in their hearts through the great shofar, the aspect of the higher Sabbath, the jubilee.”
: “But if the servant insists, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go free,””

: “Rabbi Abba said: happy is Israel’s portion, for God brought them out of Egypt to be His portion and inheritance. Come and see: Israel’s freedom was found from the side of Jubilee. So it will be in the future: ‘On that day a great shofar shall be sounded,’ and so forth.”
: “On that day a great shofar will be sounded. Those lost in the land of Assyria and those cast away in the land of Egypt will come and bow down to Hashem on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.”

: “Someone who bought produce from a person not trusted regarding tithes, and forgot to tithe it, may ask him on Shabbat and eat on his assurance. After Shabbat has ended, he may not eat until he tithes. … The companions said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: They permitted this in honor of Shabbat. If it is because of Shabbat’s honor, why must he ask? To create a basis for the permission. Rabbi Bibi said in Rabbi Hanina’s name: The awe of Shabbat rests upon him, so he tells the truth. If the awe of Shabbat rests upon him, why does the Mishnah say that once Shabbat ends he may not eat until he tithes? Because there may be someone upon whom the awe of Shabbat does not rest. A baraita teaches: If he asks on a weekday, he may not eat on Shabbat. This fits the view that the awe of Shabbat rests upon him. According to the view that permission is given for Shabbat’s honor, however, even if he asked on a weekday, he should be able to eat on Shabbat.”

: ““Happy is the man who fears Hashem.” Is a man happy, but a woman not? Rav Amram said in Rav’s name: Happy is one who repents while still a man in his strength. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Happy is one who masters his inclination like a man.”

: “Rava often said: Wisdom’s purpose is repentance and good deeds. A person must not read Scripture and study Mishnah while rebelling against his father, his mother, his teacher, or someone greater than he in wisdom and seniority, as it says, “The beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem; good understanding belongs to all who practice them.” It does not merely say “those who practice,” but “those who practice them”: those who act for its own sake, rather than those who do not. Whoever acts otherwise would have been better off not having been created.”

Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:11:2: ““One who acts not for its own sake would have been better off not having been created”: this means that he does not learn in order to fulfill the teaching, but in order to provoke. For in the chapter Makom Shenahagu, Rava contrasts “Your kindness reaches to the heavens” with “Your kindness is above the heavens,” distinguishing learning not for its own sake from learning for its own sake. That passage concerns someone who fulfills the teaching in order to receive honor. This also appears from the Jerusalem Talmud on our chapter.”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”
: “When a shofar is sounded in a city, do the people not tremble? Can calamity occur in a city unless Hashem has brought it about?”
: “Be watchful concerning everything I have told you. Do not mention the name of other gods; let it not be heard from your mouth.”

: “Concerning Torah, where “truth” is written—as in “Acquire truth and do not sell it”—the Holy One, blessed be He, does not go beyond the strict line of judgment. Concerning judgment, where “truth” is not written, the Holy One, blessed be He, does go beyond the strict line of judgment.”

: “Rav Yosef said, and Rabbi Chiya likewise taught: Since the Temple was destroyed, although the Sanhedrin ceased, the four forms of execution have not ceased. Have they not ceased? Surely they have. Rather, their punitive equivalents have not ceased. One liable to stoning either falls from a roof or is trampled by a wild beast. One liable to burning either falls into a fire or is bitten by a snake. One liable to the sword is either delivered to the authorities or attacked by bandits. One liable to strangulation either drowns in a river or dies from an obstructing throat illness.”

: “Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not exact punishment from a nation until its time of dismissal, as it says, “In measure, when You send her away.” Is that so? Rava said: Why are three cups mentioned concerning Egypt? One is what it drank in Moses’ days, one in Pharaoh Necho’s days, and one it will drink with its companions in the future. Could those earlier Egyptians have disappeared and these be different people? Rabbi Yehuda taught: Minyamin, an Egyptian convert, was my fellow student of Rabbi Akiva. Minyamin said: I am a first-generation Egyptian convert and married a first-generation Egyptian woman. I will marry my son to a second-generation Egyptian woman, so that my grandson may enter the congregation. Rather, if the teaching was stated, it was stated thus: Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, does not exact punishment from a king until his time of dismissal, as it says, “In measure, when You send her away, You contend with her.””
: “For Hashem reproves the one He loves, like a father the son whom he favors.”
: “One who withholds his rod hates his son, but one who loves him is diligent in disciplining him.”
: “I had heard of You through the hearing of the ear, but now my eye has seen You.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What is meant by “For You are our Father; Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us; You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old is Your Name”? In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to Abraham: Your children have sinned against Me. He will answer: Master of the world, let them be wiped out for the sanctity of Your Name. God will say: I will tell Jacob, who suffered the hardship of raising children; perhaps he will ask mercy for them. He will say: Your children have sinned. Jacob will answer: Master of the world, let them be wiped out for the sanctity of Your Name. God will say: There is no reasoning among the elders and no counsel among the younger. He will say to Isaac: Your children have sinned against Me. Isaac will answer: Master of the world, are they my children and not Your children? When they put “We will do” before “We will hear,” You called them “My firstborn son”; now are they my children and not Yours? Moreover, how much have they sinned? A person’s years are seventy. Remove twenty for which You do not punish, leaving fifty. Remove twenty-five for the nights, leaving twenty-five. Remove twelve and a half for prayer, eating, and bodily needs, leaving twelve and a half. If You bear all of them, well and good; if not, half upon me and half upon You. And if You say that all must be upon me, I offered myself before You. They will begin saying, “For you are our father.” Isaac
: “Listen, daughter, consider and incline your ear; forget your people and your father’s house.”
: “When you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years; in the seventh he shall go free without payment.”

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. : “His master shall bring him before the judges and bring him to the door or doorpost. His master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him permanently.”

: “Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai interpreted this passage like an ornamental jewel: Why was the ear singled out from all the body’s limbs? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The ear heard My voice at Mount Sinai when I said, “For the children of Israel are My servants”—My servants, not servants of servants. Yet this man went and acquired a master for himself; let his ear be pierced. Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi interpreted the passage like an ornamental jewel: Why were the door and doorpost singled out from all the household’s furnishings? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The door and doorpost were witnesses in Egypt when I passed over the lintel and the two doorposts and said, “For the children of Israel are My servants”—My servants, not servants of servants. I brought them from slavery to freedom, yet this man went and acquired a master for himself; let his ear be pierced before them.”
: “For the Israelites are servants to Me; they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am Hashem your God.”
: “He took the book of the covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, “Everything Hashem has spoken we will do, and we will listen.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tavo 9:1: “The principal purpose of bringing first fruits is to show that a person nullifies himself and all his powers before their root. Hence it says, ‘You shall bow before the Lord your God.’ Bowing, as is known, involves spreading out hands and feet: complete self-nullification before God. Through this nullification, renewal also enters the heart. Every day a person becomes like a new creature, with renewed words of Torah. Thus it afterward says, ‘This day the Lord your God commands you to do,’ which Rashi explains as: every day they should be new in your eyes. Then comes ‘You have distinguished God today,’ likewise meaning every day. The Midrash therefore brings ‘Come, let us bow and bend the knee.’ It also refers to the continuation, ‘For He is our God and we are the people of His pasture,’ and ‘Today, if you hear His voice,’ again using ‘today.’ This certainly alludes to prayer. ‘Come, let us bow and bend the knee’ is also self-nullification before one’s root, pouring out one’s soul before God. Thus Berakhot 34b says that once a king bows, he does not straighten himself: his prayer brought such a revelation of Heaven’s kingship that he transcended bodily existence. From this, too, renewal arises in the heart each day. The verse therefore indicates that what first fruits accomplish is also accomplished through prayer. ‘For He is our God’ alludes to ‘You have distinguished God today to be your God’; ‘we are the people of His pasture’ alludes to

: “This yoke does not rest upon someone bound to another master. Therefore slaves are exempt from the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven. If they are exempt from this yoke, they are exempt from all the rest, for the rest does not rest upon a person until this yoke is with him. Therefore Israel ate in Egypt ‘for nothing.’ Here too, ‘He shall go out free, for nothing’: he had been a slave, and everything he did was ‘for nothing,’ without the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven. Although his deeds had been ‘for nothing,’ he shall go out free and have rest.”

: “His disciples asked Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai: Why did the Torah treat a secret thief more severely than an open robber? He answered: The robber treats a servant’s honor on the same footing as his Master’s; the thief does not. The thief acts as though the supernal eye did not see and the supernal ear did not hear, as it says, “Woe to those who hide their counsel deep from Hashem and do their deeds in darkness”; and, “They say: God does not see, the God of Jacob does not understand”; and, “They say: Hashem has abandoned the earth; Hashem does not see.””
: “But if the servant insists, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go free,””
: “Blessed is Hashem, God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, “Amen.” Hallelujah!”
: “For we must die, like water poured upon the ground that cannot be gathered up. Yet God does not take away a life, but devises means so that an outcast will not remain banished from Him.”
: “He drew near and kissed him. Isaac smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, saying, “See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.””
: “Open for me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them and give thanks to Yah.”

: “Thus it says, “He smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him,” and, “See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field blessed by Hashem.” He then perceived the fragrance of “his garments,” which the Midrash expounds regarding Yosef Meshita and Yakum Ish Tzerorot: read begadav, “his garments,” as bogdav, “his traitors,” as the Gemara also teaches. Even they possess a good fragrance. The Sages likewise say that the “bad figs” are the utterly wicked, yet both groups will ultimately give forth fragrance. This fragrance appears when “Your people are all righteous” becomes clear: whoever is circumcised is called righteous. Isaac, the first to be circumcised on the eighth day, perceived within Jacob that his offspring were already whole, all righteous. Hence “my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field blessed by Hashem,” from which upper, holy fragrances arise. As explained, fragrance indicates that the blemish has been repaired and one has attained the quality of the righteous person.”

: “As he traveled onward, he sat beside a spring to eat bread. He had salted fish, and as he rinsed them, a fragrance entered them. He said: This shows that this spring comes from the Garden of Eden. Some say he took some water and washed his face with it. Others say he followed it all the way to the entrance of the Garden of Eden and called out: Open the gate for me! They answered: “This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter it.””

: “The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining understanding. She took some of its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: The serpent began slandering its Creator. It said, ‘He ate from this tree and created the world. He tells you not to eat from it so that you will not create other worlds, for every craftsman hates a rival in his trade.’”
: “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, “Where are you?””

: “‘The Lord God called to the man’: ‘What has become of you? Yesterday you followed My will; now you follow the serpent’s will. Yesterday you extended from one end of the world to the other; now you are hiding among the trees of the garden.’”

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: Adam was a heretic, as it says, “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, Where are you?”—where has your heart turned? R. Isaac said: He drew his foreskin forward. Here it says, “Like Adam, they transgressed the covenant,” and elsewhere it says, “He has broken My covenant.””

: “This is the course followed by a gathering of wicked scoffers. At first they multiply empty talk, as it says, 'A fool’s voice comes through many words.' From there they come to disparage the righteous, as it says, 'Let lying lips be silenced, which speak arrogantly against the righteous.' They then become accustomed to speaking against the prophets and finding fault with their words, as it says, 'They mocked God’s messengers, despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets.' From there they come to speak against God and deny the fundamental principle, as it says, 'The children of Israel concealed improper things against the Lord their God.' It also says, 'They set their mouths against heaven, while their tongue walks through the earth.' What caused them to set their mouths against heaven? Their tongue, which first walked through the earth.”

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: Adam was a heretic, as it says, “Hashem God called to the human being and said to him, Where are you?”—where has your heart turned? R. Isaac said: He drew his foreskin forward. Here it says, “Like Adam, they transgressed the covenant,” and elsewhere it says, “He has broken My covenant.””

: “Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: During all the years that Adam was under ban, he fathered spirits, demons, and night-demons, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image.” This implies that before then he did not father beings in his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say: Adam was a great pious man. When he saw that death had been decreed through him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and placed a girdle of fig leaves upon his body for one hundred and thirty years. The earlier statement concerns semen that he emitted involuntarily.”
: “He drove the human being out, and stationed east of the Garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the ever-turning sword, to guard the way to the Tree of Life.”

: “What does keruv mean? Rabbi Abbahu said: Like a child, for in Babylonia a child is called ravya. Rav Pappa asked Abaye: But the verse lists “the first face, a cherub’s face; the second, a human face; the third, a lion’s face; the fourth, an eagle’s face.” Is a cherub’s face not the same as a human face? One is a large face, and the other a small face.”
: “When Israel was a youth, I loved him, and from Egypt I called My son.”

: “Hashem smelled the pleasing fragrance. Hashem said in His heart, “I will not again curse the ground because of humanity, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I again strike down every living thing as I have done.””

: “The Rabbis explained another secret: the generation that departs is the generation that comes; one who went lame returns lame, one who went blind returns blind. They also explained that Moses was to receive the Torah in the generation of the Flood, but they were wicked. Thus ‘Inasmuch as he is flesh’: beshaggam corresponds to Moses. Why call him beshaggam? Ecclesiastes omitted the bet to conceal the matter, saying, ‘I said that this too—shegam—is vanity,’ Hevel.”

: “Go and call out in Jerusalem’s hearing: Thus says Hashem: I remember for you the devotion of your youth, the love of your bridal days, when you followed Me into the wilderness, into an unsown land.”
: “Let a slanderer find no stability in the land; let evil hunt down a violent man, blow after blow.”
: “Say of the righteous that it will be good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.”
: “See: today I have set before you life and goodness, death and evil.”

: “Rabbi Yaakov, the son of Yaakov’s daughter, said: Anyone through whom another person is punished is not admitted into the presence of the Holy One, blessed be He. ... Rather, the proof comes from this verse: “Even punishment for the righteous is not good.” “Not good” means evil, and it is written, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You.” You are righteous, Lord, and evil will not dwell in Your dwelling.”
: “Reish Lakish said: What does “This shall be the law of the afflicted person” mean? This shall be the law of the person who gives another a bad name.”
: “This shall be the law of the person afflicted with tzaraat on the day of his purification: he shall be brought to the priest.”
: “Let the devoted rejoice in honor and sing joyfully upon their beds. The exaltation of God is in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand.”
: “This shall be the law of the person afflicted with tzaraat on the day of his purification: he shall be brought to the priest.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: What remedy is there for those who speak maliciously? If he is a Torah scholar, he should occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “A healing tongue is a tree of life.” “Tongue” refers to malicious speech, as it says, “Their tongue is a slaughtering arrow”; and “tree” refers to Torah, as it says, “It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it.” If he is unlearned, he should humble himself, as it says, “But perversity in it breaks the spirit.” Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Chanina says: Once he has spoken maliciously, he has no remedy, for David has already cut him off through the holy spirit: “May Hashem cut off all smooth lips, the tongue that speaks arrogantly.” Rather, what remedy prevents him from coming to malicious speech? A Torah scholar should occupy himself with Torah; an unlearned person should humble himself, as it says, “But perversity in it breaks the spirit.””

: “Rabbi Chiya taught: Whoever occupies himself with Torah at night has the Divine Presence opposite him, as it says, “Rise, sing at night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord…””

: “Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish differed. Rabbi Yochanan said: Torah’s song is only at night, as it says, “Rise, sing at night.” Reish Lakish said: By day and by night, as it says, “You shall meditate upon it day and night.” Reish Lakish would explain verses, and when he reached, “She rises while it is still night,” and, “Rise, sing at night,” he would say: Rabbi Yochanan taught me well. Then he would say: Do you not see how brightly my learning shines upon my face? Why? Because it is by night and by day.”

: “Rabbi Shefatya said in Rabbi Yoḥanan’s name: Of one who reads Scripture without melody and studies without song, Scripture says, “I also gave them statutes that were not good.” Abaye objected: Because he does not know how to make his voice pleasant, do you apply to him “laws by which they cannot live”? Rather, interpret the verse as Rav Mesharshiya did: Of two Torah scholars living in the same town who do not treat one another agreeably in matters of halakhah, Scripture says, “I also gave them statutes that were not good, and laws by which they could not live.””
: ““One who studies without song”: They customarily recited the Mishnayot with a melody, because they learned them by heart, and this helped them remember them better.”

: “Rav Yosef said in Rav Yehuda’s name, in Shmuel’s name: The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Abaye said to him: Saying that the halakha follows him implies that others dispute his ruling. Rav Yosef said to him: What practical difference does that make to you? Abaye replied: Should one learn a tradition as though it were merely a song?”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a two-edged sword, as it says, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” How does the verse indicate this? Mar Zutra—or, according to another report, Rav Ashi—said: From the beginning of the passage, “Let the devoted rejoice in honor; let them sing upon their beds,” followed by, “God’s exalted praises are in their throats, and a two-edged sword in their hands.” Rabbi Yitzchak also said: Whoever recites Shema upon his bed keeps destructive forces away, as it says, “The sons of reshef fly high.” “Flight” refers to Torah, as in, “Will you let your eyes fly toward it, and it is gone?” “Reshef” refers to destructive forces, as in, “Exhausted by hunger and devoured by reshef and bitter destruction.””

ref: Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sermons on the Night Ritual 9:2
quote: : “It is known that if a person sometimes sins, Heaven forbid, by wasting his seed, whether intentionally or involuntarily, harmful beings, demons and spirits are created from those drops. The bedtime Shema becomes a sword and kills them. Of these kinds of demons and harmful beings the Sages said, regarding ‘a double-edged sword in their hand,’ that the bedtime Shema kills a great number of them. This accords with the Zohar’s explanation of ‘He will not lie down until he devours prey.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeshev 8:1: “When Joseph descended to Egypt, he needed to repair the sin of the evil report he had spoken about his brothers. Arakhin 15b says that one who speaks maliciously magnifies sins corresponding to the three transgressions of idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed. This gave Potiphar’s wife power to assail him: he had not yet repaired his wrongful speech, since he thought he had properly reported his brothers to their father so that he would rebuke them. At that moment, before this corruption of speech was repaired, Jacob truthfully said, ‘An evil beast has devoured him,’ referring to the serpent, called an evil beast. The root of the serpent’s corruption is envy, desire, and honor, from which idolatry, sexual transgression, and bloodshed branch out; malicious speech magnifies sins corresponding to all three. This is ‘Joseph has surely been torn’: he had stumbled through the evil report about his brothers. The brothers, knowing themselves innocent, suspected that Joseph was condemning others for his own defect. They thought he himself was flawed, and therefore sold him as a slave. He had thus caused his brothers also to speak maliciously about him: ‘Joseph has surely been torn.’ The Midrash Rabbah says that holy inspiration flashed within Jacob, and ‘an evil beast’ referred to Potiphar’s wife. Joseph’s failure to repent of his wrongful speech gave her power to assail him, because the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the
: “To carry out vengeance among the nations and rebuke among the peoples.”
: “Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone afflicted with tzaraat, everyone with a discharge, and everyone made impure through contact with a corpse.”

: “Come and hear how we explained in the teaching: Lot’s two daughters are the two bodily powers that stir the evil inclination. Now that it is not so defiled and has immersed from its filth, it is called Laban; those two daughters are not actually abolished. Thus ‘Laban had two daughters.’”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “How do we know that Ishmael repented during Abraham’s lifetime? Ravina and Rav Chama bar Buzi were sitting before Rava while he dozed. Ravina asked Rav Chama bar Buzi: Is it indeed your teaching that every death described as “expiring” is the death of a righteous person? He answered: Yes. But what of the generation of the Flood? He answered: We mean where both “expiring” and “being gathered” are written. But both expressions are written of Ishmael! Meanwhile Rava awoke and told them: “Young students, Rabbi Yochanan said this: Ishmael repented during his father’s lifetime, as it says, ‘Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him.’” Perhaps they are listed according to their wisdom? If so, why does “Esau and Jacob his sons buried him” not list them according to their wisdom? Rather, Ishmael’s allowing Isaac to precede him shows that he accepted Isaac’s leadership; this shows that he repented during Abraham’s lifetime.”

: “The house of Jacob will be fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau straw. They will ignite them and consume them; no survivor will remain of the house of Esau, for Hashem has spoken.”
: “A thousand may fall beside you, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not approach you.”
: “Saul became very angry, and the matter displeased him. He said, “They have assigned David tens of thousands, but me only thousands. What more does he lack except the kingship?””

: “‘The same words’: they spoke sharp words against ‘The Lord our God, the Lord is One,’ and against ‘Abraham was one man in the land.’ They said, ‘Abraham is a barren mule; he cannot produce offspring.’ Of the Lord our God they said, ‘He has no right to choose the upper realms for Himself and give us the lower realms! Come, let us build a tower, place an idol on its top, and put a sword in its hand, so that it will appear to wage war against Him.’”

: “Thus Scripture says, “For I know the thoughts that I think concerning you: thoughts of peace and not evil, to give you an end and a hope.” The Sages interpret this as palm trees and flax garments. The meaning is that Babylonian exile was where the Oral Torah was principally established through the Men of the Great Assembly. The same continued in later generations. The Gemara says, “What you say is theirs,” and that, when Torah was forgotten in Israel, Ezra ascended from Babylonia and established it; later Hillel the Babylonian established it, and Rabbi Chiyya and his sons ascended and established it. In the Amoraic period came the Babylonian Talmud, the principal Oral Torah that we possess. Thus the Midrash says, “She raised up more righteous people for Me in her destruction than in her building.” This is the good that comes at the end.”
: “Pharaoh commanded all his people: “Every newborn boy you shall throw into the Nile, but every girl you shall keep alive.””

: “The explanation follows what was said above. These souls had sunk into the kelippot among the Egyptians. Because they first sinned in the generation of the Flood by wasting seed, and were therefore dissolved in the Flood’s boiling waters, Pharaoh now likewise decreed, ‘Every newborn son you shall cast into the Nile.’ The decree concerned males, who had committed this sin, rather than females. Corresponding to their sin in the generation of the Dispersion—‘Come, let us make bricks and burn them,’ to build the city and tower, rise up, deny the divine foundation and wage war against Him—‘Come, let us deal wisely with him’ now answered ‘Come, let us make bricks.’ ‘They embittered their lives,’ building Pithom and Raamses, corresponded to that city and tower.”
: “He drove the human being out, and stationed east of the Garden of Eden the cherubim and the flame of the ever-turning sword, to guard the way to the Tree of Life.”

: “If he merits more, he is given a nefesh through Atzilut, from the side of the only daughter, called the king’s daughter. If he merits more, he is given a ruach of Atzilut from the middle pillar’s side, and is called God’s son: ‘You are children of the Lord your God.’ If he merits more, he is given a neshamah from Father and Mother, as in ‘He breathed into his nostrils a soul of life.’ What is life? Yod-he, of which it says, ‘Let every soul praise Yah.’ Through him the divine Name is completed.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak taught: ‘A mother of children rejoicing, hallelujah.’ The Mother is known; who are the children? Rabbi Shimon said: we learned that God has two children, male and female. He gave the male to Jacob: ‘My firstborn son, Israel,’ and ‘Israel, in whom I glory.’ The daughter He gave to Abraham: ‘The Lord blessed Abraham with All.’ Abraham had a daughter named Bakol.”
: “He said to me, “You are My servant, Israel, through whom I will display My glory.””
: “Abraham was old, advanced in years, and Hashem had blessed Abraham in everything.”

: “It is written, “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says, “One who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.””
: “A loving doe, a graceful mountain-goat: let her breasts satisfy you at all times; be ever absorbed in her love.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said: What is meant by “A beloved doe and a graceful mountain goat”? Why are words of Torah compared to a doe? Just as a doe has a narrow womb and is beloved to her mate each time as at the first, so words of Torah are beloved to those who learn them each time as at the first. “A graceful mountain goat”—Torah brings grace upon its students. “May her breasts satisfy you at all times”—why are words of Torah compared to a breast? Just as whenever an infant handles the breast, it finds milk, so whenever a person studies words of Torah, he finds flavor in them.”
: “The human soul is Hashem’s lamp, searching all the innermost chambers.”

: “A lamp burns above the unborn child’s head, and the child gazes from one end of the world to the other, as it says, “When His lamp shone above my head, by His light I walked through darkness.” Do not find this astonishing: A person sleeps here and sees a dream in Spain. No days offer a person greater well-being than those days, as it says, “If only I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me.” Which days are measured in months but not in years? The months of pregnancy.”

: “Antoninus also said to Rabbi: From when does the evil inclination control a person—from the moment he is formed, or from the moment he emerges? He answered: From the moment he is formed. Antoninus said: If so, he would kick his way out of his mother’s womb! Rather, it begins when he emerges. Rabbi said: Antoninus taught me this, and Scripture supports him, as it says, “Sin crouches at the entrance.””
: “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it separates into four headwaters.”

: “For six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce. In the seventh, let it rest and leave it untended, so that the poor of your people may eat; what they leave, the wild animals shall eat. Do the same with your vineyard and olive grove. For six days do your work, but on the seventh day cease, so that your ox and donkey may rest, and your maidservant’s son and the stranger may be refreshed.”

: “'On the seventh day you shall rest': even in the seventh year, the Sabbath commemorating creation must not be displaced. Do not say that since the whole year is called a sabbath, the weekly Sabbath need not be observed during it. 'So that your ox and donkey may rest': give it repose, permitting it to pluck grass from the ground and eat. Or does this mean you should confine it inside the house? That would be distress, not rest. 'The son of your maidservant': Scripture speaks of an uncircumcised slave. 'And the stranger': a resident alien.”

: ““Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and donkey may rest, and your maidservant’s son and the stranger may be refreshed.” “Six days you shall do your work.” The weekly Shabbat is stated here in connection with the sabbatical year so that the weekly Shabbat will not be displaced from its established position.”

: ““Be mindful of everything I have told you.” Why is this said? Since it says, “You shall not perform any labor, you, your son, or your daughter,” I know only matters classified as labor. How do I include matters classified as cessation from work? Scripture says, “Be mindful of everything I have told you,” including matters classified as cessation from work.”

: “‘In all that I have said to you, you shall be guarded.’ Why tishameru, ‘be guarded,’ rather than tishmeru, ‘guard’? Precisely ‘be guarded.’ ‘All that I have said’ means the assurance I have given you concerning My service: you shall be guarded so that no evil reaches you, through My protection alone. ‘Do not mention the name of other gods’ is as explained. Another interpretation: do not bring about your falling among the nations in a foreign land, so that ‘There you shall serve other gods’ is fulfilled in you.”
: “Guard My charge, so as not to practice the abominable customs practiced before you, and do not become impure through them. I am Hashem your God.”

: “Rav Kahana derives it from “You shall safeguard My charge”: Make a safeguard for My charge. Abaye asked Rav Yosef: Does that not make the prohibition biblical? He replied: It is biblical, and the Sages explained it. But the Sages explained the whole Torah! Rather, it is rabbinic, and the verse is merely a supporting allusion.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “Therefore Shabbat is equal to Torah, and whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah. Thus ‘Happy is the person who does this, and the human being who holds fast to it: guarding Shabbat from profaning it, and guarding his hand from doing any evil.’ It follows that one who guards Shabbat is like one who guards the entire Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yoḥanan again found Reish Lakish’s child sitting and reciting, “A person’s folly distorts his way, and his heart rages against Hashem.” Rabbi Yoḥanan sat in astonishment and said: Can anything be written in the Writings without being alluded to in the Torah? The child replied: Is this not alluded to? It says, “Their hearts failed, and they trembled, saying to one another: What is this that God has done to us?””

: “But we learned that the Passover offering and circumcision are positive commandments. Must this disagree with Rabbi Akiva? For if it follows Rabbi Akiva, who applies this statute to Passover, there should also be a negative commandment, as Rabbi Avin said in Rabbi Ilaai’s name: Wherever “Take care,” “lest,” or “do not” is stated, it denotes a negative commandment. The Mishnah may follow Rabbi Akiva: “Take care” attached to a negative commandment is negative, while “take care” attached to a positive commandment is positive.”

: “Rav Adda bar Ahavah said: Women are obligated by Torah law to sanctify Shabbat in Kiddush. Why? It is a positive commandment dependent upon time, from which women are generally exempt. Abaye answered: Their obligation is rabbinic. Rava told him: But he said “by Torah law.” Moreover, by that reasoning let us impose every time-dependent positive commandment upon them rabbinically. Rather, Rava said: Scripture says “Remember” and “Observe.” Whoever is included in observing Shabbat is included in remembering it; since women are included in its prohibitions, they are included in Kiddush.”

: “‘In all that I have said to you, you shall be guarded.’ Why tishameru, ‘be guarded,’ rather than tishmeru, ‘guard’? Precisely ‘be guarded.’ ‘All that I have said’ means the assurance I have given you concerning My service: you shall be guarded so that no evil reaches you, through My protection alone. ‘Do not mention the name of other gods’ is as explained. Another interpretation: do not bring about your falling among the nations in a foreign land, so that ‘There you shall serve other gods’ is fulfilled in you.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” followed by “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed. For it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Sabbaths,” and afterward, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.””

: “Hashem said to Moses: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you. Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people. Work may be done for six days, but on the seventh day there is complete rest, holy to Hashem; whoever performs work on the Shabbat day shall be put to death. The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant. It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.””

: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done. Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day shall be holy for you, a Shabbat of complete rest for Hashem. Whoever performs work on it shall be put to death. Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbat day.””
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “A baraita teaches: They said of Shammai the Elder that throughout his life he ate in honor of Shabbat. If he found a fine animal, he said, “This is for Shabbat.” If he found a finer one, he reserved the second and ate the first. Hillel the Elder followed another measure, for all his deeds were for Heaven’s sake, as it says, “Blessed is Hashem, day by day.” A baraita likewise teaches: Beit Shammai say, “From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat”; Beit Hillel say, “Blessed is Hashem, day by day.””

: “Come and see: when all the craftsmen began their craftsmanship, the very work they began completed itself. They began, and it completed the work—actually itself. How do we know? ‘All the work of the Tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed.’”
: “All the work of the Tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything exactly as Hashem had commanded Moses; so they did.”
: “Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day is a Shabbat of complete rest, a sacred assembly. You shall do no work; it is a Shabbat for Hashem in all your dwellings.”

: “I can explain both my reasoning and yours.
