Your reasoning is this: Shabbat is already fixed and established, so both in prayer and in Kiddush one says, “Who sanctifies Shabbat.” A festival is established by Israel, who intercalate the months and determine the years, so one says, “Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.””

: “Rava bar Mehasya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: A person who gives a gift to another must inform him, as it says, “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” A baraita likewise teaches: “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: I have a fine gift in My treasure house, and its name is Shabbat. I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them. From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: One who gives a child bread must inform the child’s mother.”

: “Someone who conducts himself according to medicine, intending only that his whole body and its limbs be healthy and that his children perform his work and labor for his needs, does not follow a good path. Rather, he should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul may be upright in knowing God. A person cannot understand and contemplate wisdom when hungry or ill, or when one of his limbs hurts. He should intend to have a child who may become wise and great in Israel. A person who follows this path serves God constantly throughout his life, even while doing business or having marital relations, because his purpose in everything is to obtain his needs so that his body may be healthy enough to serve God. Even when sleeping, if he deliberately sleeps to rest his mind and body, lest he become ill and unable to serve God while ill, his sleep itself becomes service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this the sages commanded, 'Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.' Solomon likewise said in his wisdom, 'Know Him in all your ways, and He will straighten your paths.'”

: “A person must subject all the faculties of his soul to reason, as we explained in the preceding chapter. He should always place before himself one goal: apprehending God, blessed be He, to the extent human beings can know Him. He should direct all his actions—his movements, his rest, and everything he says—toward this goal, so that none of his actions is purposeless, meaning an action that does not lead toward this goal. For example, he should intend his eating, drinking, sexual relations, sleeping, waking, movement, and rest solely for his body’s health. His intention in maintaining bodily health should be that the soul finds its instruments healthy and sound, enabling it to acquire knowledge and the virtues of character and intellect until it reaches that goal.”

: “They again sat and asked: The Mishnah teaches that the principal categories of labor are forty minus one. To what do they correspond? Rabbi Hanina bar Hama said: To the labors of the Tabernacle. Rabbi Yonatan, son of Rabbi Elazar, said: Thus said Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Yose ben Lakonya: To the forty-minus-one appearances of “labor,” “his labor,” and “the labor of” in the Torah. Rav Yosef asked: Is “He came into the house to do his work” included in the count? Abaye said: Let them bring a Torah scroll and count! Did Rabba bar bar Hana not say in Rabbi Yohanan’s name that they did not leave until they brought a Torah scroll and counted them? Rav Yosef answered: My uncertainty concerns “The labor was sufficient.” Is that included, following the view that Joseph entered to satisfy his own desire? Or is “He came into the house to do his work” included, while “The labor was sufficient” merely means that their work had been completed? The question remained unresolved.”
: “By Hashem’s word the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their hosts.”

: “Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Even someone praying alone on Friday evening must recite “The heavens and the earth were completed.” For Rav Hamnuna said: Whoever prays on Friday evening and recites this passage is regarded by Scripture as though he became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation. It says vaykhullu, “were completed”; read it as vaykhallu, “they completed.” Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we learn that speech is comparable to action? From “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.””

: “It was stated: If someone muzzles an animal by his voice, or drives a mixed team by his voice, Rabbi Yochanan holds him liable, whereas Reish Lakish exempts him. Rabbi Yochanan holds him liable because moving his mouth constitutes an action; Reish Lakish exempts him because a voice does not constitute an action.”
: “For a human being is born to toil, just as sparks rise upward in flight.”

: “R. Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “A human being is born to toil.” I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or for manual labor. When it says, “For his mouth compels him,” you must conclude that he was created for toil of the mouth. But I still do not know whether this means toil in Torah or toil in conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must conclude that he was created for toil in Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies must labor; fortunate is the one who merits laboring in Torah.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 99b:2:1: ““Burdened with toil”—that is, all bodies were created for labor.”

: “Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer, as it says, “Isaac went out to converse in the field toward evening.” “Conversation” means prayer, as it says, “A prayer of the afflicted when he is overwhelmed and pours out his conversation before Hashem.””

: “This is the receiving of reward on Shabbat, which resembles the World to Come, for one’s actual deeds during the six weekdays. All the World to Come’s pleasure is enjoyment of the radiance of the Divine Presence, as stated in the end of Berakhot 17a, and likewise for those who merit tasting on Shabbat one-sixtieth of the World to Come. This was the sages’ blessing to Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Chanina: 'May you see your world in your lifetime.' Certainly this refers to Shabbat, when one can attain a foretaste of the World to Come through enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence. Each person’s attainment of repose on the coming Shabbat, through resting from that labor, corresponds to his labor during the weekdays.”

: “He commanded us to rest on Shabbat, as the exalted One said, 'On the seventh day you shall rest.' This commandment is repeated, explaining that ceasing from labor is obligatory for us, our animals, and our slaves. The laws of this commandment are explained in the tractates Shabbat and Yom Tov.”

: ““He knew of Shabbat through the limits on travel.” It cannot mean that he knew it through Issi’s ruling, since that labor also incurs a sin-offering, as I explained in the first chapter, 6b. Ri finds this difficult: Why does the Gemara not say that he knew of Shabbat through its positive commandment? For it is written, “On the seventh day you shall cease,” and it is also written, “You shall observe the Sabbath.””

k: volume-i|1760|0|Teaching of Rav Tzadok’s teacher, report
quote: : “Rambam counts resting on Shabbat as a positive commandment. Tosafot on Shabbat likewise asks why the Gemara does not say that a person knew about Shabbat’s positive commandment, and cites this verse. Our holy master answered Tosafot’s question that, regarding Shabbat, there is no such positive commandment. The positive commandment to rest applies to a festival: since Israel sanctifies it, an active positive command is appropriate. Shabbat, however, is fixed and enduring. Indeed, the Gemara mentions a positive and negative commandment together only regarding a festival. We have proofs of this, as explained elsewhere.”

: “'So that your ox and donkey may rest': since lema’an means 'in order that,' we explain the verse as saying: Perform all your work in the house and field during six days, so that on the seventh your maidservant’s son and the resident alien may rest, all of them serving as witnesses to creation. This is like 'Bake what you will bake.' Likewise, it says, 'Six days you shall labor and do all your work,' as I explained there.”
: “Then you will delight in Hashem. I will have you ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for Hashem’s mouth has spoken.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

k: volume-i|1763|1|Peri Tzadik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat VII:
quote: : “The blessing of Shabbat is repose: the bestowal of great understanding entirely without labor or exertion. Only through one’s earlier exertion during the six weekdays, according to the effort of preparation, is one’s attainment in the holiness of Shabbat determined. Likewise, attainment in the World to Come corresponds to exertion in this world: one who did not toil before Shabbat, what will he eat on Shabbat? 'I did not labor, yet I found'—do not believe it. Only after labor does the finding come, unexpectedly, as explained above: it is attained without any labor, beyond the reach of one’s own knowledge.”

: “Twenty-two foundation letters are set in a wheel with 231 gates. The wheel turns forward and backward. This is the sign of the matter: there is nothing higher in goodness than oneg, ‘delight,’ and nothing lower in evil than nega, ‘affliction.’”

: “The Master taught: Gentiles value Israel’s livestock more than their own wives. For Rabbi Yochanan said: When the serpent approached Eve, he infused her with defilement. If so, does this not also apply to Israel? Israel stood at Mount Sinai, and their defilement ceased; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, retained their defilement.”
: “Rava said: The tenth animal becomes consecrated of its own accord.”

: “Rabbi Yirmeya sent Rabbi Zeira a basket of figs. Rabbi Yirmeya thought, ‘Would Rabbi Zeira possibly eat them without their being tithed?’ Rabbi Zeira thought, ‘Would Rabbi Yirmeya possibly send them without their being tithed?’ Between the assumptions of the two, the figs were eaten untithed. The next day Rabbi Yirmeya met Rabbi Zeira and asked, ‘Did you tithe those figs?’ He replied, ‘No.’ Rabbi Abba bar Yemina told Rabbi Zeira: ‘If the earlier generations were angels, we are human beings; if they were human beings, we are donkeys. Yet we are not even like Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair’s donkey: they gave it untithed barley and it refused to eat, while we have eaten untithed figs!’”

: “Robbers stole Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair’s donkey at night. It remained hidden with them for three days without eating anything. After three days they decided to return it to its owner, saying: Let us send it back so that it does not die with us and make the cave stink. They released it. It went and stood at its owner’s gate and began braying. He told his household: Open for this poor creature, which has not eaten for three days. They opened, and it entered. He said: Give it something to eat. They placed barley before it, but it would not eat. They told him: Rabbi, it will not eat. He asked: Has it been properly prepared? They answered: Yes. He asked: Have you separated the demai tithe? They replied: Did Rabbi not teach us that someone buying produce for seed or animal feed, flour for hides, oil for a lamp, or oil to anoint utensils is exempt from demai? He answered: What can we do for this poor creature, which is extremely stringent upon itself? They separated the demai tithe, and it ate.”

: ““This was explained: Rabbi Yohanan said.” In Shekalim, chapter five, halakha one, in the Jerusalem Talmud’s Demai, and in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter sixty, no such distinction is given. Instead, he answered them that the donkey was stringent upon herself.”

: “Our Rabbis said: A Jew had a cow that plowed. He became poor and sold it to a gentile. The gentile plowed with it for six weekdays. On Shabbat he brought it out to plow, but it lay down under the yoke. He struck it, yet it would not move. He told the Jew: Take back your cow; perhaps it is ill, for I strike it and it will not move. The Jew understood: it was accustomed to resting on Shabbat. He said: Come, I shall make it rise. He whispered in its ear: Cow, cow, when you belonged to me, you plowed on weekdays and rested on Shabbat. Now my sins have brought you into a gentile’s possession. Please rise and plow. It immediately rose and plowed. The gentile said: Take your cow! Must I keep fetching you to make it rise? Besides, I will not let you go until you tell me what you did in its ear. I exhausted myself striking it, and it would not rise. The Jew reassured him: I used no sorcery; I merely said such-and-such in its ear. The gentile was immediately awestruck: If a cow, possessing neither speech nor understanding, recognizes its Creator, shall I, whom my Maker formed in His likeness and endowed with understanding, fail to recognize my Creator? He converted, studied, and attained Torah. They called him Yochanan ben Torta, and our Rabbis still report laws in his name. If you marvel that a cow brought one person beneath the wings of the Divine Presence, a cow also brings purification to all Israel, as we read in the passage, “This is the statute of the Torah.””
: “R. Yohanan ben Torta: The Pesikta, Rabbati 14, explains that he converted through a cow, although there the name is written R. Judah ben Torta.”

Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik 197:1: “‘With all your resources,’ however, does not lie within human service but requires heavenly assistance. It means that love of God becomes fixed within all one’s property and possessions themselves. It does not mean one’s desire and longing for property, which is already included in ‘with all your heart.’ Rather, the property itself is involved. As is known, property belongs with a person; a person can be so filled with love of God throughout his depths that all his possessions, which are extensions of himself, consequently become filled with His love. Such was Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair’s donkey, which was stringent with itself against eating forbidden food, as Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 60, relates. This applies to living creatures, and presumably also to inanimate things: in the future, a stone will cry out from the wall when a person wishes to transgress, as the Sages say in the Midrash on Psalms, Psalm 73. This is the meaning of his utensils resting on Shabbat: then he belongs entirely to God, including all his possessions.”

: ““That the son of your maidservant may be refreshed”: The verse speaks of an uncircumcised slave. Do you say an uncircumcised slave, or perhaps a circumcised slave? When Scripture says, “That your male slave and female slave may rest like you,” it already speaks of a circumcised slave. Thus “That the son of your maidservant may be refreshed” speaks of an uncircumcised slave. “And the stranger”—this is a resident alien. Do you say a resident alien, or perhaps a full convert? When it says, “Your convert within your gates,” it already speaks of a full convert. Thus “And the stranger” refers to a resident alien.”

: “And R. Meir? The word “or” teaches that giving to a resident stranger takes priority over selling to a gentile. And R. Judah? This needs no verse: since you are commanded to sustain the resident stranger but are not commanded to sustain the gentile, no verse is necessary; it follows from reasoning.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, gives a person an additional soul on the eve of Shabbat and takes it from him when Shabbat ends, as it says, “He ceased and was refreshed.” When the Shabbat rest has ceased: woe, the soul has gone.”
Commentary: Rashi on Beitzah 16a:11:2: ““An additional soul”: a heart broadened for rest and joy, freely open, so that a person may eat and drink without his appetite recoiling.”

: “I am the One who planted this tree for the whole world to delight in. With it I spread out All, and I named it All, since everything depends on it, everything comes forth from it, and everything needs it. They gaze toward it and await it, and from there the souls fly forth in joy. I was alone when I made it; no angel can boast over it, saying, ‘I preceded you.’ Even when I spread out My earth, in which I planted and rooted this tree, and rejoiced together in them—who was with Me, to whom I revealed this secret?”

: “He asked him: Will I enter the World to Come? He answered: Yes. He asked: But is it not written, “There shall be no survivor of the house of Esau”? That refers to one who acts as Esau did. A baraita likewise teaches: “There shall be no survivor of the house of Esau”—might this apply to everyone? The words “of the house of Esau” teach that it applies to one who acts as Esau did.”

: “Anyone who accepts the seven commandments and takes care to observe them is among the righteous of the nations of the world and has a share in the World to Come. This is provided that he accepts and fulfills them because the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded them in the Torah and informed us through Moses our teacher that the descendants of Noah had previously been commanded concerning them.”

: “Rabbi Acha said: The conversation of the servants of the patriarchs’ households is more precious than the Torah of their descendants. Eliezer’s account occupies two or three pages, and Scripture tells it and repeats it. Yet the impurity of a creeping creature is a fundamental Torah law, and the rule that its blood conveys impurity like its flesh is derived only from an extra expression in Scripture. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai derives it from ‘tamei—hatamei’; Rabbi Eliezer ben Yosei derives it from ‘zeh—vezeh.’”

: “An idolater who occupies himself with Torah incurs liability to death; he should study only their seven commandments. Likewise, an idolater who rests—even on a weekday—if he establishes it for himself as a Sabbath, incurs liability to death; all the more so if he establishes a festival for himself. The general principle is that they are not permitted to invent a religion or create commandments for themselves on their own initiative. Rather, one should either become a righteous convert and accept all the commandments, or remain within one’s own law without adding or subtracting. If he studies Torah, observes such a Sabbath, or introduces something new, he is beaten and punished and informed that he incurs liability to death for this; nevertheless, he is not executed.”

: “A Noahide who wishes to perform one of the Torah’s other commandments in order to receive reward is not prevented from performing it properly. If he brings a burnt offering, it is accepted from him.”

: “The Zohar explains “Be guarded in all that I have said to you”: why “be guarded,” rather than “guard”? It means: regarding the words of My service about which I threatened you, be guarded so that no harm reaches you. This is initially difficult. Such language would fit Ki Tavo’s admonitions, of which Zohar Chadash says that the curses are given in love, like a father who loves his son. He holds the strap, makes great noise and raises his voice, but his blows are light and merciful. There the language “I threatened you” is appropriate, but here the admonitions have not yet been stated. Perhaps the allusion is to “Tell the children of Israel,” where Rashi explains that penalties and exacting details were set out to the men, matters hard as sinews. The Gemara similarly expounds “Moses told” as matters hard as sinews. Thus, “Be guarded in all that I have said to you,” so that no harm reaches you.”
: “You shall serve Hashem your God, and He will bless your bread and your water; I will remove illness from your midst.”

: “From where do we know that rain is mentioned in prayer? It was taught: “To love Hashem your God and serve Him with all your heart.” What service takes place in the heart? This means prayer. The next verse says, “I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early and the late rain.””
: “Come, eat of my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.”

: “Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master and the Matron with every kind of delight, fulfilling ‘This is the table before the Lord.’ Until now all delight in the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread’: the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, the varied flavors of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”
: “He forms all their hearts together and understands all their deeds.”

: “On Rosh Hashanah everyone in the world passes before Him like bnei maron. What does bnei maron mean? Here they explained: like lambs. Reish Lakish said: like the ascent of Beit Maron. Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel’s name: like the soldiers of David’s army. Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Nevertheless, they are all surveyed in one glance. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Our Mishnah also teaches this, citing “He who forms their hearts together, who understands all their deeds.” What does that mean? If it means that He created everyone and made their hearts alike, we see that this is not so. Rather, it means that the One who formed them sees their hearts all together and understands all their deeds.”

Parallel: Resisei Layla 26:1: “Just as the Torah has six hundred thousand letters, and each Jewish soul has its own portion in Torah through the wisdom of the mind attached to God, so each Jewish soul has its own particular portion in the Tabernacle and Temple through the will of the heart attached to God. The joining of Israel’s minds forms the Torah’s letters; the joining of Israel’s service of the heart is the work of the Tabernacle. The census is called ‘Raise the head,’ for each person has a distinctive elevation. Every portion of Torah or of the Tabernacle is necessary: if it is missing, the whole is invalid. Each person thus has a particular respect in which he is elevated.”
: “There will be no woman who miscarries or is barren in your land; I will fulfill the number of your days.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: “There shall be no barren man among you”—you will not be barren of students; “nor barren woman”—your prayer will not be uprooted before the Omnipresent. When is this so? When you make yourself like an animal.”
Commentary: Rashi on Bekhorot 44b:8:2: ““Like an animal”: do not delay urinating.” Context: Rashi places the phrase in its physiological context; Rav Tzadok takes up the image of fruitful prayer.
: “Abraham was old, advanced in years, and Hashem had blessed Abraham in everything.”

: “Come and see: Abraham drew close to Him, and this was his longing throughout his life. Abraham did not draw close in one day or at one moment. Rather, his deeds brought him close throughout all his days, level by level, until he ascended in his levels.”
: “You arrange a table before me in the presence of my adversaries. You have enriched my head with oil; my cup is filled to overflowing.”

: “It was taught: Issi ben Judah says: The manna that descended for Israel kept rising higher until all the kings of east and west could see it, as it says, “You arrange a table before me in the presence of my adversaries,” and, “My cup is overflowing.” Abaye said: We learn from this that David’s cup in the World to Come holds two hundred and twenty-one log, as it says, “My cup is overflowing”—the numerical value of revayah is that amount.”

: “He himself raised the objection and resolved it: The teaching concerns the amount needed for food. Rabba bar bar Hana likewise said in R. Yohanan’s name: The teaching concerns the amount needed for food. From where do we know that man denotes sustenance? It is written, “The king allotted for them,” and so forth.”
: “I will provide grass in your field for your animals, and you will eat and be satisfied. Guard yourselves, lest your heart be enticed and you turn aside to serve other gods and bow down to them.”

: “Rav Acha son of Rav Huna said in Rav Sheshet’s name: This is what people mean when they say, “Filling the belly is a kind of evil.” For it says, “As they grazed they became satisfied; they were satisfied and their hearts grew haughty; therefore they forgot Me.” Rav Nachman derived it from here: “Your heart will grow haughty, and you will forget Hashem.” The Sages derived it from: “He will eat, become satisfied and grow fat, and turn away.” Or, if you prefer, from: “Jeshurun grew fat and kicked.””

Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 32a:12:1: ““A full belly—evil kinds”: Filling the belly is among the evil kinds of sin. Zenei means “kinds,” as the Aramaic translation renders “according to its kind” as li-zenohi.”

: “There was also an incident involving Rabbi Yochanan ben Matya, who told his son: “Go and hire workers for us.” His son went and promised them meals. When he returned, his father told him: “My son, even if you prepare for them a banquet like Solomon’s in his day, you will not have fulfilled your obligation toward them, for they are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Does this mean that our father Abraham’s meal surpassed Solomon’s? It is written: “Solomon’s daily provisions were thirty kor of fine flour and sixty kor of flour, ten fattened oxen, twenty pastured oxen, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.” Guryon son of Astyon said in Rav’s name: These were for the cooks’ starch preparation; Rabbi Yitzchak said they were for the pot’s seasonings. Rabbi Yitzchak also said: Solomon had a thousand wives, each of whom prepared such a meal in her house, thinking that perhaps he would eat with her that day. Of Abraham, however, it says, “Abraham ran to the herd and took a calf, tender and good.” Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: “A calf” indicates one, “tender” a second, and “good” a third. There, three oxen were provided for three men; here, the meal was for all Israel and Judah, as it says, “Judah and Israel were numerous as the sand by the sea.””
: “Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; provide me with my allotted bread.”

: “Solomon’s food for one day was thirty kor of fine flour and sixty kor of meal, ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, fallow deer, and fattened birds.”

: “A person’s entire sustenance is allotted during the period from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, except for expenses for Shabbat, festivals, and his children’s Torah education. If he reduces these expenses, his allotment is reduced; if he increases them, it is increased. Rabbi Abbahu asked: What verse teaches this? “Sound the shofar at the new moon, at the concealment, for our festival day.” Which festival falls when the new moon is concealed? Rosh Hashanah. The next verse says, “For it is an allotment for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob.” How do we know that chok, “allotment,” refers to sustenance? Because it says, “They ate their allotment that Pharaoh gave them.” Mar Zutra derived it from here: “Provide me with my allotted bread.””

: “'Five shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you ten thousand': is that the correct proportion? It should have said only that a hundred of you would pursue two thousand. Rather, a few people fulfilling the Torah cannot be compared to many people fulfilling the Torah.”

: ““Five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand.” “Of you”—from the weak among you, not from the strong. “A hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand”—is that the correct proportion? Should it not say, “A hundred of you shall pursue two thousand”? Rather, a multitude fulfilling Torah is not like a few fulfilling Torah. “Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword”—they shall fall before you in an extraordinary manner.”

Parallel: Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 32:2–3: “Once the body is repugnant and loathsome to a person, who can know the greatness and elevation of the soul and spirit in their root and source in the living God? All are kindred, and all have one Father. Therefore all Israel are truly called brothers because their souls are rooted in the one God; only their bodies are divided. Those who make the body primary and the soul secondary cannot have true love and brotherhood among them, only love dependent upon something. This is why Hillel the Elder said of fulfilling this commandment, ‘This is the whole Torah; the rest is its explanation.’ The foundation of all Torah is to raise the soul far above the body to the root of all worlds, and to draw the light of the Infinite, blessed be He, into the community of Israel—that is, into the source of all Israel’s souls, as explained below—so that one is united with One, without division among the souls, God forbid. For ‘the Holy One does not dwell in a damaged place,’ as we say, ‘Bless us, our Father, all as one, with the light of Your countenance,’ as explained at length elsewhere.”

: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon the Devout’s name: A fast that includes none of Israel’s transgressors is not a fast. For galbanum smells foul, yet Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients. Abaye derived this from, “He founded His united company upon the earth.””
: “He builds His upper chambers in heaven and establishes His united structure upon the earth. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the earth’s surface; Hashem is His name.”

: “Of the four species taken with the lulav, two produce fruit and two do not. The fruit-bearing species must be joined to those that bear no fruit, and those that bear no fruit must be joined to the fruit-bearing species. A person does not fulfill his obligation with them until all are joined in one bundle. So too, Israel is accepted favorably only when all are joined in one union, as it says, “He builds His upper chambers in heaven, and founded His united company upon the earth.””

: “Another interpretation: “The fruit of a beautiful tree”—these are Israel. Just as the etrog has taste and fragrance, so Israel includes people with Torah and good deeds. “Palm branches”—these are Israel. Just as the date palm has taste but no fragrance, so Israel includes people with Torah but without good deeds. “A branch of a leafy tree”—these are Israel. Just as myrtle has fragrance but no taste, so Israel includes people with good deeds but without Torah. “Willows of the brook”—these are Israel. Just as the willow has neither taste nor fragrance, so Israel includes people with neither Torah nor good deeds. What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do with them? Destroying them is impossible. Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let them all be bound into one bundle, and they will atone for one another. If you do so, at that moment I am exalted, as it is written, “He builds His upper chambers in heaven.” When is He exalted? When they form one bundle, as it says, “His band He founded upon the earth.” Therefore Moses warns Israel, “You shall take for yourselves on the first day.””

: ““The Lord shall remove all illness from you”—it depends upon you that illnesses should not come upon you. Rabbi Avin said: This is the evil inclination, which is sweet at its beginning and bitter at its end.”

: “Did Rabbi Elazar really say this? Rabbi Elazar also said: A person should always consider himself as though a holy one dwells within his innards, as it says, “A holy one is within you, and I will not enter the city.” There is no difficulty: The teaching favoring fasting concerns one who can bear self-affliction; the other concerns one who cannot bear it.”
: “I will not carry out My fierce anger; I will not return to destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not a man, the Holy One within you, and I will not enter a city.”

: “A person’s entire sustenance is allotted during the period from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, except for expenses for Shabbat, festivals, and his children’s Torah education. If he reduces these expenses, his allotment is reduced; if he increases them, it is increased. Rabbi Abbahu asked: What verse teaches this? “Sound the shofar at the new moon, at the concealment, for our festival day.” Which festival falls when the new moon is concealed? Rosh Hashanah. The next verse says, “For it is an allotment for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob.” How do we know that chok, “allotment,” refers to sustenance? Because it says, “They ate their allotment that Pharaoh gave them.” Mar Zutra derived it from here: “Provide me with my allotted bread.””

k: volume-i|1803|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “This explains the exception for Shabbat and festival expenses: whatever one adds to Shabbat expenditure is in holiness. As the Arizal wrote, on Shabbat even eating for bodily pleasure is holy. Eating on Shabbat is therefore like eating manna, as is every meal that fulfills a mitzvah. Eating in holiness does not lead to an accusation by the evil inclination.”

: “Rabbi Avin said: What is meant by “In my poverty”? There is no wealth before the One who spoke and the world came into being. Another interpretation: “In my poverty” means through affliction—David would fast and dedicate his meal to Heaven.”
: “Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chalafta said: All the kingdoms are called by the name ‘Egypt,’ because they bring distress upon Israel.”

k: volume-i|1806|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “When God sets the table, it stands against the kelippot. As we have said in the holy Ari’s name, at the end of Shabbat we also pray concerning weekday meals, ‘Set a table before me,’ asking that all our food be the bread God allots me—that He determine and apportion it in holiness. It will then be ‘against my adversaries,’ since what comes from God is holy.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 10:1: “Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 6, says that they all cry out in their Yom Kippur prayers like dogs: ‘Give, give us food!’ This resembles ‘Feed me like a dog.’ Its criticism seems contradicted by Bava Batra 8a, where Yonatan ben Amram told Rabbi, ‘Feed me like a dog,’ so as not to benefit from the honor of Torah. Certainly a person must not congratulate himself and boast that he is among those dwelling in God’s house all his days, with no connection at all to this world’s needs. But neither should he go to the opposite extreme and place all his hope and purpose solely in bodily needs. This is what Tikkunei Zohar criticizes in their doglike cries of ‘Give, give.’ Even if a person bears the burden of earning a livelihood, he should hope and long to merit being among those dwelling in God’s house. Rabbi Bunim of Pshischa explained ‘One thing I have asked of God, that shall I seek’: King David did not assume that he already belonged among those dwelling in God’s house. He asked God for this itself: ‘that shall I seek’—that at least this be his entire aspiration, to merit ‘dwelling in God’s house all the days of my life.’”
: “You shall be holy people to Me. Do not eat flesh torn by a beast in the field; throw it to the dog.”

: “Since Israel are called holiness in complete perfection, it says, ‘You shall not eat flesh torn in the field.’ Israel, perfected above all, do not draw nourishment from harsh judgment’s side. ‘Cast it to the dog’: certainly to the dog, the most brazen and powerful judgment. Once harsh judgment rests upon it and casts impurity into it, it is forbidden to those called holy. Rather, ‘Cast it to the dog,’ the most brazen and powerful judgment, as in ‘The dogs are fierce of appetite.’”
: “The dogs have a fierce appetite and know no satisfaction. They are shepherds who know no understanding; all have turned to their own way, each to his own gain, every last one.”

k: volume-i|1810|0|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 121b, pr
quote: : “On ‘You shall cast it to the dog’: a marginal gloss states that the female aspect of the Other Side is called ‘dog’—kelev—the reversal of the letters of bakol, ‘in everything.’”

: “Rabbi Abba said: when they unite, the world’s inhabitants cannot withstand them. Therefore, ‘Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together’—precisely together. We learned that a person should not make room for evil kinds, for a person’s action below arouses what should not be aroused. When they unite, their combined force brings forth what is called Dog, the most brazen of all. Hence ‘Against all the children of Israel, no dog shall sharpen its tongue.’ God said: ‘You asked, “Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?” I now hand you over to the dog.’ Immediately, ‘Amalek came.’”
: “You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.”
: “Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.”

k: volume-i|1812|0|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 65a, pre
quote: : “‘Which is called dog’: the marginal gloss explains that the middle letters of shor, ‘ox,’ and chamor, ‘donkey’—vav in shor, mem and vav in chamor—have the numerical value of kelev, ‘dog.’ Or Yisrael adds that they are called choshekh, ‘darkness,’ an acronym for donkey, ox and dog.”
: “He saw Amalek and took up his discourse, saying, “Amalek was first among nations, but his end is utter destruction.””

: “We learned that this serpent always follows the mystery of the woman of valor. The woman of harlotry seeks to adorn herself like her, but cannot. The woman of valor’s mark and letter is he, fitting for her. The woman of harlotry’s mark resembles it but is not properly formed: her letter is qof, arranged like he, as an ape beside human beings follows them yet cannot become like them. Moses likewise fashioned that serpent according to its fitting sign. It is continually prepared for evil. Through it Adam sinned and was driven from the Garden of Eden, his dwelling, which mirrored the dwelling above.”
: “The snake was more cunning than any wild animal Hashem God had made. It said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You shall not eat from any tree in the garden’?””

: “R. Jeremiah ben Elazar said: They divided into three factions. One said, “Let us ascend and dwell there”; one said, “Let us ascend and worship idols”; and one said, “Let us ascend and wage war.” Of the faction that said, “Let us ascend and dwell there,” Scripture says, “Hashem scattered them.” Those who said, “Let us ascend and wage war,” became apes, spirits, demons, and night-demons. Of those who said, “Let us ascend and worship idols,” Scripture says, “For there Hashem confused the language of the whole earth.””

: “If he merits more, he is given a nefesh through Atzilut, from the side of the only daughter, called the king’s daughter. If he merits more, he is given a ruach of Atzilut from the middle pillar’s side, and is called God’s son: ‘You are children of the Lord your God.’ If he merits more, he is given a neshamah from Father and Mother, as in ‘He breathed into his nostrils a soul of life.’ What is life? Yod-he, of which it says, ‘Let every soul praise Yah.’ Through him the divine Name is completed.”
: “You shall say to Pharaoh, “Thus says Hashem: Israel is My son, My firstborn.””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak taught: ‘A mother of children rejoicing, hallelujah.’ The Mother is known; who are the children? Rabbi Shimon said: we learned that God has two children, male and female. He gave the male to Jacob: ‘My firstborn son, Israel,’ and ‘Israel, in whom I glory.’ The daughter He gave to Abraham: ‘The Lord blessed Abraham with All.’ Abraham had a daughter named Bakol.”

: “The ninth is Shaddai—another reading has El Shaddai—who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ Enough means sufficiency, and sufficiency comes to the world only from the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ The tenth is Adonai, for the kingdom’s law is certainly law. This wages the King’s battles in the world; it is lower Might, Tzedek.”
: “For the Holy One, blessed be He, placed His name upon Israel. What is the name and seal He placed upon them? Shaddai: shin He placed in the nose, dalet in the hand, and yod in circumcision.”

: “If one vows, “Benefit from the uncircumcised is forbidden to me,” he may benefit from uncircumcised Israelites but may not benefit from circumcised members of the nations. If he vows against benefit from the circumcised, he may not benefit from uncircumcised Israelites, but may benefit from circumcised members of the nations. For the designation “uncircumcised” is applied to the nations, as it says, “All the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in heart.” It also says, “This uncircumcised Philistine,” and, “Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.””

: “We learned that this serpent always follows the mystery of the woman of valor. The woman of harlotry seeks to adorn herself like her, but cannot. The woman of valor’s mark and letter is he, fitting for her. The woman of harlotry’s mark resembles it but is not properly formed: her letter is qof, arranged like he, as an ape beside human beings follows them yet cannot become like them. Moses likewise fashioned that serpent according to its fitting sign. It is continually prepared for evil. Through it Adam sinned and was driven from the Garden of Eden, his dwelling, which mirrored the dwelling above.”

: “R. Jeremiah ben Elazar said: They divided into three factions. One said, “Let us ascend and dwell there”; one said, “Let us ascend and worship idols”; and one said, “Let us ascend and wage war.” Of the faction that said, “Let us ascend and dwell there,” Scripture says, “Hashem scattered them.” Those who said, “Let us ascend and wage war,” became apes, spirits, demons, and night-demons. Of those who said, “Let us ascend and worship idols,” Scripture says, “For there Hashem confused the language of the whole earth.””
: “On a good day, enjoy the good; on a bad day, consider: God made the one corresponding to the other, so that a person cannot discover anything that will come afterward.”
: “I declare the outcome from the beginning, and from ancient times things not yet done. I say, “My plan will stand, and I will carry out all I desire.””
: “Let a slanderer find no stability in the land; let evil hunt down a violent man, blow after blow.”

: “This letter differs from qof: qof finds no settled place anywhere in the world, as in ‘A slanderer shall not be established in the land.’ Tet settles everywhere and is properly fitted for settled existence. Therefore, wherever tet is present, qof has no place to settle. The Other Side has no dominion at all in this place, which gives life in this world to those dwelling beneath this letter. One must not go outside; once outside, the Other Side has permission to rule over him. Just as this letter rules in this place, another letter rules in Gehinnom: qof.”
: “Another interpretation: ‘A slanderous man’ refers to the serpent, which slandered its Creator. ‘Let him not be established in the land’ corresponds to the sentence, ‘Upon your belly.’”

: “'Who encountered you on the way': an expression of chance occurrence. Another explanation: an expression of seminal emission and impurity, for he defiled them through intercourse with males. Another explanation: an expression of cold and heat—he cooled you and diminished your boiling heat. All the nations feared fighting you, but this one came, began, and showed the way to the others. This resembles a boiling bath into which no creature could descend. One scoundrel came and leaped into it; although he was burned, he cooled it for others.”
: “He encountered you on the road and attacked all the weak stragglers behind you, while you were weary and exhausted; he did not fear God.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 7:1: “In truth, we explained this concerning the Zohar’s statement on Mishpatim 123b: ‘In everything I have said to you, you shall be guarded.’ It asks why the word does not have the form of a command to guard, and answers: you shall indeed be guarded—from what I threatened you with concerning My service, so that no harm reaches you. On that reading, it should have said ‘From everything I have said to you, you shall be guarded,’ meaning guarded from all the threatened punishments. We explained that precisely through the threats and punishments, ‘in everything I have said to you,’ you will be guarded. This is placed after the Shabbat of the sabbatical year: through it, God’s fear will be before you, and consequently you will be guarded from every evil, discharging the matter through fear of the threat. This was explained in Mishpatim II and VII. But Heaven forbid that one rely on this and take the punishments lightly, following the counsel of the evil inclination and Amalek, the serpent’s root. Of this it says, ‘Do not trust in evil; do not rely upon the intimate companion.’”
: “He saw Amalek and took up his discourse, saying, “Amalek was first among nations, but his end is utter destruction.””

: “Rabbi Akiva expounded: If a man and woman merit, the Divine Presence is between them; if they do not merit, fire consumes them. Rava said: The woman’s fire is stronger than the man’s. Why? In her name the letters of “fire” are adjacent, whereas in his they are not.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sotah 17a:15:2: ““The Divine Presence is between them”: God divided His name and placed it between them—a yud in ish, “man,” and a heh in ishah, “woman.””

Commentary: Rashi on Sotah 17a:16:2: ““Why? Here the letters are joined”: The woman’s fire is readily kindled, for no letter of the divine name separates its letters; they are joined and read esh, “fire.” In ish, “man,” the letters of “fire” are not joined, because the yud of the Divine Presence separates them.”
: “For you are a people holy to Hashem your God. Hashem chose you to be His treasured people from all the peoples upon the earth.”
: “You shall be holy people to Me. Do not eat flesh torn by a beast in the field; throw it to the dog.”

: “Rabbi Abba was traveling with Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Chiyya. Rabbi Chiyya asked: ‘You shall be people of holiness to Me’—how do we know this? He answered: Rabbi Yose and all the companions have explained it well, and it is so. Whence do we know? ‘Israel is holiness to the Lord, the first of His harvest.’ ‘First’ certainly means Wisdom, which is called beginning, as in ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord.’”

: “'Meat torn in the field': the same law applies inside the house. Scripture speaks of the usual situation, the place where animals are commonly attacked. Similarly, 'For he found her in the field,' and 'Who is not pure because of a nocturnal emission'—the same law applies to a daytime emission, but Scripture speaks of the usual situation. The Aramaic means meat torn from a living animal: meat ripped by a wolf or lion from a permitted wild or domesticated animal while it was alive.”

: ““Meat torn in the field”—this tells me only about the field; how do I know the rule also applies in a house? Scripture says, “A carcass or a torn animal,” comparing a torn animal to a carcass. Just as the rule for a carcass makes no distinction between a house and a field, so the rule for a torn animal makes no such distinction. What, then, does “Meat torn in the field you shall not eat” teach? Scripture speaks of the usual case.”
: “He drew near and kissed him. Isaac smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, saying, “See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.””

: “Another interpretation: ‘king’ is the woman who fears the Lord, as in ‘A woman who fears the Lord shall be praised.’ ‘Served by the field’ is the alien woman, as in ‘to guard you from an alien woman.’ For there is one field and another. In one field all blessings and sanctifications rest, as in ‘the fragrance of a field the Lord has blessed.’ In another rest devastation, impurity, destruction, killing and wars. This king is sometimes subjected to that field, as in ‘Under three things the earth trembles…under a slave when he reigns…and a maidservant who inherits her mistress.’ This king’s light is concealed and darkened until he is purified and joined above.”
: “For he found her in the countryside; the betrothed young woman cried out, but there was no one to rescue her.”
: “What did the house of Amalek do? They cut off the circumcised organs of the Israelites, threw them upward, and said, ‘Is this what You chose? Here is what You chose!’”

: ““There is one people”: Rava said: No one understood malicious speech as Haman did. He said to Ahasuerus: Come, let us destroy them. The king replied: I fear their God, lest He deal with me as He did with earlier rulers. Haman answered: They have fallen asleep in their observance of the commandments. The king said: There are rabbis among them. Haman replied: They are all one people. Perhaps you think I am making a gap in your kingdom? They are scattered among the nations. Perhaps you think they benefit you? They are “separate,” like a mule that bears no offspring. Perhaps you think they occupy one province? Scripture says, “In all the provinces of your kingdom.” “Their laws differ from every people’s”: they neither eat our food nor marry our women, nor give their women to us in marriage. “They do not observe the king’s laws”: they spend the whole year saying, “It is Shabbat today; it is Passover today.” “It is not worthwhile for the king to leave them”: they eat, drink, and disparage the king. If a fly falls into someone’s cup, he throws it out and drinks; but if my lord the king touches the cup, he smashes it on the ground and will not drink.”
Commentary: Rashi on Megillah 13b:19:3: ““They spend the year with ‘Shabbat today; Passover today’”: It is Shabbat today, it is Passover today, and we are forbidden to work.”
: “Peoples heard and trembled; anguish seized the inhabitants of Philistia.”

ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Shabbat, Third Meal, Atkinu 9
quote: : “Those impudent dogs go outside and do not enter. And behold, I summon the Ancient of Days at Minchah, until they pass away.”

: “He made the letter tzadi king over eating, bound a crown upon it, combined them with one another, and through them formed Aquarius in the universe, Shevat in the year, and the gizzard in the person, male and female.”
: “The righteous person eats to satisfy his soul, but the belly of the wicked goes wanting.”

: “Why was the passage of forbidden sexual relationships placed next to the passage of holiness? To teach that wherever you find restraint from forbidden sexual relationships, you find holiness. This accords with Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi, who said: Whoever guards himself against sexual immorality is called holy.”

: “Kuf signifies the Holy One; resh signifies a wicked person. Why does the face of the kuf turn away from the resh? The Holy One, blessed be He, says: I cannot look at the wicked. Why does the crown of the kuf turn toward the resh? The Holy One, blessed be He, says: If he repents, I will bind a crown upon him like My own. Why does the leg of the kuf hang apart? So that if he repents, he may enter. Let him enter through the other opening! This supports Reish Lakish, who said: What is meant by “With scoffers He scoffs, but to the humble He gives favor”? One who comes to defile himself is given an opening; one who comes to purify himself receives help.”

: “He made the letter tzadi king over eating, bound a crown upon it, combined them with one another, and through them formed Aquarius in the universe, Shevat in the year, and the gizzard in the person, male and female.”
: “Hashem said to Moses, “Come up to Me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you the stone tablets, the Torah, and the commandment that I have written to teach them.””
: “The tablets were God’s handiwork, and the writing was God’s writing, engraved upon the tablets.”

: “Ten things were created at twilight on the eve of Shabbat: the earth’s mouth, the well’s mouth, the donkey’s mouth, the rainbow, the manna, the staff, the shamir, the script, the inscription, and the tablets. Some add the destructive spirits, Moses’ burial place, and our father Abraham’s ram. Others add tongs, which are made with tongs.”

: “We learned that ten things were created on Shabbat eve, including writing, the inscription and the tablets. Thus ‘The tablets were God’s work, and the inscription was God’s inscription.’ How does this show it was Shabbat eve? Perhaps it was a thousand years later, or when Israel stood at Sinai? It was certainly Shabbat eve. Throughout creation, the complete Name is not mentioned: everything created is described with Elohim alone, until all the work was completed on Shabbat eve. Once everything was perfected, He was called ‘the Lord God,’ the complete Name.”

: “Another interpretation: Amon means ‘craftsman.’ The Torah says: I was the instrument of the Holy One’s craftsmanship. Ordinarily, when a human king builds a palace, he does not build it according to his own understanding, but according to an architect’s understanding. The architect, too, does not proceed solely from his own understanding: he has plans and notebooks showing how to make rooms and doorways. So the Holy One, blessed be He, looked into the Torah and created the world. The Torah says, ‘In the beginning God created.’ ‘Beginning’ means Torah, as it says, ‘The Lord acquired me at the beginning of His way.’”

: “If you ask the fundamental question—why did Adam give David life rather than leave him stillborn?—the reason is that Adam’s principal repair was to take place through David. This is the secret of the name Adam, an acronym for Adam, David and Messiah. Know this principle: before Adam sinned, life came to humanity from Arikh Anpin, and human beings therefore enjoyed long lives. After he sinned and his children again rebelled against the Most High, it was said, ‘My spirit shall not contend with man forever, since he is flesh; his days shall be 120 years’—from Ze‘ir Anpin.”

: “‘This is the book of Adam’s generations’ concerns their forms. Rabbi Yitzchak said: God showed Adam the forms of every generation that would enter the world, all the world’s sages, and the kings destined to rule over Israel. When he reached David, king of Israel, who would be born and die, Adam said, ‘I shall lend him seventy years of my own.’ Seventy years were deducted from Adam, and God assigned them to David.”
: “These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day Hashem God made earth and heaven.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak said: ‘Behold, it was very good’ refers to the angel of life; ‘behold, it was very good’ also refers to the angel of death. Is the angel of death very good? This is like a king who made a banquet, invited guests, and set a dish filled with every good thing before them. He said, ‘Whoever eats and blesses the king may eat and enjoy himself; whoever eats and does not bless the king shall have his head struck off with the sword.’ So, for one who accumulates mitzvot and good deeds there is the angel of life; for one who does not accumulate mitzvot and good deeds there is the angel of death.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””

: “As we have explained, this is the meaning of the saying in Nedarim: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the land of Israel. The intent is that Joshua’s book contains the secret of the Oral Torah. Thus, “Moses received Torah at Sinai and transmitted it to Joshua” refers to Oral Torah, as the Zohar explains; he gave the Written Torah to the Levites. Had Israel not sinned, they would have seen how everything is included in the five books of Torah, for nothing lacks an allusion in the Torah. This is the arrangement of the land of Israel, the place of the Divine Presence. Its “arrangement” means each Jew’s portion in the Oral Torah, the land that is the Congregation of Israel. Although Joshua’s book records the names of towns, the secrets of the roots of Oral Torah are concealed within them, for it is the first book after Moses’ Torah.”

: “Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world: The Land of Israel took nine, and the entire rest of the world took one. Ten measures of beauty descended to the world: Jerusalem took nine, and the entire rest of the world took one.”

: “Among those possessing the holy spirit, King David, peace be upon him, was master of them all, just as Moses our teacher was master of all the prophets in prophecy. King David possessed the highest level of holy spirit: his own earlier breath clothed itself in his present breath, and he did not need that of others, paralleling what was stated concerning Moses’ level of prophecy. We already said that we are uncertain about what we heard: whether this applies specifically to present breath, or also to present voice or speech. The highest level of all belonged to King David, peace be upon him; all the other levels beneath that first one are distributed among the remaining possessors of the holy spirit, each according to his level.”

: “Esther was a prophetess, as it is written, “On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty.” Should it not say “royal garments”? Rather, she clothed herself in the holy spirit. Here it says “clothed,” and elsewhere, “A spirit clothed Amasai.””

: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama also said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: What does “I will give you the stone tablets, the Torah and the commandment which I have written, to instruct them” mean? “Tablets” means the Ten Commandments; “Torah” means Scripture; “the commandment” means Mishnah; “which I have written” means Prophets and Writings; “to instruct them” means Talmud. This teaches that all of them were given to Moses at Sinai.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”

: “They likewise said in Midrash Rabbah: 'The entire Torah depends upon justice; therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, gave laws after the Ten Commandments.' In 'These are the ordinances,' He likewise explains the laws concerning idolatry, honoring one’s father, murder, and adultery, which are mentioned in the Ten Commandments.”

: “R. Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s evil inclination overpowers him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, “The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him.” Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not withstand it, as it says, “Hashem will not abandon him into his hand, nor allow him to be condemned when he is judged.””

: “When he is about ten cubits from the place of stoning, they tell him, “Confess,” for all those facing execution confess. Whoever confesses has a share in the World to Come, as we find concerning Achan. Joshua said to him, “My son, give honor to Hashem, God of Israel, and offer Him confession.” Achan answered Joshua, “Indeed, I have sinned, and I have done thus and thus,” and so forth. From where do we know that his confession atoned for him? It says, “Joshua said: Why have you troubled us? Hashem will trouble you on this day.” On this day you are troubled, but you are not troubled in the World to Come.”

: “But for one guilty of profaning the Name, repentance alone cannot suspend punishment, nor can Yom Kippur atone, nor sufferings purge it. Rather, all of them together suspend punishment, and death purges it, as it says, “Hashem of Hosts has revealed in my hearing: This wrongdoing will not be atoned for you until you die.””

: “The Rabbis interpret “cut off” as in this world, and the repeated “cut off” as in the world to come. “His iniquity remains upon him” teaches that if he repents and then dies, death completes his cleansing.”
: “One who sacrifices to gods shall be utterly destroyed, unless it is to Hashem alone.”
: “When you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years; in the seventh he shall go free without payment.”

: “Concerning the well-known Shovavim: Israel has an ancient custom of fasting forty consecutive days, from the first day of the week of Shemot through Terumah and part of Tetzaveh. The mnemonic ‘Return, wayward children’ uses the initials of Shemot, Va’era, Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim. These forty days of fasting were instituted principally for the sin of seminal emission; this period is more suited to fasting for that sin than the rest of the year. The reason follows our explanation of Egypt’s exile through mortar and bricks. Those enslaved in Egypt were the sparks of souls that Adam emitted during the 130 years in which he separated from his wife and generated demons and spirits through seminal drops. All were repaired through that Egyptian exile. These portions therefore possess a special capacity for accepting the repentance of one fasting over that sin. The period begins with Shemot because the enslavement begins there, and ends with Mishpatim, for the reason explained concerning the adjacency of ‘When you acquire a Hebrew slave’ to the giving of the Torah: those sparks completed their repair in that passage. See that explanation.”

: “Come and see: he is the rest of those above and below. Hence the upper he and the lower he: rest above and rest below. The upper he is seven years seven times; the lower he is seven years alone. One is the sabbatical year, the other the Jubilee.”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”
: “When a shofar is sounded in a city, do the people not tremble? Can calamity occur in a city unless Hashem has brought it about?”

: “Nevertheless, he has a remedy through the Jubilee, the holiness of the higher Shabbat, which is the great shofar. The Zohar teaches that the great shofar will awaken even those lost in the land of Assyria, so immersed there that they no longer know their root, and those dispersed in Egypt, who know their root but are surrounded by impurity like an embryo in its mother’s womb. Through that great shofar, the higher Jubilee, Hashem will awaken genuine thoughts of repentance in their hearts. Certainly, the saying that one who observes Shabbat is forgiven even for idolatry like that of Enosh does not mean forgiveness for nothing. Observing Shabbat brings awe and fear: “The awe of Shabbat is upon the unlearned.” Through awe one comes to repentance, for awe and repentance are bound together, each depending on the other. This is the lower Shabbat, which is awe and in which awe abides.”
: “Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever—the shoot of My planting, My handiwork, through which I display My glory.”

Parallel: Tanya, Iggeret HaTeshuvah 10:5–6: “Since prayer is a form of higher repentance, lower repentance must precede it. Thus our Sages taught in the Mishnah, ‘One should rise to pray only with gravity,’ which Rashi explains as humility. This is lower repentance, awakening mercy as explained above, as the Gemara derives there from ‘She was bitter in soul.’ Yet the baraita there teaches, ‘One should rise to pray only with joy.’ In this orphaned generation, not everyone can turn his heart instantly from one extreme to the other. The counsel therefore is to undertake lower repentance beforehand, in the midnight vigil, as explained above. Whoever cannot do so every night should at least do it once a week, before Shabbat. Those who know understand that Shabbat is higher repentance. Shabbat contains the letters of tashev, ‘You return,’ in ‘You return mortals,’ for on Shabbat the worlds ascend to their source, especially through the prayers of Shabbat. This suffices for one who understands.”
: “A song of ascents. When Hashem restored Zion’s captives, we were like dreamers.”

: “Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: During all the years that Adam was under ban, he fathered spirits, demons, and night-demons, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image.” This implies that before then he did not father beings in his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say: Adam was a great pious man. When he saw that death had been decreed through him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and placed a girdle of fig leaves upon his body for one hundred and thirty years. The earlier statement concerns semen that he emitted involuntarily.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tavo 10:1: “This is also the meaning of ‘You will not believe in your life’ in the rebuke: a person will not believe that he possesses holy vitality. In truth, however, holy vitality is inherently present in every Jewish soul and never ceases, whatever happens. This is also hinted in ‘When God restores Zion’s return, we shall have been like dreamers.’ In the future we shall see plainly that all the rebukes were like a dream. The Gemara says that the distress caused by a bad dream suffices for it. The rebukes were spoken to frighten and sadden a person’s heart so that he would improve his ways from now on; consequently they will all turn to good. So it was with Bar Hedya and the verses of rebuke dreamed by Abaye and Rava: he interpreted those very verses for good. As it says there, all dreams follow the mouth; through the mouth, the verses themselves can turn to good. The haftarah concludes, ‘Your people are all righteous; forever they shall inherit the land.’ Ultimately every Jewish soul will be called righteous, whatever it has undergone, because ‘forever they shall inherit the land,’ the land of life. The point of truth, Jacob’s attribute, is present in every Jewish soul, as it says, ‘A truthful lip endures forever.’ Therefore, even if someone sometimes damaged the attribute of Tzaddik, he can return to his holiness through the point of truth remaining in him. Through it he takes to heart the need to repent and repair everything. Hence ‘The shoot o
: “When you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve six years; in the seventh he shall go free without payment.”

: “Because the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves,” what does He say concerning a Hebrew slave? “When you acquire a Hebrew slave.” The Holy One, blessed be He, declared: I spent six days creating the world, and took My rest on day seven. Your servant should likewise serve you for six years, and then go free.”
: “But if the servant insists, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go free,””

: “Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim freedom throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a Jubilee for you: each of you shall return to his holding, and each shall return to his family.”

: “This pleasantness is the sweetness proceeding from the world to come, illuminating all the lamps as they spread in every direction. An alternative reading says that all the lamps shine from the world to come. That goodness and light, from which the patriarchs draw nourishment, are called pleasantness. Another interpretation: the world to come is called pleasantness. When it awakens, all goodness, joy, lights and freedom in the world awaken. Therefore it is called pleasantness.”
: “Light is planted for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.”

: “Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: I too say that not everyone attains light, and not everyone attains joy. The righteous attain light, and the upright attain joy. The righteous attain light, as it says, “Light is sown for the righteous”; the upright attain joy, as it says, “And joy for the upright of heart.””
: “The light of the righteous shines joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “Light is planted for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.”
: “For they are life to those who find them and healing for all their flesh.”
: “May the pleasantness of the Lord our God rest upon us. Establish the work of our hands for us; establish the work of our hands.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”
: “Through wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.”
: “For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.”

: “A person must subject all the faculties of his soul to reason, as we explained in the preceding chapter. He should always place before himself one goal: apprehending God, blessed be He, to the extent human beings can know Him. He should direct all his actions—his movements, his rest, and everything he says—toward this goal, so that none of his actions is purposeless, meaning an action that does not lead toward this goal. For example, he should intend his eating, drinking, sexual relations, sleeping, waking, movement, and rest solely for his body’s health. His intention in maintaining bodily health should be that the soul finds its instruments healthy and sound, enabling it to acquire knowledge and the virtues of character and intellect until it reaches that goal.”

: “Someone who conducts himself according to medicine, intending only that his whole body and its limbs be healthy and that his children perform his work and labor for his needs, does not follow a good path. Rather, he should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul may be upright in knowing God. A person cannot understand and contemplate wisdom when hungry or ill, or when one of his limbs hurts. He should intend to have a child who may become wise and great in Israel. A person who follows this path serves God constantly throughout his life, even while doing business or having marital relations, because his purpose in everything is to obtain his needs so that his body may be healthy enough to serve God. Even when sleeping, if he deliberately sleeps to rest his mind and body, lest he become ill and unable to serve God while ill, his sleep itself becomes service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this the sages commanded, 'Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.' Solomon likewise said in his wisdom, 'Know Him in all your ways, and He will straighten your paths.'”

: “The preparation during the six working days is that all one’s deeds should be for Hashem’s sake. As Rambam explains in Hilkhot De’ot and in chapter five of the Eight Chapters, there is no merely neutral activity: when someone acts for bodily pleasure, it is an animal’s action and something forbidden; when his intention is for the sake of Heaven, everything becomes a mitzvah. If he earns a living with the intention of setting fixed times for Torah and raising his children to Torah study, his business too is a mitzvah and service of the Omnipresent. Everything becomes like the construction of the Tabernacle, bringing holiness into the Shabbat that follows, so that it gains additional holiness like the Shabbat following the Tabernacle’s construction.”

: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction: It is written, “I will take My grain in its season,” but also, “You shall gather your grain.” There is no contradiction: one concerns a time when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will; the other, a time when it does not. The Sages taught: What does “You shall gather your grain” teach? Since it says, “This book of Torah shall not leave your mouth,” one might take that literally. “You shall gather your grain” therefore teaches that one should combine Torah with the ordinary conduct of worldly life. This is Rabbi Yishmael’s view. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: If a person plows at plowing time, sows at sowing time, reaps at reaping time, threshes at threshing time, and winnows when the wind blows, what will become of Torah? Rather, when Israel fulfills the Omnipresent’s will, its work is done by others, as it says, “Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks.” When Israel does not fulfill His will, it must do its own work, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.” Moreover, it does the work of others, as it says, “You shall serve your enemy.” Abaye said: Many followed Rabbi Yishmael’s course and succeeded; they followed Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s course and did not succeed.”

: “This is the subject of “If you diligently listen to My commandments ... you shall gather your grain.” They fulfill Hashem’s commandments by resting on Shabbat and in the Sabbatical year, but do not fulfill the Omnipresent’s will to be free solely for the toil of Torah. Their work is therefore done by their own hands. Whoever attains complete devotion to Torah, free for its toil alone in accordance with the Omnipresent’s will, has his work done by others. Not everyone attains this. Thus the Gemara says that many acted according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s approach and did not succeed.”

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

Parallel: Malbim on Psalms 90:17:1, on “Establish the work of our hands upon us”: ““Establish the work of our hands upon us”: A person’s handiwork in material matters is not established upon him; he does not become a support and foundation for what he makes. For example, when someone builds a house to live in, the house is established upon a foundation of stones, and the stones upon the earth, rather than upon the builder. On the contrary, the builder relies upon his house for a dwelling and for shelter from storm and rain. Good deeds in spiritual matters are different: the person himself becomes the foundation and support for his handiwork. For example, the Torah someone studies is established upon his intellect and soul, and a commandment performed for its own sake has its foundation in the soul of the person who performs it. This is the meaning of asking that the work of our hands be established upon us, rather than upon something outside our own being. “And the work of our hands”—let these be things that He “establishes”: may God establish everything we do because it is good in His eyes.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Erev Yom Kippur 6:2: “The truth is that repentance is possible even for one who has not sinned at all: when he merits and grasps the greatness of the Creator, he is ashamed in himself of his service of Hashem, for what is he worth against His greatness and exaltedness, in the manner of what is said (Chullin 89a): ‘When I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me’, meaning greatness in grasping the Creator. This is ‘I gave greatness to Abraham’: not greatness in this world, which was nothing to him, but greatness in comprehension, and he said, ‘I am but dust and ashes.’ So too Moses and Aaron, who grasped more, said ‘And what are we?’, for they were not worth even dust and ashes in their own eyes. And so whenever Israel merits to grasp something of the greatness of the Creator, he is ashamed of his deeds and returns in repentance over his service, which was not as it should be according to His greatness. This is why we say on Rosh Hashanah, ‘Our Father our King, return us in complete repentance before You’, for this is possible even without sin and iniquity. … Submission is possible for anyone, even for the great who did not corrupt anything at all, as stated in the Gemara: ‘you diminish yourselves before Me’.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 4:1: “At the Splitting of the Sea, on the seventh day of Pesach, a maidservant saw at the Sea what Ezekiel did not see (Mekhilta Beshalach and elsewhere), and the holy Rebbe of Izhbitz said that this was the aspect of the seeing that is shown to a person at his beginning. According to what is said in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, that he envied the strength of awakening in the days of youth upon entering the gates of Chassidus; and as the Rokeach wrote, there is no strength like the piety of the beginning.
