Know that these four death penalties stated in the Torah include all punishments; for in every sin a person separates himself from cleaving to the honored Name in different ways, and these four deaths are there to repair the blemish and to unite the letters of the honored Name, so that all the sins are repaired. … Third introduction: these four death penalties were given to the court to punish with them the individual who separated himself from cleaving to Hashem, so that after he receives the punishment he will come to the life of the World to Come; for Hashem, may His Name be blessed, devises means that none who is banished be cast away from Him.”

Parallel: Takanas HaShavin 6:66: “Rather directly by the Sanhedrin, for through this atonement comes at once, as with all those liable to death at the hands of the court and those punished by the court, who are atoned at once and are better off than those punished at the hands of Heaven. For through this they recognize the sin at once, since the court makes their sin known to them and they return in repentance, as they said in Sanhedrin (43b): ‘All who are executed confess.’ What they said, ‘all,’ and so forth, does not mean only by order of the court, for is there no brazen one who defies the court? Rather it came about of itself: through the court’s decree of the punishment upon him and leading him to carry out the judgment, thoughts of repentance were stirred in his heart to return and confess. Only of the nations of the world did they say in Eruvin (19a) that even at the entrance of Gehinnom they do not return, as stated there, because their sin is in the essence of their soul, for such is their essence, and it is impossible for them to return; which is not so with the children of Israel, whose sin is not of their essence, and this holds even of the wicked and of those guilty of grave transgressions.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shevat 1:1: “This month is suited to repairing damage to the covenant. The holy Ari wrote that the six weeks of Shovavim are suited to this, and the four weeks of Bo, Beshalach, Yitro and Mishpatim always fall in this month. … Of this it says, ‘He dwells by its breaches’: even one who has broken through into the sea, the raging waters, will also dwell there to repair the past, again through Torah, awe and prayer. … He says that no refuse will remain from the house of Israel: whoever wishes to become pure will receive help from above to repair the past and overcome the evil inclination in the future. … Nevertheless, none of Israel’s banished will remain banished: ‘Although he has sinned, he remains Israel,’ as Sanhedrin 44a states. … This month corresponds to Asher: whoever turns toward Hashem and wishes to be good can repair everything, and bring holiness into food, Asher’s quality, ‘From Asher, rich is his bread,’ so that it becomes bread of delight. He can repair the damage he caused to the attribute of the righteous one through Torah and the heart’s cry, prayer and awe, the qualities of Moshe and Yosef, whose numerical values together equal Asher.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 51:1: “But it accords with what is said, ‘When Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers,’ like a dream: that in truth He did not rend His purple robe, and it is called rent only because it appears as if torn, but in truth the garment is whole. This is why it says that He will restore it in the future, and why he cites the verse ‘Then our mouth will be filled with laughter’: it will become clear that the garment of splendor, on which every ‘then’ (az) is engraved, which is the joining of alef to zayin, which is the Congregation of Israel, was whole from the start and was never torn. … So too, ‘Those who sow in tears will reap in song’ shows that it will become clear there was nothing at all to weep over, as the Gemara says (Taanit 5a) … at first they thought that hope was lost, since Adar had passed and no rain had fallen, and afterward they saw there had been no cause for worry at all … and the worry and weeping were only like a dream, ‘as a man dreams.’ So too, when Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion they will see that the garment was never torn at all, for even in exile Hashem was the ruler and the king, as it says, ‘I will set My throne in Elam,’ and wherever they were exiled the Shechinah was with them.”

k: volume-i|1967|0|R. Avraham Dov Ber of Ovruch, Bat Ayin,
quote: Parallel: R. Avraham Dov Ber of Ovruch, Bat Ayin, Shemot 55: “One may say that in the portions of Shovavim one must rectify the aspect of Daat, and one can come to this aspect in these portions. The hint to this from the holy Torah is that the book of Bereshit ends, ‘and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt (b’Mitzrayim),’ and the word b’Mitzrayim has the value of the Name of forty-two, and ve’eleh, ‘and these,’ of ‘And these are the names’ (Exodus 1:1), has the value of forty-two. This hints that the Name of forty-two is the names of the children of Israel, the aspect of the Name of the children of Israel, which is light-darkness, the aspect of Daat, to turn darkness into light. ‘Who came to Egypt with Jacob’ means that the Name of forty-two went down with him to Egypt; and when Jacob died they were closed, as said above, and this must be rectified. Therefore it is written in the writings of the Ari, of blessed memory, that during Shovavim one says, in the Shema at bedtime, the verse ‘Let me pass through your land; we will go along the king’s road; we will not turn to the right or to the left,’ hinting that in Shovavim one must rectify the aspect of Daat, to go on the king’s road, which is the aspect of Daat called ‘road.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemot 8:1: “The haftarah of this parashah: ‘On that day a great shofar will be sounded.’ The shofar denotes fear and awe, as it says, ‘Shall a shofar be blown in a city and the people not tremble?’, and the ‘great shofar’ is Binah, as in the holy Zohar (III 266b). That is, when the awe enters the point in the heart, the awakening in the depths of the heart helps even those ‘dispersed in the land of Egypt’: those who know that their root is from Israel, as in Egypt where they were distinguished, only that they are cast away, surrounded by the husk on every side like a fetus in its mother’s womb, as in the Egyptian exile, and they despair. And even ‘those lost in the land of Assyria,’ who have assimilated among the nations and do not know at all that they are of the seed of Israel, nonetheless will also be awakened to repentance through the great shofar. This is the Zohar’s ‘it rules in this world and in the World to Come’: Malkhut and Binah, lower awe and supernal awe, and both are the aspect of the heart; and the crying out is in the heart, as it says, ‘their heart cried out to Hashem,’ and it helps even for this blemish, to repair the root through supernal repentance.”

k: volume-i|1969|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or Einayim, Ki Tisa 3: “[The Sages said that even] the unlearned man has the dread of Shabbat upon him, and so on. This is because on every Shabbat the aspect of Moses is revealed, who returns to Israel the two crowns, which are love and awe, and this is the additional soul. So in every Jew who keeps Shabbat there is revealed da’at, in which love and awe are included, and this is the aspect of Moses. Then, since awe has entered him, as said, he is afraid to lie on Shabbat. Therefore, whoever keeps Shabbat according to its law, even if he worshipped idols like the generation of Enosh, is forgiven, for those crowns were acquired at the standing at Mount Sinai ... and on every Shabbat they are revealed again as they are returned to them, so they return to be as they were at the standing at Mount Sinai, when they received His Godliness, which was freedom from the angel of death; so now there comes about freedom from the sitra achra.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 7:1: “It is the counsel of the evil inclination itself to put into a person’s thoughts that all the warnings and punishments are only to frighten and to exaggerate to a man, like a father who trains his son from his youth, frightening him and exaggerating punishments to him so that he will go in the straight path, but certainly he will not punish his beloved son even if he transgresses his command. ... On this matter we spoke in truth of what is said in the holy Zohar (Mishpatim 123b) on ‘and in all that I have said to you, tishameru’: ‘it should have said tishmeru; but tishameru certainly, that is, I have exaggerated to you about My service, so that you be guarded and no evil reach you.’ ... We said that it hints that precisely through the exaggerations and punishments, ‘in all that I have said to you,’ through this you will be guarded; ... and through this the fear of Hashem will be upon your faces, and so you will be guarded from all evil and will discharge the exaggeration through the fear. But Heaven forbid that one rely on this and make light of the punishments in his eyes, as the evil inclination and Amalek, the root of the serpent, counsel; and therefore, ‘Do not trust in a companion (aluf).’”

k: volume-i|1971|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Mishpatim 22: “Consider the verse, ‘I love my master, my wife, my children; I will not go free … and he shall pierce his ear,’ and the Sages said, ‘the ear that heard, For the children of Israel are servants to Me.’ It is difficult: since he sinned in deed and not in hearing, why should they blemish the ear? ... One may explain further by the words of the Zohar on Parashat Behar on the verse ‘free, for nothing’: free of the mitzvot. The matter is that Israel said, ‘All that Hashem has spoken we will do and we will hear,’ meaning that they do not wish to be exempt from any mitzvah, but are always ready to hear and to do His blessed will, for this they were created, and their whole aim is to hear and to do. Had they said only ‘we will do,’ it would seem that they fulfil the mitzvah merely to discharge their obligation as the law requires; but the trait of the chasid, beyond the letter of the law, is that discharging his obligation is not enough for him, but he burns at every moment to fulfil the commandments of the Creator. This is the aspect of the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, and it says there in the holy Zohar, like that ox on which they place a yoke, to be ready to do its master’s will. This is more essential than fulfilling the mitzvah. ... Therefore one who says, ‘I love … I will not go free,’ blemishes the hearing.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 12:2: “At the time of the giving of the Torah (Shabbat 88a) they tied two crowns to each one of Israel, one for ‘we will do’ and one for ‘we will hear.’ ‘We will do’ corresponds to Abraham our father, whose occupation was the attribute of love and alacrity in the positive commandments, ... and ‘we will hear’ corresponds to Isaac, whose attribute was fear and awe and carefulness in the negative commandments. For hearing does not mean that he hears with this ear and lets it out the other, but that it enters the heart so that he will not transgress it, as we find (Kiddushin 22b): ‘The ear that heard at Mount Sinai, For the children of Israel are servants to Me, and went and acquired a master for himself, shall be pierced’; and as Rashi brings from the Mekhilta: ‘The ear that heard at Mount Sinai, Do not steal,’ and so on. Seemingly, what has the ear done that it should be pierced? The ear heard, and the limbs of action that transgressed what they heard should be pierced! But it is as we said: had the ear heard properly, it would have entered the heart and he would not have transgressed what he heard, as it says (Midrash Rabbah, Haazinu): the ear is to the body as a fumigating vessel to garments, and so on; all 248 limbs of a person live through the ear, as it says, ‘Listen, and your soul shall live.’ And this is the crown of ‘we will hear,’ that it be fixed in the heart to guard against negative commandments.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 5:2: “And afterward [the Zohar] says: servants are exempt from the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, since the yoke of flesh and blood is upon them; and it says that the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven comes first of all. That is as it says, ‘What does Hashem your God ask of you but to fear,’ and as it says, ‘The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem,’ and this is the kingdom of Heaven, as said, for through it one enters the rest of holiness. ... Therefore the Hebrew servant, in his own sabbatical, which is the seventh year, accepts upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven and goes out free. Afterward it says that if he is sunk, Heaven forbid, so far that he says, ‘I love my master,’ ... and then ‘his ear’: why? Because hearing depends on this place. ... As in Rashi on Mishpatim from the Mekhilta: ‘the ear that heard at Mount Sinai, Do not steal, and went and stole, shall be pierced; the ear that heard at Mount Sinai, For the children of Israel are servants to Me,’ and so in the Gemara, Kiddushin 22b. Hearing means that it enter the heart, as it says, ‘Listen, and your soul shall live’; and had the hearing been proper he would not have transgressed this, for he would have accepted upon himself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven properly and would not have accepted the yoke of flesh and blood. And this is the meaning of ‘hearing depends on this place,’ on Malkhut.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Matot 11:1: “‘I shall sing with praises, to enter within the gates of the field of apples.’ It is written, ‘Open for me the gates of righteousness’; righteousness (tzedek) denotes the attribute of Malkhut, as in Patach Eliyahu, ‘tzedek is the holy Malkhut.’ ‘I will enter them and thank Yah’: one can come to this through songs and praises. ... So too the gates of the Garden of Eden are called, which is also the aspect of the field of apples, as we said, for it is written afterward, ‘This is the gate of Hashem; the righteous shall enter it.’ This is what they answered Alexander of Macedon at the gates of the Garden of Eden, that only the righteous may enter (Tamid 32b). And in the future each one will be clarified as being in the aspect of a righteous man, as it says, ‘And your people are all righteous.’ ... On Shabbat, which corresponds to Malkhut, the mouth, which we call the Oral Torah, ... when a person speaks and is in the aspect of the mouth of Hashem, the words are effective to enter the heart, ‘and his heart will understand and he will repent.’ Therefore it is written, ‘It is good to give thanks to Hashem’: through the confession itself he will merit that it enter the heart, and he will confess and forsake, and he will be included in ‘your people are all righteous,’ so that he can come into the gates of righteousness, the gate through which the righteous enter.”

k: volume-i|1975|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayera 30: “One comes to this by removing the foreskin, for the foreskin came after the sin, since ‘God made man upright,’ and the foreskin is the part of the sitra achra, which is the lip of falsehood and will have no standing in the future. Through the removal of the foreskin he is called ‘a seed of truth,’ as it is written, ‘Save my soul from the lip of falsehood,’ and the Holy One, blessed be He, saved the souls of Israel from the lip of falsehood through the removal of the foreskin; ... and that is the covenant of the flesh. So too there is a deceitful tongue in speech, from which afterward, in the days of the Dispersion, came the spread into seventy languages; but to Israel there remained the holy tongue, which is ‘the lip of truth that shall be established forever.’ These are the two covenants, as it says (Sefer Yetzirah): He made a covenant with him between the ten toes of his feet, which is circumcision, and between the ten fingers of his hands, which is the tongue, for the main vitality is in these two places. Therefore they have the guarding of ‘the flame of the revolving sword, to guard the way to the Tree of Life,’ and through the two covenants they take hold of the Tree of Life.”

k: volume-i|1976|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Emor 17:3: “In the passage of the showbread, ‘On the Sabbath day he shall arrange it’: as it is written, ‘Come, eat of my bread,’ so that the receiving of the flow of blessing from Heaven be attached to its supernal root; this is the inwardness of the flow. ... The root of the bread from Heaven, which flows on the holy Sabbath upon all the days of the week through the power of the Torah, accords with the preparation of the Children of Israel to whom the Torah was given. Just as there are fifty-three portions of the Torah, and every Shabbat a different portion is read, so it is in Heaven ... The Torah is a gift to the Children of Israel, and according to their level so the Torah is revealed to them, for there are seventy faces to the Torah. Every Shabbat the flow is renewed through the power of the Torah. [‘In His goodness He renews’ refers to the Torah, which is called good, and of Shabbat it is written, ‘It is good to give thanks’; and this is the allusion in ‘Let us invite her now with a new table.’]”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 5:1: “We say ‘with a new table’ because each Shabbat brings a new holiness, since Shabbat is called a bride, and a bride is a bride only seven days; it follows that each Shabbat has a new holiness, as we say, ‘But new faces, and spirits with souls,’ meaning that each Shabbat a Jew attains a new additional soul. ... Afterward we say, ‘and a table with bread in the north,’ using the word shulchan, which is the Holy Tongue and alludes to the Written Torah; but here we say pesora, in the language of Targum, which is the hind side of the Holy Tongue and alludes to the Oral Torah. The Oral Torah was founded chiefly in Babylonia ... and renewal belongs chiefly to the Oral Torah, for the letters of the Written Torah are counted and numbered. Therefore we say ‘with a new table’ in the language of Targum.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 4:4: “We say [at the redemption of the firstborn], ‘who sanctified the fetus in its mother’s womb,’ for even in its mother’s womb, where it does not yet have an evil inclination, since the soul comes from the time of formation and the evil inclination from the time of emergence, as stated in Sanhedrin 91b, it has holiness, which they merited from our father Jacob. This is what is said in Niddah 30b, that in its mother’s womb a lamp burns above its head and it gazes from one end of the world to the other. It is like the light created on the first day, by which Adam gazed from one end of the world to the other, as stated in Chagigah 12a, since there is no evil inclination. And te’omim is written lacking an alef, for the letters of alef spell pele, wonder, which is the crownlet of the yod, which is from the supernal Crown.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 6:1: “So too here: at the very beginning of Israel’s entry into the Land, ‘the land shall rest a Sabbath unto Hashem,’ that it should always be like Sabbaths, when they would be free only for Torah and divine service, as at the beginning of creation, ‘and I was created to serve my Maker’ (Kiddushin 82a), with their work done by others, as at the giving of the Torah, ‘I said, you are angels.’ But afterward it is written, ‘Six years you shall sow your field … and gather in its produce,’ in a manner that one must toil at labor. ‘But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of rest for the land’: that is, as with Shabbat, which has a holiness fixed and established from Hashem (Pesachim 117b), and is nevertheless called ‘the first of the holy convocations’ (‘Remember it to sanctify it,’ ‘Observe it to sanctify it’), so in Shemitah too there is holiness from Hashem, and Israel also bring holiness into Shemitah by fulfilling the mitzvah of Shemitah. This is ‘a Sabbath unto Hashem, as is said of the Sabbath of Creation.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kuntres Shvitas Shabbos 6:1: “However, it is simple in my eyes that the Rambam holds they are not to be counted as positive commandments, since they were not stated in the language of command, but only as explaining the preceding commandment ‘you shall rest’ or the prohibition ‘you shall not do’: ‘in order that your ox may rest,’ ‘and may be refreshed,’ meaning that through your resting they too will rest, and only by implication were a prohibition and an obligation concerning their rest stated. … And perhaps one could suggest, according to what I wrote above, that ‘you shall rest’ in Parashat Mishpatim refers to Shabbat in the Shemitah year, to restore it to its prohibition, and is not a positive commandment; then one can say that its concluding clause, ‘in order that, etc.,’ also refers to it, to restore the resting of one’s animal in Shemitah as on all other Sabbaths, so that it stays under the prohibition ‘you shall not do any work … nor your cattle’ of the Ten Commandments, and is not a mitzvah of its own.”

k: volume-i|1981|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Mishpatim 10:2: “The whole matter of receiving the Torah was to rectify the realm of action through the agency of the Children of Israel. So too Shabbat, as it is written, ‘Six days you shall do your deeds … and on the seventh day you shall rest, in order that your ox may rest,’ and so forth. We explained it through the nullification of the days of action to Shabbat, as it is said, to remember Shabbat every day. And when the holy Shabbat comes and one sets aside all labors, the holiness of Shabbat is thereby drawn into the realm of action as well; through this ‘your ox and your donkey may rest,’ which is the rectification of materiality, of the animal soul and of all action. ‘In order that it may rest’ may also be explained as a promise for the future: through the nullification of the material, even if one cannot subdue it and rectify it completely, then according to one’s toil in this world (whoever toiled on the eve of Shabbat will eat on Shabbat), in the future, on the day that is entirely Shabbat, your ox and your donkey will truly rest in completeness. For then will come the final rectification for each according to his service in this world, and a slight taste of it is in every holy Shabbat, which is a semblance of the World to Come.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Re'eh 1:1: “It says there first, ‘And you shall serve Hashem your God,’ in the plural, and afterward ‘and He will bless your bread … from your midst,’ in the singular; so too in Parashat Eikev it opens in the plural, ‘you will hearken, and keep and do,’ and afterward the blessings, ‘Hashem your God will keep for you,’ all in the singular. The matter is that at first, before the blessing, they are still in the aspect of many, not yet on the level of ‘like one man’; but after the service, when the blessing comes, they all become like one man with one heart, as we find at the giving of the Torah, where it says ‘and Israel encamped there,’ and the Mekhilta expounded: like one man with one heart. Therefore it is written first ‘and you shall serve,’ in the plural, for they are not yet like one man; and afterward ‘and He will bless your bread and your water’ in the singular, meaning that Hashem allots to each one his portion of bread, specifically what he needs for words of Torah and service. And afterward He said ‘and I will remove sickness from your midst,’ for afterward they all became like one man with one heart, and therefore it is written in the singular.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuos 8:1: “One may say that this is alluded to in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 18a): ‘He Who fashions their hearts together’: if you say it means that He created everyone and unites their hearts with one another, do we not see that it is not so? That is, we see that they have differences of opinion and division of hearts. Rather, say: the Creator sees their hearts together. That is, when the illumination of the Creator of all appears in the hearts of Israel, then truly their hearts are united as one. This is the union of the Holy One blessed be He and the Congregation of Israel, which belongs specifically to the festival, as said above, and especially to this festival, the time of the giving of the Torah, as it is written, ‘and Israel encamped there opposite the mountain,’ and Rashi explained: like one man with one heart; that is, through the revelation of the illumination of the Creator of all in the souls of Israel, their hearts were united as one, like one man with one heart.”

k: volume-i|1984|0|R. Chaim Tyrer of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayi
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Tyrer of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Shemot 23:26:9: “This is called ‘she has cast down many slain’: these mitzvot are like stillborn infants, born in the body alone without the life of the soul shining in them. This is the aspect of meshakeilah stated in the verse, one who is bereaved of her children, for the main children are the mitzvot and good deeds, as the Sages said, ‘the offspring of the righteous are good deeds.’ When the mitzvot are not complete in body and soul, he has, Heaven forbid, been bereaved of his children, so that they lack the life of the soul to fly upward. And one who does not do mitzvot at all is the aspect of akar, barren, who does not give birth at all. It is known from the holy Zohar (I 224a) that if among all a person’s days there are found a day or two that are desolate and dry of mitzvot and good deeds, in which he did not engage, they do not enter the number of his days. This is the blessing the Holy One blessed be He gave His people Israel when they serve Hashem their God, as it says, ‘And you shall serve Hashem your God’: that He will help them … that there be no meshakeilah or akarah in your land, that you not have these aspects of doing mitzvot like stillborn infants without a soul, or of not doing them at all, but that you always fulfill your mitzvot properly for His service. And then ‘the number of your days I will fulfill’: that you will not lack even one day of all your days, like our father Abraham, who ‘came with

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukosai 10:2: “For it is written, ‘For it is a statute (chok) for Israel,’ and from it they expounded (Beitzah 16a) that all of a person’s sustenance is allotted from Rosh Hashanah. ‘A person’ means Israel, who are called adam, and chok is a term for food: that is, Hashem allots the sustenance of each one of Israel, as much as will benefit him for the service of Hashem. This is ‘Feed me my allotted bread’ that King Solomon, peace be upon him, requested; although his meal for one day was great, as stated in the verse, nevertheless it was his allotted bread. So it is stated (Eruvin 64a) of Rav Nachman, who was the son-in-law of the Nasi’s house: ‘As long as I have not drunk a revi’it of wine my mind is not clear,’ and likewise unless he ate the meat of an ox (Bava Kamma 72a, as Tosafot explain), for he needed meat and wine for Torah, and that was his allotted bread. … Through the Grace after Meals it helps that the eating be only from the good and be one’s allotted bread that serves the service of Hashem, and not lead to the rule of the evil inclination.”

k: volume-i|1986|0|R. Moshe Chaim Ephraim of Sudilkov, Dege
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Chaim Ephraim of Sudilkov, Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Mishpatim 11: “Or one may say: ‘And you shall serve Hashem your God, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.’ To explain the change of language in the verse: regarding service it uses the plural, ‘and you shall serve,’ and afterward it concludes in the singular, ‘your bread,’ and so forth. One may say that this is a true double blessing, for service is better in a multitude, both in the material and in the spiritual. … The righteous before the Shechinah are like a candle before a torch, and the Sages said that when one person studies, the Shechinah stands opposite him. When a torch comes opposite a candle, the candle is extinguished by the light of the torch; so when one studies alone and the Shechinah rests there, he is like a candle before the torch, and the Shechinah must, as it were, contract itself and clothe itself as a small torch so that the candle not be extinguished. But when many serve Hashem and study, the torch grows and the light of the Shechinah spreads more toward those who go out to meet it in Torah and service. … This is ‘And you shall serve Hashem your God’ in the plural: that you merit to serve Hashem in a multitude, openly, and the light of the Shechinah increases toward the lights of the souls that serve. Therefore it is written in the plural, for this is a great blessing. ‘And He will bless your bread’ is in the singular, for there the

Parallel: Et HaOchel 12:1: “When one’s eating is as it should be, that is, with the knowledge that Hashem, blessed be He, is the one who feeds, of this it is said, ‘And He will bless your bread [and your water], and I will remove [sickness from your midst],’ that the bread and water he eats and drinks will have the power to remove every kind of sickness. For a thing that Hashem established to give life to a person’s soul surely holds a power of life from Hashem, and surely has the power to sustain his life completely so that no sickness befall him; it even has the power of lasting forever so that death not befall him at all, for the power of food is to hold his life in him all the days of the world. Only through the sin of Adam with food was death decreed, that is, a spoiling of the power of sustaining life that is in food. … The two draw one from the other, as it is written, ‘When his belly is full, he commits evil’ (Berakhot 32a); and through Eve’s eating from the Tree of Knowledge she caused the serpent to come upon her afterward.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 11:1: “The Zohar says that when they couple together, there goes forth from their strength what is called ‘dog’ … ‘Behold, I hand you over to the dog,’ immediately ‘and Amalek came’; and Rabbi Chaim Vital wrote that the inwardness of shor and chamor, the vav of shor and the mem-vav of chamor, has the numerical value of kelev. This is the husk of Amalek, which barks without reason. It stands opposite the holiness of Atika, which is above the grasp of human intellect; so the husk of Amalek is against reason, as there, after the splitting of the Sea, when it is written, ‘Peoples heard and trembled,’ and ‘no spirit remained in any man,’ as Rahab said, yet he paid no heed to it. Now on Shabbat there is a revelation of Atika: on the day of Shabbat the revelation is still concealed, and at the third meal the Forehead of Atika is revealed, when the aspect of Atika comes into revelation, that is, the light of the Face. Then the husk of Amalek is nullified, for it becomes clear that Israel are bound to the root of holiness; and then ‘they are cast outside and do not enter, these brazen dogs,’ for the husk of Amalek is nullified, since Israel merit to be bound to the root and to the light of the face of the living King.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Adar 3:1: “Opposite this in holiness they said (Bava Batra 58a), ‘A man before the Shechinah is like an ape before a man.’ For the root of the commandment ‘and you shall walk in His ways’ is that Hashem emanated, for the creation of the world, words of Torah and mitzvot by which He conducts His world, and commanded Israel to walk in His ways and fulfill the mitzvot that He fulfills first … and so all the mitzvot are a likening to the ways of Hashem, and this is ‘like an ape before the Shechinah.’ In Israel the letter kuf alludes to kadosh, holy (Shabbat 104a), and it is written, ‘You shall be holy, for I am holy’ … that they be separate and set apart from all matters of this world. This is the work of the month of Adar, which was formed through the letter kuf, kadosh. It comes after the month of Shevat, formed through the letter tzadi, of swallowing, to rectify eating so that it be in holiness, which is the rectification of the root of the serpent’s enticement. Thereby the holiness of the covenant, the aspect of tzaddik, who fences himself against desire, is rectified; then comes the month of Adar, formed through the letter kuf, kadosh, for ‘whoever fences himself against immorality is called holy.’ Therefore in this month was the blotting out of Amalek, whose whole accusation is against the holiness of the covenant.”

k: volume-i|1990|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Adar 1:3: “In the Zohar (Terumah 148b): ‘The Woman of Valor, that mark and letter of hers is the letter heh, and so it appears to her. The harlot woman, that mark and letter of hers is in the same pattern, but it is not formed to be so; her letter is kuf, her letter adorned in the adornment of the letter heh, like an ape beside human beings, which goes after a person and is not formed to do so.’ Understand from this that the kingdom of Heaven, the holy kingdom, is alluded to in the letter heh, and the kingdom of the Other Side is alluded to in the letter kuf; and whoever adds, detracts. The number of kuf exceeds the number of heh by ninety-five. From this understand what is said in the Megillah, ‘After these things the king (ha-melech, ninety-five) Ahasuerus promoted Haman (ninety-five),’ to raise himself above the kingdom of Heaven and above Israel, the children of kings. … The letter kuf reigns in Adar and the letter heh in Nisan; and just as the kingdom of Heaven grew strong in the month of Nisan through its mark and letter heh, so the guilty kingdom sought to grow strong in the month of Adar through its mark and letter kuf, like an ape before a man. Through this ‘the king promoted Haman,’ the added number, and ‘for a hand is upon the throne of Yah’ (ninety-five), ‘Hashem has war with Amalek’ (Exodus 17:16).”

k: volume-i|1991|0|R. Chaim Vital (Arizal), Pri Etz Chaim,
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 24:1
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Vital (Arizal), Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 24:1, 24:4: “On Motzaei Shabbat, when you say ‘And let the pleasantness (no’am) be,’ you must say it standing, to receive the returning light from the secret of Binah, which is called no’am. … We say ‘And let the pleasantness be’ as a drawing of Binah, which is called no’am; and because now there is no union, and the addition does not come about of itself, we therefore pray. For what we do every day by our own effort comes about of itself on Shabbat; therefore we pray, ‘and establish the work of our hands upon us,’ for it is the union that is made through us, that it be established and completed through us. … He explained which are the two unions. Corresponding to the first he said, ‘and establish the work of our hands upon us.’ Its meaning is that after what was done on Shabbat by itself, it is now done through our prayer and the work of our hands on the weekdays; this is ‘and the work of our hands,’ meaning that this union is made by us on the weekdays, ‘establish it upon us’ through this no’am.”

k: volume-i|1992|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Yitro 19:3: “It is written, ‘And let the pleasantness of Hashem our God be upon us, and the work of our hands,’ and so forth. The pleasantness of Hashem is the soul that descends on the holy Shabbat and spreads a shelter of peace over us. ‘And establish the work of our hands upon us’ means that a person must receive the illumination of Shabbat and cleave to it, so that an illumination from the day of Shabbat remains in him; this is the aspect of the three days after Shabbat. Afterward, by this power, he can merit to draw an illumination on the next holy Shabbat, and this is the three days before Shabbat. Of this it is written, ‘and the work of our hands, establish it’: that is, to arouse by the work of our hands the root of Shabbat above. … So it is with all the mitzvot, … ‘one mitzvah draws another mitzvah,’ and all six hundred thirteen mitzvot depend on one another and are one unity.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 4:4: “We have already spoken about what is said in the formula of Pidyon HaBen, ‘Who sanctified the embryo in its mother’s womb,’ on which the Rosh (Kiddushin ch. 1, end of siman 41) asked that the Merciful One made the sanctity of the firstborn depend on the opening of the womb. But at the birth of Jacob their defilement had already ceased, since he was like Adam before the corruption, as it says (Shabbat 146a): ‘For three generations the defilement did not cease … Jacob fathered twelve tribes in whom there was no flaw.’ Only it was not revealed until the Giving of the Torah, when it was revealed that their defilement had ceased entirely; this is the statement, ‘Israel who stood at Mount Sinai, their defilement ceased.’ And though the Gemara says this disputes Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, it is known that in the disputes of the Sages both are the words of the living God. This is what we say, ‘Who sanctified the embryo in its mother’s womb’: while still in its mother’s womb, where it has no evil inclination yet, for the soul is from the time of formation and the evil inclination from the time of emergence (Sanhedrin 91b), it possesses a holiness that they merited from Jacob our father. And this is what is said (Niddah 30b), that in its mother’s womb a lamp is lit above its head and it gazes from one end of the world to the other. It is like the light created on the first day, by which Adam gazed from one end of the world to the other (Chagi

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 8:2: “The Ramban wrote that the command ‘You shall be holy’ is a positive commandment for every Jew: sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you. That is, one should not feel self-gratification, for that is the counsel of the serpent, as we find regarding Jesse, the father of David, of whom the verse ‘daughter of Nachash’ is expounded, that he died through the counsel of the serpent (Shabbat 55b). And we find in the Midrash Rabbah (beginning of Tazria, in the Yalkut’s reading): ‘Behold, I was formed in iniquity’ (be-avon, written full): even if one is the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that there be no aspect of iniquity in him. That is, he never did any forbidden act; only he felt self-gratification, which is the counsel of the serpent, caused when it cast defilement into Eve (Shabbat 146a), so that each of their descendants feels self-gratification. For this came the commandment ‘You shall be holy’: sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you, to bring holiness into optional matters, like Rabbeinu HaKadosh, who said of himself, ‘I did not derive benefit even with my little finger.’ Tosafot (Avodah Zarah 11a) already asked from the statement that delicacies never ceased from their table; but the explanation is that he was like Jacob our father, who felt no gratification at all, and all his enjoyments were in holiness, like Adam before the sin.”

k: volume-i|1995|0|R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chai
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Bereshit 30:26: “‘Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you.’ Seemingly the service was for the wives alone, not for the children, and he should have said, ‘Give me my wives for whom I have served you.’ But it is known what the Sages said (Bereshit Rabbah 70:18) on the verse ‘Give me my wife’ (Genesis 29:21): even the most vulgar of men does not speak this way! Rather, he said it in order to raise offspring. For Jacob was entirely stripped of the aspect of evil, and did not know at all whether there was in this any desire or craving other than for the sake of Hashem, to fulfill the commandment to be fruitful and multiply. Just as a person is not ashamed to say to his friend, ‘Give me tefillin to put on,’ so he was not ashamed to say, ‘Give me my wife,’ to fulfill through her Hashem’s commandment to be fruitful and multiply. Therefore he said here, ‘Give me my wives and my children for whom I served you,’ for all the service was only for these children whom his wives would bear.”

k: volume-i|1996|0|R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat
quote: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat Levi, Shemot, Bo 31: “Further it may be explained: ‘Hashem spoke to Moses: Sanctify unto Me every firstborn … among the children of Israel … And Moses said to the people: Remember this day …’ (Exodus 13:1–4). The Ari wrote that this is why Moses said ‘Remember this day’ and only afterward ‘you shall set apart every first issue of the womb’, though seemingly he should have said ‘you shall set apart’ immediately when the Holy One said ‘Sanctify unto Me every firstborn’. For the sanctification of the firstborn applies only to Israel, but the Mixed Multitude that came up with Israel from Egypt were not yet rectified, and it was not fitting to sanctify their firstborn. Moses feared great jealousy among the Mixed Multitude, so he first said a different commandment that would apply equally to all. To me it seems that he did not say the commandment of sanctifying the firstborn immediately, and first spoke of Pesach and matzah, for this reason: the Holy One renewed His world from nothing, and the first creation grasps the Ayin that renews His whole world in His goodness, called ‘and wisdom shall be found from Ayin’ (Job 28:12). This applies in World, Year and Soul. In the World it is matzah, which alludes to grasping the Renewer, the first taste that remains. In the Year it is alluded to in Pesach, for in it we saw the Holy One as the Renewer who did miracles for us, and Nisan is the first of the months of the year. In the Soul it is

Parallel: Maharal, Gevurot Hashem 39:1–2: “‘And it shall be for a sign upon your hand and for a memorial between your eyes’ (Exodus 13:9) … Because at the Exodus from Egypt the Holy One performed signs and wonders with Israel, showing that the Name Hashem, the unique Name that does great wonders, is called upon them, this is written in the tefillin, and the tefillin are bound upon a person to show that the great and holy Name is called upon them. This is what is written (Deuteronomy 28:10): ‘And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of Hashem is called upon you, and they shall fear you’, and Rabbi Eliezer said, these are the tefillin of the head (Berakhot 6a). … And Rabbi Eliezer said ‘these are the tefillin of the head’ because the tefillin on the arm show that Israel cleave to the Holy One, and therefore ‘and you shall bind them’ is written of them (Deuteronomy 6:8). This is the difference between the tefillin of the hand and the tefillin of the head: the hand-tefillin are the joining and cleaving of Israel to the Holy One, and from that side there is no fear, only joining and cleaving to Him, for where there is joining there is no fear. But the head-tefillin, where there is no binding, only that the Name is called upon them; and in that His Name is called upon them He is separate from them, for He is called ‘the God of Israel’ (Exodus 5:1), and in being their God He is separate from them; and from this side there is fear.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 44:1: “In the Gemara (Berakhot 6a): ‘Whence do we know that the Holy One puts on tefillin? … And by the arm of His strength, these are tefillin, as it says, Hashem will give strength to His people; and whence that tefillin are strength for Israel? As it is written, And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of Hashem is called upon you … these are the tefillin of the head.’ The phrase ‘the arm of His strength’ implies the hand-tefillin, yet the proof is brought from the head-tefillin. … The matter of the tefillin of the Master of the world, who is praised in the praise of Israel, is this: in Israel, the hand-tefillin mean subjugating the desires and thoughts of our heart to His service, for they are placed opposite the heart; and the head-tefillin mean meriting to be bound at the root, the skull of the tefillin, Keter Elyon, which is above Chokhmah, the brain. But it is not in a person’s hand to bring about through his own action that he be bound at the root, only through the help of Hashem, for the beginning of Keter is the intellect hidden from all thought. And from the tefillin of Israel are made, with Hashem, the hand-tefillin. This is the meaning of ‘and by the arm of His strength, these are tefillin’, the hand-tefillin of the Master of the world. And it is written ‘Hashem will give strength to His people’: Hashem gives strength and power to Israel, and from this they merit to be bound at the root.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 26:1: “It is stated in the holy Zohar (III 230a): He is Truth and She is Faith. For the essence of the Unity is when one recognizes, like Jacob our father, ‘You are He before the world was created, You are He since the world was created’: even after the creation there is nothing besides Him. To this the Name Havayah points: He was, is, and will be. But this Name is not pronounced in this world, for there is no grasp of this in this world, where one sees forces that seem to act against His will. Only Jacob our father recognized the Unity in the attribute of Truth; but the tribes said, ‘Just as there is only One in your heart, so there is only One in our heart’ (Pesachim 56a); that is, even though we do not recognize it in the attribute of Truth, we recognize the Unity through faith. And this is the root of faith. … Faith, which one can transmit to another, as Rabbi Eliezer said to his students, ‘May the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood’ (Berakhot 28b); but of the Name Havayah it is written, ‘Her husband is known in the gates’, and in the holy Zohar (I 103b): this is the Holy One, who is known and cleaved to according to what each one measures in his heart … and this is ‘the secret of Hashem is for those who fear Him’, which one cannot pass on to his fellow.”

k: volume-i|2000|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Shaar
ref: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 7:1-10
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 7: “With this we can understand what is written in the holy Zohar, that the verse ‘Hear, O Israel’ is the Higher Unity, and ‘Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever’ is the Lower Unity, for va’ed is echad with its letters exchanged. For the cause and reason of this contraction and concealment, by which the Holy One concealed the life-force of the world so that the world would appear a thing separate in itself, is known to all: the purpose of the creation of the world is the revelation of His kingship, for there is no king without a people. … Although He is above place and time, He is nevertheless found also below, in place and time; that is, He unites with His attribute of Kingship, from which place and time are drawn and come into being. This is the Lower Unity, the interweaving of Havayah with Adnut. … And from what has been explained one will understand what is written, ‘I, Hashem, have not changed’: there is no change at all; as He was alone before the world was created, so He is alone after it was created. This is what we say, ‘You are He before the world was created, You are He since the world was created,’ with no change in His essence or His knowledge, for in knowing Himself He knows all creatures, since all is from Him and nullified in existence before Him.”

k: volume-i|2001|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Shemot 11:2: “After the redemption from Egypt Israel were raised above nature, and the Torah was given to them, which is the Tree of Life and the root of all creation; hence they are free men, and therefore they are commanded to remember the Exodus every day. And therefore it is written, ‘But the more they afflicted them [the more they multiplied]’: that is, in this way Hashem, blessed be He, conducted matters, that the exile should be a preparation for the redemption that follows, as it says in the Midrash: three gifts were given through suffering, Torah, the Land of Israel and the World to Come. And this is for the reason of ‘he that loves him disciplines him early,’ see the Midrash there. That is, the Holy One, blessed be He, wished the gifts to be something enduring; therefore He preceded their giving with suffering. And just as the Egyptian exile was suffering for the sake of the gift of the Torah, so too we must understand the sufferings of our bitter exile, which is a preparation for the days of Mashiach and for the World to Come.”

k: volume-i|2002|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Shemot 21:4: “It is stated in the Midrash on the verse ‘You shall no longer give [the people straw]… let the work be heavier’ that he would not allow them to rest on Shabbat, according to the Midrash that Moses our teacher had instituted the Sabbath for them; see there. The matter is as the Sages said: the roads seek their appointed task; and so too the times that were set apart for Israel. Even though the Sabbath had not yet been given to them, nevertheless in the supernal root the Sabbath was set apart for them. Therefore the righteous, such as the Patriarchs and Moses our teacher, sensed the holiness of the Sabbath and brought it from potential into actuality even before it was given. And not only that, but even that wicked Pharaoh understood that they had an illumination of the redemption through the power of the rest on the Sabbath day. … And therefore there is freedom on Shabbat, for the whole exile is in the part of the body below and not in the part of the soul, which is the aspect of freedom. Therefore Shabbat is a remembrance of the Exodus, for in every Shabbat there is a measure of redemption; all the more so now that the Sabbath has already been given to us.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 3:2: “And so too the mitzvah of Shabbat, as it is written, ‘On the day that Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow and from your trouble and from the hard labor,’ which is expounded in the holy Zohar (I 48b) as the Sabbath day, the ‘day of giving rest,’ when Hashem, blessed be He, grants rest from the evil inclination and from all evil. Therefore He stated the reason, ‘And you shall remember [that you were a slave in the land of Egypt], and Hashem your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand… therefore Hashem your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day’; that is, a Jew is able to draw holiness into Shabbat. And the remembrance of Egypt comes in these three mitzvot, for by remembering that Hashem brought us out then, even though we were like an embryo in its mother’s womb, through this the light of the aspect of Atika will shine forth in the heart, as it did at the Exodus.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sh’lach 5:1: “The aspect of chen (favor) is applied to something that is above a person’s grasp. As it is said, ‘And Noach found favor,’ and it says in the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah 28), ‘Even Noach ... was not worthy, except that he found favor’; and as they said (Megillah 13a), ‘Esther was greenish, and a thread of kindness was drawn over her,’ meaning not by virtue of beauty but by bearing favor, as it says, ‘And Esther bore favor.’ And as it is said of Moshe our teacher, ‘For how shall it be known that I have found favor in Your eyes, I and Your people’; for of Moshe it is said, ‘and she saw him that he was good,’ immediately at the time of his birth, before his own choice came into play, and that is by way of finding favor in His blessed eyes. So too the holiness of Israel, as it is said, ‘The people that survived the sword found favor in the wilderness’ ... for Israel belong to Hashem even without their choice ... and that is only by way of finding favor in His blessed eyes, as it is said, ‘Was not Esav Yaakov’s brother ... yet I loved Yaakov,’ and as the Sages said (Gittin 57a), ‘Come and see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations.’ And the holiness of the Shabbat day is likewise only by way of finding favor, beyond comprehension, as it says, ‘Most coveted of days You called it,’ from the side of desire.”

k: volume-i|2005|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Noach 32: “‘And he called his name Noach ... this one will comfort us (yenachamenu).’ It is taught that he was born circumcised. Through the sin of man the foreskin was drawn over and covers the inner flesh, and from this came the whole curse, ‘our work and the toil of our hands’ ... Noach, who was born circumcised, revealed in himself the inner form, where Hashem commanded the blessing; he was called ‘this one,’ a blessed form without dross. That is the comfort that came out to teach about the whole: that beneath the foreskin a hidden light is found. Therefore ‘Noach found favor in the eyes of Hashem,’ for favor rests on the inner form. So too in the time of holy Shabbat, the day of rest, as it is written ‘and He rested (vayanach),’ there is favor, and that is the comfort, as it says, ‘He called his name Noach ... this one will comfort us.’ Therefore Shabbat is a remembrance of the work of creation, as it is written, ‘And God saw ... and behold it was very good,’ and the Midrash says that the Holy One said, ‘My world, My world, if only you would find favor before Me as at this hour.’ On every holy Shabbat this favor is present; therefore it is a remembrance of the work of creation.”

Parallel: Maharal, Gevurot Hashem 18:2–3: “‘And she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter’ (Exodus 2:10): our Sages were roused in Midrash Rabbah (Shemot Rabbah 1:26) to the reason that Moshe our teacher was raised in Pharaoh’s house, when the rescue of Moshe could have come through some other Egyptian without his being in Pharaoh’s house. That is what they said there: ‘... and even King Mashiach, who is destined to exact punishment from Edom, dwells with them in the province,’ as it says, ‘There the calf shall graze and there it shall lie down.’ This matter is very wondrous to those who understand: privation clings to existing things, and from the side of the privation that clings to them another form takes hold. Thus the form that comes is drawn after the thing in which the privation lies, for the privation within the existing thing itself brings on another form. Therefore he said that King Mashiach dwells with them in the province: the form that will come, the kingship of Mashiach, is drawn after the thing in which the privation lies; because privation clings to the kingdom of Edom, the world receives the kingship of King Mashiach, as though they were wholly attached to one another. For this reason Yaakov’s hand held Esav’s heel.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tu BiShvat 2:1: “I heard from the holy Rav, of blessed memory, that the root of Moshe our teacher was the utterance ‘I am (Anochi),’ and the root of Rabbi Akiva was the utterance ‘You shall have no (lo yihyeh lecha).’ And the Arizal wrote that Rabbi Akiva was the root of the Oral Torah ... That is, the root of Moshe our teacher was the Written Torah, which is the Tree of Life, to bring words of Torah into ‘the heart of the wise man at his right.’ Moshe our teacher knew of no evil, for when he was born the house filled with light (Sotah 12a), and he wanted all Israel to be so, as at the Giving of the Torah, as it is written, ‘I said: you are godly beings.’ And Rabbi Akiva, who was a son of converts and said ‘When I was an unlearned man’ (Pesachim 49b), had as his root the Oral Torah, which is the ‘much wisdom’ that repairs the ‘much anger,’ as they said (Nedarim 22b): ‘Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah.’ This is why his root was the utterance ‘You shall have no,’ which is to uproot and eradicate evil from the heart of the fool, so that there be only the Tree of Knowledge of good. And this is what the holy Zohar says: from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, that is prohibited and permitted, fit and unfit, impure and pure.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 1:6–7: “The Yetzer Hara from the very beginning of the husk does not entice to plain evil; rather he disguises himself as one who shows the way to good, as we find with Samael, the angel of Esav, of whom it says (Chullin 91a), ‘He appeared to him as a Torah scholar’ ... He puts darkness for light and calls evil good, and he is the root of the serpent, which in truth includes all the husks. For although the serpent’s enticement began with desire, it nevertheless also contained the husk of jealousy and murder, since he knew he would bring death into the world. We find that he said, ‘You shall surely not die’; how could he say so, when Hashem had said explicitly, ‘on the day you eat of it you shall surely die’? But first he put into Chavah’s heart that she changed it and said ‘lest you die,’ and afterward he told her, ‘You shall surely not die’: that is, it is true that Hashem was concerned for your good and said not to eat of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil lest you taste of its evil side and die; but He wants even more that you eat of it and taste of the good alone, and then ‘you will be like God.’”

k: volume-i|2009|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 22: “Consider the matter of the staff that became a serpent, and the Midrash comparing the kingdoms to a serpent, and in parashat Shemot, ‘Cast it to the ground ... and Moshe fled from it ... grasp its tail.’ The matter is that the exile came to sift out the mixture of good and evil made through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge ... and this itself is the turning of the serpent into a staff and the staff into a serpent. His blessed will was that man cleave to the Tree of Life through the Torah, the inner mode of His governance, and were it not for the sin, nature would not hold man back at all ... Therefore Israel had to be in Egypt before they merited to receive the Torah, to repair the way of nature, for it is in the power of a man of Israel to nullify nature, and then the serpent becomes a staff. For the staff is the end of His blessed governance, and from there it separates to clothe itself in physicality and nature, and there the Other Side grows strong to become a serpent ... All of this comes through the withdrawal of holiness, as it says, ‘Cast it to the ground.’ But when the Holy One said to him, ‘Put forth your hand,’ which is the power of Moshe, the master of Torah, ‘grasp its tail,’ at once it turned from a serpent into a staff, and all of nature became subject to the inner dimension, and the Other Side flees.”

k: volume-i|2011|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayishlach 1:1–3: “‘I have oxen and donkeys’: in the Midrash, ‘ox’ is the one anointed for war ... ‘donkey’ is King Mashiach, as it says, ‘a poor man riding on a donkey.’ ... It is stated in Sefer HaYashar of Rabbeinu Tam that since man has two parts, body and soul, they draw toward two things: the body toward bodily, material things, and the soul toward pride, since the soul is from a high place and pride in its root is also from a high place. My holy grandfather of Kotzk said that the main evil inclination of pride is in a person from whom desire has already departed. Since Israel in exile are in a lowly state, the material and bodily desires must first be removed from them, and that is through guarding the covenant; this is the power of Yosef, and Mashiach ben Yosef will accomplish it in them. Afterward, when the material and the desires have been removed from them, and then the evil inclination of pride and self-elevation grows strong, King Mashiach will come, who is David, the head of those who submit, to subdue them to the service of Hashem and to nullify their sense of self ... Mashiach ben David is alluded to in the donkey, which hints at submission, ‘poor and riding on a donkey,’ as it is written, ‘Issachar is a strong-boned donkey ... and he bent his shoulder to bear.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 2:1: “This will be understood through what is said (Bava Metzia 33b): ‘And to the house of Jacob their sins’ – these are the unlearned, whose willful sins are made like errors for them. For certainly our father Jacob, peace be upon him, in the very root of his soul was already complete when he strove with the angel and prevailed, who was the guardian angel of Esau, the power of the evil inclination. … But since the whole matter of our father Jacob was to bear the pain of raising children in order to root holiness in his offspring after him for all generations, even in the lowly souls who are designated by the name Jacob, so that they too would merit the life of the World to Come without the evil inclination: this happened precisely in the seventeen years he was in the land of Egypt, for then the vitality was completed also in the souls of the aspect of Jacob. … And this is the matter of this parashah, the end of the Book of Bereishit, ‘And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years’: through it the completeness of creation was perfected even for the lowest souls in Israel, that they merit eternal life.”

k: volume-i|2013|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Shemot 6:2: “In the Midrash: ‘he that loves him disciplines him early.’ It comes to give the reason for the Egyptian exile decreed upon our forefathers at the very beginning of the root of the Children of Israel: that it was for good, and a preparation for all the exiles. And the meaning of ‘the names of the Children of Israel who are coming’ in the present tense is that these names are the forces that assist the Children of Israel at every time and season of trouble, as the Midrash hints: they were named for their redemption; and in the holy Zohar it is stated explicitly, see there. Had the exile begun at another time, they would not have been fit to draw these holy forces along with them. Therefore Hashem, blessed be He, brought about that the Egyptian exile should be at the root of the Children of Israel, and thereby this promise remains at every time of trouble, as it is written, ‘I will be with them in this trouble as I will be’: through this trouble it is drawn to be with them in all the troubles. And this is ‘those who are coming, Jacob shall take root’: that it was a preparation and a root.”

k: volume-i|2014|0|R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Toldot Yaako
quote: Parallel: R. Yaakov Yosef of Polonne, Toldot Yaakov Yosef, Vayishlach 69: “What touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was not the essential blow, that the supports of Torah were nullified; rather this touches the sinew of the thigh-vein, which is harder. For once faith is taken from them as well, then day and night they do not rest from travelling here and there to seize the provision of their household’s livelihood, ‘the people went about and gathered it’ (Numbers 11:8): they took foolishness upon themselves, as stated in the Zohar there (Beshalach 63a). And through this it is called gid ha-nasheh, for it makes them forget (menasheh) the service of their Master, as stated in the Midrash HaNe’elam on Parashat Vayishlach. And this, the taking of faith from them, is harder than the taking of the supports, as is written in Chovot HaLevavot (Sha’ar HaBitachon, the opening): someone said to a pious man who used to wander from his home for his bread, ‘Can your God not sustain you in your place?’ And he conceded to him and returned to his place.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayikra 6:1: “By day is the time of work, as it says, ‘Man goes out to his work’; and at night, when a person is free and occupies himself with Torah, then Hashem, blessed be He, draws upon him a thread of grace, so that he will be free even by day and his work will be done by others. … And in the Gemara (Shabbat 31a): when a person is brought to judgment they say to him, ‘Did you deal in faith? Did you fix times for Torah?’ And Tosafot (Kiddushin 40b) raised a difficulty from what is said there, that a person’s judgment begins only with words of Torah. But the matter follows the holy Zohar (Beshalach 62b): ‘Before the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the Torah He distinguished between those who were people of faith and those who were not… and with what did He test them? With the manna.’ … For one who believed in Hashem ate the manna as it was, knowing that Hashem, blessed be He, places in it the power to sustain life, and did not toil to gather and collect; but one who did not believe toiled and laboured, and afterwards ‘ground it in mills.’ And about this a person is asked, ‘Did you deal in faith,’ that he believed in Hashem and consequently was not harried over his livelihood and fixed times for Torah; and this is ‘his judgment begins with words of Torah.’”

k: volume-i|2016|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Iggere
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Iggeret HaTeshuvah 4:1–2: “However, all that is mentioned above concerns the completion of atonement and the cleansing of the soul for Hashem after repentance, as explained above from the Gemara in the first chapter of Zevachim: the burnt-offering is a gift brought after the advocate has secured acceptance. But the beginning of the mitzvah of repentance and its essence, to return to Hashem in truth and with a whole heart, must be explained thoroughly and at length. First, what is written in the holy Zohar explaining the word teshuvah by way of mystery: ‘tashuv heh,’ the lower heh, ‘lower repentance’; the upper heh, ‘higher repentance.’ And also what is written in the holy Zohar in some places, that repentance does not avail one who blemishes his covenant and emits seed in vain. This is very astonishing, for ‘nothing stands before repentance,’ even idolatry and forbidden relations. And Reishit Chochmah explained that the Zohar’s intent is that lower repentance does not avail, only higher repentance.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pinchas 15:1–2: “At the second Shabbat meal we say ‘Nehora yashrei bah.’ … That is, the first light that was hidden away for the righteous, and one who guards the covenant is called righteous, as it says, ‘Light is sown for the righteous’: it is impossible to merit this light except through the attribute of the righteous. And the Zohar says, ‘once the covenant is repaired, everything is repaired,’ for this is the root and beginning of the blemish that the serpent introduced; for this all the exiles came, and the root of the Egyptian exile was to repair it, as it says (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12): Joseph went down to Egypt and fenced himself off from immorality, and all the males were fenced off in his merit. … And through repairing this blemish one afterwards merits the first light. … And the Tanna DeVei Eliyahu expounded the verse ‘Where is the place of My rest’ as the Sabbath day, and it is written, ‘But to this one will I look: to the poor and broken in spirit who trembles at My word’; for on Shabbat a Jew becomes poor and broken in spirit and attains a broken heart, and then is the time to repair this blemish.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 10:1: “‘Rejoice, reapers of the field, with speech and with voice, and speak a word sweet as honey.’ The holy Zohar states that the mouth of Hashem was created on Shabbat, and also that Shabbat is called ‘speech,’ for Shabbat is the attribute of Malchut, the mouth. … The whole creation of man is to serve his Maker, and he was created chiefly for the toil of the mouth; the creation of speech and the mouth is to serve one’s Maker, that they be only in matters of holiness, in Torah and prayer, as it is written, ‘The voice is the voice of Jacob’: the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer. And it concludes, ‘but the hands are the hands of Esau,’ which hints that with this one cuts down and clears away the thorns, that is, the husks. … Just as ‘the hands are the hands of Esau,’ who has power with the sword in his hands, so opposite him Jacob was blessed, ‘the voice is the voice of Jacob’: in the voice of Jacob there is the power of the double-edged sword, to do what Esau does with his hands. As it is written, ‘Fear not, worm of Jacob,’ and the Sages said: just as the worm has no power except in its mouth, so Jacob has no power except in his mouth. … So Jacob, with the voice of Torah and prayer, cuts off all the wicked and all the forces of the husks in the world, as it says, ‘The high praises of God in their throat, and a double-edged sword in their hand.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 2:1: “It is stated in Midrash Tanchuma (Bereishit 7): the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called righteous and upright, created man in His image only so that he be righteous and upright like Him. And if you ask, why did He create the evil inclination? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: You make it evil. And it has already been explained that yetzer means desire, as in ‘the desire (yetzer) of the thoughts of the heart of Your people.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, created the desire to be a longing for Torah, as it will be in the future (as stated in Zohar I 138a); only you make it evil. And about this they said (Kiddushin 30b): I created the evil inclination and I created Torah as its antidote. And they said: if this repulsive one meets you, drag him to the house of study; that is, that the desire and the inclination go to the house of study, to become the joy of learning.”

Parallel: Poked Akarim 3:1: “The Sages said that this sign was handed down to them, that whoever comes with this expression is the true redeemer. Seemingly, what sort of sign is this? Since it was handed down to them, everyone knew of this tradition, and surely whoever came boasting that he would redeem them would use the expression according to the tradition. But in truth it is known what the Sages said on the verse ‘Hashem is your shadow,’ that He is like the shadow that does whatever the body does; all His attributes are measure for measure, and not for nothing, but because they too remember Him. Only, Hashem wishes the arousal from below to come first: ‘Return to Me and I will return to you’; and we ask, ‘Bring us back to You, Hashem, and we shall return,’ for it is not in our power to begin, only You bring us back by an arousal from above, and then we shall return. And so it was in Egypt: through an arousal from above Hashem sent them ‘I have surely remembered you,’ and through this ‘they will listen to your voice,’ believing this word at once. That is, through Moses’ speaking ‘pakod pakadeti’ to them he placed in their heart complete faith in Hashem’s providence over them. … For the removal of providence and of Hashem’s remembrance from a person is only when the person too is in concealment from Hashem; but when a person remembers Hashem and believes that Hashem is with him, surely Hashem too remembers him. … And this is the sign of the redeemer who speaks in the langua

k: volume-i|2021|0|Tiferes Yosef, Seventh Day of Pesach 2
ref: Tiferet Yosef, The Seventh Day of Pesach 2
quote: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Seventh Day of Pesach 2: “It is stated in the Midrash (Tanchuma, Shemot 24): this sign was handed down to them from the days of Abraham and Isaac; Jacob handed it to Joseph, and he told them: every redeemer who comes and says to you ‘pakod pakadeti’ is the true redeemer. He explained this: in the redemption from Egypt there was not yet any ground to say that Israel had earned the redemption by their service, for there were still accusations against the garments of Israel, ‘how are these different from those?’ Nor did they yet have Torah and mitzvot. Rather, Hashem looked into the inner depth of Israel and testified about them that in the depth of their heart they are full of will, and their will is to be drawn after the will of Hashem in all that He will command them. … And this is the matter of the sign: the redeemer who would come with the expression ‘pakod pakadeti’ is the true redeemer. For it is stated in the holy Zohar (Vayetzei 159b): remembering (zechirah) above and visiting (pekidah) below; zechirah indicates a place where the light shines from the point of the heart’s inner depth all the way to the outer garment. But in this redemption, where they were not yet refined down to the last garments, and Hashem looked only at the inner light of the depth of their heart, where they are clean, this is called only pekidah.”

k: volume-i|2022|0|R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShem
quote: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Shemot 10: “It is known that when the name Havayah appears in order in the initial letters of a verse, it indicates simple mercy, and when it appears in the final letters it indicates that the mercy is within the judgments and is not yet simple mercy. Now in the Egyptian exile there were great accusations against Israel, as we find that even after they were redeemed and stood at the sea there was still a great accusation: ‘these are idol worshippers and these are idol worshippers’; all the more so while they were in Egypt. And the proof is that the harshness of the bondage was completing the time, for mercy was still mixed within the judgments and was not yet simple mercy; therefore Moses declined the mission. And among the six hundred thousand of Israel there were surely great sages and men of holy spirit who understood this from the Names, that the mercy was still mixed within the judgments. Therefore Moses our teacher said, ‘And they will say to me, What is His name (li mah shemo mah),’ for the name Havayah is hinted there in the final letters, which shows that the mercy is not simple; how then can the redemption be? If they ask me this, what shall I answer them? … And Hashem said to him, ‘Ehyeh asher Ehyeh,’ which is mercy; through it they can be redeemed. … Three times Ehyeh equals sixty-three, and that Name is in Binah, as is known, which is the world of freedom, the great Jubilee, and from there came the redemption

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vaera 2:1: “The matter of the question ‘What is His name’ is this: since they knew that Israel were sunk in the husk of Egypt like an embryo in its mother’s womb, and a light needed to shine forth in them, about this he said, ‘they will say to me, What is His name,’ that is, through which Name will the light shine in them. And about this Hashem said to him, ‘Ehyeh asher Ehyeh’: the name Ehyeh indicates Keter and Binah, which is the World to Come, as is known, and then it is called ‘that day,’ meaning it will shine like the light of day. … In truth the Exodus was so that they would receive the Torah, as it is written, ‘I said: You are godlike beings,’ that they would repair everything and it would be like the World to Come. But Hashem foresaw that they would spoil it and the evil inclination would return to its place, and about this it says ‘asher Ehyeh,’ in subjugation, and afterward the light of ‘that day’ will be revealed. And to Israel Hashem commanded him to say ‘Ehyeh has sent me to you,’ that is, to repair everything so that the light of the future be revealed; and He did not tell them that they would spoil it, for ‘sufficient is the trouble in its hour.’ … And through complete faith they can merit to attain the light of the name Ehyeh.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 1:1: “The repair is also through crying out and prayer, as it is said, ‘The face of Hashem is against evildoers,’ which hints at this blemish, called ‘evil,’ as is known; and it is written, ‘They cried out and Hashem heard,’ for crying out avails. And as stated in the holy Zohar (II 20a): crying out is greater than all of them, for crying out is in the heart, as it is written, ‘Their heart cried out to the Lord’; and it concludes there that it never returns empty. That is, it avails even for this blemish, for which the Zohar (I 219b) withheld repentance. And it is stated in the holy Zohar there: great is crying out, for it rules in this world and in the World to Come; through crying out a person inherits this world and the World to Come, as it is written, ‘Then they cried out to Hashem in their distress, and He saved them from their straits.’ We must understand where in the verse it is hinted that he inherits this world and the World to Come. It seems that it refers to the verse ‘Those who go down to the sea in ships,’ which refers to those who occupy themselves with Torah and go down into the sea of the Talmud … ‘and all their wisdom is swallowed up,’ for the Torah alone will not avail them … ‘Then they cried out to Hashem in their distress, and He brought them out of their straits.’ … And it is written, ‘He leads them to their desired haven,’ that is, to the World to Come, which is the purpose of man.”

k: volume-i|2025|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Tora
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Rosh Hashanah 3:10: “This is the very reason for the blowing: it is a simple voice that comes out of the breath of the heart and has not yet come to be revealed in letters at all, because it is from the innermost point of the heart, which does not yet come to be revealed in letters; for the letters have their root in the wisdom that is in the brain, while this breath, which comes out as a simple voice, is from the innermost point of the heart, higher than the wisdom in the brain. … There are two kinds of voice. The first is called the voice of speech, which also comes from the breath of the heart, but from the outer heart, the emotions in the heart that are drawn from the intellect … But the simple voice comes from the inner breath in the depth of the heart, which is above intellect, being the innermost will that is not bounded by intellect; therefore it is a simple voice, like a sudden cry that comes from the point of the depth of the heart, when the very essence of the soul is stirred, as in ‘Their heart cried out to Hashem.’ And this cry is higher than the root of the letters in wisdom. And by blowing the shofar of the mitzvah with a simple voice and with the will of the heart, which is above knowledge and above letters, one also arouses above the aspect of Keter, which is higher than wisdom and knowledge.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 12:1: “In the end they will hear, as it is written, ‘So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth: it shall not return to Me empty, but it shall accomplish what I desire and prosper in what I sent it for.’ And this is along the lines of what they said (Berakhot 6b): every person who has fear of Heaven, his words are heard, as it says, ‘The end of the matter, all having been heard.’ That is because a person who has fear of Heaven becomes a chariot for the attribute of Malchut, ‘which is fear, and fear dwells in it’ (as stated in the holy Zohar I 5b), and he is in the aspect of ‘My word that goes forth from My mouth’; therefore his words are heard. And it is written, ‘The end of the matter, all is heard,’ that is, even if he is not heard at the time, in the end his words will be heard. And so too the word of Hashem will not return empty but will accomplish and prosper in what I sent it for; and if they are not heard in their time, in the end they will be heard.”

k: volume-i|2027|0|R. Elimelech of Lizhensk, Noam Elimelech
quote: Parallel: R.
