Elimelech of Lizhensk, Noam Elimelech, Tetzaveh 3: “The main thing is that a person must serve the Creator, blessed be He, with complete fear, and all his limbs should always be heated and trembling with the fear of the Creator. And this person, with the fear of Hashem always upon his face, cannot hold himself back from rebuking people, ‘you shall surely rebuke your fellow,’ and his words arouse the hearts of the people who hear his words to return to the Creator, as it is stated: whoever has fear of Heaven, his words are heard. And after he has accomplished this, bringing fear into the heart of others, afterward he will merit through this to come to love of the Creator with a whole heart, and to cleaving, through which he can draw great influx into the world. And this is ‘Happy is the man who fears Hashem, who greatly desires His commandments,’ that is, love. … ‘And they shall take to you’: through their taking the fear of Hashem into their heart, this will cause you to come to love.”

k: volume-i|2028|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me’or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me’or Einayim, Ki Tavo 1–2: “It is known what is said in the Talmud: had Israel kept two Shabbatot, they would immediately have been redeemed. To understand what the two Shabbatot are ... the Holy One gave Israel the Shabbat, which is intermediate between Israel and their Father in Heaven and unites and binds them to the Creator, because it has both parts, resembling both Israel and the Holy One ... As is known from the Zohar, Shabbat is the Name of the Holy One, complete on every side; Shabbat is the life of the upper world and the life of this world, which is the emanation of His glory drawn down and contracted into this seventh day in this world. The seventh day that we call Shabbat is like a body and garment for the upper Shabbat (Shabbat ila’ah), which is the Name of the Holy One ... This is ‘had Israel kept two Shabbatot’: the upper Shabbat, which is the light of His blessed glory, the supernal life, and the lower Shabbat, which is this actual seventh day in time. They would immediately have been redeemed, for through this they would draw very near to the Creator, and all the good would be sifted from the bad completely until Mashiach comes. Each person draws near to the Creator according to how he keeps the Shabbatot; if the keeping is not complete, there is no complete redemption, but if the keeping of both Shabbatot were complete, the nearness would be complete until they would be redeemed.”

k: volume-i|2029|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Shemot 14:7–9: “‘And these are the names’: the early authorities asked why Scripture repeated and listed the names of the tribes after it had already mentioned them in parashat Vayigash. It seems that, as the Midrash says, the tribes were named for the redemption of Israel: Reuven, for ‘I have surely seen the affliction of My people’; Shimon, for ‘I have heard their cry’ ... This can be understood by the Gemara in Megillah: the Holy One does not strike Israel unless He has first created a cure for them, as it says, ‘When I would heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim is uncovered’; but the nations He strikes first and afterward creates a cure, as it says, ‘striking and healing.’ The reason is that the punishments of Israel are not by way of retribution, but to scour and polish them so that they become fit to receive the good. The cure is therefore the cause of the punishment: were the good not envisioned first and foremost, the punishment would not come; so He creates the cure for them first. With the nations, the punishment is payment for their sins and does not depend on the cure. By this the matter is understood: the tribes were named for the redemption of Israel to show that the cure precedes the blow, and the redemption precedes and causes the exile, for without the redemption coming first the exile would not be possible. Now it is understood why it listed the names of the tribes again: to show that their names a

k: volume-i|2030|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Torah Ohr, Va
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Torah Ohr, Vaera 1:14–18: “‘But My Name Havayah I did not make known to them.’ For the Sages said that Avraham our father fulfilled the entire Torah before it was given; that is, he fulfilled the deeds of the commandments out of love, and as the Sages said, Avraham instituted the morning prayer, which is drawing down the light of Hashem so that ‘Hashem is One’ rests and is revealed in the lower beings, to love Hashem with delight and serve Him with heart and soul. Nevertheless, all this is still called the service of a servant, who listens to his master’s voice and does his command out of love, joy and gladness of heart ... But Moshe our teacher had another quality, for he said, ‘And what are we?’, the aspect of total self-nullification; therefore he merited that the Torah be given through him in the aspect of speech, and the Sages said that the Shechinah spoke from Moshe’s throat ... Through the Torah he draws down His blessed unity and oneness, His glory and Himself, as before the world was created, so that it is revealed below ... And since the Torah had not yet been given to the Patriarchs, it is written, ‘But My Name Havayah I did not make known (noda’ti) to them.’ It does not say ‘I did not inform (hoda’ti)’ ... but ‘noda’ti’: I Myself was not known to them, the aspect of ‘I Myself,’ the Singular One. And that is ‘these words which I (anochi) command you today’: Anochi, Who I am, the aspect of the Singular One.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 8:1: “Although it is written of Avraham, ‘And Hashem appeared to him’ with the Name Havayah, Avraham our father had a grasp of Him only through the glass that does not shine. As we said on the verse ‘But My Name Havayah I did not make known to them’: although the Name Havayah is mentioned several times with the Patriarchs as well, they nevertheless did not attain the da’at, which is the inner dimension of the Supernal Crown, but only through the glass that does not shine, which is the Name Adnut ... But with Moshe, the glass that shines was with him as soon as he was born, as it is written, ‘and she saw him that he was good’ ... And the Zohar concludes: Yaakov called it ‘angel’ at the time he was departing from the world ... Moshe in his body, Yaakov in his spirit. That is, although Yaakov’s body too was like that of Adam before the sin, it was so only when he was close to his passing, for then he was like spirit without body. This is not so of Moshe our teacher, who was so in his lifetime, for he immediately merited the revelation of the entire Name Havayah, the Tree of Life, with the crown of the yod, which is the Supernal Crown, as it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 13): ‘And Yaakov is surely the image of the central pillar from the outside, and Moshe was there, but from the inside; this one from the body and this one from the soul.’”

k: volume-i|2032|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissasc
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Kislev and Tevet 14:3: “It is known what is explained in the Zohar, that for the sin of the covenant, Heaven forbid, repentance does not avail. Reishit Chokhmah wrote that it cannot be meant literally, for we hold that nothing stands in the way of repentance. And the Sages expounded ‘Return, O Israel, unto (ad) Hashem your God’: is there then a repentance that does not reach Hashem? They expounded it to mean even one who denied the very root, that is, even if your iniquity touched Hashem your God, Heaven forbid; so how could one say that repentance does not avail for any transgression in the world? Therefore the holy author of Reishit Chokhmah explained that the Zohar means there is teshuvah and there is teshuvah: there is the lower teshuvah, tashuv heh, the final Heh, which is called the Oral Torah, and there is the upper teshuvah, the first Heh, the supernal Mother, which is the aspect of the Written Torah. The Zohar's statement that repentance does not avail for the sin of the covenant refers to the lower teshuvah. ... Thus ‘Return, O Israel, unto Hashem your God’ means the upper teshuvah, which is Binah, where the Name Havayah is vocalized as Elokim; this is ‘unto Havayah your God.’ The lower teshuvah is not enough for you, ‘for you have stumbled in your iniquity.’”

k: volume-i|2033|0|Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuva
ref: Peri Tzadik, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 12
quote: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 12: “This level no one can merit except a penitent, not even a completely righteous person, for ‘in the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous cannot stand,’ since they draw close to the Holy One, blessed be He, to the root, which is the intellect hidden from all thought. So too even one who blemished the root itself, who increased his iniquities up to the Throne of Glory, can also repair it through repentance. ... From the side of the neshamah, ‘Your people are all righteous,’ for once he is circumcised on the eighth day he cleaves to the root ... but at the time of sin the aspect of neshamah departs from him, and there is one who increases his sin so much that he is uprooted entirely from the root. ... This is the verse of Ezra cited in the Pesikta, ‘Our iniquities have increased over our head’: the expression ‘over our head’ means up to the root, which is above the head. And this is what the Gemara says, great is repentance which reaches the Throne of Glory: even if the transgressions reach the Throne of Glory, one can also repair them through repentance.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sefer Kedushat Shabbat 6: “This is the place where penitents stand, where the completely righteous cannot stand, for out of the bitterness of repentance they merit the light hidden away for the righteous in the future, which was not revealed to them in this world, since it cannot be revealed in this world except out of the darkness that precedes it, like the creation of the world, ‘first darkness and then light.’ So too the six days of work and afterward the Shabbat day, when the light is revealed; and in actuality these are the six thousand years of this world, and afterward the day that is entirely Shabbat and rest and holiness, for there will no longer be any existence of evil. And this is the feast of the Leviathan and the wild ox (Bava Batra 74b), which is the slaughter of the two inclinations: of lust, ‘like the space of a man and wreaths,’ for fish are wanton, as it says in the chapter HaSefinah; and of anger, pride and envy, which is the attribute of the goring ox, as it says in the chapter HaRo'eh (Berakhot) that a beast too has an inclination to bite and kick. Corresponding to this are the Shabbat meals, at which there is a mitzvah to eat meat and fish, for it is a semblance of the World to Come and one-sixtieth of it.”

k: volume-i|2035|0|R. Avraham Dov of Avritch, Bat Ayin, Pin
quote: Parallel: R. Avraham Dov of Avritch, Bat Ayin, Pinchas 33-39: “Through envy his evil inclination grew strong and fat. But there is also an aspect of envy in holiness, as in ‘And Rachel envied her sister,’ which is the aspect of ‘the envy of scribes increases wisdom’ (Bava Batra 21a), for Rachel envied the mitzvot and good deeds of Leah (Bereshit Rabbah 71:6). She overturned the envy of physical things, which is the envy of impurity, the fattening for a strange god, that is, the strengthening of the evil inclination, and she cleaved to the envy of holiness. So the aspect of a strange god, the evil inclination, was nullified, and the aspect of Rachel came about, whose numerical value equals el zar, ‘a strange god.’ And from the aspect of Rachel was born the aspect of holy Joseph, the aspect of an addition of holiness, which was transformed from the aspect of envy into the aspect of Joseph, whose numerical value equals kin'ah, ‘envy.’”

k: volume-i|2036|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or Einayim, Ki Tisa 5-7: “‘Verily My Sabbaths you shall keep, for it is a sign between Me and you, to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you.’ ... The essential thing is that the service be with complete knowledge (da'at), for ‘a minor, who has no da'at, his act is no act,’ meaning that the unification and union above is not completed through him, for ‘without knowledge the soul is not good,’ and he remains in smallness and his deeds do not cleave to the unification of their root. ... Everyone agrees that on Shabbat the Torah was given to Israel; that is, da'at, the secret of the Torah, is revealed on Shabbat, and then one speaks with da'at. ... Therefore the Sages said, ‘Whoever keeps Shabbat according to its law, even if he worshipped idols like the generation of Enosh, is forgiven,’ as it says, ‘keeps the Sabbath from profaning it (mechalelo)’: do not read mechalelo but machul lo, ‘he is forgiven.’ The reason is that da'at means ‘through knowledge chambers are filled’: he understands in his knowledge that there is nothing besides Him, so to speak, and that His glory fills the whole earth, with no place empty of Him, and he does not move from his attachment. ... One who turns aside after other gods has removed Hashem from that place in his mind, and it is called a void (chalal), for the place is empty of His vitality. And this is ‘keeps the Sabbath from making it a void.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 12: “Jacob includes the holiness of Abraham and Isaac, as it says (Zohar I 207a), ‘The secret of the Patriarchs is Jacob, who is their inclusion,’ ... and it is written, ‘You will grant truth to Jacob,’ and ‘The lip of truth shall be established forever (la'ad).’ ... So too the holiness of Shabbat itself: the holy Zohar (II 204a) says that the shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs who unite with the only daughter, and she is crowned with them. That is, on Shabbat a Jew merits the holiness of the three Patriarchs, through the three Shabbat meals corresponding to the Patriarchs. Therefore at the Shabbat Minchah, which corresponds to Jacob (as the three prayers correspond to the Patriarchs, Tikkunei Zohar 18), we say ‘And as for me, may my prayer ... answer me in the truth of Your salvation,’ for then a Jew merits the holiness of Jacob, ‘the lip of truth established forever,’ and we ask that the salvation be from the evil inclination and from all evil, forever. So too we ask in the Havdalah prayer for the days of work, that we be held back from all sin, cleansed of all iniquity and attached to the fear of You.”

k: volume-i|2038|0|R. Aharon HaLevi of Staroselye, Sha'arei
quote: Parallel: R. Aharon HaLevi of Staroselye, Sha'arei HaYichud VeEmunah, First Gate 5: “The aspect of Ze'eir Anpin, the ten sefirot of Atzilut, is called ‘Ad,’ which is ‘the endurance and nexus of all,’ for the ten sefirot of Atzilut bind Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah to the Infinite. ... The yearning of the Jubilee, that is Binah, where the light of the Infinite is revealed, is to crown it, that is, to draw down to Ze'eir Anpin the aspect of Keter ... and the yearning of the Shemitah is to be blessed from it, that is, to draw the unity of His attributes, the higher unification, into the lower unification: to draw His unity into Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah and to contemplate that all the levels divided in them are also in one unity ... and to bind them to His unity through the service of those below, in the reading of Shema, prayer, Torah and mitzvot. This is ‘Trust in Havayah adei ad’: Ad is the aspect of Ze'eir Anpin, for ad is an expression of binding and strengthening ... and bitchu, ‘trust,’ is an expression of attachment and binding.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bo 12:1: “‘Outward they depart and enter not, these insolent dogs.’ ... The dog is the husk of Amalek, as is written in the holy Zohar (II 65a) ... and it is only a barking dog: why are these different from those? Its main accusation is against the holiness of the covenant ... And Haman, of his descendants — it is taught (Megillah 13b): there was none who knew slander like Haman, meaning that he accused Israel above: they have slept from the commandments, and even the Rabbis are one people. ... But on Shabbat, which is the revelation of holiness, when the yod is revealed ..., we say ‘Outward they depart, etc.’: there is no need to stop their mouths, for they have no place of accusation at all, and they do not enter at all, since Shabbat is in the secret of the covenant, as is known. And on Shabbat one can repair this blemish, as we said from what is written (Shabbat 118b), that whoever keeps Shabbat, even if he served idols like the generation of Enosh, is forgiven, and all the more so this blemish. And also for the future, through keeping Shabbat one is guarded from transgression and saved from the accusation of the evil inclination ... and there is no room for the dog to enter at all.”

k: volume-i|2040|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayikra 10:17–20: “‘Outward they depart and enter not, these insolent dogs.’ It is known that the insolent dogs are the aspect of Amalek, which comes from the mixture of the husks of ox and donkey, as explained in the holy Zohar, and it is known that Shabbat is the opposite of the husk of Amalek ... Why, then, do we not say this at all the meals of Shabbat, but only at the third meal? ... Abraham drew heaven close to earth, and Isaac drew earth close to heaven; Jacob had both their traits together. He was ‘a perfect man dwelling in tents,’ which the holy Zohar explains as one who joined the upper world and the lower world ... My father, of holy memory, said that Amalek is the opposite of Jacob: Jacob is yashar, straight, and Amalek is the reverse, from the word for crooked ... Opposite Jacob, who joined the two worlds, was Amalek, ‘a cutter son of a cutter,’ the one who separates doubly, who blocks the supernal light from shining below ... According to the order of the Arizal, the night meal of Shabbat belongs to Isaac, the day meal to Abraham, and the third meal to Jacob ... the third meal is the time of cleaving from both sides together, from above to below and from below to above, and this belongs to Jacob.”

k: volume-i|2041|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Tora
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Vaetchanan 7:1, 7:13: “‘Know this day and lay it upon your heart (levavecha) that Havayah is God (HaElokim); there is none else.’ The meaning of ‘know this day’: just as the day is together with the night and the two are one, as it is written, ‘and there was evening and there was morning, one day,’ so ‘lay it upon your heart’: as it is in time, so it is in the soul, that the two hearts, the good inclination and the evil inclination, are both as one, so that the evil inclination too returns to the service of Havayah, when the Other Side is subdued; as it is written, ‘with all your heart (levavecha)’: with both your inclinations. And from this, ‘know’ that thus Havayah is God. ... This revelation depends on the arousal from below, through ‘lay it upon your heart,’ that the two hearts be as one, that the evil inclination too return to the service of Hashem by way of subduing it and nullifying one's will ... and from this, ‘know this day that Havayah is God’: there comes about a joining and unification of the Name Havayah with the Name Elokim.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 15:2: “King David, peace be upon him, also said ‘Hashem is my shepherd,’ just as Jacob said ‘The God Who has shepherded me,’ and afterward he said ‘Yea, though I walk ... for You are with me,’ meaning that Hashem is the Redeemer of Israel, and ‘You are with me’ to redeem me. ... And although King David was the man who raised up the yoke of repentance, David mentioned the Name Havayah, which includes the upper three as well, as is known; that is, the penitent can draw from the fiftieth gate, which belongs to the penitent, as is indicated by ‘Though your sins be like the years (shanim) that are arranged and come from the six days of Creation, they shall be white as snow’ (Shabbat 89b), and intentional sins become merits. And this is only through Hashem, Who causes it to appear for one who repents out of love. ... He put first that everything is from Hashem, for even the awakening of repentance comes only through an arousal from above.”

k: volume-i|2043|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayeshev 4:3: “In the Midrash: his gathering together and the gathering together of his children ... Jacob's labor with Laban was the aspect of the weekdays, days of work, and now ‘Jacob settled’ is the aspect of holy Shabbat. And the counsel is through the gathering together, as it is taught, that it becomes united in the secret of One. ... My grandfather, my master, of blessed memory, explained the camels laden with flax: flax is stalk by stalk, and they are called chieftains, each one a distinct thing by itself. ... Esau wants to make of everything a spreading out, to be a thing by itself, while Jacob wants to bring every spreading out near to the inner point, to be one. And so on Shabbat all creatures draw near to the root of life, as it is written, ‘And on the seventh day God finished His work’: that is, holy Shabbat gives unity to all creatures, and through this they become a vessel for Hashem, as it is taught: the vessel that holds blessing is peace.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Nasso 19:1: “‘May He Whose peace it is place upon us blessing and peace’ ... This meal corresponds to our father Jacob, and it is taught in the holy Zohar (III 13b): Peace is Jacob, as it is written, ‘You will give truth to Jacob,’ and it is written, ‘Love truth and peace,’ for truth and peace are bound to one another. For peace is the attribute of Joseph the righteous, of whom it is written, ‘And Joseph recognized his brothers’ ... and of them it is written, ‘they could not speak peaceably to him.’ And this is the main root of the exiles: one who is not clean of this blemish cannot attain the attribute of peace. ... All the exiles came because of baseless hatred, the opposite of peace ... and one who is clean of this blemish, his attribute is peace. ... And in the dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel it is taught (Yevamot 14b) that love and friendship prevailed between them, to fulfill ‘love truth and peace’; that is, there cannot be truth unless there is peace afterward. And at the third meal, which corresponds to Jacob, we say ‘May He Whose peace it is place upon us blessing and peace.’ ... For through the attribute of peace one is saved from servitude and from the subjugation of the kingdoms, and every individual soul is immediately redeemed.”

k: volume-i|2045|0|R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat
quote: Parallel: R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat Yisrael, Pirkei Avot 3:7: “Another interpretation: ‘and a path (netivah) in the mighty waters.’ There are people, transgressors, who reflect and plan how to do evil, and they are called ‘plotters of iniquity,’ and their sin is very great. For those people upon whom the evil inclination comes suddenly and overpowers them, so that they have no time to settle their minds, and they sin, even though they act willfully it is reckoned for them as unwitting. But these transgressors had time to turn back from their evil ... Repentance alone is not sufficient for them, because of the greatness of their sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, digs an opening beneath the Throne of Glory and accepts them in repentance, as we find with Manasseh ... and this is ‘and a path in the mighty waters’: to these transgressors He gives a path, which is a narrow trail, and accepts them in repentance, as explained above. And netivah is the letters netiv Yah, so that they may repair what they blemished in the Name Yah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Lech Lecha 3: “The righteous are called myrtles, and all Israel have a share in the World to Come, as it is said, ‘And your people are all righteous.’ And in the holy Zohar on this parashah (93a): ‘But how many guilty ones there are in Israel, how many sinners and how many wicked ... rather, since they bring their sons on the eighth day as an offering, and when they are circumcised ... they are called righteous.’ And this follows what is written in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 44a) on the verse ‘Israel has sinned’: even though he sinned, he is Israel. Rabbi Abba said: as people say, a myrtle standing among reeds is called a myrtle. That is, since the infant is circumcised at eight days without his knowledge and through this becomes Israel, this shows that he is bound at his root with Hashem in the beginning of Thought, and whatever passes over him, in truth ‘our will is to do Your will, and who prevents us? The leaven in the dough’ (Berakhot 17a). ... To teach that whatever passes over Israel, nevertheless no one is cast away from Him, for the name Israel is not uprooted from him.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa 7:1: “Afterward a third statement was said to him: ‘And Hashem said, Behold, there is a place with Me ...’, that even in the tranquility of the wicked it would be shown to him; and that is what is said, ‘And you shall see My back.’ I heard from the holy Rav, of blessed memory, that the meaning is that after the deed Moshe our teacher at once recognized the depth and the good hidden in it; but to understand the good beforehand, of that it is said, ‘and My face shall not be seen.’ That is the Targum: ‘and you shall see what is after Me, but what is before Me shall not be seen,’ meaning to understand beforehand that it too is for the good. So too in the Egyptian exile Hashem showed him how all the tranquility of the Egyptians, which was for their destruction, was for the good, for through it all the wisdoms were there, and in the exile they brought out the holy sparks from them, and it was a preparation for the Giving of the Torah. And so in truth all the exiles are for the good, but in the present a person cannot grasp this.”

k: volume-i|2048|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 14: “We have already written about the difference in level between the Patriarchs and Moshe our teacher. Moshe was set apart to be a man of God as soon as he was created, as it says, ‘Moshe, Moshe’ with no pause between them, and he was prepared for the Torah, which is above creation; while the Patriarchs were prepared to repair the work of creation and nature ... The Sages said: ‘Alas for those who are lost: they did not question after Me, while you said, What is His name, what shall I say ... Why have You done evil ...’ Heaven forbid that the Sages meant to speak against Moshe our teacher. Rather, these are two levels. The level of the Patriarchs was faith, to serve Hashem in this way, without questioning; and the level of Moshe our teacher was only in Torah and in knowledge (da’at), and so he needed to know every matter clearly, as it says, ‘He made known His ways to Moshe.’ But the generation was not yet ready for this way.”

Parallel: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 189: “There are two kinds of perception of Godliness. One: from the side of creation a person recognizes that there is a Creator, and this is called ‘the work of creation.’ Two: from the side of His governance, and this is called ‘the work of the chariot,’ how Hashem rides upon the creatures. These are the two levels of seeing and knowing, of the Patriarchs and of Moshe our teacher, mentioned in the Zohar on Vaera (23a): the Patriarchs perceived from the side of the creatures, as the Sages said of Avraham our father (Bereshit Rabbah 39), ‘He saw a palace alight’ ... and it is called the revealed seeing. Therefore that Name is mentioned with them there in the verse, which shows that He said to His world ‘Enough’ (dai), as the Sages said (Chagigah 12a), and R. Bunim, of blessed memory, explained: there is enough in this creation to recognize His blessed Godliness through it ... [Likewise the title ‘father’ is relative to a son, and that is the perception of the fathers of the world; but the title ‘master’ (rav) is relative to a disciple, and that is the perception of Moshe, the master of Israel.] Knowing is in His governance, as it is written, ‘Make known to me Your ways’ ... and this is the da’at, the level of Moshe our teacher, which includes all the souls of the Torah scholars of Israel ... But the perception of seeing of the Patriarchs, who include all the souls of Israel, is possible for every one to attain even if he is not a Torah scholar, for

k: volume-i|2050|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 24: “Concerning the Name El Shaddai, the Sages said that He said to His world ‘Enough’: El Shaddai is Godliness in measure, as the Sages said that each of the Patriarchs had one defined attribute, and these are the drawings-down of Godliness, as it is written, ‘Yours, Hashem, are the greatness and the might.’ But the aspect of the Name Havayah that was made known to Moshe our teacher is the Torah, which is water that has no end, as it is written, ‘To every end I have seen a limit’ ... ‘longer than the earth is its measure.’ The attributes are streams and vessels that receive the light of Torah, but the essence of the Torah is the Names of the Holy One; the Torah and the Holy One are one. Therefore the Torah is freedom and redemption, as the Sages said, ‘No one is free except one who occupies himself with Torah,’ for the essence of exile is that the life of Godliness is hidden and cannot be revealed out of nature. The Patriarchs were refined even before receiving the Torah, and only the commandment of circumcision was given to them ... and through the power of this commandment they repaired the attributes to be vessels and a preparation for receiving the Torah afterward.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Miketz 2:1: “It is stated in Bereshit Rabbah: ‘In all toil there is profit’: since Yosef suffered over his master’s wife, he had an advantage from her, for he took her daughter; ‘but the talk of the lips leads only to want’: because he said to the chief butler, ‘remember me ... and mention me,’ two years were added to him. And afterward it says there: ‘Happy is the man who has made Hashem his trust: this is Yosef; and has not turned to the arrogant: because he said to the chief butler ...’ ... His talk of the lips was only to want, through saying to the chief butler ‘remember me and mention me.’ This was not counted in his eyes as any sin, for in truth he did not trust in the chief butler, as it says, ‘who has made Hashem his trust: this is Yosef.’ Only, because he sensed that his salvation would truly come through the chief butler, he wanted the salvation to come about through nature, for one does not rely on a miracle. Nevertheless it led to want for him, and through it two years were added to him, to rouse him concerning the talk of the lips with which he had brought an evil report about his brothers, which had also seemed to him a light matter.”

k: volume-i|2052|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Miketz 6:1–4: “In the Midrash: ‘Happy is the man who has made Hashem his trust: this is Yosef; and has not turned to the arrogant: because he said to the chief butler, Remember me and mention me, two years were added to him.’ All the commentators wondered, for it seems on the contrary that Yosef did turn to the arrogant ... We have already asked what sin Yosef had in making an effort through the chief butler. Is this not the way of the world, to make an effort and to pray to Hashem that He prosper the effort? So it is written, ‘And Hashem your God will bless you in all that you do,’ and in the Sifrei: ‘Could it be even when he sits idle? Scripture says, in all that you do.’ ... This is the height of the trait of trust, as the Chovot HaLevavot explains: not that one trusts that the matter will certainly change for the better, but that he believes and trusts in Hashem that He surely desires to benefit His creatures more than they desire to benefit themselves, and that all that Hashem does with him is for his good even though he does not know or see the good ... It may be said that the Patriarchs were the chariot and the Name of Hashem rested upon them because of this trait ... because they were given over in every aspect to Hashem even in what they did not understand, without calculation, like a chariot nullified to its rider. So too Yosef was a chariot, as is known, and all because of the trait of trust.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 12:1: “Of the husk of desire something will remain in the future as well, as it says in Midrash HaNe'elam (Zohar I 137a) ... and likewise there will remain of it the longing for the delight of Torah (chamidu de-oraita), for which purpose it was created. As it says there (138a), ‘Were it not for the evil inclination, there would be no joy of halachic discourse,’ for the essence of the inclination (yetzer) was created so that there would be desire for words of Torah. ... And this is what Rashi explains on ‘I will give you the good of the land of Egypt’: he prophesied without knowing what he prophesied, that in the end they would make it like a deep without fish. That is, they would bring out from there all the holy sparks, which are called life. ... Fish indicate the root of life, for with fish life is first mentioned in the Torah, as it says ‘a living soul.’ And it says (Bereshit Rabbah 97) that Israel are likened to fish: just as fish grow in water, yet when a single drop falls from above they receive it with thirst, so Israel grow in the water of the Torah, yet when they hear a new thing from the Torah ... that is, the novel insights of the Oral Torah. Therefore fish allude to the light of the Oral Torah.”

k: volume-i|2054|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or Einayim, Yitro 33-34: “One of the names of the evil inclination is ‘evil,’ and since he cleaves to the letters of the Torah, to gaze at the pleasantness of the radiance of the vitality of the Infinite that spreads within the letters of the Torah, he is attached to Him, blessed be He, and of him it says, ‘evil shall not dwell with You.’ ... On this our Sages said, ‘If this disgraceful one confronts you, drag him to the study hall (beit hamidrash): if he is stone, he dissolves.’ They were precise in saying ‘drag him to the beit hamidrash,’ and did not simply say ‘drag him to words of Torah’ (what difference whether one learns in the study hall or elsewhere?). Rather they intended that the Oral Torah is called ‘the midrash of the Sages,’ which the Sages expounded from the Written Torah by the thirteen principles by which the Torah is expounded. So ‘drag him to the beit hamidrash’ means: to the inwardness of the midrash, to cleave to the vitality within the letters, for they are the palace of Hashem and He dwells within them. Then ‘if he is stone, he dissolves.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 10:1: “The creation of speech and the mouth is to serve one's Maker, for they must be only in matters of holiness, in Torah and prayer, as it is written, ‘The voice is the voice of Jacob’: kol with a vav and kol without a vav, the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer. And it concludes, ‘but the hands are the hands of Esau,’ which hints that through this one cuts off and clears away the thorns, that is, the husks. To this ‘Rejoice, reapers of the field’ alludes: the cutting of the thorns from the vineyard. Just as ‘the hands are the hands of Esau,’ who has power by his sword in his hands, so opposite him Jacob was blessed, ‘the voice is the voice of Jacob,’ for in the voice of Jacob there is also the power of a double-edged sword. ... As the Sages said, ‘Just as the worm's strength is only in its mouth, so Jacob's strength is only in his mouth’ ... so Jacob, by the voice of Torah and prayer, cuts off all the wicked and all the powers of the husks in the world.”

k: volume-i|2056|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 23 (5654): “Consider the verse ‘Behold, the children of Israel did not listen to me ... and I am of uncircumcised lips.’ The holy Zohar says on ‘I am of uncircumcised lips’ that speech was in exile. The explanation: just as there is a foreskin at the opening of the circumcision, the covenant of the flesh, which Abraham merited to have removed so that the covenant of circumcision would be revealed to him, so at the covenant of the tongue, which is the opening of speech in Torah, there is a foreskin. For these two covenants are the openings of the inner self: all the limbs are closed except these two, and wherever there is an inner opening there is a foreskin and a concealment, so that not everyone who wishes to take the Name may come and take it. So in general Israel had to pass through all that befell them in Egypt in order to remove the foreskin of the mouth and merit the covenant of the tongue and the Torah. Moreover, every day they need the help of remembering the exodus from Egypt to merit the opening of the mouth; this is the joining of redemption to prayer, ‘Who redeemed Israel’ and then ‘Hashem, open my lips.’ These are the two signs in every Jew, circumcision and Shabbat and tefillin, for Shabbat and tefillin are a remembrance of the exodus, and through them one merits the Torah, which is the covenant of the tongue.”

k: volume-i|2057|0|R. Kalonymus Kalman Shapira of Piaseczno
quote: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Shapira of Piaseczno, Hakhsharat HaAvrekhim 7:14-19: “They believed that Hashem would one day redeem them, but the harsh and so bitter present before their eyes removed from them both their past radiance and their future hope, very far, as if to other worlds. ... They had both faith and despair. It was not from a lack of faith that despair seized them and hope was lost to them, but from the brokenness of their spirit; for even to believe one needs the substance of a man and a spirit that believes, and in them the substance of the man was trampled and the spirit melted: the self that would believe was broken and the man who would hope was crushed. When they read their scrolls that promised them their redemption, the Israelite spirit rose in them and their faith was strengthened; and when their troubles grew harsher they fell, and with them the spirit of their faith was shattered as well, ‘and they did not listen ... from shortness of spirit and from hard labor.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Nisan 1: “This accords with Berakhot 6b: the words of anyone who has awe of Heaven are heeded ... But Moses called the evil inclination ‘uncircumcised’ (Sukkah 52a) ... for although ‘uncircumcised’ properly applies only to idolaters, it sits inside the heart of a Jew and blocks his heart from hearing. But the speech of Moses was the very mouth of Hashem, and it is written, ‘So shall be My word that goes forth from My mouth: it shall not return to Me empty.’ Had his speech not been in exile, his words would have entered even the heart of the wicked Pharaoh. But since his speech was in exile, meaning that the husk then surrounded the speech, this is ‘Behold, the children of Israel did not listen to me, and how will Pharaoh listen to me, and I am of uncircumcised lips’: the foreskin surrounds the lips, and my speech is in exile. And in Rosh Chodesh Nisan, when the redemption of speech had already begun ... the time came for speech to go out of exile, as it says in the holy books, Pesach is peh sach, the mouth that speaks; that is, then their mouth was opened to sing the song at the sea.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 14: “Afterward it says, ‘I will restore your judges as at first’: this is Moses and Aaron. It corresponds to the Written Torah, which is the portion of Moses our teacher. And of Aaron it is written, ‘He shall be a mouth for you’; that is, he brings the Written Torah of Moses into the heart of Israel, for which reason he is called the attendant of the Matronita. And the Oral Torah of Moses our teacher is also ‘halakhah to Moses from Sinai.’ This is called ‘your judges,’ from the word mishpatim, meaning what is clear to the intellect and known to be from Hashem, like the Written Torah.”

k: volume-i|2060|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 24 (5656): “It is said that Shabbat is the aspect of Moses, as it says, ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion,’ and on it the Torah was given. This is the difference: all the prophets prophesied through a lens that does not shine, ‘Thus says Hashem,’ while Moses prophesied with ‘This is the word,’ a shining lens. A lens that does not shine is an illumination that must be clarified out of the darkness, as it says, ‘There was evening and there was morning,’ for the light renewed each day accords with the clarification that is made ... and it depends on a person's service; whereas Shabbat is a good gift and an additional soul that comes from the upper world. ... Before the redemption from Egypt there could not be a revelation of the Torah. Therefore even Moses did not prophesy with ‘This is the word,’ only with ‘Thus says Hashem,’ until after the exodus from Egypt. And therefore he said ‘I am of uncircumcised lips,’ for he felt in himself that his speech was not yet complete, the speech that was prepared for the prophecy of ‘This is the word.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 13: “Israel also merited this unification through the offering of Elijah, which he brought outside the Sanctuary at a time when high places were forbidden, which is punishable by karet; through the descent of the fire the Name of Heaven was sanctified and they said, ‘Hashem, He is God.’ And it says in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 7, on the verse ‘Your head upon you is like Carmel’: the empty ones among you are as beloved to Me as Elijah who went up Mount Carmel. We must understand why the empty ones are compared specifically to Elijah, and why Elijah is called here by the name Carmel. The intent is: just as Elijah on Mount Carmel offered at a time when high places were forbidden, only it was a temporary necessity, and not only was it not reckoned a sin but it was even favorable before Hashem, so too the empty ones among you: if they merit to repent out of love, then Hashem will clarify, as it says (Shabbat 89b), ‘If your sins be like scarlet’ ... and then ‘they shall be white as snow.’ That is, not only will they be atoned ... but they will become white as snow, like merits. This comes by the power of repentance out of love, through which deliberate sins become like merits (Yoma 86b), and he made this depend on Elijah, for this power comes through him.”

k: volume-i|2062|0|R. Dov Ber of Mezritch, Maggid Devarav L
quote: Parallel: R. Dov Ber of Mezritch, Maggid Devarav LeYaakov 105: “The general principle is that everything a person sees and hears, and all the occurrences that happen to him, all come to arouse him, whether in a matter of love, or of awe, or of glory, victory, acknowledgment, bonding or sovereignty. ... At times a person becomes afraid of something or of some creature; it all comes to him so that he may raise it up. At times he sees a matter of love or awe; for example, a person accustomed to mockery is shown mockery ... he should understand that he did not see this for nothing, or if he hears mockery, it is all so that he may rectify the mockery and sweeten it in its root, raising it to the root of love. ... And this is the principle: all his deeds should be in attachment to Hashem, and he should watch over everything he sees and hears and everything he does. This is what is said of Solomon, ‘He spoke of the trees and the stones,’ for on everything he saw he gave reasons that reach to the service of Hashem.”

k: volume-i|2063|0|R. Avraham Dov of Avritch, Bat Ayin, She
quote: Parallel: R. Avraham Dov of Avritch, Bat Ayin, Shemot 55–56: “One may say that in the parashiyot of Shovavim one must rectify the aspect of Da'at, and one can come to this aspect in these parashiyot. ... Therefore it is written in the writings of the Arizal to say during Shovavim, in the Shema recited at bedtime, the verse ‘Let me pass through your land; we will go by the king's highway; we will not turn to the right or the left’ (Numbers 21:22). This alludes that in Shovavim one must rectify the aspect of Da'at, to go on the king's highway, which is the aspect of Da'at that is called a ‘way,’ and not to turn right or left, but rather to include the left, which is the aspect of Gevurah, in the right, which is the aspect of Chesed (Zohar III 142a). And we may also say that this is the Arizal's intention, that Shovavim is the rectification of the blemish of the covenant, which is the aspect of peace, as it is written, ‘My covenant was with him, of life and peace’ (Malachi 2:5), which is the aspect of Da'at that is called peace, as above: the joining of Chesed and Gevurah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemot 1: “These six parashiyot correspond to the six sefirot from Chesed to Yesod. ... And Shemot, which is the account of the exile, is from the side of Chesed, as written at the beginning of Shemot Rabbah on this the verse ‘but he who loves him disciplines him early’ and ‘whom Hashem loves He rebukes,’ that it is from the side of love and kindness. ... Their afflictions and sufferings are not like the sufferings of the nations, which are to destroy them; but to Israel it is ‘as a man chastises his son,’ which is out of his love, his kindness and his goodness, since he cannot yet do him good and must chasten him and reprove him, for through this he will afterward be able to receive abundant good. And concerning this it is said, ‘All the sickness that I placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you, for I am Hashem your healer.’ And if there is no wound, why a cure? But the meaning is: even if there is a wound, it is not like the sickness in Egypt, which was to strike them and destroy them with the attribute of judgment; that I will not place upon you. Only when, Heaven forbid, it comes upon you, know that I am Hashem, the Name Havayah, which is from the side of the attribute of mercy, and I am your healer in this, like a physician who causes pain through the remedies, and the patient accepts it with love and affection, for he knows that he does not wish to afflict and strike him but only to do him good through it.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 8:2: “The intent is that the one depends on the other: if one wishes to sanctify the tongue, one must guard the mouth from foods that are not in holiness. … As Tosafot (Ketubot 104a) cite from the Midrash: before a person prays that words of Torah enter his mouth, let him pray that delicacies not enter his body. … And this is the meaning of what is said in the Mekhilta: the Torah was given only to those who ate the manna, and second to them, those who eat terumah. If the simple intent were that their hearts were free for Torah and they were not burdened with earning a living, there were men like R. Elazar ben Charsom and others who were wealthy; and why did they not mention those who eat the tithe, for the Levites too were free for Torah? Rather, the intent is as we said: for words of Torah to enter one’s heart, one must strive that one’s eating be in holiness. Therefore they mentioned the eaters of the manna, which was bread from heaven, and the eaters of terumah, which is also called holy. … And therefore Shabbat, when eating is in holiness, is called “speech,” which is the Oral Torah, for that is the time when words of Torah are absorbed within one’s heart.”

k: volume-i|2066|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Tamuz and Av 4:1: “The holy Rav, R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, said, as an allusion in the words of the Sages, ‘There were no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av’: the Sages said, ‘In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a circle-dance for the righteous.’ The matter of the circle-dance is that one who goes in a circle goes round and round the circumference, and there is no above and below, no head and end there. So too, in the future the righteous will have no envy or hatred, saying that this one is higher and above that one. It is like the constellations, each of which rises upward by way of its back, its face toward the back of its fellow below it, so that it appears to each one that it is rising first. And that is the festive day for Israel, when there is no envy, hatred, or rivalry among them. This is the allusion of ‘no festive days for Israel like the fifteenth of Av’: the fifteenth letter of the alphabet is samekh, which is round, all around, without head or end; that is the aspect of the circle-dance, and that is the great festive day for Israel.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tavo 11:2–3: “In Asarah Ma’amarot of the Rama of Fano it is stated that Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera, when he came upon Yael, the wife of Chever the Kenite. And it is brought from the holy Ari that Moses our teacher was the root of the Written Torah and Rabbi Akiva the root of the Oral Torah. For this reason Rabbi Akiva came from Sisera and from the wife of Chever the Kenite: in them were sparks of the aspect of the Oral Torah, and Sisera was the husk that encircled this holiness. And the Kenites, it is stated (Mekhilta, Yitro), went up from the city of palms, left the fat land of Jericho, and came before Jabez to learn Torah; and Jabez is Othniel ben Kenaz, who through his dialectic restored the laws forgotten in the days of mourning for Moses … and was the first to open the Oral Torah after Moses our teacher. The Kenites went to him because they too were of the root of the Oral Torah. … And this was the matter of the war with Sisera: because there was still included within him, in exile, the soul of Rabbi Akiva, who was the root of the Oral Torah. Therefore it is written, ‘From heaven the stars fought.’”

k: volume-i|2068|0|R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat
quote: Parallel: R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat Yisrael, Shavuot 2: “‘On this day they came into the wilderness of Sinai’: Rashi explains that it did not need to write ‘on this day’; rather, that words of Torah should be new to you as though He gave them today. It seems that his holy words allude that in truth, every single year, all the days of the world, that which happened in those days is revealed again. Just as in the days of Pesach, when they left Egypt, so every year there are souls of Israel who go out of Egypt; so too in this month, since they drew near before Mount Sinai, it is revealed again that one can draw oneself near to the Holy One, blessed be He, and receive the Torah. ... This is what Rashi meant, that words of Torah should be new to you as though He gave them today: that in truth each thing is revealed in its time, as it says, ‘they came into the wilderness of Sinai,’ meaning that they made themselves like this wilderness, which is empty and has nothing good in it; they too regarded themselves as a wilderness, as people who had not yet begun the service of Hashem at all.”

Parallel: Tzidkas HaTzaddik 151: “The times of descent a person has, when he has no desire at all for Torah and Divine service, are a preparation for a great ascent; that is, through the outcry he cries out when he reflects on his ways and sees his lowliness and his descent. As it is written, ‘They journeyed from Rephidim and came to the wilderness of Sinai’ (Exodus 19:2), and the Sages’ exposition of ‘Rephidim’ is well known (Sanhedrin 106a): that they slackened their hands from words of Torah. And this was the preparation for the Giving of the Torah, which is the ultimate strengthening of the hands in words of Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Sivan 5:1, 5:3: “Here four expressions of arrival are stated: ‘they came,’ ‘and they came,’ ‘and they encamped,’ ‘and he encamped.’ That is, there are several aspects and levels until one arrives at the point of truth. ... Disunity of hearts comes about because people's opinions are not alike, and that is only when there is self-interest in it and one intends one's own benefit. But when ‘truth springs from the earth,’ meaning that Hashem cast the aspect of truth down to flow into the earth, then of itself there comes about a unity of hearts and peace between divided opinions, since all of them together intend the goal of the point of truth. ... Afterward it says ‘and they encamped (vayachanu) in the wilderness,’ in the plural, each one by himself. But the culmination of the level of holiness is what is said after that, ‘and Israel encamped (vayichan) there,’ in the singular, as the Sages said: like one man with one heart. And these four levels pass over every human soul in the gradual stages of its entry into holiness, and they correspond to the four worlds, from below to above: Asiyah, Yetzirah, Beriah, Atzilut.”

k: volume-i|2071|0|R. Yitzchak Eizik Epstein of Homel, Chan
quote: Parallel: R. Yitzchak Eizik Epstein of Homel, Chanah Ariel, Pinchas 3:2: “So too one can understand the giving of the Torah to Israel below: because He opened the heavens for them, and ‘I am’ and ‘You shall have no’ we heard from the mouth of the Almighty Himself, through this it came about that ‘My Torah is in their heart’ (Isaiah 51:7), so that it is truly present within them, as written in the Kabbalistic writings on ‘And God spoke all these words, saying (lemor)’: ‘saying’ means that at every time and season that Israel will say [words of Torah], this will be ‘And God spoke,’ in the sense of ‘the word of Hashem, this is halakhah,’ as is known in several places. And this is the giving of the Torah: that the Torah from its highest root comes to dwell in glory within Israel, and from it spread forth the words of Torah that Israel speaks below. ... But in Torah, the main force that comes into a person’s Torah is the word of Hashem itself, and it is the principal mover that makes the words into words of Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 2: “The holiness of the new moon is the moon, which has nothing of its own, and especially on Rosh Chodesh, when it receives anew from the light of the sun and has nothing of its own; it signifies humility and lowliness. So too Shabbat: Tanna DeBei Eliyahu, at the beginning, expounds the verse ‘and what is the place of My rest’ as referring to Shabbat, and it is written after it, ‘and to this one will I look, to the poor and contrite of spirit.’ That is, on Shabbat, when fear and awe fall upon a person, he becomes poor and contrite of spirit by taking to heart all that has passed over him, and his spirit is broken and lowly within him. Therefore it is written, ‘And it shall be, from new moon to new moon and from Shabbat to Shabbat, all flesh (basar) shall come to bow down,’ because then he attains his own lowliness. This is the opposite of the plague of tzara’at, for of ‘flesh’ it is written, ‘and he shall be healed’; but one who is the opposite of this and grows proud like a cedar, holding himself in the aspect of ‘man’ (adam), of him ‘and he shall be healed’ is not written, until he lowers himself like the hyssop. This is the Gemara’s statement (Sotah 5a): ‘unless he makes his heart like flesh.’”

k: volume-i|2073|0|R. Chaim Tyrer of Chernowitz, Be'er Mayi
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Tyrer of Chernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Devarim 12:11: “It is known that when this one rises, that one falls, and the reverse: immediately when evil departs from a place through a person who brings holiness to rest there with Torah, prayer or good deeds, at once, as the evil departs, holiness and the light of Hashem rest upon that place. For the whole earth is full of His glory, and the eyes of Hashem roam over all the earth, and He greatly desires to spread the light of His holiness and providence over whatever He can. ... As soon as the evil departs, holiness is already prepared and ready to rest in that place, and in proportion to the driving out of the evil and the sitra achra is the spreading of the light of holiness. Therefore Scripture said, ‘In every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned I will come to you and bless you’: it says ‘I cause to be mentioned’ and not ‘you mention,’ to say that in every place where I Myself am able to mention My Name, where there is nothing of evil and the sitra achra, ... at once ‘I will come to you and bless you.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim 6:1: “The six days are mentioned first, for Scripture always mentions the days of work before Shabbat. See the Mekhilta, Yitro, on ‘Remember’: ‘remember it beforehand,’ for the six days of work are a preparation for Shabbat, and according to the preparation of the six days of work, so one merits the holiness of the Shabbat that follows them. This is also hinted in what is said (Beitzah 16a): ‘From the first day of the week, [prepare] for your Shabbat.’ Besides the preparation for the Shabbat meal in the plain sense, which is also the holiness that Israel brings into Shabbat, as it says, ‘sanctify it with food and drink,’ it hints further at the preparation during the days of work: the intention for the sake of Heaven that one has in every permitted act during the weekdays, through which one merits added holiness on the coming Shabbat. That is ‘from the first day of the week for your Shabbat.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 11:1: “‘A psalm of David: Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not want.’ On the Shabbat day we rest from all labor and from all dealings to provide for our livelihood, and we spend money on the delight of Shabbat. The nations mock us and say that whatever Israel toils for during the days of the week they eat on Shabbat, as in Eichah Rabbah 3:14; and with this argument R. Reuven ben Istroboli annulled the decree against keeping Shabbat, telling them, ‘Let them not work on Shabbat so that they become poor’ (Me’ilah 17a). Therefore, immediately at the entry of Shabbat after the evening prayer we say it, for we know that Hashem is my shepherd and so I shall lack nothing at all. And so we say this psalm after the third Shabbat meal, to draw this holiness into our hearts, so that we know even on the days of work, when we strive in the business of earning a living, that nonetheless Hashem is our shepherd and provider, and not the strength of our own hands; and therefore I shall not want even on a weekday.”

k: volume-i|2076|0|R. Chaim Vital, Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar Ha
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 18:7-12
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Vital, Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaShabbat 18: “When Ze’ir Anpin ascends and is wholly included in Arikh Anpin, it is close to the supernal Forehead, in the secret of the three upper levels of Atika Kadisha, and this is ‘a time of will’ (et ratzon). ... The judgments in Ze’ir Anpin are nullified, even though this is their time, because the supernal Forehead gazes upon it ... and all the worlds are in quiet and tranquility. ... Although on weekdays the judgments awaken at the time of Minchah, and one needs nefilat apayim and to give oneself over to death, now at the Minchah of Shabbat everything is simple mercy, for the supernal Chesed is revealed in the Forehead of Arikh Anpin, and when it gazes below all the judgments are subdued. Therefore, to show that those three righteous men did not die through judgment, they passed away at the Minchah of Shabbat, at the hour called ‘a time of will.’ ... At the time of the third meal no judgments are mentioned at all and everything is complete mercy, and therefore Moses departed at this hour and not in the morning, to show that he was hidden away in the secret of simple mercy. But the three, Moses, Joseph and David, needed to depart on Shabbat for the sake of the three lower levels of Malkhut that remain, to raise them up with her husband.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 13:1–2: “Our father Jacob, who said, ‘The God who shepherds me,’ whose eating was in holiness and who knew nothing at all of bodily pleasure, being like Adam before the corruption, thereby merited eternal life and did not die. Even though embalming, burial and eulogy were written of his body, it was only like sleep, as it says, ‘Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust.’ ... In the Midrashim and the Yerushalmi death is called ‘he slept’ (demakh), meaning that it is only like sleep, but there this is said of great men. Yet we find (Bereshit Rabbah 65) the story of a band of lawless men who used to eat and drink in the synagogue every Friday night ... and of one of them it says ‘he slept.’ Although they are called lawless, death is spoken of there as sleep, because it is mentioned that they ate every Friday night, keeping Shabbat; and one who keeps Shabbat merits eternal life. ... Then the whole flaw would be repaired as in the future; but the world is judged by its majority, while each soul individually, when it keeps Shabbat, merits eternal life, and although death has not yet been abolished, it is only like sleep and awakening.”

k: volume-i|2078|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayikra, Behar 15: “Israel merited the receiving of the Torah through the wilderness, as it is written, ‘I remember for you the kindness of your youth … your following Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.’ For the Torah is from the upper world, and one cannot merit the Torah until one sets aside all of this world and is drawn to trust in Him, blessed be He, alone. And so we ask, ‘And for the sake of our fathers who trusted in You, and You taught them the statutes of life.’ In truth, not every mind can bear this, only special ones, who are called His angels. So among the generations, the generation of the wilderness had this power, and all the generations are drawn after them; and in every generation there are individuals who have this power. … And so in the Shemitah year it is literally ‘your following Me in a land not sown,’ and the illumination of the receiving of the Torah was revealed to them. … For in the Shemitah year they were occupied only with the Torah of Hashem, and something like this applies to Shabbat, which should be made entirely Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayakhel 10:1: “The matter follows what is said in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 48): ‘The children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat, to make the Shabbat.’ Shabbat is mentioned here twice, corresponding to the upper and the lower Shechinah, that is, the upper heh and the lower heh, the upper Shabbat and the lower Shabbat. Afterward it says ‘for their generations (le-dorotam)’: happy is he who makes for them a dwelling (dirah) on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination is cleared out from there. … These are the two Shabbatot: first a person merits the lower Shabbat, which is fear, and afterward he merits bringing holiness into the heart until it benefits even the weekdays that follow, so that all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven and are like the work of the Mishkan. … ‘And on the seventh day there shall be holy to you a Shabbat of complete rest’: that they merit the upper Shabbat, so that the heart is a dwelling for the Shechinah in its two chambers. Then the evil inclination is cleared out entirely, and through this it can no longer enter to make him, Heaven forbid, desecrate the Shabbat.”

k: volume-i|2080|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Agra
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Yitro 11: “‘And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God (Elokim)’ (Exodus 18:12). I was asked why Scripture says he took the sacrifices for Elokim, when ‘one who sacrifices to the gods (elohim) shall be destroyed’ (Exodus 22:19). … The Zohar on Yitro (II 67b) says: there is a King above, there is a Priest, the mystery of the primordial light; on the side that is not the side of holiness there is also a king, the ‘old and foolish king,’ and beneath him a priest. The mystery of the matter: when this king and priest are subdued and broken and acknowledge Him, then the Holy One, blessed be He, rules alone above and below. Pharaoh first said, ‘I do not know Hashem,’ and then came and acknowledged, ‘Hashem is the righteous one’; afterward the priest who served beneath him was broken and subdued, until he came and acknowledged. The Torah was not given until Jethro came and acknowledged, ‘Now I know that Hashem is greater than all the gods.’ From this, understand: before the giving of the Torah there was made a model of the future, when all the husks and the Other Side acknowledged Him. Had the matter not been spoiled by the deed of the Calf, the glory of Hashem would already have filled the whole earth with no rule of the Other Side at all. Therefore, after Jethro said, ‘Now I know that Hashem is greater than all the gods,’ he took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for Elokim, for there was n

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Hashanah 5:1: “This is what we have said several times on the verse, ‘He declares His words to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel’: ‘His judgments’ specifically, meaning that they sense the taste in them. But of the nations it says, ‘and judgments, they have not known them’: even the judgments they do have, they cannot bring knowledge (da’at) into them. Of them it is not written ‘and His judgments,’ for the judgment of Hashem, blessed be He, belongs only to Israel. Among the nations, judgment is strict law, whereas among Israel it alludes to mercy, as it says in the Introduction of Eliyahu, ‘Judgment (mishpat) is known to be mercy,’ and in the holy Zohar, ‘Judgment is the Holy One, blessed be He.’ This is ‘His judgments,’ which are mercy and were handed over only to Israel, like the judgment of the Sanhedrin, which is with mercy.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Balak 3:3: “This is the matter of what is said in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 2): Moses, who loved Israel, compared them to the stars …; but Balaam, who hated them, compared them to dust; and Hosea, who was in between, neither loving nor hating, compared them to sand. One must understand how it could be said of Hosea that he did not love Israel, Heaven forbid. But the intent is that Moses our teacher saw only the righteous of Israel, ‘and your people are all righteous’; therefore he compared them to the stars, as the Sages said (Megillah 16a), when they rise, they rise to the stars. Balaam, who hated them, saw only the sinners; therefore he compared them to dust, as it says there, when they descend, they descend to the dust. And Hosea saw both the righteous and the opposite. This is the meaning of the Midrash, ‘one who flatters with the tongue’ — this is Balaam, who flattered in his prophecies, and they fell at Shittim: he gave them assurance that no one of Israel would be lost, so that they could rely on it to sin, Heaven forbid. And although the truth is that whoever is of Israel will not be lost, Heaven forbid, they will first suffer a great deal until they are refined and purified.”

Parallel: Resisei Layla 44:3: “This is the whole matter of Parashat Balak: to clarify the superiority of Israel over the idolatrous nations, even those wicked of Israel who have no share at all in the World to Come, who deny the Torah. They have no connection to Moses our teacher, who is the da’at of Israel by way of the bond of their hearts to Hashem, for they cut themselves off from it. Therefore these words were not said through Moses our teacher, only through Balaam. And they said in Bava Batra (14b), ‘Moses wrote his book and the section of Balaam,’ as though the section of Balaam were outside the Torah. That is, the Torah is called the Torah of Moses, and ‘his book’ is what his wisdom grasped; but the section of Balaam has no connection to the wisdom of Moses our teacher, for it speaks of people who denied the Torah. … Yet once Balaam had revealed these things, Moses our teacher took what he had swallowed out of his mouth, and they were written in the Torah by him. Once it was revealed that at the end of days, by virtue of the impression, they too are counted in Israel, they also have a connection to the Torah. All the souls of Israel come from the letters of the Torah, as is known, and the souls of the deniers and the apostates come from the letters in this section. Though it seems to be outside the Torah of Moses, it is nonetheless truly part of the Torah, and there is no difference at all between this section and the section of Shema Yisrael.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 6:1: “In the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah, end of 11): Shabbat said before the Holy One, blessed be He, ‘To each of them You gave a partner, and to me You gave no partner.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her, ‘Knesset Yisrael is your partner.’ … When Israel stood before Mount Sinai, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, ‘Remember what I said to Shabbat’ — that is, the utterance ‘Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it.’ This shows that Israel brings holiness into Shabbat, as it says, ‘to sanctify it.’ Shabbat is the attribute of Malchut, and Israel is her partner, who, as it were, give to her. That is, through Israel’s acknowledging the yoke of His kingship, Hashem, blessed be He, is crowned with a crown. And Shabbat is a semblance of the World to Come, one-sixtieth of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b), meaning that in it they sense a taste like the World to Come, the day that is entirely Shabbat.”

k: volume-i|2085|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayikra, Acharei Mot 9: “So it is with Hashem’s conduct in Torah and mitzvot: the good is not recognized until one fulfills the mitzvah in faith; then one sees and grasps the good. This is ‘which a man shall do and live by them’: after the deed he will find that he lives by them. … This itself is the meaning of ‘who do His word, hearkening to the voice of His word,’ which the Sages expounded of their putting ‘we will do’ before ‘we will hear.’ So it is with every mitzvah in particular: by the power of the doing one merits to hear the voice of His word hidden within it. … This is what the Sages said, ‘Like an apple tree, whose fruit comes before its leaves, so Israel put “we will do” before “we will hear”’; and Tosafot ask, is it not the Holy One, blessed be He, who is compared to an apple tree in the verse? But it is all one. Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is like an apple tree, He ordered the way of the Torah so that one must first fulfill the mitzvot of the Torah in deed, which is the fruit and completion of the Torah, and afterward the light of the Torah is revealed. Therefore Israel had to put ‘we will do’ before ‘we will hear,’ for they could not merit the Torah until the deed was first set right. And this proves that the Holy One, blessed be He, is like an apple tree. ‘And its fruit was sweet to my palate’ — they clung to the fruit, the fulfillment of the mitzvot in faith, even before the reasons for the mitzvot w

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 2:1: “The sum of the Torah is ‘I am’ and ‘You shall have no,’ which we heard from the mouth of the Almighty. ‘You shall have no’ includes all the negative commandments, which are to clear out the evil from the heart of the fool at his left … and ‘I am’ includes the positive commandments, so that the holiness of the utterance ‘I am Hashem’ shines in the heart. … ‘Remember’ and ‘Observe’ were said in one utterance (Shevuot 20b), and the main thing is ‘Remember’ with the mouth, the awakening from below to prepare oneself to receive the holiness of Shabbat that is fixed and abiding. ‘Observe’ is the guarding against desecrating it, so that nothing prevents receiving the holiness of Shabbat. In the first Tablets only ‘Remember’ is said, for it is the main thing: with the utterance ‘I am’ the Torah was implanted in their hearts, and with ‘You shall have no’ the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. … But in the last Tablets ‘Observe’ is said, for after the spoiling they needed guarding, so that the evil inclination would not enter and spoil, preventing the Shabbat from being kept, Heaven forbid, and the holiness from being received.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayakhel 5:1: “‘And seventy crowns are hers, and the King above, that all may be crowned.’ The matter of the crowns is as stated (Berakhot 17a), ‘The righteous sit with their crowns on their heads’; and ‘their crowns’ implies their own, namely the crowns all Israel merited at Mount Sinai corresponding to ‘we will do’ and ‘we will hear’ (Shabbat 88a), which the Holy One, blessed be He, will restore to us in the future. On Shabbat too we have an illumination of these crowns, as stated in Pri Etz Chaim (Gate of Shabbat 8) on ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion’: the crowns of the giving of the Torah, all of which Moses merited and took, he returns to Israel on Shabbat. It is further stated (Megillah 15b): ‘In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a crown on the head of every righteous one … to the remnant of His people: to one who makes himself like remnants.’ For the crowns of ‘we will do’ and ‘we will hear’ every righteous person merits by his deeds, but the crown of the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself, so to speak, only one who makes himself like remnants, like nothing, merits, and through this he attains the light of Keter, which is called Ayin (Nothing). … This is also alluded to in ‘Let us make crowns for them … with seventy crowns above fifty’: the seventy crowns allude to the crowns of the flow of holiness from Hashem Himself, for the seven holy attributes each comprise ten. ‘Above fifty’ — those are the crowns of ‘we will do’ and

k: volume-i|2088|0|R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat
quote: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat Levi, Vayikra, Kedoshim 1: “‘You shall be holy’ (Leviticus 19:2). In the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 24): Might one think, as holy as I am? Scripture says, ‘for I Hashem am holy’: My holiness is above your holiness. It seems to me … that a person approaches holy service through the service of the heart, which is prayer: he sets before his eyes the greatness of the Creator, blessed be He, and says, ‘What am I, to ask and cry out before the great King, the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He? Am I not dust, a maggot and a worm, full of sins and transgressions?’ Then he resolves, ‘From this day on I accept upon myself the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven truly and with a whole heart,’ and so each day he goes from level to level. … The closer one is to the King, the more one’s own lowliness appears in one’s eyes, and through this one can come to the level of Ayin (nothingness) and to great humility. … This is the intent of the Midrash: ‘My holiness is above your holiness’ means that because of the abundance of your holiness My Name is sanctified all the more. ‘My holiness above’ means that My Name is sanctified because of your holiness. How good and pleasant it is for every Jew to cleave to humility, … for then he causes His great Name to be sanctified through people who are surely important and do mitzvot and good deeds, and are nonetheless as nothing in their own eyes before the Creator; and so His Name is magnified among the m

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Emor 10:1: “So we find with Shabbat: in Ki Tisa it is said, ‘for it (hi) is holy to you … whoever does work on it (bah)’, all in the feminine; and in Vayakhel it is written, ‘whoever does work on it (bo),’ and likewise ‘and He sanctified it (vayekadshehu),’ in the masculine. This follows the holy Zohar, ‘Remember is for the masculine and Observe for the feminine,’ and the Midrash (Bereshit Rabbah 11): Shabbat said … the Holy One, blessed be He, said, ‘Knesset Yisrael is your partner,’ which is the utterance ‘Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it.’ ‘Knesset Yisrael is your partner’ implies that Shabbat receives holiness from Knesset Yisrael, Israel being her partner; and Shabbat is called in the feminine, meaning that Israel brings holiness into Shabbat. Yet ‘to sanctify it (lekadsho)’ is masculine, for afterward Shabbat becomes masculine and imparts holiness to Israel. Israel brings holiness into Shabbat — with what do they sanctify it? With food and drink — and afterward Israel receives holiness from the eating of Shabbat. As the holy Zohar says, ‘And I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel’ first, and afterward ‘I am Hashem who sanctifies you’: first a person draws holiness from below upward, and afterward they receive the flow from above downward.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Terumah 9:1: “In the holy Zohar on this portion (II 135b): ‘Happy are you, holy people, for you bless and sanctify below so that many supernal holy camps will be blessed and sanctified above.’ This follows what is said in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, end of 24), ‘For I am holy: My holiness is above your holiness,’ which means that My holiness above comes from your holiness, through the holiness of Israel. … Yet where does holiness come to Israel from? Only from what is said, ‘And God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it’: Hashem, blessed be He, gave holiness to the day of Shabbat, which is the attribute of Malchut, and they said (Shabbat 10b), ‘That you may know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you … I have a precious gift in My treasury, and Shabbat is its name, and I wish to give it to Israel.’ That is, Hashem, blessed be He, gave holiness to Israel, and they bring holiness into the day of Shabbat, as it says, ‘Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,’ remember it with the mouth: in sanctifying the Shabbat, Israel brings holiness into it. … And this is why the Zohar first says ‘you bless and sanctify below,’ for the blessing comes before the holiness; holiness cannot be pictured except after the blessing, which is the drawing down of blessing from Keter, the source of blessings.”

k: volume-i|2091|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Shabbatot 9:8: “‘Whoever gives delight to the Shabbat (ha-me’aneg et ha-Shabbat) is granted his heart’s requests.’ The Alshich, of blessed memory, noted the precise wording: it should have said, ‘whoever delights himself on Shabbat (ha-mit’aneg be-Shabbat).’ He answered that if a person says his delight is laughter and frivolity, strolls, idle talk and other things that are not good, we too will say to him: we are not responsible for your delight, since the Shabbat has no delight from this and no honor from this. Therefore they said, ‘whoever gives delight to the Shabbat.’ This is the opposite of what our master the Rema, of blessed memory, wrote in his Shulchan Arukh, that unlearned people who take delight in telling stories are permitted to speak of them on Shabbat; and it seems to me that he too wrote this only to speak well of Israel and to find merit for them. With this we understand ‘If you turn back your foot from the Shabbat’: turn back from the Shabbat what your feet are used to, that is, what you are used to enjoying in your animal soul with the vanities of the time and with strolls. That is not part of the delight of Shabbat, for the Shabbat takes no delight from it; only ‘and you shall call the Shabbat a delight,’ as above.”
