Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 5:1–2: “There are Torah scholars who are free only for Torah, ‘laborers in the Torah’ … and there is one who does not merit so much and must engage in work for his sustenance; yet as soon as he has free time he returns to his service and occupies himself with Torah, and these are called ‘those who hold the Torah.’ … The Pesikta, cited from the Yerushalmi (Shabbat 15), establishes ‘Shabbatot were given only for delight’ as referring to Torah scholars, whose eating on Shabbat ‘feeds on faith,’ for on Shabbatot they merit words of Torah from Hashem, blessed be He, without toil and labor; of them it says, ‘Then you shall delight in Hashem.’ … ‘Happy is the man (enosh) who does this’: who makes the Shabbat, bringing holiness into Shabbat through eating, as they said, ‘With what do you sanctify it? With food and drink’; this refers to one who merits to be a laborer in the Torah. Afterward it says, ‘and the son of man (ben adam) who holds fast to it’: one who did not merit so much and must work for his living … yet he is among those who hold the Torah. … On Shabbat let it be made entirely Torah, as at the beginning of Tanna DeBei Eliyahu: even for laborers who are greatly burdened during the weekdays, the Pesikta establishes ‘Shabbatot were given only for occupying oneself in Torah’ as referring to laborers. This is ‘and the son of man who holds fast to it’: at least he holds fast to the holiness of Shabbat, and then it benefits him for the weekdays, so t

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayechi 13:1: “It is stated (Zohar II 61b): ‘The most supernal nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions who occupy themselves in Torah, who eat the nourishment of the spirit and the soul … and it is called Wisdom, as it is written, “Wisdom gives life to those who possess it.”’ Surely the eating of Shabbat is even higher than bread from heaven, and is like the nourishment of the companions, which is called Wisdom. That is what the holy Zohar says afterward in the Book of Rav Hamnuna Sava: ‘“From Asher, his bread shall be rich”: this is the bread of Shabbat, which is pannag, double over one; lechem mishneh, two breads, bread from heaven and bread from the earth. This is bread of pannag, and that is the bread of poverty; and on Shabbat the lower bread is included in the upper bread.’ That is, on Shabbat there is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and the meals are in the mystery of oneg: Eden, River, Garden, for the river goes out of Eden to water the garden.”

k: volume-i|2094|0|R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShem
quote: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Vaetchanan 14: “‘Observe the Sabbath day to sanctify it’; and in the First Commandments it says ‘Remember the Sabbath day.’ We must understand what we say in the hymn Lekhah Dodi, ‘Observe and Remember in a single utterance,’ and why the poet departed from the order and wrote ‘Observe’ before ‘Remember.’ The matter is as stated: a person should always enter two doorways and then pray. Many explanations have been given for this, and the main explanation of the two doorways is fear and love, which are two gates and openings through which one can pray so that his prayer ascends on high, for prayer without fear and love does not fly upward. Fear is the attribute of the kingdom of Heaven, and it is ‘the gate to Hashem; the righteous shall enter through it’; it is the first doorway and gate, and after it is the gate of love. And it is stated in the holy Zohar that there are two Shabbatot, the Shabbat of Shabbat eve and the Shabbat of the Shabbat day: ‘Observe’ is the attribute of Malchut, the Shabbat of Shabbat eve, and ‘Remember’ is the Shabbat day. Accordingly the hymn rightly put ‘Observe and Remember in a single utterance,’ with ‘Observe’ first and then ‘Remember,’ for the fear of Heaven is the first gate, through which the righteous enter.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vaetchanan 5:1–2: “The chief aim of the mitzvot is only to fear Hashem … and about this the son asks, ‘What are the testimonies, the statutes and the judgments?’ — why did He give us so many mitzvot? He should have commanded only the aim, to love and fear Hashem. The answer is that in truth, were it not for the evil inclination, the utterance ‘I am’, through which Torah was implanted in their hearts, would have been enough. But ‘we were slaves to Pharaoh in Egypt,’ sunk in the husk like a fetus in its mother’s womb … therefore 613 mitzvot are needed, which are 613 counsels for attaining fear, because there is the evil inclination that can spoil. So too at the giving of the Torah: in the First Commandments it is written ‘Remember the Sabbath day,’ for from Israel’s side only an awakening from below is needed, to remember the Shabbat with the mouth, and then the holiness that is fixed and abiding comes of itself from Hashem. … Therefore the reason given there is ‘For in six days … and He rested on the seventh day,’ like what is said in the She’iltot: ‘Rest on the Shabbat day, just as I rested.’ For all the mitzvot are the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, who Himself fulfills the mitzvot. … Not so in the Second Commandments, which came after the spoiling: there it says ‘Observe the Sabbath day,’ for now guarding is needed lest the Shabbat be forgotten and desecrated, Heaven forbid, and by the guarding they bring holiness into Shabbat. Therefore it is w

Parallel: Maharal, Gevurot Hashem 45:1–2: “‘Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it … for in six days Hashem made,’ and so forth (Exodus 20:8–11). In Parashat Vaetchanan (Deuteronomy 5:15), in place of ‘for in six days Hashem made,’ it says, ‘And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt.’ The explanation is this: in the First Commandments He came to warn about the Shabbat and gave a cause for the holiness of Shabbat, that ‘in six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth.’ In the Second Commandments He gave a reason why Israel specifically was commanded about the Shabbat, and no other nation. Because in the Second Commandments it says ‘Observe the Sabbath day,’ and observing, which is not doing work, is not holiness for the Shabbat, being only a refraining from work, therefore it did not say with observing, ‘for in six days Hashem made the heavens and the earth; therefore Hashem blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.’ Observing is only a command to man not to do work on the Shabbat day; therefore it had to give a reason why Israel is commanded about the Shabbat more than all the nations, and so it said, ‘And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt,’ for the Shabbat is fitting for Israel in particular. As we have said, the going out from the house of bondage indicates separation and withdrawal from the physical.”

k: volume-i|2097|0|R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat
quote: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat Levi, Beshalach 56: “From here we can understand the view of Ramban, who wrote that it is a mitzvah to mention the Shabbat on every day of the week: on the first day one says, ‘Today is the first day toward Shabbat,’ and so on all the days of the week; and he wrote that this is the plain sense of ‘Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it,’ to remember Shabbat every day. The effect is that, since he remembers Shabbat every day, he looks forward every day to the Shabbat day in order to keep it; then when Shabbat arrives he guards it properly so as not to desecrate it, since it is dear to him, having waited for it. ... This explains the verse, ‘How long will you refuse to keep (lishmor)’: it uses the word ‘keep’ because shamar is an expression of waiting, as in ‘and his father kept (shamar) the matter,’ which means looking forward and hoping for the thing, when it will come to his hand.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 17:3: “Shabbat is a day of souls and not a day of the body, as in the Zohar (II 205a), and the soul is called ‘heaven’ and the body ‘earth,’ as in Sanhedrin 91b. On Shabbat a Jew is one of the people of heaven, having no business at all with matters of the body and the earth. ... Shabbat helps to engrave on the heart to do the will of the Omnipresent, as was the intended purpose of creation, ‘God made man upright,’ to be free only for Torah and service, as at the end of Kiddushin: ‘I was created only to serve my Maker.’ Only after the corruption, when he was cursed ‘by the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread,’ did the commandment of the Omnipresent become to rest only on Shabbat, and on the days of work labor was permitted; but the will of the Omnipresent is that a person be a laborer in Torah. ... At any rate, every Jew merits through the holiness of Shabbat, for the days of work that follow it, that even if he must engage in work for his livelihood, ... he will not be so sunk in it, and will remember that ‘the earth is Hashem’s.’ Even in bodily matters, which are called ‘earth,’ the will of Hashem is found, and that is the intention for the sake of Heaven through which a permitted act is sanctified to be like a mitzvah. And this is ‘shamor after it.’”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.”

: “Is there a purchase whose seller is sold along with it? The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: I sold you My Torah; as it were, I was sold along with it, as it says, “They shall take Me as a contribution.” It is like a king who had an only daughter. Another king came and married her, then wished to take his wife back to his own country. The father told him: The daughter I gave you is my only one. I cannot part from her, yet I cannot tell you not to take her, for she is your wife. Do me this kindness: Wherever you go, make me a small room so that I may live with you, for I cannot leave my daughter. So the Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: I gave you the Torah. I cannot part from it, yet I cannot tell you not to take it. Rather, wherever you go, make Me a house in which to dwell, as it says, “They shall make Me a sanctuary.””

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth”—would that He fix Torah study in our hearts as before! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it says, “I shall put My Torah within them and write it upon their hearts.” Rabbi Nechemya said: When Israel heard “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us—“You speak with us, and we shall hear”; “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” The evil inclination immediately returned to its place. They returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth!” He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it is written, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.””

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rav Yehudah said: Where does the Torah require the blessing after a meal? “You shall eat, be satisfied, and bless.” Where does the Torah require a blessing before Torah study? “When I proclaim Hashem’s name, ascribe greatness to our God.””
: “For I proclaim Hashem’s name: ascribe greatness to our God.”
: “For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yannai was walking along the road and saw a man who appeared very distinguished. He said: Will the master consent to be our guest? He replied: Yes. He brought him home, fed him, and gave him drink. He tested him in Scripture and found him unlearned; in Mishnah, aggadah, and Talmud, and found him unlearned. He said: Take the cup and recite the blessing. The man replied: Let Yannai bless in his own house. He asked: Can you repeat what I tell you? He replied: Yes. He told him to say: A dog has eaten Yannai’s bread. The man rose, seized him, and said: My inheritance is with you, and you withhold it from me! He asked: What inheritance of yours is with me? He replied: Once I passed a school and heard the children saying, “Moses commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.” It does not say “the congregation of Yannai,” but “the congregation of Jacob.” He asked: Through what merit did you eat at my table? He replied: Never have I heard an evil report and carried it back to its subject; never have I seen two people quarrelling without making peace between them. Yannai said: You possess all this proper conduct, yet I called you a dog! He applied to him, “One who orders his way”: one who evaluates his path is worth much. For Rabbi Yishmael bar Rav Nachman said: Proper conduct preceded Torah by twenty-six generations, as it is written, “To guard the way of the tree of life.” “The way” is proper conduct, and afterward, “the tree of life” is Torah.”

: “We learned: Torah gives a person 613 kinds of counsel for becoming complete with his Master, because his Master wishes to benefit him in this world and the world to come—especially the world to come. Everything through which God perfects a person is perfected through the good he merits in the world to come. Why? Because the world to come belongs to God.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “Likewise Torah scholars, children of the King and Matron, are called Shabbatot and festivals. They have nothing of their own, for they are not workers like the other servants, children of the ordinary realm. Their reward in this world and the world to come is to be delighted with every kind of food and drink and honored with beautiful garments, like Shabbat, of which it says, ‘Honor it with clean clothing.’ Whatever a person does for Shabbatot and festivals should be done for them.”

: “When the Tree of good and evil rules—the ordinary realm of purity and the ordinary realm of impurity—the sages, who resemble Shabbatot and festivals, possess only what those belonging to the ordinary realm give them. They resemble Shabbat, which has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “Another interpretation: “They shall take a contribution for Me.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke to Moses about the Tabernacle, Moses said before Him: Master of the universe, can Israel make it? The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: Even one person of Israel can make it, as it says, “From every man whose heart moves him.””
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

: ““This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek Your face, Jacob, selah.” Rabbi Yehudah the Patriarch and the Sages disagree: one says that the generation corresponds to its leader; the other says that the leader corresponds to his generation. In what respect? If this concerns virtue—one holding that a worthy generation has a worthy leader, and the other that a worthy leader has a worthy generation—there is Zedekiah, who was worthy although his generation was unworthy; and Jehoiakim, who was unworthy although his generation was worthy. For Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: What does “At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah” teach? The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to return the world to chaos because of Jehoiakim; when He considered his generation, He was appeased. He wished to return the world to chaos because of Zedekiah’s generation; when He considered Zedekiah, He was appeased. Rather, the discussion concerns forcefulness and gentleness.”

: ““Go down.” He said: Master of the universe, yesterday You told me, “You shall ascend, and Aaron with you,” and, “To Moses He said: Ascend to the Lord.” Yet here You say, “Go down”! He replied: You ascend here for My children’s honor, not your own. I told their ancestor, “Behold, angels of God were ascending and descending upon it.” What does “upon it” mean? I told him: When your children are righteous, they rise and are exalted in the world, and their emissaries rise with them. When they descend, they and their emissaries descend. “Go down”—why? “For your people have corrupted themselves.” He told him: Since they sinned, you and they descend.”
: “Bring near to yourself your brother Aaron and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve Me as priests: Aaron, and Aaron’s sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

: “Come and see: When the ancient nations wished to appoint a king, they brought someone from elsewhere and set him over themselves, as it says, “A king reigned in Edom—from Dinhabah,” and from Bozrah, and so with all of them. Israel is different: their great people, kings, priests, prophets, and officers come from among themselves. “From him the cornerstone”—this is King David, as it says, “The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone.” “From him the peg”—this is the High Priest, as it says, “I shall fasten him as a peg in a secure place.” “From him the battle bow,” as it says, “Armed with bows, using the right and left hands.” “From him every ruler shall emerge together”—these are the judicial scribes. Likewise it says, “Bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him.” From where? “From among the children of Israel.””
: “The sons of Amram were Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, to consecrate him as most holy, he and his sons forever: to burn incense before Hashem, serve Him, and bless in His name forever.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Emor 7: “All forms of holiness are present within Israel. The priests were merely chosen to perform the sacred service, and priestly holiness flows from Israel's holiness. My holy teacher once asked why the priests do not recite every day, “Who made me a priest.” I replied: Israel likewise does not recite “Who made me an Israelite,” but “Who did not make me a gentile or a slave”; nor do we recite “Who made me a man,” but “Who did not make me a woman.” The reason one cannot bless “Who made me an Israelite” is that a person still possesses free choice. One is called Israel by choosing the good, and who knows whether he will withstand his choices? He therefore blesses only for not having been made a gentile or a slave: at least he has been placed within the sphere of choosing the good. Similarly, “Who did not make me a woman” expresses that he can choose to fulfill the additional commandments incumbent on a man. A priest likewise cannot bless “Who made me a priest,” since it remains his choice to bring holiness into his heart and to avoid profaning his priesthood. He certainly cannot bless “Who did not make me an Israelite,” for the priests themselves are also Israelites; Heaven forbid that he should say that. My teacher agreed that this was a true answer. He himself explained that priests have no intrinsic superiority, since all their holiness comes from Israel, which brings holiness into them. He added that this is the dispute in the Mishnah in Middot: t

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””

: “Rabba bar Rav Huna visited the house of Rabba bar Rav Nahman. They served him three se’a of cakes prepared with rich oil. He asked them: Did you know I was coming? They replied: Are you more important to us than Shabbat?”
: “For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””

Parallel: R. Ovadiah Sforno on Exodus 25:8:1: ““I will dwell among them, according to all that I show you.” I will dwell among them to accept their prayer and service, in the manner in which I show you My Presence on the mountain: above the cover, between the two cherubs, with the design of the Tabernacle and all its vessels. The Tabernacle’s design signifies cherubs, the seraphim standing above Him seen by the prophets. Some are in the Holy Place and some in the Holy of Holies, in two sets joined by clasps so as to become one in serving their Creator. Likewise, all Israel’s holy people should be joined to the common people, to give understanding and instruction.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “For I have given you a good teaching; do not abandon My Torah.”

: “Is there a purchase whose seller is sold along with it? The Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: I sold you My Torah; as it were, I was sold along with it, as it says, “They shall take Me as a contribution.” It is like a king who had an only daughter. Another king came and married her, then wished to take his wife back to his own country. The father told him: The daughter I gave you is my only one. I cannot part from her, yet I cannot tell you not to take her, for she is your wife. Do me this kindness: Wherever you go, make me a small room so that I may live with you, for I cannot leave my daughter. So the Holy One, blessed be He, told Israel: I gave you the Torah. I cannot part from it, yet I cannot tell you not to take it. Rather, wherever you go, make Me a house in which to dwell, as it says, “They shall make Me a sanctuary.””
: “My son, if you receive my words and store up my commandments within you—”

: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: To what may this be compared? To a man with a grown daughter who seeks to marry her off to anyone he finds. My Torah is not like that: only if you possess merit will you attain it. Thus, ‘Treasure My commandments with you.’”

: “At the giving of the Torah, all Israel said, “We shall do”: they were “those who do His word.” Their souls are rooted in the letters of Torah, and through their souls they bring Torah into being. Thus the Sages say that Zelophehad’s daughters merited having the passage of inheritance stated through them; their eyes saw what Moses’ eye had not seen. They brought that passage’s revelation into the world. All Israel likewise brought the whole Torah’s revelation into the world, becoming “those who do His word.” Through this they could “hear the voice of His word,” like ministering angels—and, in their own sphere, the sages.”

quote: : ““The man of Sokho”: He was lord of the place called Sokho. Ish means a lord, as the High Priest is addressed in Yoma, 18, as ishi, “my lord.” Bartenura explains there, in the first chapter, Mishnah three: Ishi means adoni, “my master.””

: “R. Samuel bar Nahmani said in R. Yonatan’s name: The evil inclination incites a person in this world and testifies against him in the World to Come, as it says, “One who pampers his servant from youth will have him become a manon in the end.” In R. Hiyya’s Atbach cipher, a witness is called manon.”
: “Hashem, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, preserve this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of Your people’s heart, and direct their heart toward You.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

: “It was taught: R. Shimon ben Menasya says: Alas for a great attendant lost from the world! Had the snake not been cursed, each person in Israel would have had two good snakes available. One he would send north and one south, to bring him fine sandelbonin gemstones, precious stones, and pearls. Moreover, one could loop a strap beneath its tail and use it to transport soil for his garden and ruined plot.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 59b:21:2: ““Sandelbonin”—the name of a precious stone.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 9: ““Jacob came whole to the city of Shechem,” and “he bought the portion of the field.” The Midrash says that this is one of three places concerning which the nations cannot taunt Israel by claiming that they are stolen: the Cave of Machpelah, the Temple, and Joseph's burial place at Shechem, all of which were purchased with money. Establishing a holy place requires money and a price, as the Zohar says that the practical effort to draw a holy spirit upon oneself must be made at full cost. When Jacob arrived at Shechem and “encamped before the city,” he established the Shabbat boundaries: he established the place in a holiness resembling Shabbat. This was Shechem, at his first entrance into the Holy Land, and therefore he bought the place at full cost. The meaning follows the Sages' statement that Shechem is a place appointed for calamity: there Dinah was violated, there Joseph was sold, and there David's kingdom was divided. Jacob came to repair the place through the holiness of the Land and to implant within it the holiness of the three Patriarchs, the root of eternal life. He therefore had to repair jealousy, desire, and the pursuit of honor, the three defects opposing the Patriarchs' holiness and removing a person from eternal life. Shechem was especially prepared for these defects. Dinah's violation was the defect of desire. Joseph's sale arose from jealousy, as it says, “His brothers were jealous of him.” The Sages also say that murdere
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “The silver is Mine, and the gold is Mine, declares Hashem of Hosts.”

: “A student of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai went abroad and returned wealthy. The other students saw him and envied him, and wished to go abroad too. Rabbi Shimon learned of this and took them to a valley facing Meron. He prayed: Valley, valley, fill with gold dinars! Gold dinars began flowing before them. He said: If you seek gold, here is gold; take it. But know that whoever takes now takes his portion of the world to come, for Torah’s reward is only in the world to come. Thus: “She laughs at the final day.””

: ““They brought him further willing offerings morning by morning”—what is meant by “morning by morning”? R. Samuel bar Nahmani said in R. Yonatan’s name: From something that descended for them morning by morning. This teaches that precious stones and pearls descended for Israel with the manna. “The nesiyim brought the onyx stones”—a tanna taught: Actual clouds. Likewise Scripture says, “Clouds and wind, but no rain.””

: ““I sleep.” The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I sleep concerning commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I sleep concerning charitable deeds, but my heart is awake to perform them. I sleep concerning sacrifices, but my heart is awake for reciting the Shema and prayer. I sleep concerning the Temple, but my heart is awake for synagogues and houses of study. I sleep concerning the appointed end, but my heart is awake for redemption. I sleep concerning redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: Where do we find the Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel’s heart? In this verse: “God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.””
: “My flesh and my heart are spent; God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.”

: “If you object, ‘Come, buy and eat; come, buy wine and milk without money or price’—so it is free, an occupation with God—the answer is this: whoever wishes may merit Torah study. Whoever wishes to occupy himself with knowing God may merit it without payment at all. But service of God fulfilled through an action must not be acquired freely and empty-handed. Through such an action one merits drawing the spirit of holiness upon oneself only by paying the full price.”

: “How do we know that God delights in him and has made His dwelling within him? When we see that person’s desire to pursue and labor after God with his heart, soul and will—joyfully and willingly—we know with certainty that the Shekhinah rests within him. We must then acquire that person at full price, joining him and learning from him. Therefore the ancients said, ‘Acquire a companion for yourself’: one must acquire him at full price to merit the Shekhinah. Up to this point, one must pursue the righteous person and acquire him.”

: “I know, my God, that You examine the heart and desire uprightness. With an upright heart I willingly offered all these things; now I have seen Your people present here joyfully offering willingly to You.”
: “The people rejoiced in their willing offerings, for they offered to Hashem with a whole heart. King David, too, rejoiced greatly.”
: “Hashem, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, preserve this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of Your people’s heart, and direct their heart toward You.”
: “From new moon to new moon, and from Shabbat to Shabbat, all flesh will come to bow down before Me, says Hashem.”

: “On Shabbatot and festivals they shed their garments and ascend to behold their Master’s glory and properly delight in upper delight: ‘From new moon to new moon and Shabbat to Shabbat, all flesh shall come to bow before Me, says the Lord.’ Does all flesh come? Should it not say every spirit or every soul? What is ‘all flesh’? God made a person in this world after the pattern of the exalted Glory above. That upper Glory is spirit to spirit and soul to soul, until it reaches a lower place called body. A spirit from the source of life, called All, enters this place. Through it come all that body’s goodness, nourishment and provision. Thus ‘The earth’s advantage is through All’: this All is the spirit of that body. Likewise, a person in this world is a body with a ruling spirit, patterned upon the upper spirit called All that rules the body above. This is called ‘all flesh’; hence ‘All flesh shall come to bow before Me.’ Of that delight it says, ‘No eye has seen, O God, besides You, what You will do for one who awaits You.’”

: “When Adam was created, what is written? ‘You clothed me with skin and flesh.’ If so, what is the person? If you say he consists only of skin, flesh, bones and sinews, that is not so. A person is certainly nothing other than the soul. The skin, flesh, bones and sinews are only clothing, the person’s garments, not the person himself. When this person departs, he removes the garments he was wearing.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

: “Therefore it is written, ‘Let them take an offering for Me, from every man’: from one called ish, who has overcome his inclination. Whoever overcomes his inclination is called ish. ‘Whose heart makes him willing’: what does this mean? One in whom God takes delight. Thus ‘On Your behalf my heart says,’ ‘the Rock of my heart,’ ‘the good-hearted,’ and ‘his heart was gladdened’ all speak of God. So too here, ‘whose heart makes him willing’: from him take My offering, for it is found there, not elsewhere.”

: “Another interpretation: “They shall take a contribution for Me.” When the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke to Moses about the Tabernacle, Moses said before Him: Master of the universe, can Israel make it? The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: Even one person of Israel can make it, as it says, “From every man whose heart moves him.””
: “If Hashem delights in us, He will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.”

: “Concerning these three it is written, 'They shall make Me a sanctuary.' Every Israelite has a share in this, for the making comes from Israel: the sanctuary and Tabernacle were made through Israel’s voluntary hearts. Midrash Rabbah says that even one Israelite could make it, as it says, 'From every person whose heart moves him.' The principal thing is made through the heart’s generosity, as the Zohar states. Every Israelite likewise has a share in Shabbat’s holiness, as in 'To make the Sabbath': Israel make and introduce holiness into Shabbat, as in 'Remember it to sanctify it' and 'Guard it to sanctify it.'”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “Take from among yourselves a contribution for Hashem. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it as Hashem’s contribution: gold, silver, and copper.”

: “Rava asked: If a woman says, “Here is a maneh, and I will become betrothed to you,” what is the law? Mar Zutra said in Rav Pappa’s name: She is betrothed. Rav Ashi said to Mar Zutra: If so, property carrying security would be acquired together with property that carries no security. But we learned the reverse: Property carrying no security is acquired together with property carrying security, through money, a deed, or possession. He answered: Do you think she said, “Acquire me along with it”? Here we are dealing with a distinguished man. Through the benefit she receives from his accepting a gift from her, she resolves to transfer herself to him in betrothal.”

: “How do we know that God delights in him and has made His dwelling within him? When we see that person’s desire to pursue and labor after God with his heart, soul and will—joyfully and willingly—we know with certainty that the Shekhinah rests within him. We must then acquire that person at full price, joining him and learning from him. Therefore the ancients said, ‘Acquire a companion for yourself’: one must acquire him at full price to merit the Shekhinah. Up to this point, one must pursue the righteous person and acquire him.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “Take from among yourselves a contribution for Hashem. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it as Hashem’s contribution: gold, silver, and copper.”

: ““Make a teacher for yourself”: Do not learn by your own reasoning alone, but from a teacher and from received tradition. “Acquire a companion for yourself”: Some explain this as books, and some as an actual companion, because two are better than one. So it says, “A sword against those who are alone, and they become foolish.””

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Tzidkat HaTzadik 187:1: “Help with Torah comes through a teacher, companions, and pupils. We ask, “Graciously grant us wisdom, understanding, and knowledge from You”—the three just mentioned in section 186—so that they should come from You without human assistance. This accords with the Midrash’s statement about our forefather Abraham, “He had no teacher,” and with the verse, “For Hashem gives wisdom; from His mouth...” For this purpose Torah was given to Israel: it should serve as both teacher and companion. As Rashi’s commentary on Avot explains, some interpret “Acquire a companion for yourself” as referring to books. In truth, books are a person’s teachers. As Shvut Yaakov, part II, writes, for this reason, when one could consult a book, ruling can be comparable to ruling in one’s teacher’s presence. This, however, describes the beginning. Later, when one develops new insights through them, they enter the category of a companion.”

Parallel: Resisei Layla 12: “Prayer is principally in the heart, as the Sages say: “What is service in the heart? Prayer”; and “One who prays must direct his heart,” with many similar teachings. Torah seems principally to belong to the mind, yet we ask, “Place understanding in our hearts.” As is known, wisdom and understanding correspond to mind and heart. Wisdom means the general teachings of Torah that are explicit; understanding means reflecting upon one thing from another explicit teaching, so as to judge and give instruction when an actual situation arises. The Sages likewise speak of a person's heart forgetting, indicating that new understanding springs from the heart. Wisdom and understanding are two inseparable companions, for only what instructs the heart is called Torah. Thus the Sages say that, for one who learns without intending to act, it would have been better not to have been created; and one who claims to possess Torah alone does not possess even Torah. It is written, “Why is there a price in a fool's hand to buy wisdom, when he has no heart?” Whoever has no heart is called a fool even if he knows teachings of Torah. He merely holds the price with which to buy wisdom; he does not actually possess wisdom if it is absent from his heart. Hence the Sages say of Doeg that all his Torah was only from the lips outward, meaning that it had not been absorbed into his heart. Similarly, “To the wicked God says, ‘What have you to do with recounting My statutes ... upon y

: “Rabbi Berekhiah sat and expounded: what does ‘Let them take an offering for Me’ mean? Raise Me up through your prayers. Who should do so? One whose heart volunteers to withdraw from this world. Honor him, for I rejoice in him because he knows My Name. It is fitting to receive My offering from him, as it says, ‘From everyone whose heart volunteers, take My offering’—from that willing person. Rabbi Rechumai said: Israel’s righteous and pious raise Me above the whole world through their merits. The heart is nourished from them, and the heart nourishes them.”

: “'And this is the contribution': according to the way of truth, it resembles 'The Lord gave wisdom to Solomon.' Likewise, it is written, 'And this is what their father spoke to them, and he blessed them'; 'And this is the blessing'; and 'This came from the Lord.' They already alluded to this in Bereshit Rabbah, in the exposition of 'I gain understanding from elders'; let the understanding person discern. Shemot Rabbah explains 'And this is the contribution you shall take from them' as the congregation of Israel, which is a contribution, as it says, 'Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of His produce.' Elsewhere there, the Holy One, blessed be He, says to Israel, 'I sold you My Torah, and, as it were, I was sold with it,' as it says, 'Let them take a contribution for Me.' That is, the contribution will be Mine, and I shall be with it, like 'My beloved is mine, and I am his.' Likewise, He said, 'According to all that I show you,' for 'I' am the One showing; and 'He showed you' alludes to the word ani, 'I'; likewise, 'Which you are shown.' David similarly said, 'Everything in writing, from the Lord’s hand upon me, He gave understanding,' for the Lord’s hand was upon him.”

: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me? says Hashem of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. Yet you ask, “How have we despised Your name?””

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”

: “There was another incident: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa went to learn Torah with Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, whose son became ill. He told him, “My son Chanina, pray for mercy upon him, so that he may live.” Chanina placed his head between his knees, prayed for mercy, and the child recovered. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said: “Had Ben Zakkai pressed his head between his knees all day, they would not have heeded him.” His wife asked him: “Is Chanina greater than you?” He answered: “No; he is like a servant before the king, while I am like a minister before the king.””

: “Rabbi Yochanan said: The especially devoted would finish reciting Shema at sunrise. A baraita likewise teaches: They would finish at sunrise so as to join the redemption blessing directly to prayer and thus pray by daylight. Rabbi Zeira said: What verse supports this? “May they fear You with the sun, and before the moon, through all generations.””
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

: “He began: ‘Let them take an offering for Me.’ Here is a single comprehensive union, above and below. It does not say, ‘Let them take an offering,’ but ‘Let them take an offering for Me’: above and below together in one whole, without any separation.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

: “Rabbi Berekhiah sat and expounded: what does ‘Let them take an offering for Me’ mean? Raise Me up through your prayers. Who should do so? One whose heart volunteers to withdraw from this world. Honor him, for I rejoice in him because he knows My Name. It is fitting to receive My offering from him, as it says, ‘From everyone whose heart volunteers, take My offering’—from that willing person. Rabbi Rechumai said: Israel’s righteous and pious raise Me above the whole world through their merits. The heart is nourished from them, and the heart nourishes them.”
: ““Six days you shall labor and perform all your work.” Can a human being perform all his work in six days? Rather, rest on Shabbat as though all your work were complete.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””
Commentary: Rashi on Taanit 8b:12:2: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”

: “On Shabbat it corresponds to the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, called All and called Shabbat, to add delights to him from the concealed brain. On the new moon it corresponds to the Congregation of Israel, called the moon.”
: “On the third day Joseph said to them, “Do this and live, for I fear God.””

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Rabbi Berekhiah sat and expounded: what does ‘Let them take an offering for Me’ mean? Raise Me up through your prayers. Who should do so? One whose heart volunteers to withdraw from this world. Honor him, for I rejoice in him because he knows My Name. It is fitting to receive My offering from him, as it says, ‘From everyone whose heart volunteers, take My offering’—from that willing person. Rabbi Rechumai said: Israel’s righteous and pious raise Me above the whole world through their merits. The heart is nourished from them, and the heart nourishes them.”

: “Because he has set his love upon Me, I will deliver him; I will raise him securely because he knows My name. He will call upon Me, and I will answer him. I am with him in distress; I will rescue him and honor him.”
: “Therefore My people will know My name; therefore, on that day, they will know that I am the One speaking: here I am.”

: “‘But I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.’ If it is true, why call it merely ‘inscribed’? And if it is merely inscribed, why call it ‘true’? Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi asked, ‘Did you not know how to answer?’ Rabbi Levi replied: ‘It is inscribed before the decree is issued; it is true once the decree has been issued.’ What is truth? The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our Master said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: It is emet, ‘truth.’ What is emet? Reish Lakish said: Alef stands at the beginning of the alphabet, mem in the middle, and tav at the end, corresponding to ‘I am the first, and I am the last.’”
: “Thus says Hashem, King of Israel and its Redeemer, Hashem of Hosts: I am first and I am last, and apart from Me there is no god.”

: “Israel has not yet rejoiced in My world. It does not say “Israel rejoiced in its Maker,” but “Israel shall rejoice”: they will rejoice in the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the future. As it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, has not yet rejoiced in His world. It does not say “The Lord rejoiced in His works,” but “The Lord shall rejoice”: the Holy One, blessed be He, will rejoice in the deeds of the righteous in the future.”
: “May Hashem’s glory endure forever; may Hashem rejoice in His works.”

: “One must establish delight in her: the Righteous One issuing from Eden, which is Binah, the world to come, ‘to water the garden,’ the lower Shekhinah. The river is vav, issuing from yod-he and extending five hundred years, the five sefirot, until it reaches the Righteous One, from whom the garden, he, is watered. Thus ‘A man shall leave his father and his mother and cling to his wife,’ and so forth.”

: “What distinguishes lower Eden from upper Eden? As light surpasses darkness. Lower Eden is called feminine Eden; upper Eden is called masculine Eden, of which it says, ‘No eye has seen, O God, besides You.’ Lower Eden is called a garden in relation to Eden above, while this garden is called Eden in relation to the garden beneath it. Those in the lower garden delight in this Eden above them every Shabbat and every new moon, as in ‘From new moon to new moon and from Shabbat to Shabbat.’”

: “Bereshit bara can be read ‘house, head’: Father and Mother. Bara is rendered in Aramaic bera, ‘son,’ the middle pillar, of which it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden.’ There is one Eden and another, as in ‘You give them drink from the stream of Your delights’—Your Edens, indeed. Upper Eden is the upper Crown; a lower Eden is yod. There is another lower Eden, the upper Mother, dalet: she is Eden relative to the river beneath her. Thus it is written, ‘A river goes out from Eden to water the garden.’”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry is described by ‘A river goes out from Eden’—vav—‘to water the garden.’ The river is the middle pillar; ‘goes out from Eden’ means from the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ means the lower Shekhinah.”

: “Her priests violated My Torah and profaned My sacred things. They did not distinguish between holy and ordinary, nor teach the difference between impure and pure. They hid their eyes from My Shabbats, and I was profaned among them.”
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”

: “‘Wisdom—from where is it found?’ Torah proceeds from Wisdom, the place called Holiness. Wisdom proceeds from the place called Holy of Holies. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Jubilee is likewise called holy, as in ‘It is Jubilee; it shall be holy to you.’ Israel includes these aspects, as it says, ‘You shall be people of holiness to Me.’”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rabbi heard that Rabbi Pinhas ben Yair had arrived, went out to meet him, and asked: Would you like to dine with me? He answered: Yes. Rabbi’s face shone. Rabbi Pinhas said: Do you imagine that I have vowed not to benefit from Israel? Israel are holy. Some are willing to give but have nothing; others have something but are unwilling to give. Chaim Vital, Sha'arei Kedusha, Part I, Gate 2:3: “Character traits are implanted in a person within the lower soul, called the elemental soul, which comprises four aspects: mineral, vegetative, animal, and speaking. These too consist of good and evil. Good and bad traits depend upon this soul. They form the seat, foundation, and root of the higher, rational soul, upon which the Torah's 613 commandments depend, as explained in the first gate. Thus character traits are not counted among the 613 commandments. Yet they are essential preparations for fulfilling or nullifying those commandments, because the rational soul cannot fulfill the commandments through the body's 613 limbs without the mediation of the elemental soul, which is joined to the body itself. This is the mystery of “The life of all flesh is its blood, bound up with its life.” Therefore the matter of bad character traits is far more severe than the transgressions themselves.”
