: “Rabbi Eleazar said: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”
: “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield. Hashem grants favor and honor; He does not withhold goodness from those who walk wholeheartedly.”

: “Similarly, it says, “You shall confer some of your splendor upon him”—some, but not all your splendor. The elders of that generation said: “Moses’ face is like the face of the sun; Joshua’s face is like the face of the moon. Alas for that shame! Alas for that humiliation!””

: “When the sukkah becomes complete in its thigh, it is said of Jacob, ‘Jacob came whole.’ Jacob is certainly the image of the middle pillar on its outer side. Moses was there too, but on its inner side: this one pertains to the body, and that one to the soul. Therefore the middle pillar’s two thighs are complete: Netzach and Hod.”
: “Hashem said to Moses, “See, I have made you as a god to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.””

k: volume-ii|166|0|Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of Shabbat 8:51–52
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 8:51-52
quote: : “Also intend the following, as already explained regarding ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion.’ When Moses ascended the mountain to receive the Torah, he was given a thousand portions of light, represented by the large alef of ‘Adam, Seth, Enosh.’ When Israel made the calf, these were lost through Israel’s sin. He was left with only one of the thousand portions, hence the small alef of Vayikra. Moses himself had not sinned; the loss came through Israel’s sin. God therefore made up his loss from Israel’s portion: the crowns and lights that were Israel’s ornaments, removed at Horeb, were subsequently taken by Moses to replace what he had lost because of them. Every Friday night, however, Moses again receives the thousand portions he lost, as the additional holiness of Shabbat. He then returns Israel’s crowns to them; from these crowns Israel inherits the additional holiness of Shabbat each Friday night.”
: “Overlay it with pure gold; overlay it inside and outside, and make a gold rim around it.”

k: volume-ii|168|0|Rashi on Exodus 25:11, s.v. MiBayit uMiC
quote: : “'Cover it inside and outside': Bezalel made three chests, two of gold and one of wood, each with four walls and a base, open at the top. He placed the wooden chest inside a golden one and a golden one inside the wooden one, then covered its upper rim in gold. It was thus covered inside and outside, as stated in Yoma 72.”
: ““Overlay it inside and outside.” Rava said: Any Torah scholar whose inside is not like his outside is not a Torah scholar.”

k: volume-ii|170|0|Mizrachi on Exodus 25:11, quoting Ibn Ez
quote: : “'Cover it inside and outside': Bezalel made three chests, two of gold and one of wood, as stated in Yoma, chapter Ba Lo, and Tanchuma. The sage Ibn Ezra objected: Once the ark was made of gold, what need was there for wood? Our sages already explained the reason in Tanchuma: the Omnipresent alluded to us that just as you honor the ark although wood is placed within it—as it says, 'Place them in the ark,' and both the tablets and the broken tablets rested in the ark—so, if you see poor Torah scholars, honor them for their Torah. The sages further expounded in Mekhilta: Why was it made from acacia wood? Because Torah is called a tree of life, as it says, 'It is a tree of life to those who hold it,' and it was placed inside. Why was it covered in gold? Because the words of Torah are more desirable than gold and much fine gold.”
: “Shittim: They committed folly, shetut, and angered Me with the calf. Let the acacia wood, atzei shittim, come and atone for their folly.”

: “I also asked Rabbi Eliezer: What does the name Shittim mean? He answered me: Shittim is its name. This is a dispute between tannaic opinions: Rabbi Eliezer says, “Shittim is its name”; Rabbi Yehoshua says, “It means that they engaged in foolish conduct.””

: “Reish Lakish said: A person commits a transgression only when a spirit of folly enters him, as it says, “If any man’s wife goes astray.” The word “goes astray” is written in a form that suggests folly.”

: “Rav Kahana said: What is meant by “For He spoke, and it came to be”? This refers to a wife. “He commanded, and it stood”—this refers to children. It was taught: A woman is a skin-bag filled with excrement, and her mouth is filled with blood; yet everyone pursues her.”

: “Abaye heard a man say to a woman, “Let us set out early on the road.” He said, “I will go and keep them from wrongdoing.” He followed them for three parasangs through a marsh. When they parted, he heard them saying, “The road is long, but our company was pleasant.” Abaye said, “Had I been there, I could not have restrained myself.” He went, leaned against the door bolt, and grieved. An elder came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow has a greater evil inclination.”
: “Hashem, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, preserve this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of Your people’s heart, and direct their heart toward You.”
: “Hashem saw that human wickedness had become great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was only evil, all day long.”

k: volume-ii|178|0|Arizal, teaching quoted by R. Tzadok, Pe
quote: : “The roots of the kelippot are Ishmael and Esau. As the Arizal wrote, thirty-five branches spread from one on the right and thirty-five from the other on the left. Ishmael’s kelippah is desire and alien longing; Esau’s is murder and anger. At present, anger is still needed within holiness for blotting out Amalek and for the indignation of Torah scholars. In the future, when all evil is removed, this kelippah will cease.”

: “Rabbi Shimon taught: he is a deceiver and always has been, dwelling with the evil inclination, which deceives. Thus ‘the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean’—the cunning bone; ‘from Paddan Aram’—from a pair of deceivers, as padna of oxen means a pair. ‘Sister of Laban’: sister of the evil inclination, the Aramean. We learned that when it was defiled by sins in this world, it was called Lot. In the future, when no longer defiled as before, like one bathing and immersing from impurity, it is called Laban, ‘white.’ In any event, the evil inclination does not disappear from the world.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. Rabbi Yitzchak asked: ‘Did our companions, the sages of Mishnah, teach that the evil inclination will be forgotten from the world except at the time of coupling?’ He answered: ‘By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed. Without it there would be no joy in learning; but it will not be debased as formerly, leading to sin. Thus “They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.”’ Rabbi Shimon said: it is the heart, the evil inclination’s dwelling. Rabbi Eliezer said: a good heart builds body and soul. Hence ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart,’ for this is the foundation of everything.”

Parallel: Tzidkat HaTzadik 44: “A person who has an intense longing for bodily desires should not become despondent and think how defective he must be to possess so great a longing. On the contrary, he is a vessel prepared for a powerful love and longing in the search for truth. This is how the old man—Elijah, according to the interpretation cited by Tosafot, which I have heard is correct; the difficulty raised by Tosafot there is not our subject—consoled Abaye. Accordingly, the Sages say that in the future the righteous will perceive the evil inclination as a mountain, while the wicked will perceive it as a strand of hair. This is no falsehood: both are true, because the righteous possess exceedingly powerful longing and desire.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””
: “On a good day, enjoy the good; on a bad day, consider: God made the one corresponding to the other, so that a person cannot discover anything that will come afterward.”

: “On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s channels will flow with water. A spring will come forth from Hashem’s house and water the Valley of Acacias.”

: “Rahava said in Rav Judah’s name: Bezalel made three arks: the middle wooden one was nine handbreadths high, the inner golden one eight, and the outer one ten and a little more. … “Overlay it inside and outside.” Rava said: Any Torah scholar whose inside is not like his outside is not a Torah scholar.”

Parallel: Maharal, Gur Aryeh on Exodus 25:11:1: “Ibn Ezra asks: since one had in any event to make three arks, two of gold and one of wood, why not make one gold ark? Our Sages already gave a reason in the Midrash: because Torah is called “a tree of life,” the ark was wooden. This is profound. Torah is called “a tree of life to those who grasp it,” and wood is an enduring planting. So the words of Torah are joined, planted, and attached to God, who exists eternally, and thereby they endure forever. Gold, for all its importance, is no planting. But the covering is gold, and there is a wondrous reason that what appears should be gold: “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, wealth and honor.” Length of days is the World to Come, which is unseen: “No eye has seen, God, besides You.” Hence the wood, signifying the eternal planting, was covered and hidden, while honor belongs to this world and is visible. Therefore wood was within, and wealth and honor were seen. With understanding you will find further that wood within, and gold outside and inside, is the right and fitting arrangement according to wisdom.”

: “When Israel begin to bless, a voice travels through all the heavens sanctified by Shabbat eve’s holiness: ‘Happy are you, holy people, blessing and sanctifying below so that many upper holy camps may be blessed and sanctified above!’ Happy are they in this world and the world to come. Israel do not recite this blessing until crowned with crowns of holy souls, as we said. Happy is the people granted merit in this world, to merit the world to come.”

: “‘Now I know that he is a holy man of God who passes by us,’ followed by ‘Let us make a small walled upper room.’ This verse gives us support for the arrangement of prayer. ‘Now I know’ is the intention one must place within oneself during prayer. ‘He is a holy man of God’ is the upper world: He sits upon His glorious throne, all sanctifications proceed from Him, and He sanctifies all worlds. ‘He passes by us continually’: from the holiness by which He sanctifies the upper worlds, He sanctifies us in this world. There is no holiness above unless there is holiness below, as in ‘I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel.’”
: “Do not profane My holy name; I shall be sanctified among the Israelites. I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “When it says that the three holinesses are considered as one, it does not mean that they are equal in degree, but that they are all one holiness. This follows the holy books’ explanation of “My holiness is above your holiness”: My holiness above comes from your holiness. In truth, God cannot be grasped at all, and the description “holy” would not apply to Him except because Israel recognizes His holiness. Their apprehension is precisely that He is holy, set apart from all apprehension; through this He is called holy. Thus the verse cited concerning God’s holiness is “You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel.” Through Israel’s praises, God is called holy, because they recognize His holiness and kingship. “Enthroned upon the praises of Israel” follows the Midrash’s explanation of “Your throne is established from then”: When You stood at the sea and we sang before You with “Then,” Your kingship became established and Your throne secure. Through the praises of Israel, who recognize His kingship and praise Him as one praises a king, He is, so to speak, enthroned, as the Midrash explains.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: ‘Since you were consecrated to My name before I created the world, be holy just as I am holy,’ as it says, ‘For I am holy.’ Therefore it says, ‘You shall be holy.’ To what is this comparable? To a king who betrothed a woman. He told her: ‘Since you are betrothed in my name, I am king and you are queen. My honor is your honor, because you are my wife.’ So the Holy One told Moses, ‘Go and sanctify the people,’ as it says, ‘Sanctify them today and tomorrow.’ He sanctified Israel and said to them, ‘You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ Why? ‘For I, the Lord, am holy.’ You, too, shall be holy, since I consecrated you to My name, as it says, ‘Speak to the entire congregation of the children of Israel and tell them: You shall be holy.’”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “Rava bar Mehasya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: A person who gives a gift to another must inform him, as it says, “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” A baraita likewise teaches: “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: I have a fine gift in My treasure house, and its name is Shabbat. I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them. From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: One who gives a child bread must inform the child’s mother.”
: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it.”

: “The laws of obstructions to immersion are from the Torah, for it says, “He shall wash all his flesh in water”: Nothing may intervene between his flesh and the water. “In water” means the water of a mikveh. “All his flesh” means enough water for his entire body to enter. How much is that? A cubit by a cubit to a height of three cubits; the Sages assessed the mikveh’s water at forty se’a. The received law is needed for his hair, as Rabba bar Rav Huna said: One knotted hair forms an obstruction; three do not; about two I do not know. But hair is also included by the Torah! A baraita teaches: “He shall wash et all his flesh”—the word et includes what is subordinate to his flesh, namely his hair.”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people alone, leave exile, the river that had been parched and dry is described by ‘A river goes out from Eden’—vav—‘to water the garden.’ The river is the middle pillar; ‘goes out from Eden’ means from the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ means the lower Shekhinah.”

: “Come and see: ‘Blessed is Adonai, day by day He loads us.’ Adonai is spelled alef-dalet-nun-yod, and this verse is a secret of wisdom. ‘Day by day’ is the two full years, as in ‘At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and he was standing over the river.’ It is a secret, as explained: this is Joseph. This river is Joseph the Righteous.”

: “‘Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.’ The companions explained this verse. Dominion is Abraham: ‘You are a prince of God among us,’ and ‘I shall bless you and magnify your name.’ Fear is Isaac: ‘The Fear of Isaac was mine.’ ‘He makes peace in His heights’ is Jacob: ‘Grant truth to Jacob,’ and ‘Love truth and peace.’ Truth and peace are bound to one another. Therefore he is the perfection of everything.”
: “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it separates into four headwaters.”

: “Through the righteous man called All, this drawing-down is attained. The supernal crown is the crown of kingship, and one merits uniting above and below without any separation at all: 'Let them take for Me a contribution.'”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: Go and tell Israel: My children, just as I am set apart, so you shall be set apart; just as I am holy, so you shall be holy. Thus it is written, “You shall be holy.””

: “Therefore ‘Between Me and the children of Israel’ is written. Because all faith is found within Shabbat, a person is given another soul: an upper soul containing every perfection, an image of the world to come. Hence it is called Shabbat. What is Shabbat? God’s Name, the Name complete on every side.”
: “The human soul is Hashem’s lamp, searching all the innermost chambers.”

Parallel: Resisei Layla 24: “The whole meaning of the Tabernacle, the altar, and the order of service is to bring the Divine Presence down into the lower world, to arrange repairs and atonements for sins, to cleanse every kind of stain, and to beautify and adorn the bride. This follows from His dwelling below: once His Presence is revealed within Israel's hearts, every stain is naturally cleansed, and evil and darkness are driven away, for light dwells with Him. That is the meaning of Mishkan: a place of indwelling. Mikdash, however, means a place of holiness, which is precisely the opposite of indwelling. Holiness means separation and distinction, something set apart; the Divine Presence means dwelling and joining, without separation, as it says, “Who dwells with them amid their impurities.” Holiness, by contrast, is separation from impurity. Yet we find the Tabernacle called a sanctuary and the sanctuary called a Tabernacle. They are all one, and both are simultaneously true: the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells within Israel and is also separate from them. This resembles the teaching, “I feared through my joy, and rejoiced through my fear.” Joy is like that between companions, arising from love and union; fear arises from the respect due to someone greater and separate. With God, both exist together, and neither suffices without the other: fear alone brings folly, while joy alone brings frivolity.”

: “Why did the Torah begin with bet, as does berakhah, ‘blessing’? How do we know that Torah is called blessing? It says, ‘Full of the Lord’s blessing, inherit sea and south.’ The sea signifies Torah, as in ‘broader than the sea.’ What is ‘full of the Lord’s blessing’? Wherever bet occurs, it expresses blessing, as in bereshit. Reshit means wisdom, as in ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord’; and wisdom is blessing, as it says, ‘God blessed Solomon,’ and ‘The Lord gave Solomon wisdom.’ This resembles a king who married his daughter to his son, gave her to him at the wedding, and said, ‘Do with her as you wish.’”
: “Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali is satisfied with favor and filled with Hashem’s blessing; possess the west and the south.”

: “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: What does “Happy are you who sow beside every water, sending forth the foot of ox and donkey” mean? Whoever occupies himself with Torah and acts of kindness merits the inheritance of two tribes. It says, “Happy are you who sow”: sowing means charity, as it says, “Sow for yourselves in righteousness and reap according to kindness.” Water means Torah, as it says, “Let everyone who thirsts come to the water.””

: “At that time it will be said of Moses and Israel, ‘Then you shall delight above the Lord,’ with oneg: ayin for Eden, nun for river, gimel for garden. ‘Then Moses will sing’ will be fulfilled: it does not say ‘sang,’ but ‘will sing.’ For the mixed multitude, delight, oneg, will turn into affliction, nega, and likewise for the idolatrous nations, as happened to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, upon whom blistering boils broke out. For Israel, however, there will be delight.”

: “This is what the teaching means: “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it over wine as it enters. This establishes the obligation at night; from where do we derive it by day? Scripture says, “Remember the Shabbat day.””

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “Rabbi Chelbo asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani: It is written, “When Rachel had given birth to Joseph”—why did Joseph’s birth make the difference? He answered: Our father Jacob saw that Esau’s descendants could be delivered only into the hands of Joseph’s descendants, as it says, “The house of Jacob shall be fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble.” He objected: “David struck them from twilight until the evening of the following day.” He answered: The person who taught you Prophets did not teach you Writings, where it says, “When he went to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh joined him: Adnah, Yozavad, Yediael, Michael, Yozavad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of the thousands belonging to Manasseh.” Rav Yosef objected: “Five hundred men from the children of Simeon went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Yishi; they struck the remnant of Amalek that had escaped and lived there to this day.” Rabbah bar Shila answered: Yishi descended from Manasseh, as it is written, “The sons of Manasseh: Chepher and Yishi.””
: “Yours, Hashem, are greatness, strength, beauty, endurance, and splendor, for everything in heaven and on earth is Yours. Yours, Hashem, is the kingship, and You are exalted as head over all.”

: “Scripture specifies these six upper days: ‘Yours, Lord, are greatness, might and beauty,’ and so forth. ‘For all’ is the Righteous One; ‘in heaven’ is Tiferet; ‘and on earth’ is the Congregation of Israel. The Targum renders it ‘which unites heaven and earth’: the foundation of the world, called All, unites Tiferet, called heaven, with the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.”

: “Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.” “He summons the heavens above”—this is the soul. “And the earth to judge His people”—this is the body.”
: “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it separates into four headwaters.”

: “Scripture specifies these six upper days: ‘Yours, Lord, are greatness, might and beauty,’ and so forth. ‘For all’ is the Righteous One; ‘in heaven’ is Tiferet; ‘and on earth’ is the Congregation of Israel. The Targum renders it ‘which unites heaven and earth’: the foundation of the world, called All, unites Tiferet, called heaven, with the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.”

: “Rabbi Shimon taught: ‘The middle bar within the boards, running from end to end’ is holy, perfect Jacob, as explained from ‘Jacob was a complete man, dwelling in tents.’ It does not say ‘dwelling in a tent,’ but ‘in tents’—two, holding this one and that one. So here, ‘The middle bar within the boards, running from end to end’: holding this one and that one.”
: “Abraham was old, advanced in years, and Hashem had blessed Abraham in everything.”

: “‘I ate of everything.’ Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Nechemya differed. Rabbi Yehudah said: He tasted everything created during the six days of Creation. Rabbi Nechemya said: He tasted all the good prepared for the future. Esau asked him, ‘But what did he actually feed you?’ Isaac replied, ‘I do not know; I tasted bread, meat, fish, locusts, and every delicacy in the world.’”
: “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.”
: “The land’s benefit extends to all; even a king is served by the field.”

: “On Shabbatot and festivals they shed their garments and ascend to behold their Master’s glory and properly delight in upper delight: ‘From new moon to new moon and Shabbat to Shabbat, all flesh shall come to bow before Me, says the Lord.’ Does all flesh come? Should it not say every spirit or every soul? What is ‘all flesh’? God made a person in this world after the pattern of the exalted Glory above. That upper Glory is spirit to spirit and soul to soul, until it reaches a lower place called body. A spirit from the source of life, called All, enters this place. Through it come all that body’s goodness, nourishment and provision. Thus ‘The earth’s advantage is through All’: this All is the spirit of that body. Likewise, a person in this world is a body with a ruling spirit, patterned upon the upper spirit called All that rules the body above. This is called ‘all flesh’; hence ‘All flesh shall come to bow before Me.’ Of that delight it says, ‘No eye has seen, O God, besides You, what You will do for one who awaits You.’”

: “If he merits more, he is given a nefesh through Atzilut, from the side of the only daughter, called the king’s daughter. If he merits more, he is given a ruach of Atzilut from the middle pillar’s side, and is called God’s son: ‘You are children of the Lord your God.’ If he merits more, he is given a neshamah from Father and Mother, as in ‘He breathed into his nostrils a soul of life.’ What is life? Yod-he, of which it says, ‘Let every soul praise Yah.’ Through him the divine Name is completed.”

: “Come and see: ‘Blessed is Adonai, day by day He loads us.’ Adonai is spelled alef-dalet-nun-yod, and this verse is a secret of wisdom. ‘Day by day’ is the two full years, as in ‘At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and he was standing over the river.’ It is a secret, as explained: this is Joseph. This river is Joseph the Righteous.”

: “Why was the passage of forbidden sexual relationships placed next to the passage of holiness? To teach that wherever you find restraint from forbidden sexual relationships, you find holiness. This accords with Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi, who said: Whoever guards himself against sexual immorality is called holy.”
: “For when he sees his children, My handiwork, in his midst, they will sanctify My name. They will sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.”

: “When Adam was created, what is written? ‘You clothed me with skin and flesh.’ If so, what is the person? If you say he consists only of skin, flesh, bones and sinews, that is not so. A person is certainly nothing other than the soul. The skin, flesh, bones and sinews are only clothing, the person’s garments, not the person himself. When this person departs, he removes the garments he was wearing.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Noach 4: “Moses, too, possesses the holiness of Shabbat, as we say, “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion,” which is Shabbat. Moses selected Shabbat for Israel in Egypt, as the Midrash says. Tikkunei Zohar asks, “Was Moses not there?” and answers that he was on the inner side: this one is from the body and this one from the soul. Jacob corresponds to the body, and from him comes the bodily holiness of all Israel who descend from him. Jacob and Joseph are one, as the Zohar says. The life-force, which is the blood, is the body's vitality; Joseph is called the Life of the worlds, and his aspect is the body's vitality, corresponding to nefesh. He establishes that Israel's souls are holy. Moses corresponds to neshamah, the holiness of the root of Israel's souls, which derive from Torah, as it says, “A person's soul is the lamp of the Lord.” Every Jewish soul has a root in Torah, a letter or part of a letter; Moses is the root of all the Torah teachings, called the Torah of Moses. These three come to repair Adam's defect in body, life-force, and soul.”

: “When this lower point rises, becomes visible and adorns herself—another reading says rises to be crowned with the patriarchs—all joy is found above and below, and every world rejoices. On this night this point spreads its light and extends its wings over the world. Every other dominion is removed, and protection rests upon the world.”

: “On Shabbat it corresponds to the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, called All and called Shabbat, to add delights to him from the concealed brain. On the new moon it corresponds to the Congregation of Israel, called the moon.”

k: volume-ii|229|0|R. Bachya ibn Pakuda, Duties of the Hear
ref: Duties of the Heart, Fourth Treatise on Trust 3:62-64
quote: Parallel: R. Bachya ibn Pakuda, Duties of the Heart, Gate of Trust 3:62–64: “He will receive reward for directing his heart and innermost intention toward God in these activities, whether his aim is achieved or not. As Scripture says, “When you eat the labor of your hands, happy are you, and it is well with you”; and our Sages said, “Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.” His trust in God will remain whole. Seeking the means through which to obtain his livelihood will not impair that trust at all, when his heart and inward intention in doing so are for Heaven's sake. He must not imagine that his livelihood depends on one particular means, so that if that means is withheld no other can supply it. Rather, he should trust God for his provision, knowing that all means are equal before the Creator. He provides through whichever He chooses, whenever He chooses, from whichever source He chooses. As Scripture says, “Nothing prevents the Lord from saving through many or through few”; “It is He who gives you strength to make wealth”; and “Not by force and not by strength, but by My spirit, says the Lord of hosts.””

This teaches you: If an individual sins, he is told, “Go to that individual”; if a community sins, it is told, “Go to that community.” Both examples are needed. Had only the individual been mentioned, one might attribute the possibility of repentance to his sin’s not being public, unlike a community’s public sin. : “The festivals are called “sacred convocations” because Israel imparts holiness to them. Although Shabbat’s holiness is fixed and enduring, the portion of Emor also calls it a “sacred convocation”: a Jew must bring holiness into Shabbat as well. Thus “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it” is fulfilled through the day’s Kiddush, and the second version says, “Observe it to sanctify it”: accepting the sovereignty of Heaven through observing Shabbat brings holiness into it. The essential ability of Israel to impart holiness exists only through the Exodus. Before this, holiness was mentioned only regarding Shabbat—“He sanctified it”—meaning holiness bestowed by Hashem. When the Exodus began, “This month shall be for you” gave Israel the power to sanctify the month. Thus the head of the court declares, “Sanctified.””

: “This is the meaning of the first version of the Ten Commandments. Through “I am Hashem,” Torah study was implanted in their hearts, and through “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They were thus free from the evil inclination and subjugation, without the burden of earning a livelihood. In the wilderness they ate manna and their clothing did not wear out, so that they could occupy themselves with Torah. Their Shabbat commemorated the work of Creation. The later tablets came after the sin, when toil in worldly affairs became necessary. Shabbat then provides rest from labor for bodily needs, so that one can study Torah on Shabbat; this is one’s rest. That is why “observe” is said there: it requires vigilance in the heart. Someone occupied with bodily needs during the working week might forget on Shabbat and do something forbidden, and therefore needs vigilance. The first version says “remember,” the place where forgetfulness has no hold, as the Zohar teaches. In the later commandments, Shabbat commemorates the Exodus: liberation from Pharaoh’s service in order to become servants of Hashem. So too, on Shabbat one is freed from worldly labor to serve Hashem through Torah. Every Jew possesses both these aspects of Shabbat, although one predominates in some people and the other in others.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “‘Wisdom—from where is it found?’ Torah proceeds from Wisdom, the place called Holiness. Wisdom proceeds from the place called Holy of Holies. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Jubilee is likewise called holy, as in ‘It is Jubilee; it shall be holy to you.’ Israel includes these aspects, as it says, ‘You shall be people of holiness to Me.’”

: ““She saw that he was good.” It was taught: Rabbi Meir says that his name was Tov. Rabbi Yehuda says his name was Toviyah. Rabbi Neḥemya says he was suited for prophecy. Others say he was born circumcised. The Sages say: When Moses was born, the entire house filled with light. Here it says, “She saw that he was good,” and elsewhere, “God saw that the light was good.””
: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn, whatever first opens a womb among the Israelites, whether human or animal; it is Mine.”
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”

: “An objection is raised: “Would that their heart were always like this”—it was impossible to remove the angel of death from them, for the decree had already been issued. Israel received the Torah only so that no nation or tongue would rule over them, as it says, “So that it may be well with them and their children forever.” Reish Lakish follows the other tanna, for a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose says that Israel received the Torah only so that the angel of death would not rule over them, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings, all of you children of the Most High.” But you ruined your deeds, and therefore, “Yet like Adam you shall die.””
: “I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.””

: “‘A king is bound by the channels.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: ‘I have made you king. Just as a king’s people carry out his decree, so you shall decree upon them and they shall carry it out.’”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave Israel three good gifts, all of them through suffering: Torah, the Land of Israel, and the World to Come. What is the source for Torah? “Happy is the man whom You discipline, God, and teach from Your Torah.” For the Land of Israel: “As a man disciplines his son, Hashem your God disciplines you,” followed by, “For Hashem your God brings you to a good land.” For the World to Come: “The commandment is a lamp and Torah is light; the way of life is the reproof of discipline.””

k: volume-ii|381|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Tetzaveh 5635, s.v. BaMidrash nimsh'lu: “Israel's first generosity was certainly without dregs, when they said, “We will do and we will hear.” By properly giving their first strength to God, they merited that even after they had gone wrong they could still be refined from the waste. This is “beaten for the light”: the first drop stands before the Lord in the holy Sanctuary. Yet bringing satisfaction to God comes through refinement from the dregs. This is the meal offering: “Who usually volunteers a meal offering? A poor person.” All this is attained through the first drop. Thus “pure, beaten” enables “raising a lamp continually,” even during periods of mixture. That is why, while rebuking them, the prophet called them “a flourishing olive tree”: he told them that they possess the power to refine their deeds even in troubled times. This also applies to each individual. If an action begins properly, with a true desire for Heaven's sake, one merits refining it afterward, even when waste becomes mixed into it.”

: “'And you shall command.' Moses is not mentioned in this section, unlike every other section of the Torah from his birth onward, apart from Deuteronomy. The reason is that he said, 'Erase me, please, from Your book that You have written'; the curse of a sage takes effect even when conditional, and it was fulfilled here.”

: “According to the view that David’s question concerned concealed property consumed by fire, they sent him a received teaching; why, then, does it say, “David would not drink it”? He did not transmit the ruling in their names. He said: “This is the tradition I received from the court of Samuel of Ramah: When someone exposes himself to death for words of Torah, no halakhic teaching is transmitted in his name.” “He poured it out to Hashem”: according to the other two interpretations, he acted for Heaven’s sake. But according to the concealed-property interpretation, what does “He poured it out to Hashem” mean? He transmitted the ruling as an anonymous received teaching.”

: “Another interpretation of “Be attentive and hear, Israel”: Wear yourselves down for words of Torah. This accords with Reish Lakish’s teaching: From where do we learn that words of Torah endure only in one who sacrifices his life for them? It says, “This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 63b:14:1: ““Wear yourselves down”: they also interpret “be attentive” as “make”—make yourselves crushed, taking pains over words of Torah.”

: “Concerning them Scripture says, “For Your sake we are killed all day long; we are regarded as sheep for slaughter.” … Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: This refers to Torah scholars who sacrifice their lives for words of Torah, following Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish. For Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Words of Torah endure only in one who sacrifices his life for them, as it says, “This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent.””
: “For Your sake we are killed all day long; we are considered sheep for slaughter.”

k: volume-ii|387|0|Oral teaching reported by Rav Tzadok in
quote: : “This follows what I heard from our holy teachers concerning 'David did not desire to drink them': he did not transmit the teachings in their names. 'Anyone who gives himself over to death for Torah has no halakhic teaching stated in his name'; 'He poured them out to the Lord' means he stated them as an anonymous teaching of the Gemara. Why should someone who gives himself over to death for Torah be punished? The sages said that Torah endures only in someone who puts himself to death over it. This means actual self-sacrifice, since Gittin 57 b cites that teaching concerning 'For Your sake we are killed all day.' His longing for Torah is so great that he does not feel his self-sacrifice at all, although Torah is not among the matters that override preserving life. The teacher explained that this is no punishment. Since he gives himself over to death for Torah, his Torah is included in its supernal source and no longer belongs to his individual soul: it is literally God’s word. Therefore no halakhah is stated in his name, but anonymously as the Gemara’s teaching, like a law given to Moses at Sinai.”
: “Now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, please erase me from Your book that You have written.”

: “Rabbi Kruspedai said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah: one for the wholly wicked, one for the wholly righteous, and one for those in between. The wholly righteous are immediately inscribed and sealed for life; the wholly wicked are immediately inscribed and sealed for death. Those in between remain suspended from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur. If they merit it, they are inscribed for life; if they do not, they are inscribed for death. Rabbi Avin asked: Which verse teaches this? “Let them be erased from the book of the living, and not be inscribed with the righteous.” “Let them be erased from the book” refers to the wicked person’s book; “the living” to the righteous person’s book; and “not be inscribed with the righteous” to the book of those in between. Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak derived it from this verse: “If not, erase me, please, from Your book which You have written.” “Erase me, please” refers to the wicked person’s book; “from Your book” to the righteous person’s book; and “which You have written” to the book of those in between.”
: “'Approach the altar': Aaron was ashamed and afraid to approach. Moses said to him, 'Why are you ashamed? For this you were chosen,' as taught in Sifra.”
: “He said, “Please, my Lord, send through whomever You will send.””

: “The matter is disputed by tannaim: “The Lord’s anger burned against Moses.” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says: Every instance of divine anger in the Torah leaves a mark, but no mark is stated here. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: A mark is stated here too: “Is not Aaron your brother the Levite?” Was he not a priest? Rather, He said: I had intended you to be a priest and him a Levite; now he will be priest and you a Levite. The Sages say: Moses served as a priest only during the seven days of inauguration. Some say: Priesthood ceased only from Moses’ descendants, as it says, “Moses, the man of God—his sons were called after the tribe of Levi”; and, “Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who called His name.” Why add the second verse? You might have said that the first passage concerns later generations; therefore it also says, “Moses and Aaron among His priests.””

: “What anger was there? The priesthood was taken from Moses and given to Aaron. Our Rabbis of blessed memory said: “Is not Aaron your brother the Levite?” Once it says “your brother,” do I not know that he is a Levite? Rather, He told him: You were fit to be priest, and he a Levite. But because you refuse My words, you will be a Levite and he a priest.”

: “Moses’ name is therefore absent from this entire portion, which discusses priestly holiness, because a person’s name comes from the root of his soul, and Moses’ soul is rooted in Torah’s crown. He is mentioned only by allusion: 'And you shall command,' and 'And you shall bring near,' because the holiness of priesthood and kingship also flow from Moses’ holiness, the aspect of Torah’s crown. His kingship is alluded to in 'And you shall command,' as the Midrash says: just as a king’s people obey his decrees, you too decree and they perform. 'And you shall bring near' likewise alludes to his priestly service during the seven days of inauguration.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pinchas 3:2: “This explains the Zohar's question: the verse should have said “whom Phinehas struck,” rather than “the slain man who was struck.” Once Phinehas had been elevated to the high priesthood, Scripture did not wish to mention him in connection with taking a human life; before his elevation, it had named him. This is difficult to understand: what difference does concealed wording make? Phinehas did kill them, which would seem unsuitable for a high priest. It becomes clear through what I heard from my holy teacher about the Sages' interpretation of “David would not drink them”: he did not repeat the teachings in their names. “Whoever exposes himself to death for Torah has no halakhic teaching repeated in his name.” “He poured them out to the Lord” means that he repeated them in the name of the accepted teaching. Why should one who exposes himself to death for Torah be punished by having his teaching left unattributed? My holy teacher explained that this is no punishment. Once he has given himself over to die for it, the teaching no longer belongs to him: it belongs to God. Therefore it is repeated in the name of the accepted teaching. “He poured them out to the Lord” means that it comes solely from God, rather than from the person's own power. Here, too, since Phinehas attained eternal priesthood for himself and his descendants through self-sacrifice, as it says, “Because he was zealous,” the killing is not assigned to his own name but to God's.

: “The priests gathered the table’s fruit from one Shabbat eve to the next—another reading says from Shabbat to Shabbat—to show that upper nourishment proceeds from the table’s nourishment. Through the bread the priests gathered, every food and drink they consumed was blessed, so that the evil inclination would not accuse them. For the evil inclination is found through eating and drinking, as in ‘Lest I become full and deny.’ Through food and drink, the evil inclination grows within a person’s innards.”

: “Does Rava accept the principle that one act draws another into its atonement? It was stated: Someone ate two olive-sized portions of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness, learned of one of them, and then ate another olive-sized portion while still unaware of the second. Rava said: If he brings an offering for the first, the first and second are atoned for, but not the third. If he brings an offering for the third, the third and second are atoned for, but not the first. If he brings an offering for the middle one, all are atoned for. Abaye said: Even if he brings an offering for any one of them, all are atoned for. After Rava heard the principle from Abaye, he accepted it. If so, let one act of grinding also draw the other act of grinding into its atonement! He accepts one act drawing another, but not a second drawing that follows from the first.”

: “Through one food or one meal each week—or a Shabbat meal—which a person eats with the proper intention, for the glory of Heaven and to raise the animal soul’s powers to God, all his foods and meals are elevated. This resembles what the masters of truth said concerning prayer: through one prayer, a person raises all the defective prayers of the entire year. Prayer corresponds to sacrifices, and eating does as well.”

: “Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Even someone praying alone on Friday evening must recite “The heavens and the earth were completed.” For Rav Hamnuna said: Whoever prays on Friday evening and recites this passage is regarded by Scripture as though he became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation. It says vaykhullu, “were completed”; read it as vaykhallu, “they completed.” Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we learn that speech is comparable to action? From “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.””
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Zeira found Rav Yehuda standing at the entrance of his father-in-law’s house. He saw that Rav Yehuda was in a cheerful frame of mind, so that if asked about all the world’s hidden matters he would answer. He asked him: Why do goats walk first, followed by sheep? He answered: It is like the world’s creation, in which darkness came first and light afterward.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”
: “See, this alone I found: God made the human being upright, but they sought out many schemes.”

: “The ninth is Shaddai—another reading has El Shaddai—who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ Enough means sufficiency, and sufficiency comes to the world only from the Righteous One, the world’s foundation, who said to the world, ‘Enough.’ The tenth is Adonai, for the kingdom’s law is certainly law. This wages the King’s battles in the world; it is lower Might, Tzedek.”

: “R. Yohanan bar Hanina said: The day consisted of twelve hours. In the first hour his dust was gathered; in the second he became an unformed body; in the third his limbs were extended; in the fourth a soul was cast into him; in the fifth he stood upon his feet; in the sixth he named the creatures; in the seventh Eve was paired with him; in the eighth two ascended the bed and four descended; in the ninth he was commanded not to eat from the tree; in the tenth he sinned; in the eleventh he was judged; in the twelfth he was driven out and departed, as it says, “A person in honor does not remain overnight.””

: “In the seventh hour on the eve of Shabbat, Adam entered the Garden of Eden; the ministering angels praised him and brought him into the Garden. At twilight on the eve of Shabbat he was expelled and went out. The ministering angels called out concerning him, “A human does not remain in honor overnight; they are likened to beasts that perish.” It does not say “like a beast,” but “like beasts”—both of them. The Shabbat day came and became Adam’s advocate. It said before Him: Master of the worlds, throughout the six days of creation no one was killed; will You begin with me? Is this my holiness and my blessing? As it says, “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.” Through the merit of Shabbat, Adam was saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. Adam saw Shabbat’s power and said: The Holy One, blessed be He, did not bless and sanctify Shabbat in vain. He began singing praise to Shabbat, as it says, “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.” Rabbi Yishmael says: Adam composed this psalm. It was forgotten through all generations until Moses came and renewed it: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day”—for the day that is entirely Shabbat and rest in the life of the world to come.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: A mortal who does not know his exact times, moments, or hours adds some weekday time to the sacred day. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows His exact moments, times, and hours, entered it at a boundary as fine as a hair.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in Rav Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: ‘Behold, it was very good’ refers to the good inclination, and ‘behold, it was very good’ also refers to the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination really very good? Rather, without the evil inclination, a person would not build a house, marry a woman, have children, or conduct business. So Solomon says, ‘It is a person’s rivalry with his fellow.’”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”
: “Hashem God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to cultivate the ground from which he had been taken.”

: ““He expelled the human.” Expelled, he left the Garden of Eden and settled on Mount Moriah, for the entrance to the Garden of Eden is near Mount Moriah. From there he had been taken, and there he was returned, to the place from which he had been taken, as it says, “The Lord God took the human.” From what place did He take him? From the site of the Temple, as it says, “To work the soil from which he had been taken.””

: “Another interpretation: ‘To work it and guard it’ refers to the sacrifices. Concerning service it says, ‘You shall serve God’; and concerning guarding it says, ‘You shall take care to offer it to Me at its appointed time.’”
: “Hashem God formed the human being from dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human became a living soul.”

: “‘From the earth’: Rabbi Berekhya and Rabbi Chelbo said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Adam was created from the place of his atonement, as it says, ‘An altar of earth you shall make for Me.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘I shall create him from the place of his atonement; would that he remain steadfast!’”
: “Hashem God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to cultivate the ground from which he had been taken.”
: “Hashem God took the human being and settled him in the Garden of Eden, to cultivate it and to guard it.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Hizkiyya said: What is meant by “From heaven You made judgment heard; the earth feared and became still”? If it feared, why was it still? If it was still, why did it fear? Rather, at first it feared and afterward became still. Why did it fear? As Reish Lakish taught: What is meant by “There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day”? Why the additional definite article? It teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the works of creation: If Israel accepts the Torah, you will endure; if not, I will return you to chaos and emptiness.”

: ““Engraved upon the tablets”—what does “engraved” mean? Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Nechemya, and the Rabbis differed. Rabbi Yehuda said: Read not “engraved,” but “freedom”—freedom from exile. Rabbi Nechemya said: Freedom from the angel of death. Our Rabbis said: Freedom from suffering. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei the Galilean said: If the angel of death comes and says before the Holy One, blessed be He, “You created me in the world for nothing,” He tells him: I gave you power over every nation in the world except this nation, to which I granted freedom. Thus: “Engraved upon the tablets.””
: “Hashem said to Moses, “Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.””

: “It also says, “The tablets were God’s work, and the inscription was God’s inscription, engraved upon the tablets.” Read “freedom” in place of “engraved,” for no one is truly free except the person occupied with Torah study.”
: “See, this alone I found: God made the human being upright, but they sought out many schemes.”
: “They said to Moses, “You speak with us, and we will listen; but let God not speak with us, lest we die.””

: “Rabbi Yehuda says: When Israel heard “I am the Lord your God,” Torah study became fixed in their hearts. They learned without forgetting. They came to Moses and said: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us, as it says, “You speak with us, and we shall hear,” and, “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” They reverted to learning and forgetting. They said: As Moses is flesh and blood and passes away, so his teaching passes away. They immediately returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth”—would that He fix Torah study in our hearts as before! He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it says, “I shall put My Torah within them and write it upon their hearts.” Rabbi Nechemya said: When Israel heard “You shall have no other gods,” the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. They came to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, become an intermediary between us—“You speak with us, and we shall hear”; “Now, why should we die? What benefit is there in our destruction?” The evil inclination immediately returned to its place. They returned to Moses, saying: Moses our teacher, would that He reveal Himself to us a second time! “Would that He kiss me with the kisses of His mouth!” He told them: This is not for now, but for the future, as it is written, “I shall remove the heart of stone from your flesh.””

: “Rabbi Eliezer said: What is meant by “Tablets of stone”? If a person makes his cheeks like this stone that does not wear away, his learning endures in his hands; otherwise, his learning does not endure.”

: “Ten things were created at twilight on the eve of Shabbat: the earth’s mouth, the well’s mouth, the donkey’s mouth, the rainbow, the manna, the staff, the shamir, the script, the inscription, and the tablets. Some add the destructive spirits, Moses’ burial place, and our father Abraham’s ram. Others add tongs, which are made with tongs.”

: ““The inscription”—their engraving and form: this is what I heard. It seems to me, however, that “the writing” means the engraving of their shapes, while “the inscription” refers to the pen and stylus with which the tablets’ engraving was written. This resembles the passage in Kiddushin 21: “From where do we include the thorn, the splinter, and the writing instrument?” My explanation seems correct, since reading would not be called ketav, “writing.””
: “Make this people’s heart unresponsive, make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and return and be healed.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”
: “Because you are precious in My eyes, honored, and loved by Me, I will give people in your place and nations in exchange for your life.”

: “Rabbi Eleazar began: ‘Because you became precious in My eyes, you were honored, and I loved you; I shall give a person in your place and nations for your soul.’ Why ‘became precious,’ rather than simply ‘are precious in My eyes’? It implies that he made himself precious. Certainly so: a person guilty before God is initially dishonored and abhorrent before Him. After reconsidering and returning from his sin, he now makes himself precious. God proclaims over him, ‘Because you became precious’—you made yourself precious.”

: “‘This is what you shall do for them.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘The wise shall inherit honor.’ Honor befits the sages who labor in Torah. The Torah says, ‘Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.’ You find thirty-six generations from Adam to Jabez, yet ‘honor’ is not written of any of them except Jabez, as it says, ‘Jabez was more honored than his brothers.’ Why is honor written of him? Because he was a Torah scholar who assembled gatherings and expounded the reasons of Torah publicly, as it says, ‘The families of scribes dwelling at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, Sucathites; these are the Kenites who came from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab.’”
: “Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother called his name Jabez, saying, “For I gave birth to him in pain.””

: “It was taught: Othniel and Jabez are the same person. What was his name? Judah, Simeon’s brother. “Othniel”—God answered him; “Jabez”—he gave counsel and spread Torah in Israel. How do we know that God answered him? It is written, “Jabez called to the God of Israel, saying: If You will indeed bless me, enlarge my border, let Your hand be with me, and act against my harm so that it not grieve me; and God granted what he asked.” “If You will indeed bless me”—with Torah. “Enlarge my border”—with students. “Let Your hand be with me”—so that my learning not be forgotten from my heart. “Act against my harm”—so that I may find companions like myself. “So that it not grieve me”—so that the evil inclination not overpower me and prevent me from studying. If You do this, well and good; otherwise I shall go in my sorrow to Sheol. Immediately, “God granted what he asked.””

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shavuot 20: “It further says, “And those that were broken came from these.” This follows the Sages' teaching that the broken tablets rested in the Ark. With the second tablets, too, after an Israelite engraves and hews the stone heart, he attains what existed with the first tablets, which came from the Tree of Life: “He shall eat and live forever.” “The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever”; as the Zohar cited above says, it remains constantly in that purity and never departs from it—freedom from the evil inclination. Every year, when the season of the giving of our Torah arrives, one can attain “engraved upon the tablets” and “I shall write it upon their hearts”: freedom from the evil inclination, which is the essential freedom mentioned in Avot. Although the world is judged according to its majority, and the whole defect has not yet been repaired so as to attain “He shall eat and live forever,” someone who attains “engraved upon the tablets” nevertheless does not die. Death is only like sleeping and waking, as it says, “Awake and sing,” like a person asleep who awakens. Thus the Midrash and the Jerusalem Talmud refer to death as “when he slept,” a term of sleep. “When you awaken, it will speak with you” refers to the future resurrection.”

: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: If someone tells you, “I toiled but did not attain,” do not believe him; “I did not toil but attained,” do not believe him; “I toiled and attained,” believe him. This applies to Torah study. In business, however, success depends on help from Heaven. Even in Torah, this was said only about sharpening one’s understanding; retaining one’s learning depends on help from Heaven.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””
: “Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother called his name Jabez, saying, “For I gave birth to him in pain.””
: “All this I saw as I applied my heart to every deed performed beneath the sun, at a time when one person rules over another to his detriment.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”
: “Wine gladdens the human heart, oil makes the face shine, and bread sustains the human heart.”

: “‘He said: see, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field the Lord has blessed.’ ‘He said’ is concealed: some say the Shekhinah spoke, others Isaac. ‘Like the fragrance of a field the Lord has blessed’: what field? The field of apples, the field that the upper patriarchs support and adorn.”
: “He drew near and kissed him. Isaac smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him, saying, “See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.””
: ““He said: See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed.” Rav Yehuda son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat said in Rav’s name: Like the fragrance of an apple orchard.”

: “‘He approached and kissed him, and he smelled the fragrance of his garments.’ Rabbi Yochanan said: Nothing smells fouler than this washing of goatskins; how, then, can Scripture say that he smelled the fragrance of his garments and blessed him? Rather, when our father Jacob entered his father’s presence, the Garden of Eden entered with him. This is what Isaac told him: ‘See, my son’s fragrance is like the fragrance of a field.’ But when Esau entered his father’s presence, Gehinnom entered with him, as it says, ‘When arrogance comes, disgrace comes.’”

: “The Divine Presence originally dwelled chiefly in the lower world. When Adam sinned, it withdrew to the first heaven; when Cain sinned, to the second; through the generation of Enosh, to the third; through the generation of the Flood, to the fourth; through the generation of the Dispersion, to the fifth; through the Sodomites, to the sixth; and through the Egyptians in Abraham’s time, to the seventh. Corresponding to them, seven righteous men arose: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehat, Amram, and Moses. Abraham brought it down to the sixth heaven; Isaac, from the sixth to the fifth; Jacob, from the fifth to the fourth; Levi, from the fourth to the third; Kehat, from the third to the second; Amram, from the second to the first; and Moses brought it down from above to below.”
: “They heard the sound of Hashem God moving through the garden in the day’s breeze. The man and his wife hid from Hashem God among the garden’s trees.”
: “See, this alone I found: God made the human being upright, but they sought out many schemes.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, does likewise for a person created from the four elements. When he returns in repentance and occupies himself with Torah, God takes him out from there. Of this it says, ‘From there it separates’: he separates himself from their desire, and God places him in His garden, the Shekhinah, ‘to work it’ through positive commandments and ‘to guard it’ through prohibitions. If he merits guarding her, he becomes head over the four elements, becoming the river through which they are watered, rather than through another. They recognize him as their master and ruler.”

: “Rabban Gamliel was again sitting and expounding: The Land of Israel will one day produce ready-made loaves and fine woolen garments, as it says, “May there be an abundance of grain in the land.” That student mocked him, saying, “There is nothing new under the sun.” He answered: Come, and I will show you their counterparts in this world. He went out and showed him truffles and mushrooms; for the woolen garments, he showed him the fibrous covering of a young palm.”

: “Ben Zoma saw a multitude from a step on the Temple Mount and said: “Blessed is the Knower of secrets, and blessed is He who created all these to serve me.” He used to say: “How much effort Adam had to expend before finding bread to eat! He plowed, sowed, reaped, gathered the sheaves, threshed, winnowed, sorted, ground, sifted, kneaded, and baked; only then did he eat. I rise in the morning and find all these things prepared for me.””

: “Rabbi Haggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahman’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for eating and drinking. Because the mouth takes pleasure in its utterance, they permitted a person to occupy himself with words of Torah on them. Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Hiyya bar Ba’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for occupying oneself with words of Torah. A baraita supports each view: What does one do? Either sit and eat, or sit and occupy oneself with words of Torah. One verse says, “It is a Sabbath to the Lord,” and another says, “An assembly to the Lord your God.” How are they fulfilled? Give a portion to Torah study and a portion to eating and drinking.”
