quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:4: ““Because this mouth blossoms”: This uses the expression “It will blossom and flower.” The meaning is that, because a person enjoys the breath issuing from his mouth, they permitted him to occupy himself with words of Torah on Shabbat and festivals, which were originally given only for delight through eating and drinking.”

k: volume-ii|447|3|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:7: ““One verse says”: This is another baraita. It should read: One verse says, “An assembly to the Lord your God,” and another says, “An assembly shall be for you.” How can both be fulfilled? Divide the day. This supports Rabbi Berekhya, because one must in any event occupy oneself with words of Torah, while also giving a portion to eating and drinking, to fulfill “for you.””

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “Rav Chisda said: What does “Hashem loves the gates of Zion more than all Jacob’s dwellings” mean? Hashem loves the gates distinguished by halakhah more than synagogues and houses of study. This accords with Rabbi Chiya bar Ami’s statement in Ulla’s name: Since the Temple was destroyed, the Holy One, blessed be He, has only the four cubits of halakhah in His world.”
: “It is good to give thanks to Hashem and sing praise to Your name, Most High.”
: “Planted in Hashem’s house, they will flourish in the courtyards of our God.”

: “Rabbi Simlai expounded: A person should first arrange praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, and then pray for his requests. From whom do we learn this? From Moses: “I pleaded with Hashem at that time,” followed by, “Hashem God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand; what power in heaven or earth could act as You act, with Your might?” Only afterward does it say, “Let me cross over, please, and see the good land.””

: “Rabbi Yochanan said: The especially devoted would finish reciting Shema at sunrise. A baraita likewise teaches: They would finish at sunrise so as to join the redemption blessing directly to prayer and thus pray by daylight. Rabbi Zeira said: What verse supports this? “May they fear You with the sun, and before the moon, through all generations.””

: “I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them rejoice in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted upon My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”

: “There was another incident: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa went to learn Torah with Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, whose son became ill. He told him, “My son Chanina, pray for mercy upon him, so that he may live.” Chanina placed his head between his knees, prayed for mercy, and the child recovered. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai said: “Had Ben Zakkai pressed his head between his knees all day, they would not have heeded him.” His wife asked him: “Is Chanina greater than you?” He answered: “No; he is like a servant before the king, while I am like a minister before the king.””
: ““Like a servant”: A member of the household who enters and leaves without asking permission.”

: “A baraita teaches: One who recites Shema in the morning must mention the Exodus from Egypt in the blessing “True and Firm.” Rabbi says: He must mention kingship in it. Others say: He must mention the splitting of the Sea of Reeds and the striking of the firstborn in it. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: He must mention all of these and say, “Rock of Israel and its Redeemer.””

: “Why must the splitting of the Sea of Reeds be mentioned in the blessing “True and Firm”? Because when He split the sea for them, they believed in Him, as it says, “They believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant.” Through the merit of their faith they merited to sing, and the Divine Presence rested upon them, for immediately afterward it is written, “Then Moses sang.” Therefore a person must place redemption immediately before prayer, just as they placed song after faith and the splitting of the sea. Just as they purified their hearts and sang—for it is written, “The people feared the Lord and believed,” followed by, “Then Moses sang”—so a person must purify his heart before praying.”

: “Redemption means the praise and glorification a person offers God for all His works. This is the arranging of the Omnipresent’s praises before prayer through King David’s praises, for he represents the place called redemption. This was his whole concern in the Book of Psalms: he was called 'the sweet singer of Israel,' serving as the emissary of the entire congregation of Israel in this matter. From there one comes to prayer, which is the aspect of fearing Him, as they expounded 'They shall fear You with the sun' concerning prayer at sunrise. Likewise, 'One should not withhold oneself from mercy.' These two matters constitute creation’s principal purpose: it was for His glory and for fear of Him. Through them one merits reaching the initial thought of creation, the aspect of Atika, called the will of wills, resembling the future revelation of which it says, 'Then our mouths shall be filled with laughter.'”

: ““Remember, please, how I walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and did what is good in Your eyes.” What does “I did what is good in Your eyes” mean? Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: He joined the redemption blessing directly to prayer. Rabbi Levi said: He put away the book of remedies.”

: “Rabbi Yaakov, the son of Yaakov’s daughter, said: Anyone through whom another person is punished is not admitted into the presence of the Holy One, blessed be He. ... Rather, the proof comes from this verse: “Even punishment for the righteous is not good.” “Not good” means evil, and it is written, “For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You.” You are righteous, Lord, and evil will not dwell in Your dwelling.”
: “Amalek dwells in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites dwell in the mountains; and the Canaanites dwell beside the sea and along the Jordan.”

: “Further, ‘Amalek dwells in the land of the south.’ If a person says he can merit it despite everything, ‘Amalek dwells in the south’: the evil inclination, the prosecutor accusing a person, is constantly found in the body. ‘The Hittite and Amorite,’ and so forth: many accusers are found there, so that a person cannot enter that world at all. Who can merit it, who can enter it? With these words ‘they turned away the children of Israel’s heart,’ spreading a bad name about it: ‘They brought out an evil report of the land.’”

: ““When she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field, and she alighted from the donkey.” What does “she alighted” signify? Rava said in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: She told him: Just as a donkey cries out immediately when it has no food in its manger, so a woman cries out immediately when there is no grain in her house. “She said: Give me a blessing, for you have given me land of the south”—a house dry of every good thing. “Give me springs of water”—a man who possesses nothing but Torah. “Caleb gave her upper springs and lower springs”—he told her: Would a man who dwells in the upper and lower realms need someone to seek sustenance for him?”

: “This is what Scripture says: “Vanity of vanities, said Kohelet; vanity of vanities; all is vanity.” Kohelet spoke of seven vanities: “vanity” is one; “vanities” is two; “vanity of vanities” brings the count to six; “all is vanity” makes seven. Why? They correspond to the seven days of creation. Solomon said: What was created on the first day? Heaven and earth. What will be their end? “The heavens will dissolve like smoke, and the earth wear out like a garment.” He said: Vanity. What was created on the second day? The firmament. Its end? “The heavens will be rolled up like a scroll.” He said: Vanity. On the third day? “Let the waters be gathered.” Their end? “The Lord will destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea.” He said: Vanity. On the fourth day? The lights, as it says, “God set them in the firmament of heaven.” Their end? “The moon will be abashed.” He said: Vanity. On the fifth day? “Let the waters teem.” Their end? “I will utterly sweep everything from the face of the earth.” He said: Vanity. On the sixth day? The human being. His end? “For dust you are, and to dust you will return.” He said: Vanity. What was created on the seventh day? Shabbat. He looked this way and that, seeking to find a flaw in it, but found only holiness and rest. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Afterward he considered that a person sins on it and incurs death, and said: This too is vanity. Therefore he said, “All is vanity”—making seven.”
: “Israel is holy to Hashem, the first of His harvest. All who consume him incur guilt; calamity will come upon them, declares Hashem.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: blessing is prepared for those upper days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills Ze‘ir Anpin’s head with dew descending from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all. Three times from Shabbat’s entrance, He casts it upon the Field of Holy Apples, so that all may be blessed together.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: ““Wisdom built her house”—this is the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, who created the entire world through wisdom. “She hewed its seven pillars”—these are the seven days of Creation. “She slaughtered her meat, mixed her wine, and also arranged her table”—these are the seas, rivers, and all the world’s needs. “She sent her maidens to call”—these are Adam and Eve.”

: “The Sages say that the earth stands upon twelve pillars, as it says, “He fixed the boundaries of peoples according to the number of Israel’s children.” Others say seven pillars, as it says, “She hewed out her seven pillars.” Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says: Upon one pillar, named Righteous, as it says, “The righteous is the world’s foundation.””

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Had Israel observed the first Shabbat, no nation or language would have ruled over them, as it says, “On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather,” followed by “Amalek came.” Rabbi Yohanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai’s name: If Israel were to observe two Shabbatot according to their laws, they would immediately be redeemed. For it says, “Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs who observe My Sabbaths,” and afterward, “I will bring them to My holy mountain.””

: “When Hashem your God grants you rest from all your surrounding enemies, in the land Hashem your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall erase the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens. Do not forget.”
: “On the day Hashem grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil, and the harsh labor imposed upon you—”

: “Rabbi Shimon also said: we learned that Shabbat is an image of the world to come, and certainly it is. Thus the sabbatical year and Jubilee mirror one another, as do Shabbat and the world to come. The additional soul comes from the mystery of ‘remember’ to this Shelter of Peace, which receives it from the world to come and gives this addition to the holy people. They rejoice in that addition and forget every weekday matter, every sorrow and distress, as in ‘On the day the Lord grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil and the hard labor,’ and so forth.”

ref: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Torah Shebikhtav, Shemot, Introduction 2-3
quote: : “I include all these Torah portions under one heading, since they are connected in a leap year, when Israel’s custom is to arouse themselves to repentance with greater strength, as mentioned by early and later authorities. Most mentioned only the portions Shovavim, while later authorities added the portions Tetzaveh and Terumah as well, with greater intensity. Whoever adds to repentance will receive further additions from Heaven. I therefore call this extensive discourse, encompassing these portions, 'Shovavim Tat.'”

: “In my view one can also explain the opposite: the additional days of a leap year are especially suited to repentance because they come to equalize the lunar years with the solar years, resembling the World to Come, when the moon’s light will be like the sun’s and the shells and evil inclination will be entirely annulled. Terumah and Tetzaveh were selected for this because they discuss constructing the Tabernacle and its vessels, so that God will dwell within Israel. The principal intention is that the heart of Israel become a dwelling for the Divine Presence. Had the corruption not occurred, the entire camp of Israel would have been such a dwelling, as in 'The earth is My footstool'—meaning Israel’s hearts as a dwelling for the Divine Presence. There would then be no accusation from the evil inclination, as in 'They shall neither harm nor destroy throughout My holy mountain.'”

: “At that moment He calls Yofi’el, the great appointed ruler, and the fifty-three holy chariots beneath him, assigned to the Torah’s service. He appoints each chariot over a particular portion on a particular Shabbat. Each serves the Torah of its own Shabbat. We may not mix them or bring one chariot into another’s domain, even by a hair’s breadth—even in one word or one letter. Each must remain as God apportioned and appointed it over those portions, each at its post. Therefore, when this portion is crowned, the words of that portion, completed by the congregation, ascend. The chariot appointed over that portion receives them and brings them before the Holy One, blessed be He. These very words stand before Him and say: ‘I am such-and-such a portion, completed by such-and-such a congregation, in this manner.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Kislev 2: “The names of the months came up from Babylonia, as the Jerusalem Talmud and Midrash teach. In the Torah, the months are identified only by their number from Nisan: “in the third month,” “in the seventh month.” Later, in Nehemiah, they are mentioned by name. The meaning is that originally, while the Temple stood, “the burnt offering of each month in its renewal” expressed how people felt a distinctive holiness in every month. Likewise, “from month to month and from Shabbat to Shabbat” means that a new aspect of Torah is renewed each month and each Shabbat. Each year, too, a new aspect of Torah is renewed on Rosh Hashanah, and throughout the year in every month and every Shabbat. Something resembling this appears in the Sages' teaching that Manasseh taught fifty-five interpretations of Torat Kohanim, corresponding to the years of his reign: Rashi explains that he renewed the book of Leviticus each year, interpreting it through his dialectical study. People felt this renewal of Torah in every Shabbat and month. Later, when they forgot that feeling of renewal, and after the Temple's destruction there was no longer “the burnt offering of each month in its renewal,” the Men of the Great Assembly, who established the Oral Torah, instituted the months' names. Thus the Midrash interprets Tishrei as “release, forgive, and atone for Your people's debts,” since Yom Kippur occurs in it. The name of the month indicates its purpose.”

: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon the Devout’s name: A fast that includes none of Israel’s transgressors is not a fast. For galbanum smells foul, yet Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients. Abaye derived this from, “He founded His united company upon the earth.””

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

k: volume-ii|478|0|Shiltei HaGibborim, part I, as reported
quote: : “This blemish produces a foul and deeply unpleasant odor. Galbanum, whose odor is exceedingly foul and exceptionally strong, alludes to it, as stated in Shiltei HaGibborim, partI. Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients to indicate that even those who transgress in this matter will ultimately give forth good fragrance. As the preceding exposition concerning utterly wicked people asks: 'Perhaps you will say their hope is lost? Scripture says: The mandrakes give fragrance—both these and those will ultimately give fragrance.'”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Chanina’s name: Pinchas did not become a priest until he killed Zimri, as it is written, “It shall be for him and his descendants after him a covenant of everlasting priesthood.” Rav Ashi said: Not until he made peace between the tribes, as it says, “Pinchas the priest, the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of Israel’s thousands heard…” But how does Rav Ashi explain, “For him and his descendants after him”? That verse was written as a blessing. And how does Rabbi Elazar explain, “Pinchas the priest heard”? That passage traces the lineage of his descendants after him.”
: “For him and his descendants after him it shall be a covenant of everlasting priesthood, because he acted zealously for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”

: “Thus Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by “Those passing through the valley of weeping make it a spring; the teacher is also clothed in blessings”? “Those passing” are people who transgress the will of the Holy One, blessed be He. “The valley”—Gehinnom is deepened for them. “Weeping”—they weep and shed tears like a spring flowing into the depths. “The teacher is also clothed in blessings”—they accept their judgment as just, saying: Master of the world, You have judged well, acquitted well, condemned well, and rightly prepared Gehinnom for the wicked and Eden for the righteous. Is that so? Reish Lakish said: The wicked do not repent even at Gehinnom’s entrance, as it says, “They shall go out and see the corpses of the people who rebel against Me.” It does not say “who rebelled,” but “who rebel,” meaning that they continue rebelling forever. There is no difficulty: One statement concerns Israel’s sinners, the other the sinners of the nations. This is also reasonable, since otherwise Reish Lakish would contradict himself. Reish Lakish said: Gehinnom’s fire does not rule over Israel’s sinners. This follows all the more from the golden altar: Though covered by only a dinar’s thickness of gold, it stood for many years without fire ruling over it. How much more so Israel’s sinners, who are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate! For “Your temples are like a slice of pomegranate” may be read, “Even your empty ones are filled with mitzvot like a pomegranate.” What then of

: “Faithful Shepherd: this commandment requires the priest to arrange the lamps in the Temple every day, as we explained in the secret of the menorah. It mirrors what is above: the upper illumination in the anointing oil first descends upon the priest’s head; afterward he kindles and illuminates all the lamps. Thus ‘Like the good oil upon the head,’ and ‘For the anointing oil of his God is upon him.’ Therefore the priest alone is authorized to arrange and kindle the lamps twice daily, corresponding to the illumination of union twice daily. The offering, too, comes twice daily, and all is necessary.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya the Great expounded this. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it says, ‘The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.’ ‘The earth was waste and void’ refers to the deeds of the wicked; ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to the deeds of the righteous. Yet I do not know which He desires—the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, ‘God saw that the light was good,’ we know that He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wicked.”

: “‘Joseph was brought down to Egypt.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘Come, see the works of God, awesome in His dealings with human beings.’ Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said: Even the awesome events You bring upon us, You bring through a pretext. Consider: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created the angel of death on the first day. From where do we know this? Rabbi Berekhya said: ‘Darkness was over the face of the deep’—this is the angel of death, who darkens people’s faces. Adam was created on the sixth day, yet the blame was attached to him, as though he had brought death into the world: ‘On the day you eat from it, you shall surely die.’ To what is this comparable? To a man who wishes to divorce his wife. Before going home he writes a bill of divorce, then enters his house holding it and looks for a pretext to give it to her. He tells her, ‘Mix me a cup to drink.’ She does so. When he takes the cup from her, he says, ‘Here is your bill of divorce.’ She asks, ‘What was my offense?’ He replies, ‘Leave my house: you mixed me a lukewarm cup!’ She says, ‘You already knew that I would mix a lukewarm cup, since you wrote the bill of divorce and brought it with you!’ So Adam said before the Holy One: ‘Master of the world, two thousand years before You created Your world, the Torah was with You as a craftsman, as it says, “I was beside Him as a craftsman, a delight day by day”—two thousand years. It already contained, “This is the Torah: when a person dies in a tent.”

: “Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, “Satan went out from Hashem’s presence.” He is the evil inclination: elsewhere it is written, “Only evil all the day,” and here, “Only do not reach out your hand against him.” He is the angel of death, as it is written, “Only preserve his life”—showing that taking it lies within his power.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”
: “Come, let us reason together, says Hashem. Though your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.”

: ““Like scarlet”—shanim? Should it not say shani, in the singular? Rabbi Yitzhak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years, shanim, ordered in succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.”

: “Come and see: When the ancient nations wished to appoint a king, they brought someone from elsewhere and set him over themselves, as it says, “A king reigned in Edom—from Dinhabah,” and from Bozrah, and so with all of them. Israel is different: their great people, kings, priests, prophets, and officers come from among themselves. “From him the cornerstone”—this is King David, as it says, “The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone.” “From him the peg”—this is the High Priest, as it says, “I shall fasten him as a peg in a secure place.” “From him the battle bow,” as it says, “Armed with bows, using the right and left hands.” “From him every ruler shall emerge together”—these are the judicial scribes. Likewise it says, “Bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him.” From where? “From among the children of Israel.””

: “The holiness of the priests likewise comes from Israel, following the teaching, 'A leader corresponds to his generation.' Shemot Rabbah says: 'Go, descend!' He said, 'You ascend here not for your own honor, but for My children’s honor. I told their ancestor: The angels of God ascend and descend upon him. When your children are righteous, they rise and are elevated, and their emissaries rise with them.' The Midrash similarly emphasizes, 'From him the peg'—the high priest; and, 'Bring near to yourself Aaron your brother and his sons with him'—from where? 'From among the children of Israel.' As long as the mixture remains and a person experiences bodily pleasure, death is necessary to separate the good from the evil, leaving only good. On Shabbat, however, even bodily pleasure is holy and does not arouse the accusation of the evil inclination, as the Ari writes. This is especially true of one who attains the higher Shabbat, from which the evil inclination is removed, as Tikkunei Zohar says, just as it will be in the future.”

: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon the Devout’s name: A fast that includes none of Israel’s transgressors is not a fast. For galbanum smells foul, yet Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients. Abaye derived this from, “He founded His united company upon the earth.””

Parallel: Resisei Layla 50:2: “All the souls of Israel form one bond. When one Jewish soul is bound completely to God, all are naturally drawn along with it, like someone pulling the end of a rope and drawing the whole rope after it. “Jacob is the rope of His inheritance”: one end is bound above, in Jacob's form engraved upon the Throne of Glory, and its lower end consists of the very worst sinners of Israel, extending from level to level. On Yom Kippur, when the individual who repents is awakened to enter before God, into the Holy of Holies, the entire rope is naturally drawn along with him through an awakening of repentance and ascent. Each rises according to his own standing and level, and atonement consequently extends to them as well.”
: “Aaron shall burn fragrant incense upon it every morning; when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.”

: “Through the priest, the lamps shine everywhere, above and below, bringing joy and making joy present on every side. Two services are performed through the priest to bring joy everywhere: lighting the lamps and offering incense. We have explained: ‘Oil and incense gladden the heart.’”
: “Oil and incense gladden the heart, and so does a friend’s sweetness through heartfelt counsel.”

: “Rabbi Yosei said: ‘When he tends them’—behetivo—is like ‘Your love is better than wine.’ ‘Good’ means filled with wine, as in ‘We had our fill of bread and were well.’ Rabbi Yehudah said: it means making good in the literal sense, as in ‘A good heart has a continual feast.’ ‘When he raises them’ means that when they are watered and filled from the river’s flow, they rise aloft. Blessings are found in them all, and joy is in everything. Therefore it says, ‘When he raises them.’”
: “All the poor person’s days are bad, but a good heart is a continual feast.”
: “May my prayer be established before You as incense, and the lifting of my hands as the evening offering.”

: “Rabbi Chizkiyah began: ‘Let my prayer be established as incense before You, the raising of my hands as the evening offering.’ Why the evening offering rather than morning prayer? It does not say, ‘Let my prayer be established in the morning.’ Rather, incense comes only for joy, as in ‘Oil and incense gladden the heart.’ Therefore when the priest kindled the lamps, he offered incense: ‘When he tends the lamps, he shall burn it,’ and ‘When Aaron raises the lamps toward evening, he shall burn it.’ In the morning, it is for joy brought by the hour; in the evening, to gladden the left side, as fitting. It always comes only for joy.”

: “Furthermore, words of Torah become settled only there, for there is no light except the light that emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted above and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One, blessed be He, except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters an evil path and then abandons it, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His glory. Therefore the completeness of everything is good and evil together, followed by rising into good; there is no good except that which has emerged from evil. Through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.”
: “Oil and incense gladden the heart, and so does a friend’s sweetness through heartfelt counsel.”
: “Hashem’s precepts are upright, gladdening the heart; Hashem’s commandment is clear, illuminating the eyes.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””
: “Oil and incense gladden the heart, and so does a friend’s sweetness through heartfelt counsel.”
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”
