quote: : “Not only the tribe of Levi, but every individual among all those who enter the world whose spirit moves him and whose understanding leads him to separate himself, to stand before God and minister to Him, serve Him, and know Him—who walks uprightly as God made him and removes from his neck the yoke of the many calculations people pursue—is sanctified as holy of holies. God will be his portion and inheritance forever and ever, and will provide him in this world with enough to sustain him, just as He provided for the priests and Levites. David, peace be upon him, said, 'The Lord is my allotted portion and my cup; You uphold my lot.'”
: “You will be called priests of Hashem; you will be spoken of as servants of our God. You will consume the wealth of nations and take pride in their splendor.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What is meant by “For You are our Father; Abraham does not know us and Israel does not recognize us; You, Lord, are our Father, our Redeemer from of old is Your Name”? In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to Abraham: Your children have sinned against Me. He will answer: Master of the world, let them be wiped out for the sanctity of Your Name. God will say: I will tell Jacob, who suffered the hardship of raising children; perhaps he will ask mercy for them. He will say: Your children have sinned. Jacob will answer: Master of the world, let them be wiped out for the sanctity of Your Name. God will say: There is no reasoning among the elders and no counsel among the younger. He will say to Isaac: Your children have sinned against Me. Isaac will answer: Master of the world, are they my children and not Your children? When they put “We will do” before “We will hear,” You called them “My firstborn son”; now are they my children and not Yours? Moreover, how much have they sinned? A person’s years are seventy. Remove twenty for which You do not punish, leaving fifty. Remove twenty-five for the nights, leaving twenty-five. Remove twelve and a half for prayer, eating, and bodily needs, leaving twelve and a half. If You bear all of them, well and good; if not, half upon me and half upon You. And if You say that all must be upon me, I offered myself before You. They will begin saying, “For you are our father.” Isaac

k: volume-ii|573|1|Arizal, Pri Etz Chaim, Sha’ar HaShabbat
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 17:2-4
quote: : “From the companions: at every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should declare, ‘These are meals of complete faith.’ On Friday night one arranges twelve loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Field of Apples; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with her.’ This is Isaac’s meal: he is its master and guides it. Whoever delights in it is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Field of Holy Apples come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Abraham, the pious elder; through his merit one is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. At the afternoon meal one arranges four loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of Ze‘ir Anpin; the Field of Holy Apples and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Jacob, father of seventy souls; through his merit one is saved from the wars of Gog and Magog.”

: “Someone who bought produce from a person not trusted regarding tithes, and forgot to tithe it, may ask him on Shabbat and eat on his assurance. After Shabbat has ended, he may not eat until he tithes. … The companions said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: They permitted this in honor of Shabbat. If it is because of Shabbat’s honor, why must he ask? To create a basis for the permission. Rabbi Bibi said in Rabbi Hanina’s name: The awe of Shabbat rests upon him, so he tells the truth. If the awe of Shabbat rests upon him, why does the Mishnah say that once Shabbat ends he may not eat until he tithes? Because there may be someone upon whom the awe of Shabbat does not rest. A baraita teaches: If he asks on a weekday, he may not eat on Shabbat. This fits the view that the awe of Shabbat rests upon him. According to the view that permission is given for Shabbat’s honor, however, even if he asked on a weekday, he should be able to eat on Shabbat.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: This is like a king who built a palace, saw it, and was pleased with it. He said, ‘Palace, palace, may you always find favor in my eyes as you have at this moment!’ So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to His world: ‘My world, My world, may you always find favor before Me as you have at this moment!’”

: “The words 'There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day' allude to drawing holiness down and to a person’s awakening to rectify the corruption through adding to Shabbat: there is no light except that emerging from darkness. 'The heavens were completed' concerns Shabbat itself, holiness appearing from above, as it says, 'He blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.' We therefore begin the prayer, 'You sanctified...and so it is written in Your Torah: The heavens were completed'—we feel Shabbat’s holiness flowing from above. Then, in Kiddush over wine, we begin 'There was evening and there was morning': the initial awakening to holiness must come from the person, drawing it upon himself through service and effort to transform darkness into light. Afterward we feel the holiness from above in 'The heavens were completed.'”

: “R. Yohanan said: There are three crowns: that of the altar, that of the Ark, and that of the table. Aaron merited taking the altar’s crown; David merited taking the table’s crown. The Ark’s crown still lies available: whoever wishes to take it may come and take it. Perhaps you might think it is inferior? Scripture says, “Through me kings reign.””

: “Rabbi Eliezer again told them: “If the law follows my view, let Heaven prove it.” A heavenly voice declared: “Why do you contend with Rabbi Eliezer, when the law follows him everywhere?” Rabbi Yehoshua rose to his feet and declared: “It is not in heaven!” What does “It is not in heaven” mean? Rabbi Yirmiyah said: The Torah has already been given at Mount Sinai. We pay no attention to a heavenly voice, for You already wrote in the Torah at Mount Sinai, “Follow the majority.” Rabbi Natan met Elijah and asked him: “What was the Holy One, blessed be He, doing at that moment?” He answered: “He was smiling and saying, ‘My children have prevailed over Me! My children have prevailed over Me!’””

: “Do not seek greatness for yourself or covet honor. Let your deeds exceed your learning. Do not long for kings’ tables, for your table is greater than theirs and your crown greater than theirs. The Master for whom you work is trustworthy to pay you for your labor.”

: “‘Wisdom—from where is it found?’ Torah proceeds from Wisdom, the place called Holiness. Wisdom proceeds from the place called Holy of Holies. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Jubilee is likewise called holy, as in ‘It is Jubilee; it shall be holy to you.’ Israel includes these aspects, as it says, ‘You shall be people of holiness to Me.’”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”

Parallel: R. Moshe Cordovero, Tomer Devorah 4:1: “One must return in repentance, for nothing is as precious as repentance: it repairs every blemish. Just as Binah sweetens all judgments and removes their bitterness, so a person should repent and repair every blemish. One who thinks of repentance throughout his days causes Binah to shine throughout his days. All his days are thus spent in repentance, which means including himself within Binah, which is repentance, and his lifetime is crowned with the mystery of supernal repentance. Consider: repentance contains the root of everything that exists, in the mystery of Jubilee. Even the root of the external forces, the mystery of the River of Fire included within holiness through the powers of judgment, is rooted there. It spreads from there and is called the outflow of burning anger. Through the mystery of “The Lord smelled the pleasing aroma,” that outflow returns to its source. The judgments are sweetened, anger subsides, and the Lord relents from the harm. A person accomplishes this very mystery through his repentance.”

: “The priests gathered the table’s fruit from one Shabbat eve to the next—another reading says from Shabbat to Shabbat—to show that upper nourishment proceeds from the table’s nourishment. Through the bread the priests gathered, every food and drink they consumed was blessed, so that the evil inclination would not accuse them. For the evil inclination is found through eating and drinking, as in ‘Lest I become full and deny.’ Through food and drink, the evil inclination grows within a person’s innards.”

: “The highest nourishment of all is the nourishment of the companions who labor in Torah. They eat nourishment of spirit and soul, not bodily nourishment at all, from the exalted place more precious than all, called Wisdom. The companions’ bodies are therefore weaker than those of other people, for they do not eat bodily nourishment; they eat nourishment of spirit and soul from that distant, exalted and supremely precious place. This food is subtler than the subtlest, beyond all else. Happy is their portion: ‘Wisdom gives life to its possessors.’ Happy is the body that can be nourished by the soul’s food.”

: “Toward evening on Friday, they saw an old man holding two bundles of myrtle and running at twilight. They asked him: What are these for? He answered: In honor of Shabbat. Would one not suffice? He replied: One corresponds to “Remember,” and one to “Observe.” Rabbi Shimon said to his son: See how precious the commandments are to Israel. Their minds were set at ease.”

: ““Israel has sinned.” R. Abba bar Zavda said: Although he has sinned, he remains Israel. R. Abba said: This accords with the popular saying: A myrtle standing among reeds is named myrtle, and myrtle is what people call it.”

: “The Gemara says of Achan that he transgressed the five books of the Torah, that he drew out his foreskin, and similar things. Why expound so much to his disgrace? Because “Israel has sinned” was written about Achan to teach that, even after sinning, he remains Israel. The Sages therefore attached to him every evil that could be attached to him, teaching that whatever befalls a Jew, no castaway is ultimately cast off: the name Israel has not been uprooted from him.”
: “Mar son of Ravina said to his son: Regarding all the others, do not make a point of expounding against them, except for Balaam the wicked; expound against him as much as you can find.”

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

: “This may be explained through 'He will sense through fear of the Lord,' and concerning Joseph, 'I fear God.' Thus the Gemara says, 'The mandrakes give fragrance' refers to Israel’s young men who have never tasted sin. The expression 'Israel’s young men' appears to concern this blemish, which youth causes. Likewise, in Sotah: 'I smell the fragrance of chanunita'; he told him, 'My son, you possess purity.' This too follows 'He will sense through fear of the Lord' and 'Fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.' A complete sense of smell indicates fear and purity; therefore 'The mandrakes give fragrance' is said of those pure from this blemish.”

: “Rav Huna found a fragrant date, took it, and wrapped it in his scarf. His son Rabba came and said: I smell a fragrant date. Rav Huna replied: My son, you possess purity. He gave it to him. Meanwhile, Rabba’s son Abba came, and Rabba took the date and gave it to him. Rav Huna said: My son, you gladdened my heart but set my teeth on edge. This is what people say: A father’s affection is for his children; the children’s affection is for their own children.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sotah 49a:10:2: ““You possess purity”: Therefore you can smell it; fragrance has not ceased for you.”

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

: “The principal power of incense is learned from galbanum being counted among its ingredients: a fast must include Israel’s transgressors. Although galbanum smells bad, it produces a good fragrance when combined with the incense. This points to 'The mandrakes give fragrance'—Israel’s young men who have never tasted sin. As we often explained, the expression 'young men' indicates the blemish of the covenant, caused by youth. That blemish gives off a foul and deeply unpleasant odor; galbanum, with its exceptionally foul odor, alludes to it, as stated in Shiltei HaGibborim, partI. Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients to indicate that even those who transgress in this matter will ultimately give forth good fragrance. The preceding exposition in Eruvin 21 b concerns utterly wicked people: 'Perhaps you will say their hope is lost? Scripture says: The mandrakes give fragrance—both these and those will ultimately give fragrance.'”

: “The aspect of Aaron the priest is to draw near even someone who, to outward appearance, has lost this holiness through a blemish so grave that his foreskin is drawn over again. Even Abraham our father, who raises all Israel’s transgressors, does not recognize him. Nevertheless, Aaron’s holiness has the power to raise even this person and testify that the holiness of the covenant remains within him, concealed at the root.”
: ““That old man found him”: Some explain that wherever “that old man” is mentioned, it means Elijah. This cannot be maintained in the account of Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai in Shabbat 34a.”

: “Abraham called the place Yireh, as it says, ‘Abraham called that place The Lord Will See.’ Shem called it Shalem, as it says, ‘Malki-Tzedek, king of Shalem.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘If I call it Yireh, as Abraham did, Shem, a righteous man, will object. If I call it Shalem, Abraham, a righteous man, will object. Rather, I shall call it Jerusalem, combining what they both called it: Yireh-Shalem, Jerusalem.’ Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chelbo’s name: While it was still Shalem, the Holy One made Himself a shelter there and prayed within it, as it says, ‘His shelter was in Shalem, and His dwelling in Zion.’ What did He say? ‘May it be My will that I behold My house built.’”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. God included it by saying, ‘I am the Lord.’ I heard my father explain it thus: et adds the Shabbat boundary; ‘My Shabbatot’ is the circle and the square within it, two. Corresponding to them are two sanctifications we must mention: Vayekhullu and Kiddush. Vayekhullu contains thirty-five words, and the sanctification we recite contains thirty-five. Together they amount to the seventy Names with which God and the Congregation of Israel are crowned.”

: “What distinguishes one who serves out of love from one who serves out of fear? Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar taught: One who serves out of love is greater than one who serves out of fear, for the latter’s merit extends to a thousand generations, and the former’s to two thousand. Here it says, “To two thousand, to those who love Me and keep My commandments,” and elsewhere, “To those who keep His commandments, to a thousand generations.” But the latter verse also says, “To those who love Him and keep His commandments, to a thousand generations”! Each number is applied to the expression adjacent to it.”
: “Now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you? Only to fear Hashem your God, to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve Hashem your God with all your heart and all your soul.”

: “The Gemara regards the additional offering of Rosh Chodesh as more sacred than the additional offering of Shabbat. Rashi explains that it is more sacred because Rosh Chodesh is called an appointed time. This is difficult: does being called an appointed time make it more sacred than Shabbat, which Hashem Himself sanctified? According to what we have explained, the meaning is clear. From Hashem’s side, Shabbat’s holiness is certainly greater than that of the new month. Hence Ezekiel says, “On the Shabbat day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new month it shall be opened”: there the verse describes what Hashem opens, and Shabbat’s fixed, enduring holiness takes precedence. From Israel’s side, however, the new month’s holiness is dearer, because Israel sanctifies it, and a person prefers his own measure. Thus, when Scripture speaks of Israel coming to bow down, and of receiving one’s teacher, it puts the new month before Shabbat. Its holiness is dearer from Israel’s side because it comes through them. The same applies to their offering: Rosh Chodesh’s additional offering is considered more sacred than Shabbat’s. This is also the deeper intent of Rashi’s “it is called an appointed time”: Israel determines it.”

: “Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: The Holy One, blessed be He, promised two people His protection, yet they were afraid: the chosen patriarch and the chosen prophet. The chosen patriarch was Jacob, as it says, ‘The Lord chose Jacob for Himself.’ God told him, ‘Behold, I am with you,’ yet afterward he was afraid, as it says, ‘Jacob was afraid.’ The chosen prophet was Moses, as it says, ‘Had not Moses, His chosen one’; God told him, ‘For I shall be with you,’ yet afterward he was afraid, as it says, ‘The Lord said to Moses: Do not fear him.’ ‘Do not fear him’ is said only to someone who is afraid.”
: “What is Heaven? The mystery of the patriarchs. Their mystery is Jacob, who encompasses them, for Jacob is the patriarchs’ glory and stands to illuminate the world.”

: “Another interpretation of ‘Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac’: this is the secret of upper faith, enabling Isaac to cleave properly to the level of his portion. Here fire was included in water—certainly fire received water—as indicated by Abraham giving everything to Isaac: water was included in fire. Previously fire had been included in water. When? When Abraham bound Isaac to execute judgment upon him, fire was included in water. Now water was included in fire, so that everything might become the secret of upper faith.”
: “Like golden apples in silver settings is a word spoken with fitting consideration.”

: “Silver is below, the mystery of the right arm, for the upper head is gold, as in ‘You are the head of gold’; below are ‘his chest and arms of silver.’ When silver is perfected, it is included in gold: ‘Apples of gold in settings of silver.’ Silver thus turns to gold, and its place is perfected. There are therefore seven kinds of gold.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Nasso 15: “The third Shabbat meal corresponds to Jacob, as taught in Pri Etz Chaim and the Zohar, which identifies “I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father” with the meal of Zeir Anpin. This is the quality of truth: holiness that endures forever, as it says, “The lip of truth endures forever.” Love and fear, the aspects of Abraham and Isaac, may exist in a person's heart only for a time and then pass away; there is not yet proof that they will endure. What does not endure is not truth, as it says, “For but a moment.” Jacob's aspect establishes that holiness will remain forever and never cease. Thus Rabbi Bunim taught concerning “The children struggled within her”: Rebecca thought that she bore one child whose inclinations shifted, sometimes toward the house of study and sometimes toward its opposite. Therefore she went to inquire of the Lord, and Rashi explains that she asked what would happen at the end. She wished to know the ultimate outcome, what would endure, for amid changes there is no certainty until something endures. She was told that two nations were in her womb, and the essential one would be Jacob, the wholehearted man, through whom it would become clear that holiness would ultimately endure in his descendants. All Jewish souls are called the house of Jacob. Whatever may happen to each individual soul, ultimately they will remain within holiness, for none of His banished will remain banished. “Even when I walk in the valley of

: “If one vows, “I will not benefit from Abraham’s descendants,” he is forbidden to benefit from Israel but may benefit from the nations. The Gemara asks: But there is Ishmael! It is written, “Through Isaac shall descendants be called yours.” But there is Esau! “Through Isaac” means through some of Isaac’s descendants, not all of them.”

: “What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.”

: “‘When you lift up the head.’ Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: This hints that Moses would one day bring the first of the tribes close to the Divine Presence. Which tribe is this? Reuben, as it says, ‘Let Reuben live and not die.’ This is ‘When you lift up the head of the children of Israel’—the first of the tribes.”
: “Unrestrained as water, you shall not excel, for you ascended your father’s bed. Then you profaned it—he ascended my couch!”
: “Cursed is their anger, for it is fierce, and their fury, for it is harsh. I will divide them within Jacob and scatter them within Israel.”

: “Why are the nations tainted? Because they did not stand at Mount Sinai. When the serpent came upon Eve, it implanted pollution in her. Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai, had their pollution cease; the nations, who did not stand at Mount Sinai, did not have their pollution cease. Rav Aha, Rava’s son, asked Rav Ashi: What about converts? He answered: Though they themselves were not there, their heavenly roots were there, as it says, “Those standing here with us today before the Lord our God, and those who are not here.” This disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, who said: The pollution did not cease from our ancestors until three generations had passed. Abraham fathered Ishmael; Isaac fathered Esau; Jacob fathered twelve tribes among whom there was no flaw.”

: “An objection is raised: “Would that their heart were always like this”—it was impossible to remove the angel of death from them, for the decree had already been issued. Israel received the Torah only so that no nation or tongue would rule over them, as it says, “So that it may be well with them and their children forever.” Reish Lakish follows the other tanna, for a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose says that Israel received the Torah only so that the angel of death would not rule over them, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings, all of you children of the Most High.” But you ruined your deeds, and therefore, “Yet like Adam you shall die.””
: “I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.””

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”
: “Rabbi Elazar was eating terumah when the Angel of Death appeared to him. He said to him, “I am eating terumah; is it not called holy?” The appointed moment passed him by.”
: ““I give you your priesthood as a service of gift, and the outsider who approaches shall die.” They treated the eating of terumah outside the Temple as equivalent to Temple service.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””
: “My covenant with him was life and peace. I gave them to him for reverence; he revered Me and stood in awe of My name.”

: “Rather, this is what was taught: all the miracles and mighty acts performed for Israel, when the light of the Holy Ancient shone in His crowns, are carved and inscribed in az, in its alef. The alef pierces darkness and shines in every direction. When the light of alef joins and reaches zayin—what is zayin? ‘The Lord has a sword filled with blood’—He then performs miracles and mighty acts, because alef has joined with zayin. This is song, song from every side; this is ‘Then Moses will sing.’”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: then, when everything shone together, the sea performed the upper ordinances, and those above and below were entrusted into its hands. Therefore everything is difficult before God like the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as the teachings explain. Why? Because the splitting of the Sea of Reeds depends upon the Ancient One.”

: ““This is my God.” Rabbi Eliezer says: How do you know that a maidservant at the sea saw what Isaiah and Ezekiel did not see? For it says, “Through the prophets I use likenesses,” and, “The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.” They compared it to a flesh-and-blood king entering a province, surrounded by bodyguards, with warriors on his right and left and troops before and behind him. Everyone asked, “Which one is the king?” because he was flesh and blood like them. But when the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself at the sea, no one needed to ask, “Which one is He?” As soon as they saw Him, they recognized Him, and all opened their mouths and said, “This is my God, and I shall glorify Him; my father’s God, and I shall exalt Him!””

: “Rabbi Abba asked: what is ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Were Israel so foolish that they did not know this? They saw the Shekhinah before them and clouds of glory surrounding them. Those who saw their King’s glorious radiance at the sea—for we learned that a maidservant saw at the sea what Ezekiel did not see—could they be foolish enough to ask, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’ Rather, Rabbi Shimon explained: they wished to distinguish between the Ancient One, concealed beyond all concealment, called Nothingness, and Ze‘ir Anpin, called the Lord. Thus it does not say, ‘Is the Lord among us or not?’ as in ‘Will he follow My Torah or not?’ It says, ‘Is the Lord among us or Nothingness?’”

: “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah taught: Israel saw here what Ezekiel son of Buzi did not see, and all cleaved to precious upper Wisdom. Israel saw five levels of voices at Sinai, and Torah was given through these five levels. The fifth is ‘the voice of the shofar.’ Corresponding to them, Ezekiel saw five levels outside these: storm wind, a great cloud, flashing fire, radiance surrounding it and the appearance of Chashmal.”

: “From yod emerge male and female, vav-dalet: here vav is male and dalet female. Hence du, two—male and female, two forms. Yod alone is male, he female. He was initially dalet; when it became pregnant with vav within it, it brought forth vav. The parenthetical explanation says: he thus contains dalet-vav and he-he, yielding yod-he-vav. Yod appears in its form as the totality of yod-he-vav. After yod brought forth male and female, it settled afterward and covered the Mother.”
: “When you count the Israelites by their numbers, each man shall give Hashem a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them through the counting.”
: “Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.”
: “For three days no one could see his fellow, and no one rose from his place; but all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.”
: “Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””
: “When you count the Israelites by their numbers, each man shall give Hashem a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them through the counting.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””

: “Ten measures of wisdom descended to the world: The Land of Israel took nine, and the entire rest of the world took one. Ten measures of beauty descended to the world: Jerusalem took nine, and the entire rest of the world took one.”

: “‘He said’: what is this? As explained, ‘You shall say in your heart’—speech in silence. ‘Gather yourselves’: should it not say ‘Gather,’ as in ‘Gather My pious ones to Me’? We have established that ‘gather yourselves’ comes from the place above. Gather yourselves in a complete bond, in a single union. ‘I shall tell you’: what is ‘tell’? A mystery of wisdom.”

: “From that dew, the supremely holy ones are sustained. It is the manna ground for the righteous in the world to come. The dew drips into the Field of Holy Apples, as it says, ‘The layer of dew rose, and on the wilderness surface was a fine, flaky substance.’ The dew appears white, like crystalline stones in which all colors are visible. Thus ‘Its appearance was like the appearance of crystal.’”
: “When you count the Israelites by their numbers, each man shall give Hashem a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them through the counting.”
: “When you count the Israelites by their numbers, each man shall give Hashem a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them through the counting.”

: “‘When you lift up the heads of the children of Israel.’ Thus Scripture says, ‘Many say of my soul: There is no salvation for him in God, forever.’ Rabbi Shmuel bar Ami and the sages differed. Rabbi Shmuel bar Ami applied the verse to Doeg and Achitophel. ‘Many’ refers to Doeg and Achitophel, who were great in Torah. ‘Say of my soul’: they said of David, ‘Can one who seized the ewe, killed the shepherd, and caused Israel to fall by the sword have salvation?’ Hence, ‘There is no salvation for him in God, forever.’ ‘But You, Lord’: David said, ‘Master of the world, You agreed with them in Your Torah, saying, “The adulterer and the adulteress shall surely die.” Yet You are “a shield about me,” through the merit of my fathers; “my glory,” for You restored me to kingship; and “the One who raises my head,” for although I deserved to have my head removed, You granted me a lifting of the head through Nathan the prophet, who said, “The Lord has also put away your sin; you shall not die.”’”
: “David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against Hashem.” Nathan said to David, “Hashem has also removed your sin; you will not die.””

: “Abaye asked Rav Dimi: What is the plain meaning of the verse? He answered: It concerns someone teaching an unsuitable student. For Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Whoever teaches an unsuitable student falls into Gehinnom, as it says, “Every darkness is hidden for his treasures; a fire not fanned will consume him; it will harm the survivor in his tent.” “Survivor” means a Torah scholar, as it says, “Among the survivors whom the Lord calls.” Rabbi Zeira said in Rav’s name: Whoever teaches an unsuitable student is like someone throwing a stone at the idol Markulis, as it says, “Like binding a stone in a sling, so is giving honor to a fool”; and it says, “Delight is not fitting for a fool.””
: “Honor means Torah, as it says, “The wise inherit honor,” and, “The upright inherit good.” Good means Torah, as it says, “For I have given you a good acquisition; do not abandon My Torah.””
: “Restore to me the joy of Your deliverance, and sustain me with a willing spirit.”

: “Rav Judah said in Rav’s name: For six months David was afflicted with tzaraat, the Divine Presence withdrew from him, and the Sanhedrin separated from him. He was afflicted with tzaraat, as it says, “Cleanse me with hyssop and I will be pure; wash me and I will be whiter than snow.” The Divine Presence withdrew, as it says, “Restore to me the joy of Your deliverance, and sustain me with a willing spirit.” The Sanhedrin separated from him, as it says, “Let those who fear You return to me,” and so forth.”
: “David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against Hashem.” Nathan said to David, “Hashem has also removed your sin; you will not die.””
: “When you count the Israelites by their numbers, each man shall give Hashem a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them through the counting.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu said: Moses asked the Holy One, blessed be He, “Master of the world, by what will Israel’s horn be raised?” He answered him: “Through ‘When you raise’”—the passage commanding the contribution when Israel is counted.”
: ““He answered him: In ‘When you take’”: If you wish to lift their heads high, take from them a ransom for charity.”

: “Furthermore, words of Torah become settled only there, for there is no light except the light that emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted above and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One, blessed be He, except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters an evil path and then abandons it, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His glory. Therefore the completeness of everything is good and evil together, followed by rising into good; there is no good except that which has emerged from evil. Through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.”
: “He distributed freely and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever, and his strength will be raised in honor.”

: “When the Tree of good and evil rules—the ordinary realm of purity and the ordinary realm of impurity—the sages, who resemble Shabbatot and festivals, possess only what those belonging to the ordinary realm give them. They resemble Shabbat, which has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “For wisdom offers shelter, as money offers shelter; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of its possessor.”

: “Rabbi Huna and Rabbi Yirmeya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: The Holy One, blessed be He, will make shade and canopies in the Garden of Eden for those who perform commandments beside those devoted to Torah. There are three supporting verses: “In the shade of wisdom, in the shade of silver”; “Fortunate is the person who does this”; and, “It is a tree of life to those who support it.””
: “For R. Yohanan said: Anyone who provides commercial capital for Torah scholars merits sitting in the heavenly academy, as it says, “For in the shelter of wisdom is the shelter of money.””
: “Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa says: If a person’s fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures. If his wisdom precedes his fear of sin, his wisdom does not endure.”
: “Fear of Hashem is pure and endures forever. Hashem’s judgments are truth; together they are righteous.”

: “Another interpretation: ‘Fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.’ Come and see: if a person first labors in the place called Fear of the Lord, his Torah then endures forever. Why? Because he enters faith from here, through this gate to everything. When he fears this place, it is exalted and sits illuminated with the King, having brought a good son into the world.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””
Commentary: Rashi on Taanit 8b:12:2: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”
: “He distributed freely and gave to the poor; his righteousness endures forever, and his strength will be raised in honor.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “Take for yourself choice spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh; fragrant cinnamon, half that amount, two hundred and fifty; and fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty.”

: “‘A king is bound by the channels.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: ‘I have made you king. Just as a king’s people carry out his decree, so you shall decree upon them and they shall carry it out.’”

: “The Midrash appears to resolve this by saying: The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses, 'I have made you a king...you too decree upon them, and they perform.' Had it said, 'You shall command the children of Israel,' its meaning would have been like the rest of the Torah, where Moses commands as God’s emissary. Here, however, God told him that he himself would issue the command, and they would perform his decree.”

: “A baraita teaches: Moses did three things on his own judgment, and the Holy One, blessed be He, agreed with him: He added one day on his own judgment, separated from his wife, and broke the tablets. In adding a day, what did he expound? “Today and tomorrow”: Today must be like tomorrow. Just as tomorrow includes its preceding night, so today must include its preceding night. But the night of this day has already passed; hence two days besides today are required. From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, agreed with him? The Divine Presence did not rest upon them until Shabbat morning.”

: “Why did Moses decide to break the tablets? This is like a king who traveled overseas and left his wife with her maidservants. Because she was among them, an evil report spread about her. The king heard and sought to kill her. Her attendant heard and tore up her marriage contract, saying, ‘If the king says, “My wife has done such-and-such,” we shall tell him, “She is not yet your wife.”’ The king investigated and found no sexual misconduct in her; only the maidservants had acted corruptly. He immediately became reconciled with her. Her attendant told him, ‘My lord, prepare another marriage contract, since the first was torn.’ The king replied, ‘You tore it; go and supply the paper yourself, and I shall write it in My own hand.’”

: “Another interpretation: “Write for yourself.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses: I wrote the first tablets, as it says, “Written by the finger of God,” but you must write the second ones; would that I might put My hand to them. It is like a king who married a woman and wrote her marriage document himself. After a time she went astray, and he expelled her. Her attendant came and reconciled her to the king. The king told the attendant: I have accepted her, but you must prepare her marriage document; would that I might put my hand to it. Thus it is written, “I shall write upon the tablets.””

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””

k: volume-ii|661|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Ki Tisa, 5656 (1896), paragraph 2: “Thus, after Israel were accepted in repentance and the tablets were restored to them, their form was different: Torah had to clothe itself in midrashim and aggadot. These are called “hidden depths of wisdom.” Earlier everything had been revealed as the good light. That is why the thirteen attributes appear first. They correspond to the thirteen rules through which Torah is interpreted; the books explain that the thirteen divine attributes are the root of those thirteen interpretive rules, and the two are one matter. Originally these measures were unnecessary, for Torah is “longer than the earth in measure,” and Israel clung to the Ten Commandments. Afterwards it had to clothe itself in thirteen measures, vessels through which Torah can be grasped even in this world.”

: “Rabbi Eliezer again told them: “If the law follows my view, let Heaven prove it.” A heavenly voice declared: “Why do you contend with Rabbi Eliezer, when the law follows him everywhere?” Rabbi Yehoshua rose to his feet and declared: “It is not in heaven!” What does “It is not in heaven” mean? Rabbi Yirmiyah said: The Torah has already been given at Mount Sinai. We pay no attention to a heavenly voice, for You already wrote in the Torah at Mount Sinai, “Follow the majority.” Rabbi Natan met Elijah and asked him: “What was the Holy One, blessed be He, doing at that moment?” He answered: “He was smiling and saying, ‘My children have prevailed over Me! My children have prevailed over Me!’””

: “They were debating in the heavenly academy: If a bright skin lesion preceded the white hair, the person is impure; if the white hair preceded the lesion, he is pure. In a case of doubt, the Holy One, blessed be He, said “pure,” while the entire heavenly academy said “impure.” They asked: “Who shall decide? Let Rabbah bar Nachmani decide, for he said: ‘I am uniquely proficient in the laws of skin lesions and of tent impurity.’” They sent a messenger for him, but the angel of death could not approach him because his mouth did not cease its learning. Meanwhile a wind rustled among the reeds. Thinking it a troop of cavalry, he said: “Better that this man die than be handed over to the royal authorities.” As his soul departed he said: “Pure, pure.” A heavenly voice declared: “Happy are you, Rabbah bar Nachmani: your body is pure, and your soul departed with ‘pure’ upon your lips.””

: “This also explains the Midrash’s statement that Hashem told Aaron, “You are prepared for something greater: when you light the lamps.” The offerings apply while the Temple stands, but the lamps endure forever. The princes’ dedication consisted of offerings that they brought from their own property, yet the priests performed the sacrificial service. What consolation, then, was Aaron given by being told that he would light the Menorah? The oil for the Temple lamps was also communal property, as it says, “They shall take oil to you”; Aaron’s privilege was only to light it. Yet Aaron and his sons likewise performed all the sacrifices, including those of the princes. The essential meaning of lighting the lamps is that Aaron was given the power to illuminate the light of the Oral Torah. This is “Come and shine before Me.” Through lighting the Temple lamps, Aaron was empowered to cause the light of the Oral Torah to appear and shine in every Jewish heart.”

: “The oil for illumination—Israel’s shining before Him, as the Midrash says—is the Oral Torah, through which they renew the light. This is the dialectical reasoning of Torah, which Nedarim 38 says God gave to Moses, who generously gave it to Israel. The Gemara therefore repeatedly uses the expression, 'Moses, you have spoken well,' because every renewal of Torah occurs through the root of Moses our teacher’s soul in all the sages of Israel. All Israel have a share in Torah, as it says, 'The inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.' Jacob includes the masses, whereas Torah scholars are called Israel; Torah is the inheritance of them all.”

: “That which is called Mishneh Torah, Moses spoke from his own mouth, as we have explained. Why? Upper Wisdom is called the totality of Torah, from which everything proceeds through the inner Voice. Afterward all becomes settled and united in the place called the Tree of Life. General and particular depend upon it: Written and Oral Torah. It is called Torah and Mishneh Torah. At first there was uninterrupted Might; now all is together. Therefore these Ten Commandments are marked with vav: ‘and do not commit adultery,’ ‘and do not steal,’ ‘and do not bear witness,’ ‘and do not covet,’ ‘and do not desire,’ as explained.”
: “You shall command the Israelites to bring you pure olive oil, crushed for lighting, to kindle a lamp continually.”
: “Speak to all the wise-hearted people whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and let them make Aaron’s garments, to consecrate him to serve Me as priest.”

: “When their garments are upon them, their priesthood is upon them; when their garments are not upon them, their priesthood is not upon them. They are then like non-priests, and the Master said: A non-priest who performs the service incurs the death penalty.”
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”
: “You will be called priests of Hashem; you will be spoken of as servants of our God. You will consume the wealth of nations and take pride in their splendor.”
: “Take for yourself choice spices: five hundred shekels of flowing myrrh; fragrant cinnamon, half that amount, two hundred and fifty; and fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty.”

: “The Sages taught: The roots used for the anointing oil Moses made in the wilderness were boiled in it; this is Rabbi Yehudah’s view. Rabbi Yose says: There was not even enough oil to coat the roots. Rather, the roots were soaked in water, oil was poured over them, absorbed their fragrance, and was skimmed off. Rabbi Yehudah answered: Was only one miracle performed with the anointing oil? Its original quantity was only twelve log. From it the Tabernacle and its vessels, Aaron and his sons were anointed throughout the seven days of inauguration; yet all of it remains for the future, as it says, “This shall be holy anointing oil for Me throughout your generations.””

: “Rav Hisda said that Mari bar Mar expounded: What is meant by “There were two baskets of figs set before the Lord’s Temple: One basket had very good figs, like the first-ripe figs, and the other had very bad figs, too bad to eat”? The good figs are the completely righteous; the bad figs are the completely wicked. Might you say that their hope is lost and their expectation has ended? Scripture says, “The mandrakes have given fragrance”: Both groups will one day give fragrance. Rava expounded: “The mandrakes have given fragrance”—these are Israel’s young men who have not tasted sin. “At our doors are all delicacies”—these are Israel’s daughters who tell their husbands when their openings are permitted; another interpretation is that they reserve their openings for their husbands. “New and old, my beloved, I have stored away for you”—the congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the world, I imposed many decrees upon myself beyond those You decreed upon me, and I fulfilled them.”

: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon the Devout’s name: A fast that includes none of Israel’s transgressors is not a fast. For galbanum smells foul, yet Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients. Abaye derived this from, “He founded His united company upon the earth.””

: “R. Yohanan said: There are three crowns: that of the altar, that of the Ark, and that of the table. Aaron merited taking the altar’s crown; David merited taking the table’s crown. The Ark’s crown still lies available: whoever wishes to take it may come and take it. Perhaps you might think it is inferior? Scripture says, “Through me kings reign.””

: “Furthermore, words of Torah become settled only there, for there is no light except the light that emerges from darkness. When this side is subdued, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted above and honored in His glory. There is no service of the Holy One, blessed be He, except from within darkness, and no good except from within evil. When a person enters an evil path and then abandons it, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His glory. Therefore the completeness of everything is good and evil together, followed by rising into good; there is no good except that which has emerged from evil. Through this good His glory is exalted, and this is complete service.”

: “To what may this be compared? A ruler sent an intermediary to betroth a woman, but she went astray with another man. What did the innocent intermediary do? He took the marriage document the ruler had given him for her betrothal and tore it up, saying: Better that she be judged as unmarried than as a married woman. So Moses, when Israel committed that deed, took the tablets and broke them—meaning that, had they seen their punishment, they would not have sinned. Moses also said: Better that they be judged as inadvertent offenders than as deliberate ones. Why? The tablets contained “I am the Lord your God,” with its punishment alongside: “One who sacrifices to gods shall be destroyed.” Therefore he broke the tablets.”

: “The matter is disputed by tannaim: “The Lord’s anger burned against Moses.” Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says: Every instance of divine anger in the Torah leaves a mark, but no mark is stated here. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: A mark is stated here too: “Is not Aaron your brother the Levite?” Was he not a priest? Rather, He said: I had intended you to be a priest and him a Levite; now he will be priest and you a Levite. The Sages say: Moses served as a priest only during the seven days of inauguration. Some say: Priesthood ceased only from Moses’ descendants, as it says, “Moses, the man of God—his sons were called after the tribe of Levi”; and, “Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who called His name.” Why add the second verse? You might have said that the first passage concerns later generations; therefore it also says, “Moses and Aaron among His priests.””

: “‘Let no one leave his place on the seventh day.’ We learned: ‘his place’ is the place within which he is fit to walk. Its secret is ‘Blessed is the Lord’s glory from His place’: this is the Place. This is also the secret of ‘The place upon which you stand is holy ground.’ We call that known site ‘Place,’ where the upper glory becomes known.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “Rava bar Mehasya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: A person who gives a gift to another must inform him, as it says, “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” A baraita likewise teaches: “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: I have a fine gift in My treasure house, and its name is Shabbat. I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them. From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: One who gives a child bread must inform the child’s mother.”

: “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel put “We will do” before “We will hear,” six hundred thousand ministering angels came and bound two crowns upon each Israelite, one for “We will do” and one for “We will hear.” When Israel sinned, one million two hundred thousand angels of destruction descended and stripped them off, as it says, “The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.” Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said: At Horeb they put them on, and at Horeb they took them off. That they put them on at Horeb is as we have said; that they took them off there follows from “The children of Israel stripped themselves.” Rabbi Yohanan said: Moses merited them all and took them, for immediately afterward it says, “Moses would take the tent.” Reish Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, will one day return them to us, as it says, “The Lord’s redeemed will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads”—the joy that was upon their heads long ago.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Everything concerning Shabbat is doubled. Its omer is doubled: “Two omers for each person.” Its offering is doubled: “On the Shabbat day, two lambs.” Its punishment is doubled: “Those who profane it shall surely be put to death.” Its reward is doubled: “You shall call Shabbat a delight, and the Lord’s holy day honored.” Its commands are doubled: “Remember” and “Observe.” Its psalm is doubled: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.””
: “Observe Shabbat, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death; whoever performs work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”
: “Work may be done for six days, but on the seventh day there is complete rest, holy to Hashem; whoever performs work on the Shabbat day shall be put to death.”
: “Rabba said: Everyone agrees that on Shabbat a portion must also be for your own enjoyment. Why? Because it says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight.””

: “Rabbi Haggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahman’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for eating and drinking. Because the mouth takes pleasure in its utterance, they permitted a person to occupy himself with words of Torah on them. Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Hiyya bar Ba’s name: Shabbatot and festivals were given only for occupying oneself with words of Torah. A baraita supports each view: What does one do? Either sit and eat, or sit and occupy oneself with words of Torah. One verse says, “It is a Sabbath to the Lord,” and another says, “An assembly to the Lord your God.” How are they fulfilled? Give a portion to Torah study and a portion to eating and drinking.”
