quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:4: ““Because this mouth blossoms”: This uses the expression “It will blossom and flower.” The meaning is that, because a person enjoys the breath issuing from his mouth, they permitted him to occupy himself with words of Torah on Shabbat and festivals, which were originally given only for delight through eating and drinking.”

k: volume-ii|692|3|Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat
ref: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2
quote: Commentary: Penei Moshe on Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 15:3:2:7: ““One verse says”: This is another baraita. It should read: One verse says, “An assembly to the Lord your God,” and another says, “An assembly shall be for you.” How can both be fulfilled? Divide the day. This supports Rabbi Berekhya, because one must in any event occupy oneself with words of Torah, while also giving a portion to eating and drinking, to fulfill “for you.””

: “In the Jerusalem Talmud we read: Rabbi Chaggai said, 'Sabbaths and festivals were given only for eating and drinking.' Rabbi Berechyah said, 'They were given only to occupy oneself with Torah.' Tanchuma explains that they do not disagree. Rabbi Berechyah’s statement about Torah study concerns laborers, who work throughout the week and come on Shabbat to study Torah. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement about enjoyment concerns Torah scholars, who labor in Torah throughout the week and enjoy themselves on Shabbat. As for Rava’s statement that everyone agrees Shabbat requires an element 'for you,' as explained in section 242: one may answer that he addresses Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua; alternatively, there he requires some enjoyment, whereas here the discussion concerns devoting the whole day to enjoyment.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name: Shabbat was given only for delight. Rabbi Chaggai said in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: Shabbat was given only for Torah study. They do not disagree. Rabbi Berekhya’s statement in Rabbi Chiya bar Abba’s name, “for delight,” concerns Torah scholars, who toil in Torah all week and come on Shabbat to enjoy themselves. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement in Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman’s name, “for Torah study,” concerns workers, who are occupied with their labor throughout the week and come on Shabbat to occupy themselves with Torah.”

: “In the Jerusalem Talmud we read: Rabbi Chaggai said, 'Sabbaths and festivals were given only for eating and drinking.' Rabbi Berechyah said, 'They were given only to occupy oneself with Torah.' Tanchuma explains that they do not disagree. Rabbi Berechyah’s statement about Torah study concerns laborers, who work throughout the week and come on Shabbat to study Torah. Rabbi Chaggai’s statement about enjoyment concerns Torah scholars, who labor in Torah throughout the week and enjoy themselves on Shabbat. As for Rava’s statement that everyone agrees Shabbat requires an element 'for you,' as explained in section 242: one may answer that he addresses Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua; alternatively, there he requires some enjoyment, whereas here the discussion concerns devoting the whole day to enjoyment.”

: “The Jerusalem Talmud states, 'Rabbi Chaggai said: Sabbaths were given...' as explained in Perishah. Beit Yosef writes concerning this: Rava’s statement that everyone agrees Shabbat requires an element 'for you' may address Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua. His meaning is as follows. Apparently everyone agrees that 'for you' is required; how, then, could Rabbi Berechyah say Sabbaths were given only for Torah? Although Tanchuma interprets this as referring to laborers, Rava’s statement would apparently include them too and require 'for you.' Beit Yosef answers that this is incorrect: Rava addresses the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who were not discussing laborers. They too may agree that laborers must occupy themselves with Torah all day. Their discussion concerns other people, who also study during the week, setting aside times for Torah while engaging in business. Regarding these, Rabbi Eliezer allows the day to be entirely 'for you,' while Rabbi Yehoshua requires it to be divided. Understand this.”

: “The Sages taught: The Ten Commandments were given to Israel on the sixth day of the month. Rabbi Yose says: On the seventh. Rava said: All agree that they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai on the New Moon. Here it says, “On this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai,” and elsewhere, “This month shall be for you the first of the months.” Just as the latter refers to the New Moon, so does the former. All agree that Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat. Here it says, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it,” and elsewhere, “Moses said to the people: Remember this day.” Just as the latter was said on that very day, so the former was said on that very day.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “As soon as Israel, the holy people by themselves, leave exile, the river that had been desolate and dry will immediately be described by ‘A river issues from Eden’—this is vav—‘to water the garden.’ ‘River’ is the middle pillar; ‘issues from Eden’ is the upper Mother; ‘to water the garden’ is the lower Shekhinah. At that time it will be said of Moses and Israel, ‘Then you will delight in the Lord,’ with oneg, delight: ayin is Eden, nun is nahar, river, and gimel is gan, garden. The verse ‘Then Moses will sing’ will be fulfilled: it does not say ‘sang,’ but ‘will sing.’ For the mixed multitude and the idol-worshipping nations, oneg, delight, will turn into nega, affliction, as with Pharaoh and the Egyptians, upon whom blistering boils erupted. For Israel, however, there will be delight.”

: “Abaye asked Rav Dimi: What is the plain meaning of the verse? He answered: It concerns someone teaching an unsuitable student. For Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Whoever teaches an unsuitable student falls into Gehinnom, as it says, “Every darkness is hidden for his treasures; a fire not fanned will consume him; it will harm the survivor in his tent.” “Survivor” means a Torah scholar, as it says, “Among the survivors whom the Lord calls.” Rabbi Zeira said in Rav’s name: Whoever teaches an unsuitable student is like someone throwing a stone at the idol Markulis, as it says, “Like binding a stone in a sling, so is giving honor to a fool”; and it says, “Delight is not fitting for a fool.””
: “Honor means Torah, as it says, “The wise inherit honor,” and, “The upright inherit good.” Good means Torah, as it says, “For I have given you a good acquisition; do not abandon My Torah.””

: “Does Rabbi Akiva hold that Shabbat is a time for tefillin? A baraita teaches: Rabbi Akiva says: Might a person put on tefillin on Shabbat and festivals? Scripture says, “It shall be a sign for you upon your hand”: This concerns days that require a sign, excluding these days, which are themselves a sign.”

k: volume-ii|700|0|Birkei Yosef, Orach Chaim §31, citing Ra
quote: : “Some sought to introduce the ruling that an uncircumcised man whose brothers died from circumcision should put on tefillin on Shabbat, since everyone needs two signs: on weekdays, tefillin and the covenant; on Shabbat, Shabbat and the covenant. This is not the law; see Birkei Yosef, Orach Chaim 31, in the name of a manuscript responsum of Radbaz and of the Arizal. The reason is that the sign of Shabbat itself also includes the sign of the covenant.”

: “‘Remember Shabbat’s day to sanctify it’: this is the mystery of the holy covenant. All the sources of the body’s limbs stand in this covenant, which embraces everything. Likewise Shabbat embraces Torah, and all Torah’s secrets depend upon it. Establishing Shabbat is like establishing the whole Torah; whoever guards Shabbat is as though he guards the entire Torah.”

: “Why are both ‘remember’ and ‘guard’ stated? ‘Remember’ pertains to the male, and ‘guard’ to the bride. Why does it say, ‘You shall revere My sanctuary’? Guard yourselves against impure thought, for My sanctuary is holy. Why? Because ‘I am the Lord who sanctifies you’ in everything.”

: “From the side of Chesed, God is ‘remember,’ and the Shekhinah is ‘guard.’ The masters of Mishnah explained: ‘remember’ pertains to the male, and ‘guard’ to the bride. On right and left the branches are separate, like the lung’s lobes, separated above; corresponding to them are the living creatures, ‘their faces and wings separated above,’ and the open sections of a Torah scroll. Below, the two form a single union, like a Torah scroll’s closed sections, where there is no separation. Therefore in the place of union, the body, resembling the lulav’s spine, if its leaves are broken apart or separated it is invalid.”

: “‘Remember’ is the place without forgetfulness, where forgetfulness does not exist, for there is no forgetting in the place of the upper covenant, still less above it. Below there is forgetfulness, a place requiring reminders. Hence ‘Let his fathers’ iniquity be remembered.’ There are appointed powers there that recall a person’s merits and sins.”

: “Another interpretation: this teaches that the souls fly forth from there, as it says, vayinnafash, ‘and He was refreshed’—for a thousand generations, as in ‘the word He commanded for a thousand generations,’ followed by ‘which He made with Abraham.’ What did He make? He made a covenant with him between the ten fingers of his hands and the ten toes of his feet. Abraham was ashamed. God told him, ‘As for Me, here is My covenant with you’; through it you shall become the father of many nations.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”
: “It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “Rav Huna said: A person traveling on the road or in the wilderness who does not know when Shabbat falls counts six days and observes one day. Hiyya bar Rav says: He observes one day and then counts six. What is their disagreement? One follows the order of the world’s creation; the other follows Adam’s experience. An objection was raised: A traveler who does not know when Shabbat falls observes one day for six. Does that not mean he counts six and observes one? No, it means he observes one and counts six. If so, it should say, “He observes one day and counts six.” Furthermore, a baraita explicitly teaches that a traveler on the road or in the wilderness who does not know when Shabbat falls counts six days and observes one. This refutes Hiyya bar Rav; it is a refutation. Rava said: Each day he performs enough labor for his subsistence, except on that day. Must he die on that day? Let him prepare two days’ provisions the previous day. But perhaps the previous day was Shabbat! Rather, each day he prepares his subsistence, even on that day. How, then, is that day distinguished? Through kiddush and havdala.”

: “The ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, differ from human ways. A human instructs others to act, while doing nothing himself. The Holy One, blessed be He, is different: what He does, He tells Israel to do and observe.”

: “Everyone beside Sarah is like an ape beside a human being. Sarah beside Eve is like an ape beside a human being. Eve beside Adam is like an ape beside a human being. Adam beside the Divine Presence is like an ape beside a human being.”

: ““They shall be a people for Me.” Rabba bar Rav Huna said: Israel possesses an additional distinction in comparison with converts. Regarding Israel it is written, “I will be their God, and they shall be My people.” Regarding converts it is written, “Who is this who pledged his heart to approach Me, declares the Lord?” followed by, “You shall be My people, and I will be your God.””

: “For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares Hashem: I will place My Torah within them and write it upon their heart. I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

k: volume-ii|714|0|Netziv, Haamek Davar on Exodus 31:13, se
quote: Parallel: Netziv, Haamek Davar on Exodus 31:13, second comment: “The meaning of “that you may know that I…” is this: Anything that awakens holiness in Israel, such as the Temple and the like, does so through the impression made by a sacred object. That object thus contributes to the effect. Even a gentile who sees a synagogue or a Torah scroll experiences some stirring of the soul, knowing this is something sacred. But when an Israelite attains holiness of soul on Shabbat and festivals, without any outward sensation distinguishing that day from other days, this is a sign that the Holy One Himself, as it were, assists in sanctifying one who comes to sanctify himself. That is why this holiness is precious in God’s sight and takes precedence over all work that makes sacred objects.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”

: “Everyone beside Sarah is like an ape beside a human being. Sarah beside Eve is like an ape beside a human being. Eve beside Adam is like an ape beside a human being. Adam beside the Divine Presence is like an ape beside a human being.”

: “It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai likewise said: Gentile graves do not impart impurity through a shared covering, as it says, “You are My sheep, the sheep of My pasture; you are adam.” You are called adam, whereas the nations are not called adam. An objection was raised: “Sixteen thousand human persons”! There the term distinguishes them from animals. Another verse says, “In which there are more than one hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left”! There too it distinguishes them from animals. But Scripture says, “Everyone who killed a person or touched a slain person must purify himself”! Perhaps an Israelite was killed. The Rabbis reply: “Not a man of ours is missing.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai understands that verse to mean none was lost through sin. Ravina said: Granted, the verse excludes them from imparting impurity through a shared covering, for it says, “An adam who dies in a tent”; does Scripture exclude them from impurity through touching or carrying?”
: “It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.”

: “What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.”
: “Isaac had come from the approach to Beer-lahai-roi, and he was living in the land of the Negev.”

: ““When she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field, and she alighted from the donkey.” What does “she alighted” signify? Rava said in Rabbi Yitzchak’s name: She told him: Just as a donkey cries out immediately when it has no food in its manger, so a woman cries out immediately when there is no grain in her house. “She said: Give me a blessing, for you have given me land of the south”—a house dry of every good thing. “Give me springs of water”—a man who possesses nothing but Torah. “Caleb gave her upper springs and lower springs”—he told her: Would a man who dwells in the upper and lower realms need someone to seek sustenance for him?”

: “The Sages taught: How many meals must a person eat on Shabbat? Three. Rabbi Hidka says: Four. Rabbi Yohanan said: Both derive their views from a single verse: “Moses said: Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the Lord; today you will not find it in the field.” Rabbi Hidka holds that these three occurrences of “today” refer to meals in addition to the evening meal. The Sages hold that they include the evening meal.”

: “This is explained by the Talmud’s dispute: one view follows the world’s creation, and the other follows Adam. As soon as Adam was created, Shabbat’s light shone upon him; only afterward came the six working days. From the human perspective, the first Shabbat is therefore the holiness that Hashem bestows through an awakening from above, without any awakening from below. One subsequently merits the observance of a second Shabbat through the six working days that preceded it and came through one’s own effort. This follows the heavenly pattern: “Let us make man in our image.” The Midrash says that Hashem observes the commandments and tells Israel to do and observe what He does. Thus, “Walk in His ways”: before the Divine Presence, man is like an ape before a human being. Just as Hashem appointed rest for Himself after the six days of Creation, a person must make Shabbat after his own six working days.”

: “When the sukkah was completed in its thigh, it was said of Jacob, ‘Jacob arrived whole.’ Jacob is indeed the likeness of the middle pillar from its outer side. But was not Moses there? Moses was on its inner side: one is associated with the body, the other with the soul. The middle pillar’s two thighs, Netzach and Hod, are therefore complete.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “R. Yohanan said: A person’s sustenance is twice as difficult as childbirth. For childbirth Scripture says, “in pain,” whereas for sustenance it says, “in painful toil.””

k: volume-ii|728|0|R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yeshar
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yesharim 21:8–11: “A person could have sat idle and the decreed provision would still have been fulfilled, had the penalty not first been imposed upon all humanity: “By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread.” Therefore one must make some effort for one’s livelihood, as the supreme King decreed. It is a tax the entire human race pays, from which there is no escape. Hence the Sifrei asks whether even someone sitting idle might see blessing, and answers: “In all the work of your hands that you do.” Effort does not produce the benefit; it is required. Once one has made an effort, one has discharged one’s obligation and made room for Heaven’s blessing. One need not spend one’s days in frantic exertion. David said, “Not from the east or west…but God judges”; Solomon said, “Do not exhaust yourself becoming rich; desist from your understanding.” The true path is that of the early pious: Torah was central, work secondary, and both endured. After doing some work, one should trust the Creator and cease grieving over worldly matters. The mind then remains free and the heart prepared for true piety and wholehearted service.”
: “He blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has shepherded me all my life until this day—””

: “Nevertheless, Israel attained this through Moses our teacher. At the giving of the Torah, when all Israel was fit for the crown of priesthood, angels came and tied two crowns upon each person: one for “we shall do,” and one for “we shall hear.” The crown of “we shall do” is priesthood, the practical work of divine service; the crown of “we shall hear” is Torah, which also includes kingship, as in “Through me kings reign.” When they sinned, the crowns were removed, and Moses received them all. Pri Etz Chaim teaches that on Friday night Moses returns the crowns to Israel. Thus, “Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion”: on Shabbat he regains the light he attained at Sinai and returns the crowns to Israel. Hence “And you, speak ... My Shabbatot ... to know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you.” This is Moses’ power to return the crowns on Shabbat, and therefore “you” is specified. Yet the verse says “speak,” not “you shall speak”: Hashem was commanding Moses to tell Israel this passage, so that through it they could receive His holiness and become a sanctuary. By telling Israel this passage, Moses empowered them always to receive Shabbat’s holiness. Returning their crowns allows them to regain their level at Sinai; this particular power belongs to Moses.”

: ““Moses your teacher said, ‘A human being cannot see Me and live,’ but you said, ‘I saw Hashem sitting on a high and exalted throne.’” … Nevertheless, do the verses not contradict each other? “I saw Hashem” is understood according to the teaching: All the prophets looked through a mirror that was not clear; Moses our teacher looked through a clear mirror.”

: “Creation’s purpose was to reveal the glory of His kingship in the world. When the wicked prosper and the righteous do not, His glory’s revelation is concealed. God showed Moses and told him, 'You shall see My back.' I heard from my holy teacher concerning the Targum, 'You shall see what is after Me, but what is before Me shall not be seen,' that its meaning is: after an action became manifest, Moses immediately recognized its depth and the good within it. Before the action became manifest, however, its depth could not be grasped, for His thoughts are exceedingly deep, beyond apprehension.”

: “Another interpretation: “He said: Show me, please, Your glory.” He desired to understand the reward of the righteous and the prosperity of the wicked. How do we know that the righteous’ reward is called glory? “The wise shall inherit glory”; likewise, “Before His elders, glory.” How do we know that the wicked’s prosperity is called glory? “After glory You shall take me.” What did the Holy One, blessed be He, answer? “You cannot see My face.” Here “My face” signifies the wicked’s prosperity, as it is written, “He repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them.” “The Lord said: Behold, there is a place with Me; stand upon the rock.” Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: It does not say, “Here I am in this place,” but, “There is a place with Me”: My place is subordinate to Me; I am not subordinate to My place. “I shall remove My palm.” The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: I shall show you the reward I will give the righteous at the end of days.”
: “He said, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim Hashem’s name before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and compassion to whom I show compassion.””

: “Rabbi Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in Rav Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: ‘Behold, it was very good’ refers to the good inclination, and ‘behold, it was very good’ also refers to the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination really very good? Rather, without the evil inclination, a person would not build a house, marry a woman, have children, or conduct business. So Solomon says, ‘It is a person’s rivalry with his fellow.’”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: ““Who forms light and creates darkness.” Why not say, “Who forms light and creates brightness”? We use Scripture’s wording. But do we recite “Who makes peace and creates evil” exactly as Scripture writes it? Rather, it writes “evil,” while we say “everything,” using a finer expression. Here too, let us say “brightness,” using a finer expression. Rava answered: This is to mention the quality of day at night and the quality of night by day. Mentioning night by day is clear from “Who forms light and creates darkness”; but where is day mentioned at night? Abaye answered: “Who rolls away light before darkness and darkness before light.””
: “He said, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim Hashem’s name before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and compassion to whom I show compassion.””
: “He said, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim Hashem’s name before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and compassion to whom I show compassion.””

: ““Hashem will be King over the whole earth; on that day Hashem will be One and His name One.” Is He not One already? R. Aha bar Hanina said: The World to Come is unlike this world. In this world, over good news one says, “Blessed is the One who is good and does good,” and over bad news one says, “Blessed is the true Judge.” In the World to Come, everything will be “the One who is good and does good.””
: “He said, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim Hashem’s name before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and compassion to whom I show compassion.””
: “Hashem said, “Here is a place beside Me; stand upon the rock.””

k: volume-ii|741|0|R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Da’at Tevunot 1
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Da’at Tevunot 128:3: “Indeed, you will see that even among events evil exists only in the parts of things before they join to complete the whole; there is no completed whole that is evil. Since we know that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, does is entirely very good, a lack seen on one side, in one of an event’s conditions, is supplied by another condition that completes it. The deficiency existed only because all the conditions had not yet been completed; once they are complete, it is certainly good. Particular events themselves confirm this. The same will become clear at the end concerning the general course of the world, when the promise is fulfilled: “I shall thank You, Hashem, for You were angry with me” (Isaiah 12:1). Then all the parts of the process will be finished, and the process will truly be wholly good.”
: “He said, “You cannot see My face, for a human being cannot see Me and live.””
: “I will remove My hand, and you will see My back, but My face will not be seen.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu said: From here we learn that the Holy One, blessed be He, created worlds and destroyed them, created worlds and destroyed them, until He created these. He said: ‘These please Me; those did not please Me.’”
: “He said, “I will cause all My goodness to pass before you, and I will proclaim Hashem’s name before you. I will show favor to whom I show favor, and compassion to whom I show compassion.””
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”

: “When Israel are properly complete, complete witnesses testify concerning them: God and the Congregation of Israel. At that time the upper dew flows from the Ancient One’s place. When? When they are united. Thus ‘My head is filled with dew.’ The numerical value of tal, dew, is ‘the Lord is One’: God and the Congregation of Israel. At that hour Israel are found fit for the dew.”
: “Many who sleep in the dusty ground will awaken: some to everlasting life, and some to disgrace and everlasting abhorrence.”

: “I sleep, but my heart is awake. The sound of my beloved knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew, my locks with the droplets of night.””
: “My flesh and my heart are spent; God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.”

: ““I sleep.” The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I sleep concerning commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I sleep concerning charitable deeds, but my heart is awake to perform them. I sleep concerning sacrifices, but my heart is awake for reciting the Shema and prayer. I sleep concerning the Temple, but my heart is awake for synagogues and houses of study. I sleep concerning the appointed end, but my heart is awake for redemption. I sleep concerning redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: Where do we find the Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel’s heart? In this verse: “God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.””

: ““When you walk, it will guide you”—this refers to this world. “When you lie down, it will guard you”—this refers to death. “When you awaken, it will speak with you”—this refers to the future world.”

: “‘Let no one leave his place’: this is the precious place of holiness, for outside it are other gods. ‘Blessed is the Lord’s glory’ is the glory above; ‘from His place’ is the glory below. This is the secret of Shabbat’s crown, hence ‘Let no one leave his place.’ Happy is the portion of one who merits Shabbat’s glory, in this world and the world to come.”

: “This is ‘Let the waters beneath heaven gather into one place, and let the dry ground appear.’ ‘Let the waters gather’ is Torah; ‘into one place’ is Israel, whose souls depend upon the place of which it says, ‘Blessed is the Lord’s glory from His place.’ ‘The Lord’s glory’ is the lower Shekhinah; ‘from His place’ is the upper Shekhinah. Since their souls come from there, the Lord certainly rests upon them, and it is said of them, ‘The Lord’s portion is His people.’ This is ‘Let the waters gather into one place.’”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak asked Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman: ‘Since I have heard that you are a master of aggadah, tell me: from where was light created?’ He replied: ‘This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself in it like a cloak, and made the radiance of His splendor shine from one end of the world to the other.’ He said this to him in a whisper. Rabbi Shimon said: ‘It is an explicit verse, “He wraps Himself in light like a cloak,” yet you tell it to me in a whisper?’ He replied: ‘Just as I heard it in a whisper, so I told it to you in a whisper.’”
: “Shmuel the Small says: “Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart exult when he stumbles, lest Hashem see and be displeased, and turn His anger away from him.””

: “Another interpretation: “This shall be the law of the leper.” This is what Scripture says: “Who is the man who desires life?” A peddler traveled among the towns near Tzippori, calling: Who wishes to buy the elixir of life? People crowded around him. Rabbi Yannai was sitting and studying in his room. Hearing the cry, “Who wants the elixir of life?” he told him: Come up here and sell it to me. The peddler replied: Neither you nor people like you need it. Rabbi Yannai insisted, and he came up, took out a book of Psalms, and showed him the verse, “Who is the man who desires life?” What follows? “Guard your tongue from evil”; “Turn from evil and do good.” Rabbi Yannai said: Solomon too proclaims, “One who guards his mouth and tongue guards his soul from troubles.” Rabbi Yannai said: All my days I read this verse without recognizing its plain meaning, until this peddler came and made it known: “Who is the man who desires life?” Therefore Moses warns Israel, saying, “This shall be the law of the leper”—the law of one who spreads an evil name.”
: “Who is the person who desires life, who loves days in which to see goodness?”

quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 1:1: “A second interpretation takes “These are the words” as words of rebuke, as the Sifrei teaches and Rashi cites. : “If so, why does ‘Keep My Shabbatot’ imply two? Shabbat eve and Shabbat day are never separated.”

: “Rabbi Zekharya said in Rabbi Yishmael’s name: The Holy One, blessed be He, intended to bring forth the priesthood from Shem, as it says, “He was a priest of God Most High.” Once Shem put Abraham’s blessing before God’s blessing, He brought it forth from Abraham. quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Nasso 5:1: “Faith's principal hold is in the attribute of Keter, beyond knowledge, as Patach Eliyahu says: it is the crown of kingship. We have already discussed why the Torah begins with the letter bet in Bereshit: this is the level of the beginning of wisdom, as the Jerusalem Targum renders it, “With wisdom.” It is the first contraction in the revelation of the ten utterances. Rosh Hashanah 32a therefore says that “In the beginning” is also an utterance. Although “And He said” is not explicitly written until the creation of light, the creation of darkness over the face of the deep is itself the first contraction's coming into being. Yet this is recognition beyond knowledge, darkness as absence of comprehension; therefore “And He said” is not written. There is, however, a still higher level, where no conception applies—not even the absence of comprehension represented by darkness. This is the alef preceding the bet: “The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord.” This fear is wisdom's beginning, the level of the alef in “I am the Lord your God,” with which the Ten Commandments begin. Ramban's explanation is well known: “I am” is not expressed as a command because faith cannot be commanded. Rather, through the utterance “I am,” faith in God was fixed within the totality of Israel's souls, without investigation or reasoning, through attachment at the root beyond reason and knowledge.”

: “The third prayer, ‘You are One and Your Name is One,’ corresponds to the Lord, the middle pillar, which unites with both. These are the additional neshamah, additional ruach and additional nefesh. The additional nefesh belongs to Shabbat eve, ‘You sanctified’; the additional neshamah, ‘The soul of every living being,’ is described by ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion’; and the additional ruach is ‘You are One and Your Name is One.’”
: “A truthful lip endures forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.”

: “This is the meaning of the verse: ‘The lips of truth will endure forever’—these are Israel, who are the lips of truth: ‘The Lord our God, the Lord is One.’ Everything is truth and the mystery of truth. They conclude, ‘The Lord your God is truth.’ This is ‘The lips of truth will endure forever.’”

: “‘But I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.’ If it is true, why call it merely ‘inscribed’? And if it is merely inscribed, why call it ‘true’? Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi asked, ‘Did you not know how to answer?’ Rabbi Levi replied: ‘It is inscribed before the decree is issued; it is true once the decree has been issued.’ What is truth? The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our Master said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: It is emet, ‘truth.’ What is emet? Reish Lakish said: Alef stands at the beginning of the alphabet, mem in the middle, and tav at the end, corresponding to ‘I am the first, and I am the last.’”
: “Thus says Hashem, King of Israel and its Redeemer, Hashem of Hosts: I am first and I am last, and apart from Me there is no god.”
: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: You have given a name to your swine; I, too, give a name to My firstborn son: ‘Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son.’”
: “Deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingship will belong to Hashem.”
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”

: “Rabbi Shimon taught: the Matron will not enter His palace in joy until Esau’s kingdom is judged and she takes vengeance upon it for causing all this. First, ‘Saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau’; afterward, ‘The kingship shall belong to the Lord.’ What is kingship? The Matron. After their union, ‘The Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His Name One.’”

: “At that time, ‘Saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge Esau’s mountain, and the kingship shall belong to the Lord.’ Esau’s kingship in this world will be given to God alone. Does kingship not belong to God already? Although God rules above and below, He has given each of the other nations a portion and inheritance in this world to use. Hence ‘The kingship shall belong to the Lord’—His alone—and ‘The Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His Name One.’”

: ““Hashem will be King over the whole earth; on that day Hashem will be One and His name One.” Is He not One already? R. Aha bar Hanina said: The World to Come is unlike this world. In this world, over good news one says, “Blessed is the One who is good and does good,” and over bad news one says, “Blessed is the true Judge.” In the World to Come, everything will be “the One who is good and does good.””
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”
: “On the day Hashem grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil, and the harsh labor imposed upon you—”

: “Rabbi Shimon also said: we learned that Shabbat is an image of the world to come, and certainly it is. Thus the sabbatical year and Jubilee mirror one another, as do Shabbat and the world to come. The additional soul comes from the mystery of ‘remember’ to this Shelter of Peace, which receives it from the world to come and gives this addition to the holy people. They rejoice in that addition and forget every weekday matter, every sorrow and distress, as in ‘On the day the Lord grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil and the hard labor,’ and so forth.”
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”

: “When Hashem your God grants you rest from all your surrounding enemies, in the land Hashem your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall erase the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens. Do not forget.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”
: “On the day Hashem grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil, and the harsh labor imposed upon you—”
: “Deliverers will ascend Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingship will belong to Hashem.”
: “Hashem will be King over the whole earth. On that day Hashem will be One and His name One.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

: “Rabbi Chiyya said: certainly so; everything depends upon repentance. If you say that all can now arouse repentance together, they cannot. Why? Because it says, ‘When all these things come upon you,’ followed by ‘You shall take it to heart among all the nations where He has driven you,’ and ‘You shall return to the Lord your God.’ Then, ‘Even if your outcast is at the end of heaven, from there He shall gather you.’ Until all those things are fulfilled, they cannot arouse repentance of themselves. Rabbi Yose said: how you have sealed every road and path for those in exile, leaving them no opening to speak! If so, let them remain as they were in every generation, neither bearing exile nor receiving a reward, leaving the Torah’s law and mixing with the other nations. He began: ‘Like a pregnant woman approaching childbirth, writhing and crying out in her pains.’ What does ‘like a pregnant woman’ mean? Ordinarily a woman completes nine full months, yet many women have passed only one or two days of the ninth month. All the labor pains belong to the ninth month; even if only one day has passed, it is counted as though the entire ninth month had passed. So too with Israel: once they have tasted exile, if they repent it is counted as though all the things written in Torah had passed over them. How much more so, when so many sufferings have already passed over them since exile began.”
: “Like a pregnant woman nearing birth, writhing and crying out in her labor pains, so were we before You, Hashem.”

: “They sinned as before. What did God do? He again sent this son out of His palace, with his mother beside him. He said: ‘From now on, mother and son shall suffer many evils together.’ Thus ‘For your transgressions your mother was sent away.’ Hence ‘When you are in distress and all these things find you at the end of days.’ What is ‘the end of days’? The holy Mother, who is the end of days; with her they suffered everything they suffered in exile. If they return in repentance, even one misfortune or one suffering that passes over them is counted as though they had suffered it all. If not, it will be when the appointed end and all its generations have been completed, as the Holy Lamp said concerning ‘permanently, to the one who purchased it, throughout his generations.’ Everything depends upon repentance. Rabbi Chiyya said: certainly so, and therefore exile has been prolonged.”

: “All ten sefirot that Hashem emanated to create His world are called “days,” as explained at the end of discourse nine. Thus Malkhut, the Divine Presence, is called “the end of days.” The Zohar says that they suffered everything they suffered in exile together with Her. Were they to return in repentance, even a single affliction or pain that passed over them would be counted as though they had endured it all. This resembles the preceding image, “Like a pregnant woman”: the whole ninth month is a time for labor pains. The Midrash speaks of a hundred cries, ninety-nine toward death and one toward life. Yet she may emerge through one cry, one pain and one day in that ninth month. “So have we been before You, Hashem”: we too can emerge through a single pain and cry, if only we return in complete repentance.”

: “‘You are from nothing’: from nothing at all—from a putrid drop. ‘Your work is from a cry’: from the hundred cries a woman utters during childbirth, when she sits upon the birthstool—ninety-nine toward death and one toward life.”
: “Like a pregnant woman nearing birth, writhing and crying out in her labor pains, so were we before You, Hashem.”
: “When you are in distress and all these things overtake you in the latter days, you will return to Hashem your God and listen to His voice.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: Come and see how beloved Israel is before the Holy One, blessed be He: wherever they were exiled, the Divine Presence accompanied them. They were exiled to Egypt, and the Divine Presence was with them, as it says, “Did I not reveal Myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt?” They were exiled to Babylonia, and the Divine Presence was with them, as it says, “For your sake I sent to Babylon.” When they are ultimately redeemed, the Divine Presence will also be with them, as it says, “Hashem your God will return with your captivity.” It does not say “bring back,” but “return”: the Holy One, blessed be He, returns with them from their exiles.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

Parallel: Malbim on Psalms 23:4: ““Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow,” nevertheless, “I will fear no evil, for You are with me,” because he sees the shepherd walking beside him to guard him. He presents the image of a shepherd who holds a small rod in one hand, striking the sheep with it to turn it toward the right path. In his other hand he holds his staff, a strong stick with which he drives away every predator and destroyer. He therefore says: When I see “Your rod and Your staff,” both “comfort me,” because I know that no evil will approach me. The meaning of the image is that sufferings are for his benefit, guiding him along the good path; the Lord holds His staff to save him from all his enemies. Therefore he trusts in the Lord always.”

: “Rabbi Chiyya said: certainly so; yet we see, as the world’s mighty have seen, that exile continues and David’s son has not yet come. Rabbi Yose answered: it is indeed so. What enables Israel to endure this exile? All the promises God has promised them. As explained, they enter synagogues and study halls, see all those consolations, and their hearts rejoice, enabling them to endure whatever befalls them. Without this, they could not endure.”
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””
: “Hashem will give strength to His people; Hashem will bless His people with peace.”

: “The priestly blessing has the same meaning. “May Hashem bless you”: every blessing is increase, as in the blessing of fish and the blessing of humanity. Here it means: may He bless you with an increased flow of Oral Torah. “And guard you” follows “The priest’s lips shall guard knowledge”: the priest guards Israel’s purity, called da’at, as the Gemara identifies “wisdom” with the order Kodashim and “knowledge” with the order Taharot. The Zohar calls Chokhmah the higher holiness, and Torah emerges from wisdom, from the place called holy. This is Written Torah: “Let there be light” corresponds to Chokhmah, the first apprehension of existence emerging from nothing, whereas the first utterance is entirely beyond grasp, an understanding concealed from every conception. The five mentions of light in “Let there be light” correspond to the five books of Torah. “Knowledge is Taharot” corresponds to Oral Torah, whose abundant wisdom purifies and repairs the abundant anger.”

: “Why did the Torah begin with bet, as does berakhah, ‘blessing’? How do we know that Torah is called blessing? It says, ‘Full of the Lord’s blessing, inherit sea and south.’ The sea signifies Torah, as in ‘broader than the sea.’ What is ‘full of the Lord’s blessing’? Wherever bet occurs, it expresses blessing, as in bereshit. Reshit means wisdom, as in ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord’; and wisdom is blessing, as it says, ‘God blessed Solomon,’ and ‘The Lord gave Solomon wisdom.’ This resembles a king who married his daughter to his son, gave her to him at the wedding, and said, ‘Do with her as you wish.’”
: “Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali is satisfied with favor and filled with Hashem’s blessing; possess the west and the south.”

: “For we learned: Rabbi Yose says: On the garments of builders, a stain on one side is an obstruction to immersion; on an ordinary person’s garments, it is an obstruction only when it penetrates both sides. A saddlecloth should not be more important than an ordinary person’s garment. Who are these “builders”? Rabbi Yohanan said: They are Torah scholars, who devote all their days to building the world.”

: “What is meant by “With enemies at the gate”? Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said: Even a father and son, a teacher and student, who study Torah at one gate become enemies to one another. Yet they do not leave there until they become loving friends, as it says, “Vahev in Supha”: Read the phrase as “Love at its end.””

: “Although Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed about co-wives, sisters, an old bill of divorce, a woman whose marital status was uncertain, a man who divorced his wife and then lodged with her at an inn, silver and its equivalent, and a perutah and its equivalent, Beit Shammai did not refrain from marrying women from Beit Hillel, nor Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai. This teaches that they treated each other with affection and friendship, fulfilling “Love truth and peace.” Rabbi Shimon says: They refrained in definite cases, but did not refrain in doubtful cases. … Do not read “in doubtful cases,” but “in unspecified cases”: they would inform one another, and the others would abstain.”

: “Jacob came and desired it, but it was not given to him. He was told: since Abraham is above and Isaac below him, you shall stand in the middle and take all three. What is the middle? Peace. But does it not say, ‘You grant truth to Jacob’? Truth and peace are one, as in ‘words of peace and truth’ and ‘there shall be peace and truth in my days.’ This is ‘I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father’: a complete inheritance, containing kindness, fear, truth and peace. Thus ‘The stone rejected by the builders became the cornerstone’: the stone rejected by Abraham and Isaac, who built the world, has now become the cornerstone.”

: “‘Dominion and fear are with Him; He makes peace in His heights.’ The companions explained this verse. Dominion is Abraham: ‘You are a prince of God among us,’ and ‘I shall bless you and magnify your name.’ Fear is Isaac: ‘The Fear of Isaac was mine.’ ‘He makes peace in His heights’ is Jacob: ‘Grant truth to Jacob,’ and ‘Love truth and peace.’ Truth and peace are bound to one another. Therefore he is the perfection of everything.”
