quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Korach 5:1: “Even the disagreements within the Oral Torah serve the world's repair, with peace at their conclusion. “And Vahev in Suphah” is explained in Kiddushin 30b: even a father and son become enemies of one another in study, yet do not leave until they become friends again. The Zohar earlier says that Korah pursued controversy, that controversy divides peace. His mistake was to think controversy would do no harm. He imagined that he acted solely for Heaven's sake: because his fellow's conduct did not please him, he could oppose him without the dispute causing harm. In truth, truth and peace are one, as Sefer HaBahir teaches; Zohar III 12b says they are bound together. Truth is possible only with peace. Shammai and Hillel's controversy was truly for Heaven's sake, and even during their disagreement they treated one another with affection and friendship, fulfilling “Love truth and peace,” as Yevamot 14b teaches. Torah scholars are likewise called companions because they are truly joined together, like the angels called companions because there is no hostility, jealousy, hatred or rivalry among them (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 8:9). But resentment in the heart and anger at one's fellow are a sign that the controversy serves the world's confusion rather than its repair. This was Korah's error in opposing Aaron, who loved peace, pursued peace, loved people and brought them near to Torah. Aaron's power was to bring words of Torah into Israe

: ““Israel encamped there.” Wherever it says “They journeyed” and “They encamped,” they journeyed in disagreement and encamped in disagreement. Here, however, it says, “Israel encamped”: they all joined in one heart.”

: “‘God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.’ It is written, ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches, and He adds no sorrow with it.’ ‘The Lord’s blessing brings riches’ refers to Shabbat, as it says, ‘God blessed the seventh day.’ ‘He adds no sorrow with it’ refers to mourning, as in the verse, ‘The king was grieved over his son.’”
: “Hashem’s blessing brings wealth, and He adds no sorrow with it.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “The Sages taught: When our teachers entered the vineyard at Yavne, they said: Torah will one day be forgotten in Israel. For it says, “Days are coming, declares the Lord God, when I will send famine into the land—not a famine for bread or thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the Lord”; and, “They will wander from sea to sea, from north to east; they will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it.” “The word of the Lord” means halakha; “the word of the Lord” means the end of exile; “the word of the Lord” means prophecy. A baraita teaches: Rabbi Shimon ben Yohai says: Heaven forbid that Torah should be forgotten in Israel, for it says, “It will not be forgotten from the mouth of his descendants.” How, then, do I understand “They will roam seeking the word of the Lord, but will not find it”? They will not find a clear halakha and a clear Mishnah together in one place.”

: “If not, both sides come to the Great Court in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from which Torah goes out to all Israel, as it says, “From that place Hashem will choose.” If he returns to his city and repeats and teaches as he previously taught, he is exempt; if he issues a practical ruling, he is liable, as it says, “The man who acts willfully.” He is liable only when he issues a ruling directing practice.”
: “Blessing comes from Zion, as it says, “May the Lord bless you from Zion.””
: “Like the dew of Hermon descending upon Zion’s mountains, for there Hashem ordained the blessing: life forevermore.”
: “For a priest’s lips should preserve knowledge, and people should seek Torah from his mouth, for he is an angel of Hashem of Hosts.”
: “You shall come to the Levitical priests and to the judge serving in those days. You shall inquire, and they will tell you the legal ruling.”
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””
: “Take from among yourselves a contribution for Hashem. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it as Hashem’s contribution: gold, silver, and copper.”

: “Come and see what was first written: ‘From every man whose heart makes him willing,’ including everyone. God wished the Tabernacle’s work to embrace every side, kernel and husk. Because the mixed multitude were among them, ‘from every man whose heart makes him willing’ was said to include them among Israel, who are the kernel. All were commanded. Later, kind turned toward its own kind: the mixed multitude came and made the calf. Those who died followed them astray, bringing death and slaughter upon Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: from now on the Tabernacle’s work shall come only from Israel’s side. Immediately, ‘Moses assembled the whole congregation of the children of Israel,’ followed by ‘Take from yourselves an offering for the Lord’—from yourselves specifically, unlike the earlier ‘from every person whose heart moves him.’ From where did Moses gather them? Because the mixed multitude were among them, Moses had to gather Israel and set them apart from their midst.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.””

: “The Divine Presence originally dwelled chiefly in the lower world. When Adam sinned, it withdrew to the first heaven; when Cain sinned, to the second; through the generation of Enosh, to the third; through the generation of the Flood, to the fourth; through the generation of the Dispersion, to the fifth; through the Sodomites, to the sixth; and through the Egyptians in Abraham’s time, to the seventh. Corresponding to them, seven righteous men arose: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehat, Amram, and Moses. Abraham brought it down to the sixth heaven; Isaac, from the sixth to the fifth; Jacob, from the fifth to the fourth; Levi, from the fourth to the third; Kehat, from the third to the second; Amram, from the second to the first; and Moses brought it down from above to below.”

: ““The Lord said: I have surely seen.” It does not merely say “I have seen,” but “I have surely seen.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Moses, you see one sight, but I see two. You see them coming to Sinai and receiving My Torah; I see them receiving My Torah—this is “seeing”—and I have seen the making of the calf, as it says, “I have seen this people.” When I come to Sinai to give them Torah, I descend in My fourfold chariot; they contemplate it, detach one of its figures, and provoke Me through it. Nevertheless I judge them according to their present circumstances, not their future deeds: “For I have heard their cry,” although “I know their pains”—what they will eventually do. Thus: “I have surely seen.” What is “I know their pains”? I know how much they will pain Me in the wilderness, as it says, “How often they rebelled against Him in the wilderness and grieved Him in the wasteland.” Nevertheless I do not refrain from redeeming them.”

: ““Go down, for your people have corrupted themselves.” It does not say “the people,” but “your people.” Moses said: Master of the universe, how are they my people? The Holy One, blessed be He, replied: They are your people. While they were still in Egypt I told you, “I shall bring out My hosts, My people.” I told you not to mingle a mixed multitude with them. In your humility and goodness you told Me: Those who return are always accepted. I knew what they would do; I told you no, yet fulfilled your wish. They were the ones who made the calf. They worshipped idols, made it, and caused My people to sin. See what is written: Not “These are our gods,” but “These are your gods,” for the converts who went up with Moses made it and told Israel, “These are your gods.” Therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, told Moses, “Go down, for your people have corrupted themselves.””
: “The Sages taught: Converts will not be accepted in the days of the Messiah. Similarly, converts were not accepted in David’s days or in Solomon’s days.”

: “The court therefore did not accept converts throughout the days of David and Solomon: in David’s days, lest they had turned back out of fear; in Solomon’s days, lest it was for Israel’s kingship, prosperity, and greatness. Anyone who turns from paganism for some worldly advantage is not a righteous convert. Nevertheless, many people converted in David’s and Solomon’s days before ordinary people. The supreme court regarded them with concern: after they had immersed, it neither rejected them nor drew them close until their ultimate conduct became evident.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”
: “Speak to the Israelites, and let them take a contribution for Me. From every person whose heart moves him, you shall take My contribution.”

: “Therefore it is written, ‘Let them take an offering for Me, from every man’: from one called ish, who has overcome his inclination. Whoever overcomes his inclination is called ish. ‘Whose heart makes him willing’: what does this mean? One in whom God takes delight. Thus ‘On Your behalf my heart says,’ ‘the Rock of my heart,’ ‘the good-hearted,’ and ‘his heart was gladdened’ all speak of God. So too here, ‘whose heart makes him willing’: from him take My offering, for it is found there, not elsewhere.”
: “My flesh and my heart are spent; God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.”

: ““I sleep.” The congregation of Israel said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, I sleep concerning commandments, but my heart is awake for acts of kindness. I sleep concerning charitable deeds, but my heart is awake to perform them. I sleep concerning sacrifices, but my heart is awake for reciting the Shema and prayer. I sleep concerning the Temple, but my heart is awake for synagogues and houses of study. I sleep concerning the appointed end, but my heart is awake for redemption. I sleep concerning redemption, but the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, is awake to redeem me. Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said: Where do we find the Holy One, blessed be He, called Israel’s heart? In this verse: “God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.””

: “After praying, Rabbi Alexandri would say: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that we desire to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven within the dough and subjection to foreign kingdoms. May it be Your will to rescue us from their power, so that we may return to fulfill the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 17a:2:3: ““The leaven within the dough”: the evil inclination in our hearts, which makes us ferment.”
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””
: “Take from among yourselves a contribution for Hashem. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it as Hashem’s contribution: gold, silver, and copper.”

: “Because the mixed multitude are the leaven in the dough, while the nations of the world resemble chaff, the mixed multitude hinder Israel in exile more than the idolatrous nations do. As the Sages explained: ‘What prevents us? The leaven in the dough prevents us.’ They cling to Israel like leaven in dough. The idolatrous nations, however, are only ‘like chaff driven away by the wind.’”

: “Further, when Israel are in exile, ‘Who prevents us? The leaven in the dough’ is said of them, as the masters of Mishnah explained. When the mixed multitude are Israel’s leaders, it is as though they exert dominion over God—an alternative reading says they transgress God’s dominion—and come under the judgments of stars and constellations. Therefore they cry, ‘Lord our God, masters besides You have ruled us.’”
: ““The leaven in the dough”: The evil inclination within our hearts, which makes us ferment.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai asked his disciples, “My children, what does Scripture mean by ‘Charity raises a nation, but the kindness of peoples is sin’?” Rabbi Eliezer replied: “‘Charity raises a nation’ means Israel, for it is written, ‘Who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth?’ ‘The kindness of peoples is sin’ means that all the charity and kindness the nations perform is counted as sin for them, because they do it only to enhance their own standing, as it says, ‘So that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.’” But is an act done with such a motive not genuine charity? A baraita teaches that one who says, “I give this sela to charity so that my children may live,” or “so that I may merit the World to Come,” is completely righteous. There is no contradiction: the latter concerns an Israelite, and the former a gentile.”
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””

: “Rabbi Yitzchak then began: ‘Moses assembled the entire congregation of the children of Israel.’ Why gather them? To give them Shabbat as before. Before Israel made the calf, he had given them Shabbat; the mixed multitude did not keep it. Hearing ‘Between Me and the children of Israel,’ they said, ‘This has been withheld from us.’ Immediately ‘The people gathered around Aaron,’ and many followed them. After those who died had died, Moses gathered Israel alone and gave them Shabbat as before: ‘For six days work shall be done,’ and so forth.”
: “It is an everlasting sign between Me and the Israelites, for in six days Hashem made the heavens and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and was refreshed.”

: “Did Moses learn the entire Torah? Concerning Torah it is written, “Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea”—could Moses have learned it in forty days? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, taught Moses general principles. Thus: “When He finished speaking with him.””

: “Faithful Shepherd: this commandment is to bring an offering for the Great Sanhedrin when it errs. Tannaim and Amoraim formed the seventy of the Great Sanhedrin, with Moses above them. There were seventy of the lesser Sanhedrin, with Aaron above them. Therefore the masters of Mishnah said: Moses was the King’s attendant—Tiferet, from which comes the Great Sanhedrin. Aaron was the Matron’s attendant—Malchut, which we call the small he, as in ‘I shall serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.’ After her it is called the lesser Sanhedrin.”

: “David said: This nation has three identifying traits: compassion, a sense of shame, and acts of kindness. Compassion, as it says, “He will give you compassion, have compassion on you, and multiply you”; a sense of shame, as it says, “So that His fear may be upon your faces”; acts of kindness, as it says, “So that he may command his children and his household after him.” Whoever possesses these three traits is fit to attach himself to this nation.”

: “‘He went ahead of them.’ Thus it is written, ‘As a father has compassion on his children.’ Rabbi Chiyya taught: Like the most compassionate of the patriarchs. Who was the most compassionate patriarch? Rabbi Yehudah said: Abraham, who said, ‘Far be it from You to do such a thing!’ Rabbi Levi said: Jacob—‘He went ahead of them,’ saying, ‘Better that harm reach me than reach them.’”
: “Moses said to the people, “Do not fear, for God has come to test you, and so that awe of Him will be upon your faces, so that you do not sin.””

: “A baraita teaches: “So that His fear may be upon your faces”—this is shame. “So that you do not sin”—this teaches that shame leads to fear of sin. From here they said: Being bashful is a good sign in a person. Others say: Someone who feels shame will not readily sin; whoever lacks shame shows that his ancestors did not stand at Mount Sinai.”

: “The Teli in the universe is like a king on his throne; the wheel in the year is like a king in his realm; the heart in the person is like a king at war. God made each thing opposite its counterpart: good opposite evil, good from good, evil from evil. Good makes evil recognizable, and evil makes good recognizable. Good is reserved for the good, and evil for the wicked.”

: “A scoundrel happened to be there, named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He sounded the shofar and said, “We have no share in David and no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Each man to his tents, Israel!””

: “Princes may go out wearing bells. Who is the tanna of this ruling? Rabbi Oshaya said: It is Rabbi Shimon, who says that all Israel are royal children. Rava said: The ruling concerns a bell woven into one’s garment, and all agree to it.”

: “Rava asked Rabbah bar Mari: What is the source of the Sages’ teaching, “Rise early and eat in summer because of the heat, and in winter because of the cold,” and of the popular saying, “Sixty runners run, but cannot catch the man who ate bread in the morning”? He answered: It is written, “They shall neither hunger nor thirst; scorching heat and sun shall not strike them.” Rava said: You derive it from there, but I derive it from here: “You shall serve Hashem your God”—this is reciting Shema and praying. “He will bless your bread and your water”—this is bread with salt and a jug of water. Thereafter, “I will remove sickness from your midst.” A baraita teaches: “Sickness” here means bile. Why is it called machalah? Because eighty-three illnesses are associated with it, the numerical value of machalah. Morning bread with salt and a jug of water counteract them all.”

: “Someone used to go about saying, “A thief is not killed for two or three thefts.” Samuel said to Rav Judah: A verse states it: “Thus says Hashem: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four I will not reverse it.””

: “Rabbi Yannai was walking along the road and saw a man who appeared very distinguished. He said: Will the master consent to be our guest? He replied: Yes. He brought him home, fed him, and gave him drink. He tested him in Scripture and found him unlearned; in Mishnah, aggadah, and Talmud, and found him unlearned. He said: Take the cup and recite the blessing. The man replied: Let Yannai bless in his own house. He asked: Can you repeat what I tell you? He replied: Yes. He told him to say: A dog has eaten Yannai’s bread. The man rose, seized him, and said: My inheritance is with you, and you withhold it from me! He asked: What inheritance of yours is with me? He replied: Once I passed a school and heard the children saying, “Moses commanded us Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.” It does not say “the congregation of Yannai,” but “the congregation of Jacob.” He asked: Through what merit did you eat at my table? He replied: Never have I heard an evil report and carried it back to its subject; never have I seen two people quarrelling without making peace between them. Yannai said: You possess all this proper conduct, yet I called you a dog! He applied to him, “One who orders his way”: one who evaluates his path is worth much. For Rabbi Yishmael bar Rav Nachman said: Proper conduct preceded Torah by twenty-six generations, as it is written, “To guard the way of the tree of life.” “The way” is proper conduct, and afterward, “the tree of life” is Torah.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai expounded: What does “Declare to My people their transgression, and to the house of Jacob their sins” mean? “Declare to My people their transgression” refers to Torah scholars, whose inadvertent sins are counted as deliberate ones. “To the house of Jacob their sins” refers to the unlearned, whose deliberate sins are counted as inadvertent ones. This accords with the Mishnah: Rabbi Yehudah says, “Take care in your learning, for an error in learning is counted as deliberate wrongdoing.””
: “You shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you shall speak to the Israelites.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “The Divine Presence originally dwelled chiefly in the lower world. When Adam sinned, it withdrew to the first heaven; when Cain sinned, to the second; through the generation of Enosh, to the third; through the generation of the Flood, to the fourth; through the generation of the Dispersion, to the fifth; through the Sodomites, to the sixth; and through the Egyptians in Abraham’s time, to the seventh. Corresponding to them, seven righteous men arose: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehat, Amram, and Moses. Abraham brought it down to the sixth heaven; Isaac, from the sixth to the fifth; Jacob, from the fifth to the fourth; Levi, from the fourth to the third; Kehat, from the third to the second; Amram, from the second to the first; and Moses brought it down from above to below.”
: “For a priest’s lips should preserve knowledge, and people should seek Torah from his mouth, for he is an angel of Hashem of Hosts.”

: “Another interpretation: “Aaron saw.” What did he see? Aaron said: If they build it, the offense will be attributed to them. Better that it be attributed to me than to Israel. Rabbi Abba bar Yudan said in Rabbi Abba’s name: It is like a prince who became arrogant and took a sword to strike his father. His tutor said: Do not trouble yourself; give it to me and I shall strike. The king looked at him and said: I know your intention—better that the offense be attributed to you than to my son. By your life, you shall not leave my palace; you shall eat from my table’s remainder and receive twenty-four allowances. So, “You shall not leave My palace”—“He shall not depart from the sanctuary”; “you shall eat from My table’s remainder”—“What remains of the meal offering”; “you shall receive twenty-four allowances”—these are the twenty-four priestly gifts given to Aaron and his sons. The Holy One, blessed be He, told Aaron: “You loved righteousness”—you loved vindicating My children and hated condemning them. Therefore, “God, your God, anointed you.” He told him: By your life, from the whole tribe of Levi none but you shall be chosen for the High Priesthood: “Take Aaron and his sons with him.””
: “He shall not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of his God’s anointing oil is upon him. I am Hashem.”

: “Rabbi Hanina said: Whoever becomes amenable through his wine possesses something of his Creator’s understanding, as it says, “The Lord smelled the pleasing fragrance.” Rabbi Hiyya said: Whoever remains composed through his wine possesses the understanding of the seventy elders. The numerical value of yayin, wine, is seventy, and that of sod, secret, is seventy. When wine enters, the secret comes out.”
Commentary: Rashi on Eruvin 65a:18:1: ““One who becomes amenable through wine”: People seek to appease him about something, and he agrees when his heart is cheerful with wine.”

: “Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master and the Matron with every kind of delight, fulfilling ‘This is the table before the Lord.’ Until now all delight in the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread’: the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, the varied flavors of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”

: “There is another secret within this mystery. On this day the spirit benefits from Israel’s pleasures and delight. Therefore one must give it delight through food and drink three times, at the three meals corresponding to faith’s three levels, as explained. This spirit receives joy and delight through Israel’s meals. Happy is the portion of one who gives it enjoyment and delight on this day.”

: “With what does one make it delightful? Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, said in Rav’s name: With a dish of beets, large fish, and heads of garlic. Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said in Rav’s name: Even a small thing, if prepared in honor of Shabbat, counts as delight. What is an example? Rav Pappa said: Kasa de-harsena, a dish of small fish.”
: ““Everything on dry land died”—but not the fish in the sea.”

: “Rav Chisda said: A stew of beets is beneficial to the heart and good for the eyes, and all the more so for the intestines. Abaye said: This applies when it stands upon the stove and makes a bubbling sound.”

: “The woman saw that the tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes, and desirable for gaining understanding. She took some of its fruit and ate; she also gave some to her husband with her, and he ate.”

: “The Sages taught: Five things were said of garlic: it satisfies, warms the body, brightens the face, increases semen, and kills intestinal lice. Some add that it brings in love and drives out jealousy.”

: “With what does one make it delightful? Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, said in Rav’s name: With a dish of beets, large fish, and heads of garlic. Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said in Rav’s name: Even a small thing, if prepared in honor of Shabbat, counts as delight. What is an example? Rav Pappa said: Kasa de-harsena, a dish of small fish.”

: “Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in Rav’s name: One who regularly eats small fish does not come to intestinal illness. Moreover, small fish promote conception and plentiful offspring, and strengthen a person’s entire body.”
: “Kasa de-harsena: small fish fried in the oil of their innards together with flour.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Resisei Layla 6:1: “A sign of an accepted prayer is the joy following it. Midrash Tehillim 48 explains “The joy of all the earth” through the joy produced by the offering. The same applies to prayer, which takes the offering's place: “I will make them rejoice in My house of prayer.” A thing is verified through its opposite, for commandments produce the opposite of their apparent natural effect. Thus, “Tithe so that you become wealthy” (Taanit 9a): naturally, tithing impoverishes someone, since he pays two tithes and terumah, but as a commandment it has the opposite effect and enriches him. Shabbat 119a similarly says that wealthy people outside the Land became wealthy because of Shabbat. Eikhah Rabbah, introduction 17, describes gentiles mocking Jews as poor because of Shabbat: they refrain from work for a seventh of their days and must also provide its delights. In truth, wealth flows from this. The same applies to character: someone who delights in Shabbat is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. Ordinarily, pleasure gives the heart a craving for more pleasures. Yet the Sages say that here, on the contrary, one is saved from Gehinnom's judgment—that is, immersion in desires. Concerning the commandment of the city led astray in Re'eh, “You shall surely strike,” which could produce great cruelty through striking an entire city and everything in it and destroying it completely, Scripture concludes, “He will give you compassion and have compassion up

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, gives a person an additional soul on the eve of Shabbat and takes it from him when Shabbat ends, as it says, “He ceased and was refreshed.” When the Shabbat rest has ceased: woe, the soul has gone.”
Commentary: Rashi on Beitzah 16a:11:2: ““An additional soul”: a heart broadened for rest and joy, freely open, so that a person may eat and drink without his appetite recoiling.”

: “When that spirit descends, sixty chariots, crowned toward the six directions, descend with it into the Garden of Eden. When it reaches the garden, all the spirits and souls there awaken toward that spirit—or, according to another reading, are crowned with it. A herald proclaims: ‘Happy are you, Israel, holy people, toward whom your Master’s favor is awakened!’”
: “Who is like the wise person, and who knows how to interpret a matter? A person’s wisdom lights up his face and changes its stern appearance.”

: “There is another secret within this mystery. On this day the spirit benefits from Israel’s pleasures and delight. Therefore one must give it delight through food and drink three times, at the three meals corresponding to faith’s three levels, as explained. This spirit receives joy and delight through Israel’s meals. Happy is the portion of one who gives it enjoyment and delight on this day.”
