quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Ki Teitzei VI:1: “On Shabbat the nefesh, ruach, and neshamah are all “new faces,” as we say: “Truly, new faces and spirits with souls.” The nefesh pertains to action. Throughout Shabbat, when one refrains from all work and activity, it becomes “new faces.” Ceasing from the work habitually performed during the six working days resembles encountering a transgression and escaping it, which counts as fulfilling a commandment, as stated in Kiddushin 39b. This earns an additional nefesh. Regarding speech, it says “and speaking a word”; the Sages explain that Shabbat speech must differ from weekday speech. This includes permitted speech, not only forbidden words, as Tosafot explains from the Midrash at the end of Behar. As we have often explained, the verse says “and speaking a word,” not “and from speaking a word,” parallel to “from seeking your affairs.” It thus means one should speak on Shabbat, provided it is a “word”—Torah or matters of Heaven. Speech changes on Shabbat, so the ruach too becomes “new faces.” These two depend on the person: abstaining from action earns an additional nefesh; changing speech in fulfillment of “and speaking a word” earns an additional ruach. The neshamah, corresponding to thought, comes from God: He gives a person added holiness, so that he has only holy thoughts on Shabbat. Hence the Gemara’s precise expression, “The Holy One gives a person an additional neshamah on Shabbat eve”: God gives this.”
: ““She bore”—but she only raised him! This teaches that whoever raises an orphaned boy or girl in his home is credited by Scripture as though he had given birth to that child.”

: “Shabbat eve’s sanctification is the sanctity of creation’s Shabbat. It is sanctified through thirty-two paths and three levels of holy apples. Over this sanctification we must mention creation’s totality and its rest, in the mystery of the thirty-two paths and the three levels included within them. This is the testimony to creation: ‘The heavens and earth and all their host were completed…God completed.’ This testimony has thirty-five words: thirty-two paths and three levels of holy apples.”

: “What is Shabbat? If you say it denotes cessation, as in ‘For on it He ceased,’ that is correct. But its inner mystery is this: when this point rises and light shines, she is crowned with the patriarchs. Once crowned with them, she joins and unites with them as one, and everything is called Shabbat. Shabbat: shin-bat. Shin, as explained, is the mystery of the three patriarchs united with the only daughter. She is crowned with them, and they with the world to come. All is one. This is shin-bat, that everything become one.”

: “‘The chief cupbearer recounted: Behold, a vine was before me.’ This refers to Israel, as it says, ‘You brought a vine out of Egypt.’ ‘On the vine were three branches’ refers to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. ‘It was as though budding’: Israel’s redemption began to blossom. ‘Its blossoms emerged’: Israel’s redemption put forth blossoms. ‘Its clusters ripened into grapes’: a vine that flowered immediately blossomed, and grapes that blossomed immediately ripened.”

: “They then sang about the well, which alludes to the Oral Torah. The manna came through Moses’ merit: he brought the Written Torah down from heaven, and the manna was bread from heaven. The well’s water, coming from the earth, alludes to the Oral Torah. The Zohar likewise speaks of the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. Water includes all beverages, as the Sages infer from “He shall bless your bread and your water.” They truly tasted every kind of drink in the well, just as they tasted every kind of food in the manna, as the Mekhilta teaches. The well came through Miriam’s merit, for Oral Torah is the moon receiving from the sun, the Written Torah; this is Malkhut. Sotah says that David also descended from Miriam: “Malkhut is the mouth; we call it Oral Torah.” David and Solomon are the roots of Oral Torah and the lower wisdom.”

: “‘He meditates upon His Torah.’ Rabbi Shimon said: Abraham’s father did not teach him, and he had no teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The Holy One, blessed be He, appointed his two kidneys to be like two teachers; they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom. Thus it is written, ‘I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my kidneys instruct me.’”
: “She opens her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of kindness is upon her tongue.”

: “Come and see: a person is purified only through words of Torah. Therefore words of Torah do not receive impurity, for Torah stands ready to purify the impure. Healing is found in Torah: ‘It shall be healing to your navel and refreshment to your bones.’ Purity is found in Torah: ‘Fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever.’ What is ‘enduring forever’? It remains constantly in that purity and never loses it. He objected: ‘Fear of the Lord’ is written, not Torah. The other answered: ‘Certainly, for Torah comes from the side of might.’ He replied: ‘Does it proceed from there? It proceeds from here: “The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord,” and “Fear of the Lord is pure.”’”
: “Come, eat of my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.”

: “Meanwhile an elder came to him and said: Faithful Shepherd, prepare a table for your Master and the Matron with every kind of delight, fulfilling ‘This is the table before the Lord.’ Until now all delight in the King’s table, as it says, ‘Come, eat of My bread’: the bread of Written Torah and the wine of Oral Torah. There are many delicacies there, the varied flavors of Torah, sweeter than all the foods and delights of the world and of the king.”

: “Rav often said: The World to Come is unlike this world. In the World to Come there is no eating, drinking, procreation, business, jealousy, hatred, or rivalry. Rather, the righteous sit with their crowns upon their heads and take pleasure in the radiance of the Divine Presence, as it says, “They beheld God, and ate and drank.””

: “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel put “We will do” before “We will hear,” six hundred thousand ministering angels came and bound two crowns upon each Israelite, one for “We will do” and one for “We will hear.” When Israel sinned, one million two hundred thousand angels of destruction descended and stripped them off, as it says, “The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.” Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said: At Horeb they put them on, and at Horeb they took them off. That they put them on at Horeb is as we have said; that they took them off there follows from “The children of Israel stripped themselves.” Rabbi Yohanan said: Moses merited them all and took them, for immediately afterward it says, “Moses would take the tent.” Reish Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, will one day return them to us, as it says, “The Lord’s redeemed will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads”—the joy that was upon their heads long ago.”

: “Rabbi Simai expounded: When Israel put “We will do” before “We will hear,” six hundred thousand ministering angels came and bound two crowns upon each Israelite, one for “We will do” and one for “We will hear.” When Israel sinned, one million two hundred thousand angels of destruction descended and stripped them off, as it says, “The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb.” Rabbi Hama bar Hanina said: At Horeb they put them on, and at Horeb they took them off. That they put them on at Horeb is as we have said; that they took them off there follows from “The children of Israel stripped themselves.” Rabbi Yohanan said: Moses merited them all and took them, for immediately afterward it says, “Moses would take the tent.” Reish Lakish said: The Holy One, blessed be He, will one day return them to us, as it says, “The Lord’s redeemed will return and come to Zion with song, with everlasting joy upon their heads”—the joy that was upon their heads long ago.”

: “Rabbi Elazar said in Rabbi Ḥanina’s name: In the future, the Holy One, blessed be He, will become a crown on every righteous person’s head, as it says, “On that day Hashem of hosts will be a crown of beauty.” What is meant by “a crown of beauty and a diadem of glory”? For those who do His will and await His glory. Might this apply to everyone? The verse says, “To the remnant of His people”: to one who makes himself like something left over.”

: “For thus says the high and exalted One, who dwells forever and whose name is holy: I dwell in a high and holy place, and also with the crushed and lowly in spirit, to revive the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the crushed.”
: “Go out and see, daughters of Zion, King Solomon with the crown his mother placed upon him on his wedding day, the day his heart rejoiced.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: I searched all Scripture and did not find that Bathsheba made Solomon a crown. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai asked Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei: Have you perhaps heard from your father the meaning of “with the crown his mother crowned him”? He replied: Yes. It is like a king who had an only daughter and loved her exceedingly. He called her “my daughter,” and continued cherishing her until he called her “my sister,” and then “my mother.” So the Holy One, blessed be He, first called Israel daughter, as it says, “Hear, daughter, and see; incline your ear, and forget your people and your father’s house.” He continued cherishing them until He called them sister, as it says, “Open to me, my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew, my locks with drops of night.” He continued cherishing them until He called them mother, as it says, “Listen to Me, My people; My nation, give ear to Me, for Torah shall go forth from Me, and My judgment I shall establish as a light for peoples.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai rose and kissed him on his head.”

: ““Not because you were more numerous than all the peoples did the Lord desire you.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: I desire you because even when I bestow greatness upon you, you diminish yourselves before Me. I gave greatness to Abraham, and he said, “I am dust and ashes”; to Moses and Aaron, and they said, “What are we?”; to David, and he said, “I am a worm and not a man.” The nations are otherwise. I gave greatness to Nimrod, and he said, “Let us build ourselves a city”; to Pharaoh, and he said, “Who is the Lord?”; to Sennacherib, and he said, “Who among all the gods of the lands?”; to Nebuchadnezzar, and he said, “I will ascend above the heights of the cloud”; to Hiram king of Tyre, and he said, “I have sat in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.” Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yohanan said: What was said of Moses and Aaron is greater than what was said of Abraham. Of Abraham it is written, “I am dust and ashes,” while of Moses and Aaron it is written, “What are we?””

k: volume-ii|913|0|R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Beshalac
quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 1:2: “Moses' prayer arose from his apprehension of God's greatness. Seeing the immensity of His holiness, Moses became utterly humble. Rambam, Hilkhot Yesodei HaTorah 2, writes that when a person contemplates God's works and creatures, he immediately recoils in fear and knows that he is a small, lowly, obscure creature, standing with slight and limited understanding before the One whose knowledge is complete. Chullin 89a says that what is stated of Moses and Aaron is greater than what is stated of Abraham. Abraham said, “I am dust and ashes,” which still possess some substance; Moses and Aaron said, “What are we?”—they considered themselves to have no substance at all. Moses' prayer came from his greatness and holiness: he possessed complete holiness and the highest apprehension, and through this became humble, saying, “What are we?” before the holiness and exaltation of God's divinity. His prayer was entirely supplication, as it is written, “I pleaded with the Lord.” He considered everything he had attained a gift of God's grace. Thus the Midrash at the beginning of Vaetchanan, and Sanhedrin 44a, interpret “The poor man speaks entreaties” as Moses: in his own eyes he was poor and possessed nothing.”
: “Thus says Hashem: The heavens are My throne and the earth My footstool. What house could you build for Me, and what place could be My resting place?”
: “My hand made all these things, and all these things came to be, declares Hashem. But to this one I look: the poor and crushed in spirit, who trembles at My word.”

: “When Shabbat enters, the holy people must wash themselves clean of weekday service. Why? During the week another spirit roams about and rests upon the people. When a person wishes to leave that spirit and enter another spirit, holy and exalted, he must wash himself so that the holy, exalted spirit may rest upon him.”
: “For in six days Hashem made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in Rav Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: ‘Behold, it was very good’ refers to the good inclination, and ‘behold, it was very good’ also refers to the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination really very good? Rather, without the evil inclination, a person would not build a house, marry a woman, have children, or conduct business. So Solomon says, ‘It is a person’s rivalry with his fellow.’”
: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day. It is good to give thanks to Hashem and sing praise to Your name, Most High.”

: ““It is good to give thanks to the Lord.” Adam said: Let all generations learn from me that whoever confesses his transgressions and abandons them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as it says, “It is good to give thanks to the Lord.””

: “Through all six days, this spirit benefits from the upper spirit of the Ancient of all ancients. On Shabbat, once it descends and bathes in the Garden of Eden at night, it delights in bodily pleasure through faith’s meals. It is crowned from above and below, saturated on every side with the crown above and below.”

: “Her face shines with upper illumination, and she is crowned below among the holy people, all of whom are crowned with new souls. Then prayer begins: to bless her joyfully, with a shining face, saying, ‘Bless et the Lord who is blessed.’ Et is precise, opening toward her through blessing.”

k: volume-ii|924|0|Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 8:51-
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 8:51-52
quote: : “Also intend the following, as already explained regarding ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion.’ When Moses ascended the mountain to receive the Torah, he was given a thousand portions of light, represented by the large alef of ‘Adam, Seth, Enosh.’ When Israel made the calf, these were lost through Israel’s sin. He was left with only one of the thousand portions, hence the small alef of Vayikra. Moses himself had not sinned; the loss came through Israel’s sin. God therefore made up his loss from Israel’s portion: the crowns and lights that were Israel’s ornaments, removed at Horeb, were subsequently taken by Moses to replace what he had lost because of them. Every Friday night, however, Moses again receives the thousand portions he lost, as the additional holiness of Shabbat. He then returns Israel’s crowns to them; from these crowns Israel inherits the additional holiness of Shabbat each Friday night.”

k: volume-ii|924|1|Nitzotzei Orot, as reported in Peri Tzad
quote: : “The Zohar likewise says, ‘They are all crowned with new souls.’ Nitzotzei Orot, in the margin, explains that the additional soul means the crowns of the giving of the Torah, which Moses returns to Israel, as stated in Pri Etz Chaim. This is the meaning of ‘Woe, the soul is lost’: Israel lost those crowns after they sinned, when others came and removed them.”

: “An objection is raised: “Would that their heart were always like this”—it was impossible to remove the angel of death from them, for the decree had already been issued. Israel received the Torah only so that no nation or tongue would rule over them, as it says, “So that it may be well with them and their children forever.” Reish Lakish follows the other tanna, for a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose says that Israel received the Torah only so that the angel of death would not rule over them, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings, all of you children of the Most High.” But you ruined your deeds, and therefore, “Yet like Adam you shall die.””
: “I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.””

: “Reish Lakish said: Satan, the evil inclination, and the angel of death are one. He is Satan, as it is written, “Satan went out from Hashem’s presence.” He is the evil inclination: elsewhere it is written, “Only evil all the day,” and here, “Only do not reach out your hand against him.” He is the angel of death, as it is written, “Only preserve his life”—showing that taking it lies within his power.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”

k: volume-ii|927|1|Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 1:3-4
ref: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 1:3-4
quote: : “Everyone thus receives an additional nefesh, ruach and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person should direct his intention so that some of this addition remains with him through the weekdays; if he does so properly, his ways will be set right. He is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends on the intention.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “It is clear and evident that the laws of impurity and purity are decrees of Scripture, not matters determined by human reasoning; they belong to the statutes. Immersion from impurity also belongs to the statutes: impurity is not mud or filth washed away by water, but a decree of Scripture, and the matter depends on the heart’s intention. Therefore the sages said that one who immerses without the required intention is as though he had not immersed. Nevertheless, there is an allusion here: just as one who directs his heart to purification becomes pure upon immersion, although nothing in his body has changed, so one who directs his heart to purify his soul from its impurities—wicked thoughts and evil opinions—becomes pure as soon as he resolves to separate himself from those counsels and brings his soul into the waters of understanding. It says, 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you will be purified; from all your impurities and all your idols I will purify you.' May God, in His abundant mercy, purify us from every sin, iniquity, and guilt. Amen.”

: “Why is this a mitzvah? Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Such was Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai’s practice. On Friday they would bring him a basin filled with hot water. He washed his face, hands, and feet, wrapped himself, and sat in fringed linen garments, resembling an angel of the Lord of hosts.”

: “Moses said before Him: Master of the world, what is written in the Torah You are giving me? “I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt.” He said to the angels: Did you descend to Egypt? Were you enslaved to Pharaoh? Why should you have Torah? Again, what is written in it? “You shall have no other gods.” Do you live among nations who serve idols? Again, “Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it”—do you perform labor and need to rest? Again, “Do not take the Name in vain”—do you engage in business? Again, “Honor your father and your mother”—do you have a father and mother? Again, “Do not murder,” “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not steal”—is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you? They immediately conceded to the Holy One, blessed be He, saying, “Lord our Master, how mighty is Your Name throughout the earth”; they no longer said, “Place Your majesty upon the heavens.” Immediately each became Moses’ friend and gave him something, as it says, “You ascended on high, took captives, received gifts through man”: Because they called you “man,” you received gifts. Even the Angel of Death gave him something, as it says, “He placed the incense and made atonement for the people,” and, “He stood between the dead and the living.” Had the angel not told him, how would he have known?”

: “Antoninus also said to Rabbi: From when does the evil inclination control a person—from the moment he is formed, or from the moment he emerges? He answered: From the moment he is formed. Antoninus said: If so, he would kick his way out of his mother’s womb! Rather, it begins when he emerges. Rabbi said: Antoninus taught me this, and Scripture supports him, as it says, “Sin crouches at the entrance.””
: “When His lamp shone above my head, by His light I walked through darkness.”

: “A lamp burns above the unborn child’s head, and the child gazes from one end of the world to the other, as it says, “When His lamp shone above my head, by His light I walked through darkness.” Do not find this astonishing: A person sleeps here and sees a dream in Spain. No days offer a person greater well-being than those days, as it says, “If only I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me.” Which days are measured in months but not in years? The months of pregnancy.”

: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I placed a quarter-log of blood within you; I therefore warned you concerning blood. I called you the first portion; I therefore warned you concerning the first portion. The soul that I placed within you is called a lamp; I therefore warned you concerning the lamp. If you fulfill these duties, well and good; otherwise, I will take your soul.”
: “On the day Hashem grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil, and the harsh labor imposed upon you—”

: “Rabbi Shimon also said: we learned that Shabbat is an image of the world to come, and certainly it is. Thus the sabbatical year and Jubilee mirror one another, as do Shabbat and the world to come. The additional soul comes from the mystery of ‘remember’ to this Shelter of Peace, which receives it from the world to come and gives this addition to the holy people. They rejoice in that addition and forget every weekday matter, every sorrow and distress, as in ‘On the day the Lord grants you rest from your pain, your turmoil and the hard labor,’ and so forth.”

: “It was taught: Othniel and Jabez are the same person. What was his name? Judah, Simeon’s brother. “Othniel”—God answered him; “Jabez”—he gave counsel and spread Torah in Israel. How do we know that God answered him? It is written, “Jabez called to the God of Israel, saying: If You will indeed bless me, enlarge my border, let Your hand be with me, and act against my harm so that it not grieve me; and God granted what he asked.” “If You will indeed bless me”—with Torah. “Enlarge my border”—with students. “Let Your hand be with me”—so that my learning not be forgotten from my heart. “Act against my harm”—so that I may find companions like myself. “So that it not grieve me”—so that the evil inclination not overpower me and prevent me from studying. If You do this, well and good; otherwise I shall go in my sorrow to Sheol. Immediately, “God granted what he asked.””

: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, “Be stirred, and do not sin.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “Speak in your hearts.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recite Shema, as it says, “Upon your beds.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recall the day of death, as it says, “And be silent, selah.””

: “Then a spirit of soul is added to every individual in Israel. Through that additional soul, they forget all sorrow and anger; only joy is found above and below. When this spirit descends to be added among the world’s people, it bathes in the fragrances of the Garden of Eden, then descends and rests upon the holy people. Happy are they when this spirit awakens.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: All forms of Gehinnom rule over anyone who becomes angry, as it says, “Remove anger from your heart and put evil away from your flesh.” “Evil” means Gehinnom, as it says, “The Lord has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for a day of evil.” Moreover, hemorrhoids afflict him, as it says, “The Lord will give you there an agitated heart, failing eyes, and a pained soul.” What causes the eyes to fail and the soul to ache? Hemorrhoids.”

: “As for the reason water purifies every impure person, I think, on the plain level, that a person should regard himself after immersion as though created at that moment, just as the entire world was water before human beings existed, as it says, 'The spirit of God hovered over the surface of the waters.' Through this image he should take to heart that just as his body has been renewed, he should likewise renew his actions for the good, improve his deeds, and be meticulous in the ways of God, blessed be He.”
: “See, this alone I found: God made the human being upright, but they sought out many schemes.”

: “It is clear and evident that the laws of impurity and purity are decrees of Scripture, not matters determined by human reasoning; they belong to the statutes. Immersion from impurity also belongs to the statutes: impurity is not mud or filth washed away by water, but a decree of Scripture, and the matter depends on the heart’s intention. Therefore the sages said that one who immerses without the required intention is as though he had not immersed. Nevertheless, there is an allusion here: just as one who directs his heart to purification becomes pure upon immersion, although nothing in his body has changed, so one who directs his heart to purify his soul from its impurities—wicked thoughts and evil opinions—becomes pure as soon as he resolves to separate himself from those counsels and brings his soul into the waters of understanding. It says, 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you will be purified; from all your impurities and all your idols I will purify you.' May God, in His abundant mercy, purify us from every sin, iniquity, and guilt. Amen.”

: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name—or, according to another report, it was taught in a baraita: “Sanctify yourselves” refers to washing the hands before the meal; “and be holy” refers to washing after the meal; “for holy” refers to the oil; “I am Hashem your God” refers to the blessing.”

: “A baraita teaches: They said of Shammai the Elder that throughout his life he ate in honor of Shabbat. If he found a fine animal, he said, “This is for Shabbat.” If he found a finer one, he reserved the second and ate the first. Hillel the Elder followed another measure, for all his deeds were for Heaven’s sake, as it says, “Blessed is Hashem, day by day.” A baraita likewise teaches: Beit Shammai say, “From the first day of your week, prepare for your Shabbat”; Beit Hillel say, “Blessed is Hashem, day by day.””

: “Another interpretation: “A man of kindness benefits his own soul”—this is Hillel the Elder. When he parted from his students, they walked along with him. His students asked: Our teacher, where are you going? He replied: To show kindness to the guest in my house. They asked: Do you have a guest every day? He replied: Is this poor soul not a guest within the body? Today it is here; tomorrow it is not here.”

: “Shammai wanted his eating to be a meal of a commandment. He therefore prepared everything for Shabbat and ate in order to leave something better for Shabbat, experiencing in his eating the commandment’s delight of Shabbat. With Hillel, however, Vayikra Rabbah 34 says, 'One who shows kindness to his soul is a man of kindness' refers to Hillel the Elder. He said he was going to show kindness to the guest within his house, asking, 'Is this poor soul not a guest?' Thus, 'He had a different quality, for all his deeds were for Heaven': all his eating was a meal of a commandment. He felt no bodily pleasure, but was like someone feeding a guest and fulfilling the commandment of kindness; he did not need Shammai’s method. Every holy person similarly seeks to make his eating a meal of a commandment.”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”

: “Since this spirit stays with a person, he must guard it. Therefore it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep et Shabbat.’ ‘Shabbat’ is that lower point; ‘et Shabbat’ is this spirit, the extension of that point. When sanctifications and blessings from above are added to that point, its extension becomes entirely radiant and becomes a spirit shining in every direction. It branches above and shines, and branches below and shines. This is what is written, ‘Between Me and the children of Israel’: we share a portion of inheritance together.”

k: volume-ii|950|0|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 204b, pr
quote: : “‘Sanctifications and blessings’: the marginal gloss identifies them as Chokhmah and Binah. The Zohar means that when the higher mental powers enter Malchut, the additional spirit benefits from them—both the part remaining in Malchut and the part descending to Israel. ‘It divides above and shines’ refers to the portion remaining in Malchut; ‘it divides below and shines’ refers to the portion descending to Israel. ‘Between Me and the children of Israel’: Malchut says that this spirit is between herself and Israel, half for her and half for them.”

: “If you say this praise belongs to him, do not say so: the praise rises to the upper place. Here is the secret. When male and female are prepared together beneath the upper King, that King rises above and becomes filled with every sanctification and blessing flowing below. He becomes full and pours out below. This is the upper King’s desire: to be filled with sanctifications and blessings and pour them downward.”

k: volume-ii|952|0|Ḥayyim Vital, gloss on Zohar II 145b, pr
quote: : “On ‘it becomes filled with all sanctifications’: the marginal gloss explains, ‘from Chokhmah’; and on ‘with all blessings,’ it explains, ‘Binah.’”

: “Rabbi Abba said: blessing is prepared for those upper days, which are blessed from this day. This day fills Ze‘ir Anpin’s head with dew descending from the Holy Ancient One, concealed beyond all. Three times from Shabbat’s entrance, He casts it upon the Field of Holy Apples, so that all may be blessed together.”

: “The inheritances were exchanged in another manner: the daughter inherited Father’s inheritance through the ascent of this holy Name, and she too is called Holiness, Wisdom. The son inherited Mother’s inheritance and is called Holies, for he takes all those upper sanctifications and gathers them to himself. Afterward he gives them and brings them to the bride.”
: “For Hashem gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”

: “Rather, Rav Ashi said: You can recognize this from a great scholar’s stating a teaching and a law transmitted to Moses at Sinai subsequently being found to agree with it. But perhaps he chanced upon the truth, like a blind person finding an opening? Does he not also give a reason for his teaching?”

: “Regarding the statement, “Since the Temple was destroyed, although prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages”: Rashi explains that it was taken from prophets who were not Sages. This may be challenged, since Nedarim 38a says that the Holy One, blessed be He, rests His Presence only upon someone wise, mighty, and wealthy. Some answer that uninterrupted indwelling requires wisdom, but prophecy for a particular mission, such as Jonah son of Amittai’s mission to Nineveh, does not. I am not satisfied with that answer. Rather, the meaning is this: Although the prophets’ prophecy, consisting of appearances and visions, was taken away, the Sages’ prophecy, which comes through wisdom, was not taken away. They know the truth through the holy spirit within them. For a time He may rest His Presence even upon pious people who are not Sages. There the proof is drawn from Moses, whose prophecy never ceased; this is the meaning of “rests His Presence.” Although wealth is also proved from Jonah, Jonah too was a prophet without interruption, even though he was sent only to Nineveh.”
: “'Wisdom': what a person hears from others and learns. 'Understanding': discerning something in one’s own heart from things one has learned. 'Knowledge': the holy spirit.”

: “'The Lord gives wisdom' is the Written Torah, strength and power for Israel. 'The Lord blesses'—blessing means abundant flow in Oral Torah. Sefer HaBahir likewise asks why the Torah begins with bet: as the beginning of berakhah, blessing. How do we know Torah is called blessing? 'Full of the Lord’s blessing; inherit sea and south'; sea means Torah, as in 'Broader than the sea.' This concerns Oral Torah, which is longer than the earth, whereas the Written Torah’s letters are counted and numbered, possess a measure, and cannot receive even one additional letter. This blessing comes only through peace, as the conclusion of Berakhot says, 'Torah scholars increase peace...great is the peace of your children'—read not children but builders.”

: “Why did the Torah begin with bet, as does berakhah, ‘blessing’? How do we know that Torah is called blessing? It says, ‘Full of the Lord’s blessing, inherit sea and south.’ The sea signifies Torah, as in ‘broader than the sea.’ What is ‘full of the Lord’s blessing’? Wherever bet occurs, it expresses blessing, as in bereshit. Reshit means wisdom, as in ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord’; and wisdom is blessing, as it says, ‘God blessed Solomon,’ and ‘The Lord gave Solomon wisdom.’ This resembles a king who married his daughter to his son, gave her to him at the wedding, and said, ‘Do with her as you wish.’”
: “Hashem’s blessing brings wealth, and He adds no sorrow with it.”

: “Similarly, Scripture says, “A poor man and a man of intrigues meet; the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” When a student approaches his teacher and says, “Teach me Torah,” if he teaches him, “the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” If not, “Rich and poor meet; the Lord makes them all”: the One who made this one wise makes him foolish, and the foolish one He makes wise. This is Rabbi Natan’s teaching.”

: “Eleazar ben Poira said to King Yannai: King Yannai, is this the treatment even an ordinary Israelite deserves—and you are both king and High Priest? Yannai asked: What should I do? He answered: If you listen to my advice, trample the Sages. But what will become of Torah? It lies rolled up in a corner; anyone who wishes to learn may come and learn. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak said: At once heresy was cast into him, for he should have said: That may suffice for Written Torah, but what about Oral Torah? Immediately evil sprang up through Eleazar ben Poira: All Israel’s Sages were killed, and the world was desolate until Shimon ben Shetah came and restored Torah to its former state.”

k: volume-ii|964|0|R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Masei 8:
quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Masei 8:1: “After the holiness of Shabbat night appeared in the meal of the Field of Holy Apples, additional blessing and holiness appeared from the dew descending from Atika Kadisha. This is a place so exceedingly high that human comprehension cannot grasp it as manna descending in physical reality. As the Zohar, Yitro, states: on this day the head of Zeir Anpin fills with dew descending from Atika Kadisha, the concealment of all, and casts it into the Field of Holy Apples three times from Shabbat's entrance. Malchut thus receives from a place still higher than Zeir Anpin, the refinement of the attributes, to the point where this has no connection with embodiment in this world. This also explains the giving of the Torah. Torah was given to Israel on Shabbat, but its physical presentation as writing upon the tablets did not take place then. It was given then through voices and lightning, because Shabbat's holiness, from Atika's dew, is above embodiment in this world. On that Shabbat of the giving of the Torah He likewise brought down the dew that will revive the dead. For Shabbat's holiness is a foretaste of the World to Come.”
: “Hashem founded the earth through wisdom; He established the heavens through understanding.”

: “‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the Oral Torah, which is the seventh day. Through it the world was perfected, for it sustains everything. ‘His work which He had made,’ rather than ‘all His work,’ for the Written Torah brought everything forth through the power of the writing that proceeds from Wisdom.”

: “The passage in Proverbs begins, 'The Lord founded earth through wisdom.' Wisdom is the Written Torah; earth means this world’s six thousand years, corresponding to the six weekdays, founded through the Written Torah, as Bereshit Rabbah begins, 'I was God’s instrument of craftsmanship.' 'He established the heavens through understanding': understanding means discerning one thing from another, the Oral Torah. The Zohar explains, 'On the seventh day'—this is the Oral Torah, the seventh day, through which the world was perfected. This is 'He established': perfection comes through understanding, the Oral Torah.”

: “Vav is completed within ten six times, making sixty to raise her from the dust. Every sixty years of that sixth millennium, he strengthens and rises in her levels. In the six-hundredth year of the sixth millennium, the gates of wisdom above and the springs of wisdom below will open, and the world will be prepared to enter the seventh. It resembles a person preparing on the sixth day as the sun declines to enter Shabbat. So it is here. The sign is ‘In the six-hundredth year of Noah’s life…all the springs of the great deep burst open.’”
: “Through wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.”
: “Through knowledge its chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.”
: “Through knowledge its chambers are filled with every precious and pleasant treasure.”
: “God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on it He ceased from all His work that God created to be done.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””

: “When the Tree of good and evil rules—the ordinary realm of purity and the ordinary realm of impurity—the sages, who resemble Shabbatot and festivals, possess only what those belonging to the ordinary realm give them. They resemble Shabbat, which has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.”

: “Rabbi Yehudah says that the blessing is “Who creates varieties of grasses.” Rabbi Zeira—or, according to another report, Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa—said: The law does not follow Rabbi Yehudah. Rabbi Zeira—or Rabbi Chinena bar Pappa—also explained Rabbi Yehudah’s reasoning: Scripture says, “Blessed is Hashem, day by day.” Do we bless Him by day but not at night? Rather, this teaches: Each day, give Him the blessing appropriate to that day. Here too, for each kind, give Him the blessing appropriate to that kind.”

: ““Every day according to its appropriate blessings”—on Shabbat, blessings appropriate to Shabbat; on a weekday, blessings appropriate to a weekday; and on a festival, blessings appropriate to the festival that occurs.”
: ““Every single day”: On Shabbat, something appropriate to Shabbat; on a festival, something appropriate to the festival.”

: “In the Shabbat evening prayer we say, “You blessed it above all days and sanctified it above all appointed times.” “Appointed times” ordinarily means the holiness of the three pilgrimage festivals, whose holiness is also included in Shabbat. The holiness of Passover concerns redemption from Egypt, and its root is found in the holiness of Shabbat, as the Sages said: If Israel kept two Sabbaths properly, they would immediately be redeemed. … Through the Torah and prayer of each day, that day’s food is blessed, for each day brings its own particular blessing to a person’s livelihood. The Zohar, commenting on “They shall gather each day’s portion on its day,” says that a person should not cook food from one day for another. The Mekhilta says on this verse: He who created the day created its sustenance.”

: “Rav Huna said: A person traveling on the road or in the wilderness who does not know when Shabbat falls counts six days and observes one day. Hiyya bar Rav says: He observes one day and then counts six. What is their disagreement? One follows the order of the world’s creation; the other follows Adam’s experience. An objection was raised: A traveler who does not know when Shabbat falls observes one day for six. Does that not mean he counts six and observes one? No, it means he observes one and counts six. If so, it should say, “He observes one day and counts six.” Furthermore, a baraita explicitly teaches that a traveler on the road or in the wilderness who does not know when Shabbat falls counts six days and observes one. This refutes Hiyya bar Rav; it is a refutation. Rava said: Each day he performs enough labor for his subsistence, except on that day. Must he die on that day? Let him prepare two days’ provisions the previous day. But perhaps the previous day was Shabbat! Rather, each day he prepares his subsistence, even on that day. How, then, is that day distinguished? Through kiddush and havdala.”

: “The Divine Presence originally dwelled chiefly in the lower world. When Adam sinned, it withdrew to the first heaven; when Cain sinned, to the second; through the generation of Enosh, to the third; through the generation of the Flood, to the fourth; through the generation of the Dispersion, to the fifth; through the Sodomites, to the sixth; and through the Egyptians in Abraham’s time, to the seventh. Corresponding to them, seven righteous men arose: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Levi, Kehat, Amram, and Moses. Abraham brought it down to the sixth heaven; Isaac, from the sixth to the fifth; Jacob, from the fifth to the fourth; Levi, from the fourth to the third; Kehat, from the third to the second; Amram, from the second to the first; and Moses brought it down from above to below.”
: “Hashem founded the earth through wisdom; He established the heavens through understanding. Through His knowledge the depths burst open and the clouds drip dew.”

: “They were debating in the heavenly academy: If a bright skin lesion preceded the white hair, the person is impure; if the white hair preceded the lesion, he is pure. In a case of doubt, the Holy One, blessed be He, said “pure,” while the entire heavenly academy said “impure.” They asked: “Who shall decide? Let Rabbah bar Nachmani decide, for he said: ‘I am uniquely proficient in the laws of skin lesions and of tent impurity.’” They sent a messenger for him, but the angel of death could not approach him because his mouth did not cease its learning. Meanwhile a wind rustled among the reeds. Thinking it a troop of cavalry, he said: “Better that this man die than be handed over to the royal authorities.” As his soul departed he said: “Pure, pure.” A heavenly voice declared: “Happy are you, Rabbah bar Nachmani: your body is pure, and your soul departed with ‘pure’ upon your lips.””

: “For we learned: Rabbi Yose says: On the garments of builders, a stain on one side is an obstruction to immersion; on an ordinary person’s garments, it is an obstruction only when it penetrates both sides. A saddlecloth should not be more important than an ordinary person’s garment. Who are these “builders”? Rabbi Yohanan said: They are Torah scholars, who devote all their days to building the world.”
: “For in six days Hashem made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore Hashem blessed the Shabbat day and sanctified it.”

: “Someone who conducts himself according to medicine, intending only that his whole body and its limbs be healthy and that his children perform his work and labor for his needs, does not follow a good path. Rather, he should intend that his body be sound and strong so that his soul may be upright in knowing God. A person cannot understand and contemplate wisdom when hungry or ill, or when one of his limbs hurts. He should intend to have a child who may become wise and great in Israel. A person who follows this path serves God constantly throughout his life, even while doing business or having marital relations, because his purpose in everything is to obtain his needs so that his body may be healthy enough to serve God. Even when sleeping, if he deliberately sleeps to rest his mind and body, lest he become ill and unable to serve God while ill, his sleep itself becomes service of the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Concerning this the sages commanded, 'Let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.' Solomon likewise said in his wisdom, 'Know Him in all your ways, and He will straighten your paths.'”

: “A person must subject all the faculties of his soul to reason, as we explained in the preceding chapter. He should always place before himself one goal: apprehending God, blessed be He, to the extent human beings can know Him. He should direct all his actions—his movements, his rest, and everything he says—toward this goal, so that none of his actions is purposeless, meaning an action that does not lead toward this goal. For example, he should intend his eating, drinking, sexual relations, sleeping, waking, movement, and rest solely for his body’s health. His intention in maintaining bodily health should be that the soul finds its instruments healthy and sound, enabling it to acquire knowledge and the virtues of character and intellect until it reaches that goal.”

: “Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and Hashem your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore Hashem your God commanded you to observe the Shabbat day.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “Rava bar Mehasya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: A person who gives a gift to another must inform him, as it says, “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.” A baraita likewise teaches: “To know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you”—the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: I have a fine gift in My treasure house, and its name is Shabbat. I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them. From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: One who gives a child bread must inform the child’s mother.”

: “Moses, after commanding Aaron, the princes, and all the Israelite men concerning everything the Lord had spoken with him on Mount Sinai after the breaking of the tablets, and after placing the veil upon his face, again gave instructions, and the entire congregation—men and women—assembled before him. Possibly this occurred the day after his descent. He told them all about the Tabernacle, concerning which he had originally been commanded before the tablets were broken. Once the Holy One, blessed be He, was reconciled to them, gave Moses the second tablets, and made a new covenant with him that God would go among them, they had returned to their former state and to the love of their bridal days. His Presence would assuredly be among them, as He had originally commanded: 'They shall make Me a sanctuary, and I shall dwell among them.' Moses therefore now commanded them everything he had originally been commanded.”

: “Come and see what was first written: ‘From every man whose heart makes him willing,’ including everyone. God wished the Tabernacle’s work to embrace every side, kernel and husk. Because the mixed multitude were among them, ‘from every man whose heart makes him willing’ was said to include them among Israel, who are the kernel. All were commanded. Later, kind turned toward its own kind: the mixed multitude came and made the calf. Those who died followed them astray, bringing death and slaughter upon Israel. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: from now on the Tabernacle’s work shall come only from Israel’s side. Immediately, ‘Moses assembled the whole congregation of the children of Israel,’ followed by ‘Take from yourselves an offering for the Lord’—from yourselves specifically, unlike the earlier ‘from every person whose heart moves him.’ From where did Moses gather them? Because the mixed multitude were among them, Moses had to gather Israel and set them apart from their midst.”

: “‘Moses assembled’: he restored to them the Tabernacle’s work as before. Rabbi Chiyya said: everything is as stated. The Tabernacle’s work was performed by Israel alone, not the mixed multitude, for the mixed multitude had drawn the Angel of Death down into the world. Once Moses perceived this, he cast them outside and gathered Israel alone. Thus ‘Moses assembled,’ and so forth.”
: “One thing I have asked of Hashem, and that I seek: to dwell in Hashem’s house all the days of my life, to behold Hashem’s pleasantness and visit His sanctuary.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”

: “At the giving of the Torah, the whole camp of Israel was dedicated to the Divine Presence, and every place where Israel dwelled possessed the holiness of the Temple. Only after the corruption was the Tabernacle selected as a particular place for the Divine Presence. Just as the Temple was chosen in the world, Shabbat was chosen in the year, and the priest and those who labor in Torah were chosen in the soul. Wherever a person stands on Shabbat is therefore holy ground, as the Zohar teaches. Thus, “To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you” means: I make you a sanctuary, a place prepared for the Divine Presence. This is the good gift called Shabbat, which He gave to Israel.”

: “At the giving of the Torah, 'I said: You are divine' meant that they would not die. Freedom from the angel of death was also freedom from the evil inclination, since they are one. Song of Songs Rabbah likewise states that hearing 'You shall have no other' uprooted the evil inclination from their hearts. When an Israelite receives the additional soul at Shabbat’s entrance—the crowns from the giving of the Torah that Moses restores to Israel—the inclination is uprooted from his heart. Through keeping Shabbat, a person is guarded from transgression, as Mekhilta teaches; Pri Etz Chayim’s opening to the Shabbat gate says he is saved from the inclination’s accusation throughout the week. This follows 'Who keeps Shabbat from profaning it, and guards his hand from doing any evil.'”

quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 8:1: “This is the meaning of “This is the way of Torah…you shall live a life of hardship.” Although “The Lord's precepts are upright, rejoicing the heart,” that is after someone attains Torah's light, which brings joy into his heart. The way toward Torah, before he attains it, involves hardship: “In Torah you shall toil,” with great exertion, little sleep and little pleasure, as Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 3, explains at length. Amalek came against them with an argument drawn from Torah: “It is vain for you who rise early…who eat the bread of sorrows.” Bread means Torah, as in “Come, eat of My bread”; this is the bread of sorrows attained through pain, great exertion and loss of sleep. “So He gives His beloved sleep”: the beloved is King Solomon, who received the whole of the lower wisdom in a dream while asleep. He was called Yedidyah, and Scripture says, “The Lord loved him.” This is the interpretation of “He cooled you”: he made you cold as water. He used arguments from Torah to say that one need not toil at Torah or live a life of hardship even on the way toward it. Thus the Midrash cites “Cold water upon a weary soul”: he appears to teach a person what is good and beneficial according to Torah. This is the battle above, defiling the sanctuary—the wise heart on the right, God's dwelling place.”

: “This is what Scripture says: “Vanity of vanities, said Kohelet; vanity of vanities; all is vanity.” Kohelet spoke of seven vanities: “vanity” is one; “vanities” is two; “vanity of vanities” brings the count to six; “all is vanity” makes seven. Why? They correspond to the seven days of creation. Solomon said: What was created on the first day? Heaven and earth. What will be their end? “The heavens will dissolve like smoke, and the earth wear out like a garment.” He said: Vanity. What was created on the second day? The firmament. Its end? “The heavens will be rolled up like a scroll.” He said: Vanity. On the third day? “Let the waters be gathered.” Their end? “The Lord will destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea.” He said: Vanity. On the fourth day? The lights, as it says, “God set them in the firmament of heaven.” Their end? “The moon will be abashed.” He said: Vanity. On the fifth day? “Let the waters teem.” Their end? “I will utterly sweep everything from the face of the earth.” He said: Vanity. On the sixth day? The human being. His end? “For dust you are, and to dust you will return.” He said: Vanity. What was created on the seventh day? Shabbat. He looked this way and that, seeking to find a flaw in it, but found only holiness and rest. Rabbi Yitzchak said: Afterward he considered that a person sins on it and incurs death, and said: This too is vanity. Therefore he said, “All is vanity”—making seven.”
: “Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbat day.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Natan says: Why does Scripture state, “Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day”? It says, “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the children of Israel: These are the matters ... Six days shall labor be done.” “Matters,” “the matters,” and “these are the matters” indicate the thirty-nine labors stated to Moses at Sinai. Might someone who performs them all during one lapse of awareness be liable for only one offering? Scripture says, “In plowing and harvesting you shall cease.” I might still say that plowing and harvesting incur two offerings, while all the other labors incur only one. Scripture therefore says, “Do not kindle fire.” Kindling was already included in the general category; why was it singled out? To serve as a comparison: Just as kindling is a principal labor for which one is separately liable, so each principal labor incurs separate liability. Shmuel holds Rabbi Yose’s view, that kindling was singled out to make it merely a negative commandment. For a baraita teaches: Kindling was singled out as a negative commandment—Rabbi Yose’s view. Rabbi Natan says: It was singled out to divide liability among the labors.”

: “Happy is the one who guards a dwelling for Shabbat—the heart—so that the spleen’s sadness and the gall’s anger do not approach it. That anger is the fire of Gehinnom, concerning which it says, ‘Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbat day.’ This is certainly so: whoever becomes angry is as though he kindled the fire of Gehinnom.”

: “Come and see: once Shabbat enters and that furnace is hidden, all fierce fires are concealed and subdued, even Gehinnom’s fire; the wicked in Gehinnom have rest. Everything below and above has rest. When Shabbat departs and Israel bless the fire, all the concealed fires emerge, each to its place. To avoid awakening another fire, ‘Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on Shabbat’ is written, as we have explained.”
: “They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker, who ceases stoking it from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.”

: “Some captive women were brought to Nehardea and lodged in the upper room of Rav Amram the Pious. The ladder was removed from before them. When one of them passed by, light fell through the opening. Rav Amram took the ladder, which ten men could not lift, and lifted it alone. He began climbing. Halfway up, he braced himself apart and cried: Fire in Amram’s house! The Sages came and said: You have embarrassed us. He answered: Better that you be embarrassed through Amram in this world than through him in the World to Come. He made the evil inclination swear to leave him; it emerged like a pillar of fire. He said to it: See, you are fire and I am flesh, yet I am stronger than you.”

: “Place me like a seal upon your heart, like a seal upon your arm, for love is strong as death and jealousy fierce as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of Yah. Abundant waters cannot extinguish love, nor can rivers wash it away. If someone offered all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.”

: “There are three kinds of impurity corresponding to the three impure powers: jealousy, desire and the pursuit of honor. Leprosy-impurity comes through slander, arising from hatred of other people and the impure force of anger and jealousy, the force of Esau. Discharge-impurity comes through desire, the force of Ishmael—illicit cravings and loves. Corpse-impurity corresponds to pride and the pursuit of honor, the root of the serpent’s enticement, “You shall be like divine beings.” From these three impure powers developed the three grave transgressions: idolatry, forbidden sexual relations and bloodshed. Pride’s ultimate expression is, “I shall ascend above the heights of the clouds; I shall resemble the Most High.” Forbidden relations and bloodshed correspond to desire and jealousy.”

: “They undertook a fast for three days and three nights, and it was delivered to them. It came out of the Holy of Holies like a fiery lion cub. The prophet said to Israel, “This is the inclination toward idolatry,” as it says, “He said: This is wickedness.””

: “A baraita likewise teaches: Nine hundred and three kinds of death were created in the world, as it says, “The exits of death”—the numerical value of the Hebrew word for “exits” is nine hundred and three. The harshest of all is asphyxiating illness; the gentlest is the divine kiss.”
: “‘For the Lord listens to the needy’ refers to Israel. Rabbi Yochanan said: Wherever Scripture speaks of the poor, the impoverished, or the needy, it is speaking of Israel.”

: “'If you lie down, you shall not fear' follows 'I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down with none to make you tremble.' The principal peace is from the evil inclination’s war, as in 'There is no peace in my bones because of my sin.' 'You shall lie down with none to make you tremble' means free of the inclination’s turmoil and war. The Midrash therefore interprets not fearing as not fearing Esau and Laban: Jacob’s main fear was that he might learn from their actions, for the leaven in the dough enters the heart from their shells. 'You shall lie down, and your sleep shall be pleasant' corresponds to 'He lay down in that place,' where God showed him that even in sleep he remained attached to God, as in 'Behold, the Lord stood over him.'”
: “A song for ascents. I raise my eyes toward the mountains: from where will my help come?”

: “Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai says: It is neither a day nor Gehinnom, but a fire issuing from the bodies of the wicked themselves that burns them. What is the basis? It is written, ‘You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your own spirit is a fire that shall consume you.’”
: “Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbat day.”

quote: : “Everyone thus receives an additional nefesh, ruach and neshamah, according to the portion allotted to him. A person should direct his intention so that some of this addition remains with him through the weekdays; if he does so properly, his ways will be set right. He is assured that he will not sin, that sins will not come about through him, and that the evil inclination will not accuse him. Everything depends on the intention.”

: “Perhaps you will ask: What reward does one who observes Shabbat receive? Scripture says, “Fortunate is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it: who observes Shabbat against profaning it and guards his hand against doing any evil.” We thus learn that whoever observes Shabbat under hardship is saved from transgression.”

: “Rava said: The teacher was troubled by the word “dwelling places.” What does it teach? Shabbat is a personal obligation, and personal obligations apply both within the Land and outside it; why, then, does Scripture write “dwelling places” concerning Shabbat? … Scripture says, “You shall not kindle fire in any of your dwelling places,” and elsewhere, “These shall be for you a statute of judgment throughout your generations, in all your dwelling places.” Just as “dwelling places” there concerns a court, so “dwelling places” here concerns a court. The Merciful One says: Do not kindle fire.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Tzidkat HaTzadik 218:1: “The inclination is principally desire, as we saw when the inclination first entered Adam, which is why it was through woman, the feminine. The murderous inclination was born from desire, entering the world through Cain, their child, through his craving and desire to inherit the entire world. But the inclination's creation within a person is in desire, which also contains good in longing for Torah. Of this it was said: “I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its seasoning.” Torah seasons it and makes it food fit to enter Israel's camp. Through this the inclination toward anger and murder is also naturally shattered: since a person's only desire and longing are for Torah, he becomes angry only where Torah itself makes him seethe, as in “Those who hate You, Lord, I hate.” “Ten thousand at your right hand” refers to Torah on the right, into which he brings all his longing. On the left, however, Scripture does not say “at your left hand.” Using one's strength and anger for good cannot defeat anger, because one may also come to evil anger. Rather, victory here too comes through Torah: when one desires only Torah, one naturally has no desire for worldly matters and neither anger nor jealousy over them, only over Torah. Its defeat is therefore through subjugation, with the left concealed, subdued and inactive. At the splitting of the sea, when Egypt—the powers of imagination, as explained above in section 205—drowned,

k: volume-ii|1013|0|Tosafot Yom Tov on Mishnah Parah 12:11
