quote: : ““All of these, if performed”: It would have been better to say, “If he performed them,” since there are only two operations here, dipping and sprinkling, and “all of these” is not quite suitable. But the tanna was following the wording of the Mishnah in the second chapter of Megillah. This is my explanation.”
: “The seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph had said. There was famine in every land, but throughout the land of Egypt there was bread.”

: “Earlier authorities wrote that kol, 'all,' applies to at least three. In truth, we find several verses and statements of the Mishnah and Gemara using 'all' even for two. Nevertheless, Bereshit Rabbah’s exposition of 'There was famine in all lands' says: in three lands—Phoenicia, Arabia, and Palestine. They appear to infer three lands from 'all,' following the earlier authorities. It appears that 'all' is indeed three: two extremes and the middle that includes them, the usual reckoning in holiness. Opposite this, the shells have three familiar evil qualities: jealousy, desire, and honor, the three roots of idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.”

: “‘But I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth.’ If it is true, why call it merely ‘inscribed’? And if it is merely inscribed, why call it ‘true’? Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi asked, ‘Did you not know how to answer?’ Rabbi Levi replied: ‘It is inscribed before the decree is issued; it is true once the decree has been issued.’ What is truth? The seal of the Holy One, blessed be He. Our Master said in Rabbi Reuven’s name: It is emet, ‘truth.’ What is emet? Reish Lakish said: Alef stands at the beginning of the alphabet, mem in the middle, and tav at the end, corresponding to ‘I am the first, and I am the last.’”
: “Thus says Hashem, King of Israel and its Redeemer, Hashem of Hosts: I am first and I am last, and apart from Me there is no god.”
: “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Afterward faith spreads, and two children emerge from a single whole in their ways. A son emerges from both: vav of the holy Name. A daughter emerges from Mother’s side: the final he of the holy Name. She becomes complete only with vav, for she is nourished from him. Therefore vav must be written first, and afterward he.”

: “A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me? says Hashem of Hosts to you priests who despise My name. Yet you ask, “How have we despised Your name?””
: “If so, why does ‘Keep My Shabbatot’ imply two? Shabbat eve and Shabbat day are never separated.”

: “Rabbi Eleazar said: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”

: “Rav Adda, son of Rabbi Hanina, said: Had Israel not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah and the book of Joshua, because it contains the arrangement of the Land of Israel. What is the reason? “For with much wisdom comes much vexation.””
: “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things Hashem commanded to be done.””

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Natan says: Why does Scripture state, “Do not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day”? It says, “Moses assembled the entire congregation of the children of Israel: These are the matters ... Six days shall labor be done.” “Matters,” “the matters,” and “these are the matters” indicate the thirty-nine labors stated to Moses at Sinai. Might someone who performs them all during one lapse of awareness be liable for only one offering? Scripture says, “In plowing and harvesting you shall cease.” I might still say that plowing and harvesting incur two offerings, while all the other labors incur only one. Scripture therefore says, “Do not kindle fire.” Kindling was already included in the general category; why was it singled out? To serve as a comparison: Just as kindling is a principal labor for which one is separately liable, so each principal labor incurs separate liability. Shmuel holds Rabbi Yose’s view, that kindling was singled out to make it merely a negative commandment. For a baraita teaches: Kindling was singled out as a negative commandment—Rabbi Yose’s view. Rabbi Natan says: It was singled out to divide liability among the labors.”
: “The Israelites shall observe Shabbat, keeping Shabbat throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.”

: “Within bereshit are trei, ‘two,’ and Shabbat: ‘In the beginning,’ ‘He created six.’ These are two Shabbatot, of which it says, ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat, to make Shabbat,’ and so forth. Shabbat is mentioned twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shekhinah. What is ‘throughout their generations’? Happy is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, clearing out the evil inclination, which desecrates Shabbat. ‘An eternal covenant’ is the Righteous One, upon whom both rest: one to fill him and one to be filled from him.”

: “When the Temple was built, every work performed there came about of itself. The craftsmen began; the work appeared before them, showed them what to do, took form before them and completed itself. We have explained: ‘The house, when it was being built’—not ‘when they built it,’ but ‘when it was being built,’ completing itself. Likewise ‘It was built of whole, prepared stone’: not ‘they built it,’ but ‘it was built’—it built itself. So it is with every holy work: it completes itself.”

: “Bar Kappara expounded: The righteous person’s work is greater than the creation of heaven and earth. Concerning heaven and earth it says, “My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens”; concerning the work of the righteous it says, “The place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem; the sanctuary, Lord, Your hands established.” A Babylonian named Rabbi Chiya objected: “His hands formed the dry land.” “His hand” is written in the singular. But “formed” is plural! Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak answered: His fingers formed it, as it says, “When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and stars You established.” An objection is raised: “The heavens declare God’s glory, and the firmament tells the work of His hands.” This means: Who tells of the righteous person’s handiwork? The firmament. What does it tell through? Rain.”
The pigeon dictum is at Bava Batra 24a:1: a fledgling continues hopping only while its nest remains in view. The Beit Yaakov printing cites 11a.
: “Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day shall be holy for you, a Shabbat of complete rest for Hashem. Whoever performs work on it shall be put to death.”
: “Happy is the person who does this and the human being who holds fast to it: who keeps Shabbat from being profaned and guards his hand from doing any evil.”

: “A person might say he can rely upon this: on Shabbat Moses restores Israel’s crowns from the giving of the Torah, meaning they merit what occurred then, when the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. He might therefore rely upon Shabbat’s holiness. For this reason it says, 'You shall guard Shabbat...those who profane it...': the person must nevertheless guard himself lest the inclination enter. Although someone who keeps Shabbat properly is truly guarded from transgression and the inclination’s accusation, it can still enter his heart and lead him, God forbid, to profane Shabbat.”

: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Everything concerning Shabbat is doubled. Its omer is doubled: “Two omers for each person.” Its offering is doubled: “On the Shabbat day, two lambs.” Its punishment is doubled: “Those who profane it shall surely be put to death.” Its reward is doubled: “You shall call Shabbat a delight, and the Lord’s holy day honored.” Its commands are doubled: “Remember” and “Observe.” Its psalm is doubled: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day.””

: “One may explain 'in all your dwellings' as alluding to your repose. The evil inclination misleads a person into seeking repose from jealousy, desire, or honor. Scripture therefore says not to kindle fire in all your dwellings: do not find repose in the shells’ fire, but in the holiness of the three patriarchs that you merit on Shabbat. It uses 'all' because that expression can apply to three, as Tosafot Yom Tov explains at the end of Parah. We supported this from Bereshit Rabbah’s interpretation of 'There was famine in all lands' as three lands. 'In all your dwellings' thus means all the repose the inclination misleads you to seek from the three shells called fire. Rather, find repose in the patriarchs’ three holy attributes, opposite those shells. On Shabbat, the Daughter is crowned with the patriarchs. This is the allusion in singling out kindling to distinguish the labors.”

: “Why did the Torah begin with bet, as does berakhah, ‘blessing’? How do we know that Torah is called blessing? It says, ‘Full of the Lord’s blessing, inherit sea and south.’ The sea signifies Torah, as in ‘broader than the sea.’ What is ‘full of the Lord’s blessing’? Wherever bet occurs, it expresses blessing, as in bereshit. Reshit means wisdom, as in ‘The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord’; and wisdom is blessing, as it says, ‘God blessed Solomon,’ and ‘The Lord gave Solomon wisdom.’ This resembles a king who married his daughter to his son, gave her to him at the wedding, and said, ‘Do with her as you wish.’”

: “'The Lord gives wisdom' is the Written Torah, strength and power for Israel. 'The Lord blesses'—blessing means abundant flow in Oral Torah. Sefer HaBahir likewise asks why the Torah begins with bet: as the beginning of berakhah, blessing. How do we know Torah is called blessing? 'Full of the Lord’s blessing; inherit sea and south'; sea means Torah, as in 'Broader than the sea.' This concerns Oral Torah, which is longer than the earth, whereas the Written Torah’s letters are counted and numbered, possess a measure, and cannot receive even one additional letter. This blessing comes only through peace, as the conclusion of Berakhot says, 'Torah scholars increase peace...great is the peace of your children'—read not children but builders.”

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: This refers to the evil inclination. Ordinarily, when a person grows up with a companion in a town for two or three years, he forms a bond of affection with him. Yet this inclination grows up with a person from youth to old age, and if it finds an opportunity when he is seventy, it brings him down; if it finds one when he is eighty, it brings him down. This is what David said: ‘All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like You, rescuing the poor from one stronger than he, the poor and needy from his robber?’ Rabbi Acha said: Is there a greater robber than this? Solomon said, ‘If your enemy is hungry, feed him bread; if he is thirsty, give him water to drink’—the bread of Torah, as it says, ‘Come, eat of my bread,’ and the water of Torah, as it says, ‘All who thirst, come to the water.’”
: “When a person’s ways please Hashem, He makes even his enemies be at peace with him.”
: “I will grant peace in the land. You will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will remove dangerous beasts from the land, and no sword will pass through your land.”
: “There is no soundness in my flesh because of Your indignation, no peace in my bones because of my sin.”

: “Rabbi Levi bar Chama said in Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name: A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination, as it says, “Be stirred, and do not sin.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him occupy himself with Torah, as it says, “Speak in your hearts.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recite Shema, as it says, “Upon your beds.” If he overcomes it, well and good; if not, let him recall the day of death, as it says, “And be silent, selah.””

: “'The Lord gives wisdom' is the Written Torah, strength and power for Israel. 'The Lord blesses'—blessing means abundant flow in Oral Torah. Sefer HaBahir likewise asks why the Torah begins with bet: as the beginning of berakhah, blessing. How do we know Torah is called blessing? 'Full of the Lord’s blessing; inherit sea and south'; sea means Torah, as in 'Broader than the sea.' This concerns Oral Torah, which is longer than the earth, whereas the Written Torah’s letters are counted and numbered, possess a measure, and cannot receive even one additional letter. This blessing comes only through peace, as the conclusion of Berakhot says, 'Torah scholars increase peace...great is the peace of your children'—read not children but builders.”

k: volume-ii|1038|0|R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Bereshit
quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Bereshit 15:1: “From God's side, however, “Dominion and dread are with Him.” Zohar III 12b interprets dominion as Michael and dread as Gabriel: one is founded on water and the other on fire, and the Holy One makes peace between them. The actual conflict comes from the human side and opposes peace. This is “He makes peace and creates evil.” “It was good” is not said here because battle and disagreement have begun. Bereshit Rabbah says: even of a division that sustains the world, “It was good” is not said—the firmament was created to divide heaven from earth, meaning soul from body. The body is called earth, as Sanhedrin 91b explains: “He calls to the heavens above” means the soul, “and to the earth” means the body. But from God's side everything is one: He makes peace in His heights. Evil was created only to be sweetened, as Tanchuma teaches. In the Zohar's additions to Balak 206b, Rabbi Elazar expounds “Because you are precious in My eyes, you are honored”: everyone who stands sinful before the Holy One is held in low esteem; after reconsidering and repenting of his sin, he becomes precious in his own right, and the Holy One declares of him, “Because you are precious in My eyes, you are honored.” Through repentance he afterwards becomes very good. This resembles the Baal Shem Tov's parable of a prince redeemed from captivity: he is dearer to the king than the son who constantly remains with him. Thus Berakhot 34b puts “the distant” be

: “When the Tree of good and evil rules—the ordinary realm of purity and the ordinary realm of impurity—the sages, who resemble Shabbatot and festivals, possess only what those belonging to the ordinary realm give them. They resemble Shabbat, which has only what is prepared for it during the weekdays.”

: “We learned: a person should always stir the good inclination against the evil inclination and pursue it. If it departs, well and good. If not, let him occupy himself with Torah, for nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah. If it departs, good; if not, let him remind it of the day of death, to break it.”

: “The school of R. Ishmael taught: If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall. If he is stone, he will dissolve; if he is iron, he will shatter. If he is stone, he dissolves, as it says, “All who are thirsty, come to water,” and, “Water wears down stones.” If he is iron, he shatters, as it says, “Is not My word like fire, declares Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?””

: “Come and see: ‘This is the Torah that Moses set before the children of Israel.’ He set it before the children of Israel, not before the other nations. Hence the recurring expressions ‘Speak to the children of Israel’ and ‘To the children of Israel you shall say.’ May the fathers of the world, Hillel and Shammai, rest in peace: they spoke thus to Onkelos and taught him no word of Torah until he was circumcised.”

: “The Faithful Shepherd said: Hillel and Shammai, you come, one from the side of compassion and one from the side of judgment—Chesed and Gevurah, the levels of Abraham and Isaac—and you are of their lineage. Gather here, you and Hillel’s eighty disciples, and likewise the disciples of Beit Shammai, to the King’s meal.”

k: volume-ii|1044|0|Arizal, teaching preserved in Mikdash Me
quote: : “Another interpretation of ‘it endured’: every dispute pursued for Heaven’s sake will ultimately endure. A heavenly voice declared, ‘These and those are the words of the living God,’ for Shammai’s words, too, have a root above. Although the law does not follow them in this world, they will endure in the future. As the Arizal explained concerning this mishnah, in the future, in the Messianic era, the law will follow Beit Shammai. The words of both are enduring and true; the Holy One, blessed be He, distinguished between them and brought them into agreement.”

: “Although Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagreed about co-wives, sisters, an old bill of divorce, a woman whose marital status was uncertain, a man who divorced his wife and then lodged with her at an inn, silver and its equivalent, and a perutah and its equivalent, Beit Shammai did not refrain from marrying women from Beit Hillel, nor Beit Hillel from Beit Shammai. This teaches that they treated each other with affection and friendship, fulfilling “Love truth and peace.” Rabbi Shimon says: They refrained in definite cases, but did not refrain in doubtful cases. … Do not read “in doubtful cases,” but “in unspecified cases”: they would inform one another, and the others would abstain.”

k: volume-ii|1046|0|Maharal of Prague, Be’er HaGolah, Well I
quote: Parallel: Maharal of Prague, Be’er HaGolah, Well I, 5:6: “He says, “masters of assemblies.” This means that the sages’ opinions cannot all take one form. Differences between them are unavoidable because their intellects differ. Every single thing necessarily has more than one aspect. Even if it is impure, it must have some aspect tending toward purity; likewise, even if pure, it must have some aspect tending toward impurity. Human intellects differ, and all cannot follow one path, as will be explained. Each therefore receives one aspect according to the distinctive character of his intellect. For this reason they are called “masters of assemblies”: they sit in assemblies and occupy themselves with Torah. Although their intellects differ, they nonetheless assemble together; when they assemble, all the differing opinions are present among them.”
: “One thing I have asked of Hashem, and that I seek: to dwell in Hashem’s house all the days of my life, to behold Hashem’s pleasantness and visit His sanctuary.”

: “When God wished to create the world, He looked into Torah and created it. He contemplated the holy Name, the entirety of Torah, and established the world. The world was established through three aspects: wisdom, understanding and knowledge. Wisdom: ‘The Lord founded earth through wisdom.’ Understanding: ‘He established heaven through understanding.’ Knowledge: ‘Through His knowledge the depths were split.’ All sustain the world. Through these three the Tabernacle was built: ‘I filled him with God’s spirit, with wisdom, understanding and knowledge.’”
: “Hashem founded the earth through wisdom; He established the heavens through understanding.”

: ““Wisdom built her house”—this is the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, who created the entire world through wisdom. “She hewed its seven pillars”—these are the seven days of Creation. “She slaughtered her meat, mixed her wine, and also arranged her table”—these are the seas, rivers, and all the world’s needs. “She sent her maidens to call”—these are Adam and Eve.”
: “Through wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is established.”
: “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.”

: “Likewise, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul, casts it into the body, and judges them together, as it says, “He summons the heavens above and the earth to judge His people.” “He summons the heavens above”—this is the soul. “And the earth to judge His people”—this is the body.”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”

: “Scripture specifies these six upper days: ‘Yours, Lord, are greatness, might and beauty,’ and so forth. ‘For all’ is the Righteous One; ‘in heaven’ is Tiferet; ‘and on earth’ is the Congregation of Israel. The Targum renders it ‘which unites heaven and earth’: the foundation of the world, called All, unites Tiferet, called heaven, with the earth, called the Congregation of Israel.”

: “Vav is completed within ten six times, making sixty to raise her from the dust. Every sixty years of that sixth millennium, he strengthens and rises in her levels. In the six-hundredth year of the sixth millennium, the gates of wisdom above and the springs of wisdom below will open, and the world will be prepared to enter the seventh. It resembles a person preparing on the sixth day as the sun declines to enter Shabbat. So it is here. The sign is ‘In the six-hundredth year of Noah’s life…all the springs of the great deep burst open.’”
: “Now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you? Only to fear Hashem your God, to walk in all His ways, to love Him, and to serve Hashem your God with all your heart and all your soul.”

: “‘Before human beings’: through this craftsmanship made by this light, human beings endure in the world; it sustains them. Although it is concealed, through it people endure in this world. ‘You have made’ refers to this world’s craftsmanship, through which everything was made by reckoning. The Tabernacle’s craftsmanship is likewise patterned after the world’s craftsmanship, as we explained.”

: “Rabbi Abba said: we learned that wherever holiness rests, blessing is not withheld, even when something is counted. Rabbi Eleazar agreed. He then asked: Israel are holy and come from holiness, as in ‘Israel is holiness to the Lord’ and ‘You shall be holy, for I am holy.’ Why, when David counted Israel, did a plague strike them? He answered: because he did not receive their shekels as ransom. Thus ‘Each shall give the Lord a ransom for his soul when they are counted, so that no plague comes upon them.’ Holiness must give a holy ransom, and that ransom was not received from them. Come and see: Israel are holy and stand beyond counting. Hence a ransom must be taken from them: the ransom is counted, while they themselves are not counted.”

: “Rabbi Simon said: Light is mentioned here five times, corresponding to the five books of the Torah. ‘God said, Let there be light’ corresponds to Genesis, with which the Holy One, blessed be He, occupied Himself in creating His world. ‘And there was light’ corresponds to Exodus, in which Israel emerged from darkness into light. ‘God saw that the light was good’ corresponds to Leviticus, which is filled with many laws. ‘God separated the light from the darkness’ corresponds to Numbers, which distinguishes those who left Egypt from those who entered the Land. ‘God called the light day’ corresponds to Deuteronomy, which is filled with many laws. The companions objected to Rabbi Simon: ‘But Leviticus is already filled with many laws!’ He replied: ‘Deuteronomy repeats a matter as well.’”
: “Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.”

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Tzidkat HaTzadik 196:1: “But from God's side, “The first of His produce” means that the fruit and harvest He desired in planting the world are Israel's souls, which contain the whole Torah. Within them, however, it is concealed, and Torah explains it. Thus, for someone who has attained completeness, love of Israel comes first, since they are the essence and root of Torah. Torah then follows, to explain and understand the depths hidden in each individual soul of Israel.”
: “These are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of the Testimony, recorded at Moses’ command, the work of the Levites under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”

: “Every Jew is distinguished and elevated in some particular respect in which no other Jew is exactly like him. The root of Israel’s souls is the Torah. The six hundred thousand of the wilderness generation derive from the Written Torah; therefore the Midrash says that, had even one been missing, the Torah could not have been given. A letter would have been missing, and a Torah scroll is invalid without a letter; even the tip of a yod is indispensable. This is why they were counted. The Zohar calls them the Torah’s hosts, for that number of souls encompasses the whole Torah. The souls in each later generation, descended from the wilderness generation, derive from that generation’s new revelations in Oral Torah, which flows from Written Torah like the moon receiving from the sun. Their total is six hundred thousand, the wilderness generation’s number and the root of all later souls. Thus Kohelet Rabbah says that no generation has fewer than six hundred thousand. On seeing a multitude of Israel one therefore blesses “the Knower of secrets,” since their minds differ, and such a multitude is no fewer than six hundred thousand. Each individual’s understanding accords with his own root in Torah.”
: “These are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of the Testimony, recorded at Moses’ command, the work of the Levites under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”

: “But when that verse was written, it concerned the Tabernacle! We find that the Tabernacle is called a sanctuary, and the sanctuary is called a tabernacle. Otherwise, consider Rav Yehuda’s teaching in Shmuel’s name: Peace-offerings slaughtered before the doors of the Temple hall are opened are invalid, as it says, “He shall slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting”—when its doors are open, not when they are closed. But that verse was written about the Tabernacle! Rather, we find that the sanctuary is called a tabernacle and the Tabernacle is called a sanctuary. That the sanctuary is called a tabernacle is understandable, for it says, “I will place My tabernacle among you.” But where is the Tabernacle called a sanctuary? If from “The Kohathites, bearers of the sanctuary, shall travel, and they shall erect the Tabernacle before they arrive,” that verse concerns the Ark. Rather, it is from “They shall make Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.””

: “Another interpretation: ‘The Tabernacle of Testimony.’ Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: ‘Testimony’ means Torah, as it says, ‘These are the testimonies, statutes, and ordinances.’ This is like a king who had a daughter, built her a palace, and placed her within seven halls. He proclaimed, ‘Anyone who comes against my daughter is regarded as coming against me.’ So the Tabernacle is called by two names: ‘the Tabernacle of Testimony,’ referring to Torah, and elsewhere ‘the Tabernacle of the Lord.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, says: ‘If a person dishonors My daughter, it is as though he dishonors Me. If someone enters a synagogue and dishonors My Torah, it is as though he has risen up and dishonored My glory.’”
: “The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was an unassuming man who dwelt in tents.”

: “Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said: Why are tents placed beside streams, as it is written, “Like streams stretched out, like gardens by a river, like tents planted”? To teach you: just as streams bring a person up from impurity to purity, so tents bring a person from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit.”
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 16a:1:2: ““Tents likewise”: houses of study. The expression “planting” can apply to tents, as it says, “He shall plant his royal tents.””

: “Another interpretation of “Be attentive and hear, Israel”: Wear yourselves down for words of Torah. This accords with Reish Lakish’s teaching: From where do we learn that words of Torah endure only in one who sacrifices his life for them? It says, “This is the Torah: a person who dies in a tent.””
Commentary: Rashi on Berakhot 63b:14:1: ““Wear yourselves down”: they also interpret “be attentive” as “make”—make yourselves crushed, taking pains over words of Torah.”
: “This is the law: when a person dies in a tent, everyone who enters the tent and everything within the tent shall be impure for seven days.”

: “This is Torah’s way: eat bread with salt, drink water by measure, sleep upon the ground, live a life of hardship, and labor in Torah. If you do so, “Happy are you, and it is good for you”—happy are you in this world, and it is good for you in the World to Come.”

: “What is “She shall be brought to the king”? This is Moses, who is called king, as it is written, “There was a king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.” “She shall be brought”—they brought the Tabernacle to him. “Virgins following her, her companions”—these are Israel, called virgins, as it is written, “A locked garden is my sister, my bride; a locked fountain, a sealed spring.” “Her companions”—they are the companions of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “For my brothers and companions, let me speak peace within you.” “Brought to you”—on the day the Tabernacle was completed they brought it to him. Therefore it says, “They brought the Tabernacle to Moses.””
: “Until I find a place for Hashem, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob.”

: “Rabbi Chelbo said in Rav Huna’s name: The God of Abraham helps anyone who establishes a fixed place for his prayer. When that person dies, people say of him, “What a humble man, what a devoted man, one of our father Abraham’s disciples!” How do we know that Abraham established a place? It says, “Abraham arose early in the morning to the place where he had stood.” “Standing” means prayer, as it says, “Pinchas stood and prayed.””
: “Abraham rose early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before Hashem.”
: “Remember Hashem your God, for He is the One who gives you strength to acquire wealth, in order to uphold His covenant that He swore to your ancestors, as it is today.”
: “Thus says Hashem, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am Hashem your God, who teaches you for your benefit and guides you along the way you should walk.”

: “R. Elazar said: Every person was created for toil, as it says, “A human being is born to toil.” I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth or for manual labor. When it says, “For his mouth compels him,” you must conclude that he was created for toil of the mouth. But I still do not know whether this means toil in Torah or toil in conversation. When it says, “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” you must conclude that he was created for toil in Torah. This is what Rava said: All bodies must labor; fortunate is the one who merits laboring in Torah.”
Commentary: Rashi on Sanhedrin 99b:2:1: ““Burdened with toil”—that is, all bodies were created for labor.”

: “A baraita teaches: “When you sit in your house” excludes a person occupied with a commandment; “when you travel on the way” excludes a bridegroom. Accordingly, they said: One marrying a virgin is exempt from Shema, whereas one marrying a widow is obligated. How is this derived? Rav Pappa said: It is like a journey. Just as the journey is voluntary, so the obligation applies to voluntary activity. But could the verse not be speaking of a journey to perform a commandment, while still requiring Shema? If so, Scripture could have said simply “when sitting and traveling.” Why say “when you sit and when you travel”? You are obligated during your own sitting and traveling, but exempt while engaged in a commandment.”

k: volume-ii|1077|0|R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 5:1
quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 5:1: “There are likewise Torah scholars entirely free for Torah, bearers of Torah's burdens. Ra'aya Meheimna at the beginning of Tzav 29b calls Torah scholars children of the King and Queen, called Sabbaths. Others do not attain this and must work for food—as Kiddushin 82a says, “I worsened my deeds and deprived myself of my livelihood.” Yet whenever they have free time they immediately return to their service and study Torah. They are called those who grasp Torah. Even in their work, their intention is for Heaven: to establish times for Torah and raise children who are Torah scholars; they are called supporters of those who grasp Torah. Jeremiah rebuked the priests, who were free solely for Torah and ought constantly to have the blessed divine name before them, as in the future when everyone points with his finger, as the end of Taanit describes. “They did not say: Where is the Lord?” Had they conducted themselves properly, God would constantly have been before them. Of those who grasp Torah, who also engage in worldly affairs yet hold to Torah whenever free, he said: “They did not know Me.” They must at least attain knowledge through faith. When a person takes to heart in complete faith that the King of kings stands over him and sees his actions, fear immediately comes upon him, as Rema explains at the beginning of Orach Chaim. Why, then, “did they not know Me”? They should at least attain knowledge through faith, as Ra'aya Meh
: “Do not build a house, sow seed, or plant a vineyard, nor shall you own one. Instead, live in tents all your days, so that you may live many days upon the land where you dwell as strangers.”
: “These are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of the Testimony, recorded at Moses’ command, the work of the Levites under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”

: “Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Even someone praying alone on Friday evening must recite “The heavens and the earth were completed.” For Rav Hamnuna said: Whoever prays on Friday evening and recites this passage is regarded by Scripture as though he became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation. It says vaykhullu, “were completed”; read it as vaykhallu, “they completed.” Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we learn that speech is comparable to action? From “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.””

quote: : “The Gemara says: Whoever prays on Friday night and recites “The heavens and the earth were completed” is regarded by Scripture as though he had become a partner with the Holy One in the work of Creation. Do not read vayekhullu, “they were completed,” but vayekhallu, “they completed.” The holy Shelah’s teaching is well known: wherever the Sages say “Do not read,” they are not correcting the biblical verse. Rather, one cannot truly read it in the written way until one first reads it according to the exposition; only then can it be read as written.”

: “Come and see: when all the craftsmen began their craftsmanship, the very work they began completed itself. They began, and it completed the work—actually itself. How do we know? ‘All the work of the Tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed.’”

: “Rabbi Elazar said: Ordinarily, a flesh-and-blood king issues a decree. If he wishes to fulfill it, he does; otherwise he has others fulfill it. The Holy One, blessed be He, is different: He issues a decree and fulfills it first, as it is written, “Rise before gray hair, honor an elder’s presence, and fear your God; I am the Lord.” I am the One who first fulfilled the commandment of rising before an elder.”

: “What do the people of faith say? ‘If the Lord desires us, He will give it to us.’ Once a person labors toward God with the heart’s desire, He asks of us only the heart, and that they guard that holy mark, as in ‘Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever.’”

: “Rabbi Berekhya, Rabbi Chiyya, and the sages there said in Rabbi Yehudah’s name: No day passes without the Holy One, blessed be He, originating a halakhah in the heavenly court. What is the scriptural basis? ‘Listen closely to the trembling of His voice and the utterance that issues from His mouth.’ ‘Utterance’ means Torah, as it says, ‘You shall meditate upon it day and night.’ Abraham knew even those halakhot.”

: “Rav said: Our father Abraham observed the entire Torah, as it says, “Because Abraham listened to My voice,” and so forth. Rav Shimi bar Hiyya said to Rav: Perhaps this means the seven commandments? But there was circumcision as well! Perhaps it means the seven commandments and circumcision? He answered: If so, why does Scripture say, “My commandments and My teachings”? Rav, or according to others Rav Ashi, said: Our father Abraham observed even eruv tavshilin, as it says, “My teachings”—one is the Written Torah and one the Oral Torah.”

: “What is the source for these laws? Shmuel said: Scripture states, “Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it”—remember it in view of another day that may cause it to be forgotten. Why institute the cooked-food eruv? Rava said: So that a person will select a fine portion for Shabbat and a fine portion for the festival. Rav Ashi said: So that people will say, “One may not bake on a festival even for Shabbat without prior preparation; certainly not for a weekday.” The Mishnah teaches that one prepares a cooked dish before the festival and relies on it for Shabbat. This is clear according to Rav Ashi’s reason: it must be before the festival rather than on it. But according to Rava, why specifically before the festival? Why not on the festival itself? Indeed, that would suffice for his stated purpose, but the earlier preparation is required lest a person neglect it.”

: “The world was created through the Written Torah, as Bereshit Rabbah begins, 'I was His instrument of craftsmanship.' 'In His goodness He renews creation every day' refers to the new halakhah God introduces each day in the heavenly court, as Bereshit Rabbah 49 states. During the weekdays God was occupied with the Tabernacle’s work, for the entire world was created as a dwelling for the Divine Presence below. Shabbat then came, and He commanded Israel, 'Rest on Shabbat as I rested.' He commanded them likewise to occupy themselves during the weekdays with the Tabernacle’s work: renewal of Oral Torah’s laws was entrusted to the sages, and even God listens to the earthly court. Torah scholars are therefore called builders, occupied in building the world.”

: “For we learned: Rabbi Yose says: On the garments of builders, a stain on one side is an obstruction to immersion; on an ordinary person’s garments, it is an obstruction only when it penetrates both sides. A saddlecloth should not be more important than an ordinary person’s garment. Who are these “builders”? Rabbi Yohanan said: They are Torah scholars, who devote all their days to building the world.”

: “Bar Kappara expounded: The righteous person’s work is greater than the creation of heaven and earth. Concerning heaven and earth it says, “My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens”; concerning the work of the righteous it says, “The place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem; the sanctuary, Lord, Your hands established.” A Babylonian named Rabbi Chiya objected: “His hands formed the dry land.” “His hand” is written in the singular. But “formed” is plural! Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak answered: His fingers formed it, as it says, “When I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and stars You established.” An objection is raised: “The heavens declare God’s glory, and the firmament tells the work of His hands.” This means: Who tells of the righteous person’s handiwork? The firmament. What does it tell through? Rain.”
: “You will bring them and plant them upon the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem—the sanctuary, my Lord, that Your hands established.”
: “You will bring them and plant them upon the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem—the sanctuary, my Lord, that Your hands established.”
: “The heavens recount God’s glory, and the firmament declares His handiwork.”

: “Rava said: Length of life, children, and livelihood depend on mazal rather than merit. After all, Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both righteous sages: when either prayed, rain came. Yet Rav Chisda lived ninety-two years, while Rabbah lived forty. Rav Chisda’s household celebrated sixty weddings; Rabbah’s suffered sixty bereavements. At Rav Chisda’s house, fine flour was available even for the dogs, and they did not want it. At Rabbah’s house, there was not even enough barley bread for the people.”
: “My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens. When I summon them, they stand together.”
: “You will bring them and plant them upon the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem—the sanctuary, my Lord, that Your hands established.”

: “Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Even someone praying alone on Friday evening must recite “The heavens and the earth were completed.” For Rav Hamnuna said: Whoever prays on Friday evening and recites this passage is regarded by Scripture as though he became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation. It says vaykhullu, “were completed”; read it as vaykhallu, “they completed.” Rabbi Elazar said: From where do we learn that speech is comparable to action? From “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.””
: “He touched my mouth and said, “This has touched your lips; your wrongdoing has departed, and your sin is atoned for.””
: “He touched my mouth and said, “This has touched your lips; your wrongdoing has departed, and your sin is atoned for.””

: “‘In his hand was a glowing coal.’ What does ritzpah mean? Retz peh: crush the mouth of one who slanders My children. What does ‘with tongs’ mean? It teaches that there were two tongs. The angel went to take the coal and was burned. He took one pair of tongs to lift it and was burned. He returned and brought a second pair, placed one pair inside the other, lifted the coal, and put it upon Isaiah’s mouth, as it says, ‘He touched my mouth and said: This has touched your lips; your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for’—because Isaiah had said, ‘Among a people of unclean lips.’ The seraph could not take that coal in his hand, but only with two pairs of tongs; yet he placed it on Isaiah’s mouth, and Isaiah was not burned.”
: “There is fire that consumes fire—this is the fire of the Divine Presence. For the Master said: He extended His finger among them and burned them.”
: “I said, “Woe to me, for I am undone! I am a man of impure lips and live among a people of impure lips, yet my eyes have seen the King, Hashem of Hosts.””

: “R. Isaac said: What is meant by “To the wicked God says: What right have you to recount My statutes?” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Doeg the wicked: What right have you to recount My statutes? When you reach the passage about murderers and the passage about slanderers, how do you expound them? “You carry My covenant upon your mouth.” R. Ami said: Doeg’s Torah goes no deeper than his lips.”

: “Rabbi Berekhya said in Rabbi Levi’s name: In two places Israel dealt with the Holy One, blessed be He. At Sinai they acted with their mouths but not with their hearts, as it says, “They enticed Him with their mouths and lied to Him with their tongues; their hearts were not steadfast with Him.” In Babylon they acted with their hearts but not with their mouths, as it says, “For he did not afflict from his heart.” Nevertheless, “He grieved the sons of man”: He brought a man against them, as it says, “A man, an adversary and enemy—this wicked Haman”—and through him cured their wound.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai’s students asked him: Why did Israel in that generation deserve annihilation? He said: You tell me. They answered: Because they enjoyed that wicked man’s banquet. If so, only those in Shushan should have been killed, not those throughout the world! They said: You tell us. He answered: Because they bowed to the image. They asked: Does God then show favoritism? He replied: They acted only outwardly, and the Holy One, blessed be He, likewise acted toward them only outwardly. This is the meaning of “For He does not afflict from His heart.””

: “The Sages taught: “Her husband annulled them, and Hashem will forgive her.” Scripture speaks of a woman whose husband annulled her vow without her knowing it: she still requires atonement and forgiveness. Whenever Rabbi Akiva reached this verse, he would weep and say: “If someone who intended to take pork but actually obtained lamb requires atonement and forgiveness, how much more so someone who intended to take pork and actually obtained pork!””

: “Isaiah uttered the divine name and was absorbed into a cedar. They brought the cedar and sawed it. When the saw reached the place of his mouth, he died, because he had said, “I dwell among a people of impure lips.””

Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Machshavot Charutz 9:7: “All Israel is truly one body and one nation. In the future, when Israel's freedom from pride is clarified through Messiah son of David, Messiah son of Joseph will also live, since he too belongs to that body. Likewise in Egypt, when Joseph guarded himself against sexual transgression, they were all guarded. Exile began specifically with him—he was sold as a slave—even though its central purpose was the refinement of desires, in which he was cleaner than they were and about which he reported their misconduct. Nevertheless, every accusation quickly returns upon the accuser himself, for he is also accusing himself, since he too belongs to the body of the community of Israel. Tanchuma, Vayishlach 2, therefore says of Isaiah, who said “In the midst of a people of unclean lips,” that the angel held a glowing coal: crush this mouth. Through God's spirit speaking within him, Isaiah himself first said, “I am a man of unclean lips.” This was because of the very act of accusing Israel of unclean lips. Otherwise he certainly possessed pure lips. But by making this accusation against Israel he accused himself as well, and that very speech was his own impurity of lips. Punishment therefore began with him, through crushing the mouth.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Nachman bar Shmuel bar Nachman said in Rav Shmuel bar Nachman’s name: ‘Behold, it was very good’ refers to the good inclination, and ‘behold, it was very good’ also refers to the evil inclination. Is the evil inclination really very good? Rather, without the evil inclination, a person would not build a house, marry a woman, have children, or conduct business. So Solomon says, ‘It is a person’s rivalry with his fellow.’”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Chiyya the Great expounded this. Rabbi Abbahu said: From the beginning of creation, the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked, as it says, ‘The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish.’ ‘The earth was waste and void’ refers to the deeds of the wicked; ‘God said, Let there be light’ refers to the deeds of the righteous. Yet I do not know which He desires—the deeds of these or the deeds of those. Once it says, ‘God saw that the light was good,’ we know that He desires the deeds of the righteous and does not desire the deeds of the wicked.”

: “Rabbi Chiya bar Avin said: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday; Rabbi Yoshiyah prayed the prayer for after Shabbat while it was still Shabbat. When Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday, did he also recite Kiddush over a cup? Come and hear: Rav Nachman said in Shmuel’s name that a person may pray the Shabbat prayer on Friday and recite Kiddush over a cup. The law follows that ruling.”
: “Rabbi Zerika said: The two ministering angels who accompany a person testify about him, as it says, “He will command His angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.””
: “For Hashem will be your confidence and guard your foot from being caught.”
: “'For the Lord will be bekhislekha': in your trust. Another explanation: in matters in which you are a fool. This is how I found it in the Jerusalem Talmud, Peah 1:1.”
: “God saw everything He had made, and it was very good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.”

: “Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: Whoever observes Shabbat according to its laws is forgiven, even if he has served idols like the generation of Enosh. For it says, “Happy is the mortal who does this ... who keeps Shabbat from profaning it.” Do not read mehallello, “from profaning it,” but mahul lo, “he is forgiven.””
: “Come, let us reason together, says Hashem. Though your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.”

: ““Like scarlet”—shanim? Should it not say shani, in the singular? Rabbi Yitzhak said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: Even if your sins are like these years, shanim, ordered in succession from the six days of creation until now, they shall become white as snow.”

: “Further, words of Torah become settled only there. There is no light except what emerges from darkness: when this side is subdued, God is exalted above and honored in His glory. Service of God comes only from darkness, and goodness only from evil. When a person enters an evil path and abandons it, God is exalted in His glory. Thus the perfection of everything is good and evil together, afterward rising through good. There is no good except what emerges from evil. Through this good His glory rises; this is complete service.”
: “On the seventh day God completed the work He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all the work He had done.”

: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: A mortal who does not know his exact times, moments, or hours adds some weekday time to the sacred day. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows His exact moments, times, and hours, entered it at a boundary as fine as a hair.”

: “A person should not say: I will not fulfill the elders’ commandments, since they are not from the Torah. The Holy One, blessed be He, says: No, My child! Fulfill everything they decree upon you, as it says, “According to the Torah that they instruct you.” Why? They decree even upon Me, as it says, “You will decree a matter, and it will be established for you.” Know this from Jacob: When he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh, “he placed Ephraim before Manasseh.” He put the younger before the elder, and his decree was fulfilled. When? At the princes’ offerings: Ephraim’s tribe offered first, as it says, “On the seventh day, the prince of the children of Ephraim”; “On the eighth day, the prince of the children of Manasseh.””
: “On the seventh day God completed the work He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all the work He had done.”
: “On the seventh day God completed the work He had done, and on the seventh day He ceased from all the work He had done.”
: “Speak to the Israelites and say: Nevertheless, you must observe My Shabbats, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.”
: “For Hashem will be your confidence and guard your foot from being caught.”

: “A baraita teaches: Rabbi Yose bar Yehuda says: Two ministering angels accompany a person from the synagogue to his home on Friday evening, one good and one evil. If he enters his home and finds a lamp lit, the table prepared, and his bed arranged, the good angel says, “May it be the will of Heaven that the next Shabbat be like this,” and the evil angel answers “Amen” against its will. If it is otherwise, the evil angel says, “May it be the will of Heaven that the next Shabbat be like this,” and the good angel answers “Amen” against its will.”

: “Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah teaches that two ministering angels accompany a person from the synagogue to his home on Friday night, one good and one evil. The good angel says, “May it be Your will that the next Shabbat be like this,” and the evil angel is compelled to answer Amen. These two accompanying angels are the good and evil inclinations, as we explained. The Zohar says that they are appointed to watch all those who observe Shabbat and delight in it properly. The essential purpose of the creation of heaven and earth is Shabbat, “a day of souls, not a day of the body,” as the Zohar says. This is the Omnipresent’s essential will: that a person be occupied solely in serving his Creator and have no involvement in worldly affairs. This explains the Zohar’s “They are appointed.””

: “Beneath this living creature are four blazing seraphim: Seraf’el, Barki’el, Krishi’el and Kedumiyah. These four stand beneath it toward the world’s four directions. They are appointed to watch over all who keep Shabbat and delight it properly. When these four move, sparks of fire emerge from them. From those sparks seventy-two wheels blazing with fire are formed, and from here the river of fire is formed. Thousands of thousands serve that river. These four appointed beings watch over all who delight Shabbat; this living being stands over them, and they journey beneath it for its sake.”
: “This day belongs to souls, rather than the body, for the Bundle of Souls rules. All those above and below stand in a single union, crowned with the additional upper holy spirit.”

: “I kept watching until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His garment was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool. His throne was flames of fire, its wheels burning fire. A river of fire flowed forth from before Him. A thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him. The court took its seat, and books were opened.”

: “One verse says, “A thousand thousands minister to Him, and ten thousand myriads stand before Him,” while another says, “Is there a number to His troops?” There is no contradiction: the verses concern the Temple’s existence and its absence; so to speak, the heavenly retinue was diminished. A baraita teaches: Rabbi says in Abba Yose ben Dosai’s name that “a thousand thousands minister to Him” numbers a single troop, while His troops themselves have no number. Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba interprets “a thousand thousands minister to Him” with reference to the river of fire, as it says, “A river of fire streams forth from before Him; a thousand thousands minister to Him, and ten thousand myriads stand before Him.” From where does it issue? From the living creatures’ sweat. Where does it pour? Rav Zutra bar Tuvya said in Rav’s name: Upon the heads of the wicked in Gehinnom, as it says, “Hashem’s storm has gone forth in fury, a whirling storm falling upon the heads of the wicked.””

: “Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai says: It is neither a day nor Gehinnom, but a fire issuing from the bodies of the wicked themselves that burns them. What is the basis? It is written, ‘You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your own spirit is a fire that shall consume you.’”

: “All three shells—jealousy, desire, and honor—are called fire. Of jealousy and anger it says, 'His wrath burned within him.' This is Esau’s shell, the waste of Isaac, holy fire and severity. Desire too is described as fire: 'They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker'; in Kiddushin 81 it emerged like a pillar of fire, and he said, 'See that you are fire.' This is Ishmael’s shell, the waste of Abraham’s holy kindness. Love also is described through 'Many waters cannot extinguish love' and 'Its sparks are sparks of fire'; its waste, foreign cravings and loves, are likewise called fire. As for pride, fire’s nature is known to rise upward.”
: “A river flows out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it separates into four headwaters.”

: “Rabbi Yochanan said in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: What does “Happy are you who sow beside every water, sending forth the foot of ox and donkey” mean? Whoever occupies himself with Torah and acts of kindness merits the inheritance of two tribes. It says, “Happy are you who sow”: sowing means charity, as it says, “Sow for yourselves in righteousness and reap according to kindness.” Water means Torah, as it says, “Let everyone who thirsts come to the water.””

: “The Sages taught: “You shall place”—vesamtem—may be read sam tam, a perfect medicine. Torah is compared to a life-giving medicine. A man struck his son a severe blow, placed a dressing upon the wound, and told him: My son, while this dressing remains on your wound, eat what gives you pleasure, drink what gives you pleasure, and bathe in hot or cold water without fear. If you remove it, the wound will develop sores. So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: My children, I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning. If you occupy yourselves with Torah, you will not be delivered into its hand, as it says, “If you do well, will there not be uplift?” If you do not occupy yourselves with Torah, you will be delivered into its hand, as it says, “Sin crouches at the doorway.” Moreover, its entire concern is with you, as it says, “Its desire is toward you.” If you wish, however, you can rule over it, as it says, “You shall rule over it.””

: “R. Samuel bar Nahmani said in R. Yonatan’s name: The evil inclination incites a person in this world and testifies against him in the World to Come, as it says, “One who pampers his servant from youth will have him become a manon in the end.” In R. Hiyya’s Atbach cipher, a witness is called manon.”

: “The evil inclination was created for good; a person corrupts it and makes it evil. Its roots are jealousy, desire, and honor, all of which are also needed in holiness. Jealousy appears in “The rivalry of scholars increases wisdom.” Concerning desire, the Midrash HaNeelam says that without the evil inclination there would be no joy in studying a teaching. Honor too has a holy form, as in “His heart was elevated in the ways of Hashem”: a person needs the confidence to know that his deeds affect all the worlds, and thus to walk in God’s ways. This resembles pride, but is holy. Thus the Sages said: When people engage in Torah and acts of kindness, their inclination is in their hands, and they are not in its hands. It was created to be subject to a person, who can direct it toward good, bringing all three of its powers into holiness and using them to serve God. … The Sages interpret “One who pampers his servant from youth” as referring to the evil inclination. Rashi explains that it is a person’s servant: if he wishes, it is subject to him, as it says, “You shall rule over it.” If he pampers it from youth, however, he becomes subject to it, and it becomes a ruler and lord. Likewise, the Zohar interprets “Better is one lightly esteemed who has a servant” as referring to the evil inclination: it can grow arrogant over a person and draw him toward Gehinnom, whereas one lightly esteemed who does not follow it sees it transformed into his servant. It was indeed created to serve him;

: “'One who pampers his servant from youth': the evil inclination. 'Manon': a ruler, as in 'Before the sun, may his name endure.' Likewise, every nin in Scripture refers to a descendant, because the descendant arises in his father’s place to rule his possessions.”

quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Dover Tzedek, Miscellany 4:19: “It is known that attaining wisdom comes through longing and desire. Midrash HaNe'elam in Chayei Sara says that even in the future the evil inclination will not be abolished, for without it there would be no longing for Torah. Thus Kiddushin 30b says: “I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as seasoning.” This means exactly like seasoning that flavors food until that same food becomes very good. The Sages in Bereshit Rabbah interpret “Very good” as the evil inclination: a person places all his longing, wishes and inborn bodily power of desire into longing for words of Torah. There is truly great desire and longing there, to know the depths of its wisdom. The evil inclination then becomes a good inclination, which is also called an inclination—meaning longing in his mind and heart.”
: “Then you will delight in Hashem. I will have you ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for Hashem’s mouth has spoken.”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”

: “It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. No word of Torah, nor even a small letter, fails to allude to upper Wisdom; heaps upon heaps of its secrets depend on each, as in ‘His locks are curled in heaps.’”
: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day. It is good to give thanks to Hashem and sing praise to Your name, Most High.”

: “We learned: before the world was created, no one existed to acclaim and recognize God. When He created His world, He created angels, holy living creatures, heaven and all its host, and humanity, all prepared to praise and glorify their Maker. Yet there was still no glory and praise before Him until Shabbat entered. All became still, and those above and below burst into song and praise. Then He sat upon His glorious throne: then there was someone to recognize His glory and praise it.”

: “Come and see: when this nard sends its fragrance upward, love is bound together and the nard ascends to unite above. All the holy chariots send fragrances upward to be crowned above. These chariots are all called ‘maidens of song,’ as in ‘Upon maidens: a song,’ which we have explained. What are maidens of song? As in ‘maidens without number.’ What is ‘without number’? As in ‘Is there any number to His troops?’ Because they cannot be counted, ‘maidens without number’ is written.”

: “It is written, “Through kindness and truth, sin is atoned.” “Kindness” means acts of kindness, as it says, “One who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.” “Truth” means Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.””

: “Hashem spoke these words to your entire assembly on the mountain, from within the fire, cloud, and thick darkness, with a mighty voice that did not cease. He wrote them upon two stone tablets and gave them to me.”

: “Just as the heavens and all within them praise Him, so the earth and all within it praise Him, as it says, “Praise the Lord from the earth.” Everyone praises the king. Who praises him first? The people of his palace, and afterward the people of the province. Therefore it says, “Praise the Lord from the heavens”—after He has been praised in heaven.”

: “Therefore the high priest places them upon his heart to remember them constantly: ‘Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel upon his heart before the Lord always.’ Everything is thus the mystery of twelve: twelve upper ones hidden above in the upper holy mystery. They are the mystery of Torah and proceed from a single fine voice, as explained. Twelve others, concealed below after their pattern, proceed within another voice, which is stone, as in ‘From there, the shepherd, the stone of Israel.’”
: “Ruth—what does “Ruth” signify? Rabbi Yochanan said: She merited that David descend from her, who lavishly offered the Holy One, blessed be He, songs and praises.”

: “R. Isaac said: Let boiling gold be poured into that wicked man’s mouth! Had an angel not come and struck his mouth, he would have sought to put to shame all the songs and praises David recited in the Book of Psalms.”

ref: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Vayehi Beshalach 7:29
quote: : “Thus, great is faith before the One who spoke and the world came into being. As the reward for faith, the holy spirit rested upon them, and they sang, as it says, “They believed in the Lord and in Moses His servant. Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the Lord.” Likewise it says, “They believed His words; they sang His praise.””

: “Therefore the masters of Mishnah explained: study is not the principal thing, but action. God is concealed within the Torah’s secrets; through what is He known? Through the commandments, which are His Shekhinah, His likeness. As He is humble, His Shekhinah is humility; He is pious and she is pious; He is mighty and she is mistress over all nations; He is truth and she is faith; He is prophet and she prophetess; He is righteous and she righteous; He is King and she kingship; He is wise and she wisdom; He understands and she is His understanding; He is Crown and she His crown, a crown of beauty. Therefore the Rabbis ruled: anyone whose inside does not match his outside should not enter the study hall. This mirrors God: He is the inside and the Shekhinah the outside. He is within; she is without. The outside does not differ from the inside, making known that she is His emanation, without any separation at all: ‘Within and without you shall cover it.’”

: “Another Shabbat remained unmentioned and was ashamed. She said before Him: ‘Master of the world, since You made me, I have been called Shabbat; yet there is no day without night.’ He answered: ‘My daughter, you are Shabbat, and Shabbat I call you; but I now crown you with a still higher crown.’ He issued a proclamation: ‘Revere My sanctuary.’ This is Shabbat eve, which is fear, and fear rests within her. : “Esther was a prophetess, as it is written, “On the third day Esther clothed herself in royalty.” Should it not say “royal garments”? Rather, she clothed herself in the holy spirit. Here it says “clothed,” and elsewhere, “A spirit clothed Amasai.””

: ““On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine”: Had his heart not been merry with wine before then? Rava said: The seventh day was Shabbat. When Israel eats and drinks, they begin speaking words of Torah and praise; when the nations of the world eat and drink, they begin speaking obscenities.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: From where do we learn that song is recited only over wine? It says, “The vine said to them: Shall I leave my wine, which gladdens God and people?” It gladdens people, but with what does it gladden God? From here we learn that song is recited only over wine.”

: “Levi sent Rabbi beer that had been strained thirteen times. He tasted it and found it exceedingly pleasant. He said, “Something like this is fit for Kiddush, and for reciting over it all the songs and praises in the world.” That night it caused him pain. He said, “It afflicts and appeases.””

: “Rav Mattanah derives it from this verse: “Because you did not serve Hashem your God with joy and gladness of heart.” What service is performed with joy and gladness of heart? It is song. Might this mean words of Torah, of which it is written, “Hashem’s precepts are upright, gladdening the heart”? They are called “gladdening the heart,” but are not called “good.” Might it mean first fruits, of which it is written, “You shall rejoice in all the good”? They are called “good,” but not “gladness of heart.””

: ““When he sets his eye upon the cup, he walks on level paths.” R. Ami and R. Asi explained it: One said that whoever fixes his eye upon his cup sees all forbidden sexual relations as level ground; the other said that whoever fixes his eye upon his cup sees the entire world as level ground.”

: “Rav Kahana contrasted the written form tirsh with its reading tirosh: If one is worthy, one becomes a rosh, a leader; if not, rash, poor. Rava likewise contrasted the word “gladden” as written with shin and as read with sin: If one is worthy, it gladdens him; if not, it leaves him desolate. : “They would bring her up to the Great Court in Jerusalem and warn her, as witnesses in a capital case are warned. Act for the sake of His great name, written in holiness, so that it need not be erased in the water.”

: “Rabbi says: Why is the passage about a nazirite placed beside the passage about a suspected adulteress? To teach that anyone who sees a suspected adulteress in her disgrace should abstain from wine.”

: “Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: I too say that not everyone attains light, and not everyone attains joy. The righteous attain light, and the upright attain joy. : “Rather, this is what was taught: all the miracles and mighty acts performed for Israel, when the light of the Holy Ancient shone in His crowns, are carved and inscribed in az, in its alef. : “In Hod is ‘Give thanks to the Lord.’ In the Righteous One is ‘Sing, righteous ones, to the Lord,’ and ‘Sing to Jacob in joy.’ In Tiferet is ‘Praise God.’ Hallelujah means ‘Praise Yah,’ for there is the divine Name. Melody and song correspond to Chesed and Gevurah; shir and blessing to Chokhmah and Binah; ashrei to Keter; praise to Malchut.”
: “On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine, he spoke to Mehuman, Bizzetha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven officers attending King Ahasuerus.”

: “‘On the seventh day’: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: This was Shabbat. ‘When the king’s heart was as though merry with wine’: Rabbi Yitzchak said: The nations have no true well-being, as it says, ‘It shall not be well with the wicked.’ They objected: But does it not say, ‘When the king’s heart was merry with wine’? Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Resisei Layla 17:1: “Song arises from longing; hence the expression “songs of passionate love.” When someone's soul yearns for God and is lovesick for Him, his mouth opens to sing before Him. No songs awaken Israel's love for their Father in Heaven and their union with Him like the Song of Songs. This love is the opposite of love for this world. The Song of Songs is therefore the holy of holies: it belongs entirely to God, completely separated from worldly desires and having no connection with them at all. Such is the measure: the very heart that tastes darkness to its furthest limit and seeks God from there tastes light to its furthest limit, until it apprehends that there is no darkness—“Even darkness is not dark…the night shines like the day.” The same applies to every character trait: where there was a begrudging eye there is generosity, and where there was a bad heart there is a good heart.”

: “Concerning them he says, “May the words of my mouth be acceptable.” May the words of my mouth be made for generations, written for generations, and inscribed for generations. : “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yose was coming from Cappadocia to Lod when Rabbi Yehudah met him. : “Impurity from the dead comes from the pursuit of honor and self-exaltation. : “When Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi died, humility and fear of sin ceased. Rav Yosef said to the reciter: Do not teach that humility ceased, for I am here. Rav Naḥman said to the reciter: Do not teach that fear of sin ceased, for I am here.”

: “'And dread': upon those nearby, as in the statement, 'For we heard how the Lord dried up...' in Joshua 2.”
: “Isaac had come from the approach to Beer-lahai-roi, and he was living in the land of the Negev.”

: ““When she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field, and she alighted from the donkey.” What does “she alighted” signify? : “Did Esau hate blood? Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said: The verse refers to the blood associated with the birthright and the sacrifices. Rabbi Levi said: It refers to the blood of circumcision.”

: “The tenth commandment: ‘The children of Israel shall keep Shabbat.’ The Shekhinah is called Shabbat from the side of the three upper levels: shin, with three crowns—Keter, Chokhmah and Binah. : “Every day that river of fire flows and burns many spirits and rulers. When Shabbat enters, a proclamation goes out and that river of fire becomes still; its rages, sparks and flames subside. quote: : “From the companions: at every Shabbat meal, including the meal after Shabbat, one should declare, ‘These are meals of complete faith.’ On Friday night one arranges twelve loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Field of Apples; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Holy Ancient One come to feast with her.’ This is Isaac’s meal: he is its master and guides it. Whoever delights in it is saved from the birth pangs of the Messiah. At the morning meal one arranges eight loaves and says, ‘This is the meal of the Holy Ancient One; Ze‘ir Anpin and the Field of Holy Apples come to feast with Him.’ It corresponds to Abraham, the pious elder; through his merit one is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. : “A truthful lip endures forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.”

: “Similarly, Scripture says, “A poor man and a man of intrigues meet; the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” When a student approaches his teacher and says, “Teach me Torah,” if he teaches him, “the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.” If not, “Rich and poor meet; the Lord makes them all”: the One who made this one wise makes him foolish, and the foolish one He makes wise. : “One who moves stones may be hurt by them; one who splits wood may be endangered by it.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Whoever says that David sinned is mistaken, for it says, “David acted wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.” Could a sin have come into his hands while the Divine Presence remained with him? : “Rabbi Avin said: What is meant by “In my poverty”? There is no wealth before the One who spoke and the world came into being. Another interpretation: “In my poverty” means through affliction—David would fast and dedicate his meal to Heaven.”
: “Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; provide me with my allotted bread.”

: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in Rabbi Shimon the Devout’s name: A fast that includes none of Israel’s transgressors is not a fast. For galbanum smells foul, yet Scripture counted it among the incense ingredients. Abaye derived this from, “He founded His united company upon the earth.””

: “Rabbi Eliezer again told them: “If the law follows my view, let Heaven prove it.” A heavenly voice declared: “Why do you contend with Rabbi Eliezer, when the law follows him everywhere?” Rabbi Yehoshua rose to his feet and declared: “It is not in heaven!” What does “It is not in heaven” mean? quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Beha'alotcha 10:3: “God therefore showed Zechariah that the menorah, representing the Oral Torah's light, truly comes from God: the olive trees pour out their oil of themselves, as it is written, “Those pouring the gold from themselves.” A person must indeed toil with all his strength, through suffering and loss of sleep, to attain the Oral Torah. Jacob said, “The God before whom my fathers walked”: Abraham and Isaac each served God through their effort. Of himself, he said, “The God who shepherds me,” recognizing that even the effort comes solely from God, who shepherds and guides him. Might means wealth, here words of Torah, as Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 3, says, “I speak of those wealthy in Torah”; Temurah 16a likewise interprets “rich and poor” as wise and foolish. “Nor by strength”: strength means fear of God, as in “Who is mighty? : “The alternative reading explains: the mystery of ‘guard,’ the glory of night, is ‘The Lord’s Torah is perfect,’ the Oral Torah. ‘Moses received Torah from Sinai’: the teaching was explained as concerning Oral Torah. For regarding Written Torah it says, ‘Moses commanded the Levites…Take this book of the Torah.’ This belongs to the Levites, to the one cleaving to the sun and the King from whom it proceeds. Moses illuminated Israel for forty years, the sun in his days; ‘the Lord’s Torah’ is Shabbat eve.”

: “The intention is that the table’s crown stands in the Sanctuary, whereas Torah’s crown is in the Holy of Holies. We already explained that the Holy of Holies alludes to Atika, the attribute Nothing, as in the Zohar: 'Wisdom issues from the place called Holy of Holies.' Concerning this it says, 'Wisdom is found from nothing'—the concealed Ancient One called Nothing. The utterance 'Let there be light' corresponds to wisdom, and its five occurrences of light correspond to the five books of Torah, according to Bereshit Rabbah. This is the yod of the Name, whose upper tip alludes to Nothing. Torah’s crown comes from the supernal crown; the two crowns of the table and incense altar come from understanding.”

: “At that time it will be said of Moses and Israel, ‘Then you shall delight above the Lord,’ with oneg: ayin for Eden, nun for river, gimel for garden. ‘Then Moses will sing’ will be fulfilled: it does not say ‘sang,’ but ‘will sing.’ For the mixed multitude, delight, oneg, will turn into affliction, nega, and likewise for the idolatrous nations, as happened to Pharaoh and the Egyptians, upon whom blistering boils broke out. : “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

Moshe Chaim Luzzatto, Mesillat Yesharim 3:21–23: “The second error, which is worse than the first, is that it so distorts their sight that evil appears genuinely good and good evil. Consequently they reinforce and cling to their evil deeds. It is not enough that they lack clear sight of the evil before them; they also imagine finding compelling proofs and experiences that confirm their evil reasoning and false opinions. This is the great evil that enfolds them and brings them to the pit of destruction. Of this Scripture says: “Make the heart of this people fat, make its ears heavy, and seal its eyes, lest…” (Isaiah 6:10). All this happens because they remain in darkness, held under their inclination’s rule. Those who have already escaped this prison see the truth as it truly is and can advise others about it.”
