Bathsheba daughter of Eliam was destined for David from the six days of Creation, but she came to him through pain. The school of R. Ishmael likewise taught: Bathsheba daughter of Eliam was destined for David, but he consumed her as an unripe fruit. … David continued: Moreover, when they study the four judicial death penalties, they interrupt their learning and say to me, “David, what is the death penalty for one who has relations with a married woman?” I told them: One who has relations with a married woman is punished by strangulation, but he has a share in the World to Come; one who publicly humiliates his fellow has no share in the World to Come. … “And I will be clear of great transgression.” He said before Him: Master of the world, forgive that wrongdoing entirely! He answered: Your son Solomon is already destined to say in his wisdom, “Can a man gather fire into his lap without his garments burning? Can a man walk upon coals without his feet being scorched? So is one who approaches his fellow’s wife; whoever touches her will not go unpunished.” He said: Must that man be rejected so completely? He answered: Accept sufferings upon yourself. He accepted them.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Whoever says that David sinned is mistaken, for it says, “David acted wisely in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.” Could a sin have come into his hands while the Divine Presence remained with him? How, then, do I understand “Why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil”? He sought to do it, but did not do it. Rav said: Rabbi, who descended from David, interprets the passage in David’s favor. “Why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil”—Rabbi says: This evil differs from all the evils described in the Torah. Everywhere else it says, “He did”; here it says, “To do,” meaning that he sought to do it but did not. “You struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword”—you should have tried him before the Sanhedrin, but did not. “You took his wife as your wife”—you had the right to marry her. For Rabbi Shmuel bar Nahmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: Anyone going out to the wars of David’s house wrote a bill of divorce for his wife. It says, “Bring these ten cheeses to the commander of the thousand; inquire after your brothers’ welfare, and take their pledges.” What are “their pledges”? Rav Yosef taught: The matters connecting husband and wife. “You killed him by the sword of the Ammonites”—just as you are not punished for the Ammonites’ sword, so you are not punished for Uriah the Hittite. Why? He was a rebel against the monarchy, for he said to David, “My lord Joab and my lord’s servants are camped in th

: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Israel made the calf only to provide an opening for penitents, as it says, “Would that their heart were always like this, to fear Me all the days.” This accords with Rabbi Yochanan’s statement in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s name: David was not the sort of person to commit that act, nor were Israel the sort to commit their act. David was not, for it is written, “My heart is slain within me”; Israel were not, for it is written, “Would that their heart were always like this, to fear Me all the days.” Why, then, did they act so? This teaches you: If an individual sins, he is told, “Go to that individual”; if a community sins, it is told, “Go to that community.” Both examples are needed. Had only the individual been mentioned, one might attribute the possibility of repentance to his sin’s not being public, unlike a community’s public sin. Had only the community been mentioned, one might attribute it to their abundant pleas for mercy, unlike an individual whose merit is less powerful. Both are therefore needed. This is the teaching of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does “The utterance of David son of Jesse, the utterance of the man raised on high” mean? The utterance of David son of Jesse, who established the yoke of repentance.”
: “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield. Hashem grants favor and honor; He does not withhold goodness from those who walk wholeheartedly.”

: “He began: ‘For the Lord God is a sun and shield.’ The sun is God, and the shield is God. The sun is the secret of the holy Name yod-he-vav-he, in which all the levels rest. The shield is the secret of the holy Name Elohim, as in ‘I am a shield for you.’ Sun and shield together are the secret of the complete Name. ‘The Lord grants favor and glory,’ so that everything may be a single mystery.”

: “Rabbi Levi offered another interpretation: Our father Abraham was afraid and said, ‘Perhaps the sons of those kings whom I killed will gather armies and come to wage war against me.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, told him: ‘Do not fear; I am a shield for you. Just as a shield withstands every sword that strikes it, so even if all the nations assemble against you, I shall fight against them.’”
: “After these events, Hashem’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not fear, Abram. I am your shield; your reward is exceedingly great.””
: “I was with you wherever you went, and I cut off all your enemies before you. I will make you a great name, like the names of the great ones upon the earth.”
: ““I will make you a great name, like the names of the great ones.” Rav Joseph taught: This refers to our saying, “Shield of David.””
: “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield. Hashem grants favor and honor; He does not withhold goodness from those who walk wholeheartedly.”
: “Even when I walk through a valley of death’s shadow, I will fear no evil, for You are with me. Your rod and Your staff comfort me.”

: “What blessing does he pronounce over the table properly arranged and delighted? ‘Then you shall delight above the Lord…for the Lord’s mouth has spoken.’ They all say, ‘Then you shall call and the Lord will answer.’ The upper spirit, called Zekhut El, when that table has been delighted through all its meals, concludes at the last, third meal on behalf of all the earlier ones: ‘Then your light shall break forth like the dawn…the Lord’s glory shall gather you in.’ All the other seventy lights on every side begin: ‘Behold, so shall the man who fears the Lord be blessed.’”
: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”

: “Rather, this is what was taught: all the miracles and mighty acts performed for Israel, when the light of the Holy Ancient shone in His crowns, are carved and inscribed in az, in its alef. The alef pierces darkness and shines in every direction. When the light of alef joins and reaches zayin—what is zayin? ‘The Lord has a sword filled with blood’—He then performs miracles and mighty acts, because alef has joined with zayin. This is song, song from every side; this is ‘Then Moses will sing.’”
: “Then you will delight in Hashem. I will have you ride upon the heights of the earth and feed you the inheritance of your father Jacob, for Hashem’s mouth has spoken.”

: “Rabbi Shimon said: happy is the righteous one who merits ‘Then you shall delight above the Lord.’ It does not say ‘with the Lord,’ but ‘above the Lord.’ What is above the Lord? The place from which those above and below extend, and for which they long: ‘From ayin, where, shall my help come?’ and ‘He reached the Ancient of Days, and they brought him near before Him.’ The righteous ones’ longing and delight is to gaze upon that radiance from which every radiance proceeds and all those crowns extend.”

: “It was taught: ‘The Shabbat burnt offering on its Shabbat, above the continual burnt offering.’ One must direct the heart higher and higher, more than on other days. Hence precisely ‘above the continual burnt offering.’ Of Hannah it says, ‘She prayed above the Lord’—precisely ‘above,’ since children depend upon the holy mazal, as explained. : “The Master of the world’s tefillin are Keter. What is His Keter? The Name yod-he-vav-he: yod is Chokhmah; he is Binah; vav is Tiferet, containing six sefirot; the final he is Malchut.”

: “Come and see: yod initially embraces everything, concealed on every side, its paths unopened, containing male and female together. The upper tip of yod alludes to Nothingness. Afterward, yod brings forth the river that flows and proceeds from it, from which the letter he receives conception. Of this it says, ‘A river goes out from Eden’—‘goes out,’ not ‘went out.’ It therefore must not separate from it; hence ‘My companion’ is written.”
: “Then you will call, and Hashem will answer; you will cry for help, and He will say, “Here I am”—if you remove from your midst the yoke, the pointing finger, and harmful speech.”

: “Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: Whoever makes Shabbat a delight is granted the requests of his heart, as it says, “Delight in the Lord, and He will grant you the requests of your heart.” I do not know what kind of delight is meant. When Scripture says, “You shall call Shabbat a delight,” you must conclude that this refers to the delight of Shabbat.”

: “Rabbi Abbahu said: Moses asked the Holy One, blessed be He, “Master of the world, by what will Israel’s horn be raised?” He answered him: “Through ‘When you raise’”—the passage commanding the contribution when Israel is counted.”

: “The Gemara says that Moses asked the Holy One, “Through what shall Israel’s horn be raised?” He answered, “Through ‘When you raise.’” Rashi explains: take from them a ransom as charity. The biblical passage actually concerns shekels for the Tabernacle and Temple; it does not mention charity to the poor, whose command appears elsewhere. Yet the whole preceding and following Talmudic discussion concerns charity. It cites “He distributed, he gave to the poor ... his horn will be raised in glory,” “He shall dwell on high ... his bread is given,” and “Charity exalts a nation.” This implies that now, without the Temple, charity to the poor also serves as a ransom for the soul, like the Temple’s shekels. Although the ransom would seem only to prevent harm when their heads are raised, rather than itself raising them, our explanation resolves this: raising their horn means returning the crowns, and the shekels’ ransom atones for the calf, because of which the crowns were removed. When this is atoned for through the ransom, the crowns return of themselves and their horn is raised.”

Parallel: Malbim on Isaiah 58:10: “He now says: If, beyond avoiding evil, you also do good out of love for goodness itself and love for God, to the point that “you bring forth your soul for the hungry,” you give him your soul besides what the Torah obligates you to give. You give wholeheartedly, your soul rejoicing in the commandment itself. You give him not only your bread, as in “Share your bread with the hungry,” but your soul too. And “you satisfy an afflicted soul”: beyond feeding his body, you satisfy his soul with generosity of spirit and comforting words. Your reward is then much greater than before. In place of “Then your light will break forth like dawn,” he says, “Your light will shine in darkness”: it will shine suddenly, all at once. The light will not wait for its appointed time, like dawn at night’s end; it will shine for you even in darkness. He adds, “Your deep darkness will be like noon.” Deep darkness exceeds ordinary darkness; nevertheless, it will shine with the great light of noon. Thus your light’s shining will be providential, miraculous, and wondrous, rather than natural. The meaning is that spiritual success will not merely break forth at its appointed time, at the dark night’s end, when dark bodily life ends and the souls’ dawn shines after death. Great light and spiritual deliverance will shine for you during your lifetime too, and you will attain eternal delights even in this world, in the sense of “You will see your world while still alive.””
: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”

: “Jacob says, ‘Then your light shall break forth like the dawn.’ The other righteous say, ‘The Lord shall guide you always and satisfy you,’ and so forth. King David says, ‘No weapon formed against you shall succeed,’ for he is appointed over all the world’s weapons. Happy is the person who merits all this! Happy are the righteous in this world and the world to come, of whom it says, ‘Your people are all righteous.’”

: “‘They traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.’ Water means Torah, as it says, ‘Everyone who thirsts, come to the water.’ Rabbi Yeisa asked: who had given them Torah here? The Torah had not yet been given to them. Rabbi Eleazar answered: they went out into the wilderness to gaze, but God removed the radiance of His glory from there. They went to gaze upon Him and did not find Him. We have learned that God is called Torah: water means Torah, and Torah means the Holy One, blessed be He.”
: “A truthful lip endures forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.”
: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”
: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”
: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””

: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”

: “They also fear heights, and terrors lie along the road. The almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and desire fails, for the person is going to his everlasting home, while mourners move about the marketplace.”
: “When it came to rest, he would say, “Return, Hashem, to the myriad thousands of Israel.””

: “This is the receiving of reward on Shabbat, which resembles the World to Come, for one’s actual deeds during the six weekdays. All the World to Come’s pleasure is enjoyment of the radiance of the Divine Presence, as stated in the end of Berakhot 17a, and likewise for those who merit tasting on Shabbat one-sixtieth of the World to Come. This was the sages’ blessing to Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Chanina: 'May you see your world in your lifetime.' Certainly this refers to Shabbat, when one can attain a foretaste of the World to Come through enjoying the radiance of the Divine Presence. Each person’s attainment of repose on the coming Shabbat, through resting from that labor, corresponds to his labor during the weekdays.”

k: volume-ii|1242|0|R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim
quote: Parallel: R. Tzadok HaKohen, Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim 15:1: “The Pesikta asks: you might say that just as a bride returns to her work when her days of rejoicing end, so too here. Scripture therefore says, “Everlasting joy upon their heads.” A bride is a bride only during the seven days of the wedding feast; afterwards she is no longer called a bride. Israel, however, are always called a bride. This is because on Shabbat they attain an additional soul, a new soul, a soul containing all completeness in the likeness of the World to Come, as the Zohar states. Through this they are called a bride, and the weekdays are the seven days of the wedding feast. On the following Shabbat they attain a still newer soul and become a new bride, and so forever. Likewise, concerning the future, Berakhot 64a says that Torah scholars have no rest either in this world or in the World to Come: “They go from strength to strength; he appears before God in Zion.” Throughout the weekdays they go from strength to strength, as Rashi explains, from one academy to another. On Shabbat one “appears before God”: it is the day of rest, “And when it rested, he would say: Return, Lord.””

: “Come and see: this Tabernacle was subject to counting, and therefore required Moses’ prayer for blessings to rest upon it: ‘Moses blessed them.’ What blessing did he offer? ‘May it be the divine will that blessing rest upon your handiwork.’ Blessings did not rest upon this accounting until Moses bound it to the Tabernacle above. Thus ‘These are the accounts of the Tabernacle, the Tabernacle of Testimony, counted at Moses’ word.’ Had the counting not been performed through Moses, they could not have made this accounting. Hence ‘counted at Moses’ word.’”
: “The third rectification is ‘through blessing’: this is the upper Shekhinah. Of her it says, ‘Bless the Lord, my soul.’ From her a living soul is given within a person.”

: “In Hod is ‘Give thanks to the Lord.’ In the Righteous One is ‘Sing, righteous ones, to the Lord,’ and ‘Sing to Jacob in joy.’ In Tiferet is ‘Praise God.’ Hallelujah means ‘Praise Yah,’ for there is the divine Name. Melody and song correspond to Chesed and Gevurah; shir and blessing to Chokhmah and Binah; ashrei to Keter; praise to Malchut.”

: “This pleasantness is the sweetness proceeding from the world to come. All the lamps shine from the world to come and spread in every direction. The goodness and light of the world to come, from which the patriarchs draw nourishment, are called pleasantness. Another interpretation: the world to come itself is called pleasantness. When it awakens, all the world’s joy, goodness, lights and freedom awaken. Therefore it is called pleasantness.”
: “Then your light will break through like dawn, and your healing will quickly spring forth. Your righteousness will go before you, and Hashem’s glory will gather you in from behind.”
: “The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, growing ever brighter until the day is fully established.”
: “But in the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will heal that wound, as it says, ‘He shall heal the wound of His blow’: He shall heal the wound inflicted upon the world.”

: “How do we know that Ishmael repented during Abraham’s lifetime? Ravina and Rav Chama bar Buzi were sitting before Rava while he dozed. Ravina asked Rav Chama bar Buzi: Is it indeed your teaching that every death described as “expiring” is the death of a righteous person? He answered: Yes. But what of the generation of the Flood? He answered: We mean where both “expiring” and “being gathered” are written. But both expressions are written of Ishmael! Meanwhile Rava awoke and told them: “Young students, Rabbi Yochanan said this: Ishmael repented during his father’s lifetime, as it says, ‘Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him.’” Perhaps they are listed according to their wisdom? If so, why does “Esau and Jacob his sons buried him” not list them according to their wisdom? Rather, Ishmael’s allowing Isaac to precede him shows that he accepted Isaac’s leadership; this shows that he repented during Abraham’s lifetime.”
: ““Those who fear My name”—those who keep Shabbat.”
: “Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Sunshine on Shabbat is charity for the poor, as it says, “For you who fear My name, a sun of charity will rise, with healing.””

: “Someone who bought produce from a person not trusted regarding tithes, and forgot to tithe it, may ask him on Shabbat and eat on his assurance. After Shabbat has ended, he may not eat until he tithes. … The companions said in Rabbi Yohanan’s name: They permitted this in honor of Shabbat. If it is because of Shabbat’s honor, why must he ask? To create a basis for the permission. Rabbi Bibi said in Rabbi Hanina’s name: The awe of Shabbat rests upon him, so he tells the truth. If the awe of Shabbat rests upon him, why does the Mishnah say that once Shabbat ends he may not eat until he tithes? Because there may be someone upon whom the awe of Shabbat does not rest. A baraita teaches: If he asks on a weekday, he may not eat on Shabbat. This fits the view that the awe of Shabbat rests upon him. According to the view that permission is given for Shabbat’s honor, however, even if he asked on a weekday, he should be able to eat on Shabbat.”

k: volume-ii|1253|0|R. Chaim Tyrer of Tchernovitz, Sidduro S
ref: Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume I, Shoresh VI 2:21
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Tyrer of Tchernovitz, Sidduro Shel Shabbat I, Shoresh VI, ch. 2, §20 (digital 2:21): “It seems that Shabbat’s holiness can shelter a person throughout the week: the first three days receive from the holiness of the previous Shabbat, while in the second three days the holiness of the coming Shabbat begins to shine upon him. The traces and blemishes that pass away from a person in fear of Shabbat’s light then dread approaching holiness even as that light only begins to shine. Trembling and terror seize them before Hashem and His majestic splendor. His kingship rules over everything, removing idols from the earth and utterly cutting them off. But all this applies when, during the weekdays, a person does not accustom himself to evil at all: he must not approach its doorway and must withhold his feet from its path. If, Heaven forbid, he becomes accustomed during the week to evil’s dross, even merely through thought and sinful imaginings, then “a transgression extinguishes a mitzvah.” The great light upon him grows dim, and evil can return to its former place, where it originally made its dwelling.”
: “The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, growing ever brighter until the day is fully established.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beshalach 3:7–8: “Nevertheless the Zohar taught: whoever comes from the side of the feminine, death goes before his steps. For although she [the Shunammite] rectified the entire blemish of the serpent like Eve, she did not achieve this permanently for her offspring, just as Eve did not achieve it for her descendants to remove the cause of death. For the chief rectification of the serpent’s blemish is through words of Torah, as stated (Zohar I 212a): there is nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah. Women are not commanded in Torah study; through what do they merit? Through bringing their children to learn Torah (Berakhot 17a), and she had not yet taught this child Torah. … Elisha is called here ‘man of God,’ the aspect of Moses our teacher, who shone words of Torah even upon the unlearned who never studied, as it is said, ‘an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob’: even the common people who know nothing, whose deliberate sins are counted as errors, who are called ‘the house of Jacob’ (Bava Metzia 33b). Therefore Elisha had the power to revive the child.”

k: volume-ii|1256|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Ki
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Ki Tisa 12: “In the Tanchuma: ‘When you raise the head’ — R. Yehoshua ben Levi said: It alluded to him that he would in the future bring near the first of the tribes. Who is this? Reuben, as it says, ‘Let Reuben live and not die.’ … The shekalim are the uniting of Israel as one man, in a new vitality for the service of Hashem. Now Reuben was clean of the sin of the sale of Joseph, as the Torah testified of him, ‘Reuben heard and rescued him from their hand … in order to rescue him from their hand, to return him to his father.’ Joseph is called ‘living’ (chai), and the opposite of this is one who sins in forbidden relations, as it is written, ‘Her feet go down to death.’ Therefore Reuben, because he rescued from their hand Joseph, who is called ‘living,’ merited life; and this is ‘Let Reuben live and not die,’ that the incident of Bilhah not be remembered against him. Therefore when He told Moses the portion of shekalim, which are a rectification for the sin of the sale of Joseph, He alluded to him that he would bring Reuben near, as it says, ‘Let Reuben live,’ drawing life upon him for rescuing Joseph. It emerges that the shekalim are a rectification for the corruption and blemish of the covenant, and renew life.”

k: volume-ii|1257|0|R. Chaim Tyrer of Chernovitz, Be'er Mayi
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim Tyrer of Chernovitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Shemot 1:1: “The name Yaakov, yod–akev, points to the descent of holiness to the lower levels, the place of impurity, in order to separate the impure from the pure, to send the impure away and raise the pure, to gather the dispersed and return them to their mother’s bosom, like a father who goes down into the house of captivity, a filthy place, in order to bring his son up from there. Therefore, when the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to tell him of the exile of Egypt and said to him, ‘I will go down with you’ (Genesis 46:4), meaning the holiness that went down to Egypt with Yaakov so as not to let Israel sink there, Heaven forbid, He called him Yaakov. ... Here their names are mentioned on account of the redemption, for the whole essence of the redemption was that holiness went down with them to Egypt, as Scripture says, ‘whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, nations and its god’ (II Samuel 7:23). Of this it is said, ‘Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me’ (Psalms 23:4): for when the Holy One, blessed be He, redeems Himself from exile, He will redeem His children as well. Holiness wrapped itself and went down with them in order to redeem them.”

k: volume-ii|1258|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Devarim 25:2: “In truth, the exile too, and all the punishments of Israel, come according to the Torah. The Pesikta brings a parable of a king’s son for whom a golden ornament was made for his head; when he did not do his father’s will, it was made into fetters for his feet. So the twenty-two letters of the Torah were turned into lamentations. That is, our punishments too come through the Torah, and in this we have something to hold on to in order to return to Him by the power of the Torah. It is written, ‘Even when I walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil, for You are with me’: these are the twenty-two letters of the Torah. ‘Your rod’: these are the sufferings; ‘Your staff’: this is the Torah, as the Midrash writes. That is, as it is written, ‘It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it’ (Proverbs 3:18): ‘those who hold fast’ implies that even when one does not merit to cleave to the tree of life completely, one can still take hold of the Torah to merit life. This is ‘Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me’: we know that the sufferings come by the power of the Torah, and from this is our consolation.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 7:1: “In the heh, which is the attribute of Malkhut, ‘I am Hashem who dwells among the children of Israel,’ there, as it were, He stands. As it says (Megillah 29a), wherever they were exiled the Shechinah was with them; and as the holy Zohar says (III 115a), ‘And if you say I will abandon you, I too am with you.’ ... That is, the Holy One, blessed be He, is also with them, only the union is not manifest but in concealment. ... ‘And yet for all that’ (Leviticus 26:44): ‘gam’ comes to include the Community of Israel, called ‘zot,’ which never abandons them; ‘to destroy them’ (lechalotam), because of their bride (kalatam), whom I love. That is, on Shabbos all Israel are called a bride, for they attain a new additional soul every Shabbos. ... So even in the exiles there is Shabbos, when all Israel are called a bride, and then the union is found, as the holy Zohar says (III 79b): ‘On the Sabbath day ... the soul is added, for Atika is revealed and the union is prepared.’ ... And especially in this meal, which is the meal of Atika Kadisha, as the holy Zohar says: Atika is revealed and the union is prepared.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Shekalim 15: “It is stated (Bava Batra 10b): By what will Israel’s horn be exalted? Through ‘When you raise the head.’ That is, through the shekalim Israel’s horn is exalted up to the head, so that they are bound to the root. And likewise through charity, as in Rashi, and as it says afterward: through the power of charity, ‘his horn shall be exalted in glory.’ This accords with the statement (Vayikra Rabbah 25): The Holy One, blessed be He, will make shade and canopies for those who perform commandments beside the people of Torah. ‘His horn shall be exalted’ indicates without measure, up to Atika; ‘in glory,’ beside the people of Torah, as stated (Chullin 133a): glory means only Torah. And this is the holiness of Shabbat, the revelation of Atika that one merits on Shabbat, and this is ‘in My treasure house.’ … Of them it is said, ‘When you raise the head,’ that Israel’s horn is exalted through the shekalim in the plain sense, or through charity as Rashi explains, as appears from the order of the passage, which speaks of it before and after in the Gemara. … For Israel give from generosity of heart and from love of Hashem, and their horn is exalted in glory.”

k: volume-ii|1261|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Parashat Shekalim 24: “The Sages said: When the portion of shekalim is read, Moses raises the heads of the children of Israel, as it is written, ‘Charity exalts a nation, and the kindness of the nations is sin.’ For charity is particular to Israel, as it says, ‘Justice and charity You have made in Jacob’; through charity one arouses kindness and mercy in heaven as well, and this power belongs only to Israel, who have attachment to the Holy One, blessed be He, and can change the decree, which is within nature. … A Jew is born without completion, and through circumcision, Torah and commandments he is exalted and rises from level to level, and he can be exalted up to heaven. … Therefore Israel have an exaltation every year, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gave us the commandment of the shekalim to arouse through it the power of exaltation through charity; and this is ‘When you raise … and they shall give.’ … The shekalim of Israel are in order to be exalted, to receive a supernal power above nature, … for Israel have a place and root in the supernal holiness, and through the shekalim, of which it is written ‘When you raise the head,’ they come to that place, as it is written, ‘half a shekel by the holy shekel.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Shekalim 4: “We likewise find the number eleven in the ingredients of the incense: ten ingredients have a good fragrance and correspond to the ten sefirot, and galbanum has a foul smell, yet Scripture counts it among the ingredients of the incense. That is, even galbanum gives forth a good fragrance when it is together with them, and it alludes to Israel’s sinners (as stated in Keritot 6b): they too will ultimately give forth a good fragrance, as stated in the Gemara (Eruvin 21b). … There is a remedy even for those considered to have no portion in the World to Come, since they are of Jacob’s seed, even one who kicked at the root, at ‘I am’ and ‘You shall have no.’ That is, it will become clear that the darkness was in order that there be light that emerges from darkness, as stated in the holy Zohar (II 184a). … When the galbanum, the lowest of the tribes, is clarified, it is one with the greatest of the tribes; that is, it is not counted among evil at all, but the evil was only in order that there be ‘very good,’ for there is no good except that which emerges from evil, as stated in the holy Zohar.”

k: volume-ii|1263|0|R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohe
quote: Parallel: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Vayakhel 1: “It is known from the words of our Sages that at the chosen assembly at Mount Sinai, when Israel put ‘we shall do’ before ‘we shall hear,’ Hashem, blessed be He, placed two crowns on the head of each one of Israel. Afterward, when they sinned with the calf, this was removed from them, as it is written, ‘The children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb,’ for they lost all the illumination of holiness they had received at Mount Horeb. All the lights and crowns, which are Israel’s ornaments taken from them at Horeb, Moses our teacher took for himself. But Moses is a faithful servant, and on holy Shabbat, when holiness rests upon Israel, he returns the crowns to each one of Israel, and each one receives according to his holiness, as is known from the Arizal’s intention on ‘Moses rejoices in the gift of his portion.’ … This is ‘These are the things … six days’: through keeping Shabbat, each one of the seed of Israel can again take the lights and crowns that were lacking through the sin of the calf, for Shabbat is a great rectification for the sin of the calf, … and then Moses returns to each one of Israel his portion.”

k: volume-ii|1264|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Ki Tisa 16: “‘But (akh) My Shabbatot you shall observe.’ The Sages said: ‘akh’ means a portion, as it is written, ‘It is a sign between Me and you.’ Hence Shabbat is an intermediary, having a portion in the spiritual and in the physical, as stated in the holy Zohar (Vayakhel) on the verse ‘The children of Israel shall observe the Shabbat’: that spirit, the extension of that point … delights above and below. … Also according to the plain sense, since Shabbat is a covenant, it is an intermediary between the upper and the lower beings, and therefore it is called peace; for this world is in truth the reverse of the upper world, and only on Shabbat is there a union of the upper with the lower, and it is called a day of rest and peace. Therefore it is a commandment on Shabbat to delight in eating and drinking, and it is written, ‘It is holy to you’: even in the physical, holiness rests on Shabbat. … ‘It is holy to you’: the holiness is found in the souls of Israel themselves, as the Sages said that on holy Shabbat tefillin are not needed, for they themselves are a sign; and this is through the power of the additional soul that rests on holy Shabbat in the souls of Israel.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vaetchanan 20: “As we find (Shocher Tov, Psalms 92): Everything pertaining to Shabbat is doubled: its omer is doubled, its offering is doubled, and so forth; its admonitions are doubled, ‘Remember’ and ‘Observe’; its psalm is doubled, ‘A psalm, a song.’ … The explanation follows the statement (Zohar II 118b): the Holy One, blessed be He, is ‘Remember,’ and the Shechinah is ‘Observe.’ … That is, Written Torah and Oral Torah. … Its reward is doubled: Shabbat corresponds to the attribute of Malkhut, the aspect of the Community of Israel, and it is written, ‘You shall call Shabbat a delight’: oneg, delight, is the initials of Eden, nahar, gan (river, garden), ‘and a river goes out of Eden to water the garden,’ which is the lower Shechinah (Zohar I 26a). ‘And Hashem’s holy day honored’ is the Name Havayah, in keeping with the statement (Chullin 133a): glory means only Torah, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah. The meals, which are in the mystery of oneg, rectify the corruption of the serpent, which was in eating, and the evil inclination departs, and they merit ‘Hashem’s holy day honored,’ that is, Torah: upper holiness and lower holiness.”

k: volume-ii|1266|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vay
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vayakhel 4:4: “I said in the name of my holy father, the Admor, the explanation of the Gemara (Shabbat 69b): Rav Huna said, one walking in the wilderness who does not know when Shabbat is counts six days and observes one; Chiya bar Rav says, he observes one and counts six. He said that Shabbat has two aspects: it comes after the working days as their completion, and it also gives strength and vitality for what follows, ‘and from it the six days are blessed.’ … The order of creation, as man was made upright, was that a person should do his service in the physical and the spiritual, to clarify all the portions of holiness, … and afterward, according to his deeds, he would merit the light of Shabbat’s holiness: whoever toiled on Shabbat eve will eat on Shabbat. But once Adam sinned and fell from his level and was at the lowest rung, had Shabbat not come and given him strength and vitality he could not have begun to do anything at all; rather, Shabbat breathed into him a spirit of new life, and with that power he then worked through all six working days, and afterward the holiness of Shabbat again shone on them and he attains further new life, and so it goes round. … This is what we find in the Gemara (Sanhedrin): Why was man created on Shabbat eve? So that he would enter a commandment immediately.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedushas Shabbos 2:7: “This follows the dispute of R. Chiya bar Rav and Rav Huna (Shabbat 69b) concerning one who does not know when Shabbat is: one master holds he counts six and observes one, like the creation of the world; the other holds he observes one and counts six, like Adam. These and those are the words of the living God, and they are the two Shabbatot mentioned. All the days of the world one must observe these two Shabbatot: the preceding Shabbat is an influx of holiness for the service of the six days after it, and the service of the six days is preparation to receive the holiness of the Shabbat after it. So it is with every Shabbat: last for the one before it and first for the one after it, until the final one comes, the day that is entirely Shabbat. … Only from the side of man, that he be a vessel to receive the holiness, are two Shabbatot needed; but from the side of the Holy One, blessed be He, one suffices, and that is the second. … Before one has absorbed the fixed holiness of Shabbat, there is no benefit in his effort during the six working days and his preparing himself for the holiness of the coming Shabbat. … Had Hashem not first imparted holiness to him, through which he can sanctify himself and add holiness, what is man that he should come after the King, and liken himself to his Maker at all? It is impossible to put the second Shabbat before the first.”

k: volume-ii|1268|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala,
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Chayei Sara 41: “‘And Yitzchak came from the way of Be’er Lachai Ro’i … and he was dwelling in the land of the Negev’ (Genesis 24:62). … It is known that the essence of service is joy in the service. … Sometimes a person has joy and thinks it is the heart’s joy in service, yet it may come from the wanton waters and strange fire of some craving that overpowered him, in eating and drinking, strolling and the like. … The test for knowing whether his joy is the joy of a commandment, which comes to him from the arousal of the supernal union, or the opposite, Heaven forbid, is this: he strips from himself all the joy of this world, sets it before his eyes and sees that all of it is null to him, that he does not crave its delicacies, that his desire is reined in by the bridle of righteousness, and that at the time of his joy his heart yearns only for His Torah and His service. … The sign for this is ‘and he was dwelling in the land of the Negev’: such joy settles only in a land drained of all the good of this world and its pleasures, as our Sages said (Temurah 16a) on ‘For you have given me the land of the Negev’ (Joshua 15:19): a body drained of all good, with only the moisture of the waters of Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shabbat HaGadol 3: “All the festivals are called in the Torah shabbaton, a holy convocation: shabbaton is a small Shabbat, with the diminutive nun. … In livelihood there is doubled sorrow: from Hashem’s side, from the curse, … and itzavon from the side of man, who troubles himself in work with anguish of soul; had he trusted in Hashem, a little effort would have sufficed him. … This is itzavon, a small sorrow, from man’s side, which is in his power to be saved from; and this is ‘double,’ from Hashem’s side and from man’s side (and it is explained in Ki Tisa, discourse 6). So too Shabbat is called ‘Shabbat shabbaton’: Shabbat is holiness fixed and enduring from Hashem, and shabbaton, a small Shabbat, is also from man’s side, for it is called first among the holy convocations, as it says, ‘Remember it, to sanctify it.’ A festival is called only shabbaton, a small Shabbat, from Israel’s side, for they intercalate and fix the years (as stated in Pesachim 117b). Of Pesach, however, ‘shabbaton’ is not written, only ‘holy convocation’ … for the holiness of Pesach was without preparation from Israel’s side, only from Hashem’s side in His kindness, and therefore it is called Shabbat.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vaera 2:5, 2:7: “As I heard from our holy teacher, may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing, on the verse ‘You shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen,’ which Onkelos translates, ‘You shall see what is behind Me, but what is before Me shall not be seen’: after an event, Moses our teacher grasped its entire depth, up to the Supernal Thought; but ‘My face,’ before the event, ‘shall not be seen,’ for no creature can grasp that depth beforehand, since His thoughts are exceedingly deep. … Afterward, when Moses saw that they had not yet been redeemed, and on the contrary, ‘since I came to Pharaoh … he has done evil to this people,’ he attributed it to his own deficiency, reasoning that earlier he had been worthy to see and now he had declined and was no longer fit to grasp Hashem’s workings. But in truth it was only because this was before the event and its revelation, and therefore it did not yet shine to him. … Moses our teacher grasped through the shining lens after the event, as it says, ‘You shall see My back’: after the event he grasped Hashem’s deeds in full perfection. Therefore now, seeing no salvation, he cried, ‘Why have You sent me?’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sh’lach 12: “‘May He send us His beauty (shufrei) and may we behold His glory (bikarei)’ … that we may behold, as by a find, His glory, that is, the holiness of Atika, as it says, ‘And his eye saw every precious thing (yakar),’ and they said in the Midrash: this is R. Akiva and his companions; things not revealed to Moses were revealed to R. Akiva and his companions. This is the fiftieth of the fifty gates of understanding, which is Da’at, and it belongs to the penitent, to the supernal repentance. … ‘And may He show us His hidden mystery’ is the primordial light hidden for the righteous. … ‘Which is spoken in a whisper’ follows Bereishit Rabbah 3: … ‘Just as I received it in a whisper, so I told it to you in a whisper.’ … The matter of a whisper is as in ‘You shall say in your heart,’ speech in silence, so that one feels it in the depth of the heart: by saying ‘This teaches that He wrapped Himself,’ and so forth, he brought into him a feeling in the heart of the primordial light. … So we have said several times from our holy teacher, that even in the Written Torah there is the power of Oral Torah, from that peddler (Vayikra Rabbah 16) … Although he told him only the verse as it stands, because the peddler had been corrupt in this matter and after repentance felt a renewed light, R. Yannai too, though he heard only this verse from him, felt that renewed light. And we have brought proof from Rabbi’s teaching in the Mishnah (Avot 4), ‘Shmuel HaKatan says,

k: volume-ii|1272|0|R. Shlomo HaKohen Rabinowicz of Radomsk,
ref: Tiferet Shlomo, on Torah, Ki Tisa 1
quote: Parallel: R. Shlomo HaKohen Rabinowicz of Radomsk, Tiferet Shlomo, Ki Tisa 1: “‘When you raise the head of the children of Israel according to their numbers’: … ‘the supernal bundle, in which is the life of all; may its strength increase and may it ascend to the head.’ The chief service of the righteous is self-sacrifice. … This is the meaning of ‘the supernal bundle’: the righteous one is bound in the supernal bundle, as it is written, ‘May my lord’s soul be bound in the bundle of life,’ which is self-sacrifice, the soul of David, as it is written, ‘To You, Hashem, I lift up my soul’; ‘in which is the life of all,’ for he is included in the supernal light of life, which is the life of all. ‘May its strength (chayla) increase,’ as it is written, ‘Through God we shall do valiantly (chayil),’ and ‘Israel does valiantly’; this is ‘men of valor who fear God,’ and for this the Shechinah is called ‘a woman of valor’ (eshet chayil). ‘And may it ascend to the head’: this righteous one rises up to the head of all heads, as it is written, ‘exalted as head over all’; and for this they are called ‘heads of the children of Israel,’ and ‘heads of the thousands of Israel,’ for they rise up to the head. And this is the verse ‘When you raise the head of the children of Israel,’ to raise them on high.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tazria 6:1: “The holy Zohar (Ki Tisa 189b) then says: ‘In the end of days the mountain of Hashem’s house shall be established at the head of the mountains.’ Who is the head of the mountains? This is Avraham the Elder, the great priest, the head of all, … first before the other mountains. This follows the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, end of 36): ‘mountains’ are the patriarchs, and Avraham our father, first before the other mountains, is called the head of the mountains. ‘The mountain of Hashem’s house’ refers to the Shechinah. Avraham is called the great priest: a priest is the attribute of Chesed, and he is called the great priest because he merited the attribute of an elder, as it is said, ‘Avraham was old, coming into days,’ and in the holy Zohar (Chayei Sarah 129a), ‘into those supernal days.’ He merited grasping that there is an intellect concealed from all thought, and his attribute was clarified up to Atika, as we said on ‘Until Avraham there was no old age’ (Bava Metzia 87a), that is, Atika. … The Gemara (Pesachim 88a) says: not like Avraham, of whom ‘mountain’ is written, but like Yaakov, who called it ‘house,’ a house fixed for all eternity. … ‘Who shall ascend the mountain of Havayah,’ … up to Atika; that is, ‘who will merit being within it in completeness,’ meaning perfect faith.”

Parallel: Maharal, Gevurot Hashem 36: “One may further say why it was slaughtered ‘in the afternoon’: day is related to existence and night to non-existence, as is known. All existing things pass away, and He, blessed be He, alone endures; for this reason He, blessed be He, is One, because all existing things pass away and return to the One who created them. From the beginning of evening, when the sun begins to set, is the beginning of the passing and absence of light, and then the Pesach offering is slaughtered for His Name, for He is One; this time indicates unity, when existing things pass away and He endures eternally. With the beginning of sunset all things in the world incline, as the day turns to evening, toward sleep, which is like death and absence, and darkness is like the absence of existing things, while He, blessed be He, is eternal. … By this you will understand why we say in the Minchah prayer of Shabbat, ‘You are One and Your Name is One’: this time indicates unity most of all, since all existing things pass away, as explained.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Kedoshim 13: “In the Minchah prayer we mention every kind of rest: a rest of love and generosity, a rest of truth, and so forth. The chief rest is from the evil inclination, as it is said, ‘On the day Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow and your turmoil.’ ‘Your sorrow’ is the root of the evil inclination, as stated (Temurah 16a): ‘that it not pain me,’ that the evil inclination not overpower me to repeat; ‘your turmoil’ is the agitation of the evil inclination, as stated (Berakhot 5a): a person should always stir up the good inclination against the evil inclination. This verse is expounded in the holy Zohar (I 48a) concerning Shabbat, the day of rest, when Hashem places repose in the heart of Israel. So too in the Megillah, after the erasing of Amalek, ‘and they rested from their enemies,’ for Amalek is the root of the evil inclination; after they merited erasing Amalek they merited rest. So too in this prayer, after one has passed the day of Shabbat in observance, one merits rest from the evil inclination. … Hashem does not speak with a person to reprove him except by sending into his heart an awakening to repentance, and the person imagines that he awoke to repentance by himself; and this happens chiefly on Shabbat. … We ask that the salvation be in truth, ‘the lip of truth shall endure forever,’ that the thought of repentance widen until he returns in complete repentance, confessing and forsaking in truth. And this one merits at this meal of Yaako

k: volume-ii|1276|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Shemot, Pekudei 2:2: “In the Midrash: ‘A man of faithfulness abounds with blessings’: this is Moshe; ‘but one who hastens to be rich’: this is Korach. For it was difficult to him why the items of the Mishkan were counted, when blessing rules only over what is not counted. The answer is in the holy Zohar as well: since the count was made by Moshe our teacher, there was blessing in it. The general principle is this: over what is counted blessing does not rule, since each one is separated by itself; without counting it is within the whole, and in the whole there is blessing, for the whole is attached to the root and source of blessing, from which life flows to all. Therefore one who is a ‘man of faithfulness,’ meaning that he is drawn after the root, and although he does physical deeds in the working of nature he still knows and remembers that all is from God, blessing rests on his deeds. ... All his deeds are drawn after God’s life force, and therefore blessing rests even though it is counted. ... And so on holy Shabbat blessing rests, because all things are unified on Shabbat to cleave to the root of life, and it becomes a vessel that holds blessing.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 1:1–2: “‘When the ark journeyed … let Your enemies scatter and Your foes flee before You.’ ‘Your foes’ does not refer to the nations, for there were none in the wilderness; it means those who make Hashem hateful in Israel’s eyes, the evil inclination. The journeying was to be rescued from the evil inclination. ... ‘When it rested, he would say: Return, Hashem’: Rashi explains it from ‘in returning and rest you shall be saved,’ which is expounded on Shabbat. ... Just as each Shabbat radiates holiness into the working days after it, so that the second Shabbat comes with greater holiness than the one before it, so are all a person’s days: in the working days he journeys and walks in the service of Hashem, and when Shabbat comes, rest comes, as it says, ‘For man journeys to the house of his world’; and the Midrash says, ‘It does not say worlds, but his world.’ ... This is the meaning of ‘Had Israel kept two Shabbatot they would immediately be redeemed’ (Shabbat 118b): the first Shabbat radiates holiness into the working days, the days of journeying, and then comes the second Shabbat, more exalted than the one before, and they attain a Shabbat as it should be, so that one is completely redeemed.”

k: volume-ii|1278|0|R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat
quote: Parallel: R. Yisrael Hopstein of Kozhnitz, Avodat Yisrael, Shemini 1: “When Israel completed the work of the Tabernacle, Moses came and blessed them: ‘May it be His will that the Shechinah dwell in the work of your hands.’ ... Just as the union is made on holy Shabbat between the aspect called ‘holy’ and the aspect called ‘lofty’: Abba, Father, is called ‘holy,’ in the mystery of ‘Wisdom is holiness,’ and Binah, Understanding, which is raised above the attributes, is called ‘lofty’; therefore the liturgy says, ‘He dwells forever, lofty and holy is His Name,’ and the Ari wrote that marom, ‘lofty,’ and kadosh, ‘holy,’ equal Shabbat in numerical value, for then they are united and reckoned as one. ... Thus Moses our teacher blessed them, ‘May it be His will that the Shechinah dwell,’ meaning the upper Shechinah, ‘in the work of your hands.’ ... Therefore the Midrash says that Israel answered, ‘May the pleasantness of Hashem our God be upon us,’ to draw down the light of Binah as well, just as we say it at the conclusion of Shabbat, to shield us with the light of Binah and rescue us from all evil, as it says, ‘With His pinion He will cover you.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Eikev 14: “‘And Zion said, Hashem has forsaken me, and my Lord has forgotten me.’ Zion is the name of the place of the Mikdash, and it is the place of Torah, as it is said, ‘For from Zion shall Torah go forth, and the word of Hashem from Jerusalem,’ and there is the revelation of the Oral Torah ... And the Mikdash is likewise called ‘the house of My prayer,’ as King Solomon said in his prayer, ‘and he comes and prays toward this house’; and so they said that one who prays must direct himself toward the Mikdash, as it is said, ‘and they pray toward this house,’ and as they said (Berakhot 30a), ‘built as a talpiyot, a hill toward which all mouths turn.’ ... This is the whole strength of Israel, that their strength is only in their mouth ... and that is the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer. And this is ‘And Zion said, Hashem has forsaken me’: the name Havayah is mentioned, corresponding to the voice of Torah; ‘and my Lord has forgotten me’ corresponds to the voice of prayer. For both of them come only from the power of God: in prayer one says first, ‘My Lord, open my lips,’ meaning that God sends the prayer into a person’s mouth ... and in Torah too we find, ‘In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned,’ which they expounded (Berakhot 6a) on one who sits and studies Torah, that the Shechinah is with him.”

ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Vayakhel 4
quote: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, Vol. II, Vayakhel 4: “In the work of the Mishkan it is written, ‘in whom God put wisdom and understanding,’ meaning that the work was done above their understanding. From the side of those who did the work it was done only like the work of a monkey, for the work was completed only from the side of God, entirely above their knowledge, as it is written, ‘By the understanding of His hands He led them’: the understanding in their hands was only from God, for they did according to God’s will without any knowledge or calculation. Yet in their own perception it seemed to each of the craftsmen that he had done wonders by his own effort and wisdom of heart. But when Israel brought abundant donations, and each craftsman intended to do God’s will, each one grasped that he had no cause for self-exaltation in his work and his wisdom, as the holy Zohar says (Pekudei 222b): ‘At the hour that all the craftsmen began to do that work ... it completed itself; they began, and it completed the work.’ ... Therefore it is written, ‘Six days work shall be done,’ in the reflexive form, for all of them understood that everything is from God and they have no reason to credit themselves.”

k: volume-ii|1281|0|R. Chaim ibn Attar, Ohr HaChaim, Bereish
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim ibn Attar, Ohr HaChaim, Bereishis 2:3: “We find that the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed the matter in the Ten Commandments: ‘For in six days God made the heavens,’ and so on. This reveals that at the time of creation God created no power in the world except to stand for six days, for a reason known to Him and known also to the knowers of truth. God acted wisely and created one day, known to God, on which He again bestows a soul upon the world, the measure that sustains it another six days, and so on. Without this day the world would be destroyed at the end of six days and return to chaos and void, and God would have to prepare it a second time; through Shabbat the world stands. ... By this explanation we find satisfaction in a statement of our Sages (Shabbat 119b): ‘Whoever sanctifies ... and says Vayechulu ... is as though he became a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation.’ Their words seem far-fetched: who has heard of a person becoming a partner in something whose work is already finished? ... But since Shabbat sustains the world for all six days, and after six days another Shabbat comes and revives it and sustains it another six days, know that the existence of Shabbat in the world is its being kept: if Shabbat is not kept there is no Shabbat. ... Thus ‘whoever sanctifies Shabbat,’ meaning keeps and guards its holiness, through him there is Shabbat, and through it the world is sustained. He sustains the world, and there is

ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 5
quote: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, Vol. I, Bereishis 5: “‘And the heavens and the earth and all their host were completed.’ The Gemara (Shabbat 119b) says that whoever says Vayechulu becomes a partner with the Holy One, blessed be He, in the work of creation. The matter is that the main purpose of the creation of the world was that Israel recognize His kingship and His oneness, as Abraham our father began to bring about, calling in the name of God, God of the earth, and for this every soul of Israel hopes; without it heaven and earth would not have endured, as the Gemara says (Shabbat 88a), ‘If Israel accepts the Torah, good; and if not ...’ One who recognizes God’s kingship in the world completes the creation, for speech is like deed. And one who recognizes on the Shabbat day and crowns God over all that He made in the six days of work, although what is the worth of a mortal before God, even so the judgment of that man is that the two angels who accompany him, that is, the good inclination and the evil inclination, place their hands on his head and say to him, ‘Your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tetzaveh 5:1: “The Holy One, blessed be He, knows His times and moments and entered it by a hair’s breadth, as stated in Bereshit Rabbah, section 10. Of that very instant, before Shabbat’s entrance, it says, ‘God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good,’ which Bereshit Rabbah 9:7 interprets concerning the evil inclination ... This occurred specifically at twilight’s final hour, the time of the addition to Shabbat, which is the holiness of the person drawing Shabbat’s holiness upon himself through his own awakening. All this is alluded to in ‘There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day’: precisely through evening and darkness comes preparation for the sixth day’s aspect, the attribute of the righteous one, the foundation of the world. ... This is alluded to specifically by ‘There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day’: the introduction of the addition to Shabbat specifically from the human side, to transform darkness into light, through which the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted in His glory.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Iyar 5: “We have already said that the organs the Blessed One created were created only for good. In the fool’s heart the Holy One, blessed be He, created a wondrous inclination of desire, so that he would have a longing for Torah, as it will be in the future, and as the Zohar says (I 138a, Midrash HaNe’elam), ‘Were it not for the evil inclination, the joy of learning would not exist’; and this is what Bereshit Rabbah 27 says, ‘You make it bad.’ Likewise the left kidney was created so that a person subdue his inclination and remove the evil from the fool’s heart, on his left. ... And the gall too, which the Blessed One created, is for good, as the holy Zohar says (II 182b), ‘The anger of the rabbis is good on every side’; and anger was created chiefly to rouse oneself against the evil inclination, as Berakhot 5a says, ‘A person should always rouse his good inclination against his evil inclination.’”

k: volume-ii|1285|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or Einayim, Bereishis 32: “As is known, there are two chambers of the heart in a person: the dwelling of the good inclination on his right and the dwelling of the evil inclination on his left. Through the good of his overcoming, the left is included in the right, the evil is erased and becomes good, and on the contrary it helps him in the service of the Blessed One, as our Sages said, ‘Were it not for the evil inclination, the joy of learning would not exist.’ For the main zeal and desire in divine service comes from the side of the evil inclination once it is sweetened, and the accuser becomes a defender. This is the meaning of ‘You shall love ... with all your heart’: with both your inclinations; and as it is written, ‘His left hand is under my head and his right hand embraces me,’ for the main longing and desire for service comes from sweetening the evil inclination. ... All this is because the Creator gave the Torah to Israel, which is the spice that seasons and sweetens the evil inclination.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 29: “In the Gemara (Eruvin 65b): ‘A person is recognized by his cup, by his purse, and by his anger’; these are the three kelipot of jealousy, desire, and honor. ‘His cup’ is desire, as the holy Zohar says (I 202a) that the evil inclination dwells only where there is the joy of wine and adultery; and in the Gemara (Yoma 75a): whoever sets his eye on his cup, all forbidden relations seem to him like a level plain. Conversely, ‘if he merits, it gladdens him,’ when he drinks wine for the sake of a mitzvah ... the wine helps to straighten the heart, so that he has one heart for his Father in Heaven, the upright for joy, as it is written, ‘and joy for the upright of heart’ (Taanit 15a). ... And corresponding to the three kelipot there are three impurities. The metzora, who is sent out even from the camp of Israel, corresponds to the kelipah of jealousy, which has no portion in Israel at all ... The zav corresponds to the kelipah of desire, and he is sent out only from the camp of the Levites, of whom it is written, ‘They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob,’ for Torah scholars can conquer the evil inclination of desire, as Sukkah 52b says, ‘If this repulsive one meets you, draw him to the study hall,’ ... so that he draws the desire toward Torah, as it will be in the future, when it will remain.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Behar 14:1: “Israel on Shabbat is as in the Sanctuary, for Shabbat in time is like the Sanctuary in space (as explained several times). Just as dread and awe fall upon one who enters the Sanctuary, so on Shabbat dread and awe fall upon every Jew, as in the Sanctuary. ... So we say in the Song of the Shabbat Day, ‘Planted in the house of Hashem, they will flourish in the courtyards of our God.’ ‘Planted in the house of Hashem’: when Israel fulfill the three meals they are called children of the King’s palace, as stated in the holy Zohar (II 88b, 252b). ‘They will flourish in the courtyards of our God’: the flourishing at the very entry of Shabbat is also in the courtyards of our God. ... On Shabbat, when they fulfill it, they are ‘planted in the house of Hashem,’ the revelation of Atika, which is called Ayin (Zohar II 64b) and called Holy of Holies (ibid. 121a). And the flourishing at Shabbat’s entry is ‘in the courtyards of our God,’ for as soon as one accepts Shabbat’s holiness upon himself, Israel are called ‘those who fear My Name’ (Taanit 8b), and ‘the awe of Shabbat is upon the unlearned’ (Jerusalem Talmud Demai 4). ... Those who labor in Torah are always in the house of Hashem, but even one who is not a Torah scholar is, on Shabbat, in the courtyards of the house of Hashem, for the awe of Shabbat is upon the unlearned.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa 3:1: “The chief purpose of the incense is to rectify all Israel’s sinners so that they give forth a good fragrance, like galbanum, whose smell is foul, but when included among the ten incense ingredients gives forth a good fragrance. Likewise, even the completely wicked will ultimately give forth fragrance (as stated in Eruvin 21b), as they learned from galbanum to include Israel’s sinners in a fast (Keritot 6b). The crown of priesthood, which Aaron attained for himself and his descendants, is on the incense altar (Yoma 72b), for the priests burn the incense. Nevertheless, the fundamental power to rectify Israel’s sinners, revealing in the future that everything occurred so as to become very good, as stated (Zohar II 184a), ‘There is no light except that which emerges from darkness, and no good except that which emerges from evil’—this power Moses our teacher introduced by breaking the tablets.”

k: volume-ii|1289|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Lec
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Lech Lecha 11:9, 11:12: “It is written, ‘Happy is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courtyards; we will be sated with the goodness of Your house, Your holy Sanctuary.’ The holy Zohar says: First ‘Your courtyards,’ then ‘Your house,’ then ‘Your Sanctuary,’ each more inward than the other. ‘Your holy Sanctuary’ comes after, and it is the completion of all, as we learned: What is heichal? Hei kol, ‘here is all,’ this and that, all completed as one. ... Correspondingly, on Shabbat one attains three distinct times. Shabbat night is ‘Guard,’ for the holy Zohar says that ‘Guard’ is the attribute of night, and its meal is that of the field of apples; it is the aspect of the courtyard. Shabbat day is ‘Remember’: one attains a more concealed level, and its meal is the meal of Atika. ... At Shabbat afternoon one attains the aspect of heichal, and that is why we then sing, ‘Children of the palace who yearn.’ Then is the time of cleaving, and at that time of favor Moses departed; it corresponds to the third altar, in Hebron, from the word chibbur, joining.”

k: volume-ii|1290|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala,
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Matot 47: “Our Sages said (Sanhedrin 107a): ‘Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of Creation, but he partook of her unripe.’ David is not to be blamed in this, for he did not intend human desire. He only saw that she was fit for him, for his inheritance is the eternal inheritance of the heavenly kingdom, the Kingdom of Heaven, and she is Bat Sheva, the seven attributes of the structure, the mother of Solomon. This attribute is the gate to Hashem, the door that opens below to enter within it forever and ever. Hashem made this known in Solomon’s days through the opening of the doors, which could be opened only through David. Then they understood that he is a vehicle for Malchut, which is the gate and the opening, and retroactively they understood that Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of Creation. Therefore the faces of David’s enemies then turned black like the bottom of a pot.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeshev 12:1: “‘Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me.’ The holy Zohar on this portion expounds this verse regarding Joseph: Joseph went into the valley of the shadow of death, they brought him down to Egypt, and the Shechinah was with him. ... Joseph surely sensed that he had a connection to her root, and the evil inclination surely found him a permission based on words of Torah. ... So too with King David, peace be upon him: Abigail was truly his match, for he afterward married her and she bore him a child, and the evil inclination found room to entice him, since she was permitted to him: Naval was a rebel against the kingship, considered as dead, and his wife was permitted. ... Thus the Sages expounded it in praise of David, that ‘He guards the feet of His pious ones’ and ‘He does not forsake His pious ones; they are guarded forever.’ Though the evil inclination found room to entice him, and he truly sensed that she belonged to him and was his match, Hashem nevertheless rescued him. Of this he said, ‘Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil,’ which refers to this flaw, ‘for You are with me,’ for the Shechinah comes with him and will not abandon him into its hand.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 5:1: “The holy Zohar then concludes: When Shabbat enters, all the tables of the people of the world who are called members of the King’s palace are arranged there, and so forth. He blesses that table, and all those thousand thousands and ten thousand myriads open their mouths and say Amen. These are the thousand thousands and ten thousand myriads which the Gemara says serve the river of fire pouring onto the heads of the wicked in Gehinnom, which is the fire of the evil inclination; yet they all say Amen to the blessing bestowed on this table of those who delight in Shabbat. Thus the Gemara says that the evil angel answers Amen against his will. It then states the blessings: ‘Then you shall delight upon Hashem.’ This is the reward of one who delights in Shabbat: he merits a revelation of Atika Kadisha, the Holy Ancient One, which is ‘upon Hashem,’ above the four-letter divine Name, for the upper tip of its letter yod alludes to Ayin, divine nothingness, as stated in Zohar III 65b; see also there, 79b. From there come all blessings: life, children, and sustenance.”

k: volume-ii|1293|0|R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be’er Mayim Chai
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be’er Mayim Chaim, Bereishit 25:31:4: “Afterward his brother came out, his hand grasping Esau’s heel (akev), for akev has the letters of beka, breaking through. Jacob alludes to the light of the ruach, the spirit, which comes afterward, and his hand and power break through the light of the nefesh from the world of Asiyah to refine the body and the nefesh. This is the meaning of the verse, ‘Then your light will break forth like the dawn’: the light that comes to a person does not arrive all at once, but little by little, like the light of dawn that shines and comes little by little until the light of full day at midday. So in a person, first comes the part of nefesh and afterward the part of ruach, and the light of ruach breaks through like the sunlight that breaks through the heavens until it reaches the body. Therefore yibaka, ‘will break forth,’ has the letters of Yaakov, as said above, to hint that Jacob’s light is what breaks through the light of the nefesh to refine the body.”

k: volume-ii|1294|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Terumah 8:16–17: “Further, in the Midrash: ‘A person may buy an acquisition and people do not know what it is, but from the broker’s fee it becomes known what he bought. So too the Torah: no one knows what it is except from the fee that Moshe took, as it says, “And Moshe did not know that the skin of his face shone when He spoke with him.”’ This is understood according to what we said above: the Torah that we grasp is only the garment of the Torah, but the inwardness of the Torah is very exalted, for the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are all one. … The Divine is not seen, nor is it known what it is, just as one cannot know what the Holy One, blessed be He, is; but from the broker’s fee that Moshe took, the actual radiance of the skin of his face, it became known that the inwardness of the Torah is the light of the face of the living King. And this itself is the conclusion of the Midrash, ‘As it were, I was sold along with it’: within the revealed Torah, which is the garment of the Torah, the Divine is hidden, and one can merit it only by way of taking. This is ‘As it were, I was sold along with it’—not by way of a gift alone, but by way of taking, as it is written, “You have taken gifts for man”: by taking it was given to him.”

k: volume-ii|1295|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Terumah 17:3: “The truth is that before the sin the Children of Israel were prepared to be like angels. Only after they sinned against their “We will do” was the counsel given through the donation for the Mishkan; and the question “Is it possible to cleave to the Shechinah?” applies only after the sin. “Let them make Me a Sanctuary” is the rectification of the realm of action, as it is written, “The gate of the inner court… shall be closed the six working days, and on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon.” The aspect of Shabbat is above the realm of action. It is the aspect of Moshe our teacher, in whom is revealed the level for which the Children of Israel were prepared before the sin, as our Sages said that Moshe our teacher returns to Israel on Shabbat the crowns that were given them at the receiving of the Torah.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sh’lach 10:1: “Each one of Israel has words of Torah in him, as stated in Vayikra Rabbah 9: ‘It does not say “the congregation of Yannai” but “the congregation of Jacob,”’ and Jacob indicates the unlearned, as stated in Bava Metzia 33b: ‘“To the house of Jacob their sins”—these are the unlearned.’ That is, even an unlearned person has words of Torah in him, as stated in Shabbat 105b, ‘To what is this comparable? To a Torah scroll that was burnt,’ and Rashi explains: there is no empty one in Israel who lacks Torah and commandments. And on Shabbat each one of Israel is considered a Torah scholar, as stated at the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, ‘Shabbat—let him make it entirely Torah’; and as the Pesikta says, the Yerushalmi’s statement, ‘Shabbatot were given only to engage in Torah,’ refers to laborers. We have said that this is the meaning of Shabbat 119a, ‘Are you more important to us than it?’: on Shabbat each one of Israel is like a Torah scholar. This is what the Tikkunim say: the additional soul that is added to Israel on Shabbat eve, Torah scholars inherit on the weekdays, for those who labor in Torah are like Shabbatot and festivals (Zohar III 124b), since they are free only for Torah; and on Shabbat all Israel are included among those who labor in Torah, and then all Israel resemble the Ark.”

k: volume-ii|1297|0|R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chai
quote: Parallel: R. Chaim of Czernowitz, Be'er Mayim Chaim, Bereshit 42:19: “Therefore the attribute of Joseph is called by the name kol, ‘all,’ as is known (Zohar Chadash), for everything is in it; that is, every aspect of the six days of building, which is the whole of the service performed in bodily things. That is the service most precious before God, and for this the whole of this world was created: to join it to heaven. And all of it is in the aspect of Joseph, who unites the whole earth to heaven, as the verse says, ‘For all (kol) that is in heaven and earth’ (I Chronicles 29:11), which the Targum renders, ‘which unites heaven and earth’; for the attribute of ‘all’ is what unites earth to heaven in its six aspects. And therefore the verse says, ‘These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph’ (Genesis 37:2) ... for whatever Jacob had learned he handed over to Joseph: he taught him to unite Hashem’s name in all his ways.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayishlach 1:2: “Of Abraham and Isaac too it says ‘with everything’ (ba-kol) and ‘of everything’ (mi-kol), from which the Sages learned (end of Bava Batra, chapter 1) that the evil inclination, the Angel of Death, and maggots and worms did not rule over them, and that they tasted a foretaste of the World to Come. That is like the holiness of Shabbat, which is a foretaste of the World to Come ... and the additional soul in which there is all perfection, after the pattern of the World to Come, as the Zohar says on Yitro: that is, without the evil inclination. ... But of them it says ba-kol and mi-kol, not kol itself, as said of Jacob. Isaac merited it through the meal Jacob fed him, for he then said, ‘I ate of everything’; as explained elsewhere, that is like the holiness of eating on Shabbat. And Abraham, Hashem blessed him with it; both merited it through their deeds. But Jacob said, ‘I have everything (kol)’: of myself, and the whole itself.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'alotcha 8:1: “The holy Zohar says (II 88b): ‘Because all faith is found on Shabbat, a person is given ... a soul in which there is all perfection, after the pattern of the World to Come.’ For on Shabbat Israel attains faith in its completeness: they cast off all their affairs and rest from their labor, and moreover spend money to delight in the Shabbat. The nations laugh at this, as written in Me‘ilah 17a, that through this the decree against Shabbat was annulled, for they said, ‘If so, let them not work on Shabbat, so that they become poor.’ And so in Eichah Rabbah: ‘Those who sit in the gate talk about me: these Jews keep Shabbat, and all they toil for all week they eat on Shabbat.’ ... But we, Israel, believe that from the day of Shabbat, and from what we spend on Shabbat, further blessing and wealth will come to us, as the holy Zohar says, ‘All blessings depend on the seventh day,’ and as the Gemara says (Shabbat 119a), ‘And in other lands, by what do they merit it? Because they honor the Shabbat.’ And this is called complete faith. And so was the manna.”

k: volume-ii|1300|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vayechi 20:3: “To delight in the Shabbat means that one takes delight in the mitzvah of Shabbat, and for its sake sets aside all worries when Shabbat comes and he rests; therefore all boundaries are removed from him. ... One may further explain ‘forever’ literally: Shabbat must remain in a person even on the days of work, for it is an eternal covenant; whenever a person remembers the Shabbat he should be full of delight and joy ... And the blessing of Shabbat is above, at the root, as the holy Zohar says that no manna was found on it because all blessings depend on the seventh day. ... And it is written, ‘Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack’: this is the flow that comes down on Shabbat, which comes from Hashem Himself, the root of blessings, ‘beside still waters,’ and is not in physical form. And it gives blessing to spread afterward through the days of work, in physical and particular form. And this is ‘You prepare a table before me,’ and so on: that is in this world, ‘in the presence of my enemies,’ for on Shabbat the Other Side has no contact at all.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Devarim 8:2: “The essence of the primordial light is stored away for the righteous in the future, as they said (Kohelet Rabbah): all the Torah a person learns in this world is vanity before the Torah of the World to Come, for the essential revelation of the Oral Torah will come through Mashiach. What is the feast that the Holy One, blessed be He, will make for the seed of Isaac? That the essential secrets will be revealed, which have not been revealed to man since the day the world was created and will be revealed in the future; and this is the matter of the wine preserved in its grapes since the six days of Creation. And on Shabbat, of which it says (Tikkunei Zohar 48), ‘Fortunate is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, and the evil inclination is cleared away from there,’ one also merits the primordial light ... but only for the moment, as a foretaste of the World to Come, one-sixtieth of the World to Come.”

k: volume-ii|1302|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala,
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Vayechi 20: “The Holy One asked Abraham: through which do you want your children to be subjugated, Gehinnom or the kingdoms?
