And he chose the kingdoms. ... But is Gehinnom called subjugation? It is punishment through suffering. Understand what is meant. When a sick man is of clear and settled mind and knows his illness, and sees a physician faithful in his love trying to heal him, giving him bitter drugs against his nature, that is not called subjugation of the sick man to the physician, since he is of sound mind; on the contrary, he rejoices and is glad in it, knowing that the faithful physician will surely heal him and is acting for his good. But if the sick man is confused in mind and does not grasp the illness and the physician, the physician’s orders weigh on him like a heavy burden ... So it is with Gehinnom and the kingdoms: Hashem, the faithful physician, works to heal us. ... In Gehinnom they have full understanding, saying, ‘Master of the world, You judged well,’ and so on (Eruvin 19a); and that is not subjugation, only joy to the soul, knowing that the faithful physician is working to heal it.”

k: volume-ii|1303|0|R. Yisrael Baal Shem Tov, Sefer Baal She
quote: Parallel: R. Yisrael Baal Shem Tov, Sefer Baal Shem Tov, Vayishlach 3: “I heard from my father and teacher, in the name of the holy Baal Shem Tov, an explanation of the verse ‘Only goodness and kindness shall pursue me all the days of my life’: Sometimes a person does not know his own good, for who is the man wise enough to understand the ways of his good? And even though the good pursues him, in Hashem’s compassion for him, wishing to shine upon him the light of salvation and success, he turns his back and not his face and flees from what was truly his good, for he has no knowledge at all that if he does this he will gain and succeed. Therefore David asked with his holy spirit, on behalf of all Israel: the goodness and kindness that You wish to do with me, and I have no knowledge to receive them and bring them to me, and perhaps I am even fleeing from them; therefore I ask of You that they pursue me, without my being able to flee from them, until I receive them and bring blessing into my house. And this is ‘shall pursue me’: they will chase after me until they overtake me.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 3:1: “It is written, ‘Only goodness and kindness shall pursue me all the days of my life,’ specifically. That is Torah, for good means only Torah (Berakhot 5a); and kindness is also words of Torah, for when his feet brought him to the study hall he would teach Torah to the many ... and Torah taught to others is a Torah of kindness (Sukkah 49b). And he said ‘shall pursue me all the days of my life,’ implying without his intent: that is, my feet lead me to the study hall every day, as it says (Sukkah 53a), ‘To the place I love, there my feet lead me.’ ... And the blemish that was written about him is ‘Your rod and Your staff,’ for through it he merited words of Torah, which are called a staff, as it says (Chagigah 14a), ‘every kind of support.’ ... And Shabbat is the day on which ‘Hashem gives you rest from your sorrow and your turmoil,’ the sorrow and turmoil of the evil inclination; for Shabbat is the time of Torah, when the words of Torah are engraved in the heart, and therefore we recite this psalm on Shabbat.”

k: volume-ii|1305|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Tora
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Shemini Atzeret 1:15: “In the Gemara at the end of the first chapter of Kiddushin, one view holds that deed is greater. This is because the deed is the person’s own arousal from below, for he exerts himself in a great deed; whereas Torah is in the aspect of speech, which is an arousal from above, higher than the arousal from below. Since the deed is the work of a person’s hands, his own action and his own arousal—by analogy, a person takes pride in what is his own, even his foot, whereas he takes no pride in what belongs to others, even a hand, which is more important, since it is not his—so in this measure the deed is truly an arousal from below, whereas the Torah is essentially a gift from above. See Zohar II, Terumah 128a, that this is why of engagement in Torah it is said, ‘Go, buy and eat… without money and without price, wine and milk,’ whereas engagement in the commandments must be at a full price specifically; see there. Therefore he said that deed is greater.”

k: volume-ii|1306|0|R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohe
quote: Parallel: R. Avraham Yehoshua Heschel of Apta, Ohev Yisrael, Terumah 3:5: “Or it may say, ‘Let them take for Me an offering,’ which Targum Yonatan renders, ‘Let them take before Me a separation.’ One may allude to this through the Gemara in Kiddushin: a woman who said to a man, ‘Here is a maneh, and I will be betrothed to you,’ is betrothed; and the Gemara concludes that this holds only for an important man, whose way is not to accept gifts from anyone in the world, so that through the pleasure she has from his accepting it from her, it is as though he gave her a perutah’s worth, and she is betrothed to him thereby. The term kiddushin is known to mean separation and setting apart: the husband says to his wife, ‘You are betrothed to me’—separated and set apart from all men, to be only mine. Now of the Creator, blessed be He, it is written, ‘Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold,’ and ‘Who has given Me anything beforehand, that I should repay him?’ He needs no donation, Heaven forbid, to help or support the building of the Mishkan, and nevertheless He commanded His holy people to raise the offering of Hashem. … Although it is not His way, as it were, to accept gifts, He nevertheless accepts from them because of the great generosity of their good hearts and their desired intent. Therefore, through that pleasure that He receives from them, they become betrothed—separated and set apart from every hold of the external forces—holy of holies and united with Him, blessed be He.”

ref: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Terumah 1
quote: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Terumah 1: “‘Speak to the Children of Israel, and let them take for Me an offering.’ That is, Hashem commanded that Israel should assist Him in all His modes of conduct, each thing in its time, as it is stated in Sefer HaBahir: ‘Raise it through your prayers. And who is the one whose heart moves him to be drawn away from this world? Honor him, for in him I rejoice, that he makes My Name known, and from him it is fitting to take My offering,’ as it says, ‘From every man whose heart moves him to give you shall take My offering’—from that one who offers himself. For Rabbi Rechumai said: The righteous and the pious of Israel, who raise Me above the whole world through their merits, and so forth.”

k: volume-ii|1308|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Ki Tisa 12:3: “So too with holy Shabbat, which is called ‘a good gift’: according to one’s toil in the working days, one is given help and support of holiness on holy Shabbat. Indeed it is written, ‘and do all your work,’ for one who serves Hashem with all his strength certainly receives Shabbat afterward in completeness. This is the hint that Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come: just as all the toil of this world is in order to attain afterward, in the World to Come, with God’s help, so it is fulfilled on Shabbat. And this is the hint of the additional soul: it is not according to the service of the one who serves; rather, as a gift, he is given more than his service. Our Sages added that it should be ‘as though all your work is done.’ This comes through longing and thoughts of repentance when holy Shabbat arrives: one who is pained over his scant preparation, that he is not ready to receive the holiness of Shabbat, can be as though all his work is done—just as the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts those who return in repentance before their departure from the world. So the books write that the eve of holy Shabbat is a day prepared for repentance.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Rosh Chodesh Shvat 1:1: “Torah without fear of Heaven is nothing, for it is called ‘a price in the hand of a fool’ (Yoma 72b); and likewise awe and prayer without Torah are nothing. As it is written in Shocher Tov on Psalms 91: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will make it known to them, as it says, ‘Therefore My people shall know My name’; at that hour they will pray and be answered, and of this it says, ‘For he knows My name; he will call Me, and I shall answer him’; see there. The Name of Hashem means the words of Torah, as Berakhot 21a derives the blessing over Torah from ‘For I shall proclaim the name of Hashem,’ for the whole Torah is the names of the Holy One, blessed be He. This is the meaning of ‘Hashem is near to all who call Him, to all who call Him in truth.’ Vayikra Rabbah 17 says: ‘To all who call Him’—could it be to all? Scripture says, ‘to all who call Him in truth’; that is, as the Gemara says, ‘Truth is Torah.’ The reason is that since Hashem gave man counsel to overcome the evil inclination through Torah, which is its antidote, he must first overcome it through Torah and afterward pray before Hashem; then he will be answered, and ‘Hashem will not leave him in his hand.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Tzav 5:2: “In Ra’aya Mehemna (Emor 92b): ‘And you shall keep—this is shamor; and you shall do—this is zachor,’ and so forth. Zachor is the place in which there is no forgetting, as stated in the holy Zohar (II 92b). That is, as it was at the giving of the Torah with the first Tablets, when it was said to all Israel, ‘And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests.’ Had it not been for the corruption, all of them would always have been free only for the Torah of Hashem, as it will be in the future: ‘Strangers shall stand and shepherd your flocks… and you shall be called the priests of Hashem; ministers of our God shall be said of you,’ and the Name Havayah, blessed be He, would be before their faces always. … Afterward it says, ‘and the son of man who holds fast to it’: one who has not merited so much and must engage in work for his livelihood, as came to be after the corruption—‘I have made my deeds evil and forfeited my livelihood.’ … Nevertheless, on Shabbat ‘let him make it entirely Torah,’ as stated at the beginning of Tanna DeVei Eliyahu, for even for laborers, who are very burdened during the working days, the Pesikta applies the statement, ‘Shabbatot were given only to engage in Torah.’”

k: volume-ii|1311|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Korach 4:13: “Still, we must understand: since he was a great sage, why did he not know and sense the difference between them? One may say, following what my father and master, of blessed memory, said: Moshe is the aspect of da’at, and he imparted da’at to all Israel, and da’at is the power to distinguish between things. This is the Gemara’s statement that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe, ‘I have a good gift in My treasure house, and Shabbat is its name, and I wish to give it to Israel; go and inform them’—that is, that he should impart to them the attribute of da’at, to know how to distinguish between Shabbat and the weekday. Therefore Korach, who separated himself from Moshe, then lacked the aspect of da’at to distinguish between his own stature and the stature of Aaron. Thus far his words. According to our approach the matter is clear: to recognize levels in their root and source requires a very clear and pure da’at.”

k: volume-ii|1312|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkut
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 5:3–10: “For example, when a person understands and grasps some halakhah in the Mishnah or Gemara clearly and thoroughly, his intellect grasps and encompasses it, and his intellect is also clothed in it at that time. Now this halakhah is the wisdom and will of the Holy One, blessed be He, for it arose in His will that if Reuven claims thus and Shimon thus, the ruling between them shall be thus. Even if this case never came and never will come to judgment, nevertheless, since so it arose in the will and wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, when a person knows and grasps this ruling with his intellect, he grasps and encompasses the will and wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, and his intellect is also clothed in them. This is a wondrous union, like which there is no other and nothing comparable anywhere in the physical world. … Because in knowing the Torah the Torah is clothed in a person’s soul and intellect and enveloped within them, it is called ‘bread’ and ‘food of the soul.’ For just as physical bread nourishes the body when one takes it inside him, where it becomes blood and flesh of his flesh, so with knowledge of the Torah in the soul of one who studies it well, until it is grasped by his intellect and unites with it and they become one: it becomes food for the soul and life within it.”

k: volume-ii|1313|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Bechukotai 4:3: “‘If you walk in My statutes (bechukotai)’ is the aspect of self-nullification to the root, for everything has a root in Heaven, and above all the soul of man. The Children of Israel cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, through the Torah, for every Jew has a portion in the Torah, and for this we ask, ‘Grant our portion in Your Torah.’ Through toil in Torah a person’s portion can become clear to him, for all things are engraved in the Torah, and so too each of the souls of the Children of Israel has an engraving in the Torah. This is ‘If you walk in My statutes,’ which our Sages expounded, ‘that you be toiling in Torah’; through this they can cleave to the root of the soul, above nature. From this comes the teaching, ‘All Israel have a share in the World to Come.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bechukotai 1:2: “Rashi explains from Torat Kohanim: ‘If you walk in My statutes’—that you be toiling in Torah, namely the Oral Torah. … And this is bechukotai, that it be engraved (nechkak) in the heart. … Shabbat too is called a statute (chok), as the Mekhilta says, ‘Statute—this is Shabbat’: on Shabbat one merits that the Oral Torah be engraved in the heart without toil. For the Yerushalmi (Shabbat 15:3) says, ‘Shabbatot were given only for eating and drinking,’ and another says, ‘Shabbatot were given only to engage in words of Torah’; and the Pesikta says they do not disagree: the one who says ‘for Torah study’ speaks of laborers, the one who says ‘for delight’ speaks of Torah scholars. … Even in engaging in Torah, one merits on Shabbat a Torah that comes without toil and is engraved in the heart. This is ‘If you walk in My statutes’: that the words of Torah be engraved in rest, on Shabbat. … This is what we say in the Havdalah prayer at the departure of Shabbat: ‘You have graced us with knowledge of Your Torah’—the Oral Torah—‘and taught us to perform the statutes of Your will,’ namely Shabbat, which is called a statute, for the words of Torah are engraved in the heart.”

k: volume-ii|1315|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Terumah 5:4–8: “In the holy Zohar: when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world He began from the side of silver, which is the right, … and in the work of the Mishkan He began from the left and afterward from the right, because the Mishkan was from the left side. This is not understood, for the whole of the Mishkan is Hashem’s kindness, that He consented to make His glory dwell among the lower beings. … There are two kinds of love. When the chamber of love above is opened, love comes from it into the heart of Israel; this is an influence from above to below. And there is love that grows from the person’s side: one who flees from external loves comes, in their place, to love of the Divine; and the source of this love is from below to above. … Love that comes through the opening of the chamber of love, from above to below, belongs to the right, for everywhere the right is an extension from above to below; but love that comes through fleeing, from below to above, belongs to the left, which is returning light. Now the words of the holy Zohar are understood, that the Mishkan was from the left side: the whole indwelling of the Shechinah in the Mishkan came through the love that belongs to the left, from below to above, which was the first intermediary; for love from the opening of the chamber is no praise for Israel, since it comes from above to below.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Masei 8: “As for the order of the Shabbat meals, the meal of Yitzchak at night before the meal of Avraham, as stated in the Writings: one may say that Avraham our father was the first soul to stir in his heart that there is a Creator of all the worlds, and he came to this through the aspect of loving-kindness all his days, until at the end of his days he came to the aspect of fear, as it was said to him, ‘Now I know that you fear God’; and Yitzchak was born to him, who is the root of the aspect of fear. But we, the Children of Israel, in whom faith is rooted from our holy fathers—believers, children of believers—and in whose nature it is implanted that Hashem created the world: for us the arousal from below must begin from the aspect of fear, and afterward we come to loving-kindness. Therefore we first say ‘Hear, O Israel,’ which is the acceptance of the kingship of Heaven, and from this we come afterward to ‘And you shall love.’ Therefore the first meal is that of the Field of Apples, the aspect of ‘a woman who fears Hashem,’ and it corresponds to Yitzchak our father, the aspect of ‘the fear of Hashem is the beginning of knowledge.’”

k: volume-ii|1317|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkut
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 42:2–5: “Every single soul of the house of Israel has within it something of the aspect of Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him. For he is one of the seven shepherds who draw down vitality and Godliness to the totality of the souls of Israel, which is why they are called ‘shepherds’; and Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, is the sum of them all and is called ‘the faithful shepherd,’ meaning that he draws down the aspect of da’at to all Israel, to know Hashem, each according to the grasp of his soul and its root above, and its nurture from the root of the soul of Moshe our teacher. … Moreover, in every generation sparks of the soul of Moshe our teacher descend and are clothed in the body and soul of the sages of the generation, ‘the eyes of the congregation,’ to teach the people da’at, to know the greatness of Hashem and to serve Him with heart and soul. … This power and attribute, to bind one’s da’at to Hashem, exists in every soul of the house of Israel through its nurture from the soul of Moshe our teacher; only, since the soul has been clothed in a body, it needs great and intense toil, double and redoubled.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa 3: “At the giving of the Torah the whole camp of Israel was designated for the Shechinah, and every place Israel encamped had the holiness of the Sanctuary; only after the corruption was the Mishkan chosen as a designated place for the indwelling of the Shechinah. … Nevertheless Israel merited this through Moshe our teacher. For at the giving of the Torah all Israel were fit for the crown of priesthood; angels came and tied two crowns on them, one corresponding to ‘We will do’ and one corresponding to ‘We will hear’ (Shabbat 88a). The crown of ‘We will do’ is the crown of priesthood, of the deed of service, and the crown of ‘We will hear’ is the crown of Torah; and the crown of Torah included the crown of kingship as well, as it says, ‘Through me kings reign.’ Once they sinned, they were stripped of them, and Moshe merited them all and took them. And concerning Shabbat, Pri Etz Chaim (Gate of Shabbat 8) states that Moshe our teacher returns the crowns to Israel on Shabbat eve. Of this we say, ‘Moshe rejoices in the gift of his portion’: on Shabbat he attains the level of light he attained at the giving of the Torah and returns the crowns to Israel. This is ‘And you, speak… but My Shabbatot you shall keep… to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you’: this is Moshe’s power, to return the crowns to Israel on Shabbat, and therefore it says of him, ‘And you.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 11: “Ox and donkey are the two kelippot of Esau and Ishmael, from which the seventy kelippot branched out, thirty-five on the right and thirty-five on the left, as the Arizal wrote. The kelippah of Ishmael is lust and evil cravings, and to this the donkey alludes, as it is written of the Egyptians, ‘whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys,’ for they were steeped in lewdness. … Every lustful person also does a deed of folly, … as it says (Sanhedrin 106a), ‘Shittim—for they engaged in matters of folly,’ and (Sotah 3a), ‘A person does not commit a transgression unless a spirit of folly enters him.’ For there is no greater folly than this, since it is a repulsive thing, ‘a woman is a skin full of filth,’ and this fool loses his world for one moment of degraded lust; therefore the kelippah of Ishmael, lust, is called a donkey. And the kelippah of Esau, jealousy and murder, is called an ox. … The Gemara (Avodah Zarah 5b) says: When they engage in Torah and acts of kindness, their inclination is given into their hand. … Issachar in holiness stands against the kelippah of Ishmael: ‘Issachar is a strong-boned donkey’—just as the donkey bears the burden, so Issachar bears the Torah; … and the burden nullifies lust. As stated (Sukkah 52b), ‘If this repulsive one meets you, drag him to the study hall’: the evil inclination of lust, called repulsive, is to be drawn to the study hall to become desire and yearning for Torah, as it will remain in the future

k: volume-ii|1320|0|R. Moshe Chaim Ephraim of Sudilkov, Dege
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Chaim Ephraim of Sudilkov, Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Terumah 7: “‘And you shall make the boards for the Mishkan of acacia wood (atzei shittim), standing.’ I received from my grandfather, of blessed memory, that the keresh (board) is a person: the letters of keresh are the letters of kesher (bond), alluding to man, who binds all the worlds and unites them with one another. Therefore a person must always bind himself and his thought to his Creator. … But if, Heaven forbid, he binds himself to folly (shtut) and the vanities of the world, which have no endurance, he is bound to falsehood (sheker), which is also the letters of keresh. … The chief purpose is that he strive to bind all things to their root and to make good of the evil in them, … for every aspect of evil is good at its root: for example, eating, drinking and marital union—when he cleaves to their root while engaged in them, through eating and drinking he raises holy sparks. … This is ‘And you shall make the boards for the Mishkan’: even when he is engaged in things that come from the side of the evil inclination, he should bind himself to their root, and thereby he raises them, and they are elevated and become good from evil. And this is ‘acacia wood’: atzei in the sense of counsels; shittim is the numerical value of satan—those things that come even from the side of the satan. ‘Standing’: they will have rising and elevation; he raises up even the aspect of evil that comes from the side of the satan

k: volume-ii|1321|0|R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat
quote: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat Levi, Vaera 3: “Let us first bring what is written in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 24): ‘You shall be holy’ (Leviticus 19:2): can it be, like Me? Scripture says, ‘for I am holy’: My holiness is above your holiness. For in truth, the more a person sanctifies and purifies himself and serves Hashem, the more he knows that he has not yet even begun to serve Him; for a person who thinks he serves Hashem, that is a sign he does not serve Him at all. ... Or it may be explained according to what our Sages said, that Israel adds strength to the heavenly retinue: the more Israel sanctifies itself, the more it adds strength and holiness above. And this is ‘My holiness above is from your holiness’: that is, through your holiness My holiness is raised and exalted higher and higher.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 5:5: “The holy Zohar says: ‘“Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who sanctified us,” and so on: this Kiddush stands in one balance opposite the testimony of faith, and they are thirty-five further words, as many as are in Vayechulu; all together they rise to seventy words, with which the Shabbat of Shabbat eve is crowned.’ The matter is that Israel must bring holiness into Shabbat, as it says, ‘Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it’: remember it with the mouth, as written in Torat Kohanim at the beginning of Bechukotai, ‘Remember: that it be repeated in your mouth.’ For Shabbat is the attribute of Malchut; and when Israel accepts the yoke of His kingship, setting aside all their affairs for the honor of Hashem on the seventh day, He is exalted and sits upon His Throne of Glory. And Israel rejoices in this acceptance of the yoke of His kingship and delights in the Shabbat, and further thanks and praises Hashem for having given them the Shabbat: by this they bring holiness into Shabbat.”

k: volume-ii|1323|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Torah Ohr, Le
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Torah Ohr, Lech Lecha 3:4: “Within this weekday there are two aspects. The first is the wholly mundane ... The second is the aspect of ordinary food prepared in the purity of holy things, like the intermediate days of a festival: that is, an illumination from holiness, the aspect of self-nullification, is drawn even into the mundane. So too, through keeping Shabbat there is an illumination in the six weekdays from the holiness of Shabbat: the first three days from the Shabbat that has passed and the last three from the coming Shabbat. And this is drawn to Israel in the six working days from the holiness of Shabbat, so that all their deeds in the weekday are like ordinary food prepared in the purity of holy things. (And this is the meaning of Havdalah at the departure of Shabbat, ‘Blessed is He who distinguishes,’ and so on: the blessing is a drawing down, that the mundane things become as if prepared in the purity of holy things.) Of this it says, ‘Six days you shall do your work’; and the six working days must come about specifically through the concealment and the screen that distinguishes between holy and mundane, for otherwise there would be complete nullification.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Toldot 10:6: “Through keeping Shabbat one is saved from the accusation of the evil inclination, as written in Pri Etz Chaim. And at the departure of Shabbat we pray, ‘Begin for us the coming days ... withheld from all sin and cleansed of all iniquity,’ that the holiness of Shabbat should help the working days too, to be saved from the accusation of the evil inclination. ‘And attached to the awe of You’: for on Shabbat Israel is called ‘those who fear My name’ (Ta‘anit 8b), and the awe of Shabbat is upon the unlearned, as stated in the Yerushalmi. And we ask concerning the working days that they be attached to the attribute of Shabbat, which is awe. And so the holy Zohar says (I 5b): ‘The Shabbat of Shabbat eve is awe, and awe dwells in it.’ And as we said, this is why the meal after Shabbat is called Melaveh Malkah: it is joined and attached to the holiness of the Shabbat meals, from the expression ‘my husband will be joined (yilaveh) to me.’ For this meal is David’s, who is the fourth leg of the Chariot.”

k: volume-ii|1325|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vay
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain, Shem MiShmuel, Vayigash 2:16: “Since the beginning was in cleaving, love, and the unity of Hashem, all the judgments were turned into kindness and mercy, and the whole exile followed after the beginning. ... And through this one may explain the matter of Havdalah at the departure of the holy Shabbat, as the Sages said, ‘Sanctify it at its departure’: that is, at the very start of entering the six working days, which are like an exile compared with the day of Shabbat. Therefore one binds oneself then in love and in blessing, and over wine specifically, whose root is above, in the place where all is joy and from which all blessings issue, as the holy Zohar says; and after the beginning of the working days everything follows. And perhaps from this came the custom of Chassidim and men of deeds to have the third meal specifically then, to draw out the holiness and cleaving with which they cleave to Hashem in songs and praises at the ‘will of wills’ as Shabbat departs and the weekdays enter ... so that all six working days will be drawn after the beginning.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Bamidbar 3:1–2: “This is why the command was that the census be done by Moshe and Aaron, together with the leaders. Moshe was for the hosts of the Torah, for every soul has a share in the Torah: a letter or part of a letter in the Torah scroll, such that if the letter or part of it is missing, the scroll is invalid. And Moshe our teacher was the root of all six hundred thousand souls, which are the letters of the Torah, and the Torah is called by his name, ‘the Torah of Moshe.’ ... And the leaders correspond to ‘by their families, by their fathers’ houses,’ for their task was that each should carry the letter of his tribe ... (Bamidbar 3:2) As they said (Avot 4), ‘There is no person who does not have his hour’: that is, each Jew, at that hour and in that matter, is the greatest of all Israel, and so his fellow at another hour. That is because each Jew has a share in the Torah, a letter or part of a letter, without which the Torah scroll is invalid.”

k: volume-ii|1327|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Tetzaveh 26:2: “In the Midrash: just as oil gives light, so the Temple gives light to the world; therefore Israel are called ‘a fresh olive tree,’ for they give light to all. The oil gives light, for through it the light takes hold of the wick; and likewise through the Temple the light took hold of the souls of Israel ... I have written elsewhere about why it sometimes says ‘You light my lamp’ and sometimes ‘You are my lamp,’ as the holy Zohar says that there is ‘oil for the light’ and there is ‘oil of the light,’ which is a higher level. For there are souls that are vessels to receive the light, and there are lofty souls that are themselves the light ... And that is the level of Moshe our teacher, ‘that he was good,’ and ‘good’ means only Torah. And this is ‘they shall take to you pure olive oil for the light’: that it is oil of the light, the light itself. Therefore it says, ‘And you shall command’: for the Torah spreads into the 248 and 365 commandments, and Moshe our teacher, the prince of the Torah, joins all the souls of Israel so that they take to him oil for the light. ... And on the holy Shabbat the light of Moshe our teacher is revealed in every Jew.”

Parallel: Takanas HaShavin 10:26: “The ark alludes to the Torah, and its substance is ‘acacia wood,’ shittim; and it is known that the stream of Shittim increases harlotry, as Tanchuma and Bamidbar Rabbah 20 say, the spring of Shittim was of harlotry … The name shittim is from shetut, folly, as in ‘if she goes astray (tisteh),’ which the Sages expound (Sotah 3a): a person sins only if a spirit of folly enters him. And the Mishkan is of acacia wood ‘standing,’ which our Sages expound: ‘Lest you say their hope is lost and their prospect void, Scripture says “standing”: they stand forever and ever.’ The same language is used (Eruvin 21b) of the completely wicked: ‘Lest you say their hope is lost and their prospect void, Scripture says … they will in the future give forth fragrance.’ … The essential holiness of the Mishkan is that His Shechinah is among Israel, ‘for the whole congregation, all of them are holy, and Hashem is among them’: that is, fenced off from forbidden relations and from the desire of the evil inclination, which drives away His Shechinah. And though it was annulled for a time in this world, so that it seems otherwise, in truth this holiness endures forever, and they will in the future give forth fragrance.”

k: volume-ii|1329|0|R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Shaar
ref: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 1:3
quote: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 1:3: “It is written, ‘Forever, Hashem, Your word stands in the heavens,’ and the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, explained: ‘Your word’ that You spoke, ‘Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters,’ and so forth: these very words and letters stand and endure forever within the firmament of the heavens and are clothed within all the heavens forever, to give them life, as it is written, ‘The word of our God shall stand forever,’ and ‘His words live and endure forever.’ For were the letters to depart for an instant, Heaven forbid, and return to their source, all the heavens would be literally nothing and naught, as if they had never been at all, exactly as before the utterance ‘Let there be a firmament.’ So too with all the creatures in all the worlds, upper and lower, and even this physical earth and the inanimate itself: were the letters of the Ten Utterances through which the earth was created in the six days of creation to depart from it for an instant, Heaven forbid, it would return to literally nothing and naught, exactly as before the six days of creation.”

k: volume-ii|1330|0|R. Yonatan Eybeschutz, Ya'arot Devash II
quote: Parallel: R. Yonatan Eybeschutz, Ya'arot Devash II 12:69: “It is all as is said: Moshe told Aharon that the incense would stop the plague, because the angel of death had transmitted it to him, for otherwise how would he have known? The matter is puzzling: what is the difficulty, ‘how would he have known’? Did not the spirit of Hashem speak through him, and the whole Torah came out of his mouth, and no secret was hidden from him? But it is all understood thus: every illness and every plague stated in the Torah is handed over to the Other Side, and therefore the healing must come through it, for He gave them over and they are theirs. … Therefore, since the plague is from him, how could the remedy come through incense, which is most holy and Heaven's portion from above?”

Parallel: Likkutei Maamarim, On Shimshon 6: “Therefore, at the time of the plague, when the incense was carried, Moshe told Aharon that the incense is life, as stated in Shabbat 89a: ‘Even the angel of death transmitted something to him,’ namely the incense, which is the very opposite of the angel of death. As I heard: the angels' transmitting something to him means that each revealed to him its essence and nature; and once the essence of death became known to him, the nature of life became known to him as well, for a thing is known only through knowing its opposite. So with Adam: before he ate from the Tree of Knowledge and did not know what death is, he also did not know what life is; but once death became known to him, it is said, ‘Lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life,’ for the nature of life too became known to him. … So too for Moshe: through the angel of death the essence of life became known to him, for knowledge of opposites is one. Nevertheless he could effect it only through Aharon, as is known in the secret of the eleven spices of the incense, which hold the power of eleven levels of evil and offer them up as a pleasing fragrance to Hashem, blessed be He; and this is through his attribute, of which they said, ‘loving peace,’ for as is known, this is the opposite of the root of evil.”

k: volume-ii|1332|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Emor 20:2: “The Midrash says: ‘The fear of Hashem is pure, enduring forever’: the fear with which Aharon feared, he merited for generations. … The fear of Hashem that leads to life is the fear of His exaltedness, and upon a priest serving Hashem in the Temple there rests the awe of Heaven like a ministering angel. … And so it says of Aharon, ‘I gave them to him for fear, and he feared Me.’ Now the holy Zohar on Yitro says that true wholeness belongs to those who fear Hashem, as it says, ‘There is no lack for those who fear Him,’ and from ‘no lack’ is implied that it is called peace. Therefore Aharon merited the attribute of peace, loving peace and pursuing peace, for Peace is the name of the Holy One, blessed be He: because the pure fear of Hashem rested upon him, he merited peace. For this reason the holy city is called Jerusalem, for the fear and the wholeness found in it. And on holy Shabbat too, when the fear of Hashem rests upon Israel, as it is taught, even upon an unlearned person the awe of Shabbat rests, it is therefore called peace.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 7:1: “In the Sanctuary itself there are also three holinesses, the table in the north, the menorah in the south, and the golden altar, and they correspond to three crowns. The crown of kingship is in the table in the north, the table of kings, which King Shlomo, peace be upon him, attained, his whole meal being recorded in Scripture forever; of this he said, ‘And this was my portion from all my labor,’ that his meal was written among words of Torah, showing that it was ‘Come, eat of my bread.’ … ‘It is vain for you,’ and so forth, ‘who eat the bread of toil’: for in words of Torah too there is what one acquires through toil, called the bread of toil … ‘So He gives to His beloved in sleep’ alludes to King Shlomo, called Yedidyah, who attained the entire Oral Torah in sleep, and to him belongs the wealth of the table of kings. … The incense altar is the crown of priesthood; the rim was made on the incense altar and not on the outer altar on which all the offerings were brought, because the essence of the crown of priesthood is Aharon's power, as it says, ‘and he turned many back from iniquity,’ and his attribute is loving peace, clarifying that even Israel's sinners will give a fragrance like galbanum. The menorah corresponds to the Oral Torah, of which the Midrash on Tetzaveh says, ‘Come and give Me light.’ … The crown of kingship is the light of the Oral Torah that Hashem gives as a gift, as He gave to King Shlomo in a dream; the menorah is the

k: volume-ii|1334|0|R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat
quote: Parallel: R. Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, Kedushat Levi, Tetzaveh 2–3: “This is the hint in the Gemara (Ta‘anit 11b): in what did Moshe serve during the days of inauguration? In a white shirt without a hem. ... For Moshe our teacher was not a priest; from where did he here merit the level of a High Priest, to serve in the days of inauguration? That is the hint in the shirt: through his cleaving to the Ayin, the Divine Nothing. ... In every place where it is written ‘as Hashem commanded Moshe,’ it hints that Moshe did not attain this from his own intellect, only what Hashem commanded with Moshe, as we say in the Gemara, the Shechinah speaks from Moshe’s throat. The Mishkan corresponded to Israel, and Moshe grasped the making of the Mishkan when Hashem told it to him; but the priestly garments, since Moshe was not a priest, he did not attain except when he was nullified in his existence and the Creator spoke with him. ... And this is the hint and the answer to the question above, why Moshe’s name is not mentioned in parashat Tetzaveh: for parashat Tetzaveh was said mainly about the making of the priestly garments, and Moshe was nullified in his existence in order to attain the making of the priestly garments; and when a person is nullified in his existence his name is not called upon him.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshat Zachor 13:1: “So too Haman’s accusation, from Amalek’s seed, came when the time arrived for the spread of the Oral Torah through the Men of the Great Assembly, who enacted decrees and fences, as it says (Eruvin 21b), ‘I have imposed many decrees on myself, more than You decreed upon me.’ Daniel was the first, for it is written, ‘Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king’s food or with the wine he drank’: that is, the decree against their wine and oil on account of their daughters, and their daughters too are a decree (Avodah Zarah 36b). We have already said that Haman’s accusation, ‘Their laws differ from every people’ — they do not eat our food or marry from us (Megillah 13b) — was meant as an accusation above, before Hashem, against this decree: that their intent was not for the sake of Heaven but out of pride and hatred of people. Of this he said, ‘And they do not keep the king’s laws,’ for wherever Scripture says ‘the king’ without a name it refers to both the holy and the profane: that is, their intent in this is not to keep the laws of the King of kings.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Tisa 3:1: “The second tablets included all of the Oral Torah, midrash, laws, and aggadot ... and this was needed after the corruption, much wisdom to repair much vexation, as it says (Nedarim 22b), ‘Had they not sinned, they would have been given only the five books of the Torah.’ And this power was Moshe our teacher’s alone, as it says, ‘Carve for yourself two tablets of stone.’ ... But the essential power for Israel to receive the light of the Oral Torah came through Moshe our teacher, who is in the mystery of Da‘at. ... Therefore it is written, ‘And you shall command the children of Israel, and they shall take oil for you’: for this is a decree from Moshe’s side, and through it he gives Israel the power to receive the light of the Oral Torah, as it says, ‘Carve for yourself.’ ... So too ‘And you, bring near,’ for Aharon’s holiness would be needed after the first tablets, those of the giving of the Torah, were broken, for then it was written, ‘You shall be for Me a kingdom of priests’: all Israel were fit for the crown of priesthood ... Therefore ‘and you’ is written in all of these, for this act was needed from the side of Moshe our teacher, who broke the tablets of his own accord and was commanded to carve second tablets, as a preparation to receive much wisdom to repair much vexation.”

k: volume-ii|1337|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala,
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Agra DeKala, Tetzaveh 1: “We must consider why Hashem said this passage in such a way, ‘you will later command,’ and not command it now ... and also His saying, ‘They shall take to you oil,’ when it is a mitzvah for all generations, at every time, to light the menorah. But consider what the Sages said in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah 36:1): ‘And you shall command’—this is what Scripture says, ‘A fresh olive tree, fair with goodly fruit, Hashem called your name.’ Why did Jeremiah compare Israel to an olive tree? All liquids mix with one another, but oil does not mix; it stays apart. So Israel does not mix with the nations. It seems the Midrash is also attending to ‘and you shall command ... they shall take to you olive oil.’ For Moshe our teacher accepted the mixed multitude, as is known, and through them came about what came about. Here it was still before the sin (according to the Zohar), so He did not yet command him the details to tell Israel; Hashem only said, you will later command, ‘they shall take to you.’ For it was revealed before Him that they would sin through the mixed multitude, and then He would command him, ‘they shall take to you,’ specifically, since you accepted the mixed multitude: pure olive oil, to which Israel is compared, for they cannot mix with the nations.”

Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Hoshana Rabbah 1: “This day is the portion of King David, peace be upon him, for King David is called ‘living and enduring.’ And who is fit to be called living and enduring? One who recognizes well in his heart that Hashem, blessed be He, is living and enduring, that is, who recognized that Hashem, blessed be He, pours forth life at every moment. As we see, after all his service he took no strength at all for himself but returned everything to Hashem, blessed be He, as the Gemara says (Bava Kamma 61a): ‘David did not wish to drink them,’ for he did not state them in their names; he said, ‘Thus I have received … whoever gives himself over for words of Torah, no halakhic teaching is stated in his name.’ That is, after all the self-sacrifice he had, he took no strength for himself. Therefore Scripture says of him, ‘the faithful kindnesses of David’ (Isaiah 55:3): Hashem, blessed be He, showed him how his own grasp is joined with the light of Hashem, blessed be He.”

k: volume-ii|1339|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Tetzaveh 1:2: “It is known that because Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, said, ‘Erase me, please, from Your book,’ his name is not mentioned in this portion. My father, my teacher, of blessed memory, gave the reason: according to what the holy Zohar says in the portion Az Yashir, and the Ramak there in Zaharei Chamah, the name of Moshe our teacher corresponds to nefesh, ruach and neshamah. Now it is known that the parts of the soul are five: nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah. Nefesh, ruach and neshamah are clothed within the body, while chayah and yechidah are not clothed in the body; and a person's name expresses the bond between soul and body and its endurance. Therefore the name of Moshe our teacher extended only to those three, nefesh, ruach and neshamah. But because Moshe our teacher gave over his soul for Israel, he attained the level that is not clothed in the body; therefore his name is not mentioned in this portion, for he reached a level that has no name. If so, his name's absence from the portion is no deficiency or diminution of Moshe, Heaven forbid; on the contrary, it is to the praise and greatness of Moshe our teacher. This is what the Sages said: whoever gives himself over for words of Torah, no halakhic teaching is stated in his name, ‘his name’ precisely.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 4:1: “So too on Shabbat eve, before Shabbat entered, it is written, ‘God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good,’ which they expounded (Bereshit Rabbah 9) as referring to everything opposite: the evil inclination and Gehinnom. For then the whole of creation found favor in His eyes, blessed be He … This was during the addition to Shabbat, for afterward it says, ‘There was evening and there was morning, the sixth day. And they were completed,’ and so forth. That is, then Hashem, blessed be He, saw that even the ‘formless and void,’ which is expounded (Bereshit Rabbah 2) as the deeds of the wicked, exists only so that there be light that emerges from darkness, and it be very good. … Since the addition to Shabbat comes from the human side, whenever there is one who keeps Shabbat and adds from the weekday to the holy, Hashem, blessed be He, also keeps the addition to Shabbat. But at the hour of creation, when there was as yet no one keeping it, for Adam had corrupted on Shabbat eve, Hashem entered it by a hair's breadth and did not keep the addition. … ‘And they were completed’: it was completed of itself through the merit of the addition to Shabbat that comes from the one who keeps Shabbat. And afterward it is written, ‘God completed on the seventh day’: this is the fixed and enduring holiness from Hashem, blessed be He, which He gave to Shabbat.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Zachor 5:1: “‘And in sin my mother conceived me’: that is, the sin of the impurity of menstruation and the impurity of childbirth, which is also the serpent's blemish, for it was said to her, ‘In pain you shall bear children.’ This is the chief power of Amalek, inwardly, in every soul. So we find with Yabetz, of whom it is written, ‘His mother called his name Yabetz, saying, “For I bore him in pain.”’ She sensed that her pain was exceedingly great, and from this she sensed that such a precious soul would be born that the serpent was striving to trip it up through that pain. Therefore she called him Yabetz, to turn the pain to good, for on this account he was called Yabetz: he counseled and spread Torah in Israel (Temurah 16a). Through his dialectic he restored the laws forgotten in the days of mourning for Moshe, and this is the essential power of the Oral Torah, which is bound at its root to Atika … Through the reasons of Torah one reaches the root that is beyond comprehension, and precisely this is the power to subdue Amalek, the first of the husks, which stands against it.”

k: volume-ii|1342|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Vaera 24:2: “It is taught that Shabbat is the aspect of Moshe, as it says, ‘Moshe rejoices in the gift of his portion,’ and on it the Torah was given. This is the difference: all the prophets prophesied through a speculum that does not shine, ‘Thus says Hashem,’ while Moshe our teacher prophesied ‘This is the word,’ through the speculum that shines. A speculum that does not shine means an illumination that must be clarified out of the darkness, as it says, ‘There was evening and there was morning.’ For the light that is renewed each day accords with the clarification one effects, as it says, ‘first darkness and afterward light,’ and it depends on human service. But Shabbat is a good gift and an additional soul that comes from the upper world. … The days of labor are for repairing oneself and finding the hidden light within oneself, while Shabbat is an addition of new light from above.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayakhel 10:1: “These are the two Shabbatot: first a person merits the lower Shabbat, which is awe, ‘she is awe, and awe dwells in her.’ Afterward he merits bringing holiness into the heart, until it benefits even the weekdays that follow, so that all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven and are like the work of the Mishkan. … Otherwise, even though through keeping Shabbat one merits being guarded from sin and saved from the accusation of the evil inclination, as it says, ‘who keeps Shabbat from desecrating it and keeps his hand from doing any evil,’ nevertheless after Shabbat the evil inclination returns to its place. And even on Shabbat the evil inclination can enter to entice, so that one becomes among ‘those who desecrate it,’ for the serpent entered the Garden of Eden to entice Adam. For this reason King Shlomo, peace be upon him, said ‘This too is vanity’ concerning the day of Shabbat, as Shocher Tov, Psalms 92, says; therefore the punishment of the Shabbat desecrator is stated here. But once they merit ‘to make them,’ precisely the two Shabbatot, meriting the upper Shabbat from which the evil inclination departs entirely, then they are redeemed completely.”

k: volume-ii|1344|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Parashat Zachor 8:3: “‘The stragglers behind you’ are our generations, as it was then, especially those whom the cloud cast out; for with the inwardness of Israel he certainly has no contact. Therefore on holy Shabbat, when Hashem, blessed be He, spreads the shelter of peace over us, we can erase him. That is why the Sages set the reading of Parashat Zachor on the Shabbat before Purim, for one must prepare from Shabbat the strength to erase him during the days of labor. … The main stumbling blocks Amalek made for us are only in the later generations; on holy Shabbat Israel has the strength of the earlier generations, as it says, Moshe our teacher returns the crowns to us every Shabbat, and Israel has unity, as it says, they unite in the mystery of One, and he has no contact with us on holy Shabbat. Then is the time to remember against him enmity and hatred. This is what it says, ‘When Hashem your God grants you rest from all your enemies round about’: this is holy Shabbat, when we come to the root of rest.”

k: volume-ii|1345|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Beha'alotcha 6:3: “My father, his holy honor, said that Shabbat is like the menorah: the three days before Shabbat and the three days after Shabbat all face toward Shabbat, the seventh, like the three branches of the menorah on each side that face the middle one. And we may add after him, following our approach that the menorah is the constant renewal of love between Israel and their Father in heaven: so too Shabbat, each Shabbat in itself holds new lights that never existed before. As the Ohr HaChaim wrote, all of creation was made only until Shabbat, and on Shabbat creation is renewed again for seven days, until the next Shabbat. Therefore every Shabbat is entirely new, and it is in every person's hand to begin entirely anew: what was, was; from here on the reckoning begins. And this is the acrostic of Shabbat: shabbat, ‘in it you shall return,’ for this is the essence of repentance, to begin entirely anew, to be like a convert who has converted, who is like a newborn child.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 11:2: “The incense too serves to repair, so that they will be in the state of ‘Your people are all righteous,’ for mixed into the incense was galbanum, which indicates the sinners of Israel, as they learned from it (Keritot 6b): any fast that does not include sinners of Israel, and so forth. Chelbenah, galbanum, is the letters of levanah, whiteness, with a chet; levanah alludes to His future whitening of Israel's sins, as Yoma 39b expounds: why is it called Levanon? Because it whitens the sins of Israel. … The chet that is added, which indicates darkness, is the aspect of ‘He made darkness His hiding place,’ hidden from all thought, while He lives at the height of the world; through this the deeds of the wicked branched out, which is the galbanum, since the light was hidden. … And so it was in the first thought of creation, that first there be darkness and afterward light, for there is no light except that which emerges from darkness, as Zohar II 184a says; and then the galbanum too will give a good fragrance. This comes only through Aharon the priest, of whom it is written, ‘For the lips of the priest guard knowledge, and they seek Torah from his mouth’: the root of the Oral Torah, the abundant wisdom that repairs the abundant vexation, so that ‘Your people are all righteous.’ Through this the primordial light is revealed … and this is ‘oil and incense gladden the heart.’”

Parallel: Takanas HaShavin 10:32: “There, in Bava Metzia, they began with the account of Rabbi Yochanan's beauty, who remained of the beautiful ones of Jerusalem. This is the beauty of the righteous who guard the covenant, as with ‘Yosef was handsome of form and handsome of appearance.’ For the Torah does not speak in praise of the imaginary beauty of this world; one who has eyes will see that it is the utmost ugliness, like the children of Cushites. There is no beauty in the flesh of the body except in the holy flesh of the seed of Israel, and this is the ‘nine measures of beauty that Jerusalem took’ of the ten measures that came down to the world (Kiddushin 49b): that is, what is called beauty in truth. This is why he sat at the gates of immersion, ‘so that their children will be beautiful like me and learned in Torah like me.’ Had he meant bodily beauty alone, he would not have sat at the gates of immersion for that, and certainly he would not have put it before ‘learned in Torah.’ Necessarily it is as I have written: he meant what Hashem, blessed be He, the Torah, and Israel who follow in its footsteps call ‘beauty of the body.’ And this comes through awe … for the awe of God annuls evil desires.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 8:1: “The Shabbat meal is in the mystery of oneg, delight, which the holy Zohar (I 26a, end) says is the initials of Eden, nahar, gan: ‘a river goes out of Eden to water the garden,’ the drawing down from Eden to the garden. … What the Sages say in praise of one who delights the Shabbat applies only when the intention is for the sake of Heaven; as we noted, they said ‘one who delights the Shabbat,’ not ‘one who takes delight on Shabbat,’ and likewise it says, ‘You shall call the Shabbat a delight’: this is the additional soul, which is called Shabbat, as the holy Zohar on this portion says (II 88b), and it delights in the pleasures of Israel on Shabbat. … Afterward it speaks of Torah scholars, who are free all the weekdays for words of Torah, and Torah scholars resemble Shabbatot, as the Ra'aya Mehemna says (III 29b, 124b end). On Shabbat they give delight, as the Pesikta says, and their eating is literally words of Torah, in the sense of ‘Your Torah is within my innards’; they draw from Eden to the garden through food, drink and clean clothing.”

k: volume-ii|1349|0|R. Meir of Apta, Ohr LaShamayim, Achrei
quote: Parallel: R. Meir of Apta, Ohr LaShamayim, Achrei Mot 2: “‘No man shall be in the Tent of Meeting.’ The commentators of Rashi on the Torah asked about the expression ‘no man’: was Aharon not there? It appears that there are several levels in the service of Hashem, and the level of ‘man,’ adam, is very high; only one who has perfected his nefesh, ruach and neshamah is called by the name adam, and anyone else is called ‘human flesh.’ … Besides the levels of nefesh, ruach and neshamah there are also the levels of chayah and yechidah, and there is complete oneness, of which one cannot even speak of binding together. … The man who is not at the level of chayah and yechidah, even though he has reached the level of adam described above, nevertheless cannot approach the inner sanctum. This is ‘no man’: whoever is only at the level of adam ‘shall not be in the Tent of Meeting when he comes to atone in the Holy.’”

Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 8:12: “Eliyahu became entirely an angel, and Pinchas too was at first like an angel … and he is called ‘the angel of the covenant,’ and a chair is prepared for him at every circumcision (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 29). … Therefore Avraham our father, peace be upon him, the head of the circumcised, raises all Israel up from Gehinnom, as Eruvin 19a says … except for one who has relations with an Aramean woman, whose foreskin is drawn and he does not recognize him. Through the desire he has to cleave to the nations and be drawn after her until she is bound to him, she becomes for him a foreskin enclosing the circumcision. Yet the one whose foreskin is drawn is also circumcised by Torah law, and only because of appearance must he be circumcised again (Yevamot 72a). This is ‘he does not recognize him’: from the side of man, who sees with the eyes, he does not recognize him and thinks he is uncircumcised, and no one saves him except Hashem, blessed be He, Himself, who ‘sees into the heart,’ for even he is circumcised at the root of the depths of his heart. And Pinchas, who is Eliyahu the angel of the covenant, was zealous over this one who draws his foreskin and appears uncircumcised to human eyes, and merited to be transformed into an angel.”

k: volume-ii|1351|0|R. Moshe Teitelbaum, Yismach Moshe, Besh
quote: Parallel: R. Moshe Teitelbaum, Yismach Moshe, Beshalach 35:3: “Our Sages said in Berakhot 10b: ‘He is a holy man of God.’ How did she know? Because she never saw a fly passing over his table. This is puzzling: where do we find that no fly passes over the table of a holy man? It appears to me that it follows the Sages' statement (Berakhot 61a) that the evil inclination resembles a fly and sits between the two openings of the heart, as it says, ‘Dead flies cause a stench.’ It is clear that the wicked serves only his inclination; the intermediate serves his Maker and his inclination … and one who does nothing at all for his own pleasure, even in what is permitted to him, but all is service of Heaven, is called holy, as the Sages said, ‘Sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you.’ … One said, a linen sheet …, and there is no greater fence than not to have impure thoughts at all; and one said, she never saw a fly passing over his table, for at his table too, in his eating, she understood that the evil inclination had no hold at all. … The reason the evil inclination is likened to a fly is explained by the Kli Yakar: a fly's mouth is weak and cannot pierce whole flesh, but where it finds an open wound it settles and widens the breach. So too the evil inclination is too weak to breach the living flesh, that is, the righteous; but wherever it finds even a small breach, there it crouches to widen it.”

Parallel: Yisrael Kedoshim 1:4: “They said there (Berakhot 10b): ‘How did she know?’ For the holiness of the covenant belongs to private matters that are not visible. One said, ‘She never saw a fly on his table’: that is, she recognized in his eating that it was not with the desire of the inclination, which is likened to a fly, as they said there (61a end); and from this she knew that he was fenced off from forbidden relations as well. The other said, ‘She spread a linen sheet for him and never saw an emission on it,’ even though the strain of travel brings an emission even to the pious at times, as they said in Shabbat 127b. A person cannot guard against this through his own effort; it happens only as he is guarded from above, according to how he sanctifies himself below, as they said in Yoma 39a. One who sanctifies himself below to the utmost of human power is sanctified from above to the utmost of divine power, which has no measure, and is saved even from impurities that are unavoidable by the nature of this world.”

k: volume-ii|1353|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayakhel 8:2, 8:7–8: “‘Moses assembled the entire congregation of the children of Israel and said to them: These are the things that Hashem commanded … Six days shall work be done’ (Exodus 35:1–2), and afterward he began the work of the Mishkan. The commentators asked why here he placed ‘assembled’ first, more than with all the other commandments, and why here Shabbos comes before the work of the Mishkan, whereas in the command given to Moshe the work of the Mishkan came before Shabbos. My father, of holy memory, answered the one through the other: since the one Mishkan required that all Israel be as one man, he placed Shabbos first, for it is the mystery of One. ... And this itself was the matter of the Mishkan: one Mishkan joined together from different donations from every part of Israel. ... This is the meaning of ‘Moses assembled,’ which was not said in Hashem’s command to Moshe, given before the deed of the Calf, when there was no need for Israel’s unity, and even a single Jew could have made it. But here, after the deed of the Calf, when Israel had lost the virtue of that bond, a new joining and a collective power were needed, and it had to draw help from the power of Shabbos, the mystery of One. So they all became one band, and like one man with one heart they all gave for one Mishkan.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'alotcha 3:2: “The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Go tell Aharon, ... the lamps are forever, and all the blessings I gave you to bless My children will never be annulled. ... The power remains forever with Aharon and his sons to bestow on Israel the light of the Oral Torah. ... Through the Priestly Blessing the kohanim bestow on Israel the light of the Oral Torah. The first blessing, ‘May Hashem bless you,’ refers to words of Torah, for each one blesses with what is his power and level, and Aharon’s power is the Oral Torah, as it says, ‘For a kohen’s lips guard knowledge, and Torah shall they seek from his mouth.’ Therefore his blessing, ‘May Hashem bless you,’ is increase and abundance in the Oral Torah. ... ‘And grant you peace’: this blessing too refers to Torah, as the Sifrei expounds, for it says, ‘Hashem will give strength to His people; Hashem will bless His people with peace’; that is the Oral Torah, for the essence of the Oral Torah comes through peace, which is the level of Yosef, through whom the flow passes from the Written Torah, Tiferes, to the Oral Torah, Malchus. ... There can be no truth except where there is peace.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Mishpatim 6:8–9: “In Parashat Ki Tisa it is written, ‘Six days shall work be done,’ in the passive, and in Vayakhel, ‘te’aseh melakhah,’ rather than the active ‘six days shall you labor’ as in the Ten Commandments. The distinction is this: in the Ten Commandments, where Scripture speaks of ordinary labor, it writes ‘you shall labor’; but in Ki Tisa and Vayakhel, where they were occupied with building the Mishkan, the holy work was done as if by itself, as Shir HaShirim Rabbah expounds on Solomon’s Temple, ‘and the house, when it was being built,’ that it was built by itself; and the holy Zohar (Pekudei 222b) says the same of the Mishkan ... Therefore Scripture writes in the passive, ‘work shall be done,’ for it was done by itself. In Parashat Emor too it is written, ‘Six days shall work be done,’ although it speaks of ordinary weekdays ... For the preparation for Shabbat begins from the six working days, that all a person’s deeds be for the sake of Heaven ... and everything is elevated like the building of the Mishkan, bringing holiness into the coming Shabbat. Therefore Scripture uses the passive there too, because it belongs to the labor of the Mishkan, which is done by itself, as the holy Zohar says, ‘and so with every holy work, it is completed by itself.’”

k: volume-ii|1356|0|R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or E
quote: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Me'or Einayim, Vayakhel 1: “As one works during the six weekdays, so he feels in himself the holiness of Shabbat, and afterward the holiness of Shabbat is drawn for him also into the six weekdays to come, as is known: until Wednesday the light of the past Shabbat remains, and from Wednesday the holiness of the coming Shabbat sparkles in the soul. Through this the building of the labor of the Mishkan is done with help from above, drawn from the holiness of the past and the coming Shabbat. ... And Moshe assembled the whole congregation of Israel and said to them, These are the things that God commanded to do them: all the things of the world, in the thirty-nine labors, and all earthly speech, which God commanded to do, ‘to do’ meaning repair ... for the repair was given over to Israel, to raise all the things that fell in the shattering, and this is the building of the labor of the Mishkan. But ‘six days labor shall be done’: it shall be done by itself, as said above, through supernal help from the holiness of the past and coming Shabbat.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 9:1–4: “In the first Tablets, ‘Remember’ is written ... When Israel heard ‘I am,’ the study of Torah was fixed in their hearts, and when they heard ‘You shall have no,’ the evil inclination was uprooted from their hearts. It would have sufficed to say ‘Remember’ with the mouth at the start of Shabbat, and it would have been guarded all Shabbat by the holiness of Shabbat, which is fixed and established by God. This is not so in the second Tablets, which come after the corruption: there is written ‘Guard,’ for guarding is needed all day so that one not spoil it, Heaven forbid; as the Midrash Shocher Tov says, ... He saw that a person sins on it and becomes liable with his life, and He said, ‘This too is vanity.’ Since it is written ‘its desecrators,’ the evil inclination can enter and desecrate the Shabbat, Heaven forbid, and ‘Guard’ is needed, through awe, which is human effort. ... In the second Tablets it is written, ‘Therefore the Lord your God commanded you to make the Shabbat day,’ that is, the upper Shabbat, which the penitent attains through the effort of awe. ... And the Tikkunei Zohar: ‘Twice Shabbat is mentioned here, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah,’ that is, the upper Shabbat and the lower Shabbat, both of which are awe. When awe enters the depth of the heart ... ‘Happy is one who makes them a dwelling on Shabbat in the two chambers of the heart, and the evil inclination is cleared out from there.’”

k: volume-ii|1358|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Bamidbar, Korach 7:2: “The completeness, which is the preparation of the recipients to be a vessel that holds blessing, is also from the Creator, as it is written, ‘God will give strength to His people; God will bless His people with peace.’ This is the ‘city of strength,’ the aspect of the Oral Torah, ‘eternal life He planted within us.’ And He is called ‘the King to whom peace belongs,’ for no creature can attain completeness except with help from above. It is written, ‘He makes peace in His heights’: although above there is neither jealousy nor hatred, even so they cannot attain completeness except with God’s help. ... As the Mishnah says, ‘Every dispute that is for the sake of Heaven’: Hillel and Shammai; ‘and that is not for the sake of Heaven’: the dispute of Korach. This too is the meaning of ‘He makes peace in His heights’: those who exalt Him, all of whose disputes are for the sake of Heaven. For this one is fire and that one is water, but the whole aim of both is to fulfill the supernal will, and then He makes peace among them.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chanukah 8: “Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel are called in the Mishnah (Eduyos 1:4) ‘fathers of the world,’ and so too in the holy Zohar (III 73a), ‘fathers of the world.’ Hillel was from the side of mercy, the level of Abraham, and Shammai from the side of judgment, Gevurah, the level of Isaac, as written in the Ra’aya Mehemna (III 245a). And so the Arizal wrote that in the time to come the halacha will follow Beis Shammai. This follows what our Sages said, that at first it arose in thought to create the world with the attribute of judgment, and afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, joined the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment ... and this is ‘The world is built with kindness.’ ... Therefore in this world, which is conducted by the order in which God placed the attribute of mercy before the attribute of judgment, the halacha follows Beis Hillel. But in the time to come, when every flaw of the serpent is repaired and it will be as it arose in thought, ‘God made man upright,’ and the world will be able to be conducted by the attribute of judgment, the halacha will follow Beis Shammai. So too with the righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting even to a hairsbreadth, for they can conduct themselves according to the original thought.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 13:1: “As it says in Ra'aya Meheimna (III 232b): ‘Because the mixed multitude are the leaven in the dough …, they delay more in exile.’ ‘What prevents us? The leaven in the dough’: in the Gemara (Berakhot 17a) they said, ‘What prevents us?
