The mixed multitude came through Moshe our teacher, who accepted them, as stated (Shemot Rabbah 42): ‘Go down, for your people has corrupted … I told you not to mix the mixed multitude with them; you, being humble and upright, told Me: One always accepts those who return.’ By law there was no need to accept the mixed multitude, since they converted only because they saw Israel's greatness, just as converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah, nor were they accepted in the days of David or Solomon (Yevamot 24b). Nevertheless, since Moshe accepted them, after the fact they were converts, as the Rambam writes (Forbidden Relations 13:15). And through the mixed multitude the leaven in the dough branched out into the heart of Israel. For at the giving of the Torah it is written, ‘I said, You are divine beings,’ ... and the evil inclination was then abolished as well. ... But afterward, ‘you corrupted your deeds; therefore like men you shall die,’ and this refers to the deed of the Calf, which was done th

k: volume-ii|1361|0|R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem
quote: Parallel: R. Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayakhel 13:20–21: “In the holy Zohar: ‘Come and see, what is written at first? “From every man whose heart prompts him,” to include everyone ... and because the mixed multitude were among them, it was said, “From every man.” Afterward each kind turned to its own kind, and the mixed multitude came and made the calf. ... The Holy One, blessed be He, said: From now on the work of the Mishkan shall be only from the side of Israel alone ... “from among yourselves,” certainly, and not as at first. ... “Moses assembled”: from where did he assemble them? Because the mixed multitude was among them, Moshe needed to gather them and unite them apart from them.’ This is explained by what my father, of holy memory, said: if within a bundle and a union there is one who is unfit, he spoils the whole bundle, as he derived from the Gemara in Sanhedrin: if the lulav needs binding, a fifth species is a defect. ... Therefore, while the mixed multitude was among them, the bundle was defective and did not count as a union. ... By this one can give a reason why a gentile who rests on Shabbos is liable to death, and for the Midrash's parable of a king and a matrona who sat conversing: whoever puts his head between them is liable to death. For Shabbos is the mystery of One, and a gentile who keeps Shabbos brings a stranger into the unity of One.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Korach 2:1: “Moshe our teacher answered them that even a garment entirely of blue needs one thread of blue in its tzitzis, as it says, ‘so that you remember,’ for even a soul full of fear of Heaven can come to forgetfulness unless he constantly sets it on his heart as a reminder, as the Sages said, ‘Do not trust yourself.’ ... And for this reason Aharon specifically was chosen to be the Kohen Gadol, which is the aspect of the Holy of Holies: because he was always afraid for his soul lest he sin and fall short of the goal of His blessed will. As is known, because you are ashamed of yourself and afraid to approach, since you are distant in your own eyes, for that reason you were chosen specifically to be the Kohen Gadol, to offer sacrifices on behalf of the souls of all Israel who have become distant, even utterly distant, in order to bring them back to holiness. And this is the aspect of the Queen's attendant.”

k: volume-ii|1363|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech Shapira of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Shabbatot 10:9: “In the Gemara (Shabbat 118b): ‘The delight of Shabbat: with what does one delight it? ... With a dish of beets, large fish, and heads of garlic.’ Rashi explains: ‘it is important,’ and ‘these were important to them.’ We must consider: large fish are known to be important, ... and heads of garlic belong to the enactment to eat garlic on Shabbos nights. But a dish of beets, what is its importance? Yet Rashi was careful to say ‘it is important,’ implying that its importance is known to all. It seems to me, according to what the masters of truth wrote: one who does not delight the Shabbat, his oneg (delight) is turned for him into nega (affliction); and conversely, whoever delights the Shabbat is healed of affliction, and the nega is turned for him into oneg. Now the Sages said (Shabbat 133b): one who washed his face and did not dry it well, scabs break out on him; ... what is his remedy? Let him wash much in beet water. So you see that a dish of beets is a remedy for affliction, and the delight of Shabbat is a remedy for affliction. As a reminder of this one eats a dish of beets, which is a remedy for affliction.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Emor 6:2: “This is ‘Draw near, wedding attendants’: these are the holiness of the festivals, ... ‘make preparations,’ so that each one brings its holiness into the Shabbat day; ‘to increase varieties,’ for Shabbat is called a holy convocation, and the Midrash says, ‘With what do you sanctify it? With food and drink,’ and this is ‘to increase varieties,’ many kinds, as the holy books say, in order to complete a hundred blessings. ... ‘And fish with the small ones’ means large fish and small. The matter is as the Gemara says (Shabbat 118b): ‘With what does one delight it? ... and large fish,’ and one who cannot afford it, ‘even a small thing ... a dish of small fish.’ It is as we said, that the essence of Shabbat delight is in fish, because they have no prohibition of forbidden fat or the sciatic nerve, whereas birds at least have the prohibition of blood and carcasses. This implies that fish have no mixture of good and evil, for Chavah fed all the animals, beasts and birds from the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, but this was not said of the fish. And it mentions large fish and small according to what the holy Arizal wrote on the Gemara (Shabbat 101b): when one is poor in understanding he cannot draw out the holy sparks even from large fish, so he does a small thing in honor of Shabbat, small fish; and the rich in understanding delights it with large fish, for he is able to draw out the holy sparks from them.”

k: volume-ii|1365|0|R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet,
quote: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefat Emet, Bereshit 16:3: “In the Midrash: ‘And He blessed it’ (Genesis 2:3): He blessed it with lights; the light of a person’s face on the weekdays is not like the light of his face on Shabbos. That is, the revelation of the inner dimension, as it is written, ‘A person’s wisdom lights up his face’ (Ecclesiastes 8:1), and this is the revelation of the additional soul. In the world as a whole, too, the inner dimension is revealed on the holy Shabbos, for it is written, ‘Let there be light,’ and the Sages expounded that He hid it away for the righteous. The utterance ‘Let there be light’ is present in every detail, for every work of Creation has a share in this light, only it was hidden away, and on Shabbos something of it is revealed. On the weekdays it is the aspect of a speculum that does not shine, and on Shabbos a shining speculum. Therefore lighting a lamp on Shabbos is a mitzvah, to allude to the revelation of the light on the holy Shabbos.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeshev 6:1: “In the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 11): ‘He blessed it with the light of a person’s face: the light of a person’s face all the days of the year is not like it is on Shabbos.’ ... The Sages said: at the departure of Shabbos his radiance was taken from him and He drove him from the Garden, ‘You change his face and send him away’; so on Shabbos he had the light of his face as he was created. ... The beginning of the serpent’s corruption was through eating, and therefore whoever merits to repair his eating, so that it is in holiness, merits the image of Adam before the corruption. Therefore on Shabbos, when every Jew eats in holiness, we merit the image of Adam; this is ‘He blessed it with the light of a person’s face,’ that on Shabbos we merit new faces, the image of Adam, and this is what we say, ‘Indeed, new faces.’ ... It is written, ‘A person’s wisdom lights up his face’: there is a higher wisdom, of which it is said, ‘For Hashem gives wisdom,’ and there is a lower wisdom, the wisdom of Shlomo, the Oral Torah, and this is called ‘a person’s wisdom,’ and of it is said ‘lights up his face.’ ... And this is ‘Indeed, new faces and spirits with souls.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 5:1: “The holy Zohar says: ‘the mystery of the testimony of the work of Creation,’ that is, Vayechulu, ‘for in this testimony there are thirty-five words: thirty-two paths and three levels of holy apples.’ This is alluded to in the song ‘to make ... with two and thirty, and with three branches’: two and thirty are the thirty-two names of Elohim in the work of Creation, which are the thirty-two paths of wisdom with which Hashem created His world. ... ‘Three branches’ are boughs, for shevashin is the Aramaic rendering, the three levels of holy apples, which the holy Zohar says are the three names of Elohim in the passage of Vayechulu. And the holy Zohar says: ‘Blessed are You ... this Kiddush is in one balance opposite the testimony of faith, and they are thirty-five more words, as in Vayechulu; altogether they come to seventy words, with which the Shabbos of Shabbos eve is crowned.’ The matter is that a Jew must also bring holiness into Shabbos, as it is written, ‘Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it.’”

k: volume-ii|1368|0|R. Shlomo HaKohen Rabinowicz of Radomsk,
quote: Parallel: R. Shlomo HaKohen Rabinowicz of Radomsk, Tiferet Shlomo, Festivals, Shabbat 15: “As the Sages said: the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a crown on the head of every righteous person, as it says, ‘On that day Hashem of Hosts will be for a crown of beauty and a diadem of glory’ (Isaiah 28:5), for those who await His glory. ‘Could this be for everyone? Scripture says, “to the remnant of His people”: to one who makes himself like remnants.’ ... One may further find a hint in Rabbi Elazar’s words, ‘for those who await His glory, for one who makes himself like remnants’: it refers to those who await Hashem’s salvation and seek His unity, whose intention is not for themselves at all, not to merit by it this world or the World to Come, nor any recompense in the future salvation, but only for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, even if he should have no World to Come at all. ... This is what Rabbi Elazar meant: the Holy One, blessed be He, will be a crown of beauty for those who await His kindness and His glory and not their own glory at all; and this is ‘Could this be for everyone? Scripture says, to the remnant of His people,’ to one who makes himself like remnants and does not intend himself at all.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Yitro 6:1: “‘Let us make crowns for them ... with seventy crowns above the fifty.’ At the giving of the Torah, the Gemara says (Shabbat 88a): two crowns were tied to each Jew, one corresponding to ‘We shall do’ and one corresponding to ‘We shall hear’ ... and Moshe merited them all and took them; and it is brought from the holy Arizal that on Shabbos Moshe our teacher returns the crowns to Israel, and these are the crowns of Shabbos. ... The Torah from the side of the Tree of Life contains seven times ten, which is the seventy faces of the Torah, as it was before the corruption, when everything was contained in the Written Torah. ... From it spread out, from the side of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil, forty-nine faces pure and forty-nine faces impure, for there are fifty gates of Binah, the ‘much wisdom’ that repairs the ‘much anger.’ ... And the apprehension comes through the aspect of Da'as, which comes from the joining of Chochmah and Binah: the wisdom in the mind entering the depths of the heart, ‘Binah is the heart.’ ... And the two crowns: one is from the seventy crowns and one from the fifty.”

That is, first he should set his heart and thought on returning in complete repentance before his Creator, so that he can strip off and remove from himself the weekday garments through shame and repentance. ... But it will not help him to act like a monkey, immersing and intending in thought to cast away while casting away nothing, while his filth stays fixed in his heart like planted nails. Of such a case the Sages said (Ta'anit 16a): one who immerses with a creeping thing in his hand ... The main thing is purity of heart. The Rambam hinted at this in his clear language at the end of the Laws of Mikvaos: ‘... so one who directs his heart to purify his soul from the impurities of souls, which are thoughts of iniquity and evil

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Noach 5:3–4: “The mitzvah of lighting the lamp on Shabbos is to repair the blemish of the neshamah that comes from the blemish of the serpent. As we say, ‘And with the good lamp shining over the heads’: that is the neshamah, as one merits it in his mother’s womb: ‘a lamp burns over his head, and he looks and sees from one end of the world to the other, as it says, “When His lamp shone over my head”’ (Niddah 30b). ... In his mother’s womb the lamp is over his head, for while he is still in his mother’s womb there is no evil inclination in him, as it says (Sanhedrin 91b) from the verse ‘sin crouches at the door’; and the neshamah is pure, a portion of God, that is, from His blessed light. ... So too on Shabbos the additional soul, of which the holy Zohar says, ‘in which is all perfection, like the World to Come,’ is also the lamp over the head, a surrounding light, for the evil inclination has no dominion on Shabbos. ... Through the Shabbos lamp they repair the blemish of Adam's neshamah and are saved from the evil inclination; and this is what we say, ‘And with the good lamp shining over the heads.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 1:1: “In the holy Zohar (II 221a): ‘The world is sustained on three sides, and they are wisdom, understanding and knowledge, as it is written, “Hashem founded the earth with wisdom; He established the heavens with understanding.”’ ... And it is said, ‘A house is built with wisdom and established with understanding.’ ... ‘He established the heavens with understanding’ means understanding one thing from another, in which there is some apprehension; and this is what is said, ‘and established with understanding.’ ... ‘And with knowledge’ is the joining of mind and heart, wisdom and understanding, through the aspect of Da'as, ... and it is written, ‘Through His knowledge the depths were split,’ alluding to the Oral Torah, as the holy Zohar hinted (I 117a) in the verse ‘all the fountains of the great deep were split,’ the springs of wisdom below. ... Wisdom is the Torah, which is in a count: the five times ‘light’ in the utterance ‘Let there be light,’ which corresponds to the attribute of wisdom, correspond to the five books of the Torah, and the Torah is in number and count, all its letters and words; but the light hidden in it is ‘longer than the earth in measure and broader than the sea.’”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shoftim 5:1: “‘God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.’ In the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24): ‘“He blessed”: this is blessing; “and sanctified”: this is holiness; and facing both of them the early ones would go out to greet the bride and say twice, Come, O bride, come, O bride.’ The matter is that the holiness of Shabbos is the additional soul that comes to a person immediately at the entrance of Shabbos. And it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 48): ‘... fortunate is one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination departs from there.’ The two chambers of the heart are the wise heart at his right and the foolish heart at his left. The wise heart at his right means that words of Torah become fixed in his heart, and of this it says ‘He blessed’; ... plain ‘blessing’ means increase, an increase in the flow of words of Torah. ... The main blessing and increase belong to the Oral Torah, for the Written Torah has its letters counted and handed down, and not one letter may be added. ... And ‘He sanctified,’ this is holiness, corresponding to the foolish heart at his left, for holiness is a matter of separation, as they said, ‘You shall be holy: be separate,’ that is, to empty the evil from it, as it says, ‘and the evil inclination departs from there.’”

Shmuel Bornsztain of Sochatchov, Shem MiShmuel, Vayakhel 4:2, 4:4: “‘Moses assembled the entire congregation ... and on the seventh day it shall be holy for you,’ and Rashi: he placed Shabbos before the work of the Mishkan to say that it does not override Shabbos. One must consider: in Hashem's command to Moshe, the work of the Mishkan came before Shabbos, ... and in Moshe's charge to Israel he placed Shabbos first. Why did Moshe change the order? ... My father, of holy memory, explained the Gemara (Shabbat 69b): one who was walking in the desert and does not know when it is Shabbos, one says he counts six days and keeps one, and the other says he keeps one and counts six. He said that Shabbos has two aspects: it comes after the working days as their completion, and it also gives strength and life for what follows, for from it the six days are blessed. ... I added an explanation of the Gemara's words, ‘one holds like the creation of the world and one holds like Adam’: the order of Creation was that man, created upright, would do his work in the material and the spiritual, sifting out all the parts of holiness and raising them, and afterward, according to his deeds, he would merit the light of Shabbos's holiness: ‘whoever toiled on Shabbos eve will eat on Shabbos.’ But once Adam sinned and fell from his level, had Shabbos not come and given him strength and life, he could not have begun to do anything. Rather Shabbos breathed into him a spirit of new life, and wit

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Emor 4:1: “In the first Commandments it is written ‘Remember,’ ... and then comes the command, ‘Rest on it, as I rested on it,’ ... and this is what the Mekhilta says: ‘Remember: before it,’ that through the working days they bring holiness into Shabbos, just as with Hashem's Shabbos, where the working days came first and afterward the repose on Shabbos. Therefore it is written, ‘Six days you shall labor and do all your work,’ that everything he does should have holiness in it, intended for the sake of Heaven. ... In the later Commandments ... it says ‘Guard,’ and the Mekhilta says: ‘Guard: after it.’ That is, after the corruption Shabbos was given to them to repair the working days that come after it, so that they would be in holiness, as with Adam, to whom Shabbos was given first and afterward the working days, so that through Shabbos he would repair the working days; as the Gemara says (Shabbat 69b), one holds like the creation of the world and one holds like Adam. ... And in Ki Sisa and Vayakhel it is written ‘Six days work shall be done,’ for there they were commanded concerning the work of the Mishkan, and all the work of the working days was the work of the Mishkan, in holiness.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 10:1: “The holiness of Shabbos is always according to the holiness of the toil of the working days, which is why the six working days are always mentioned before Shabbos. And on Shabbos holiness shines onto the working days that follow it, and they are in greater holiness than the six working days before; and when the second Shabbos comes it is added to in further holiness, and so Shabbos bestows further holiness on the coming working days, and so on forever: all the days of his life he is walking. For this reason we say at the departure of Shabbos, ‘May the pleasantness of Hashem be upon us,’ which is the blessing with which Moshe our teacher blessed them, as Rashi writes: ‘What blessing did he bless them with? May it be His will that the Shechinah rest on the work of your hands’ (Bamidbar Rabbah 12) ... We ask that the working days have blessing, that is, Binah and words of Torah, which we merit on Shabbos, flowing from it into the working days, so that we can devote ourselves to the toil of Torah; ‘and may the Shechinah rest on the work of our hands,’ that it be like the work of the Mishkan, that even in the work of this world the intention be for the sake of Heaven and the deeds be sanctified.”

Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shemini 10:1: “The root of the kelipot is jealousy, desire, and honor, which are the root of the three transgressions, idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed, and all three of them are fire. The refinement of this is in this week of the attribute of Gevurah, which is the fire above, ‘a fire that consumes fire,’ to nullify the evil inclination’s fire of the three kelipot. And Shabbat is shin-bat, the daughter crowned with the patriarchs, as the holy Zohar says ... ‘Sustain me with eshishot’: these are the patriarchs. k: volume-ii|1378|0|R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissasc
quote: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Shabbatot 9:9: “The Tikkunei Zohar say that ‘Do not kindle fire ... on the Shabbat day’ means not to become angry, for whoever becomes angry is as though he kindled the fire of Gehinnom. People ask: anger is forbidden on weekdays too, so what is more severe about Shabbat? It seems to me, the humble one, that on weekdays Gehinnom burns in any case, but on Shabbat the fire of Gehinnom is extinguished, and that man kindles it and arouses, Heaven forbid, the punishments of Gehinnom even on Shabbat. Moreover, it is as though he kindled fire on Shabbat, which is a primary labor. ... One who keeps Shabbat is forgiven even for idolatry, since Shabbat is equal to the whole Torah, and a sin does not extinguish the mitzvah of Shabbat; but whoever becomes angry is as though he worshiped idols, so anger on Shabbat extinguishes the mitzvah of Shabbat. ... Thus, ‘Do not kindle fire in all your dwellings on the Shabbat day’: Shabbat is the sum of repentance, and this is ‘in all your dwellings,’ for keeping Shabbat is as though one fulfilled the mitzvot with all the limbs with which he sinned; but when he kindles the fire of anger, Heaven forbid, he extinguishes everything, and the special power of Shabbat does not help.”
